units.sanskrit: ओं सामवेदीया छान्दोग्योपनिषत्
units.english: One should meditate upon the syllable ‘Om’, the Udgītha; because one sings beginning with ‘Om’;

units.sanskrit: अथ प्रथमो ऽध्यायः
units.english: of this now follows the expounding

units.sanskrit: ओं शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः
units.english: One should meditate upon the syllable ‘Om’

units.sanskrit: केवलं च धूमादिमार्गेण चन्द्रलोकप्रतिपत्तिकारणम् ।
units.english: The syllable ‘Om’ is the most nearly appropriate name for the Supreme Self;

units.sanskrit: अत एव हि वक्ष्यतिसर्व एते पुण्यलोका भवन्ति । ब्रह्मसस्थो ऽमृतत्वमेतिइति ।
units.english: when that syllable is pronounced, the Supreme Self becomes pleased, just as an ordinary person is pleased when addressed by the name he likes best

units.sanskrit: ओम् इत्य् एतद् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपासीत । ओम् इति ह्य् उद्गायति । तस्योपव्याख्यानम् ॥ इत्युपोद्घातभाष्यम् ओमित्येतदक्षरमुद्गीथमुपासीत । ओमित्येतदक्षरं परमात्मनो ऽभिधानं नेदिष्ठम् ।
units.english: This syllable ‘Om’ is followed in the text by the particle ‘iti’ in order to show that the syllable is not expressive of does not connote the Supreme Self, and what is meant is that this verbal form is what is to be meditated upon as Self thus what is meant is that the syllable ‘Om is a representation of the Supreme SELF, just like the image and other things that people set up for worship

units.sanskrit: एवं नामत्वेन प्रतीकत्वेन च परमात्मोपासनसाधनं श्रेष्ठमिति सर्ववेदान्तेष्वगतम् ।
units.english: Thus what is learnt from all the Vedānta texts is that the syllable, being the name and the image of the Supreme SELF, is the best basis for meditating upon that SELF

units.sanskrit: जपकर्मस्वाध्यायाद्यन्तेषु च बहुशः प्रयोगात्प्रसिद्धमस्य श्रैष्ठ्यम् ।
units.english: It is a wellknown fact that this syllable is largely used in Japa, at rites and in the beginning and at the end of Vedic study;

units.sanskrit: अतस्तदेतक्षरं वर्णात्मकमुद्गीथभक्त्यवयवत्वादुद्गीथशब्दवाच्यमुपासीत ।
units.english: It is for these reasons that one should meditate upon this syllable, in the verbal form, which is spoken of as ‘Udgītha’, on the ground of its forming a constituent part of this name ‘Udgītha’;

units.sanskrit: कर्माङ्गावयवभूत ओङ्कारे परमात्मप्रतीके दृढामैकाग्र्यलक्षणां मतिं सन्तनुयात् ।
units.english: which means that one should firmly cultivate concentrated attention upon the syllable ‘Om’ which represents the Supreme SELF and which is an essential part of all sacrificial acts

units.sanskrit: स्वयमेव श्रुतिरोङ्कारस्योद्गीथशब्दवाच्यत्वे हेतुमाहओमिति ह्युद्गायति । ओमित्यारभ्य हि यस्मादुद्गायत्यत उद्गीथ ओङ्कार इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The Text itself provides the reason for the syllable ‘Om’ being spoken of as ‘Udgītha’ because one sings beginning with ‘Om’; inasmuch as one begins singing with ‘Om’, this syllable is called ‘Udgītha’

units.sanskrit: तस्योपव्याख्यानं तस्याक्षरस्योपव्याख्यानमेवमुपासनमेवंविभूत्येवंफलमित्यादिकथनमुपव्याख्यानम् ।
units.english: The ‘expounding’ of the said syllable constitutes ‘meditation’ upon it; this ‘expounding’ consists in describing its potencies, the results it brings about and so forth

units.sanskrit: प्रवर्तत इति वाक्यशेषः ॥
units.english: The term ‘follows’ ‘pravartate’ has to be supplied

units.sanskrit: एषां भूतानां पृथिवी रसः ।
units.english: The Earth is the essence of all beings;

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्या आपो रसः । अपाम् ओषधयो रसः ।
units.english: Water is the essence of the Earth; Herbs are the essence of Water;

units.sanskrit: ओषधीनां पुरुषो रसः । पुरुषस्य वाग् रसः ।
units.english: Man is the essence of Herbs; Speech is the essence of Man;

units.sanskrit: वाच ऋग् रसः । ऋचः साम रसः ।
units.english: Ṛk is the essence of Speech; Sāman is the essence of Ṛk;

units.sanskrit: साम्न उद्गीथो रसः ॥
units.english: Udgītha is the essence of Sāman

units.sanskrit: एषां चराचराणां भूतानां पृथिवी रसो गतिः परायणमवष्टम्भः ।
units.english: Of all beings,animate and inanimate;Earth is the essence,ie origin, substratum and ultimate solvent

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्या आपो रसो ऽप्सु ह्योता च प्रोता च पृथिव्यतस्ता रसः पृथिव्याः ।
units.english: Of Earth, Water is the essence; it is in Water that Earth is interwoven like warp and woof; hence Water is the essence of Earth

units.sanskrit: अपामोषधयो रसो ऽप्परिणामत्वादोषधीनाम् ।
units.english: Of Water, Herbs are the essence; as Herbs are modifications of Water

units.sanskrit: तासां पुरुषो रसो ऽन्नपरिणामत्वात् पुरुषस्य । तस्यापि पुरुषस्य वाग्रसः ।
units.english: Of these Herbs Man is the essence; as Man is developed through the food he eats Of Man, Speech is the essence;

units.sanskrit: पुरुषावयवानां हि वाक्सारिष्ठा । अतो वाक्पुरुषस्य रस उच्यते ।
units.english: Speech is the most essential, therefore, Speech is called the ‘essence’ of Man Of Speech, Ṛk is the essence

units.sanskrit: तस्या अपि वाच ऋग्रसः सारतरा । ऋचः साम रसः सारतरम् ।
units.english: Of Ṛk, Sāman is the essence ie the most essential part Of Sāman, the essence is Udgītha,ie

units.sanskrit: तस्यापि साम्न उद्गीथः प्रकृतत्वादोङ्कारः सारतरः ॥
units.english: in the present context, the syllable ‘OM’ is the most essential

units.sanskrit: स एष रसानां रसतमः परमः परार्ध्यो ऽष्टमो यदुद्गीथः ॥
units.english: This Udgītha is the best essence of the essences, the eighth, supreme and deserving of the highest position

units.sanskrit: एवं स एष उद्गीथाख्य ओङ्कारो भूतादीनामुत्तरोत्तररसानामतिशयेन रसो रसतमः ।
units.english: Thus then, the syllable ‘Om’, named the Udgītha, is the best essence among all the essences, Earth and the rest, which have been mentioned in the preceding text in the Ascending order of their ‘essentiality’

units.sanskrit: परमः परमात्मप्रतीकत्वात् ।
units.english: It is the ‘supreme’, because it represents the Supreme SELF

units.sanskrit: परार्ध्योर्ऽधं स्थानं,
units.english: It is ‘deserving of the highest position’, ‘ardha’ is position;

units.sanskrit: परं च तदर्धं च परार्धं तदर्हतीति परार्ध्यः परमात्मस्थानार्हः परमात्मवदुपास्यत्वादित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: ‘para’ is highest; hence ‘parardha’ is that which is deserving of the highest position; that is, deserving of the same position as the Supreme SELF; the sense is that it is so because it deserves to be meditated upon and worshipped as the Supreme SELF

units.sanskrit: अष्टमः पृथिव्यादिरससंख्यायां यदुद्गीथो य उद्गीथः ॥
units.english: It is the eighth,in the numbering of Earth and the other essences ‘Yad udgīthaḥ’ should be construed as ‘Yaḥ udgīthaḥ’

units.sanskrit: कतमा कतम र्क् कतमत् कतमत् साम कतमः कतम उद्गीथ इति विमृष्टं भवति ॥
units.english: What, what is Ṛk? What, what is Sāman ? What, what is Udgītha ?this is now considered

units.sanskrit: वाच ऋग्रस इत्युक्तम् ।
units.english: It has been asserted that ‘Ṛk is the essence of Speech’

units.sanskrit: कतमा सर्क्कतमत्तत्साम कतमो वा स उद्गीथः । कतमा कतमेति वीप्सा'दरार्था ।
units.english: Now the question arisesWhat is ‘Ṛk’? What is ‘Sāman’? What is the said ‘Udgītha’?

units.sanskrit: ननुवा बहूनां जातिपरिप्रश्ने डतमच् ।
units.english: The repetition of the word what is meant to indicate the importance attached to the subject

units.sanskrit: न ह्यत्र ऋग्जातिबहुत्वं कथं डतमच्प्रयोगः ।
units.english: and in the present instance, there is not a multiplicity of the genus ‘Ṛk’ ; how is it then that the affix ‘ḍatamach’ has been used?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: This objection has no force

units.sanskrit: जातौ परिप्रश्नो जातिपरिप्रश्न इत्येतस्मिन्विग्रहे जातावृग्व्यक्तीनां बहुत्वोपपत्तेः । न तु जातेः परिप्रश्न इति विगृह्यते ।
units.english: In the grammatical rule referred to there is the term ‘jātiparipraśna’ which is expounded as ‘Jātau paripraśnaḥ’, ‘question relating to the genus’, and there is multiplicity of individuals included under the single genus ‘Ṛk’, and the compound is not to be expounded as ‘question of genus, ‘Jāteḥ paripraśnaḥ’

units.sanskrit: ननु जातेः परिप्रश्न इत्यस्मिन्विग्रहे कतमः कठ इत्याद्युदाहरणमुपपन्नं जातौ परिप्रश्न इत्यत्र तु न युज्यते ।
units.english: The Opponent rejoinsIt is only when the compound ‘jātiparipraśna’ is expounded as ‘jāteḥ paripraśnaḥ’, the question of genus, that the presence of the ‘ḍatamachaaffix’ in the phrase ‘Katamaḥ kathaḥ’, ‘which one is of the Kathaclan, can be justified [as here, the question is of the genus; it could not be justified if the compound were expounded as ‘jātau paripraśnaḥ’ ‘question relating to the genus’

units.sanskrit: तत्रापि कठादिजातावेव व्यक्तिबहित्वाभिप्रायेण परिप्रश्न इत्यदोषः ।
units.english: AnswerIn the instance cited also, the question is in reference to several individuals included under the clan ‘Kaṭha’;

units.sanskrit: यदि जातेः परिप्रश्नः स्यात्कतमा कतमर्गित्यादावुपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यं स्याद्विमृष्टं भवति विमर्शः कृतो भवति ॥
units.english: so that the objection has no force If the question raised were one of the genus, then, in that case, it would be necessary to find out some other rule justifying the term in the present text, which, being Vedic, cannot be rejected as wrong

units.sanskrit: वाग् एवर्क् ।
units.english: Speech itself is Ṛk;

units.sanskrit: प्राणः साम ।
units.english: Lifebreath is Sāman;

units.sanskrit: ओम् इत्य् एतद् अक्षरम् उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the syllable Om is Udgītha

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतन् मिथुनं यद् वाक् च प्राणश् चर्क् च साम च ॥
units.english: This indeed is a couple Speech and Lifebreath Ṛk and Sāman

units.sanskrit: विमर्शे हि कृते सति प्रतिवचनोक्तिरुपपन्ना वागेवर्क्प्राणः सामेति ।
units.english: After the consideration has been done, the appropriate answer is stated Speech is Ṛk, Lifebreath is Sāman

units.sanskrit: वागृचोरेकत्वे ऽपि नाष्टमत्वव्याघातः पूर्वस्माद्वाक्यान्तरत्वादाप्तिगुणसिद्धय ओमित्येतदक्षरमुद्गीथ इति ।
units.english: Even though Speech and Ṛk are declared here to be one, this can not be regarded as selfcontradictory, in view of the eighth position assigned to the Udgītha in the text , above;

units.sanskrit: वाक्प्राणावृक्सामयोनी इति वागेवर्क्प्राणः सामेत्युच्यते । यथाक्रममृक्सामयोन्योर्वाक्प्राणयोर्ग्रहणे हि सर्वासामृचां सर्वेषां च साम्नामवरोधः कृतः स्यात् ।
units.english: In fact, Speech and Lifebreath are the sources of Ṛk and Sāman, respectively; and yet Speech itself is declared to be Ṛk and Lifebreath itself to be Saman, If the text had mentioned ‘Speech and ‘LifeBreath’ as the sources of Ṛk and Sāman respectively, then, all Ṛks and all Samans would become included;

units.sanskrit: सर्वर्क्सामावरोधे चर्क्सामसाध्यानां च सर्वकर्मणामवरोधः कृतः स्यात् ।
units.english: and the inclusion of all Ṛks and all Sāmans implies the inclusion of all those acts rites that are accomplished with the help of Ṛks and Sāmans;

units.sanskrit: तदवरोधे च सर्वे कामा अवरुद्धाः स्युः ।
units.english: so that practically all acts become included

units.sanskrit: ओमित्येतदक्षरमुद्गीथ इति भक्त्याशङ्का विनर्त्यते । तद्वा एतदिति मिथुनं निर्दिश्यते ।
units.english: There may be an idea that the expression ‘The syllable Om is ‘Udgītha’ is only figurative; this idea is set aside by what follows in the text

units.sanskrit: किं तन्मिथुनमित्याह यद्वाक्च प्राणश्च सर्वऋक्सामकारणभूतौ मिथुनम् ।
units.english: Question ‘What is that Couple?’Answer ‘Speech and Lifebreath’ are the ‘couple, the sources of all Ṛks and all Sāmans

units.sanskrit: ऋक्व साम चेति ऋक्सामकारणावृक्सामशब्दोक्तावित्यर्थः ।
units.english: The words ‘Ṛks’ and ‘Sāmans’ that follow are meant to point out that the Speech and Lifebreath spoken of are the sources of Ṛk and Sāman;

units.sanskrit: न तु स्वतन्त्रमृक्च साम च मिथुनम् ।
units.english: and ‘Ṛk and Sāman’ are not meant to be a separate independent couple

units.sanskrit: अन्यथा हि वाक्च प्राणश्चेत्येकं मिथुनमृक्साम चापरं मिथुनमिति द्वे मिथुने स्याताम् ।
units.english: If this were not so, then, ‘Speech and Lifebreath would be one ‘couple, and ‘Ṛk and Sāman would be another couple’; so there would be two ‘couples’;

units.sanskrit: तथा च तदेतन्मिथुनमित्येकवचननिर्देषो ऽनुपपन्नः स्यात् ।
units.english: and in that case, the singular number in the phrase ‘This indeed is a couple’ would be incompatible ]

units.sanskrit: तस्मादृक्सामयोन्योर्वाक्प्राणयोरेव मिथुनत्वम् ॥ तद् एतन् मिथुनम् ओम् इत्य् एतस्मिन्न् अक्षरे संसृज्यते ।
units.english: Hence what are meant to be spoken of as ‘couple here are only ‘Speech and Lifebreath’, as the sources of Ṛk and Sāman respectively This couple is joined together in the syllable Om

units.sanskrit: यदा वै मिथुनौ समागच्छत आपयतो वै ताव् अन्यो ऽन्यस्य कामम् ॥
units.english: Whenever, verily, a couple is joined together, each fulfils the desire of the other

units.sanskrit: तदेतदेवंलक्षणं मिथुनमोमित्येतस्मिन्नक्षरे संसृज्यते ।
units.english: ‘This couple’, just described, ‘is joined together in the syllable Om’

units.sanskrit: एवं सर्वकामावाप्तिगुणविशिष्टं मिथुनमोङ्कारे संसृष्टं विद्यत इत्योङ्कारस्य सर्वकामावाप्तिगुणवत्त्वं प्रसिद्धम् ।
units.english: Thus the sense is that the Couple, endowed with the quality of fulfilling all desires, remains ‘joined together in the syllable ‘Om’; and the fact of the syllable ‘Om being endowed with the quality fulfilling all desires is wellknown

units.sanskrit: वाङ्मयत्वमोङ्कारस्य प्राणनिष्पाद्यत्वं च मिथुनेन संसृष्टत्वं मिथुनस्य कामापयितृत्वं प्रसिद्धमिति दृष्टान्त उच्यते । यथा लोके मिथुनौ मिथुनावयवौ स्त्रीपुंसौ यदा समागच्छतो ग्राम्यधर्मतया संयुज्येयानां तदा'पयतः प्रापयतो ऽन्योन्यस्येतरेतरस्य तौ कामम् ।
units.english: It is wellknown that a the syllable ‘Om’ contains within itself the entire literature, b that it is brought about pronounced through the Lifebreath, c that it joins within itself the ‘couple’, and d that the ‘couple’ fulfil all desires In order to make this clear, an illustration is citedIn ordinary life, ‘whenever a couple’ie man and woman, with the physical constituents of the couple,is joined together,ie, meet together, in sexual association,they fulfil each other’s desires

units.sanskrit: तथा च स्वात्मानुप्रविष्टेन मिथुनेन सर्वकामाप्तिगुणवत्त्वमोङ्कारस्य सिद्धमित्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: What is meant is that it becomes established in the same manner, the syllable ‘Om becomes the fulfiller of all desires, through the ‘Couple that lies within it

units.sanskrit: आपयिता ह वै कामानां भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ॥
units.english: He becomes the fulfiller of desires who, knowing this thus, meditates upon this syllable as Udgītha

units.sanskrit: तदुपासको ऽप्युद्गाता तद्धर्मा भवतीत्याहआपयिता ह वै कामानां यजमानस्य भवति य एतदक्षरमेवमाप्तिगुणवदुद्गीथमुपास्ते
units.english: One becomes a fulfiller of the desires of the sacrificer if he meditates upon this syllable itselfwhich has the character of fulfilmentas Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तस्यैतद्यथोक्तं फलमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: to such a one accrues the said result;

units.sanskrit: तं यथा यथोपासते तदेव भवतिइति श्रुतेः ॥
units.english: and this is in accordance with the Vedic text Just in so far as one meditates upon a thing, one becomes that thing itself

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् अनुज्ञाक्षरम् ।
units.english: This indeed is the syllable of acquiescence;

units.sanskrit: यद् धि किंचानुजानात्य् ओम् इत्य् एव तद् आह ।
units.english: whatever one acquiesces in, he says Om;

units.sanskrit: एषो एव समृद्धिर् यद् अनुज्ञा ।
units.english: acquiescence verily is prosperity;

units.sanskrit: समर्धयिता ह वै कामानां भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ॥
units.english: he becomes à prosperer of desires who, knowing this, meditates upon this syllable Om as Udgītha

units.sanskrit: समृद्धिगुणवांश्चोङ्कारः ।
units.english: The syllable ‘Om is also endowed with the quality of fulfilment success, prosperity

units.sanskrit: कथम्तद्वा एतत्प्रकृमनुज्ञाक्षरमनुज्ञा च साक्षरं च तत् ।
units.english: How?This syllable that we are dealing with is the ‘syllable of acquiescence’; ie it is the acquiescent syllable;

units.sanskrit: अनुज्ञानुमतिरोङ्कार इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: ‘acquiescence standing for agreement;this is what the syllable ‘Om’ is

units.sanskrit: कथमनुज्ञेत्याह श्रुतिरेव । यद्धि किञ्च यत्किञ्च लोके ज्ञानं धनं वानुजानाति विद्वान्धनी वा तत्रानुमतिं कुर्वन्नोमित्येव तदाह ।
units.english: The text itself explains how the syllable is one of acquiescenceIn common practice, whatever,idea or propertyone acquiesces in,be he a teacher or a wealthy person,in expressing his agreement, he says ‘Om’;

units.sanskrit: तथा च वेदेत्रयस्त्रिंशदित्योमिति होवाचैत्यादिना ।
units.english: eg in the Veda we find such texts as‘They are thirtythree;

units.sanskrit: तथा च लोके ऽपि तवेदं धनं गृह्णामीत्युक्त ओमित्याह ।
units.english: ‘Om’ yes he said In ordinary life also, when one says to another person‘This property is yours, am taking it’, the person addressed says ‘Om’ Yes, all right

units.sanskrit: अत एषा उ एवैषैव समृद्धिर्यदनुज्ञा यानुज्ञा सा समृद्धिस्तन्मूलत्वादनुज्ञायाः ।
units.english: For this reason Acquiescence verily is prosperity; that is, what is known as ‘acquiescence’ is Prosperity itself; because acquiescence is based upon prosperity;

units.sanskrit: समृद्धो ह्योमित्यनुज्ञां ददाति तस्मात्समृद्धिगुणवानोङ्कार इत्यर्थः । समृद्धिगुणोपासकत्वात्तद्धर्मा सन्समर्धयिता ह वै कामानां यजमानस्य भवति य एतदेवं विद्वानक्षरमुद्गीथमुपास्त इत्यादि पूर्ववत्
units.english: hence what the text means is that the syllable ‘Om’ is prosperity itself Inasmuch as the syllable is endowed with the quality of ‘prosperity’, one who meditates upon that quality, thereby becomes endowed with that quality and thence becomes the prosperer of desires for the sacrificer, when he knows this and meditates upon this syllable, as Udgītha

units.sanskrit: तेनेयं त्रयी विद्या वर्तते ।
units.english: With this syllable does the threefold Science proceed;

units.sanskrit: ओम् इत्य् आश्रावयति । ओम् इति शंसति । ओम् इत्य् उद्गायति ।
units.english: with Om does one recite, with Om does one direct, with Om does one sing;

units.sanskrit: एतस्यैव अक्षरस्यापचित्यै महिम्ना रसेन ॥
units.english: all this for the adoration of the same syllable;so also with the Grandeur and the Essence of this syllable, does the act of Sacrifice proceed

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीमक्षरं स्तौत्युपास्यत्वात्प्ररोचनार्थम् ।
units.english: Now with a view to attract people to it, the Text proceeds to eulogise the syllable, on the ground of its being a fit object of worship and meditation

units.sanskrit: कथं, तेनाक्षरेण प्रकृतेनेयमृग्वेदादिलक्षणा त्रयी विद्या त्रयीविद्याविहितं कर्मेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: How?With thissaid syllable,the threefold Scienceconsisting of the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda and Sāmaveda proceeds; what thus proceeds is the action prescribed by this threefold Science;

units.sanskrit: न हि त्रयी विद्यैवाऽश्रावणादिभिर्वर्तते कर्म तु तथा प्रवर्तत इति प्रसिद्धम् ।
units.english: because, as for the threefold Science itself, that itself does not proceed with reciting, directing and singing as mentioned in the Text; it is only the act that is known to proceed with these

units.sanskrit: कथमोमित्याश्रावत्योमिति शंसत्योमित्युद्गायतीति लिङ्गाच्च सोमयाग इति गम्यते ।
units.english: QuestionIn what way does the Act proceed with this syllable? AnswerWith ‘Om’ does one recite, with ‘Om’ does one direct and with ‘Om’ does one sing

units.sanskrit: तच्च कर्मैतस्यैवाक्षरस्यापचित्यै पूजार्थम् ।
units.english: This act Sacrifice is meant for the adoration of this same syllable;

units.sanskrit: परमात्मप्रतीकं हि तत् ।
units.english: as this syllable represents the Supreme SELF;

units.sanskrit: तदपचितिः परमात्मन एव सा ।
units.english: so that the adoration of the syllable would be the adoration of the Supreme SELF itself

units.sanskrit: स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवःइति स्मृतेः ।
units.english: To this same effect there is the Smṛtitext ‘Having adored Him with his action, the man attains success’

units.sanskrit: महिम्ना रसेन । किञ्चैतस्यैवाक्षरस्य महिम्ना महत्त्वेन ऋत्विग्यजमानादिप्राणैरित्यर्थः । तथैतस्यैवाक्षरस्य रसेन व्रीहियवादिरसनिर्वृत्तेन हविषेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: So also with the Grandeur and the EssenceFurther with the ‘grandeur’greatnessof this same syllable,ie with the lifebreaths of the Priests and the Sacrificer;similarly with the ‘Essence’ of this syllable,ie with the offering made up of the essential portions of Vrīhi, Yava and other grains

units.sanskrit: यागहोमाद्यक्षरेण क्रियते । तच्चा'दित्यमुपतिष्ठते । ततो वृष्ट्यादिक्रमेण प्राणो ऽन्नं च जायते ।
units.english: It is with the syllable ‘Om that all such acts as Sacrifices, Pouring of of Libations and so forth are performed;the acts thus performed go up to the Sun, and thenceforth does it become developedthrough rain and other processesinto the Lifebreath and foodgrains;and by means of the Lifebreath and foodgrains again are sacrifices performed

units.sanskrit: प्राणैरन्नेन च यज्ञस्तायते । अत उच्यते ऽक्षरस्य महिम्ना रस्न्ति ॥
units.english: It is for this reason that it has been declared that acts of Sacrifice proceed with the Grandeur and the Essence of this syllable

units.sanskrit: तेनोभौ कुरुतः । यश् चैतद् एवं वेद यश् च न वेद ।
units.english: Objection Both kinds of persons perform acts with this, those who know as well as those who do not know

units.sanskrit: नाना तु विद्या चाविद्या च ।
units.english: But verily, Knowledge and Ignorance are totally distinct;

units.sanskrit: यद् एव विद्यया करोति श्रद्धयोपनिषदा तद् एव वीर्यवत्तरं भवतीति खल्व् एतस्यैवाक्षरस्योपव्याख्यानं भवति ॥
units.english: and in fact, what is done with knowledge, faith and due application, that becomes more effective; thus indeed is there the expounding of this syllable itself

units.sanskrit: तत्राक्षरविज्ञानवतः कर्म कर्तव्यमिति स्थितमाभिपतितेनाभरेणोभौ यश्चैतदक्षरमेवं व्याख्यातं वेद यश्च कर्ममात्रविदक्षरयाथात्म्यं न वेद तावुभौ कुरुतः कर्म । तयोश्च कर्मसामर्थ्यादेव फलं स्यात्किं तत्राक्षरयाथात्म्यविज्ञानेनेति । दृष्टं हि लोके हरीतकीं भक्षयतोस्तद्रसाभिज्ञेतरयोर्विरेचनम् ।
units.english: Against this an objection is raisedWith this syllableboth kinds of persons, perform actsone who knows the syllable as describedabove, as well as one who knows only the nature of the act to be done and does not know the real character of the syllable;to both of them the results proceeding from the performance of the Act would accrue in an equal degree;what then is the need of knowing the real nature of the syllable Om?In ordinary life, it has been seen that when two persons eat the Harītakī, the purging that follows from the eating comes equally to both,to him who is cognisant of its purgative properties as also to him who is ignorant of it

units.sanskrit: नैवम् ।
units.english: It is not so, we reply

units.sanskrit: यस्मान्नाना तु विद्या चाविद्या च भिन्ने हि विद्याविद्ये ।
units.english: Because Knowledge and Ignorance are totally distinct;

units.sanskrit: नोङ्कारस्य कर्माङ्गत्वमात्रविज्ञानमेव रसतमाप्तिसमृद्धिगुणवद्विज्ञानं किं तर्हि ततो ऽभ्यधिकम् ।
units.english: The Knowledge of the syllable ‘Om’ being the essence of the Essences, its being endowed with the qualities of fulfilment and prosperity does not consist merely in Knowledge of that syllable being a factor of the sacrifice;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तदङ्गाधिक्यात्फलाधिक्यं युक्तमित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: What is meant is that, inasmuch as it is so, the result proceeding from the former must be superior to that proceeding from the latter

units.sanskrit: दृष्टं हि लोके वणिक्शबरयोः पद्मरागादिमणिविक्रये वणिजो विज्ञानाधिक्यात्फलाधिक्यम् ।
units.english: In ordinary life also, it is found that when a merchant and a forester sell pieces of Ruby and other gems, the former who knows the real character of the gems always obtains a higher price than the latter who is ignorant;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्यदेव विद्यया विज्ञानेन युक्तः सन्करोति कर्मश्रद्धया श्रद्दधानश्च सन्नुपनिषदा योगेन युक्तश्चेत्यर्थः । तदेव कर्म वीर्यवत्तरमविद्वत्कर्मणो ऽधिकफलं भवतीति ।
units.english: From this it follows that what is done with Knowledgeby a person fully cognisantand with faithby a person imbued with due faith,and with due applicationby a person who is equipped with the faculty of concentration,that Act becomes more effective,ie more fruitfulthan the Act done by the ignorant person

units.sanskrit: विद्वत्कर्मणो वीर्यवत्तरत्वटवचनादविदुषो ऽपि कर्म वार्यदेव भवतीत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: The assertion that the Act of the man with Knowledge is ‘more effective than that of the ignorant man means that even when done by the ignorant person, the act is effective;

units.sanskrit: न चाविदुषः कर्मण्यनधिकारः ।
units.english: so that it does not mean that the ignorant man is not fit to perform the act

units.sanskrit: औषस्त्ये काण्डे ऽविदुषामप्यार्विज्यदर्शनात् ।
units.english: In fact in the section dealing with Uṣasti later on it is described that even ignorant persons have performed the priestly functions

units.sanskrit: रसतमाप्तिसमृद्धिगुणवदक्षरमित्येकमुपासनम् ।
units.english: The act of meditating upon ‘Om’ as the ‘essence of essences’, as ‘fulfilment and as ‘prosperity’ forms a single act of ‘meditation’ and worship;

units.sanskrit: मध्ये प्रयत्नान्तरादर्शनात् ।
units.english: as there are no efforts intervening in between these

units.sanskrit: अनेकैर्हि विशेषणैरनेकधोपास्यत्वात्खल्वेतस्यैव प्रकृतस्योद्गीथाख्यस्याक्षरस्योपव्याख्यानं भवति ॥
units.english: In fact, the mention of several qualities means that it is to be meditated upon several times

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषच्छाङ्करभाष्ये प्रथमाध्यायस्य प्रथम खण्डः
units.english: Hence indeed there is expounding of this syllable ‘Om’ the Udgītha End of Section Khaṇḍa , of Discourse Adhyāya i

units.sanskrit: देवासुरा ह वै यत्र संयेतिरे । उभये प्राजापत्यास् तद् ध देवा उद्गीथम् आजह्रुर् अनेनैनान् अभिभविष्याम इति ॥
units.english: On the occasion when the Devas and Asurus,both born of Prajāpati,fought each other, the Devas took away the Udgītha,thinking ‘with this shall we suppress these’

units.sanskrit: देवासुरा देवाश्चासुराश्च ।
units.english: Devas and Asuras The term ‘deva’ is derived from the root ‘div’, to shine;

units.sanskrit: देवा दीव्यतेर्द्येतनार्थस्य शास्त्रोद्भासिता इन्द्रियवृत्तयः ।
units.english: hence the word ‘devas’ stands for such functionings of the senseorgans as are illuminated regulated by the scriptures;opposed to these are the ‘Asuras’

units.sanskrit: अशिरास्तद्विरीताः स्वेष्वेवासुषु विष्वग्विषयासु प्राणनक्रियासु रमणात्स्वाभाविक्यस्तम आत्मिका इन्द्रियवृत्तय एव ।
units.english: etymologically explained as ‘Asuṣu ramaṇāḥ’ ‘delighting in the spheres of all their own natural life’, and ‘inclinations’ as appertaining to all objects of sense; hence the term stands for those natural functions of the senseorgans which are of the nature of darkness ignorance

units.sanskrit: ह वा इति पूर्ववृत्तोद्भासकौ निपातौ ।
units.english: The particles ‘havā’ are indicative of past events

units.sanskrit: सम्पूर्वस्य यततेः संग्रामार्थत्वमिति संग्रामं कृतवन्त उत्यर्थः ।
units.english: the root ‘Yama’ with the prefix ‘sam’ signifies fighting; hence ‘Samyetire’, means fought

units.sanskrit: शास्रीयप्रकाशवृत्तयभिभवनाय प्रवृत्ताः स्वाभाविक्यस्तमोरूपा इन्द्रियवृत्तयो ऽसुराः ।
units.english: That is, the natural sensual inclinations partaking of ignorance operated towards the suppression of the activities regulated by the Scriptures;

units.sanskrit: तथा तद्विपरीताः शास्रार्थविषयविवेकज्योतिरात्मानो देवा स्वाभाविकतमोरूपासुराभिभवनाय
units.english: and similarly as opposed to these, the Devas who are of the nature of enlightenment proceeding from discrimination due to the Scriptures, operated towards the suppression of the A suras, who are of the nature of inborn darkness or ignorance;

units.sanskrit: प्रवृत्ता इत्यन्योन्याभिभवोद्भवरूपः संग्राम इव सर्वप्राणिषु प्रतिदेहं देवासुरसङ्ग्रामो
units.english: and thus there has been something like ‘fighting’ in the shape of the suppressing of each other, in the bodies of all living beings,a veritable ‘Devāsurasaṅgrāma’ Battle between Devas and Asuras, since time, without beginning

units.sanskrit: ऽनादिकालप्रवृत्त इत्यभिप्रायः । स इहश्रुत्या'ख्यायिकारूपेण धर्माधर्मोत्पत्तिविवेकविज्ञानाय कथ्यते प्राणविशुद्धिविज्ञानविधिपरतया ।
units.english: Such is the sense of the text It is this war that is described here, in the shape of a story, for the purpose of bringing about the knowledge of the due difference between what should be done Dharma and what should not be done Adharma,and as tending to a knowledge of the method of purification of the senses

units.sanskrit: अत उभये ऽपि देवासुराः प्रजापतेरपत्यानीति प्राजापत्याः । प्रजापतिः कर्मज्ञानाधिकृतः पुरुषः । पुरुष एवोक्थमयमेव महान्प्रजापतिःइति श्रुत्यन्तरात् ।
units.english: Thus both these, Devas and Asuras, born of Prajāpati,ie the children of Prajāpati;‘Prajāpati’ here stands for the Personality, the Person capable of performing acts and acquiring knowledge, in accordance with the Śrutitext declaring that ‘The Person himself is Uktha, he is Mahān, he is Prajāpati;

units.sanskrit: तस्य हि शास्रीयाः स्वाभाविक्यश्च करणवृत्तयो विरुद्धा अपत्यानीव तदुद्भवत्वात् ।
units.english: and all functionings of the senseorgansboth that are in accordance with the scriptures, as well as those natural ones that are contrary to those,arise in the Person, and as such are called his ‘children

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्रोत्कर्षापकर्षलक्षणनिमित्ते ह देवा उद्गीथभक्त्युपलक्षितमौद्गात्रं कर्मा'जह्रुराहृतवन्तः ।
units.english: On this occasion of fighting, for each other s rise and fall, the Devas took away the Udgītha; the term ‘Udgītha’ indirectly indicates the functions of the Udgātṛ Priest;

units.sanskrit: तस्यापि केवलस्या'हरणासम्भवाज्जोतिष्टोमाद्याहृतवन्त इत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: and there again, inasmuch as it cannot be possible to take away these functions of that one Priest alone, what is meant is that they took away all such acts sacrifices as the Jyotiṣṭoma and the like

units.sanskrit: तत्किमर्थमाजह्रुरित्युच्यते अनेन कर्मणैनानसुरानभिभविष्याम इत्येवमभिप्रायाः सन्तः ॥
units.english: The next sentence explains for what purpose they took away the said functionsThey thought that with this,ie by means of this act of the Sacrifice we shall suppress these,Asuras

units.sanskrit: ते ह नासिक्यं प्राणम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
units.english: They meditated upon the Breath in the nose as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तं ह असुराः पाप्मना विविधुः ।
units.english: the Asuras pierced it with evil;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तेनोभयं जिघ्रति सुरभि च दुर्गन्धि च ।
units.english: hence with it one smells both what is goodsmelling and what is foulsmelling;

units.sanskrit: पाप्मना ह्य् एष विद्धः ॥
units.english: as it has been pierced with evil

units.sanskrit: यदा च तदुद्गीथं कर्मा'जिहीर्षवस्तदाते ह देवा नासिक्यं नासिकायां भवं चेतनावन्तं घ्राणं प्राणमुद्गीथकर्तारमुद्गीथभक्त्योपासांचक्रिरेझ्रुपासनण्टकृतवन्त इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: They, the Devas, meditated upon,performed meditation uponthe Breath in the nose,ie the sensory organ of olfaction,as Udgītha,ie the performer of the Sacrificial Act, Udgātṛ Priest, regarding him as the Udgītha itself

units.sanskrit: खल्वेतस्यैवाक्षरस्येत्योङ्कारमुपासांचक्रिर इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: What this means is that they meditated upon the Udgīthaie the syllable ‘Om’as the Breath in the Olfactory Organ

units.sanskrit: एवं हि प्रकृतार्थपरित्यागो ऽप्रकृतार्थोपादानं च न कृतं स्यात् ।
units.english: It is only when the text is taken to mean this that the context becomes preserved and the introduction ol foreign matter becomes avoided

units.sanskrit: खल्वेतस्यैवाक्षरस्येत्योङ्कारो ह्यापास्यतया प्रकृतः । ननूद्गीथोपलक्षितं कर्मा'हृतवन्त इत्यवोच इदानीमेव;
units.english: As a matter of fact, the context relates to this syllable ‘Om’ itself as the object of meditation ObjectionYou have declared the sense of the previous text to be that the Devas took away the Act Rite related to the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: कथं नासिक्यप्राणदृष्ट्योङ्कारमुपासांचक्रिर इत्यात्थ ।
units.english: how is it, then, that now you say that they meditated upon the syllable ‘Om’ in the form of the Breath in the Nose?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThere is no force in this objection;

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथकर्मण्येव हि तत्कर्तृप्राणदेवतादृष्ट्योद्गीथभक्त्यवयवश्चोङ्कार उपास्यत्वेन विवक्षितो न स्वतन्त्रो ऽतस्तादर्थ्येन कर्मा'हृतवन्त इति युक्तमेवोक्तम् ।
units.english: what is meant is that the syllable ‘Om’, which is a part of the Udgītha, should be meditated upon as the Breath in the Nose, and not independently by itself; and such being the sense, it is only right to say that ‘they took away the Act Sacrifice’ for the purpose of the said meditation

units.sanskrit: तमेवं देवैर्वृतमुद्गातारं हासुराः स्वाभाविकतम आत्मानो ज्योतीरूपं नासिक्यं प्राणं देवं स्वोत्थेन पाप्मनाधर्मासङ्गरूपेण विविधुर्विद्धवन्तः
units.english: When the Devas had thus selected their Udgātṛ Priest, the Asuras,ie beings characterised by inherent darkness ignorance,pierced the luminous deity of the Breath in the Nose, with Evil;

units.sanskrit: संसर्ग कृतवन्त इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, they contaminated it with attachment to Evil arising out of themselves

units.sanskrit: स हि नासिक्यः प्राणः कल्याणगन्धग्रहणाभिमानासङ्गाभिभूतविवेकविज्ञानो बभूव ।
units.english: Thereupon the Deity of the ‘Breath in the Nose had his wisdom suppressed by the feeling of attachment in the form of the egoistic notion that the perception of sweet smell belongs to himself;

units.sanskrit: स तेन दोषेण पाप्मसंसर्गी बभूव । तदिदमुक्तमसुराः पाप्मना विविधुरिति ।
units.english: and through this contact, he became contaminated with evil, This is what is meant by the assertion that ‘the Asuras pierced it with evil’

units.sanskrit: यस्मादासुरेण पाप्मना विद्धस्तस्मात्तेन पाप्मना प्रेरितो घ्राणः प्राणो दुर्गन्धिग्राहकः प्राणिनाम् ।
units.english: Because the said ‘Breath in the Nose has been pierced with evil,therefore, on becoming urged by that Evil, the olfactory organ,ie the lifebreath in the Nose,comes to apprehend foul smell, among living beings

units.sanskrit: अतस्तेनोभयं जिघ्रति लोकः सुरभि च दुर्गन्धि च ।
units.english: It is for this reason that people smell ‘what is goodsmelling and also what is foulsmelling;

units.sanskrit: पाप्मना ह्येष यस्माद्विद्धः ।
units.english: because it has been pierced with Evil

units.sanskrit: उभयग्रहणमविवक्षितम् । यस्योभयं हविरार्तिमार्छतीति यद्वत् ।
units.english: No significance attaches to the term ‘both’,just as in the case of the text ‘If both offeringmaterials become spoilt etc’

units.sanskrit: यदेवेदमप्रतिरूपं जिघ्रतीति समानप्रकरणश्रुतेः ॥
units.english: which says, ‘When one does perceive improper smell, it is due to that Evil’

units.sanskrit: अथ ह वाचम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
units.english: Then they meditated upon Speech as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तां हासुराः पाप्मना विविधुः ।
units.english: the Asuras pierced this with evil;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तयोभयं वदति सत्यं चानृतं च ।
units.english: hence one speaks both what is true and also what is untrue;

units.sanskrit: पाप्मना ह्य् एषा विद्धा ॥
units.english: because it is pierced with evil

units.sanskrit: अथ ह चक्षुर् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
units.english: Then they meditated upon the Eye as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तद् धासुराः पाप्मना विविधुः ।
units.english: the Asuras pierced it with evil;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तेनोभयं पश्यति दर्शनीयं चादर्शनीयं च ।
units.english: hence one sees both what is sightly and also what is unsightly;

units.sanskrit: पाप्मना ह्य् एतद् विद्धम् ॥
units.english: because it is pierced with evil

units.sanskrit: अथ ह श्रोत्रम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
units.english: Then, they meditated upon the Ear as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तद् धासुराः पाप्मना विविधुः ।
units.english: the Asuras pierced it with evil;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तेनोभयं शृणोति श्रवणीयं चाश्रवणीयं च ।
units.english: hence one hears both what is agreeable to hear and what Jis disagreeable to hear;

units.sanskrit: पाप्मना ह्य् एतद् विद्धम् ॥
units.english: because it is pierced with evil

units.sanskrit: अथ ह मन उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
units.english: Then they meditated upon Mind as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तद् धासुराः पाप्मना विविधुः ।
units.english: the Asuras pierced this with evil;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तेनोभयं संकल्पयते संकल्पनीयं च ।
units.english: hence one conceives both what should be conceived and what should not be conceived;

units.sanskrit: पाप्मना ह्य् एतद् विद्धम् ॥
units.english: because it is pierced with evil

units.sanskrit: मुख्यप्राणस्योपास्यत्वाय तद्विशुद्धत्वानुभवार्थो ऽयं विचारः श्रुत्या प्रवर्तितः ।
units.english: This disquisition is introduced by the Vedic text for the purpose of showing that it is the ‘Breath in the Mouth’ that is pure and hence a fit object of meditation

units.sanskrit: अतश्चक्षुरादिदेवताः क्रमेण विचार्या'सुरेण पाप्मना विद्धा इत्यपोह्यन्ते ।
units.english: With this view the presiding deities of the Eye and other organs of perception are discussed in due order and then discarded on the ground of their being ‘pierced with evil’ by the A uras

units.sanskrit: अथ ह वाचं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मन इत्यादि ।
units.english: All the rest of it is as in the preceding textThey meditated upon ‘Speech, the Eye, the Ear, the Mind’

units.sanskrit: अनुक्ता अप्यन्यास्त्वग्रसमादिदेवता द्रष्टव्याः ।
units.english: Those organs that are not actually named here,such as the organ of;Touch, the organ of Taste and so forth,should also be understood to be included;

units.sanskrit: एवमु खल्वेता देवताः पाप्मभिः इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् ॥
units.english: as is clearly declared in another Vedic text‘Thus have all these deities been pierced with evil

units.sanskrit: अथ ह य एवायं मुख्यः प्राणस् तम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
units.english: Then they meditated upon that Breath which is in the Mouth, as Udgītha; when the Asuras approached it, they were smashed;

units.sanskrit: तं हासुरा ऋत्वा विदध्वंसुर् यथाश्मानम् आखणम् ऋत्वा विध्वंसेतैवम् ॥ आसुरेण विद्धत्वाद्घ्राणादिदेवता अपोह्याथानन्तरं य एवायं प्रसिद्धो
units.english: Having discarded the Deities of the Olfactory and other organs on account of their being pierced by the Asuras, the Devas, thereafter, meditated upon that wellknown ‘Breath which is in the Mouth’ie which proceeds from the mouth,as Udgītha

units.sanskrit: मुखे भवो मुख्यः प्राणस्तमुद्गीथमुपासाञ्चक्रिरे तं हासुराः पूर्ववदृत्वा प्राप्य
units.english: As before, the Asuras approached this Breath also for piercing it; but on approachingie, getting atit, they were smashed;

units.sanskrit: विदध्वंसुर्विनष्टा अभिप्रायमात्रेण ।
units.english: that is, they perished through the mere intention of piercing the said Breath

units.sanskrit: कथं विनष्टा इत्यत्र दृष्टान्तमाहयथा लोके ऽश्मानमाखणं न शक्यते खनितुं कुद्दालादिभिरपि भेत्तुं न शक्यो ऽखण एवा'खणस्तमृत्वा सामर्थ्याल्लोष्टः पांसुपिण्डः क्षुत्यन्तराच्चाश्मनि क्षिप्तो ऽश्मभेदनाभिप्रायेण तस्याश्मनः किञ्चिदप्यकृत्वा स्वयं
units.english: In answer to the question,How, without having done anything to the Breath, were they smashed?the text supplies an illustrationIn the ordinary world, when a piece of stone which is solid,literally that which cannot be dug into with spades and other implements,is approachedhitby a clod of Earth,when the clod of Earth is hit at the hard and solid piece of stone,with the intention of breaking the stone,the clod, without doing anything to the stone, becomes itself shattered;

units.sanskrit: एवं यथाश्मानम् आखणम् ऋत्वा विध्वंसत एवं हैव स विध्वंसते य एवंविदि पापं कामयते यश् चैनम् अभिदासति ।
units.english: Thus, just as the clod of Earth striking a solid piece of stone is rent asunder, so also is rent asunder one who wishes ill to the person knowing this science; as also one who injures him;

units.sanskrit: स एषो ऽश्माखणः ॥
units.english: for he is a solid piece of stone

units.sanskrit: एवं विशुद्धो ऽसुरैरधर्षितत्वात्प्राण इति एवंविदः प्राणात्मभूतस्येदं फलमाहयथाश्मानमिति ।
units.english: Thus, inasmuch as this Breath has not been injured by the Asuras, it is pure The Text describes the result that accrues to one who knows this essential character of the BreathJust as striking etc

units.sanskrit: एष एव दृष्टान्तः ।
units.english: This is an illustration

units.sanskrit: एवं हैव स विध्वंसते विनश्यति । को ऽसावित्याहय एवंविदि यथोक्तप्राणविदि पापं तदनर्हं कर्तु कामयत इच्छति
units.english: So also is rent asunder ie perishes who?One who wishes ill,what he does not deserve,to the person who knows the Breath as described above; as also one who injures him,who harms him;

units.sanskrit: यश्चाप्येनमभिदासति हिनस्ति प्राणविदं प्रत्याक्रोशताडनादि प्रयुङ्क्ते सो ऽप्येवमेव
units.english: that is one who does such acts against the knower of the Science of Breath as abusing, assaulting and the like;such a one also is rent asunder in the same way as the clod of Earth

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्स एष प्राणवित्प्राणभूतत्वादश्माखण इवाश्माखणो ऽधर्षणीय इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The reason for this lies in the fact that hethe man knowing the Science of Breath,is LifeBreath itself and as such, is a solid piece of stone,ie not injurable

units.sanskrit: ननु नासिक्यो ऽपि प्राणो वाय्वात्मा यथा मुख्यस्तत्र नासिक्यः प्राणः पाप्मना विद्धः प्राण एव सन्न मुख्यः कथम् ।
units.english: ObjectionThe Breath in the Nose also is of the nature of Air, just like the Breath in the Mouth; how then is it that the Breath in the Nose was pierced by evil, and not the Breath in the Mouth,though both are Breath?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: There is no force in this objection

units.sanskrit: नासिक्यस्तु स्थानकरणवैगुण्याद्विद्धो वाय्वात्मापि सन्मुख्यः स्थानदेवताबलीयस्त्वान्न विद्ध इति युक्तम् ।
units.english: It is only right that, the Breath in the Nose, though of the nature of Air, was pierced on account of the defective character of its location and organ,and yet the Breath in the Mouth was not so pierced, by reason of the strength of its location and deity;

units.sanskrit: यथा वास्यादयः शिक्षावत्पुरुषाश्रयाः कार्यविशेषं कुर्वन्ति नान्यहस्तगतास्तद्वद्दोषवद्घ्राणसचिवत्वाद्विद्धा घ्राणदेवता न मुख्यः ॥
units.english: just as such implements as the Axe and the like accomplish good work only when handled by welltrained men, and not when handled by other men The Deity of the Nose was pierced because of the defective character of the Nose, its substratum,not so the Breath in the Mouth

units.sanskrit: नैवैतेन सुरभि न दुर्गन्धि विजानाति ।
units.english: By this, verily, one cognises not what is goodsmelling, nor what is foul smelling;

units.sanskrit: अपहतपाप्मा ह्य् एषः ।
units.english: indeed it has destroyed evil;

units.sanskrit: तेन यद् अश्नाति यत् पिबति तेनेतरान् प्राणान् अवति । एतम् उ एवान्ततो ऽवित्त्वोत्क्रामति ।
units.english: hence it is that whatever one eats or drinks, through this, one nourishes the other Breaths In the end, not obtaining this, the rest go out;

units.sanskrit: व्याददात्य् एवान्तत इति ॥
units.english: that is why one opens the mouth at the end

units.sanskrit: यस्मान्न विद्धो ऽसुरैर्मुख्यस्तस्मान्नैवैतेन सुरभि दुर्गन्धि वा विजानाति घ्राणेनैव तदुभयं विजानाति लोकः ।
units.english: Inasmuch as the Breath in the Mouth was not pierced by the Asuras,by this one cognises not what is goodsmelling, nor what is foulsmelling; that is, people do not apprehend either of these two

units.sanskrit: अतश्च पाप्मकार्यादर्शनादपहतपाप्मापहतो विनाशितो ऽपनीतः पाप्मा यस्मात्सो ऽयमपहतपाप्मा ह्येष विशुद्ध इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Thus, inasmuch as the effect of evil is not perceived, it follows that it has destroyed evil; ie it has removed, discarded, evil, and hence it is pure;

units.sanskrit: यस्माच्चा'त्मम्भरयः कल्याणाद्यासङ्गवत्त्वाद्घ्राणादयो न तथा'त्मम्भरिर्मुख्यः किं तर्हि सर्वार्थः ।
units.english: specially because the olfactory and other Breaths support only themselves, being attached to what is good and agreeable; while the Breath in the Mouth is not so, it does not support itself alone, it supports all

units.sanskrit: कथमिति, उच्यतेतेन मुख्येन यदश्नाति यत्पिबति लोकस्तेनाशितेन पीतेन चोतरान्घ्राणादीनवति पालयति ।
units.english: How? AnswerWhatever one eats or drinks, through thisthrough the Breath in the Mouthby what is eaten and drunk, one nourishes,supportsthe other Breaths, Olfactory and the rest;

units.sanskrit: तेन हि तेषां स्थितिर्भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, it is with this help that they continue to exist;

units.sanskrit: अतः सर्वम्भरः प्राणो ऽतो विशुद्धः ।
units.english: hence the Breath in the Mouth is the nourisher of all,hence pure

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनर्मुख्याशितपीताभ्यां स्थितिरेषां गम्यत इति, उच्यतेएतं (तमु एव)
units.english: Question How do you know that the continued existence of the Olfactory and other Breaths is due to the food and drink eaten and drunk through the Breath in the Mouth?

units.sanskrit: मुख्यं प्राणं मुख्यप्राणस्य वृत्तिमन्नपाने इत्यर्थः । अन्ततो ऽन्ते मरणकाले ऽवित्त्वालब्ध्वोत्क्रामति । घ्राणादिप्राणसमुदाय इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: AnswerNot obtaining thisnot securing the help of the Breath in the Mouth,ie, the feeding and drinking functions of the Breath in the Mouth,in the endat the time of death,the rest,ie, the whole lot consisting of the Olfactory and other Breaths,go out

units.sanskrit: अप्राणो हि न शक्नोत्यशितुं पातुं वा ।
units.english: When one is deprived of Breath, one cannot eat and drink;

units.sanskrit: तेन तदोत्क्रान्तिः प्रसिद्धा घ्राणादिकलापस्य ।
units.english: and hence it is wellknown that there follows the departure of the whole lot consisting of the Olfactory and other Breaths

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते ह्युत्क्रान्तौ प्राणस्याशिशिषा ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, it is seen that the Lifebreath actually hankers after food and drink when on the point of departure;

units.sanskrit: अतो व्याददात्येवा'स्यविदारणं करोतीत्यर्थः । तद्ध्यन्नालाभ उत्क्रान्तस्य लिङ्गम् ॥
units.english: that is why one opens the mouth,ie there is opening of the mouth; and this absence of food as shown by the hankering after food is indicative of the departed Breath

units.sanskrit: तं हाङ्गिरा उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रे ।
units.english: Aṅgiras meditated upon this as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: एतम् उ एवाङ्गिरसं मन्यन्ते ऽङ्गानां यद् रसः ॥
units.english: thus they regard it as Aṅgirasa, as this is the essence rasa of the limbs aṅgānām

units.sanskrit: तं हाङ्गिरास्तं मुख्यं प्राणं हाङ्गिरा इत्येवङ्गुणमुद्गीथमुयासाञ्चक्रे बक इत्येव सम्बन्धं कृतवन्तः केचित् । एतमु एवाऽङ्गिरसं बृहस्पतिमयास्यं प्राणं मन्यन्त इति चनात् ।
units.english: On the strength of the text‘They regard this Aṅgirasa as the Bṛhaspati and the Āyāsya Breath’,some people have interpreted this passage as followsBakaDālbhyaspoken of later onmeditated upon the Breath in the Mouth which is ‘Aṅgiras’ as the Udgītha; and similarly the same BakaDalbhya meditated upon the Breath which is Bṛhaspati, and which is Āyāsya as described in texts and below

units.sanskrit: भवत्येवं यथाश्रुतासम्भवे,
units.english: This would be all right if the natural direct meaning of the sentence were not compatible;

units.sanskrit: सम्भवति तु यथाश्रुतमृषिचोदनायामपि श्रुत्यन्तरवत् ।
units.english: as a matter of fact, however, the natural meaning is quite compatible, even when the terms ‘Āṅgiras’ and ‘Bṛhaspati’ are taken as names of sages represented as Breath;

units.sanskrit: तस्माच्छतर्चिन इत्याचक्षत एतमेव सन्तमृषिमपि ।
units.english: as we find in another Vedic text, viza ‘Hence they called it Śatarcinaḥ’ where the name of the sage is mentioned as standing for the Breath;

units.sanskrit: तथा माध्यमा गृत्समदो विश्वामित्रो वामदेवो ऽत्रिरित्यादि ऋषीनेव प्राणमापादयति श्रुतिः ।
units.english: b similarly in the Ṛgveda the Veda speaks of Gṛtsamada, Viśvāmitra, Vāmadeva, Atri and other revered sages to whom the middlemost hymns were revealed, as representing Breath

units.sanskrit: तथैतानप्यृषीन्प्राणोपासकानङ्गिरोबृहस्पत्ययास्यान्प्राणं करोत्यभेदविज्ञानाय ।
units.english: In the same manner the present texts 0, and speak of the sages Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati, Āyāsyawho are really meditators upon Breathas Breath itself, in order to indicate the fact of their being nondifferent from it;

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ह पिता प्राणो माताइत्यादिवच्च ।
units.english: just as such nondifference is shown in such passages asBreath is Father, ‘Breath is Mother’

units.sanskrit: तस्मादृषिरङ्गिरा नाम प्राण एव सन्नात्मानमङ्गिरसं प्राणमुद्गीथमुपासाञ्चक्र इत्येतत् । यद्यस्मात्सो ऽङ्गानां प्राणः सन्रसस्तेनासावाङ्गिरसः ॥
units.english: Hence the meaning of the text should be taken to be as followsThe sage named Aṅgīras, being Breath itself, meditated upon himself,the sage Aṅgīras, the Breath, as Udgītha; asbecauseit,Breathis the essence of the limbs aṅgas, hence this Breath is ‘Aṅgirasa’

units.sanskrit: तेन तं ह बृहस्पतिर् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रे ।
units.english: Bṛhaspati meditated upon this as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: एतम् उ एव बृहस्पतिं मन्यन्ते । वाग् घि बृहती तस्या एषपतिः ॥
units.english: thus they regard it as Bṛhaspati; as Speech is Bṛhatī, and this is the Lord thereof

units.sanskrit: तेन तं हायास्य उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रे । एतम् उ एवायास्यं मन्यन्ते ।
units.english: Āyāsya meditated upon this as Udgītha; thus they regard it as Āyāsya;

units.sanskrit: आस्याद् यद् अयते ॥
units.english: as it proceeds from the Āsya Mouth

units.sanskrit: तथा वाचो बृहत्याः पतिस्तेनासौ बृहस्पतिः ।
units.english: Speech,therefore the sage is Bṛhaspati, Similarly because Breath proceeds from,comes out ofthe mouth, ‘āsya’;

units.sanskrit: यथा यद्यस्मादास्यादयते निर्गच्छति तेना'यास्य ऋषिः प्राण एव सन्नित्यर्थः तथान्यो ऽप्युपासक आत्मानमेवाऽङ्गिरसादिगुणं प्राणमुद्गीथमुपासीतेत्यर्थः
units.english: Both these sages, being Breath itselfmeditated etc, etc, etc In the same manner other Worshippers also should meditate upon themselves as Udgītha endowed with the properties connoted by the names ‘Āṅgīrasa’ ‘Bṛhaspati’ and ‘Āyāsya’

units.sanskrit: तेन तं ह बको दाल्भ्यो विदां चकार ।
units.english: BakaDalbhya knew this;

units.sanskrit: स ह नैमिशीयानाम् उद्गाता बभूव ।
units.english: he acted as the Udgātṛ priest for the Naimiṣīyas;

units.sanskrit: स ह स्मैभ्यः कामान् आगायति ॥
units.english: he sang out their desires for them

units.sanskrit: न केवलमङ्गिरःप्रभृतयः उपासाञ्चक्रिरे ।
units.english: It was not only Aṅgīras Bṛhaspati and Āyāsya who thus meditated

units.sanskrit: तं ह बको नाम दल्भ्यस्यापत्यं दाल्भ्यो विदाञ्चकार यथादर्शितं प्राणं विज्ञातवान् ।
units.english: The sage by name Baka, who was ‘Dālbhya’ie„ the son of Dalbhyaknew this; ie, he understood the Breath as described above

units.sanskrit: विदित्वा च स ह नैमिशीयानां सत्त्रिणामुद्गाता बभूव ।
units.english: Equipped with this knowledge, he acted as the Udgātṛ Priest for the Naimiṣīyas, who were performing a Sattra

units.sanskrit: स च प्राणविज्ञानसामर्थ्यादेभ्यो नैमिशीयेभ्यः कामानागायति स्म हा'गीतवान्किलेत्यर्थः ॥ आगाता ह वै कामानां भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ।
units.english: By virtue of his knowledge of the Science of Breath, he sang outto the Naimiṣīyas,their desires; that is, it is said that he helped them in the fulfillment of their desires He becomes a singer out of desires who, knowing this thus, meditates upon the syllable, Udgītha;This is in relation to the Self

units.sanskrit: तथान्यो ऽप्युद्गाता'गाता ह वै कामानां भवति एवं विद्वान्यथोक्तगुणं प्राणमक्षरमुद्गीथमुपास्ते तस्यैतद्दृष्टं फलमुक्तम्
units.english: As Baka, so any other Udgātṛ Priest becomes a ‘singer out of desires’, if he, knowing the Breath as described above, meditates upon it as the syllable ‘Udgītha’; to Kim accrues this visible secular reward;

units.sanskrit: प्राणात्मभावस्त्वदृष्टम्देवो भूत्वा देवानप्येतिइति श्रुत्यन्तरात्सिद्धमेवेत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: the invisible spiritual reward consisting in the identification of one’s Self with the Lifebreath; the sense is that this is already known from such texts as ‘becoming a Divine Being, one reaches the Divine Beings’

units.sanskrit: इत्यध्यात्ममेतदात्मविषयमुद्गीथोपासनमित्युक्तोपसंहारो ऽधिदैवतोद्गीथोपासने वक्ष्यमाणे बुद्धिसमाधानार्थः ॥ इति छान्दोग्योपनिषच्छाङ्करभाष्ये प्रथमाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: ie what has been just described is the meditation upon the Udgītha in relation to one’s self the Breath within one’s own body This summing up is meant to attract the attention to that meditation upon Udgītha relating to the Deities which is going to be described below End of the Section Khaṇḍa ii of Discourse Adhyāya

units.sanskrit: अथाधिदैवतम् । य एवासौ तपति तम् उद्गीथम् उपासीत ।
units.english: Now, in relation to the Deities One should meditate upon Him who Shines, as the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: उद्यन् वा एष प्रजाभ्य उद्गायति ।
units.english: verily, on rising, He sings out for the living beings;

units.sanskrit: उद्यंस् तमो भयम् अपहन्ति ।
units.english: on rising, He dispels darkness and danger

units.sanskrit: अपहन्ता ह वै भयस्य तमसो भवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: He who knows this becomes the dispeller of danger and darkness

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरमधिदैवतं देवताविषयमुद्गीथोपासनं प्रस्तुतमुत्यर्थो ऽनेकधोपास्यत्वादुद्गीथस्य ।
units.english: Now, after this, follows the meditation of the Udgītha as relating to Deities; since the Udgītha is capable of being meditated upon in several ways

units.sanskrit: य एवासावादित्यस्तपति समुद्गीथमुपासीता'दित्यदृष्ट्योद्गीथमुपासीतेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: He who shinesas the Sun,upon Him one should meditate as Udgītha; that is; one should meditate upon Udgītha as represented by the Sun

units.sanskrit: तमुद्गीथमित्युद्गीथशब्दो ऽक्षरवाची सन्कथमादित्ये वर्तत इति?उच्यते । उद्यन्नुद्गच्छन्वा एष प्रजाभ्यः प्रजार्थमुद्गायति प्रजानामन्नोत्पत्त्यर्थम् ।
units.english: ObjectionIn the text we have the phrase ‘tam udgītham; here the term ‘Udgītha stands for a syllable; how then can it be applied to the Sun?Answer On rising,when the sun rises,He sings out for the living beings,ie for the benefit of the living beings;

units.sanskrit: न ह्यनुद्यति तस्मिन्व्रीह्यादेः पक्तिः स्यादत उद्गायतीवोद्गायति,
units.english: As a matter of fact, if the Sun does not rise, the Vrīhi and other corns do not ripen;

units.sanskrit: यथैवोद्गातान्नार्थमत उद्गीथः सवितेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: it is in this sense that the Sun is figuratively spoken of as ‘singing out’;just as the Udgātṛ Priest sings for the acquiring of food;

units.sanskrit: किञ्चोद्यन्नैशं तमस्तज्जं च भयं प्रणिनामपहन्ति तमेवङ्गुणं सवितारं यो वेद सो ऽपहन्ता नाशयिता ह वै भयस्य जन्ममरणादिलक्षणस्या'त्मनस्तमसश्च तत्कारणस्याज्ञानलक्षणस्य भवति ॥
units.english: One who knows the Sun as endowed with these qualities becomes the dispeller destroyerof dangerie danger to the Self, of being born and dying;as also of Darkness,in the shape of ignorance,which is the source of that danger Though the Lifebreath and the Sun appear to be different, on account of the difference in their location,yet there is no difference in their essence

units.sanskrit: समान उ एवायं चासौ च ।
units.english: This and that are equal;

units.sanskrit: उष्णो ऽयम् उष्णो ऽसौ ।
units.english: This is warm and that is warm;

units.sanskrit: स्वर इतीमम् आचक्षते स्वर इति प्रत्यास्वर इत्य् अमुम् ।
units.english: this they call svara, and that they call svara and pratyāsvara;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् वा एतम् इमम् अमुं च उद्गीथम् उपासीत ॥
units.english: therefore one should meditate upon this and that as Udgītha This and that are equal;

units.sanskrit: कथम्समान उ एव तुल्य एव प्राणः सवित्रा गुणतः सविता च प्राणेन ।
units.english: ie, in quality, the Lifebreath is equal to the Sun and the Sun is equal to the Lifebreath;

units.sanskrit: किञ्च स्वर इतीमं प्राणमाचक्षते कथयन्ति तथा स्वर इति; प्रत्यास्वर इति चामुं सवितारम् ।
units.english: because This,the Lifebreathis Warm, and Thatthe Sunalso is warm;further, thisthe Lifebreaththey call ‘Svara’ and thatthe Sunthey call ‘Svara’ and ‘Pratyāsvara’

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्प्राणः स्वरत्येव न पुनर्मृतः प्रत्यागच्छति । सविता त्वस्तमित्वा पुनरप्यहन्यहनि प्रत्यागच्छति ।
units.english: This is so, because the Lifebreath only goes out ‘Svarati’, dies, and does not come back ‘pratyāsvarati’ after death,while the Sun, after having gone,set,again comes back day after day;

units.sanskrit: अतः प्रत्यास्वरो ऽस्माद्गुणतो नामतश्च समानावितरेतरं प्राणादित्यौ । अतः सतत्त्वाभेदादेतं प्राणमिमममुं चा'दित्यमुद्गीथमुपासीत ॥
units.english: hence the latter is called ‘pratyāsvara’ Thus through their quality and name, the Lifebreath and the Sun are equal to one another; and there being thus no essential difference between the two, one should meditate, upon Thisthe Lifebreath,and That the Sun as Udgītha

units.sanskrit: अथ खलु व्यानम् एवोद्गीथम् उपासीत ।
units.english: Now, verily, one should meditate upon Vyāna as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: यद् वै प्राणिति स प्राणः ।
units.english: when one breathes out, it is Prāṇa;

units.sanskrit: यद् अपानिति सो ऽपानः ।
units.english: when one breathes in, it is Apāna;

units.sanskrit: अथ यः प्राणापानयोः संधिः स व्यानः ।
units.english: and that which is the junction of Prāṇa and Apāna is Vyāna;

units.sanskrit: यो व्यानः सा वाक् ।
units.english: that which is Vyāna is Speech;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् अप्राणन्न् अनपानन् वाचम् अभिव्याहरति ॥
units.english: hence it is that one utters speech while he is neither breathing out nor breathing in

units.sanskrit: अथ खल्विति प्रकारान्तरेणोपासनमुद्गीथस्योच्यतेव्यानमेव वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणं प्राणस्यैव वृत्तिविशेषमुद्गीथमुपासीत ।
units.english: ‘Now verily etc’The text describes another method of meditating upon the Udgītha One should meditate as Udgītha upon Vyāna,ie upon that particular functioning of Breath, which is going to be described

units.sanskrit: अधुना तत्सतत्त्वं निरूप्यतेयद्वै पुरुषः प्राणिति मुखनासिकाभ्यां वायुं बहिर्निःसारयति स प्राणाख्यो वायोर्वृत्तिविशेषो यदपानित्यपश्वसिति ताभ्यामेवान्तराकर्षति वायुं सो ऽपानो ऽपानाख्या वृत्तिः ।
units.english: First of all the text proceeds to describe things that are similar to Vyāna When the man breathes out,that is, exhales Air through the mouth and the nose,then, this functioning of the Air is what is called ‘Prāṇa’ OutbreathingWhen one breathes in,that is, inhales Air through those same two mouth and nose, this is the functioning called ‘Apāna’ Inbreathing

units.sanskrit: ततः किमिति, उच्यतेअथ य उक्तलक्षणयोः प्राणापानयोः सन्धिस्तयोरन्तरा वृत्तिविशेषः स व्यानः,
units.english: What if all this is so?AnswerThat which is the junction of Prāṇa and Apāna,that is, that function of the Air which is in between the said two functions of Breathing out and Breathing inis Vyāna

units.sanskrit: यः साङ्ख्यादिशास्रप्रसिद्धिः श्रुत्या विशेषनिरूपणान्नासौ व्यान इत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: The sense is that the term ‘Vyāna does not stand here for what is known by that name under the Sāṅkhya and other systems; because in the present text, the Śruti has described it as something totally different

units.sanskrit: कस्मात्पुनः प्राणापानौ हित्वा महता'यासेन व्यानस्यैवोपासनमुच्यते ।
units.english: Question,How is it that the text omits the Prāṇa and the Apāna, and puts forth great effort to speak of the meditation of Vyāna?

units.sanskrit: वीर्यवत्कर्महेतुत्वमित्याहयो व्यानः सा वाक् । व्यानकार्यत्वाद्वाचः ।
units.english: In what way does it lead to vigorous action?That which is Vyāna is Speech, because Speech is the effect of Vyāna;

units.sanskrit: यस्माद्व्याननिर्वर्त्या वाक्तस्मादप्राणन्ननपानन्प्राणापानव्यापारावकुर्वन्वाचमभिव्याहरत्युच्चारयति लोकः ॥
units.english: inasmuch as Speech is brought about by Vyāna,;it is while the man is neither exhaling nor inhaling breath,that is, while not performing the functions of Prāṇa and Apāna,that he uttersgives outSpeech

units.sanskrit: या वाक् सर्क् ।
units.english: That which is Speech is Ṛk;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् अप्राणन्न् अनपानन्न् ऋचम् अभिव्याहरति ।
units.english: hence it is that one recites the Ṛk while he is neither breathing out nor breathing in

units.sanskrit: यर्क् तत् साम ।
units.english: That which is Ṛk is Sāman;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् अप्राणन्न् अनपानन् साम गायति ।
units.english: hence it is that one chants the Sāman while he is neither breathing out nor breathing in

units.sanskrit: यत् साम स उद्गीथः ।
units.english: That which is Sāman is Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् अप्रानन्न् अनपानन्न् उद्गायति ॥
units.english: hence it is that one sings out while he is neither breathing out nor breathing in

units.sanskrit: तथा वाग्विशेषामृचमृक्संस्थं च साम सामावयवं चोद्गीथमप्राणन्ननपानन्व्यानेनैव निर्वर्तयतीत्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: The sense of this is that one accomplishes the Ṛk, which is a form of Speech,the Sāman which rests on the Ṛk,and the Udgītha, which is a constituent part of the Sāman,while one is neither breathing out nor breathing in,that is, through Vyāna

units.sanskrit: अतो यान्य् अन्यानि वीर्यवन्ति कर्माणि यथाग्नेर् मन्थनम् आजेः सरणं दृढस्य धनुष आयमनम् अप्राणन्न् अनपानंस् तानि करोति ।
units.english: In addition to these, even other vigorous acts,such as churning out of the fire, moving along the boundary, bending of the strong bow,are done while one is neither breathing out nor breathing in

units.sanskrit: एतस्य हेतोर् व्यानम् एवोद्गीथम् उपासीत ॥
units.english: For this reason one should meditate upon Vyāna as the Udgītha

units.sanskrit: न केवलं वागाद्यभिव्याहरणमेवातो ऽस्मादन्यान्यपि यानि वीर्यवन्ति कर्माणि प्रयत्नाधिक्यनिर्वर्त्यानि यथाग्नेर्मन्थनमाजेर्मर्यादायाः सरणं धावनं दृढस्य धनुष आयमनमाकर्षणमप्राणन्ननपानंस्तानि करोति । अतोविशिष्टो व्यानः प्राणादिवृत्तिभ्यः ।
units.english: It is not only the uttering of speech and the rest mentioned in the preceding text, but also acts other than those, which are vigorous,ie requiring special effort to accomplish,such as churning out of fire, moving alongie, running along,the boundary,the bending,ie drawingof the strong bow,all these one does while he is neither breathing out nor breathing in;for these reasons the Vyāna is superior to the Prāṇa and other functions of the Breath;

units.sanskrit: विशिष्टस्योपासनं ज्यायः फलवत्त्वाद्राजोपासनवत् ।
units.english: and the meditation and worship of the superior Being is better, on account of its being more fruitful;

units.sanskrit: एतस्य हेतोरेतस्मात्कारणाद्व्यानमेवोद्गीथमुपासीत नान्यद्वृत्त्यन्तरम् ।
units.english: For this reason,by reason of this factone should meditate upon Vyāna itself as Udgītha, and not upon the other functions of Breath;

units.sanskrit: कर्मवीर्यवत्तरत्वं फलम् ॥
units.english: and the reward of this would consist in the better and more vigorous accomplishment of the act of meditation

units.sanskrit: अथ खलूद्गीथाक्षराण्य् उपासीत उद्गीथ इति । प्राण एवोत् । प्राणेन ह्य् उत्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: Now, one should verily meditate upon the syllables of the Udgītha as Udgītha Prāṇa itself is ut, as it is through Prāṇa that one rises uttiṣṭhatī;Speech is gī;

units.sanskrit: वग् गीः । वाचो ह गिर इत्य् आचक्षते । अन्नं थम् ।
units.english: as Speeches they call giraḥ;food is tha, as it is upon food that all this subsists

units.sanskrit: अथाधुना खलूद्गीथाक्षराण्युपासीत भक्त्यक्षराणि मा भूवन्नित्यतो विशिनष्टिउद्गीथ इति ।
units.english: Now, then, one should verily meditate upon the syllables, of the Udgītha; in order to preclude the notion that what are meant to be meditated upon are the deities figuratively indicated by the constituents of the syllable ‘Om’, the text has added the qualifying phrase ‘Udgītha iti’, as Udgītha; that is, one should meditate upon the syllables of the name Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथनामाक्षराणीत्यर्थो नामाक्षरोपासने ऽपि नामवत एवोपासनं कृतं भवेदमुकमिश्रा इति यद्वत् ।
units.english: the sense being that the meditation of the constituent syllables of the name implies the meditation of the bearer of the name also; just as when one thinks of the name ‘so and so Mishra’

units.sanskrit: प्राण एवोत्, उदित्यस्मिन्नक्षरे प्राणदृष्टिः ।
units.english: Praṇa itself is ut’ as contained in the term ‘Udgītha’;

units.sanskrit: कथं प्राणस्योत्त्वमित्याहप्राणेन ह्युत्तिष्ठति सर्वो ऽप्राणस्यावसाददर्शनादतो ऽस्त्युदः प्राणस्य च सामान्यम् ।
units.english: The text next explains why Prāṇa is ut As it is through Prāṇa that all things rise as is clear from the fact that when one is devoid of Prāṇa the Lifebreath, one falls down; thus there is a similarity between Prāṇa and ‘ut’
‘Speech is gī’;

units.sanskrit: वाचो ह गिर इत्याचक्षते शिष्टाः ।
units.english: because cultured people speak of Speech as ‘gīraḥ’

units.sanskrit: तथान्नं थमन्ने हीदं सर्वं स्थितमतो ऽस्त्यन्नस्य थाक्षरस्य च सामान्यम् ॥
units.english: Similarly, ‘Food is tha’; as all this subsists upon food; this being the similarity between ‘Tha’ and food,

units.sanskrit: द्यौर् एवोत् ।
units.english: Heaven is ut;

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षं गीः ।
units.english: the Sky is gī;

units.sanskrit: पृथिवी थम् । आदित्य एवोत् ।
units.english: the Earth is tha;the Sun is ut;

units.sanskrit: वायुर् गीः ।
units.english: Air is gī;

units.sanskrit: अग्निस् थम् । सामवेद एवोत् ।
units.english: Fire is tha;Sāmaveda is ut;

units.sanskrit: यजुर्वेदो गीः ।
units.english: Yajurveda is gī;

units.sanskrit: ऋग्वेदस् थम् । दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः ।
units.english: Ṛgveda is tha;for here Speech itself milks the milk of speech;

units.sanskrit: य एतान्य् एवं विद्वान् उद्गीथाक्षराण्य् उपास्त उद्गीथ इति ॥
units.english: and he who, knowing this, meditates upon the syllables of the Udgītha as Udgītha becomes rich in food and eater of food

units.sanskrit: त्रयाणां श्रुत्युक्तानि सामान्यानि तानि तेनानुरूपेण शेषेष्वपि द्रष्टव्यानि ।
units.english: The similarities of the three things of Prāṇa with ‘ut’, of Speech with ‘gī’ and of Food with ‘tha’ have been described in the preceding Vedic text; on the same analogy, similarities are now attributed to other sets of things also,a Heaven is ‘ut’

units.sanskrit: द्यौरेवोदुच्चैः स्थानात् । अन्तरिक्षं गार्गिरणाल्लोकानाम् । पृथिवी थं प्राणिस्थानात् ।
units.english: because of its high position uccaiḥ sthāna;the Sky is ‘gī’,because it swallows gīraṇāt the regions;the Earth is ‘tha’,because living beings stand upon it sthānāt

units.sanskrit: आदित्य एवोदूर्ध्वत्वात् । वायुर्गीरग्न्यादीनां गिरणात् । अग्निस्थं यज्ञीयकर्मावस्थानात् ।
units.english: b The Sun is ‘ut’,because of its being high above;‘Air is ‘gī’,because it swallows Fire and other things;Fire is ‘tha’,because sacrificial acts rest upon it

units.sanskrit: सामवेद एवोत्स्वर्गसंस्तुतत्वात् ।
units.english: c The Sāmaveda is ‘ut’ because it has been eulogised as Heaven;

units.sanskrit: यजुर्वेदो गीर्यजुषा प्रत्तस्य हविषो देवतानां गिरणात् ।
units.english: Yajurveda is ‘gī’,because the deities swallow the offerings made with the YajuṣMantras;

units.sanskrit: ऋग्वेदस्थमृच्यध्यूढत्वात्साम्नः ।
units.english: Ṛgveda is ‘tha’ because the Sāman rests upon the Ṛkverses

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथाक्षरोपासनफलमधुनोच्यतेदुग्धे दोग्ध्यस्मै साधकास्य । का सा वाक्, कं दोहम् । को ऽसौ दोह इत्याहयो वाचो दोहः ।
units.english: The text next describes the reward following from the meditation of the syllables of the Udgītha For him,the acting agent,milks, Yields What is it that yields?Speech What does it yield?milk;What is that milk?The milk of speech;

units.sanskrit: ऋग्वेदादिशब्दसाध्यं फलमित्यभिप्रायस्तद्वाचो दोहस्तं स्वयमेव वाग्दोग्ध्यात्मानमेव दोग्धि ।
units.english: that is to say, the reward following from the Ṛgveda etc; this reward is the ‘milk of speech’; this milk, Speech itself milks; that is Speech milks itself

units.sanskrit: किञ्चान्नवान्प्रभूतान्नो ऽन्नादश्च दीप्ताग्निर्भवति ।
units.english: Further, he becomes rich in food,ie possessed of large quantities of food, and also an eater of food,ie he comes to have a keen appetite

units.sanskrit: य एतानि यथोक्तान्येवं यथोक्तगुणान्युद्गीथाक्षराणि विद्वान्सन्नुपास्त उद्गीथ इति ॥
units.english: One who, knowing this,meditates upon the syllables composing the term ‘Udgītha’ thusie as described above, possessing the qualities mentioned gets this reward

units.sanskrit: अथ खल्व् आशीः समृद्धिः । उपसरणानीत्य् उपासीत । येन साम्ना स्तोष्यन् स्यात् तत् सामोपधावेत् ॥
units.english: Now, the fulfilment of blessings One should meditate upon the contemplated things thus One should reflect upon that Sāman with which he may be going to pray

units.sanskrit: अथ खल्विदानीमाशीःसमृद्धिराशिषः कामस्य समृद्धिर्यथा भवेत्तदुच्यत इति वाक्यशेषः ।
units.english: Now, the fulfilment of blessings the full statement is that ‘the text is now going to describe the method by which the fulfilmentaccomplishmentof blessingsof desireswould be secured

units.sanskrit: उपसरणान्युपसर्तव्यान्युपगन्तव्यानि ध्येयानीत्यर्थः । कथम्, इत्युपासीत, एवमुपासीत । तद्यथायेन साम्ना येन सामविशेषेण स्तोष्यन्स्तुतिं करिष्यन्स्याद्भवेदुद्गाता तत्सामोपधावेदुपसरेच्चिन्तयेदुत्पत्त्यादिभिः ॥
units.english: The term ‘contemplated things’ stands for things sought after, things gone after, ie things that one thinks of,How is this described?One should meditate upon the things thus,ie in the following mannerThat Sāman,the particular Sāmanwith which one may be going topraythe Udgātṛ Priest maybe going to chant eulogistic hymns,on that, one should reflect;ie one should follow it up, cogitate over it, by means of arguments and reasonings

units.sanskrit: यस्याम् ऋचि ताम् ऋचं, यद् आर्षेयं तम् ऋषिं,
units.english: That Ṛk upon which the Sāman is based,on that Ṛk one should reflect; that sage with which the Sāman is connected,on that sage one should reflect;

units.sanskrit: यां देवताम् अभिष्टोष्यन् स्यात् तां देवताम् उपधावेत् ॥
units.english: that Divinity which one is going to pray to,on that Divinity one should reflect

units.sanskrit: यस्यामृचि तत्साम तां चर्चमुपधावेद्देवतादिभिः ।
units.english: That Reverse upon which the said Sāman is based,on that Ṛkverse, one should re‘lect,along with its Deity and other details

units.sanskrit: यां देवतामभिष्टोष्यन्स्यात्तां देवतामुपधावेत् ॥
units.english: That Divinity to which one is going to pray,on that Divinity one should reflect

units.sanskrit: येन च्छन्दसा स्तोष्यन् स्यात् तच् छन्द उपधावेत् । येन स्तोमेन स्तोष्यमाणः स्यात् तं स्तोमम् उपधावेत् ॥
units.english: The metre in which one is going to pray,upon that metre one should reflect;the Stoma with which one may be going to pray,upon that Stoma one should reflect

units.sanskrit: येन च्छन्दसा गायत्र्यादिना स्तोष्यन्स्यात्तच्छन्द उपधावेत् ।
units.english: The metreGāyatrī and the rest,with which one is going to pray

units.sanskrit: येन स्तोमेन स्तोष्यमाणः स्यात् ।
units.english: that metre one should reflect upon;the Stoma with which one may be going to pray,that Stoma one should reflect upon

units.sanskrit: स्तोमाङ्गफलस्य कर्तृगामित्वादात्मनेपदं स्तोष्यमाण इति ।
units.english: The Ātmanepada ending has been used in the word ‘stoṣyamāṇaḥ’ instead of the Parasmaipada ending elsewhere, in the word ‘stoṣyan’, because the result following from the use of a particular Stoma comes directly to the Agent himself

units.sanskrit: तं स्तोममुपधावेत् ॥
units.english: That Stoma one should reflect upon

units.sanskrit: यां दिशम् अभिष्टोष्यन् स्यात् तां दिशम् उपधावेत् ॥
units.english: The quarter that one is going to eulogise,that quarter one should reflect upon

units.sanskrit: यां दिशमभिष्टोष्यन्स्यात्तां दिशमुपधावेदधिष्ठात्रादिभिः ॥
units.english: The quarter that one is going to eulogise,that quarter one should reflect upon,along with its Presiding Deity and other details

units.sanskrit: आत्मानम् अन्तत उपसृत्य स्तुवीत कामं ध्यायन्न् अप्रमत्तः ।
units.english: Lastly, having approached himself, he should eulogise himself, with due care, pondering over his desire

units.sanskrit: अभ्याशो ह यद् अस्मै स कामः स्मृध्येत यत्कामः स्तुवीतेति यत्कामः स्तुवीतेति ॥
units.english: Quickly will be fulfilled for him that desire seeking for which he would sing the Prayer Yea, seeking which he would sing the Prayer

units.sanskrit: आत्मानमुद्गाता स्वं रूपं गोत्रनामादिभिः सामादीन्क्रमेण स्वं चा'त्मानमन्ततो ऽन्त उपसृत्य स्तुवीत । कामं ध्यायन्नप्रमत्तः स्वरोष्मव्यञ्जनादिभ्यः प्रमादमकुर्वंस्ततो ऽभ्याशः क्षिप्रमेव ह यद्यत्रास्मा एवंविदे स कामः समृध्येत समृद्धिं गच्छेत् ।
units.english: The UdgātṛPriest should approach and eulogise his own selfalong with the table of his gotra and other details,and also the Sāman and the rest;pondering over his desire, with due care,carefully avoiding all mistakes relating to accent and pronunciation

units.sanskrit: को ऽसौ, यत्कामो यः कामो ऽस्य सो ऽयं यत्कामः सन्स्तुवीतेति ।
units.english: Quicklysoonwill be fulfilledwill prosperthe desires for him who knows thiswhich desire?seeking for which he would sing the Prayer

units.sanskrit: द्विरुक्तिकादरार्था ॥
units.english: The repetition of the phrase is meant to indicate the importance of the subject

units.sanskrit: ओम् इत्य् एतद् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपासीत । ओम् इति ह्य् उद्गायति ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the syllable Om, the Udgītha, because one always sings with Om;

units.sanskrit: तस्योपव्याख्यानम् ॥
units.english: of this, now, the expounding

units.sanskrit: ओमित्येतदित्यादिप्रकृतस्याक्षरस्य पुनरुपादानमुद्गीथाक्षराद्युपासनान्तरितत्वादन्यत्र प्रसङ्गो मा भूदित्येवमर्थम् ।
units.english: The main subjectmatter of the syllable ‘Om’ is here reintroduced with a view to preclude the possibility of the attention being diverted to other subjects, on account of the main subject having been interrupted by the declarations regarding the meditation on the components of the name ‘Udgītha’;

units.sanskrit: प्रकृतस्यैवाक्षरस्यामृताभयगुणविशिष्टस्योपासनं विधातव्यमित्यारम्भः । ओमित्यादि व्याख्यातम् ॥
units.english: the sense of this introduction is that one should perform meditation upon the same syllable ‘Om’ which is the main subject of treatment, as endowed with the qualities of immortality and fearlessness

units.sanskrit: देवा वै मृत्योर् बिभ्यतस् त्रयीं विद्यां प्राविशन् ।
units.english: The Divinities fearing Death, entered the science of the Triadic Science;

units.sanskrit: ते छन्दोभिर् अच्छादयन् ।
units.english: they covered themselves with the ‘Metres’;

units.sanskrit: यद् एभिर् अच्छादयंस् तच् छन्दसां छन्दस्त्वम् ॥
units.english: and because they covered themselves with the metres Chandas, therefore this constitutes the metricality of the metres

units.sanskrit: देवा वै मृत्योर्मारकाद्विभ्यतः किं कृतवन्त इत्युच्यते ।
units.english: It is described now what the Divinities did when they became frightened of deathie of the killer

units.sanskrit: त्रयीं विद्यां त्रयीविहितं कर्म प्राविशन्प्रविष्टवन्तो वैदिकं कर्म प्रारब्धवन्त इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: They entered the Triadic Science; that is, they had recourse to the Act prescribed in the Triadic Science; that is, they commenced the performance of Vedic Acts;

units.sanskrit: तन्मृत्योस्राणं मन्यमानाः ।
units.english: regarding it as a protection against Death

units.sanskrit: किञ्च ते कर्मण्यविनियुक्तैश्छन्दोभिर्मन्त्रैर्जपहोमादि कुर्वन्त आत्मानं कर्मान्तरेष्वच्छादयंश्छादितवन्तः ।
units.english: Further, they proceeded to perform the acts of Japa repeating of mantras, Homa Pouring of Libations and the like, with ‘Metres’,ie Mantras, which are not specifically enjoined as to be used at any particular Acts; and coveredconcealedthemselvesamong other Acts;

units.sanskrit: यद्यस्मादेभिर्मन्त्रैरच्छादयंस्तत्तस्माच्छन्दसां मन्त्राणां छादनाच्छन्दस्त्वं प्रसिद्धमेव ॥
units.english: because,asthey covered themselves with these Mantras, therefore it is well known that Mantras have the character of being ‘Chandas’ metricalprotective covers

units.sanskrit: तान् उ तत्र मृत्युर् यथा मत्स्यम् उदके परिपश्येद् एवं पर्यपश्यद् ऋचि साम्नि यजुषि ।
units.english: There Death saw them in Ṛk, Sāman and Yajuṣ,just as one sees fish in water

units.sanskrit: ते नु वित्त्वोर्ध्वा ऋचः साम्नो यजुषः स्वरम् एव प्राविशन् ॥
units.english: Then the Divinities, knowing this, rose above Ṛk, Sāman and Yajuṣ, and entered the Vowel Svara its elf,

units.sanskrit: तांस्तत्र देवान्कर्मपरान्मृत्युर्यथा लोके मत्स्यघातको मत्स्यमुदके नातिगम्भीरे परिपश्येद्बडिशोदकस्रावोपायसाध्यं मन्यमान एवं पर्यपश्यद्दृष्टवान्मृत्युः कर्मक्षयोपायेन साध्यान्देवान्मेन इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: There Death saw themthe Divinities; just as,in the ordinary world,the fisherman sees the fish in water, which is not overdeepthinking that it would be easy to secure them by such ordinary means as angling and draining out of the water in the same manner Death saw the Divinities and regarded them as easy to be got at through the exhaustion of their ‘karma’ the resultant of their Ritualistic acts

units.sanskrit: क्वासौ देवान्ददर्शेत्युच्यतेऋचि साम्नि यजुषि ।
units.english: Wherein did Death see the Divinities?AnswerIn Ṛk, Sāman and Yajuṣ;

units.sanskrit: ऋग्यजुःसामसम्बन्धिकर्मणीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, in the Ritualistic Acts connected with the three Vedas, Ṛk, Sāman and Yajus

units.sanskrit: ते नु देवा वैदिकेन कर्मणा संस्कृताः शुद्धात्मानः सन्तो मृत्योश्चिकीर्षितं विदितवन्तः ।
units.english: As regards the Divinities, they had their minds purified through the embellishments due to the Vedic Ritual, and hence they knew what Death was going to do to them;

units.sanskrit: विदित्वा च त ऊर्ध्वा व्यावृत्ताः कर्मभ्य ऋचः साम्नो यजुष ऋग्यजुःसामसम्बद्धात्कर्मणो ऽभ्युत्थायेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: and knowing this, they rose above the Ṛk, Sāman and Yajuṣ,that is they turned away from the ritualistic acts connected with the three Vedas, Ṛk, Sāman and Yajuṣ;

units.sanskrit: तेन कर्मणा मृत्युभयापगमं प्रति निराशास्तदपास्यामृताभयगुणमक्षरं स्वरं स्वरशब्दितं प्राविशन्नेव प्रविष्टवन्तः ।
units.english: that is, having no hope of getting rid of the danger of death,with the help of the said Acts, they gave up that hope and entered,took shelter in,the Vowel,ie, the syllable, endowed with the qualities of immortality and fearlessness, which is called by the name Svara vowel;

units.sanskrit: ओङ्कारोपासनपराः संवृत्ताः ।
units.english: that is, they became engaged in the meditation of the syllable ‘Om’

units.sanskrit: एवशब्दो ऽवधारणार्थः सन्समुच्चयप्रतिषेधार्थः ।
units.english: QuestionHow does the syllable come to be called by the name ‘svara’ vowel?

units.sanskrit: तदुपासनपराः संवृत्ता इत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: The Answer follows in the following text

units.sanskrit: यदा वा ऋचम् आप्नोत्य् ओम् इत्य् एवातिस्वरति एवं सामैवं यजुः ।
units.english: When one gets at the Ṛk, one loudly pronounces Om; similarly with the Sāman; similarly with the Yajuṣ

units.sanskrit: एष उ स्वरो यद् एतद् अक्षरम् एतद् अमृतम् अभयम् ।
units.english: That indeed is Svara which is this syllable, which is immortal, fearless

units.sanskrit: तत् प्रविश्य देवा अमृता अभवन् ॥
units.english: Having entered this, the Divinities became immortal and fearless

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनः स्वरशब्दवाच्यत्वमक्षरस्येत्युच्यतेयदा वा ऋचमाप्नोत्योमित्येवातिस्वरत्येवं सामैवं यजुः । एष उ स्वरः ।
units.english: When one gets at the Ṛk, one loudly pronounces ‘Om’; similarly with the Sāman; similarly with the Yajuṣ That indeed is Svara;What is it?which is this syllable, which is immortal, fearless

units.sanskrit: स य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरं प्रणौत्य् एतद् एवाक्षरं स्वरम् अमृतम् अभयं प्रविशति ।
units.english: One who, knowing this, eulogises this syllable, enters this same syllable, the immortal and fearless Svara;

units.sanskrit: तत् प्रविश्य यद् अमृता देवास् तद् अमृतो भवति ॥
units.english: having entered it he becomes immortal just as the Divinities became immortal

units.sanskrit: स यो ऽन्यो ऽपि देववदेवैतदक्षरमेवममृतमभयगुणं विद्वान्प्रणौति स्तौति । उपासनमेवात्र स्तुतिरभिप्रेता । स तथैवैतदेवाक्षरं स्वरममृतमभयं प्रविशति ।
units.english: One,a person other than the Divinities,who, like the said Divinities, knowing this syllable, as endowed with the qualities of immortality and fearlessness,eulogisespraises, ie meditates upon it, he enters, in the same manner as the Divinities, this same syllable, immortal and fearless,Having entered it etc, etc

units.sanskrit: तत्प्रविश्य च राजकुलं प्रविष्टानामिव राज्ञो ऽन्तरङ्गबहिरङ्गतावन्न विशिष्टस्तदमृतो भवति न न्यूनता नाप्यधिकतामृतत्व इत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: Among people gaining entry into the Royal Palace, there is always a distinction made on the ground of their being more or less intimate with the King; there is no such distinction of being more or less intimate among persons entering the Supreme Brahman;

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषच्छाङ्करभाष्ये प्रथमाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: this description follows after the identification of the Praṇava and the Udgītha, which in its turn, is preceded by a reiteration of what has been already said in regard to the meditation of the Udgītha as contemplated in the form of Breath and the Sun

units.sanskrit: अथ खलु य उद्गीथः स प्रणवो यः प्रणवः स उद्गीथ इति ।
units.english: Now, verily, that which is Udgītha is Prāṇava; that which is Praṇava is Udgītha
