units.english: Being thus addressed, the white Dog said to the smaller dogsHere,at this same place,meet me in the morning The long Vowel in ‘Samīyāta’ is a Vedic anomaly;

units.sanskrit: प्रमादपाठो वा ।
units.english: or it may be a wrong reading

units.sanskrit: प्रातः कालकरणं तत्काल एव कर्तव्याझ्र्व्यताटर्थम् ।
units.english: The appointment of the morning is meant to show that what he was going to do should be best done in the morning;

units.sanskrit: अन्नदस्य वा सवितुरपराह्ने ऽनाभिमुख्यात् ।
units.english: because the Sun, who is the bestower of food, is not quite before us in the afternoon

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्रैव ह बको दाल्भ्यो ग्लावो वा मैत्रेय ऋषिः प्रतिपालयाञ्चकार प्रतीक्षणं कृतवानित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: There the sage, BakaDālbhya or GlāvaMaitreya awaited,waited for their reappearance

units.sanskrit: ते ह यथैवेदं बहिष्पवमानेन स्तोष्यमाणाः संरब्धाः सर्पन्तीत्य् एवम् आससृपुः ।
units.english: Just as the men who are going to sing the Bahiṣpavamāna hymn move round linked to each Other, in the same manner did the smaller dogs move round;

units.sanskrit: ते ह समुपविश्य हिञ् चक्रुः ॥
units.english: having sat down, they uttered the syllable ‘Hiṃ’

units.sanskrit: ते श्वानस्तत्रैवा'गम्य ऋषेः समक्षं यथैवेह कर्मणि बहिष्पवमानेन स्तोत्रेण स्तोष्यमाणा । उद्गातृपुरुषाः संरब्धाः संलग्ना अन्योन्यमेव मुखेनान्योन्यस्य पुच्छं गृहीत्वा'ससृपुरासृप्तवन्तः परिभ्रमणं कृतवन्त इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Those dogs having come to the place, moved round, in the presence of the sage; just as the??en , the assistants of the UdgātṛPriest, who are going to sing the Bahiṣpavamāna Hymn linked to each other, so the dogs moved round, each holding in his mouth the tail of the other;and having thus moved round, they sat down, and being seated, they uttered the syllable ‘Hiṃ’

units.sanskrit: ओं पिबाम । ओं देवो वरुणः प्रजापतिः सविता'न्नम् इहा'हरत् ।
units.english: ‘Om ! Let us eat! Om! Let us drink! Om! May the Deva, Varuṇa, Prajāpati, Savitṛ bring us food! O, Lord of Food, bring here food;

units.sanskrit: ओमदामों पिबामों देवो द्योतनात् ।
units.english: Om, let us eat! Om, let us drink Deva, the Sun is so called because He shines;

units.sanskrit: वरुणो वर्षणाज्जगतः । प्रजापतिः पालनात्प्रजानाम् । सविता प्रसवितृत्वात्सर्वस्या'दित्य उच्यते ।
units.english: He is Varuṇa, because He brings rain to the world;He is Prajāpati, because he nourishes the people;He is Savitṛ, because he is the progenitor of all things

units.sanskrit: एतैः पर्यायैः स एवंभूत आदित्यो ऽन्नमस्मभ्यमिहा'बरदाबरत्विति ।
units.english: It is the Sun who is addressed by these synonymous terms

units.sanskrit: त एवं हिं कृत्वा पुनरप्यूचुःस त्वं हे ऽन्नपते । स हि सर्वस्यान्नस्य प्रसवितृत्वात्पतिः ।
units.english: May the Sun who is all this, bring us food Having done this, they said againO Lord of Food,He is called the ‘Lord’ of Food, because it is He who produces all food;

units.sanskrit: न हि तत्पाकेन विना प्रभूतमन्नमणुमात्रमपि जायते प्राणिनाम् ।
units.english: in the sense that without the ripening due to the Sun, not much food is produced, even to the smallest degree, for living beings;

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽन्नपतिः ।
units.english: hence he is called the ‘Lord of Food’

units.sanskrit: हे ऽन्नपते ऽन्नमस्मभ्यमिहा'हरा'हरेति । अभ्यास आदरार्थः ।
units.english: O Lord of Food! bring here food for usyea, bring it;the repetition is meant to indicate the importance of the subject Om

units.sanskrit: ओमिति ॥
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषच्छाङ्करभाष्ये प्रथमोध्यायस्य द्वादशः खण्डः
units.english: hence, the text is next going to expound those other meditations, in their connected form, which relate to the other kind of Sāmafactors which appear in the form of the Stobha syllables ;

units.sanskrit: अयं वाव लोको हाउकारः ।
units.english: This world verily is the syllable Hāū;

units.sanskrit: वायुर् हाइकारः । चन्द्रमा अथकारः ।
units.english: Air is the syllable Hāī, the Moon is the syllable Atha;

units.sanskrit: आत्मेहकारः ।
units.english: the Self is the syllable Iha;

units.sanskrit: अग्निर् ईकारः ॥
units.english: Fire is the syllable

units.sanskrit: भक्तिविषयोपासनं सामावयवसम्बद्धमित्यतः सामावयवान्तरस्तोभाक्षर
units.english: This world verily is the syllable Hāū, which is the Stobha well known as used in the singing of the Rathantara Sāma;

units.sanskrit: वावायमेव लोको हाउकारः स्तोभो रथन्तरे साम्नि प्रसिद्धःइयं वै रथन्तरम् इति । अस्मात्सम्बन्धसामान्याद्धाउकारस्तोभो ऽयं लोक इत्येवमुपासीत ।
units.english: and it has been declared in a Vedic text that ‘This world is Rathantara’; and on account of this common relationship between this world and the Rathantara Sāma, this Stobha, the syllable Hāū, should be meditated upon as this world

units.sanskrit: वायुर्हाकारः । वामदेव्ये सामनि हाइकारः प्रसिद्धः ।
units.english: Air is the syllable Hāī;the Stobha Hāī is wellknown as used in the singing of the VāmadevyaSāma;

units.sanskrit: वाय्वप्सम्बन्धश्च वामदेवस्य साम्नो योनिरित्यस्मात्सामान्याद्धाइकारं वायुदृष्ट्योपासीत ।
units.english: and the connection between Air and Water is the source of the VāmadevyaSama; and on account of this common relationship, one should meditate upon the syllable;

units.sanskrit: चन्द्रमा अथकारः । चन्द्रदृष्ट्याथकारमुपासीत ।
units.english: The Moon is the syllable Atha; hence one should meditate upon the syllable Atha as the Moon;

units.sanskrit: अन्ने हीदं स्थितम् । अन्नात्मा चन्द्रः ।
units.english: the Moon, being not self, rests Sthita upon food;

units.sanskrit: थकाराकारसामान्याच्च ।
units.english: hence, on account of the letter tha being common to the syllable Atha and Sthita,and also because of the letter a being common to the syllable tha and the term ‘anātmā’, notself

units.sanskrit: आत्मेहकारः । इहेति स्तोभः प्रत्यक्षो ह्यात्मेति व्यपदिश्यते । इहेति च स्तोभः ।
units.english: The self is the syllable Iha;ie the stobha ‘iha’; the self, is regarded as perceptible, and so is the Stobha ‘iha’;

units.sanskrit: तत्सामान्यात् ।
units.english: and it is on account of this similarity that the syllable ‘iha’ should be meditated upon as the self

units.sanskrit: अग्निरीकारः ।
units.english: Fire is the syllable ī;

units.sanskrit: ईनिधनानि चा'ग्नेयानि सर्वाणि सामानीत्यतस्तत्सामान्यात् ॥
units.english: as a matter of fact, all the SāmaChants related to Fire always end in the vowel ‘ī’;

units.sanskrit: आदित्य ऊकारः ।
units.english: Invocation is the syllable ‘e’;

units.sanskrit: विश्वे देवा औहोयिकारः ।
units.english: the Viśvedevas are the syllable Ohoyi;

units.sanskrit: प्रजपतिर् हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Prajāpati is the syllable ‘hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: प्राणः स्वरः ।
units.english: Breath is ‘Svara’;

units.sanskrit: वाग् विराट् ॥
units.english: ‘Vāk’ is Virāṭ

units.sanskrit: आदित्य ऊकारः ।
units.english: The Sun is the syllable ‘ū’;

units.sanskrit: उच्चैरूर्ध्वं सन्तमादित्यं गायन्त्यूकारश्चायं स्तोभः । आदित्यदैवत्ये साम्नि स्तोभ ऊ इत्यादित्य ऊकारः ।
units.english: they sing to the Sun when he is on high, uccaiḥ, and the stobha is ‘ū’ and in the Sāma of which the Sun is the deity, the Stobha used is ‘ū’; hence the Sun is the syllable ‘ū’

units.sanskrit: निहव इत्याह्वानमेकारः स्तोभः ।
units.english: Invocation, callingis the stobha in the forming of the syllable ‘e’;

units.sanskrit: एहीति चा'ह्वयन्तीति तत्सामान्यात् । विश्वे देवा औहोयिकारोवैश्वदेव्ये साम्नि दर्शनात् ।
units.english: because of the similarity based upon the fact that when calling another person, they use the term ‘ehi’ Come which begins with the letter ‘e’,The Viśvedevas are the syllable ‘Ohoi’; because this Stobha is found in the Sāma connected with the Viśvedevas

units.sanskrit: प्रजापतिर्हिङ्कारः । आनिरुक्त्याद्धिङ्कारस्य चाव्यक्तत्वात् ।
units.english: Prajāpati is the syllable ‘hiṃ’; because Prajāpati cannot be described, and the syllable ‘him’ also is indistinct

units.sanskrit: प्राणः स्वरः । स्वर इति स्तोभः ।
units.english: Breath is ‘svara’, ie the Stobha ‘svara’;

units.sanskrit: प्राणस्य च स्वरहेतुत्वसामान्यात् ।
units.english: because of the similarity that Breath is the cause of svara accent

units.sanskrit: अन्नं या या इति स्तोभो ऽन्नम् ।
units.english: Food is ‘yā’;the Stobha ‘yā’ is food;

units.sanskrit: अन्नेन हीदं यातीत्यतस्तत्सामान्यात् ।
units.english: because it is by means of food that one goes along yāti whereby there is similarity between the stobha ‘yā’ and food

units.sanskrit: वागिति स्तोभो विराडन्नं देवताविशेषो वा ।
units.english: ‘Virāṭ’ may be taken as standing for food or as a particular Deity;

units.sanskrit: वैराजे साम्नि स्तोभदर्शनात् ॥
units.english: and this is ‘Vāk’, because this Stobha ‘Vāk’ is found in the VairājaSāma

units.sanskrit: अनिरुक्तस् त्रयोदशः स्तोभः संचरो हुङ्कारः ॥
units.english: Undefined is the thirteenth stobha, the indefinite syllable ‘Huṃ’

units.sanskrit: अनिरुक्तो ऽव्यक्तत्वादिदं वेदं वेति निर्वक्तुं न शक्यत इत्यतः सञ्चरो विकल्प्यमानस्वरूप इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Undefined,being indistinct, it cannot be determined whether it is this or that; hence also it is indefinite,ie having its exact form assumed according to circumstances

units.sanskrit: को ऽसावित्याहत्रयोदशः स्तोभो हुङ्कारः ।
units.english: Which is this stobha?It is the thirteenth stobha, the syllable ‘him’

units.sanskrit: अव्यक्तो ह्ययमतो ऽनिरुक्तविशेष एवोपास्य इत्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: The sense is that this is indistinct, and hence its peculiar character has not been defined, and in this undefined form it is to be meditated upon

units.sanskrit: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः । अन्नवान् अन्नादो भवति ।
units.english: If one know this esoteric doctrine of the Sāmasfor him speech itself milks the milk of speech;

units.sanskrit: य एताम् एवं साम्नाम् उपनिषदं वेदोपनिषदं वेद ॥
units.english: and he who knows this esoteric doctrine of the Sāmas becomes rich in food and eater of foodyea, one who knows this

units.sanskrit: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग्दोहमित्याद्युक्तार्थम् ।
units.english: Speech itself etc etc This has been already explained under

units.sanskrit: य एतामेवं यथोक्तलक्षणां साम्नां सामावयवस्तोभाक्षरविषयामुपनिषदं दर्शनं वेद तस्यैतद्यथोक्तं फलमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: One who knows this abovedescribed secret doctrine,philosophyof the Sāmasrelating to the stobhasyllables forming part of the Sāmachant, to such a one accrues the said result?Such is the meaning of the text

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यासो ऽध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थः । सामावयवविषयोपासनाविशेषपरिमाप्त्यर्थो वेति ॥
units.english: The repetition of the phrase ‘one who knows this’ is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse,or the end of the treatment of the subject of meditation upon the constituents of Sāma

units.sanskrit: यद् असाधु तद् असामेति ॥
units.english: End of Section of Discourse End of Discourse

units.sanskrit: ओमित्येतदक्षरम् इत्यादिना सामावयवविषयमुपासनमनेकफलमुपदिष्टम् ।
units.english: By means of the discourse beginning with the words ‘One should meditate upon the syllable Om’ has been expounded the meditation of the component factors of Sāma, which leads to various results;

units.sanskrit: अनन्तरं च स्तोभाक्षरविषयमुपासनमुक्तम् ।
units.english: after tlfat towards the end of the Discourse the meditation of the Stobhasyllables has been described;

units.sanskrit: सर्वथापि सामैकदेशसम्बद्धमेव तदित्यथेदानीं समस्ते साम्नि समस्तसामविषयाण्युपासनानि वक्ष्यामीत्यारभते श्रुतिः । युक्तं ह्येकदेशोपासनानन्तरमेकदेशिविषयमुपासनमुच्यत इति ।
units.english: all this is connected only with parts of the Sāma The Srutitext now takes up the next discourse with a view to expounding the meditations of the entire Sāma, relating to the Sāma as a whole It is only right that after the exposition of the meditation of the component parts, there should follow the meditation of the composite whole

units.sanskrit: समस्तस्य सर्वावयवविशिष्टस्य पाञ्चभक्तिकस्य साप्तभक्तिकस्य चेत्यर्थः । खल्विति वाक्यालङ्कारार्थः ।
units.english: Of the whole Sāma,ie, of the Sāma as a whole composed of all its component parts, and divided into five or seven ‘divisions’ cadences, stops,verily,this is only an ornament of speech

units.sanskrit: साम्न उपासनं साधु ।
units.english: The meditation of Sāma is good;

units.sanskrit: समस्ते साम्नि साधुदृष्टिविधिपरत्वान्न पूर्वोक्तोपासननिन्दार्थत्वं साधुशब्दः शोभनवाची । कथमवगम्यत इत्याहयत्खलु लोके साधु शोभनमनवद्यं प्रसिद्धं तत्सामेत्याचक्षते कुशलाः ।
units.english: what the term ‘good’ is meant to indicate is the injunction that ‘the whole Sāma should be looked upon as something good and it is not meant to deprecate the forms of meditation expounded in the preceding discourse But the implication certainly is that the goodness or excellence which did not belong to the previous meditations, belongs to that of the whole Sāma

units.sanskrit: यदसाधु विपरीतं तदसामेति ॥
units.english: because the section ends with the words ‘who meditates

units.sanskrit: तद् उताप्य् आहुः । साम्नैनम् उपागाद् इति साधुनैनम् उपागाद् इत्य् एव तद् आहुः ।
units.english: In this connection they declare thusWhen they say ‘he approached him with Sāma’ what they mean is that he approached him in a good manner’;

units.sanskrit: असाम्नैनम् उपागाद् इत्य् एव तद् आहुः ॥
units.english: and when they say ‘he approached him with asāma,’ what they may mean is that ‘he approached him in an improper manner’

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्रैव साध्वसाधुविवेककरण उताप्याहुःसाम्नैनं राजानं सामन्तं चोपागादुपगतवान् । को ऽसौ यतो ऽसाधुत्वप्राप्त्याशङ्का? स इत्यभिप्रायः । शोभनाभिप्रायेण साधुनैनमुपागादित्येव तत्तत्रा'हुर्लौकिका बन्धनाद्यसाधुकार्यमपश्यन्तः ।
units.english: In this same connection,in regard to the discrimination between right and wrong good and badthey declare thus When they say he has approached the King or his tributary chief ‘with Sāma’,Who is he?‘He’ stands for the person from whom they feared disrespect to the King,what they mean is that ‘he approached him in a good way’, which means that he approached him nicely

units.sanskrit: यत्र पुनर्विपर्ययो बन्धनाद्यसाधुकार्यं पश्यन्ति तत्रासाम्नैनमुपागादित्यसाधुनैनमुपागादित्येव तदाहुः ॥
units.english: So say the people when they find that the man has not been arrested or imprisoned on account of any disrespect shown to the KingWhen the case is otherwise,when for instance, they find such effects of improper behaviour as arrest or imprisonment, then, they say‘He approached him with asāma’, meaning only that ‘he approached him in the wrong manner’

units.sanskrit: अथोताप्य् आहुः ।
units.english: Then again, they say ‘Verily it is Sāma for us’;

units.sanskrit: साम नो बतेति यत् साधु भवति साधु बतेत्य् एव तद् आहुः ।
units.english: when something is good they say it is good They say ‘Verily there is asāma for us’;

units.sanskrit: असाम नो बतेति यद् असाधु भवत्य् असाधु बतेत्य् एव तद् आहुः ॥
units.english: when they say something is not good, they say it is not good

units.sanskrit: अथोताप्याहुः स्वसंवेद्यं साम नो ऽस्माकं बतेत्यनुकम्पयतः संवृत्तमित्याहुः । एतत्तैरुक्तं भवति यत्साधु भवति साधु वतेत्येव तदाहुः ।
units.english: When one says in regard to his own experience ‘Verily it is Sāma for us’,when what they mean is that ‘It is good for us’, when something is really good for them

units.sanskrit: विपर्यये जाते ऽसाम नो बतेति ।
units.english: On the contrary, when something wrong, they say ‘it is asāma for us’;

units.sanskrit: यदसाधु भवत्यसाधु बतेत्येव तदाहुः तस्मात्सामसाधुशब्दयोरेकार्थत्वं सिद्धम् ॥
units.english: when‘anything has gone wrong has happend to them, they say ‘Verily it is not good with us’From all this it becomes established that the terms ‘Sāma’ and ‘Sādhu’ good are synonymous

units.sanskrit: स य एतद् एवं विद्वान् साधु सामेत्य् उपास्ते ऽभ्याशो ह यद् एनं साधवो धर्मा आ च गच्छेयुर् उप च नमेयुः ॥
units.english: If anyone knowing thus meditate upon Sāma as good, all right duties would readily come to him and accrue to him

units.sanskrit: अतः स यः कश्चित्साधु सामेति साधुगुणवत्सामेत्युपास्ते समस्तं साम साधुगुणवद्विद्वांस्तस्यैतत्फलमभ्याशो ह क्षिप्रं ह; यदिति क्रियाविशेषणार्थमेनमुपासकं साधवः शोभना धर्माः श्रुतिस्मृत्यविरुद्धा आ च गच्छेयुरागच्छेयुश्च न केवलमागच्छेयुरुप च नमेयुरुपनमेयुश्च भोग्यत्वेनोपतिष्ठेयुरित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: For the above reasons, if any one meditates upon the Sāma as ‘good’,ie as endowed with the quality of goodness, knowing the entire Sāma as possessing goodness,then to him comes the following rewardReadily quicklythe expression ‘Kṣipram hi yat’ being an adverb,to such a meditator, the right dutiesgood acts, in accordance with the Śruti and the Smṛtiwould come,approach;nor would they only come to him, they would also accrue to him; that is, they would present themselves before him as objects of his own experience and enjoyment

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: लोकेषु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत । पृथिवी हिङ्कारः । अग्निः प्रस्तावः । अन्तरिक्षम् उद्गीथः । आदित्यः प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma in reference to the Regions Earth is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, Fire is Prastāva, Sky is Udgītha, the Sun is Pratihāra, Heaven is Nidhāna,This is with reference to the ascending Regions

units.sanskrit: इत्य् ऊर्ध्वेषु ॥ कानि पुनस्तानि साधुदृष्टिविशिष्टानि समस्तानि सामान्युपास्यानीति । इमानि तान्युच्यन्ते लोकेषु पञ्चविधमित्यादीनि ।
units.english: QuestionWhich are those extra Sāmas which are recognised as endowed with goodness, and which should be meditated upon?These are now described in the TextOne should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma in reference to the Regions etc

units.sanskrit: ननु लोकादिदृष्ट्या तान्युपास्यानि साधुदृष्ट्या चेति विरुद्धम् । न ।
units.english: ObjectionIt is said that they should be meditated upon as the Regions, and it has been said before that they should be meditated upon as good So there is selfcontradictionNot so;

units.sanskrit: साध्वर्थस्य लोकादिकार्येषु कारणस्यानुगतत्वात् मृदादिवद्घटादिविकारेषु ।
units.english: what is connoted by the term ‘good’ subsists in the form of the constituent cause in all such products as the Regions; just as Clay and other causes subsist in their products, Jar and the like

units.sanskrit: साधुशब्दवाच्योर्ऽथो धर्मो ब्रह्म वा सर्वथापि लोकादिकार्येष्वनुगतम् ।
units.english: What is connoted by the term ‘good’ is Duty Right Conduct or Brahman; in either case, it is what subsists in all such products as the Regions

units.sanskrit: अतो यथा यत्र घटादिदृष्टिर्मृदादिदृष्ट्यनुगतैव सा ।
units.english: Hence it is that wherever there is notion of the Jar and such products, it is always accompanied by the notion of their cause, such as Clay and the like

units.sanskrit: तथा साधुदृष्ट्यनुगतैव लोकादिदृष्टिः । धर्मादिकार्यत्वाल्लोकादीनाम् ।
units.english: Similarly the idea of the Regions and other products is always accompanied by the idea of the ‘Good’ which is their cause and the reason for this lies in the fact that the Regions are the products of Duty Right Conduct;

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि कारणत्वमविशिष्टं ब्रह्मधर्मयोः,
units.english: or Brahman Even though the character of being the Cause belongs equally to both Duty and Brahman and to that extent what is said may be applicable to both, yet in the present context it would be right to take the word ‘good’ as connoting Duty Right Conduct;

units.sanskrit: तथापि धर्म एव साधुशब्दवाच्य इति युक्तंसाधुकारी साधुर्भवतीति धर्मविषये साधुशब्दप्रयोगात् ।
units.english: because in such statements as ‘Sādhukārī sādhurbhavati’, ‘one who performs his duty is good’, we find the term ‘Sādhu’ ‘good’ applied to Duty

units.sanskrit: ननु लोकादिकार्येषु कारणस्यानुगतत्वादर्थप्राप्तैव तद्दृष्टिरिति साधु सामेत्युपास्त इति न वक्तव्यम् । न ।
units.english: ObjectionAs the cause always subsists in the Regions and other products, that the one should be viewed as the other is naturally implied, and hence there could be no need for the teaching that ‘the Sāma should be meditated upon as good’Not so;

units.sanskrit: शास्रगम्यत्वात्तद्दृष्टेः ।
units.english: the said view or idea is one that could be got at only from the Scriptures

units.sanskrit: सर्वत्र हि शास्रप्रापिता एव धर्मा उपास्या न विद्यमाना अप्यशास्रीयाः ।
units.english: In all cases, only such Duties are to be observed as have been enjoined in the Scriptures, and not those which may be perceptible, and yet not learnt from the Scriptures

units.sanskrit: लोकेषु पृथिव्यादिषु पञ्चविधं पञ्चभक्तिभेदेन पञ्चप्रकारं साधुसमस्तं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma,ie the entire Sāma, ie its five forms, determined according to the five divisions,as ‘good’with reference to the Regions

units.sanskrit: कथम् ।
units.english: In what manner?Earth is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’The Locative ending in the word ‘lokeṣu’ should be taken in the sense of the nominative, the sense being that the syllable ‘hiṃ’ being viewed as Earth, one should meditate upon Earth as the syllable ‘Hiṃ’

units.sanskrit: पृथिवो हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Heaven is Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: लोकेष्विति या सप्तमी तां प्रथमात्वेन वि
units.english: as it is in Heaven that departing from this world, beings are kept nidhīyante

units.sanskrit: अथावृत्तेषु । द्यौर् हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Now, with reference to those discendingHeaven is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: आदित्यः प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: the Sun is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: अग्निः प्रतिहारः । पृथिवी निधनम् ॥
units.english: Sky is Udgītha; Fire is Pratihāra; Earth is Nidhana

units.sanskrit: अथा'वृत्तेष्ववाङ्मुखेषु पञ्चविधमुच्यते सामोपासनम् ।
units.english: Now with reference to those descending ie with reference to the regions turning downwards,the meditation of the fivefold Sāma is described

units.sanskrit: गत्यागतिविशिष्टा हि लोकाः ।
units.english: Regions are endowed with faculties of going forward and coming back;

units.sanskrit: यथा ते तथादृष्ट्यैव सामोपासनं विधीयते यतो ऽत आवृत्तेषु लोकेषु ।
units.english: and as they happen to be, so should the Sāma be meditated upon;

units.sanskrit: द्यौर्हिङ्कारः प्राथम्यात् ।
units.english: hence the text says ‘with reference to those descending’Heaven is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, because both occupy the first position;

units.sanskrit: आदित्यः प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: the Sun is Prāstava;

units.sanskrit: उदिते ह्यादित्ये प्रस्तूयन्ते कर्माणि प्राणिनाम् ।
units.english: because it is only on the side of the Sun that the activities of living beings Start prastūyante

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षमुद्गीथः पूर्ववत् । अग्निः प्रतिहारः । प्राणिभिः प्रतिहरणादग्नेः । पृथिवी निधनम् ।
units.english: Sky is Udgītha, as before;Fire is Pratihāra, because Fire is carried hither and thither Pratiharaṇāt by living beings;Earth is Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: तत आगतानामिह निधनात् ॥
units.english: because those who return from Heaven die here on Earth Nidhanāt

units.sanskrit: कल्पन्ते हास्मै लोका ऊर्ध्वाश् चावृत्तश् च य एतद् एवं विद्वांल् लोकेषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: The ascending as the well as descending Regions belong to him who, knowing this thus, meditates upon the fivefold Sāma

units.sanskrit: उपासनफलंकल्पन्ते समर्था भवन्ति हास्मै लोका ऊर्ध्वाश्चा'वृत्ताश्च गत्यागतिविशिष्टा भोग्यत्वेन व्यवतिष्ठन्त इत्यर्थः
units.english: The reward of the said meditation is as follows;The Regions, ascending as well as descending, endowed with the faculty of going and coming, belong to him;

units.sanskrit: य एतदेवं विद्वांल्लोकेषु पञ्चविधं समस्तं साधु सामेत्युपास्त इति सर्वत्र योजना पञ्चविधे सप्तविधे च ॥
units.english: ie become objects of enjoyment to him;to him who, knowing this thus, meditates upon the fivefold Entire Sāma as ‘food’, with reference to the regions This same construction has to be adopted in all casesie meditating of the fivefold as well as the sevenfold Sāma,

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: वृष्टौ पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma, with reference to Rain;

units.sanskrit: पुरोवातो हिङ्कारः । मेघो जायते स प्रस्तावः । वर्षति स उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the preceding High Wind is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’ the appearance of the Cloud is the Prastāva; the Raining is Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: विद्योतते स्तनयति स प्रतिहारः ॥
units.english: the Lightning and Thunder are the Pratihāra

units.sanskrit: वृष्टौ पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma, with reference to Rain

units.sanskrit: लोकस्थितेर्वृष्टिनिमित्तत्वादानन्तर्यम् ।
units.english: The meditation on Rain is mentioned immediately after that on the Regions, because the stability of the Regions is dependent upon Rain

units.sanskrit: पुरोवातो हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The preceding wind is the syllalbe ‘Hiṃ’

units.sanskrit: पुरोवाताद्युद्ग्रहणान्ता हि वृष्टिः ।
units.english: The term ‘Rain’ here stands for the whole phenomenon, beginning with the ‘preceding wind’ and ending with ‘cessation’;

units.sanskrit: यथा साम हिङ्कारादिनिधनान्तम् ।
units.english: just as the term ‘Sāma’ stands for the whole process beginning with ‘the syllable Hiṃ and ending with the ‘nidhana’

units.sanskrit: अतः पुरोवातो हिङ्कारः । प्राथम्यात् ।
units.english: Hence the ‘preceding wind’ is the ‘syllable Hiṃ because these occupy the first place in their respective phenomena

units.sanskrit: मेघो जायते स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: The appearance of the clouds is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: प्रावृषि मेघजनने वृष्टेः प्रस्ताव इति हि प्रसिद्धिः । वर्षति स उद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: because it is a wellknown fact that on the advent of the rainyseason, the heralding of Rain Prastāva is done by the appearance of clouds The raining is Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: प्रतिहृतत्वात् ॥
units.english: because of the special importance attaching to both

units.sanskrit: उद्गृह्णाति तन् निधनं वर्षयति ह य एतद् एवं विद्वान् वृष्टौ पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: The Cessation is the Nidhana One who, knowing this thus, meditates upon the fivefold Sāma,for him it rains and he also makes it rain

units.sanskrit: उद्गृह्णाति तन्निधनम् । समाप्तिसामान्यात् ।
units.english: Cessation is the Nidhana; because both represent the end of their respective processes

units.sanskrit: फलमुपासनस्यवर्शति हास्मा इच्छातः । तथा वर्षयति हासत्यामपि वृष्टौ ।
units.english: The reward of such meditation is as followsIt rains for him,whenever he wishes it and he also makes it rainwhen there is no rain

units.sanskrit: य एतदित्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: etc,as before End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: सर्वास्व् अप्सु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत । मेघो यत् संप्लवते स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma, in reference to all waters The gathering of clouds is the syllable Hiṃ;

units.sanskrit: यद् वर्षति स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: What rains is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: याः प्राच्यः स्यन्दन्ते स उद्गीथः । याः प्रतीच्यः स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: those flowing eastward are the Udgītha; those flowing westward are the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: समुद्रो निधनम् ॥
units.english: the Ocean is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: सर्वास्वप्सु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत । वृष्टिपूर्वकत्वात्सर्वासामपामानन्तर्यम् ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sama, in reference to all waters;this comes next to rain because Water is always preceded by Rain

units.sanskrit: मेघो यत्संप्लवत एकीभावेनेतरेतरं घनीभवति मेघो यदोन्नतस्तदा संप्लवत इत्युच्यते मेघस्तदापामारम्भः स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The gathering of clouds,ie, when the clouds thicken by being piled upon each other; as a matter of fact, whenever the cloud rises, it is said to be ‘gathering’;

units.sanskrit: यद्वर्षति स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: That which rains is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: आपः सर्वतो व्याप्तुं प्रस्तुताः ।
units.english: as it is then that the Waters are proceeding Prastutāḥ to spread on all sides

units.sanskrit: याः प्राच्यः स्यन्दन्ते स उद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् । याः प्रतीच्यः स प्रतिहारः प्रतिशब्दसामान्यात् ।
units.english: Those flowing eastward are the Udgītha;because of the great importance of both these Those flowing westward are the Pratihāra because the term ‘prati’ is common to both ‘pratīcī’ and ‘pratihāra’

units.sanskrit: समुद्रो निधनम् ।
units.english: The Ocean is the Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: तन्निधनत्वादपाम् ॥
units.english: as the Ocean is the first repository of all waters

units.sanskrit: न हाप्सु प्रैत्य् अप्सुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् सर्वास्व् अप्सु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: If one who knowing this thus meditates upon the fivefold Sāma in reference to all waters, he dies not in water, and becomes rich in water

units.sanskrit: न हाप्सु प्रैति । नेच्छति चेत् । अप्सुमानंमान्भवति फलम् ॥
units.english: He dies not in waterunless he wishes it;he becomes rich in waterpossessor of much water;This is the reward following from the foregoing meditation

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: ऋतुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत । वसन्तो हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma, in reference to the seasons The Spring is the syllable‘Hiih’;

units.sanskrit: ग्रीष्मः प्रस्तावः । वर्षा उद्गीथः । शरत् प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Summer is the Prastāva; the Rainy season is Udgītha, the Autumn is Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: हेमन्तो निधनम् ॥
units.english: and the Winter is Nidhana

units.sanskrit: ॠतुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma in reference to the seasons;

units.sanskrit: ॠतुव्यवस्थाया यथोक्ताम्बुनिमित्तत्वादानन्तर्यम् ।
units.english: this comes next to the waters, because the seasons ore regulated through the waters

units.sanskrit: वसन्तो हिङ्कारः । प्राथम्यात् ।
units.english: Spring is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, because both occupy the first position

units.sanskrit: ग्रीष्मः प्रस्तावः । यवादिसंग्रहः प्रस्तूयते हि प्रावृडर्थम् । वर्षा उद्गीथः प्राधान्यात् ।
units.english: Summer is Prastāva,because it is in summer that Barley and other grains begin to be stored against the Rains The Rainy Season is Udgītha,because of the great importance of both

units.sanskrit: शरत्प्रतिहारः । रोगिणां मृतानां च प्रतिहरणात् ।
units.english: Autumn is Pratihāra, because it is during this season that the sick and the dead are removed pratiharaṇāt

units.sanskrit: हेमन्तो निधनम् ।
units.english: Winter is Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: निवाते निधनात्प्राणिनाम् ॥
units.english: because during this season, living beings take shelter in places free from draught nivāta

units.sanskrit: कल्पन्ते हास्मा ऋतव ऋतुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् ऋतुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: If one, knowing this, thus meditates upon the fivefold Sāma, in reference to the seasons,the seasons belong to him, and he becomes rich in seasons

units.sanskrit: फलंकल्पन्ते ह ऋतुव्यवस्थानुरूपं भोग्यत्वेनास्मा उपासकायर्तवः । ऋतुमानार्तवैर्भोगैश्च सम्पन्नो भवतीत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: The seasons belong to him;ie, for such a meditator, the seasons bring up all objects of enjoyment, in due accordance with the sequence of the seasons and he becomes rich in seasons; ie, he derives full enjoyment from all pleasures in due accord with various seasons

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य पञ्चमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पशुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma in reference to Animals;

units.sanskrit: अवयः प्रस्तावः । गाव उद्गीथः । अश्वः प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: Goats are the syllable ‘Hiṃ’ Sheep are the Prastāva Cows are the Udgītha Horses are the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: पुरुषो निधनम् ॥
units.english: Man is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: पशुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपासीत । सम्यग्वृत्तेष्वृतुषु पशव्यः काल इत्यानन्तर्यम् ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the fivefold Sāma, in reference to AnimalsThe sequence of Animals to the Seasons is due to the fact that it is only when the seasons function in the proper manner that the time is favourable to Animals

units.sanskrit: अजा हिङ्कारः । प्राधान्यात् प्राथम्याद्वा ।
units.english: Goats are the Syllable ‘Hiṃ’ because both are equally important, or because both occupy the first position;

units.sanskrit: अजः पशूनां प्रथमैति श्रुतेः । अवयः प्रस्तावः । साहचर्यदर्शनादजादीनाम् ।
units.english: in view of the Śrutitext to the effect that ‘goats are the first among animals’Sheep are the Prastāva;because goats and sheep are always found together just as the syllable ‘Hiṃ’ and the Prastāva are always found together

units.sanskrit: गावः उद्गीथः ।
units.english: Cows are the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: because of the great importance of both

units.sanskrit: अश्वाः प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: Horses are the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: पुरुषो निधनम् । पुरुषाश्रयत्वात्पशूनाम् ॥
units.english: because they carry over Man is the Nidhana;because animals are dependent upon Man

units.sanskrit: भवन्ति हास्य पशवः पशुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् पशुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: If one knowing this thus, meditates upon the fivefold Sāma, with reference to animals, animals come to him and he becomes rich in cattle

units.sanskrit: फलंभवन्ति हास्य पशवः पशुमान्भवति ।
units.english: Animals come to him and he becomes rich in cattle;

units.sanskrit: पशुफलैश्च भोगत्यागादिभिर्युज्यत इत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: that is, he becomes endowed with the reward of possessing cattle,in the shape of using them himself and giving them away to others

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य षष्ठः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: प्राणेषु पञ्चविधं परोवरीयः सामोपासीत । प्राणो हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the gradually higher and better fivefold Sāma in reference to the Senseorgans The Breathing organ is the syllable Hiṃ;

units.sanskrit: वाक् प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: the Vocal organ is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: चक्षुर् उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the Visual organ is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Auditory organ is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: मनो निधनम् ।
units.english: the Mind is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: परोवरीयांसि वा एतानि ॥
units.english: These, verily are gradually higher and better

units.sanskrit: प्राणेषु पञ्चविधं परोवरीयः सामोपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the gradually higher and better fivefold Sāma in reference to the Senseorgans

units.sanskrit: परंपरं वरीयस्त्वगुणवत्प्राणदृष्टिविशिष्टं सामोपासीतेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: That is, one should meditate upon the Sāma viewed as the Senseorgans, and endowed with the quality of being gradually higher and better

units.sanskrit: प्राणो घ्राणं हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The Breathing organie the Olfactory organ,is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: उत्तरोत्तरवरीयसां प्राथम्यात् ।
units.english: because it is the first among a set where each succeeding one is superior to the preceding one

units.sanskrit: वाक्प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: The Vocal organ is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: वाचा हि प्रस्तूयते सर्वम् ।
units.english: because everything is introduced prastūyate by means of speech;

units.sanskrit: वाग्वरीयसी प्राणात् । अप्राप्तमप्युच्यते वाचा, प्राप्तस्यैव तु गन्धस्य ग्राहकः प्राणः ।
units.english: and speech is superior to olfaction, inasmuch as through the Vocal organ one can speak of a thing which is not in contact with the organ, while the Olfactory organ can apprehend only such odour as is in contact with it

units.sanskrit: चक्षुरुद्गीथः ।
units.english: The Visual organ is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: वाचो बहुतरविषयं प्रकाशयति चक्षुरतो वरीयो वाचः, उद्गीथः ।
units.english: inasmuch as the Visual organ illumines renders cognisable more things than the Vocal organ, it is superior to the vocal organ;

units.sanskrit: श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: and it is the Udgītha, on account of its great importance

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: The Auditory organ is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: प्रतिहृतत्वात् ।
units.english: because it is withdrawn within pratihṛta;

units.sanskrit: वरीयस्त्वं च श्रोत्रान्मनसः ।
units.english: and this is superior to the Visual organ, because sound is heard from all sides

units.sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियविषयव्यापकत्वात् ।
units.english: because the objects apprehended through all the organs are all stored nidhīyante in the Mind;

units.sanskrit: अतीन्द्रियविषयो ऽपि मनसो गोचर एवेति ।
units.english: in fact, even things beyond the reach of the senses are apprehensible through the Mind

units.sanskrit: यथोक्तहेतुभ्यः परोवरीयांसि प्राणादीनि वा एतानि ॥
units.english: For the said reasons, all these,organs, Olfactory and the restVerily are gradually higher and better

units.sanskrit: परोवरीयो हास्य भवति परोवरीयसो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् प्राणेषु पञ्चविधं परोवरीयः सामोपास्ते ।
units.english: If one meditates upon the gradually higher and better Sāma, in reference to the Senseorgans,what is higher and better comes to him and he wins such regions as are higher and better

units.sanskrit: इति तु पञ्चविधस्य ॥
units.english: So much for the fivefold Sāma

units.sanskrit: एतद्दृष्ट्या विशिष्टं यः परोवरीयः सामोपास्ते परोवरीयो हास्य जीवनं भवतीत्युक्तार्थम् । इति तु पञ्चविधस्य साम्न उपासनमुक्तमिति सप्तविधे वक्ष्यमाणविषये बुद्धिसमाधानार्थम् ।
units.english: If one meditates upon Sāma as qualified by the said view, then his life becomes higher and better etc, etc,as already explained aboveSo much for the fivefold Sāma;;that is, so far what has been described is meditation upon the fivefold Sāma;This is meant to divert attention to what is going to be said next in regard to the sevenfold Sāma;

units.sanskrit: निरपेक्षो हि पञ्चविधे, वक्ष्यमाणे बुद्धिं समाधित्सति ॥
units.english: because not caring much for the fivefold aspect, the Speaker is going to attract attention to what he is going to say next

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य सप्तमः खण्डः अथ सप्तविधस्य । वाचि सप्तविधम् सामोपासीत । यत् किंच वाचो हुम् इति स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse Now for the Sevenfold Sāma One should meditate upon the sevenfold Sāma, in reference to Speech that particular form of Speech which consists of ‘Hum’ is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: यत् प्रेति स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: that which consists of ‘Pra’ is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: यद् एति स आदिः ॥
units.english: that which consists of ‘Ā’ is the Ādi

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरं सप्तविधस्य समस्तस्य साम्न उपासनं साध्विदमारभ्यते । वाचीति सप्तमी पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: Now follows the excellent meditation of the entire sevenfold Sāma The form ‘vāci’ Locative is to be explained as before [ in the case of the words ‘lokeṣu’ and the rest, under text of the second section, above and the following;

units.sanskrit: वाग्दृष्टिविशिष्टं सप्तविधं सामोपासीतेत्यर्थः । यत्किञ्च वाचः शब्दस्य हुमिति यो विशेषः स हिङ्कारो हकारसामान्यात् ।
units.english: the sense is that one should meditate upon the Sevenfold Sāma, viewed as SpeechThat particular form of Speechsoundwhich consists of the peculiar syllable ‘Huṃ’ is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, because the letter ‘ha’ is common to both

units.sanskrit: यत्प्रेति शब्दरूपं स प्रस्तावः प्रसामान्यात् ।
units.english: That form of speech which consists of ‘Pra’ is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: आकारसामान्यात् ।
units.english: because the letter ‘pra’ is common to both

units.sanskrit: आदिरित्योङ्कारः । सर्वादित्वात् ॥
units.english: ‘ādi’ here stands for the syllable ‘Om’, because that is the beginning of all things

units.sanskrit: यद् उद् इति स उद्गीथः । यत् प्रतीति स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: That which is ‘Ut’ is the Udgītha that which is ‘Prati’, is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: यद् उपेति स उपद्रवः ।
units.english: that which is ‘Upa’ is the Upadrava;

units.sanskrit: यन् नीति तन् निधनम् ॥
units.english: and that which is ‘ni’ is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: यदुदिति स उद्गीथः । फत्पूर्वत्वादुद्गीथस्य । यत्प्रतीति स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: That which is ‘Ut’ is Udgītha because the first part of the term ‘Udgītha’ consists of ‘ut’That which is Pra is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: प्रतिसामान्यात् ।
units.english: because the syllable ‘pra’ is common to both

units.sanskrit: यदुपेति स उपद्रव उपोपक्रमत्वादुपद्रवस्य ।
units.english: because the name ‘Upadrava’ begins with the syllable ‘upa’

units.sanskrit: यन्नीति तन्निधनम् ।
units.english: That which is ‘ni’ is the Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: निशब्दसामान्यात् ॥
units.english: because the syllable ‘ni’ is common to both

units.sanskrit: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः । अन्नवान् अन्नादो भवति । य एतद् एवं विद्वान् वाचि सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: If one knowing this thus meditates upon the sevenfold Sāma in reference to Speech,for him Speech itself milks the milk of speech, and he becomes rich in food and an eater of food

units.sanskrit: दुग्धे ऽस्मा इत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ॥
units.english: For him Speech yields milk etc, etc,this has been already explained above

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्याष्टमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ खल्व् अमुम् आदित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: Now, verily, one should meditate upon the Sevenfold Sāma as the Sun

units.sanskrit: सर्वदा समस् तेन साम ।
units.english: He is always the same; hence he is Sāma

units.sanskrit: मां प्रति मां प्रतीति सर्वेण समस् तेन साम ॥
units.english: He is the same to all, as everyone thinks ‘He faces me’, ‘He faces me’ Hence he is Sāma

units.sanskrit: अवयवमात्रे साम्न्यादित्यदृष्टिः पञ्चविधेषूक्ता प्रथमे चाध्याये ।
units.english: In the first Discourse, it was stated that parts of the Sāma should be viewed and meditated upon as the Sun; and this was in reference to the fivefold Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीं खल्वमुमादित्यं समस्ते साम्न्यवयवविभागशो ऽध्यस्य सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: What is going to be said now is that one should meditate upon the Sevenfold Sāma, viewing the entire Sāma as the Sun, in reference to the constituent factors of the Sāma and of the Sun

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनः सामत्वमादित्यस्येति । उच्यते । उद्गीथत्वे हेतुवदादित्यस्य सामत्वे हेतुः । को ऽसौ, सर्वदा समो वृद्धिक्षयाभावात्तेन हेतुना सामा'दित्यो मां प्रति मां प्रतीति तुल्यां बुद्धिमुत्पादयति ।
units.english: But in what way has the Sun the character of the Sāma?The answer is as followsThe ground for regarding the Sun as the Sāma is the same as that for regarding the Sun as Udgītha ,What is that ground?The Sun is always the same, as there is no expansion and contraction as there is in the case of the Moon;hence He is Sāma The phrase ‘He faces me, He faces me’ indicates the idea of Sameness

units.sanskrit: अतः सर्वेण समो ऽतः साम समत्वादित्यर्थः ।
units.english: For the reason the Sun is the same to all, and hence He is Sāma, Because he is the same;

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथभक्तिसामान्यवचनादेव लोकादिषूक्तसामान्याद्धिङ्कारादित्वं गम्यत इति हिङ्कारादित्वे कारणं नोक्तम् ।
units.english: When the Text spoke in the earlier discourse of the San as the syllables ‘Hiṅ’ and the rest, no special reason was assigned for it, because the similarity of the Udgīthafactor itself implies the said similarity to the Regions;

units.sanskrit: सामत्वे पुनः सवितुरनुक्तं कारणं न सुबोधमिति समत्वमुक्तम् ॥
units.english: in the present instance, however, Sameness has been assigned as the reason for the Sun being viewed as Sāman,as this reason which would not be easily intelligible

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् इमानि सर्वाणि भूतान्य् अन्वायत्तानीति विद्यात् ।
units.english: One should know that all these beings are dependent upon Him

units.sanskrit: तस्य यत् पुरोदयात् स हिङ्कारः । तद् अस्य पशवो ऽन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: That form of His which appears before his rise is the syallable ‘Hiṃ’; on this depend the animals

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् ते हिङ्कुर्वन्ति । हिङ्कारभाजिनो ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: It is for this reason that they utter the syllable ‘Hiṃ’; they being supplicants to the syllable ‘Him’ in the Sāma

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नादित्ये ऽवयवविभागश इमानि वक्ष्यमाणानि सर्वामि भूतान्यन्वायत्तान्यनुगतान्यादित्यमुपजीव्यत्वेनेति विद्यात् ।
units.english: On Hiṃ,On the various forms of the Sun, all these Beingsgoing to be describedare dependent ie depending upon Him as their support;this is what one should know

units.sanskrit: कथं, तस्या'दित्यस्य यत्पुरोदयाद्धर्मरूपं स हिङ्कारो भक्तिस्तत्रेदं सामान्यं
units.english: How?That form of it which appears before His rise,ie the form of Dharma Righteousness,is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, which is a constituent of Sāma

units.sanskrit: यत्तस्य हिङ्कारभक्तिरूपं तदस्या'दित्यस्य साम्नः पशवो गवादयो ऽन्वायत्ता अनुगतास्तद्भक्तिरूपमुपजीवन्तीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The Sun being the Sāma, that form of the Sun which is parallel to the syllable ‘Hiṃ’,on that depend the animals,cow and the rest; ie, they follow it and live upon that factor

units.sanskrit: यस्मादेवं तस्मात्ते हिङ्कुर्वन्ति पशवः प्रागुदयात् ।
units.english: Because this is so, therefore they utter the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, before sunrise

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्धिङ्कारभाजिनो ह्येतस्या'दित्याख्यस्य साम्नः तद्भक्तिभजनशीलत्वाद्धि त एवं वर्तन्ते ॥
units.english: For this reason they are supplicant to this syllable ‘Hiṃ’ of the Sāma as ‘Sun’; and because they are so supplicantinclined to worshipthat Factor, therefore they behave like this

units.sanskrit: अथ यत् प्रथमोदिते स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: That form which appears on the first rising of the Sun is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य मनुष्या अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: on this Men are dependent;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् ते प्रस्तुतिकामाः प्रशंसाकामाः ।
units.english: hence they desire Eulogy and Praise;

units.sanskrit: प्रस्तावभाजिनो ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: being supplicants to the Prastāva of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्प्रथमोदिते सवितृरूपं तदस्या'दित्याख्यास्य साम्नः स प्रस्तावस्तदस्य मनुष्या अन्वायत्ताः पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: That formof the Sunwhich appears on His first rising,is the Prastāva of the Sāma in the shape of the Sun;on this Men are dependent etc etc as before

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्ते प्रस्तुतिं प्रशंसां कामयन्ते ।
units.english: Thus for this reason that they desire Eulogy and Praise;

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्प्रस्तावभाजिनो ह्येतस्य साम्नः ॥ अथ यत् संगववेलायां स आदिः ।
units.english: because they are supplicants to the Prastāva of the said Sāma That Form which appears at the ‘assembling time’ is the ‘Ādi’;

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य वयांस्य् अन्वायत्तानि ।
units.english: on this are dependent the Birds;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तान्य् अन्तरिक्षे ऽनारम्भणान्य् आदायात्मानं परिपतन्ति ।
units.english: hence do they, without support, betake themselves to the Sky and fly about;

units.sanskrit: आदिभाजीनि ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ॥ अथ यत्सङ्गववेलायां गवां रश्मीनां सङ्गमनं सङ्गमो यस्यां वेलायां, गवां वा वत्सैः सा सङ्गववेला तस्मिन्काले यत्सावित्रं रूपं स आदिर्भक्तिविशेष ओङ्कारस्तदस्य वयांसि पक्षिणो ऽन्वायत्तानि ।
units.english: That form which appears at the ‘Saṅgavatime’;that time at which there is an assembling or coming together of the Rays,or that time at which there is assembling or coming together of the calves with the cows;that form of the Sun which appears at this ‘assembling time’ is the Adi,which is a particular part of the Sāma; this is the syllable ‘om’;on this are dependent the Birds;

units.sanskrit: यत एवं तस्मात्तानि वयांस्तन्तरिक्षे ऽनारम्बणान्यनालम्बनान्यात्मानमादाया'त्मानमेवा'लम्बनत्वेन गृहीत्वा परिपतन्ति गच्छन्त्यत आकारसामान्यादादिभक्तिभाजीनि ह्येतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: and because it is so, therefore, the Birds, without support without any thing to support them,betake themselves to the skydepending upon themselves,and fly about, move about For this reasonie on account of the common factor in the shape of the letter ‘ā’ which occurs in ‘āditya’ and also ‘ādi’, these Birds are supplicants to this factor of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यत् संप्रति मध्यंदिने स उद्गीथः ।
units.english: That form which appears at midday is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य देवा अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: on this the Deities are dependent;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् ते सत्तमाः प्राजापत्यानाम् ।
units.english: hence these are the best among the offsprings of Prajāpati;

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथभाजिनो ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: being supplicants to this Udgītha of this Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्सम्प्रति मध्यन्दिन ऋजुमध्यन्दिन इत्यर्थः । स उद्गीथभक्तिस्तदस्य देवा अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: That form which appears at midday,ie, exactly at middayis that factor of the Sāma which is known as ‘Udgītha’;On this the Deities are dependent;

units.sanskrit: द्योतनातिशयात्तत्काले ।
units.english: because at that time there is existence of light

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्ते सत्तमा विशिष्टतमाः ।
units.english: Hence they are the bestbest qualifiedamong the offsprings

units.sanskrit: प्राजापत्यानां प्रजापत्यपत्यानामुद्गीथभाजिनो ह्येतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: Prajāpati those born of Prajāpati;these are supplicants to the Udgītha of this Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् ऊर्ध्वं मध्यंदिनात् प्राग् अपराह्णात् स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: That form which appears after midday and before afternoon is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य गर्भा अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: on this the Embryos are dependent;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् ते प्रतिहृता नावपद्यन्ते ।
units.english: hence, on being held up, they do not fall down;

units.sanskrit: प्रतिहारभाजिनो ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: being supplicants to the Pratihāra of this Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यदूर्ध्वं मध्यन्दिनात्प्रागपराह्नाद्यद्रूपं सवितुः स प्रतिहारस्तदस्य गर्भा अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: That form of the Sun which appears after midday, and before afternoon is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: अतस्ते सवितुः प्रतिहारभक्तिरूपेणोर्ध्वं प्रतिहृताः सन्तो नावपद्यन्ते नाधः पतन्ति तद्द्वारे सत्यपीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: on this the Embryos are dependent; hence, when they are held up by the upholding potency of the Sun, they do not fall down; that is, even though there is a way for them to fall through;

units.sanskrit: यतः प्रतिहारभाजिनो ह्येतस्य साम्नो गर्भाः ॥
units.english: and the reaons for this lies in the fact that the Embryos are supplicants to this Pratihāra of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् ऊर्ध्वम् अपराह्णात् प्राग् अस्तम् अयात् स उपद्रवः ।
units.english: Now that form which appears after the afternoon and before Sunset is the Upadrava;

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्यारण्या अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: on these the foresters are dependent;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् ते पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा कक्षं श्वभ्रम् इत्य् उपद्रवन्ति ।
units.english: hence on seeing a man, they run away to the forest as a safe place

units.sanskrit: उपद्रवभाजिनो ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ॥
units.english: being suppliants to the Upadrava of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यदूर्ध्वमपराह्नात्प्रागस्तमयात्स उपद्रवस्तदस्या'रण्याः पश्वो ऽन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: That form which appears after the afternoon and before sunset is the Upadrava;on this the foresters wild animalsare dependent;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्ते पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा भीताः कक्षमरण्यं श्वभ्रं भयशून्यमित्युपद्रवन्त्युपगच्छन्ति दृष्ट्वोपद्रवणादुपद्रवभाजिनो ह्येतस्य साम्नः
units.english: hence on seeing a man, they,being frightened,run away to the forest as a safe placefree from danger;because they run away Upadravaṇāt on seeing a man, therefore they ere supplicants to the Upadrava of this Sāma

units.sanskrit: अथ यत् प्रथमास्तमिते तन् निधनम् ।
units.english: That form which appears on the first advent of sunset is the Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य पितरो ऽन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: on this the Pitṛs are dependent;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तान् निदधति । निधनभाजिनो ह्य् एतस्य साम्नः ।
units.english: hence they place these,these being supplicants to the Nidhana of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: एवं खल्व् अमुम् आदित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: Thus, verily, does one meditate upon the sevenfold Sāma in the Sun

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्प्रथमास्तमिते ऽदर्शनं जिगमिषति सवितरि तन्निधनं तदस्य
units.english: That form which appears on the first adven of sunsetiie, when the sun is just becoming invisible,is the Nidhana;

units.sanskrit: पितरो ऽन्वायत्तास्तस्मात्तान्निदधति पितृपितामहप्रपितामहरूपेण दर्भेषु निक्षिपन्ति तांस्तदर्थं पिण्डान्वा स्थापयन्ति । निधनसम्बन्धान्निधनभाजिनो ह्येतस्य साम्नः पितरः ।
units.english: an this the Pitṛs are dependent; hence they place them,instal them in the form of the three ancestors Father, Grandfather and Greatgrandfather,either those ancestors themselves, or the ballofferings meant for them,on Kuśagrass;because the Pitṛs, being connected with Nidhana, are supplicants to the Nidhana of this Sāma

units.sanskrit: एवमवयवशः सप्तधा विभक्तं खल्वमुमादित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते यस्तस्य तदापत्तिः फलमिति वाक्यशेषः ॥
units.english: Thus, one meditates upon the sevenfold Sāma,divided into seven parts,as the Sun;with the result that one becomes merged into the Sun,this is understood End of Section of Discourse The Sun is Death;

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य नवमः खण्डः
units.english: because he brings about the end of the world, through time divided into Day and Night;

units.sanskrit: अथ खल्व् आत्मसंमितम् अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
units.english: Now one should meditate upon the sevenfold Sāma, selfmeasured and transcending death

units.sanskrit: हिङ्कार इति त्र्यक्षरम् ।
units.english: The name Hiṃkāra consists of three letters;

units.sanskrit: प्रस्ताव इति त्र्यक्षरम् । तत् समम् ॥
units.english: the name Prastāva consists of three letters;so that is sama equal

units.sanskrit: मृत्युरादित्यः अहोरात्रादिकालेन जगतः प्रमापयितृत्वात् ।
units.english: Now,ie, after the meditation of the Sāma as pertaining to the Sun and Death

units.sanskrit: आत्मसंमितं स्वावयवतुल्यतया मितं परमात्मतुल्यतया वा संमितमतिमृत्यु मृत्युजयहेतुत्वात् । यथा प्रथमे ऽध्याय उद्गीथभक्तिनामाक्षराण्युद्गीथ इत्युपास्यत्वेनोक्तानि,
units.english: selfmeasured, ie, measured or determined through the equality of its own constituent factors; or determined by equality to the supreme self, being the means of conquering DeathIn the first Discourse the letters composing the name ‘Udgītha’ have been described as to be meditated [upon as Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: तथेह साम्नः सप्तविधभक्तिनामाक्षराणि समाहृत्य त्रिभिस्रिभिः समतया सामत्वं परिकल्प्योपास्यत्वेनोच्यन्ते ।
units.english: in the same manner, in the present context, the letters composing the names of the seven factors of the Sāma are taken together,then each of these is assumed to be Sāma on account of the equality of their component letters, taken in groups of three,and then put forth as objects to be meditated upon

units.sanskrit: तदुपासनेन मृत्युगोचराक्षरसमख्यासामान्येन तं मृत्युं प्राप्य तदतिरिक्ताक्षरेण तस्या'दित्यस्य मृत्योरतिक्रमणायैव संक्रममं कल्पयति
units.english: By this meditation one gets at Death, through the equality of the number of letters within reach of death,and then through the remaining letter there is overreaching of death in the shape of the Sun

units.sanskrit: अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपासीत मृत्युमतिक्रान्तमतिरिक्ताक्षरसंख्ययेत्यमृत्यु साम ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the sevenfold Sāma, transcending death; the Sāma ‘transcends Death’ in the sense that it transcends, passes beyond, death, through the extra twentysecond letter,of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: तस्य प्रथमभक्तिनामाक्षराणि बिङ्कार इत्येतत्त्र्यक्षरं भक्तिमान प्रस्ताव इति च भक्तेस्त्र्यक्षरमेव मान तत्पूर्वेण समम् ॥
units.english: The number of letters in the name of its first factor,which is ‘Hiṃkāra’,is three; similarly the number of letters in the name of the other factorwhich is Prastāvais also three;so, that is equalto the former

units.sanskrit: आदिर् इति द्व्यक्षरम् । प्रतिहार इति चतुरक्षरम् ।
units.english: The name ‘Ādi’ consists of two letters, and the name ‘Pratihāra’ consists of four letters

units.sanskrit: तत इहैकम् । तत् समम् ॥
units.english: One from there to here makes it equal

units.sanskrit: आदिरिति द्व्यक्षरं, सप्तविधस्य साम्नः संख्यापूरण ओङ्कार आदिरित्युच्यते ।
units.english: The name ‘Ādi’ consists of two letters; The syllable Om which makes up the number seven of the sevenfold Sāma is called ‘Ādi’

units.sanskrit: प्रतिहार इति चतुरक्षरम् । तत इहैकमक्षरमवच्छिद्या'द्यक्षरयोः प्रक्षिप्यते । तेन तत्सममेव भवति ॥
units.english: The name ‘Pratihāra’ consists of four letters,Taking one letter from there to here,ie taking away one letter from the name ‘Pratihāra’ and adding it to the two letters of the name ‘Ādi’,it thereby becomes equal

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथ इति त्र्यक्षरम् उपद्रव इति चतुरक्षरं त्रिभिस् त्रिभिः समं भवति । अक्षरम् अतिशिष्यते त्र्यक्षरम् ।
units.english: The name ‘Udgītha’ consists of three letters; the name ‘Upadrava’ consists of four letters, Three and three are equal, one letter akṣara is left, which is three lettered, and that is equal

units.sanskrit: उद्गीथ इति त्र्यक्षरमुपद्रव इति चतुरक्षरं त्रिभिस्रिभिः समं भवत्यक्षरमतिशिष्यते ऽतिरिच्यते ।
units.english: The name ‘Udgītha’ consists of three letters; the name ‘Upadrava’ consists of four letters, three and three are equal;

units.sanskrit: तेन वैषम्ये प्राप्ते साम्नः समत्वकरणाया'हतदेकमपि सदक्षरमिति त्र्यक्षरमेव भवति ।
units.english: Thus, there is a discrepancy, and with a view to restoring the uniformity of the Sāma, it is addedthough the remaining letter is one only, yet being a letter, akṣarait isin the form of this name ‘akṣara’ which is threelettered;

units.sanskrit: अतस्तत्समम् ॥
units.english: that makes it equal

units.sanskrit: निधनम् इति त्र्यक्षरम् ।
units.english: The name ‘Nidhana’ consists of three, letters;

units.sanskrit: तत् समम् एव भवति ।
units.english: and it is uniform

units.sanskrit: तानि ह वा एतानि द्वाविंशतिर् अक्षराणि ॥
units.english: These, indeed, are this twentytwo letters

units.sanskrit: निधनमिति त्र्यक्षरं तत्सममेव भवति ।
units.english: The name ‘nidhana’ consists of three letters and it is uniform

units.sanskrit: एवं त्र्यक्षरसमतया सामत्वं सम्पाद्य यथाप्राप्तान्येवाक्षराणि संख्यायन्ते तानि ह वा एतानि सप्तभक्तिनामाक्षराणि द्वाविंशतिः ॥
units.english: Thus, through uniformity consisting in the character of being threelettered, having established the character of Sāma,the said letters are now duly numbered These indeed are the twentytwo lettersconstituting the names of the seven factors of the Sāma

units.sanskrit: एकविंशत्यादित्यम् आप्नोति । एकविंशो वा इतो ऽसाव् आदित्यः ।
units.english: By twentyone one reaches the Sun the sun verily is the Twentyfirst

units.sanskrit: द्वाविंशेन परम् आदित्याज् जयति ।
units.english: By the Twentysecond, one conquers what is above the Sun;

units.sanskrit: तन् नाकम् । तद् विशोकम् ॥
units.english: it is pure Happiness, it is free from sorrow

units.sanskrit: तत्रैकविंशत्यक्षरसंख्यया'दित्यमाप्नोति मृत्युम् ।
units.english: By twentyone,the number of letters, one reaches the Sun viz, death;

units.sanskrit: यस्मादेकविंश इतो ऽस्माल्लोकादसावादित्यः संख्यया ।
units.english: because the Sun is verily twentyfirstfrom this region;

units.sanskrit: द्वादश मासाः पञ्चर्तवस्रय इमे लोका असावादित्य एकविंशैति श्रुतेरतिशिष्टेन द्वाविंशेनाक्षरेण परं मृत्योरादित्याज्जयत्याप्नोतीत्यर्थः
units.english: as declared in the Vedic text‘Twelve months, five seasons, three regions, and the Sun as the twentyfirst’ By the remaining twentysecond letter one attains victory over what is above the Sun, ie, above Death

units.sanskrit: यच्च तदादित्यात्परं किं तत्? नाकं कमिति सुखं तस्य प्रतिषेधो ऽकं तन्न भवतीति नाकं कमेवेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: What is it that is above the Sun?It is pure happiness;‘Ka’ is happiness, ‘aka’ is nonhappiness, ‘Nāka’ is what is notnonhappiness that is Happiness itself;

units.sanskrit: मृत्युविषयत्वाद्दुःखस्य विशोकं च तद्विगतशोकं मानसदुःखरहितमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: and as all sorrow pertains to death, the said region is free from sorrow,that is, free from all mental suffering;this is the region that one reaches

units.sanskrit: आप्नोतीहादित्यस्य जयम् ।
units.english: One obtains victory over the Sun;

units.sanskrit: परो हास्यादित्यजयाज् जयो भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् आत्मसंमितम् अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते सामोपास्ते ॥
units.english: verily higher than this victory over the Sun is the victory that comes to one who, with this knowledge, meditates upon the sevenfold Sāma, selfmeasured and transcending Death,yea, meditates upon the Sāma

units.sanskrit: उक्तस्यैव पिण्डितार्थमाहएकविंशतिसंख्यया'दित्यस्य जयमाप्नोति परो हास्यैवंविद आदित्यजयान्मृत्युगोचरात्परो जयो भवति द्वाविंशत्यक्षरसंख्ययेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The Text states the upshot of what has been said above By the number Twentyone, one obtains victory over the Sun Victory higher than this victory over the Sunrelating to Death,comes to one,through the Twentysecond letter,who knowing this etc, etc

units.sanskrit: य एतदेवं द्वानितिक्याद्युक्तार्थम् । तस्यैतद्यथोक्तं फलमिति द्विरभ्यासः साप्तविध्यसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥
units.english: The meaning is that the said reward comes to the said meditator The repetition of the words Meditates upon the Sāma’ is meant to indicate the end of the sevenfold treatment of Sāma

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य दशमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: मनो हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Mind is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: वाक् प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: Speech is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: चक्षुर् उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the Eye is Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Ear is Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: प्राणो निधनम् ।
units.english: Breath is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् गायत्रं प्राणेषु प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Gāyatra Sāma interwoven with the Senseorgans

units.sanskrit: विना नामग्रहणं पञ्चविधस्य सप्तविधस्य च साम्न उपासनमुक्तम् ।
units.english: Without actually naming the meditations, the text has so far described the meditation of the fivefold and sevenfold Sāma;

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीं गायत्रादिनामग्रहणपूर्वकं विशिष्टफलानि सामोपासनान्तराण्युच्यन्ते यथाक्रमं गायत्रादीनां कर्मणि प्रयोगस्तथैव ।
units.english: it now describes other forms of meditation on Sāma leading to particular results,and supplies their names as ‘Gāyatra’ and the rest On the same lines, in the same order, are the various Sāmas used as sacrificial Rites

units.sanskrit: मनो हिङ्कारो मनसः सर्वकरणप्रवृत्तीनां प्राथम्यात् । तदानन्तर्याद्वाक्प्रस्तावश्चक्षुरुद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् । श्रोत्रं प्रतिहारः प्रतिहृतत्वात् ।
units.english: Mind is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’ because Mind stands for the first of all the sensefunctions,By reason of its sequence to the Mind, Speech is the Prastāva; The Eye is the Udgītha, because of superior importance The Eye is the Pratihāra, because it is drawn within pratihṛta

units.sanskrit: प्राणो निधनं यथोक्तानां प्राणे निधनात्स्वापकाले ।
units.english: Breath is Nidhana; because all the aforesaid organs become merged in Breath, at the time of sleep

units.sanskrit: एतद्गायत्रं साम प्राणेषु प्रोतम् ।
units.english: This is the GāyatraSāma, interwoven with the senseorgans;

units.sanskrit: गायत्र्याः प्राणसंस्तुतत्वात् ॥
units.english: it is so called because the Gāyatri has been eulogised as ‘Breath’

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् गायत्रं प्राणेषु प्रोतं वेद । प्राणी भवति । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति ।
units.english: One who knows this Gāyatra Sama as interwoven with the senseorgans, retains his senseorgans, attains full life, lives gloriously, and becomes great with offspring and cattle and great in fame

units.sanskrit: महामनाः स्यात् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that ‘he should be highminded’

units.sanskrit: स य एवमेतद्गायत्रं प्राणेषु प्रोतं वेद प्राणी भवति ।
units.english: One who knows the Sāma thus as interwoven with the senseorgans retains his senseorgans;

units.sanskrit: अविकलकरणो भवतीत्येतत् ।
units.english: tlíat is, his organs remain efficient

units.sanskrit: सर्वमायुरेति । शतं वर्षणि सर्वमायुः पुरुषस्येति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: He attains full life,a hundred years constitute the ‘full life’ of man,as declared in the Veda

units.sanskrit: ज्योगुज्ज्वलं जीवति ।
units.english: He lives gloriously,ie, a glorious life

units.sanskrit: महान्भवति प्रजादिभिर्महांश्च कीर्त्या ।
units.english: He becomes great with offsprings etc,and great also in fame

units.sanskrit: गायत्रोपासकस्यैतद्व्रतं भवति यन्महामनास्त्वक्षुद्रचित्तः स्यादित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: For one who meditates upon the Gāyatra Sāma the observance is that ‘he should be highminded’; ie he should not be meanminded

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्यैकादशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अभिमन्थति स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The Rubbing is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: धूमो जायते स प्रस्तावः । ज्वलति स उद्गीथः । अङ्गारा भवन्ति स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the rising of the Smoke is the Prastāva; the glowing is the Udgītha; the appearing of embers is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: उपशाम्यति तन् निधनम् । संशाम्यति तन् निधनम् ।
units.english: the calming down is the Nidhana, complete extinguishment is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् रथंतरम् अग्नौ प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Rathantara interwoven in Fire

units.sanskrit: अभिमन्थति स हिङ्कारः प्राथम्यात् । अग्नेर्धूमो जायते स प्रस्ताव आनन्तर्यात् । ज्वलति स उद्गीथो हविः सम्बन्धाच्छ्रैष्ठ्यं ज्वलनस्य ।
units.english: The Rubbing is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’, because of its being the first step in the process;the rising of the smokefrom the fire,is the Prastāva because of its coming next to the Rubbing;the glowing is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: अङ्गारा भवन्ति स प्रतिहारो ऽङ्गाराणां प्रतिहृतत्वात् ।
units.english: the appearing of embers is the Pratihāra; because the embers are drawn together;

units.sanskrit: उपशमः सावशेषत्वादग्नेः । संशमो निःशेषोपशमः समाप्तिसामान्यान्निधनमेतद्रथन्तर मग्नौ प्रोतम् ।
units.english: the calming downthe fire still continuing to burn,is the Nidhana;the complete extinguishmentthe complete going out of the Fire,is the Nidhana; because both form the end of their respective processes

units.sanskrit: मन्थने ह्यग्नेर्गीयते ॥
units.english: as it is chanted at the churning of the Fire

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् रथंतरम् अग्नौ प्रोतं वेद । ब्रह्मवर्चस्य्
units.english: He who thus knows the Rathantara interwoven in Fire becomes radiant with Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: अन्नादो भवति ।
units.english: and an eater of food;

units.sanskrit: ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति । महान् कीर्त्या ।
units.english: he attains his full life, lives gloriously and becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great in fame

units.sanskrit: न प्रत्यङ्ङ् अग्निम् आचामेन् न निष्ठीवेत् ।
units.english: His observance is that he should not sip nor spit behind the Fire

units.sanskrit: स य इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: He who etc,as before

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मवर्चसी वृत्तस्वाध्यायनिमित्तं तेजो ब्रह्मवर्तसम् ।
units.english: Radiant with Brahmic glory;‘Brahmic glory is the radiance one acquires by completing the study of the Vedas;

units.sanskrit: अन्नादो दीप्ताग्निः ।
units.english: simple effulgence is mere brightness

units.sanskrit: न प्रत्यङ्ङग्नेरभिमुखो ना'चामेन्न भक्षयेत्किञ्चिन्न निष्ठीवेच्छ्लेष्मनिरसनं च न कुर्यात्तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: Eater of foodhaving keen appetiteHe should not sipeat, anythingnor spit throw out phlegmbehindie, while facingthe Fire This should be his observance End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: उपमन्त्रयते स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Approaching is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: ज्ञपयते स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: Fascinating is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: स्त्रिया सह शेते स उद्गीथः । प्रति स्त्रीं सह शेते स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: Sleeping with the woman is the Udgītha; Lying down with the woman is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: कालं गच्छति तन् निधनम् । पारं गच्छति तन् निधनम् ।
units.english: the Passing of the Time is the Nidhana; the going to the End is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् वामदेव्यं मिथुने प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Vāmadevya interwoven in the couple

units.sanskrit: उपमन्त्रयते सङ्केतं करोति प्राथम्यात्स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Approachingwhen the man makes the assignation,is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’; as both are the first steps in their processes

units.sanskrit: ज्ञपयते तोषयति स प्रस्तावः । सहशयनमेकपर्यङ्कगमनं स उद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: Fascinatingwinning overis the Prastāva Sleepinggoing to the same bedis the Udgītha; because of importance

units.sanskrit: प्रति स्रीं शयनं स्रिया अभिमुखीभावः स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: The lying down with the womanface to face,is the Pratihāra

units.sanskrit: कालं गच्छति मैथुनेन पारं समाप्तिं गच्छति तन्निधनमेतद्वामदेव्यं मिथुने प्रोतम् । वाय्वम्बुमिथुनसम्बन्धात् ॥ स य एवम् एतद् वामदेव्यं मिथुने प्रोतं वेद ।
units.english: The Passing of the time,the actual processand going to the endcompletion of the actis the NidhanaThis is the Vāmadevya Sāma interwoven with the couple;inasmuch as it is related to the couple consisting of Air and Water out of which the Vāmadevya Sāma was produced

units.sanskrit: मिथुनान् मिथुनात् प्रजायते । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति । महान् कीर्त्या ।
units.english: One who thus knows the Vāmadevya as interwoven in the couple becomes companionated, goes on from coupling to coupling, attains the full span of life, lives gloriously, becomes great in offspring and cattle, great in fame

units.sanskrit: न कांचन परिहरेत् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that ‘he should not avoid any woman’

units.sanskrit: स य इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: One who knows etc as before

units.sanskrit: मिथुनी भवत्यविधुरो भवतीत्यर्थः । मिथुनान्मिथुनात्प्रजायत इत्यमोघरेतस्त्वमुच्यते ।
units.english: Becomes companionated,ie, he never feels depressed,goes on from coupling to coupling,this indicates the infallibility of his virility

units.sanskrit: न काञ्चन काञ्चिदपि स्रियं स्वात्मतल्पप्राप्तां न परिहरेत्समागमार्थिनीम् ।
units.english: He should not avoid any woman,who has come to his bed, seeking intercourse

units.sanskrit: वामदेव्यसामोपासनाङ्गत्वेन विधानात् एतस्मादन्यत्र प्रतिषेधस्मृतयः वचनप्रामाण्याच्च धर्मावगतेर्न प्रतिषेधशास्रेणास्य विरोधः ॥
units.english: As such conduct has been enjoined here in connection with the meditation of the Vāmadevya Sāma,the Smṛti rules forbiding such intercourse should be taken as applying to occasions other than this particular one

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य त्र्योदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: उद्यन् हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The Rising Sun is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: उदितः प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: the Risen Sun is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: मध्यंदिन उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the Midday Sun is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: अपराह्णः प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Postmeridian Sun is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: अस्तं यन् निधनम् ।
units.english: the Setting sun is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् बृहद् आदित्ये प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Bṛhat Sāma interwoven in the Sun

units.sanskrit: उद्यन्सविता स हिङ्कारः प्राथम्याद्दर्शनस्य ।
units.english: The RisingSunis the syllable ‘Hin ’ as it is the first to be seen

units.sanskrit: उदितः प्रस्तावः प्रस्तवनहेतुत्वात्कर्मणाम् ।
units.english: The Risen Sun is the Prastāva; as all acts are brought about through their commencement prastavana

units.sanskrit: मध्यन्दिन उद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: The midday Sun is the Udgītha; on account of supreme importance

units.sanskrit: अपराह्नः प्रतिहारः पश्वादीनां गृहान्प्रति हरणात् ।
units.english: because cattle and other things are brought away home at that time pratiharaṇāt

units.sanskrit: यदस्तं यंस्तन्निधनं रात्रौ गृहे निधानात्प्राणिनाम् ।
units.english: because of the resting nidhanāt of all living beings in their homes at night

units.sanskrit: एतद्बृहदादित्ये प्रोतं बृहत आदित्यदैवत्यत्वात् ॥
units.english: This is the Bṛhat Sāma interwoven in the Sun; because the Sun is the deity of the Bṛhat Sāma

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् बृहद् आदित्ये प्रोतं वेद । तेजस्व्य् अन्नादो भवति ।
units.english: One who knows this Bṛhat Sāma as interwoven in the Sun becomes endowed with glory and an eater of food;

units.sanskrit: ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति । महान् कीर्त्या ।
units.english: he attains the full lifespan, lives gloriously and becomes great in offspring and cattle and great in fame

units.sanskrit: तपन्तं न निन्देत् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that he should not decry the shining Sun

units.sanskrit: स य इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: One who etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: तपन्तं न निन्देत्तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: The observance is that he should not decry the shining Sun

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य चतुर्दशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अभ्राणि संप्लवन्ते स हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The gathering of mists is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’

units.sanskrit: मेघो जायते स प्रस्तावः । वर्षति स उद्गीथः । विद्योतते स्तनयति स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: The Rising of clouds is the Prastāva The Raining is Udgītha The Lightning and Thunder are the Pratihāra

units.sanskrit: उद्गृह्णाति तन् निधनम् ।
units.english: The Ceasing is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् वैरूपं पर्जन्ये प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Vairūpya Sāma interwoven in the Cloud

units.sanskrit: अभ्राण्यब्भरणात्, मेघ उदकसेक्तृत्वात् ।
units.english: ‘Abhrāṇi’Mistsare so called because they contain water MeghaCloudis so called because it sprinkles Mehanāt

units.sanskrit: उक्तार्थमन्यत् ।
units.english: The rest has been already explained

units.sanskrit: एतद्वैरूपं नाम साम पर्जन्ये प्रोतम् ।
units.english: This is the Vairūpya Sāma interwoven in the cloud;

units.sanskrit: अनेतरूपत्वात् अभ्रादिभिः पर्जन्यस्य वैरूप्यम् ॥
units.english: because the Cloud is manifold in its manifestations, therefore it is distinct in form virūpa from the Mist and the rest

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् वैरूपं पर्जन्ये प्रोतं वेद । विरूपांश् च सुरूपंश् च पशून् अवरुन्धे । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति ।
units.english: One who thus knows this Vairūpa Sāma as interwoven in the Cloud secures illshaped as well as wellshaped cattle, attains the full span of life, lives gloriously, becomes great in offspring and cattle, and great in fame

units.sanskrit: वर्षन्तं न निन्देत् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that he should not decry it raining

units.sanskrit: विरूपांश्च सुरूपांश्चाजाविप्रभृतीन्पशूनवरुन्धे प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Illshaped and wellshapedgoat, sheep and other cattle,he securesie, obtainsthese

units.sanskrit: वर्षन्तं न निन्देत्तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: The observance is that one should not decry it raining

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य पञ्चदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: वसन्तो हिङ्कारः । ग्रीष्मः प्रस्तावः । वर्षा उद्गीथः ।
units.english: The Spring is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’; the Summer is the Prastāva; the Rainy Season is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: शरत् प्रतिहारः । हेमन्तो निधनम् ।
units.english: the Autumpis the Pratihāra; the Winter is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् वैराजम् ऋतुषु प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Vairāja Sāma interwoven in the Seasons

units.sanskrit: वसन्तो हिंङ्कारः प्राथम्यात् ।
units.english: The Spring is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: ग्रीष्मः प्रस्ताव इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: the Summer is the Prastāva; etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् वैराजम् ऋतुषु प्रोतं वेद । विराजति प्रजया । पशुभिर् ब्रह्मवर्चसेन । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति ।
units.english: One who thus knows the Vairāja as interwoven in the seasons shines with offspring, cattle and Brahmic glory, attains the whole lifespan, lives gloriously and becomes great in offspring and cattle, great in fame,His observance is that he should not decry the Seasons

units.sanskrit: एतद्वैराजमृतुषु प्रोतं वेद विराजति ऋतुवद्यथर्तव आर्तवैर्धर्मैर्विराजन्त एवं प्रजादिभिर्विद्वानित्युक्तमन्यत् ।
units.english: One who knows thus Vairāja interwoven in the seasons shineslike the seasons; that is, just as the seasons shine through the seasonal characteristics, so does the man through offspring and other things The rest is as explained before

units.sanskrit: ऋतीन्न निन्देत्तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: The observance is that one should not decry the seasons

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य षोडशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पृथिवी हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The Earth is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षं प्रस्तावः । द्यौर् उद्गीथः । दिशः प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Sky is the Prastāva; the Heaven is the Udgītha; the Quarters, are the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: समुद्रो निधनम् ।
units.english: the Ocean is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एताः शक्वर्यो लोकेषु प्रोताः ॥
units.english: These are the Śakvarīs Sāma interwoven in the Regions

units.sanskrit: पृथिवी हिङ्कार इत्यादि पूर्ववत् । शक्वर्य इति नित्यं बहुवचनं रेवत्य इव ।
units.english: The Earth is the syllable Him etc, etc as above’The name ‘Śakvaryaḥ’ is always in the Plural form; just like the name ‘Revatyaḥ’

units.sanskrit: लोकेषु प्रोताः ॥
units.english: Interwoven in the Regions

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एताः शक्वर्यो लोकेषु प्रोता वेद । लोकी भवति सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति । महान् कीर्त्या ।
units.english: One who thus knows the Śakvarīs as interwoven in the Regions becomes the owner of the Regions, attains the full lifespan, lives gloriously and becomes great with offspring and cattle, great in fame

units.sanskrit: लोकान् न निन्देत् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that he should not decry the Regions

units.sanskrit: लोकी भवति लोकफलेन युज्यत इत्यर्तः ।
units.english: Becomes the owner of the Regions; that is, becomes equipped with all that is good in the Regions

units.sanskrit: लोकान्न निन्देत्तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: The observance is that one should not decry the Regions

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य सप्तदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अजा हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Goats are the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: अवयः प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: Sheep are the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: गाव उद्गीथः ।
units.english: Cows are the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: अश्वाः प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: Horses are the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: पुरुषो निधनम् ।
units.english: Man is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एता रेवत्यः पशुषु प्रोताः ॥
units.english: These are the Revatīs Sāma interwoven in cattle

units.sanskrit: अजा हिङ्कार इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: Goats are the syllable ‘Hiṃ’ etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: पशुषु प्रोताः ॥
units.english: Interwoven in Cattle

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एता रेवत्यः पशुषु प्रोता वेद । पशुमान् भवति । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति ।
units.english: One who thus knows the Revatīs as interwoven, in cattle, becomes the owner of cattle, attains the full lifespan, lives gloriously and becomes great in offspring and cattle, great in fame

units.sanskrit: पशून् न निन्देत् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that he should not decry the Cattle

units.sanskrit: पशून्न निन्देत्तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: The observance is that he should not decry the Cattle

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्यस्याष्टादशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: लोम हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: The Hair is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’;

units.sanskrit: त्वक् प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: Wie Skin is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: मांसम् उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the Flesh is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: अस्थि प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Bone is the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: मज्जा निधनम् ।
units.english: the Marrow is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अङ्गेषु प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Yajñāyajñīya Sāma, interwoven in the parts of the Body

units.sanskrit: लोम हिङ्कारो देहावयवानां प्राथम्यात् । त्वक्प्रस्ताव आनन्तर्यात् । मांसमुद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: The Hair is the syllable ‘Hiṃ’,it being the first of the parts of the Body The Skin is the Prastāva,becaṇse it is next to the Hair The Flesh is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: अस्थि प्रतिहारः प्रतिहृतत्वात् । मज्जा निधनमान्त्यात् ।
