units.english: The Bone is the Pratihāra, because it is concentrated The Marrow is the Nidhana; because it is the last

units.sanskrit: एतद्यज्ञायज्ञीयं नाम साम देहावयववेषु प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Sāma named Yajñāyajñīya,interwoven in the parts of the Body

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अङ्गेषु प्रोतं वेद । अङ्गी भवति । नाङ्गेन विहूर्छति ।
units.english: One who thus knows the ‘Yajñāyajñīya’ as interwoven in the parts of the Body becomes equipped with limbs, is not crippled in his limbs;

units.sanskrit: ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति । महान् कीर्त्या ।
units.english: he attains the full lifespan, lives gloriously, and becomes great in offspring and cattle, great in fame

units.sanskrit: संवत्सरं मज्ज्ञो नाश्नीयात् । तद् व्रतम् । मज्ज्ञो नाश्नीयाद् इति वा ॥
units.english: His observance is that he should not eat marrows for a year,or that he should not eat marrows at all

units.sanskrit: अङ्गी भवति समग्राङ्गो भवतीत्यर्थः । नाङ्गेन हस्तपादादिना विहूर्छति न कुटिली भवति पङ्गुः कुणी वेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Becomes equipped with limbsthat is, he has all his limbs wholeIs not crippled in his limbs;ie, none of his limbsHands, feet and the rest,is crooked that is, he does not become lame or crippled in his hands

units.sanskrit: संवत्सरं संवत्सरमात्रं मज्ज्ञो मांसानि नाश्नीयान्न भक्षयेत् ।
units.english: For a yearjust for a year onlyhe should not eat marrow, ie, meat

units.sanskrit: बहुवचनं मत्स्योपलक्षणार्थम् ।
units.english: The plural form ‘marrows’ is meant to include fish also

units.sanskrit: मज्ज्ञो नाश्नीयात्सर्वदैव नाश्नीयादिति वा तद्व्रतम् ॥
units.english: Or, his observance is that he should not ever, at all times,eat marrows at all

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्यैकोनविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अग्निर् हिङ्कारः ।
units.english: Fire is the syllable Hiṃ;

units.sanskrit: वायुः प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: Air is the Prastāva;

units.sanskrit: आदित्य उद्गीथः ।
units.english: the Sun is the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: नक्षत्राणि प्रतिहारः । चन्द्रमा निधनम् ।
units.english: the Stars are the Pratihāra; the Moon is the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतद् राजनं देवतासु प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Rājana Sima interwoven in the Deities

units.sanskrit: अग्निर्हिङ्कारः प्रथमस्थानत्वात् । वायुः प्रस्ताव आनन्तर्यसामान्यात् । आदित्य उद्गीथः श्रैष्ठ्यात् । नक्षत्राणि प्रतिहारः प्रतिहृतत्वात् ।
units.english: Fire is the syllable ‘Hiṅ’; because it occupies the first position,Air is the Prastāva;because both are equally next to the preceding in their respective spheres,The Sun is Udgītha’, because of superior importance,The Stars are the Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: चन्द्रमा निधनं कर्मिणां तन्निधनात् ।
units.english: The Moon is the Nidhana; because men demoted to sacrificial acts abide there

units.sanskrit: एतद्राजनं देवतासु प्रोतं देवतानां दीप्तिमत्त्वात् ॥
units.english: This is the Rājana Sāma interwoven in the Deities; as the Deities are endowed with effulgence

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतद् राजनं देवतासु प्रोतं वेद । एतासाम् एव देवतानां सलोकतां सर्ष्टितां सायुज्यं गच्छति ।
units.english: One who thus knows the Rājana as interwoven in the Deities reaches the same regions and the same majesty as these Deities, and also absorption into them;

units.sanskrit: ज्योग् जीवति । महान् प्रजया पशुभिर् भवति । महान् कीर्त्या ।
units.english: he attains the full lifespan, lives gloriously and becomes great with offspring and cattle, great in fame

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणान् न निन्देत् । तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: His observance is that he should not decry the Brāhmaṇas,

units.sanskrit: विद्वत्फलमेतासामेवाग्न्यादीनां देवतानां सलोकतां समानलोकतां सार्ष्टितां समानर्द्धित्वं सायुज्यं समुग्भावमेकदेहदेहित्वमित्येतत्
units.english: The text mentions the reward that accrues to the man who knows this He reachesie,attains the same regionssimilar regionsand the same majestygreatnessas Fire and the other Deities;

units.sanskrit: वाशब्दो ऽत्र लुप्तो द्रष्टव्यः सलोकतां वेत्यादि ।
units.english: and also absorption into them,that is, he occupies the same body as the Deities, The term ‘or’ should be regarded as understood here;

units.sanskrit: भावनाविशेषतः फलविशेषोपपत्तेः ।
units.english: the exact character of the reward is dependent upon the nature of the disposition of the man concerned;

units.sanskrit: समुच्चयानुपपत्तेश्च ।
units.english: and a combination of all these rewards is not possible

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणान्न निन्देत्तद्व्रतम् । एते वै देवाः प्रत्यक्षं यद्ब्राह्मणाइति श्रुतेर्ब्राह्मणनिन्दा देवतानिन्दैवेति ॥
units.english: The observance is that he should not decry the Brāhmaṇas is as much as the Vedic text has distinctly declared that The Brāhmaṇas are the visible deities, the decrying of the Brāhmaṇas would mean the decrying of the Deities

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य विंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: त्रयी विद्या हिङ्कारः । त्रय इमे लोकाः स प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: The Threefold Science is the syllable these three regions are the Prāstava;

units.sanskrit: अग्निर् वायुर् आदित्यः स उद्गीथः ।
units.english: Fire, Air, and Sun are the Udgītha;

units.sanskrit: नक्षत्राणि वयांसि मरीचयः स प्रतिहारः ।
units.english: the Stars, the Birds and the Rays are Pratihāra;

units.sanskrit: सर्पा गन्धर्वाः पितरस् तन् निधनम् ।
units.english: the serpents, the Gandharvas and the Pitṛs are the Nidhana

units.sanskrit: एतत् साम सर्वस्मिन् प्रोतम् ॥
units.english: This is the Sāma interwoven in all

units.sanskrit: त्रयी विद्या हिङ्कारः । अग्न्यादिसाम्न आनन्तर्यं त्रयीविद्याया अग्न्यादिकार्यत्वश्रुतेः ।
units.english: The Threefold Science is the syllable ‘Hiṅ’;this section of the Threefold Science is dealt with immediately after the Sāma in the form of Agni and other deities, because the Veda has declared that the Threefold Science is the product of Agni and the rest

units.sanskrit: हिङ्कारः प्राथम्यात्सर्वकर्तव्यानाम् । त्रय इमे लोकास्तत्कार्यत्वादनन्तरा इति प्रस्तावः ।
units.english: This is the syllable ‘Hiṅ’, as it is the first step in the process of the performance of all one’s dutiesThese three worlds which come next, as the product of the preceding,are the Prastāva

units.sanskrit: अग्न्यादीनामुद्गीथत्वं श्रैष्ठ्यात् ।
units.english: Agnifire, and the rest are the Udgītha, on account of their superior importance

units.sanskrit: नक्षत्रादीनां प्रतिहृतत्वात्प्रतिहारत्वम् ।
units.english: The stars and the rest are the Pratihāra, because they are assembled together

units.sanskrit: सर्पादीनां धकारसामान्यान्निधनत्वमेतत्साम नामविश्षाभावात्सामसमुदायः सामशब्दः सर्वस्मिन्प्रोतम् ।
units.english: The Serpents and the rest are Nidhanabecause the letter ‘dha’ is common to the names ‘Gandharva’ and ‘Nidhana’ There being no special name for this Sāma, it is called here by the generic name ‘Sāma’;

units.sanskrit: त्रयीविद्यादिदृष्ट्या हिङ्कारादिसामभक्तय उपास्याः ।
units.english: the sense is that the syllable ‘Hiṅ’ and other constituent factors of the Sāma are to be meditated upon as the Threefold Science and the rest

units.sanskrit: अतीतेष्वपि सामोपासनेषु येषु येषु प्रोतं यद्यत्साम तद्दृष्ट्या तदुपास्यमिति ।
units.english: In fact, even in the case of all the particular Sāmas described above, wherever the Sāma is spoken of as ‘interwoven’ in certain things, what is meant is that it is in the form of these things that the Sāma should be meditated upon;

units.sanskrit: कर्माङ्गनां दृष्टिविशेषेणाज्यस्येव संस्कार्यत्वात् ॥
units.english: because the details of all acts become embellished and sanctified by what it is viewed as,just as the Butter becomes embellished and sanctified by being looked upon

units.sanskrit: स य एवम् एतत् साम सर्वस्मिन् प्रोतं वेद सर्वं ह भवति ॥ सर्वविषयसामविदः फलंसर्वं ह भवति सर्वेश्वरो भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: One who thus knows this Sāma as interoven in All, becomes all The following is the reward accruing to one who knows the Sāma as pertaining to all things He becomes all; that is, he becomes the lord of all things

units.sanskrit: निरुपचरितसर्वभावे हि दिक्स्थेभ्यो बलिप्राप्त्यनुपपत्तिः ॥
units.english: If ‘becoming all’ were taken in its literal sense and not figuratively in the sense of becoming the lord of all things, then there would be no possibility of receiving offerings from persons residing in the various quarters as described in text , below]

units.sanskrit: तद् एष श्लोकः । यानि पञ्चधा त्रीणि त्रीणि । तेभ्यो न ज्यायः परम् अन्यद् अस्ति ॥
units.english: To this effect there is this verse‘That which is fivefold, by threes and threes,there is nothing else higher than that’

units.sanskrit: तदेतस्मिन्नर्थ एष श्लोको मन्त्रो ऽप्यस्ति । यानि पञ्चधा पञ्चप्रकारेण हिङ्कारादिविभागैः प्रोक्तानि त्रीणि त्रीणि त्रयीविद्यादीनि तेभ्यः पञ्चत्रिकेभ्यो ज्यायो महत्तरं परं च व्यतिरिक्तमन्यद्वस्त्वन्तरं नास्ति
units.english: To this Sāma effect, there is this verse ie the Mantra Text,Those that have been described as fivefold,in five ways,in the form the syllable ‘Hin and the rest,by threes and threes,in the form of the ‘Threefold Science’ and the rest,than these five triads, there is nothing highergreater or loftier;

units.sanskrit: न विद्यत इत्यर्थः । तत्रैव हि सर्वस्यान्तभविः ॥
units.english: beyond these there is nothing else, that is, nothing else exists, all things being included in those same

units.sanskrit: यस् तद् वेद स वेद सर्वम् ।
units.english: One who knows this knows all;

units.sanskrit: सर्वा दिशो बलिम् अस्मै हरन्ति । सर्वम् अस्मीत्य् उपासित ।
units.english: all quarters carry offerings to himOne should meditate upon the idea that ‘ am all;’this is the observance;

units.sanskrit: तद् व्रतं तद् व्रतम् ॥
units.english: yea, thia is the observance

units.sanskrit: यस्तद्यथोक्तं सर्वात्मकं साम वेद स वेद सर्वं;
units.english: One who knows the said Sāma as constituting, all, knows all;

units.sanskrit: स सर्वज्ञो भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, he becomes omniscient

units.sanskrit: सर्वा दिशः सर्वदिक्स्था अस्मा एवंविदे बलिं भोगं हरन्ति प्रापयन्तीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: All quarters,ie persons residing in all directions,carry presentofferingsgifts of enjoymentto him

units.sanskrit: सर्वमस्मि भवामीत्येवमेतत्सामोपासीत तस्यैतदेव व्रतम् ।
units.english: ‘ am all’, am becoming all,thus should he meditate upon the Sāma; such is the observance for the said person

units.sanskrit: द्बिरुक्तिः सामोपासनसमाप्त्यर्प्था ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the treatment of the meditation of Sāma

units.sanskrit: विनर्दि साम्नो वृणे पशव्यम् इत्य् अग्नेर् उद्गीथः ।
units.english: ‘Of the Sāma, seek for what is highsounding and beneficial to cattle’,this is the song sacred to Agni;

units.sanskrit: अनिरुक्तः प्रजापतेः ।
units.english: the undefined one is sacred to Prajāpati;

units.sanskrit: निरुक्तः सोमस्य ।
units.english: the welldefined one to Soma;

units.sanskrit: मृदु श्लक्ष्णं वायोः ।
units.english: the soft and smooth is sacred to Vāyu;

units.sanskrit: श्लक्ष्णं बलवद् इन्द्रस्य । क्रौञ्चं बृहस्पतेः ।
units.english: the smooth and forcible to Indra; the heronlike is sacred to Bṛhaspati;

units.sanskrit: अपध्वान्तं वरुणस्य । तान् सर्वान् एवोपसेवेत । वारुणं त्व् एव वर्जयेत् ॥
units.english: the cracked is sacred to Varuṇa;One should practise all these; he should avoid only the one sacred to Varuṇa

units.sanskrit: सामोपासनप्रसङ्गेन गानविशेषादिसम्पदुद्गातुरुपदिश्यते । फलविशेषसम्बन्धात्ष विनर्दि विशिष्टो नर्दः स्वरविशेष ऋषभकूजितसमो ऽस्यास्तीति विनर्दि गानमिति वाक्यशेषः । तच्च साम्नः सम्बन्धि पशुभ्यो हितं पशव्यमग्नेरग्निदेवत्यं चोद्गीथ उद्गानम् ।
units.english: In course of the treatment of the Meditation of Sāma, the text is going to expound the rewards accruing to the Udgātṛ priest from the particular forms of singing;each form is connected with a definite result Highsoundingie that whose sound or pitch is particularly high, like the bellowing of the bull,‘Song’;this is what is understood, as qualified by the adjectives, ‘highsounding’ and the rest;this song is of the Sāma,ie, related to Senary and is beneficial to cattle It is sacred to Agni;ie Agni is its Deity;such is the Udgīthathe song

units.sanskrit: तदहमेवंविशिष्टं वृणे प्रर्थय इति कश्चिद्यजमान उद्गाता वा मन्यते ।
units.english: ‘Such a song seek for,ask for’so thinks a certain sacrificer himself, or his UdgātṛPriest

units.sanskrit: अनिरुक्तो ऽमुकसम इत्यविशेषितः प्रजापतेः प्रजापतिदेवत्यः स न गानविशेषः ।
units.english: Undefinednot discernible as resembling a wellknown sound;such sound is sacred to Prajāpati,Prajāpati is its deity; and as being undefined, this is not a particular form of song

units.sanskrit: आनिरुक्त्यात्प्रजापतेर्निरुक्तः स्पष्टः सोमस्य,
units.english: The welldefinedclearone is sacred to Soma;

units.sanskrit: सोमदेवत्यः स उद्गीथ इत्यर्थः । मृदु श्लक्षणं च गानं वायोर्वायुदेवत्यं तत् ।
units.english: that is, such song has Soma for its deityThe soft and smoothsongis sacred to Vāya; ie Vāyu is its deity

units.sanskrit: श्लक्ष्णं बलवच्च प्रयत्नाधिक्योपेतं चेन्द्रस्यैन्द्रं तद्गानम् ।
units.english: The smooth and forciblesong with much effort,is sacred to Indra

units.sanskrit: क्रौञ्चं क्रौञ्चपक्षिनिनादसमं बृहस्पतेर्बार्हस्पत्यं तत् ।
units.english: The herondike, what is like the sound made by the heron,is sacred to Bṛhaspati,related to Bṛhaspati

units.sanskrit: अपध्वान्तं भिन्नकांस्यस्वरसमं वरुणस्यैतद्गानम् । तान्सर्वानेवोपसेवेत प्रयुञ्जीत वारुणं त्वेवैकं वर्जयेत् ॥
units.english: The song that is crackedlike the sound made by the cracked bellmetal,is sacred to Varaṇa One should practise all these,should make use of all theseonly he should avoid that which is sacred to Varuṇa

units.sanskrit: अमृतत्वं देवेभ्य आगायानीत्य् आगायेत् । स्वधां पितृभ्य आशां मनुष्येभ्यस् तृणोदकं पशुभ्यः स्वर्गं लोकं यजमानायान्नम् आत्मन आगायानीत्य् एतानि मनसा ध्यायन्न् अप्रमत्तः स्तुवीत
units.english: ‘May sing Immortality for the Deities’thus should one sing;‘May sing Satisfaction for the Pitṛs, Hope for Men; Grass and Water for animals, the Heavenly Region for the Sacrificer, Food for myself’thus reflecting in his mind on all these, one should recite the eulogies with due care

units.sanskrit: अमृतत्वं देवेभ्य आगायानि साधयानि ।
units.english: ‘May singaccomplishImmortality for the Deities May sing Satisfaction for the Pitṛs;

units.sanskrit: स्वधां पितृभ्य आगायान्याशां मनुष्येभ्य आशां प्रार्थनां प्रार्थितमित्येतत् । तृणोदकं पशुभ्यः स्वर्गं लोकं यजमानायान्नमात्मने मह्यमागायानीत्येतानि मनसा चिन्तयन्ध्यायन्नप्रमत्तः स्वरोष्मव्यञ्जनादिभ्यः स्तुवीत
units.english: Desires, the desired thingfor men;Grass and Water for animals;the Heavenly Region for the Sacrificer;Food for myself;may sing all these!Reflecting onthinking ofall these in his mind, he should recite the eulogies, with due care,regarding the pronunciation of vowels, sibilants and consonants and so forth

units.sanskrit: सर्वे स्वरा इन्द्रस्यात्मानः ।
units.english: All vowels are the very selves of Indra;

units.sanskrit: सर्व ऊष्माणः प्रजापतेर् आत्मानः ।
units.english: all sibilants, of Prajāpati;

units.sanskrit: सर्वे स्पर्शा मृत्योर् आत्मानः ।
units.english: all Sparśa consonants, of Death

units.sanskrit: तं यदि स्वरेषूपालभेत । इन्द्रं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति वक्ष्यतीत्य् एनं ब्रूयात् ॥
units.english: If any one should reprove one regarding vowels, he should tell him this‘ have taken refuge in Indra He will answer thee’

units.sanskrit: सर्वे स्वरा अकारादय इन्द्रस्य बलकर्मणः प्राणस्या'त्मानो देहावयवस्थानीयाः सर्व ऊष्माणः शषसहादयः प्रजापतेर्विराजः कश्यपस्य वा'त्मानः । सर्वे स्पर्शाः कादयो व्यञ्जनानि मृत्योरात्मानस्तमेवंविदमुद्गातारं यदि कश्चित्स्वरेषूपालभेत
units.english: All vowelsthe letter ‘a’ and the rest,are the selveslike the limbs of the bodyof Indra,ie of the Lifebreath as tending to strength;all sibilants, the letters ‘śa’, ‘ṣa’, ‘sa’, ‘ha’ and the rest,are the selves of Prajāpati,ie of Virāṭ or Kaśyapa;all Sparśa consonants‘Ka’ and the other consonants,are the selves of Death

units.sanskrit: स्वरस्त्वया दुष्टः प्रयुक्त इत्येवमुपालब्ध इन्द्रं प्राणमीश्वरं शरणमाश्रयं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स्वरान् प्रयुञ्जानो ऽहं स इन्द्रो यत्तव वक्तव्यं त्वा त्वां प्रति वक्ष्यति स एव देव उत्तरं दास्यतीत्येनं ब्रूयात् ॥
units.english: When the Udgātṛ Priest knows this,if some one were to reprove him regarding vowelssaying ‘thou hast pronounced this vowel incorrectly’,he should say in answer‘ have taken refugeshelterin Indrathe Lifebreath, the God,while using the vowels; that same Indra will say all that has to be said;

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्य् एनम् ऊष्मासूपालभेत । प्रजापतिं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति पेक्ष्यतीत्य् एनं ब्रूयात् ।
units.english: ie he will give thee the answer to what thou hast told me’ If any one were to reprove him regarding the sibilants, he should say to him this‘ have taken refuge in Prajāpati;

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्य् एनं स्पर्शेषूपालभेत । मृत्युं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति धक्ष्यतीत्य् एनं ब्रूयात् ॥
units.english: he will smash thee’ If any one were to reprove him regarding the sparśa consonants, he should say to him this‘ have taken refuge in Death, he will scorch thee’

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्येनमूष्मसु तथैवोपालभेत प्रजापतिं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रतिपेक्ष्यति सञ्चूर्णयिष्यतीत्येनं ब्रूयात् ।
units.english: Similarly, if anyone were to reprove him regarding the sibilants, he should say to him have taken refuge in Prajāpati;

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्येनं स्पर्शेषूपालभेत मृत्युं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति धक्ष्यति भस्मीकरिष्यतीत्येनं ब्रूयात् ॥
units.english: He will smash thee,reduce thee to powder’ If anyone were to reprove him regarding the sparśa consonants,he should say to him ‘ have taken refuge in Death, He will scorch theereduce thee to ashes’

units.sanskrit: सर्वे स्वरा घोषवन्तो बलवन्तो वक्तव्या इन्द्रे बलं ददानीति । सर्व ऊष्माणो ऽग्रस्ता अनिरस्ता विवृता वक्तव्याः प्रजापतेर् आत्मानं परिददानीति । सर्वे स्पर्शा लेशेनानभिनिहिता वक्तव्या मृत्योर् आत्मानं परिहराणीति ॥
units.english: All vowels should be pronounced with loudness and strength with the idea that ‘May impart strength to Indra’;all sibilants should be pronounced as wellopenedout, neither swallowed nor thrown out, with the idea ‘May surrender myself to Prajāpati’; all Sparśaconsonants should be pronounced slowly, without jumbling with the idea ‘May withdraw myself from Death’

units.sanskrit: यत इन्द्राद्यात्मानः स्वरादयो ऽतः सर्वे स्वरा घोषवन्तो बलवन्तो वक्तव्याः ।
units.english: Inasmuch as the vowels and the letters are the selves of Indra and other Deities,all Vowels should be pronounced with loudness and strength;

units.sanskrit: तथाहमिन्द्रे बलं ददानि बलमादधानीति ।
units.english: the idea in the mind being ‘May impart strength to Indra’

units.sanskrit: तथा सर्व ऊष्माणो ऽग्रस्ता अन्तरप्रवेशिता अनिरस्ता बहिरप्रक्षिप्ता विवृता विवृतप्रयत्नोपेताः प्रजापतेरात्मानं परिददानि प्रयच्छानीति सर्वे स्पर्शा लेशेन शनकैरनभिनिहिता अनभिनिक्षिप्ता वक्तव्या मृत्योरात्मानं बालानिव शनकैः परिहरन् मृत्योरात्मानं परिहराणीति ॥
units.english: Similarly all sibilants should be pronounced as wellopened out,ie with that effort which is technically called ‘Vivṛta’, ‘opened out’,as neither swallowedkept withinnor thrown out,sent out; with the idea ‘May surrender myself give myself upto Prajāpati,All Sparśaconsonants should be pronounced slowlygentlywithout jumblingwithout crowding them togetherwith the idea‘May withdraw myself from Death’gently, as people withdraw boys out of the water

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि द्वितीयाध्यायस्य द्वाविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of the Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: त्रयो धर्मस्कन्धाः । यज्ञो ऽध्ययनं दानम् इति प्रथमः ।
units.english: There are three branches of Duty Sacrifice, Study and Charityconstitute the first;

units.sanskrit: तप एव द्वितीयः ।
units.english: Austerity itself is the second;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचार्याचार्यकुलवासी तृतीयो ऽत्यन्तम् आत्मानम् आचार्यकुले ऽवसादयन् ।
units.english: the Religious Student resident in the teacher’s house, constantly mertifying himself in the teacher’s house, is the third

units.sanskrit: सर्व एते पुण्यलोका भवन्ति ।
units.english: All these attain the Blessed Regions;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मसंस्थो ऽमृतत्वम् एति ॥
units.english: one who rests firmly in Brahman attains immortality

units.sanskrit: ओङ्कारस्योपासनविध्यर्थं त्रयो धर्मस्कन्धा इत्याद्यारभ्यते ।
units.english: With a view to completing the injunction of meditation of the syllable ‘Om’, the Text proceeds with the next section, beginning with the words ‘There are three branches of Duty’

units.sanskrit: नैवं मनतव्यं सामावयवभूतस्यैवोद्गीथादिलक्षणस्योङ्कारस्योपासनात्फलं प्राप्यत इति ।
units.english: It should not be thought that ‘the final reward is obtained by meditating upon the syllable Om, in the form of Udgītha and other constituent factors of Sāma as described in the foregoing sections’

units.sanskrit: किं तर्हि?यत्सर्वैरपि सामोपासनैः कर्मभिश्चाप्राप्यं तत्फलममृतत्वं केवलादोङ्कारोपासनात्प्राप्यत इति ।
units.english: On the contrary, it is by meditating upon the syllable Om purely by itself that one obtains the final reward Immortality, which cannot be attained by allthe meditations of Sāma or by other ritualistic acts

units.sanskrit: तत्स्तुत्यर्थं सामप्रकरणे तदुपन्यासः ।
units.english: It has, however, been introduced in the present context dealing with Sāma, for the purpose of eulogising it

units.sanskrit: त्रयस्रिसंख्याका धर्मस्य स्कन्धा धर्मस्कन्धाः धर्मविबागा इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: ThreeThree in numberare the branches of Duty, ie Divisions of Duty

units.sanskrit: के त इत्याह यज्ञो ऽग्निहोत्रादिः । अध्ययनं सनियमस्य ऋगादेरभ्यासः ।
units.english: ‘What are they?’Answer Ia Sacrifice,in the form of Agnihotra and other rites,b Study,the careful reading of the Ṛk and other Vedas, along with all the rules and regulations

units.sanskrit: दानं बहिर्वेदि यथाशक्तिद्रव्यसंविभागो भिक्षमाणेभ्यः ।
units.english: c Charity making gifts outside the sacrificial altar, i e distribution of wealth according to one’s resources among persons seeking for it

units.sanskrit: इत्येष प्रथमो धर्मस्कन्धः । गृहस्थसमवेतत्वात्तन्निर्वर्तकेन गृहस्थेन निर्दिश्यते प्रथम एक इत्यर्थो द्वितीयतृतीयश्रवणान्ना'द्यार्थः ।
units.english: These three constitute the first branch of Duty, the meaning of the second and the third, and it does not mean that it is the ‘first’ in the sense of initial step; in fact, the duties herein mentioned are all such as appertain to the Householder, and thus the Householder, as fulfilling these duties, serves to indicate the first Branch \ of Duty

units.sanskrit: तप एव द्वितीयस्तप इति कृच्छ्रचान्द्रायणादि तद्वांस्तापसः परिव्राड्वा न ब्रह्मसंस्थ आश्रमधर्ममात्रसंस्थो;
units.english: the Cāndrāyaṇa and other penances; one who keeps all these is the Tāpasa, Ascetic, or the Wandering Mendicant who has merely just reached the final lifestage, but has not yet rested firmly in Brahman;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मसंस्थस्य त्वमृतत्वश्रवणात् ।
units.english: that such is the sense is indicated by the separate mention of ‘one who rests firmly in Brahman

units.sanskrit: द्वितीयो धर्मस्कन्धः ।
units.english: This is the second Branch of Duty represented by the Ascetic

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचार्याचार्यकुले वस्तुं शीलमस्येत्याचार्यकुलवासी । अत्यन्तं यावज्जीवमात्मानं नियमैराचार्यकुले ऽवसादयन्क्षपयन्देहं तृतीयो धर्मस्कन्धः ।
units.english: Answer IIIThe Religious Student resident in the Teacher’s House,ie one who is habitually residing with the Teacher,constantlyie throughout his life,mortifying himselfie crushing his body by means of fasts and penances This is the third Branch of knowledge

units.sanskrit: अत्यन्तमित्यादिविशेषणान्नैष्ठिक इति गम्यते ।
units.english: The qualification ‘constantly’ indicates that this stage is represented by the lifelong Religious Student;

units.sanskrit: उपकुर्वाणस्य स्वाध्यायग्रहणार्थत्वान्न पुण्यलोकत्वं ब्रह्मचर्येण ।
units.english: as for the ordinary Religious Student, his studentship is for the definite purpose of studying the Veda, and hence such studentship could not take one to the ‘Sacred Regions’

units.sanskrit: सर्व एते त्रयो ऽप्याश्रमिणो यथोक्तैर्धर्मैः पुण्यलोका भवन्ति ।
units.english: All these three kinds of personscarrying on the prescribed duties in their respective lifestages of the Householder, the Ascetic and the Lifelong Religious Student attain the Blessed Regions

units.sanskrit: पुण्यो लोको येषां त इमे पुण्यलोका आश्रमिणो भवन्ति ।
units.english: The meaning is that the persons carrying on the duties of the lifestages come to be such as enter the Blessed Regions

units.sanskrit: अवशिष्टस्त्वनुक्तः परिव्राड्ब्रह्मसंस्थो ब्रह्मणि सम्यक्स्थितः सो ऽमृतत्वं पुण्यलोकविलक्षणममरणभावमात्यन्तिकमेति ना'पेक्षिकं देवाद्यमृतत्ववत्
units.english: The one class of persons that remains unnamed is the Wandering Mendicant, the Renunciate, the Sanyāsī who is here indicated by the term ‘one who rests in Brahman,’ie, one who rests firmly in Brahman;he attains Immortality which is entirely distinct from the said ‘Sacred Regions’, it stands for absolute cessation of death; this cessation of death is absolute not relative, like the ‘Immortality’ of the Deities;

units.sanskrit: पुण्यलोकात्पृयगमृतत्वस्य विभागकरणात् ।
units.english: that this is so is clearly indicated by the fact that it has been declared to be entirely distinct from the ‘Sacred Regions’

units.sanskrit: यदि च पुम्यलोकातिशयमात्रममृतत्वमभविष्यत्ततः पुण्यलोकत्वाद्विभक्तं नावक्ष्यत् ।
units.english: If ‘Immortality were only a higher degree of Blessed Regions,’ then the Text would not have spoken of it as some thing distinct from the Blessed Regions

units.sanskrit: विभक्तेपदेशाच्चा'त्यन्तिकममृतत्वमिति गम्यते ।
units.english: Thus, because it has been spoken of as clearly distinguished from the ‘Blessed Regions’, it follows that what is meant is Absolute Immortallity

units.sanskrit: अत्र चाऽश्रमधर्मफलोपन्यासः प्रणवसेवास्तुत्यर्थं न तत्फलविध्यर्थम् । स्तुतये च प्रवमसेवाया आश्रमधर्मफलविधये चेति हि भिद्येत वाक्यम् ।
units.english: The introduction, in the present context, of the subject of the reward of the fulfilment of the Duties of the Lifestages is meant to eulogise the meditation of the syllable ‘Om’ and it is not meant to mention the rewards that actually follow from the said fulfilment

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्स्मृतिसिद्धाश्रमफलानुवादेन प्रणवसेवाफलममृतत्वं ब्रुवन्प्रणवसेवां स्तौति ।
units.english: Hence the conclusion is that when the text speaks of Immortality as the reward of meditating on ‘Om’, with reference to the duties of the Lifestages already known through ten Smṛtitexts,it only glorifies the meditation of ‘Om’

units.sanskrit: यथा पूर्णवर्मणः सेवा भक्तपरिधानमात्रफला राजवर्मणस्तु सेवा राज्यतुल्यफलेति तद्वत् ।
units.english: This is similar to the case of such an assertion as ‘Service under Pūrṇavarman brings only food and clothing, while that under Rājavarman brings rewards equal to kingship’

units.sanskrit: प्रणवश्च तत्सत्यं परं ब्रह्म तत्प्रतीकत्वात् । एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम् इत्याद्याम्नायात्काठके युक्तं तत्सेवातो ऽमृतत्वम् ।
units.english: The syllable ‘Om’ really is the ‘true the Highest Brahman, being, as it is, the representative image, name of this latter,as declared in the KathaUpaniṣad‘This syllable indeed is the Brahman, verily this syllable is the Highest’, hence it is only right that Immortality should be the reward of meditating upon it

units.sanskrit: चतुर्णामधिकृतत्वाविशेषात् ।
units.english: in fact, for the Wandering Mendicant also

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मसंस्थत्वे ऽप्रतिषेधाच्च । स्वकर्मच्छिद्रे च ब्रह्मसंस्थतायां सामर्ध्योपपत्तेः ।
units.english: and that it is quite within the capacity of all these persons to ‘rest firmly in Brahman’ ie meditate on ‘Om’, which represents Brahman during the intervals of the performance of their duties relating to their respective lifestages;nor is the connotation of the term ‘resting firmly in Brāhman’ rigidly restricted by convention to the Wandering Mendicant only;

units.sanskrit: न च यववराहादिशब्दवद्ब्रह्मसंस्थशब्दः परिव्राजके रूढः ।
units.english: like such ordinary words as ‘Barley, Boar’ and the like;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणि संस्थितिनिमित्तमुपादाय प्रवृत्तत्वात् ।
units.english: as its use is based entirely upon the fact of ‘resting in Brahman’ which is what it literally connotes;

units.sanskrit: न हि रूढिशब्दा निमित्तमुपाददते ।
units.english: while words that have their use dependent entirely upon convention do not have their use dependent upon any such connotation of the term, etymologically

units.sanskrit: सर्वेषां च ब्रह्मणि स्थितिरुपपद्यते ।
units.english: Then again, it is possible for all men to ‘rest in Brahman’

units.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र निमित्तमस्ति ब्रह्मणि संस्थितिस्तस्य तस्य निमित्तवतो वाचकं सन्तं ब्रह्मसंस्थशब्दं परिव्राडेकविषये संकोच कारणाभावान्निरोद्धुम
units.english: Thus then wherever this basis of the use of the term, ‘resting firmly in Brahman is present,every one such person comes under the connotation of the term ‘firmly resting in Brahman’, and there is no reason for narrowing its connotation to the Wandering Mendicant alone;

units.sanskrit: युक्तम् ।
units.english: and hence it cannot be right to so restrict it

units.sanskrit: न च पारिव्राज्याश्रमधर्ममात्रेणामृतत्वम् ।
units.english: Further, Immortality cannot follow merely from entering into the lifestage of the Wandering Mendicant;

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानानर्थक्यप्रसङ्गात् । पारिव्राज्यधर्मयुक्तमेव ज्ञानममृतत्वसाधनमिति चेन्न ।
units.english: It might be argued that ‘what leads to Immortality is True Knowledge as accompanied by the life of the Wandering MendicantBut that cannot be right;

units.sanskrit: आश्रमधर्मत्वाविशेषात् ।
units.english: because the duties relating to the other three lifestages are as important ‘duties’ as those relating to that of the Wandering Mendicant;

units.sanskrit: धर्मो वा ज्ञानविशिष्टो ऽमृतत्वसाधनमित्येदपि सर्वाश्रमधर्माणामविशिष्टम् ।
units.english: hence if Duty coupled with True Knowledge be what brings Immortality, then that also applies equally to the Duties of all the lifestages not to those of the Wandering Mendicant only

units.sanskrit: न च वचनमस्ति परिव्राजकस्यैव ब्रह्मसंस्थस्य मोक्षो नान्येषामिति ।
units.english: Nor is there any direct declaration to the effect that Final Liberation comes only to the Wandering Mendicant resting firmly in Brahman, and not to others

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानान्मोक्ष इति च सर्वोपनिषदां सिद्धान्तः तस्माद्य एव ब्रह्मसंस्थः स्वाश्रमविहितकर्मवतां सो ऽमृतत्वमेतीति ।
units.english: In fact the thesis of all the Upaniṣads is that Final Liberation follows from True Knowledge Hence the meaning of the text must be that, from among persons duly performing the duties of their own lifestages, if any one ‘rests firmly in Brahman’, he attains Immortality

units.sanskrit: तच्च निमित्तं न शास्रकृतम् ।
units.english: This interpretation is not right;

units.sanskrit: सर्वप्राणिषु दर्शनात् । सदेकमेवाद्वितीयंआत्मैवेदं सर्वंब्रह्मैवेदं सर्वम् इतिशास्रजन्यः प्रत्ययो विद्यारूपः स्वाभाविकं क्रियाकारकफलभेदप्रत्ययं कर्मविधिनिमित्तमनुपमृद्य न जायते । भेदाभेदप्रत्यययोर्विरोधात् ।
units.english: without a record’, ‘All this is Self alone’, ‘All this is Brahman alone and it does not appear until it has set aside all those common notions of Action, Actor and Result on which the Injunctions of Action are based; the reason for this is that there is complete incompatibility between the notion of diversity on which all Action rests and the notion of Nodifference Onenessupon which True Knowledge rests

units.sanskrit: न हि तैमिरिकद्विचन्द्रादिभेदप्रत्ययमनुपमृद्य तिमिरापगमे चन्द्राद्येकत्वप्रत्यय उपजायते ।
units.english: For instance, until the notion of diversity involved in the perception of ‘two noons’ due to darkness has been removed, there does not appear, even on the disappearance of darkness, the notion of the ‘one Moon’

units.sanskrit: विद्याविद्याप्रत्यययोर्विरोधात् ।
units.english: And the reason for this lies in the fact that there is incompatibility between the idea based upon Knowledge and that based upon Ignorance

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति यं भेदप्रत्ययमुपादाय कर्मविधयः प्रवृताः स यस्योपमर्दितः सदेकमेवाद्वितीयं तत्सत्यं विकारभेदो ऽनृतमित्येतद्वाक्यप्रमाणजनितेनैकत्वप्रत्ययेन स सर्वकर्मभ्यो निवृत्तो निमित्तनिवृत्ते,
units.english: Such being the case, when the injunctions of Action have proceeded on the basis of the notion of diversity,it is only when for a certain person this notion of diversity has been set aside by the notion of unity brought about by the force of such texts as ‘One alone without a second’, ‘That alone is real, all diversity of modifications is unreal’,that such a person desists from all Action, for the reason that the very basis of Action has ceased to exist;

units.sanskrit: स च निवृत्तकर्मा ब्रह्मसंस्थ उच्यते,
units.english: and it is only such a person who has thus desisted from all activity who is said to ‘rest firmly in Brahman’;

units.sanskrit: स च परिव्राडेवान्यस्यासम्भवात् ।
units.english: and such a person can be only the Wandering Mendicant, Renunciate;

units.sanskrit: अन्यो ह्यनिवृत्तभेदप्रत्ययः सो ऽन्यत्पश्यञ्शृण्वन्मन्वानो विजानन्निदं कृत्वेदं प्राप्नुयामिति हि मन्यते ।
units.english: Another person, whose notions of diversity have not ceased, always sees, hears, thinks of and cognises things as different from himself and diverse, and always thinks in such terms as ‘Having done this act, shall acquire such and such a thing’;

units.sanskrit: तस्यैवं कुर्वतो न ब्रह्मसंस्थता ।
units.english: and certainly one who thinks thus cannot be said to ‘rest firmly in Brahman’;

units.sanskrit: वाचारम्भणमात्रविकारानृताभिसन्धिप्रत्ययत्वात् ।
units.english: because his ideas are all false and wrong as pertaining to unrealities which owe their existence to mere modifications of speech

units.sanskrit: न चासत्यमित्युपर्दिते भेदप्रत्यये सत्यमिदमनेन कर्तव्यं मयेति प्रमाणप्रमेयबुद्धिरुपपद्यते । आकाश इव तलमलबुद्धिर्विवेकिनः ।
units.english: When the notion of diversity has been set aside as false, there is no possibility of any such notions of means and objects of cognition as are involved in ideas like ‘this is true’, ‘this should be done by him’ or ‘by me jtst as for a man who is wise and knows the real nature of the’sky, there is no possibility of the idea that ‘the sky is dirty’

units.sanskrit: उपमर्दिते ऽपि भेदप्रत्यये कर्मभ्यो न निवर्तते चेत्प्रागिव भेदप्रत्ययोपमर्दनादेकत्वप्रत्ययविधायकं वाक्यमप्रमाणीकृतं स्यात् ।
units.english: If, even on the setting aside of the notion of diversity, a man were not to desist from Action and were to continue to act just as before the setting aside of the notions of diversitythen the text laying down the idea of Unity would become falsified;

units.sanskrit: अभक्ष्यभक्षणादिप्रतिषेधवाक्यानां प्रामाण्यवद्युक्तमेकत्ववाक्यस्यापि प्रामाण्यम् । सर्वोपनिषदां तत्परत्वात् ।
units.english: and yet, the text declaring Unity must be regarded as valid and true, just like the texts prohibiting the eating of improper food and such acts;because all the Upaniṣads bear testimony to that Unity

units.sanskrit: कर्मविधीनामप्रामाण अयप्रसङ्ग इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: It might be argued that Under the above explanation the Vedic Injunctions of Action become invalidated

units.sanskrit: अनुपमर्दितभेदप्रत्ययवत्पुरुषविषये प्रामाण्योपपत्तेः स्वप्नादिप्रत्यय इव प्राक्प्रबोधात् ।
units.english: the said injunctions would still continue to be valid, in relation to the man whose notions of diversity have not ceased; just as the cognition during dream is quite real before waking

units.sanskrit: विवेकिनामकरणात्कर्मविधिप्रामाण्योच्छेद इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: But the very fact that discriminating wise men would not perform the acts enjoined would strike at the very root of the validity of the injunctions of those acts Not so;

units.sanskrit: काम्यविध्यनुच्छेददर्शनात् ।
units.english: because we do not see any such invalidation of the injunctions of prospective Act’s;

units.sanskrit: न हि कामात्मता न प्रशस्तेत्येवंविज्ञानवद्भिः काम्यानि कर्माणि नानुष्ठीयन्त इति काम्यकर्मविधय उच्छिद्यन्ते ऽनुष्ठीयन्त एव कामिभिरिति
units.english: and these are not performed by certain wise persons who entertain no such desire on the strength of such texts as ‘This hankering after desires is not to be commended’ and yet this nonperformance by these men does not invalidate the injunctions of those Prospective Acts;

units.sanskrit: तथा ब्रह्मसंस्थैर्ब्रह्मविद्भिर्नानुष्ठीयन्ते कर्माणीति न तद्विधय उच्छिद्यन्ते ऽब्रह्मविद्भिरनुष्ठीयन्त एवेति ।
units.english: Similarly, if actions are not performed by those ‘resting in Brahman’ and knowing Brahman,that docs not invalidate the injunctions of the actions;

units.sanskrit: परिव्रादकानां भिक्षाचरणादिवदुत्पन्नैकत्वप्रत्ययानामपि गृहस्थादीनामग्निहोत्रादिकर्मानिवृत्तिरिति चेन्न ।
units.english: Says the opponentAccording to you also even for Wandering Mendicants, there is no cessation of such activities as are involved in Begging for Food and the like;in the same manner for the Householder and persons in the other lifestageseven after they have acquired the knowledge of Unity, there heed be no cessation of such acts as the Agnihotra and the like

units.sanskrit: प्रामाण्यचिन्तायां पुरुषप्रवृत्तेरदृष्टान्तत्वात् ।
units.english: because when we are considering the validity of certain sources of knowledge, the citing of an instance of human activity cannot prove anything

units.sanskrit: न हि नाभिचरेदिति प्रतिषिद्धमप्यभिचरमं कश्चित्कुर्वन्दृष्ट इति शत्रौ द्वेषरहितेनापि विवेकिनाभिचरणं क्रियते ।
units.english: For example, though the act of killing has been prohibited by the text ‘One should not encompass the death of any man’,the mere fact of some one having been found to have done the Killing does not lead the wise man who has no hatred for any body to do the act of killing merely on the strength of the example of the man who has been found to have done the killing

units.sanskrit: न च कर्मविधिप्रवृत्तिनिमित्ते भेदप्रत्यये बाधिते ऽग्निहोत्रादौ प्रवर्तकं निमित्तमस्ति, परिव्राजकस्येव भिक्षाचरणादौ बुभुक्षादि प्रवर्तकम् ।
units.english: In fact, when the notion of diversity which is the very basis of the injunction of actions, has been set aside for the wise man, there is nothing to urge the man to the performance of the Agnihotra and such acts;in the case of the Renunciate begging for food, the necessary urge comes from hunger and such other bodily needs

units.sanskrit: इहाप्यकरणे प्रत्यवायभयं प्रवर्तकमिति चेत् । न ।
units.english: In the case of the Agnihotra also, there would be the urge coming from the fear of sin involved in the nonperformance of a prescribed act Nor so, we reply

units.sanskrit: भेदप्रत्ययवतो ऽधिकृतत्वात् ।
units.english: Because the injunction of the said acts concerns and is applicable to only such persons as are still tied to the notions of diversity;

units.sanskrit: भेदप्रत्ययवाननुपमर्दितभेदबुद्धिर्विद्यया यः स कर्मण्यधिकृत इत्यवोचाम ।
units.english: we have already explained that only such persons are entitled to the performance of Actions as are still tied to the notions of diversity, which notions they have not yet got rid of;

units.sanskrit: यो ह्यधिकृतः कर्मणि तस्य तदकरमे प्रत्यवायो न निवृत्ताधिकारस्य गृहस्थस्येव ब्रह्मचारिणो विशेषधर्माननुष्ठाने ।
units.english: and it is only when a man is entitled to the performance of an act that its nonperformance by him entails sin, and not when the man has ceased to be so entitled; for example, the Householder does not incur sin by the nonperformance of the duties laid down specifically for the Religious Student

units.sanskrit: एवं तर्हि सर्वः स्वाश्रमस्थ उत्पन्नेकत्वप्रत्ययः परिव्राडिति चेत् । न । स्वस्वामित्वभेदबुद्ध्यनिवृत्तेः ।
units.english: If that be so, then each and every man, in his own particular lifestage, could be a Renunciate as soon as the notion of Unity would dawn upon him Certainly not;

units.sanskrit: कर्मार्थत्वाच्चेतराश्रमाणाम् । अथ कर्म कुर्वीयैति श्रुतेः । तस्मात्स्वस्वामित्वाभावाद्भिक्षुरेक एव परिव्राट् ।
units.english: and that it so persists is indicated by the very nature of those lifestages, which are meant for the performance of acts, as is clear from such Vedic texts as‘May we perform acts’ and the like

units.sanskrit: न गृहस्थादिः ।
units.english: not so the Householder and other persons

units.sanskrit: एकत्वप्रत्ययविधिजनितेन प्रत्ययेन विधिनिमित्तभेदप्रत्ययस्योपमर्दितत्वाद्यमनियमाद्यनुपपत्तिः परिव्राजकस्येति चेत् । न । बुभुक्षादिनैकत्वप्रत्ययात्प्राच्यावितस्योपपत्तेर्निवृत्त्यर्थत्वात् ।
units.english: When the injunction of the notion of Unity has brought about this notion of Unity, it has ex hypothesi set aside the notion of diversity based upon the injunctions of actions,and as a necessary consequence of this, there can be no possibility of such acts for the Wandering Mendicant as the keeping of observances and restraints etc

units.sanskrit: न च प्रतिषिद्धसेवाप्राप्तिः ।
units.english: prescribed for him Not so, we reply

units.sanskrit: एकत्वप्रत्ययोत्पत्तेः प्रागेव प्रतिषिद्धत्वात् ।
units.english: because the prohibition relates to the man before he has realised Unity

units.sanskrit: न हि रात्रौ कूपे कण्टके वा पतित उदिते ऽपि सवितरि पतति तस्मिन्नेव ।
units.english: Because a man has fallen into the well, or in a thornthicket at night,it does not follow that he should fall in it even after sunrise

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्सिद्धं निवृत्तकर्मा भिक्षुक एव ब्रह्मसंस्थ इति ।
units.english: From all this it follows that the only person who can be regarded as ‘resting in Brahman’ is the Renunciate, the Wandering Mendicant, who has turned his back upon all Actions

units.sanskrit: यत्पुनरुक्तं सर्वेषां ज्ञानवर्जितानां पुण्यलोकतेति । सत्यमेतत् ।
units.english: It has been argued by the Vṛttikāra that the blessed regions are for all persons, even those who are devoid of True Knowledge;this is quite true;

units.sanskrit: यच्चोक्तं तपःशब्देन परिव्राडप्युक्त इति ।
units.english: but it is not true that the term Austerity includes the Wandering Mendicant also

units.sanskrit: कस्मात् । परिव्राजकस्यैव ब्रह्मसंस्थतासम्भवात् । स एव ह्यवशेषित इत्यवोचाम ।
units.english: WhyBecause the character of ‘resting in Brahman’ can belong to the Wandering Mendicant only, as it is he alone who remains unmentioned in the text so far;

units.sanskrit: एकत्वविज्ञानवतो ऽग्निहोत्रादिवत्तपोनिवृत्तेश्च । भेदबुद्धिमत एव हि तपःकर्तव्यता स्यात् ।
units.english: Another reason for this lies in the fact that, for the man who has attained the Knowledge of Unity, Austerity also ceases; just like Agnihotra and other acts

units.sanskrit: एतेन कर्मच्छिद्रे ब्रह्मसंस्थतासामर्थ्यं अप्रतिषेधश्च प्रत्युक्तः । तथा ज्ञानवानेव निवृत्तकर्मा परिव्राडिति ज्ञानवैयर्थ्यं प्रत्युक्तम् ।
units.english: This same reasoning also serves to set aside the views that a the resting in Brahman may appear during the intervals of ritualistic performance, and b that there is no exclusion by any Vedic Text of the possibility of resting in Brahman for persons other than Wandering Mendicants Our view is that it is only when the man has attained True Knowledge that, on desisting from all activity, he can become a Wandering Mendicant;and this disposes of the argument urged against us that under our view the acquiring of knowledge becomes entirely futile

units.sanskrit: यत्पुनरुक्तं यववराहादिशब्दवत्परिव्राजके न रूढो ब्रह्मसंस्थशब्द इति तत्परिहृतम् । तस्यैव ब्रह्मसंस्थतासम्भवान्नान्यस्येति ।
units.english: Then again, it has been argued that like the terms ‘barley’ find ‘boar’, the term ‘resting in Brahman’ has not got its connotation restricted by convention, to the Wandering Mendicant onlyThis has been already answered by us, by proving that the character of ‘resting in Brahman’ can possibly belong only to the Wandering Mendicant, not to any one else

units.sanskrit: यत्पुनरुक्तं रूढशब्दा निमित्तं नोपाददत इति ।
units.english: It has been argued that words whose connotation is fixed by convention do not depend upon any other considerations as those of etymology and the like

units.sanskrit: तन्न ।
units.english: But that is not right

units.sanskrit: गृहस्थतक्षपरिव्राजकादिशब्ददर्शनात् । गृहस्थितिपारिव्राज्यतक्षणादिनिमित्तोपादाना अपि गृहस्थपरिव्राजकाश्रमिविशेषे विशिष्टजातिमति च तक्षेति रूढा दृश्यन्ते शब्दाः ।
units.english: Because we find many such words as a ‘Householder’ Gṛhastha, b ‘Woodcutter’ Takṣā c ‘Wandering Mendicant’ Parivrājaka and the like; as a matter of fact, even all these terms have their connotations dependent upon a the act of living in the House, b the act of woodcutting, and c the act of wandering about in search of food which acts are etymologically signified by the terms;

units.sanskrit: न यत्र यत्र तानि निमित्तानि तत्र तत्र वर्तन्ते ।
units.english: But it does not follow from this that those terms are applicable anywhere and everywhere where the said conditions may be present ;

units.sanskrit: प्रसिद्ध्यभावात् ।
units.english: because such is not the recognised connotation of the terms

units.sanskrit: तथेहापि ब्रह्मसंस्थशब्दो निवृत्तसर्वकर्मतत्साधनपरिव्राडेकविषये ऽत्याश्रमिणि परमहंसाख्ये वृत्त इह भवितुमर्हति ।
units.english: Similarly in the case in question also, the term ‘resting in Brahman’ can, in the present context, have its connotation restricted to the person who has desisted from all actions and their agencies and has become a Wandering Mendicant, ie the Renunciate who has entered upon the final lifestage, and is technically called ‘Paramahaṃsa’

units.sanskrit: मुख्यामृतत्वफलश्रवणात् ।
units.english: That this is so is indicated by the mention of the principal reward of Immortality accruing as to him

units.sanskrit: अतश्चेदमेवैकं वेदोक्तं पारिव्राज्यम् । न यज्ञोपवीतत्रिदण्डकमण्डल्वादिपरिग्रह इति ।
units.english: From all this it follows that it is this ‘WanderingMendicancy’ that is meant by the Veda as leading to Immortality, and not that in which people take to the Sacrificial Thread, the TripleStick, the WaterPot and the rest;

units.sanskrit: मुण्डो ऽपरिग्रहो ऽसङ्गैति श्रुतिःअत्याक्षमिब्यः परमं पवित्रम् इत्यादि च श्वेताश्वतरीये । निःस्तुतिर्निर्नमस्कारैत्यादिस्मृतिभ्यश्च ।
units.english: that this is so is also shown by such Vedic texts as With shaven head, with no belongings and no attachment etc To the same end there are such Vedic Texts as the following in the ŚvetāśvataraUpaniṣad ‘The Highest sacred place is for those who are above the ordinary lifestages,’and in such Smṛti Texts as ‘Without praise, without obeisances, etc’;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्कर्म न कुर्वन्ति यतयः पारदर्शिनः । तस्मादलिङ्गो धर्मज्ञो ऽव्यक्तलिङ्गैत्यादिस्मृतिभ्यश्च ।
units.english: so also in such SmṛtiTexts as‘It is for this reason that Renunciates, seeing through the end of things, do not perform actions’‘Hence one knowing Dharma, should be without differentiating marks, or with unobtrusive marks’, etc, etc,

units.sanskrit: यत्तु सांख्यैः कर्मत्यागो ऽभ्युपगम्यते । क्रियाकारकफलभेदबुद्धेः सत्यत्वाभ्युपगमात् तन्मृषा ।
units.english: The ‘renunciation of Action’ which is propounded by the Sāṅkhyas is wrong inasmuch as they admit the reality of such distinctions as between ‘Action’, ‘Active Agency’ and ‘Results’

units.sanskrit: यच्च बौद्धैः शून्यताभ्युपगमादकर्तृत्वमभ्युपगम्यते । तदप्यसत् ।
units.english: Similarly, the theory of ‘Void’ Nihilism propounded by the Bauddhas, and the consequent denial of the ‘Active Agent’, as the performer of Actionare not right;

units.sanskrit: तदभ्युपगन्तुः सत्त्वाभ्युपगमात् ।
units.english: as they admit the reality of the person who holds the said theory

units.sanskrit: यच्चाज्ञैरलसतयाकर्तृत्वाभ्युपगमः सो ऽप्यसन्,
units.english: This also is not right, because for such people the notion of the ‘Active Agent has not been set aside by any valid source of knowledge

units.sanskrit: कारकबुद्धेरनिवर्ततत्वात्प्रमाणेन । तस्माद्वेदान्तप्रमाणजनितैकत्वप्रत्ययवत एव कर्मनिवृत्तिलक्षणं पारिव्राज्यं ब्रह्मसंस्थत्वं चेति सिद्धम् ।
units.english: From all this it follows that it is only when on the strength of the Vedantic Texts, one has reached firm conviction regarding Unity, that he reaches the real ‘Renunciation of Action’ which constitutes the stage of the Wandering Mendicant and that of ‘Resting in Brahaman ’

units.sanskrit: एतेन गृहस्थस्यैकत्वविज्ञाने सति पारिव्राज्यमर्थसिद्धम् । नन्वग्न्युत्सादनदोषभाक्स्यात्परिव्रजन् ।
units.english: From this also it follows that if, in a certain case, a Householder has attained the knowledge of unity and thereby set aside all notions of diversity he also naturally attains the position of the Wandering Mendicant

units.sanskrit: वीरहा वा एष देवानां यो ऽग्निमुद्वासयतेइति श्रुतेः । न ।
units.english: ObjectionSuch a Householder, taking to the life of the Wandering Mendicant, would incur the sin of destroying his Fires,as declared in the Smṛti textsOne who destroys his fires becomes the murderer of the bravest among deities

units.sanskrit: वेदेनैवोत्सादितत्वात् उत्सन्न एव हि स एकत्वदर्शने जाते ।
units.english: in fact, the fire becomes destroyed by itself as soon as the conviction of Unity is realised;

units.sanskrit: अपागादग्नेरग्नित्वमिति श्रुतेः । अतो न दोषभाग्गृहस्थः परिव्रजन्निति ॥
units.english: as declared in the Śruti Texts‘The fireness of the fire has disappeared etc, etc’Hence by taking to the life of the Wandering Mendicant, the Householder does not incur any sin

units.sanskrit: प्रजापतिर् लोकान् अभ्यतपत् ।
units.english: Prajāpati brooded upon the Regions;

units.sanskrit: तेभ्यो ऽभितप्तेभ्यस् त्रयी विद्या संप्रास्रवत् ।
units.english: from these, thus brooded upon, the Threefold Science issued forth

units.sanskrit: ताम् अभ्यतपत् । तस्या अभितप्ताया एतान्य् अक्षराणि संप्रस्र्वन्त भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति ॥
units.english: He brooded upon this, and from this, thus brooded upon, issued the syllables ‘Bhūḥ’, ‘Bhuvaḥ’ and ‘Svaḥ’

units.sanskrit: यत्संस्थो ऽमृतत्वमेति तन्निरूपणार्थमाह प्रजापतिर्विराट् कश्यपो वा लोकानुद्दिश्य तेषु सारजिघृक्षयाभ्यत पदभितापं कृतवान्ध्यानं
units.english: Prajāpati ie, Virāt or Kaśyapa thought of the Regions; and in order to get at the essence of these Regions, He brooded over them,continued to think of, reflect upon, them

units.sanskrit: तेभ्यो ऽभितप्तेभ्यः सारभूता त्रयी विद्या सम्प्रास्रवत्प्रजापतेर्मनसि प्रत्यभादित्यर्थः । तामभ्यतपत् ।
units.english: From these, thus brooded upon, the Threefold Science issued forth,as the essence of the Regions; that is, the said Science became revealed to the mind of Prajāpati

units.sanskrit: पूर्ववत् । तस्या अभितप्ताया एतान्यक्षराणि सम्प्रास्रवन्त भूर्भुवः स्वरितिव्याहृतयः ॥
units.english: He brooded upon the Science etc, etc, as before;and from the Science, thus brooded upon, the following syllables issued‘bhūḥ’, ‘bhuvaḥ’ and ‘svāḥ which are called ‘Vyāhṛtis’

units.sanskrit: तान्य् अभ्यतपत् ।
units.english: He brooded upon these;

units.sanskrit: तद् यथा शङ्कुना सर्वाणि पर्णानि संतृण्णान्य् एवम् ओंकारेण सर्वा वाक् संतृण्णा ।
units.english: from them thus brooded upon, issued the syllable ‘Om’; just as alt leaves are permeated by the stalk, so is all Speech permeated by the syllable ‘Om’

units.sanskrit: ओंकार एवेदं सर्वम् ओंकार एव इदं सर्वम् ॥
units.english: The ‘Om’ syllable is all this,yea, the syllable ‘Om’ is all this

units.sanskrit: तान्यक्षराण्यभ्यतपत्तेभ्यो ऽभितप्तेभ्य ओङ्कारः सम्प्रास्रवत्तद्ब्रह्म,
units.english: He brooded over the said syllables; from them, thus brooded upon, issued the syllable ‘om’, and this is Brahman

units.sanskrit: कीदृशमित्याहतद्यथा शङ्कुना पर्णनालेन सर्वाणि पर्णानि पत्रावयवजातानि सन्तृण्णानि निविद्धानि व्याप्तानीत्यर्थः । एवमोङ्कारेण ब्रह्मणा परमात्मनः प्रतीकभूतेन सर्वा वाक्यशब्दजातं सन्तृण्णा ।
units.english: The rest describes what this is likeJust as all leaves,all parts of the leaves,are permeated pierced, ie pervadedby the stalkthe twig to which the leaves hang,so, in, the same manner is all Speechall wordspermeated by the syllable ‘Om’, which is Brahman, the very image of the Supreme Self;

units.sanskrit: अकारो वै सर्वा वाकित्यादिश्रुतेः ।
units.english: as declared in such Vedic texts as‘The letter A is all speech’

units.sanskrit: परमात्मविकारश्च नामधेयमात्रमित्यत ओङ्कार एवेदं सर्वमिति । द्विरभ्यास आदरार्थः ।
units.english: Every name is a mere evolute of the Supreme Self; hence all this is the syllable ‘Om’The repetition is meant to indicate the importance of the declaration

units.sanskrit: लोकादिनिष्पादनकथनमोङ्कारस्तुत्यर्थमिति ॥
units.english: The description of the origin of the Regions and other things serves the purpose of eulogising the syllable ‘Om’

units.sanskrit: यद् वसूनां प्रातःसवनम् ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: सामोपासनप्रसङ्गेन कर्मगुणभूतत्वान्निवर्त्योङ्कारं परमात्मप्रतीकत्वादमृतत्वहेतुत्वेन महीकृत्य प्रकृतस्यैव यज्ञस्याङ्गभूतानि सामहोममन्त्रोत्थानान्युपदिदिक्षन्नाहब्रह्मवादिनो
units.english: In course of the treatment of Meditation on Sāma, the Text has precluded the possibility of the notion that the syllable ‘Om’ is an auxiliary to Ritualistic Acts, and has raised its position to a high level by describing it as the image of the Supreme Self and as the means of attaining immortality It now proceeds to expound the ramifications of Sāma, Homa and Mantra, as constituents of the Sacrificial Act which forms the subjectmatter of the Discourse

units.sanskrit: वदन्ति यत्प्रातःसवनं तद्वसूनाम् ।
units.english: The Teachers of Brahman declare that what is known as the ‘Morning Extraction’ appertains io the Vasus;

units.sanskrit: तैश्च प्रातः सवनसम्बद्धो ऽयं लोको वशीकृतः सवनेशानैः ।
units.english: which means that this Region Earth connected with the ‘Morning Extraction’ is held in sway by these Lords of the Extraction the Vasus

units.sanskrit: तथा रुद्रैर्माध्यन्दिनसवनेशानैरन्तरिक्षलोकः ।
units.english: Similarly the region of the Sky is held in sway by the Rudras who are Lords of ‘MiddayExtraction’

units.sanskrit: आदित्यैश्च विश्वैर्देवैश्च तृतीयसवनेशानैस्तृतीयो लोको वशीकृतः ।
units.english: Similarly the third region is held in sway by the Ādityas and Viśvedevas who are Lords of the ‘Evening Extraction’

units.sanskrit: इति यजमानस्य लोको ऽन्यः परिशिष्टो न विद्यते ॥
units.english: Thus then there is no Region left for the Performer of Sacrifices

units.sanskrit: क्व तर्हि यजमानस्य लोक इति । स यस् तं न विद्यात् कथं कुर्यात् ।
units.english: Where then is the Sacrificer’s Region? If one does not know this, how can he perform the Sacrifice? If he knows it, he should perform it

units.sanskrit: अतः क्व तर्हि यजमानस्य लोको यदर्थं यजते । न क्वचिल्लोको ऽस्तीत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: For the above reason, the question arisesWhen then is the Region for the Sacrificer,for attaining which, he performs the sacrifice? The sense of the question is that there is no Region for him

units.sanskrit: लोकाय वै यजते यो यजतेइति श्रुतेः । लोकाभावे च स यो यजमानस्तं लोकस्वीकरणोपायं सामहोममन्त्रोत्थानलक्षणं न विद्यान्न विजानीयात्सो ऽज्ञः कथं कुर्याद्यज्ञं न कथञ्चन तस्य कर्तृत्वमुपपद्यत इत्यर्थः । सामादिविज्ञानस्तुतिपरत्वान्नाविदुषः कर्तृत्वं कर्ममात्रविदः प्रतिषिध्यते ।
units.english: In view of the Vedic Text‘One who performs a sacrifice does so for the purpose of attaining a Region’,if there is no Region for the Sacrificer, then if one who performs the sacrifice does not know the means of making the Region his own,such means consisting in the knowledge of the ramifications of Sāma, Homa and Mantras,he is ignorant; and being ignorant, how could he perform a sacrifice? That is to say, in no way could he ever become a sacrificer, The purpose of all this is to eulogise the knowledge of Sāma and the sacrificial details, and it does not mean that the performance of the sacrifice is forbidden for one who knows merely the sacrificial ritual and is ignorant of the aforesaid Sāma and the rest

units.sanskrit: स्तुतये च सामादिविज्ञानस्याविद्वत्कर्तृत्वप्रतिषेधाय चेति हि भिद्यते वाक्यम् ।
units.english: For if the sentence were taken as eulogising the knowledge of Sāma and the rest, and also as forbidding the performance by the ignorant,then there would be a syntactical split

units.sanskrit: आद्ये चौषस्त्ये काण्डे ऽविदुषो ऽपि कर्मास्तीति हेतुमवोचाम ।
units.english: Further, in the section dealing with UṣastiCākrāyaṇa we have already explained that the performance of sacrifices is permissible for the ignorant also

units.sanskrit: अथैतद्वक्ष्यमाणं सामाद्युपायं विद्वान्कुर्यात् ॥
units.english: On the other hand, if he knows the Sāma and other means, as are going to be described;he should perform the sacrifice

units.sanskrit: पुरा प्रातरनुवाकस्योपाकरणाज् जघनेन गार्हपत्यस्योदाङ्मुख उपविश्य स वासवं सामाभिगायति ॥
units.english: Before the commencing of the ‘Morning Chant’, sitting behind the Gārhapatya Fire, and facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Vasas

units.sanskrit: किं तद्वेद्यमित्याहपुरा पूर्वं प्रातरनुवाकस्य शस्रस्य प्रारम्भाज्जघनेन गार्हपत्यस्य पश्चादुदङ्मुखः सन्नुपविश्य स वासवं वसुदैवत्यं सामाभिगायति ॥
units.english: The text proceeds to expound what it is that should be known by the Sacrificer;Beforeprior tothe commencingbeginningof the ‘morning chant’, sitting behindat the back ofthe Gārhapatya Fire,and facing the Northhe sings the Sāma sacred to the Vasus,ie that of which the Vasas are the presiding deity

units.sanskrit: पश्येम त्वा वयं रा हु म् आ ज्या यो आ इति ॥ लोकद्वारमस्य पृथिवीलोकस्य प्राप्तये द्वारमपावृणु हे ऽग्ने तेन द्वारेण पश्येम त्वा त्वां राज्यायेति ॥
units.english: ‘Open the gate of the Region, so that we may look upon Thee, for the purpose of attaining kingdom’ O Fire, open the door of the Region of the Earth,ie for attaining this Regionthrough that Door, we may look upon Thee,for this purpose of attaining kingdom

units.sanskrit: अथ जुहोति । नमो ऽग्नये पृथिवीक्षिते लोकक्षिते ।
units.english: Then he pours the libation saying‘Adoration to Agni, dwelling on the earth, dwelling in the Region

units.sanskrit: लोकं मे यजमानाय विन्द । एष वै यजमानस्य लोकः । एता अस्मि ॥
units.english: Secure the Region for me, the Sacrificer! That would be the Sacrificer’s region to which would go’

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरं जुहोत्यनेन मन्त्रेण नमो ऽग्नये प्रह्वीभूतास्तुभ्यं वयं पृथिवीक्षिते पृथिवीनिवासाय लोकक्षिते पृथिवीलोकनिवासायेत्यर्थः
units.english: Then, after the above,he pours the libation in the firewith this Mantra ‘Adoration to Agni, we bow down to TheeThou who art dwelling on the Earth, and dwelling in the Region,’ie, dwelling in the Earthly Region Secureobtainfor me, the Sacrificerthe Region;

units.sanskrit: एष वै मम यजमानस्य लोक एता गन्तास्मि ॥
units.english: that would be the Sacrificer’s Region to which would go

units.sanskrit: अत्र यजमानः परस्ताद् आयुषः स्वाहा । अपजहि परिघम् इत्य् उक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति । तस्मै वसवः प्रातःसवनं संप्रयच्छन्ति ॥
units.english: Herein, the Sacrificer, after the lapse of his lifespan, says‘Svāhā ! Remove the bolt’, and saying this he stands up, and the Vasus offer to him the ‘Morning Extraction’

units.sanskrit: अत्रास्मिंल्लोके यजमानो ऽहमायुषः परस्तादूर्ध्वं मृतः सन्नित्यर्थः । स्वाहोति जुहोति । अपजह्यपनय परिघं लोकद्वारार्गलमित्येवं मन्त्रमुक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति एवमेतैर्वसुभ्यः
units.english: Hereinin the said Region,the Sacrificer, after the lapse of his lifespan,ie on death,pours the libation, saying ‘Svāhā! Removetake outthe boltthe bar to the entrance to the Region’;having recited this Mantra, he stands up

units.sanskrit: प्रातः सवनसम्बद्धो लोको निष्क्रीतः स्यात्ततस्ते प्रातःसवनं धसवो यजमानाय सम्प्रयच्छन्ति ॥
units.english: By all these means the Region connected with the ‘Morning Extraction’ becomes secured from the Vasus; hence these offer the ‘Morning Extraction’ to the Sacrificer

units.sanskrit: पुरा माध्यन्दिनस्य सवनस्योपाकरणाज् जघनेनाग्नीध्रीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य स रौद्रं सामाभिगायति ॥
units.english: Before the commencement of the ‘Midday Extraction’, sitting behind the Agnīdhrīya Fire and facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Rudras

units.sanskrit: लो कद्वारमपावार् णू ।
units.english: ‘Open the door for sovereignty of the Sky

units.sanskrit: तथा'ग्नीध्रीयस्य दक्षिणाग्नेर्जघनेनोदङ्मुख उपविश्य स रौद्रं सामाभिगायति यजमानो रुद्रदैवत्यंवैराज्याय ॥
units.english: Similarly, sitting behind the Agnīdhṛīya Fire,ie the Dakṣiṇāgni,and facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Rudras, ie the Sāma of which the Rudras are the Deity,for the purpose of attaining Vaiṛājya, sovereignty of the Sky

units.sanskrit: अथ जुहोति । नामो वायवे ऽन्तरिक्षक्षिते लोकक्षिते । लोकं मे यजमानाय विन्द ।
units.english: Then he pours the libation, saying‘Adoration to Vāyu, dwelling in the Sky, dwelling in the Region! Secure the Region for me, the Sacrificer

units.sanskrit: एष वै यजमानस्य लोकः ।
units.english: That would be the Sacrificer’s Region to which would go!’

units.sanskrit: अत्र यजमानः परस्ताद् आयुषः स्वाहा । अपजहि परिघम् इत्य् उक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति । तस्मै रुद्रा माध्यन्दिनं सवनं संप्रयच्छन्ति ॥
units.english: Herein the Sacrificer, after the lapse of his lifespan, says ‘Svāhā! Remove the bolt’, and saying this, he stands up and the Rudras offer to him the ‘Midday Extraction’

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षक्षित इत्यादि समानम् ॥
units.english: Dwelling in the sky etc, etc,as above

units.sanskrit: पुरा तृतीयसवनस्योपाकरणाज् जघनेनाहवनीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य स आदित्यं स वैश्वदेवं सामाभिगायति ॥
units.english: Before the commencement of the Third Extraction, sitting behind the Āhavanīya Fire, ānd facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to Āditya and that sacred to the Viśvedevas

units.sanskrit: पश्येम त्वा वयं स्वारा हुम्,
units.english: ‘Open the door for sovereignty over Heaven’

units.sanskrit: आ ज्या यो आ इत्य् आदित्यम् ॥ अथ वैश्वदेवम् ।
units.english: This to the Ādityas The following to the Visvśdevas‘Open the door

units.sanskrit: पश्येम त्वा वयं साम्रा हुम् आ ज्या यो आ इति ॥
units.english: for supreme sovereignty’

units.sanskrit: तथा'हवनीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य स आदित्यदैवत्यमादित्यं वैश्वदेवं च सामाभिगायति क्रमेण स्वाराज्याय साम्राज्याय ॥ अथ जुहोति ।
units.english: Similarly, sitting behind the Āhavanīya Fire facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to Ādityaie the Sāma of which Āditya is the deity,and also the Sāma sacred to the Viśvedevas,for the purpose, respectively, of acquiring ‘sovereignty over Heaven’ and ‘supreme sovereignty

units.sanskrit: नम आदित्येभ्यश् च विश्वेभ्यश् च देवेभ्यो दिविक्षिद्भ्यो लोकक्षिद्भ्यः । लोकं मे यजमानाय विन्दत ॥
units.english: Then he pours the libation, saying‘Adoration to the Ādityas and to the Viśvedevas, dwelling in Heaven and dwelling in the Region! Secure the region for me, the Sacrificer’

units.sanskrit: एष वै यजमानस्य लोकः । एतास्म्य् अत्र यजमानः परस्ताद् आयुषः स्वाहा ।
units.english: ‘That would be the Sacrificer’s Region, to which would go’Herein the Sacrificer, after the lapse of his lifespan, says‘Svāhā Remove the bolt’;

units.sanskrit: अपहत परिघम् इत्य् उक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति ॥
units.english: and saying this, he stands up

units.sanskrit: दिविक्षिद्भ्य इत्येवमादि समानमन्यत् । विन्दतापहतेति बहिवचनमात्रं विशेषः ।
units.english: the only difference is that the forms ‘bindata’ and ‘apahata’ are in the plural number on account of the deities addressed being many in number

units.sanskrit: याजमानं त्वेतत् । एतास्म्यत्र यजमान इत्यादिलिङ्गात् ॥
units.english: All this is to be said by the Sacrificer, as is clearly indicated by the expressions ‘etāsmi’, ‘ would go’ and ‘Atra Yajamānaḥ’ ‘Herein the Sacrificer’

units.sanskrit: तस्मा आदित्याश् च विश्वे च देवास् तृतीयसवनं संप्रयच्छन्ति ।
units.english: The Ādityas and the Viśvedevas offer to him the ‘Third Extraction’

units.sanskrit: एष ह वै यज्ञस्य मात्रां वेद य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥ एष ह वै यजमान एवंवित् यथोक्तस्य सामादेर्विद्वान्यज्ञस्य मात्रां यज्ञयाथात्म्यं वेद यथोक्तम् ।
units.english: He, verily, knows the measure of the Sacrifice who knows this,yea, who knows this He ie the Sacrificer who knows the Sāma and the details as described above, knows the measurethe real natureof the Sacrifice, as described;

units.sanskrit: य एवं वेद य एवं वेदेति द्विरुक्तिरध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्था ॥
units.english: Who knows this, yea, who knows this’the repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षम् अपूपः ।
units.english: End of the Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: मरीचयः पुत्राः ॥ असौ वा आदित्य उत्याद्यध्यायारम्भे सम्बन्धः । अतीतानन्तराध्यायान्त उक्तं यज्ञस्य मात्रां वेदेति यज्ञविषयाणि च सामहोममन्त्रोत्थानानि विशिष्टफलप्राप्तये यज्ञाङ्गभूतान्युपदिष्टानि ।
units.english: At the outset of the third Discourse beginning with the words ‘Āsau vā Ādityaḥ’, ‘This sun Verily’, we set forth the connection between the two Discourses, and IIIAt the close of the immediately preceding Discourse , it has been said‘One who knows the measure of the Sacrifice etc’ and there have been expounded the ramifications of Sāma, Homa and Mantras, as appertaining to Sacrifices, and as forming part of Sacrifices and thereby bringing about particular results

units.sanskrit: सर्वयज्ञानां च कार्यनिर्वृत्तिरूपः सविता महत्या श्रिया दीप्यते ।
units.english: It is the Sun who shines with brilliant effulgence and represents the embodiment of the successful accomplishment of all Sacrifices;

units.sanskrit: स एष सर्वप्राणिकर्मफलभूतः प्रत्यक्षं सर्वैरुपजीव्यते ।
units.english: it is the Sun who representing the fruition of the actions of all animate beings, is the visible sustainer of all

units.sanskrit: अतो यज्ञव्यपदेशानन्तरं तत्कार्यभूतसवितृविषयमुपासनं सर्वपुरुषार्थेभ्यः श्रेष्ठतमफलं विधास्यामीत्येवमारभते श्रुतिःअसौ वा
units.english: For these reasons, it is only right and proper that after the exposition at the close of Discourse of the ‘Sacrifice’ we should expound the meditation upon the Sun who is the summation of the results of all Sacrifices, as leading to the fulfilment of the highest of all purposes of men With this intention, the Text proceeds with the next Discourse

units.sanskrit: आदित्यो देवमध्वित्यादि । देवनां मोदनान्मध्विव मध्वसावादित्यः ।
units.english: The Sun is called the ‘honey’, ‘Madhu’, of the Deities because He delights them, and hence is like Honey

units.sanskrit: वस्वादीनां च मोदनहेतुत्वं वक्ष्यति सर्वयज्ञफलरूपत्वादादित्यस्य ।
units.english: It is going to be described later on how embodying the results of all sacrifices, the Sun is a source of delight to the Vasus and other Deities

units.sanskrit: कथं मधुत्वमित्याहतस्य मधुनो द्यौरेव भ्रामरस्येव मधुनस्तिरश्चीनश्चासौ वंशश्चेति तिरश्चीनवंशः ।
units.english: The Text next explains in what way the Sun is like Honey Of thisHoney in the shape of the Sun, the Heaven is what the curvedbeam is for the Beehoney;

units.sanskrit: तिर्यग्गतेव हि द्यौर्लक्ष्यते ।
units.english: as a matter of fact, the Heaven appears like a curved surface

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षं च मध्वपूपो द्युवंशे लग्नः सल्लंम्बत इवातो मध्वपूपसामान्यादन्तरिक्षं मध्वपूपो मधुनः सवितुराश्रयत्वाच्च । मरीचयो रश्मयो रश्मिस्था आपो भौमाः सवित्राकृष्टाःएता वा आपः स्वराजो यन्मरीचयैति इति हि विज्ञायते ।
units.english: The Sky is the Hive,the Shy appears to be hanging by Heaven, just as the Hive hangs by the roofbeam; and through this similarity to the Beehive, the Sky is likened to the Hive; and also because the Sky is the abode of the Sun, just as the Hive is the container of the Honey ‘The Rays etc’The Earth s moisture absorbed by the Sun’s rays, is what is known as water in the kingdom of Heaven;

units.sanskrit: ता अन्तरिक्षमध्वपूपस्थरश्म्यन्तर्गतत्वाद्भ्रमरबीजभूताः पुत्रा इव हिता लक्ष्यन्त इति पुत्रा इव पुत्रा मध्वपूपनाड्यन्तर्गता हि भ्रमरपुत्राः
units.english: and as this moisture is contained in the rays which are contained in the hivelike Sky, it has the appearance of Eggs deposited therein, like the Eggs of the Bees; they are spoken of as ‘Eggs’ in the sense of being like Eggs; resembling the eggs of the Bees contained in the Beehive

units.sanskrit: तस्य ये प्राञ्चो रश्मयस् ता एवास्य प्राच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
units.english: Its Eastward rays are the eastern honeycells;

units.sanskrit: ऋच एव मधुकृतः । ऋग्वेद एव पुष्पम् ।
units.english: the Ṛkverses are the honeyproducers; the Ṛgveda is the flower;

units.sanskrit: ता अमृता आपः ।
units.english: and those waters are the nectar;

units.sanskrit: ता वा एता ऋचः ॥
units.english: or those same Ṛkverses

units.sanskrit: तस्य सवितुर्मध्वाश्रयस्य मधुनो ये प्राञ्चः प्राच्यां दिशि गता रश्मयस्ता एवास्य प्राच्यः प्रागञ्चनान्मधुनो नाड्यो मधुनाड्य इव मध्वाधारच्छिद्राणीत्यर्थः । तत्र ऋच एव मधुकृतो लोहितरूपं सवित्राश्रयं मधु कुर्वन्तीति मधुकृतो भ्रमरा इव यतो रसानादाय मधु कुर्वन्ति ।
units.english: The Eastward raysthe rays flowing towards the Eastof the Sunwho is the Honey in the Honeyhive,are the Eastern honeycellsthe cells, holes, containing the honey;these are called ‘Eastern’ in the sense that they flow outwards,The Ṛkverses are the honeyproducers,inasmuch as they ‘produce the honey’, which is red and is contained in the Sun; as the beesextract the juice from flowers and produce honey;

units.sanskrit: तत्पुष्पमिव पुष्पमृग्वेद एव ।
units.english: and the Ṛgveda which contains the Ṛkverses is like the flowers which contain the Honey

units.sanskrit: तत्र ऋग्ब्राह्मणसमुदायस्य ऋग्वेदाख्यत्वाच्छब्दमात्राच्च भोग्यरूपरसनिस्रावासम्भवादृग्वेदशब्देनात्र ऋग्वेदविहितं कर्म ।
units.english: Inasmuch as the name ‘Ṛgveda’ is applied to the collections of Ṛks and Brāhmaṇas, which are mere words, there cannot flow from these any such juices or effects like Honey as could be tasted enjoyed; hence the term ‘Ṛgveda’ here should be taken as standing for the Acts prescribed in the Ṛgveda;

units.sanskrit: ततो हि कर्मफलभूतमधुरसनिस्रावसम्भवात् ।
units.english: as it is only from these acts that there can flow honeylike results

units.sanskrit: मधुकरैरिव पुष्पस्थानीयादृग्वेदविहितात्कर्मणो ऽप आदाय ऋग्भिर्मधु निर्वर्त्यते । कास्ता आप इत्याहताः कर्मणि प्रयुक्ताः सोमाज्यपयोरूपा अग्नौ प्रक्षिप्तास्तत्पाकाभिनिर्वृत्ता अमृता अमृतार्थत्वादत्यन्त रसवत्य आपो भवन्ति
units.english: Just as the bees produce honey out of the juices extracted from flowers,so the Ṛkverses produce ‘honey’ out of the waters results extracted from the Acts which are thus like flowers, What are those Waters?The offerings consisting of Somajuice Butter and Milk, which are thrown into the fire at sacrificial performances; and these, on fruition, become Nectar; ie they lead to immortality;

units.sanskrit: तद्रसानादाय ता वा एता ॠचः पुष्पेभ्यो रसमाददाना एव भ्रमराः ऋचः ॥
units.english: Or those same Ṛkverses,extracting the juicelike the bees extracting the juices from flowers,are themselves the nectar

units.sanskrit: एतम् ऋग्वेदम् अभ्यतपन् ।
units.english: They pressed this Ṛgveda

units.sanskrit: तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
units.english: From it, thus pressed, there proceeded its Essence, in the form of fame, resplendence, efficient senseorgans, strength and eatable food

units.sanskrit: एतमृग्वेदमृग्वेदविहितं कर्म पुष्पस्थानीयमभ्यतपन्नभितापं कृतवत्य इवैता ऋचः कर्मणि प्रयुक्ताः ।
units.english: They pressedexerted pressure uponthis Ṛgvedaie the Sacrificial Act prescribed in the Ṛgveda, which is like the flower from which Honey is extracted

units.sanskrit: ॠग्भिर्हि मन्त्रैः शस्राद्यङ्गभावमुपगतैः क्रियमाणं कर्म मधुनिर्वर्तकं रसं मुञ्चतीत्युपपद्यते पुष्पाणीव भ्रमरैराचूष्यमाणानि ।
units.english: It is only right that when the Act is performed with the Ṛkverses used as Mantras equipped with such ‘Śāstra’ Recitation and other details, it gives out the Essence which is productive of Honey; just as it is only when the flowers are sucked by bees that Honey is produced

units.sanskrit: तदेतदाहतस्यर्ग्वेदस्याभितप्तस्य ।
units.english: This is explained by the words‘From itthus pressed etc’

units.sanskrit: को ऽसौ रसो य ऋङ्मधुकराभितापनिःसृत इत्युच्यते ।
units.english: QuestionWhat is that ‘Essence’ which is described as proceeding from the pressure exerted by the bees in the shape of the Ṛkverses?

units.sanskrit: यशो विश्रुतत्वं तेजो देहगता दीप्तिरिन्द्रियं सामर्थ्योपेतैरिन्द्रियैरवैकल्यं वीर्यं सामर्थ्यं बलमित्यर्थः । अन्नाद्यमन्नं च तदाद्यं च येनोपयुज्यमानेनाहन्यहनि देवानां स्थितिः स्यात्तदन्नाद्यमेष रसो ऽजायत यागादिलक्षणात्कर्मणः ॥
units.english: AnswerFamereputation,resplendenceeffulgence of body,efficient senseorgansequipment of virile organs free from all weaknesses,strengthpower,and eatable food,food that is eatable, by the daily use of which the deities continue to live;this was the Essence that proceeded out of Action in the shape of Sacrifices

units.sanskrit: तद् व्यक्षरत् ।
units.english: It flowed out;

units.sanskrit: तद् आदित्यम् अभितो ऽश्रयत् ।
units.english: it went round the Sun;

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य रोहितं रूपम् ॥
units.english: this is what appears as the red colour in the Sun

units.sanskrit: गत्वा च तदादित्यमभितः पार्श्वतः पूर्वभागं सवितुरश्रयदाश्रितवदित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Itall this, beginning with Fame and ending with eatable food,flowed outwent forth copiously having flown out, it went round the Sun,went by the side of the Sun, to the East of it

units.sanskrit: अमुष्मिन्नादित्ये सञ्चितं कर्मफलाख्यं मधु भोक्ष्यामह इत्येवं हि यशआदिलक्षणफलप्राप्तये कर्माणि क्रियन्ते मनुष्यैः केदारनिष्पादनमिव कर्षकैः ।
units.english: Sacrificial acts are done by men with a view to obtaining such results as Fame and the like, with the idea that ‘ shall eat the Honey in the shape of the accumulated results of actions, as treasured in this Sun’; just as cultivators take to agriculture for the purpose of securing articles of food’

units.sanskrit: किं तद्यदेतदादित्यस्योद्यतो दृश्यते रोहितं रूपम् ॥
units.english: This is now exemplified in a visible formThis is what etc, etc What is it?It is what is seen as the red colour in the rising Sun

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽस्य दक्षिणा रश्मयस् ता एवास्य दक्षिणा मधुनाड्यः ।
units.english: Its Southward rays are the southern honey cells;

units.sanskrit: यजूंष्य् एव मधुकृतः । यजुर्वेद एव पुष्पम् ।
units.english: the Yajuṣverses are the honeyproducers; the Yajurveda is the flower;those waters are the nectar

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽस्य दक्षिणा रश्मय इत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: Now its southward rays etc, etc;

units.sanskrit: यजूंयेव मधुकृतो यजुर्वेदविहिते कर्मणि प्रयुक्तानि । पूर्ववन्मधुकृत इव ।
units.english: just as before The Yajuṣverses are the honeyproducers,those that are used at Actions prescribed in the Yajurvedajust like the honeyproducing bees,as before

units.sanskrit: यजुर्वेदविहितं कर्म पुष्पस्थानीयं पुष्पमित्युच्यते ।
units.english: The action prescribed in the Yajurveda has the same character as the flower, and hence it is spoken of as being the ‘flower’

units.sanskrit: ता एव सोमाद्या अमृता आपः ॥
units.english: Those watersin the shape of the Soma and the restare the nectar

units.sanskrit: तानि वा एतानि यजूंष्य् एतं यजुर्वेदम् अभ्यतपन् ।
units.english: Verily these Yajuṣverses pressed this Yajurveda;

units.sanskrit: तस्य अभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
units.english: from it, thus pressed, there proceeded its essence, in the form of fame, resplendence, efficient senseorgans, strength and eatable food

units.sanskrit: तद् व्यक्षरत् ।
units.english: It flowed out;

units.sanskrit: तद् आदित्यम् अभितो ऽश्रयत् ।
units.english: it went round the Sun;

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य शुक्लं रूपम् ॥
units.english: this is what appears as the white colour in the Sun

units.sanskrit: तानि वा एतानि यजूंष्येतं यजुर्वेदमभ्यतपन्नित्येवमादि सर्वं समानम् ।
units.english: These Yajuṣverses pressed this Yajurveda etc,all as before

units.sanskrit: मध्वेतदादित्यस्य दृश्यते शुक्लं रूपम् ॥
units.english: This ‘Honey’ is seen as the white colour in the Sun

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽस्य प्रत्यञ्चो रश्मायस् ता एवास्य प्रतीच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
units.english: Then, its Westward rays are its western honeycells;

units.sanskrit: सामान्य् एव मधुकृतः । सामवेद एव पुष्पम् ।
units.english: the Sām&verses are the honeyproducers;the Sāmaveda is the flower;those waters are the nectar

units.sanskrit: तानि वा एतानि सामान्य् एतं सामवेदम् अभ्यतपन् । तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
units.english: Verily these Sāmaverses pressed this Sāmaveda from it, thus pressed, there proceeded its essence, in the form of fame, resplendence, efficient senseorgans, strength and eatable food

units.sanskrit: तद् व्यक्षरत् ।
units.english: It flowed out;

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य कृष्णं रूपम् ॥
units.english: it went round the Sun;this is what appears as the black colour in the Sun

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽस्य प्रत्यश्चो रश्मय इत्यादि समानम् । तथा साम्नां मधु ।
units.english: Its western rays etc, etc,as beforeThe ‘Honey’ proceeds from the Sāma

units.sanskrit: एतदादित्यस्य कृष्णं रूपम् ॥
units.english: This is the black colour, in the Sun

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य तृतीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽस्योदञ्चो रश्मयस् ता एवास्योदीच्यो मधुनाड्यः । अथर्वाङ्गिरस एव मधुकृतः । इतिहासपुराणं पुष्पम् ।
units.english: Then, its Northward rays are its northern honeycellsThe Atharvāṅgirasas are the honeyproducers;the ItihāsaPurāṇa are the flower;those waters are the nectar

units.sanskrit: ते वा एते ऽथर्वाङ्गिरस एतद् इतिहासपूराणम् अभ्यतपन् ।
units.english: These Atharvāṅgirasas pressed this ItihāsaPurāna;

units.sanskrit: तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियां वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
units.english: from it, thus pressed, proceeded its essence in the form of fame, resplendence, efficient organs, strength and eatable food

units.sanskrit: तद् आदित्यम् अभितो ऽश्रयत् ।
units.english: It flowed out it went round the Sun;

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य परःकृष्णं रूपम् ॥ अथ ये ऽस्योदञ्चो रश्मय इत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: this is what appears as the very black colour in the Sun Then, its Northern rays etc, etc, etc

units.sanskrit: अथर्वाङ्गिरसो ऽथर्वणाङ्गिरसा च दृष्टा मन्त्रा अथर्वाङ्गिरसः कर्मणि प्रयुक्ता मधुकृतः ।
units.english: Atharvāṅgirasasare the mantratexts seen by revealed to AtharvanAṅgiras; these, as used at sacrificial acts, are the honeyproducers

units.sanskrit: इतिहासपुराणं पुष्पम् । तयोश्चेतिहासपुराणयोरश्वमेधे पारिप्लवासु रात्रिषु कर्माङ्गत्वेन विनियोगः सिद्धः ।
units.english: ItihāsaPurāṇa are the flowers;the use of ItihāsaPurāṇa is wellknown as to be made as part of the ‘Pāriplavanights’ at the Aśvamedha sacrifice

units.sanskrit: मध्वेतदादित्यस्य परः कृष्णं रूपमतिशयेन कृष्णमित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: This honey is what appears as the very black colour in the Sunie, that which is extremely black

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽस्योर्ध्वा रश्मयस् ता एवास्योर्ध्वा मधुनाड्यः ।
units.english: Then, its upward rays are the upper honeycells;

units.sanskrit: गुह्या एवादेशा मधुकृतः ।
units.english: the esoteric teachings are the honey producers;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मैव पुष्पं ।
units.english: Brahman itself is the flower;

units.sanskrit: ता अमृता आपः ॥
units.english: those waters are the nectar

units.sanskrit: ते वा एते गुह्या आदेशा एतद् ब्रह्माभ्यतपन् । तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
units.english: These esoteric teachings pressed this Brahman from it, thus pressed, proceeded the essence, in the shape of fame, resplendence, efficient senseorgans, strength and eatable food

units.sanskrit: तद् व्यक्षरत् ।
units.english: It flowed out;

units.sanskrit: तद् आदित्यम् अभितो ऽश्रयत् ।
units.english: it went round the Sun;

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य मध्ये क्षोभत इव ॥
units.english: this is what appears as scintillating in the centre of the Sun

units.english: The answer to this has been thus explained by the revered teacher Draviḍācārya, acc

units.sanskrit: अमरावत्यादीनां पुरीणां द्विगुणोत्तरोत्तरेण कालेनोद्वासः स्यात् ।
units.english: to ĀnandagiriIn the case of Amarāvatī Indra’s city in the East and the cities of other Deities in the South and other directions, the time taken by the depopulation of the succeeding one would be twice of that taken by the depopulation of the other;
