units.sanskrit: उदयश्च नाम सवितुस्तन्निवासिनां प्राणिनां चक्षुगोचरापत्तिस्तदत्ययष्चस्तमनं न परमार्थत उदयास्तमने स्तः । तन्निवासिनां च प्राणिनामभावे तान्प्रति तेनैव मार्गेण गच्छन्नपि नैवोदेता नास्तमेतेति चक्षुर्गोचरापत्तेस्तदत्ययस्य चाभावात् ।
units.english: the ‘rising’ of the Sun also in a certain region consists only in its becoming visible to the eyes of the persons living in that region,and its ‘setting’ consists, in its becoming invisible; and «n reality, there is neither ‘rising’ nor ‘setting’ of the Sun;so that when there are no inhabitants in any region,even though the Sun may be going by that path,there is neither ‘rising’ nor ‘setting’ so far as that region is concerned; as there can be no visibility or invisibility

units.sanskrit: तथामरावत्याः सकाशाद्द्विगुणं कालं संयमनी पुरी वसत्यतस्तन्निवासिनः प्राणिनः प्रति दक्षिणत इवोदेत्युत्तरतो ऽस्तमेतीत्युच्यते ऽस्मद्बुद्धिं
units.english: Thus then, inasmuch as the city of Saṃyamanī of Yama, in the South remains inhabited twice as long as the city of Amarāvatī of Indra in the East,so far as the inhabitants of the city of Samyamanī arc concerned, the Sun is said to rise in the South and set in the Northsthis assertion being made from the viewpoint of ourselves inhabitants of the Earth

units.sanskrit: तथोत्तरास्वपि पुरीषु योजना ।
units.english: Similar explanation applies to the case of the other cities and Regions

units.sanskrit: सर्वेषां च मेरुरुत्तरतो भवति ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, mount Meru lies to the North of all these ‘cities’ and Regions;

units.sanskrit: यदामरावत्यां मध्याह्नगतः सविता तदा संयमन्यामुद्यन्दृश्यते तत्र मध्याह्नगतो वारुण्यामुद्यन्दृश्यते, तथोत्तरस्यां,
units.english: so that when, in the city of Amarāvatī the Eastern region, the Sun is at meridian, then at that time, in the city of Saṃyamanī the Southern Region, the Sun is seen ‘rising’, and when it is seen at meridian in the southern region, it is seen ‘rising’ in the city of Vāruṇī the Western Region;

units.sanskrit: प्रदक्षिणावृत्तेस्तुल्यत्वात् । इलावृतवासिनां सर्वतः पर्वतप्राकारनिवारितादित्यरश्मीनां सवितोर्ध्व इवोदेतावगिस्तमेता दृश्यते । पर्वतोर्ध्वच्छिद्रप्रवेशात्सवितृप्रकाशस्य ।
units.english: As regards the Ilāvṛta continent which surrounds the mount Meru, people who live there have the Sun’s rays shut out from them by the encircling wall of mountains; so that for them, the Sun always appears to rise ‘overhead’ and set ‘below’;the rays of the Sun piercing through the crevices in the mountain

units.sanskrit: तथर्गाद्यमृतोपजीविनाममृतानां च द्विगुणोत्तरोत्तरवीर्यवत्त्वमनुमीयते भोगकालद्वैगुण्यलिङ्गेन ।
units.english: Similarly, as regards the beings living upon the ‘Ṛk’ and other ‘Nectars’as also the Nectars’ themselves,their gradual increase in their strength and visibility is inferred from the fact that the time of experience and enjoyment becomes gradually doubled

units.sanskrit: उद्यमनसंवेशनादि देवानां रुद्रादीनां विदुषश्च समानम् ॥
units.english: The ‘retiring’ and ‘rising’ is the same in the case of the Rudras and other Deities as in the case of persons knowing them

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्याष्टमनवमदशमखण्डाः
units.english: End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ तत ऊर्ध्व उदेत्य नैवोदेता नास्तम् एतैकल एव मध्ये स्थाता ।
units.english: Now rising from thence upward, He neither rises nor sets He stands alone in the middle

units.sanskrit: तद् एष श्लोकः ॥
units.english: To this effect there is the following verse

units.sanskrit: कृत्वैवमुदयास्तमनेन प्राणिनां स्वकर्मफलभोगनिमित्तमनुग्रहं तत्कर्मफलोपभोगक्षये तानि प्राणिजातान्यात्मनि संहृत्याथ ततस्तस्मादनन्तरं प्राण्यनुग्रहकालादूर्ध्वः सन्नात्मन्युदेत्योद्गम्य यान्प्रत्युदेति तेषां प्राणिनामभावात्स्वात्मस्थो
units.english: Through the abovedescribed ‘rising’ and ‘setting’, having helped the beings to experience the results of their acts,when this experience comes to an end, the Sun absorbs all these beings; and then, after the time of helping the creatures has ceased, the Sun, rising from thence upward, within himself,as there are no longer any living beings for whose sake He could rise,He rests within himself, and neither rises nor sets;

units.sanskrit: नैवोदेता नास्तमेतैकलो ऽद्वितीयो ऽनवयवो मध्ये स्वात्मन्येव स्थाता ।
units.english: He stands alone by himselfwithout a second, without any constituent parts,in the middle,within himselfHe stands alone

units.sanskrit: तत्र कश्चिद्विद्वान्वस्वादिसमानचरणो रोहिताद्यमृतभोगभागी यथोक्तक्रमेण स्वात्मानं सवितारमात्मत्वेनोपेत्य समाहितः सन्नेतं मन्त्रं दृष्ट्वोत्थितो ऽन्यस्मै पृष्टवते जगाद । यतस्त्वमागतो ब्रह्मलोकात्किं तत्राप्यहोरात्राभ्यां परिवर्तमानः सविता प्राणिनामायुः क्षपयति यथेहास्माकमित्येवं पृष्टः प्रत्याह । तत्तत्र यथा पृष्टे यथोक्ते चार्थ एष श्लोको भवति तनोक्तो योगिनेति श्रुतेर्वचनमिदम् ॥
units.english: A certain learned person, being in the position of the Vasus and enjoying the Red and the other kinds of ‘Nectar’,approaches the Sun standing within himself as his own ‘self’, in the manner described above and thus become selfcentred and composed,said had revealed to him this Mantratext,said to another person who had questioned him, in the following words‘In the Region of Brahman from where you come,does the Sun there also,as in our world here,revolve through days and nights and thereby cut short the lifespan of living beings?’Being thus questioned what the knowing Yogin;said in reply is expressed in the following verse, which represents the answer to the question put to the Yogin;this is what the present Vedic text declares

units.sanskrit: न वै तत्र न निम्लोच ।
units.english: ‘It is not so there; He never set

units.sanskrit: देवास् तेनाहं सत्येन । मा विराधिषि ब्रह्मणेति ॥
units.english: He never rose, O, Ye, Deities; by this truth, may not fall foul of Brahman !’

units.sanskrit: न वै तत्र यतो ऽहं ब्रह्मलोकादागतस्तस्मिन्न वै तत्रैतदस्ति यत्पृच्छसि ।
units.english: ‘It is not so there’in the Region of Brahman from where come, it is not as you ask

units.sanskrit: न हि तत्र निम्लोचो ऽस्तमगमत्सविता न चोदियायोद्गतः कुतश्चित्कदाचन कस्मिंश्चिदपि काल इति ।
units.english: There the Sun has never set nor as He ever risen,neverat any time

units.sanskrit: उदयास्तमयवर्जितो ब्रह्मलोक इत्यनुपपन्नमित्युक्तः शुथमिव प्रतिपेदे ।
units.english: Being told that it is apparently impossible that in the region of Brahman there should be neither sunrise nor sunset,the man has recourse to an oath;

units.sanskrit: हे देवाः साक्षिणो यूयं शृणुत यथा मयोक्तं सत्यं वचस्तेन स्तेयनाहं ब्रह्मणा ब्रह्मस्वरूपेण मा विराधिषि मा विरुध्येयमप्राप्तिर्ब्रह्मणा
units.english: ‘O, ye Deitieswho are witnesseslisten to thisby this truthwhat have said,may not fall foul of Brahman; that may if what say is not true not attain Brahman ‘What the man has said is quite true’says the Sruti in the following words

units.sanskrit: मम मा भूदित्यर्थः ॥ न ह वा अस्मा उदेति न निम्लोचति ।
units.english: For one who thus knows the secret doctrine of Brahman, it does not set nor does it rise;

units.sanskrit: सकृद् दिवा हैवास्मै भवति ।
units.english: for him, it is day once for all

units.sanskrit: य एताम् एवं ब्रह्मोपनिषदं वेद ॥
units.english: For him who knows the abovedescribed Brahman, the Sun rises not;

units.sanskrit: न निम्लोचति नास्तमेति किं तु ब्रह्मविदे ऽस्मै सकृद्दिवा हैव सदैवाहर्भवति
units.english: nor does it set; for this knower of Brahman, it is day once for all; that is, for him, there is always day;

units.sanskrit: स्वयञ्ज्योतिष्ट्वाद्य एतां यथोक्तां ब्रह्मोपनिषदं वेदगुह्यं वेद ।
units.english: because this man who knows the said secret doctrine of Brahman,hidden in the Veda,is selfillumined

units.sanskrit: एवं तन्त्रेण वंशादित्रयं प्रत्यमृतसम्बन्धं च यच्चान्यदवोचामैवं जानातीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The meaning is that all this refers to the person who knows all that has been said above about three ‘crossbeams’, the connected ‘nectar’ and the rest of it

units.sanskrit: विद्वानुदयास्तमयकालापरिच्छेद्यं नित्यमजं ब्रह्म भवतीत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: What it all means is that the knowing man becomes that Brahman which is not conditioned by time as measured by sunrise and sunset, it is eternal and unborn

units.sanskrit: तद् धैतद् ब्रह्मा प्रजापतय उवाच । प्रजापतिर् मनवे ।
units.english: Brahmā expounded this to Prajāpati, Prajāpati to Manu and Manu to his offsprings

units.sanskrit: मनुः प्रजाभ्यः । तद् धैतद् उद्दालकायारुणये ज्येष्ठाय पुत्राय पिता ब्रह्म प्रोवाच ॥ तद्धैतन्मधुज्ञानं ब्रह्मा हिरण्यगर्भो विराजे प्रजापतय उवाच ।
units.english: The father of UddālakaĀruṇi expounded to him, his eldest son this Brahman This doctrine of Honey,BrahmāHiraṇyagarbha expounded to PrajāpatiVirāṭ this latter expounded it to Manu, and Manu expounded to his offsprings Ikṣvāku and the rest

units.sanskrit: मनुरिक्ष्वाक्वाद्याभ्यः प्रजाभ्यः प्रोवाचेति विद्यां स्तौति ब्रह्मादिविशिष्टक्रमागतेति ।
units.english: This text eulogises the Doctrine as having come down through such distinguished tradition, from Brahmā downwards

units.sanskrit: किं च तद्धैतन्मधुज्ञानमुद्दालकाया'रुणये पिता
units.english: Further, this same Doctrine of Honey was taught by the father of UddālakaĀruṇi, to him, his eldest son,as the Science of Brahma

units.sanskrit: इदं वाव तज् ज्येष्ठाय पुत्राय पिता ब्रह्म प्रब्रूयात् प्रणाय्याय वान्तेवासिने ॥ इदं वाव तद्यथोक्तमन्यो ऽपि ज्येष्ठाय पुत्राय सर्वप्रियार्हाय ब्रह्म प्रब्रूयात् ।
units.english: Verily, this Brahman, the Father, may expound to his eldest son, or to a worthy disciple Verily, this Brahman,described above,another father also may expound to this eldest son, who is dearest and most worthyor to a worthyqualifieddisciplepupil

units.sanskrit: नान्यस्मै कस्मैचन ।
units.english: Not to anyone else;

units.sanskrit: यद्य् अप्य् अस्मा इमाम् अद्भिः परिगृहीतां धनस्य पूर्णां दद्याद् एतद् एव ततो भूय इति ॥
units.english: even though he gave him the whole of this seagirt Earth full of treasure for this is greater than that,yea, it is greater than that

units.sanskrit: नान्यस्मै कस्मैचन प्रब्रूयात्तीर्थद्वयमनुज्ञातमनेकेषां प्राप्तानां तीर्थानामाचार्यादीनाम् ।
units.english: One should not expound this to any one else For all teachers, two pupils have been permitted here, from among several possible ones

units.sanskrit: कस्मात्पुनस्तीर्थसङ्कोचनं विद्याया निष्क्रयार्थमाचार्याय धनस्य पूर्णां सम्पन्नां भोगोपररणैर्नासावस्य निष्क्रयो यस्मात्ततो ऽपि दानादेतदेव यन्मधुविद्यादानं
units.english: QuestionWhy has this limitation been placed on the dissemination of knowledge? AnswerEven though, to such a teacher, any one were to give the whole of this Earth surrounded by water,seagirtfull of treasurefully equipped with articles of enjoyment,in return for this teaching,this cannot be a fit price;

units.sanskrit: भूयो बहुतरफलमित्यर्थः । द्विरभ्यास आदरार्थः ॥
units.english: because itthe teaching of the Doctrine of Honeyis greatermore fruitfulthan thatie, the said, gift

units.sanskrit: गायत्री वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यद् इदम् किञ्च ।
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the great importance of the subject

units.sanskrit: वाग् वै गायत्री ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यत एवमतिशयफलैषा ब्रह्मविद्यातः सा प्रकारान्तरेणापि वक्तव्येति गायत्री वा इत्याद्यारभ्यते ।
units.english: Inasmuch as this Science of Brahman is conducive to such excellent results, it is right that it should be expounded in another manner also; hence the Text begins the next section with the words

units.sanskrit: गायत्रीद्वारेण चोच्यते ।
units.english: ‘Gāyatrī va’‘Gāyatrī indeed is’;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणः सर्वविशेषरहितस्य नेति नेतीत्यादिशिषप्रतिषेधगम्यस्य दुर्बोधत्वात् । सत्स्वनेकेषु च्छन्दःसु गायत्र्या एव ब्रह्मज्ञानद्वारतयोपादानं प्राधान्यात् ।
units.english: and this science is expounded through the Gāyatrī, because directly by itself Brahman is hard to comprehend, being, as it is, devoid of differentiating qualifications, and comprehensible only through such negation of qualifications as contained in the Vedic text ‘Not this, not that’

units.sanskrit: सोमाहरणात् इतरच्छन्दोक्षराहरणेनेतरच्छन्दोव्याप्त्या च सर्वसवनव्यापकत्वाच्च यज्ञे प्राधान्यं गायत्र्याः ।
units.english: and this importance of the Gāyatrī at the sacrificial performance is proved by a the fact that it was the Gāyatrī that carried the Soma to the deities, b the fact that it has absorbed the syllabus of all other metres and as such pervades over them all, and c the fact that it pervades over all ‘extractions’

units.sanskrit: गायत्रीसारत्वाच्च ब्राह्मणस्य मातरमिव हित्वा गुरुतरां गायत्रीं ततो ऽन्यद्गुरुतरं न प्रतिपद्यते यथोक्तं ब्रह्मापीति ।
units.english: Further, inasmuch as the Gāyatrī is thevery essence of the Brāhmaṇa, the abovedescribed Brahman itsself regards the Gāyatrī as its mother and never has recourse to anything more important than that;

units.sanskrit: तस्यामत्यन्तगौरवस्य प्रसिद्धत्वात् ।
units.english: specially as the supreme importance of the Gāyatrī is universally recognised

units.sanskrit: अतो गायत्रीमुखेनैव ब्रह्मोच्यते ।
units.english: It is for these reasons that Brahman is expounded through the Gāyatrī itself as the vehicle

units.sanskrit: गायत्री वा इत्यवधारणार्थो वैशब्दः ।
units.english: Gāyatrī vai;the particle ‘vai’, ‘indeed’, is meant to indicate emphasis

units.sanskrit: इदं सर्वं भूतं प्रामिजातं यत्किञ्च स्थावरं जङ्गमं वा तत्सर्वं गायत्र्येव ।
units.english: All this, whateverliving being existsanimate as well as inanimate,all this indeed is Gāyatrī itself

units.sanskrit: तस्याश्छन्दोमात्रायाः सर्वभूतत्वमनुपपन्नमिति गायत्रीकारणं वाचं शब्दयत्यसौ गौरसावश्व इति च त्रायते च रक्षत्यमुष्मान्मा भैषीः किं ते भयमुत्थितमित्यादिना सर्वतो भयान्निवर्त्यमानो वाचा त्रातः स्यात् ।
units.english: Feeling that Gāyatrī being a mere metrical concatenation of syllables, it is not possible for it to be everything, the Text proceeds to represent the Gāyatrī as Speech itself, which is the origin of the Gāyatrī;Speech indeed is Gāyatrī; and Speech is everything; because Speech, in the form of word, sings out all that exists;ie, represents everything in words, as ‘that is the cow’, ‘this is the horse,and also protects all that exists;everyone is protected from all dangers by means of such words as‘Do not fear;

units.sanskrit: यद्वाग्भूतं गायति च त्रायते च गायत्र्येव तद्गायति च त्रायते च वाचो ऽनन्यत्वाद्गायत्र्याः ।
units.english: Inasmuch as Speech sings out and protects all that exists,it is Gāyatrī itself that sings it out and protects it; as Gāyatrī is the same as Speech;

units.sanskrit: गानात्त्राणाच्च गायत्र्या गायत्रीत्वम् ॥ या वै सा गायत्रीयं वाव सा येयं पृथिवी ।
units.english: and the Gāyatrī is called ‘Gāyatrī’, because it sings out Gāyati and protects Trāyati Verily, that which is Gāyatrī is indeed this Earth;

units.sanskrit: अस्यां हीदं सर्वं भूतं प्रतिष्ठितम् । एताम् एव नातिशीयते ॥
units.english: it is on this that all that exists, rests and it does not go beyond this

units.sanskrit: या वै सैवंलक्षणा सर्वभूतरूपा गायत्री, इयं वाव सा येयं पृथिवी ।
units.english: That which is the Gāyatrī, described above as constituting all things,is indeed this that is known as the Earth

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनरियं पृथिवी गायत्रीति,
units.english: In what way is this Earth Gayātrī?

units.sanskrit: उच्यतेसर्वभूतसम्बन्धात् ।
units.english: Answer Because of its connection with all that exists

units.sanskrit: कथं सर्वभूतसम्बन्धः,
units.english: In what way is it connected with all that exists?

units.sanskrit: अस्यां पृथिव्यां हि यस्मात्सर्वं स्थावरं जङ्गमं च भूतं प्रतिष्ठितमेतामेव पृथिवीं नातिशीयते नातिवर्तत इत्येतत् ।
units.english: Because all that existsanimate as well as inanimate,rests upon this Earth; it does not go beyond this;that is, it has no existence apart from it

units.sanskrit: यथा गानत्राणाभ्यां भूतसम्बन्धो गायत्र्या एवं भूतप्रतिष्ठानादुभूतसम्बद्धा पृथिव्यतो गायत्री पृथिवी ॥
units.english: Just as the connection of the Gāyatrī with all things is due to its singing and protecting, in the same manner the Earth is connected with all things, because all things rest upon it; in this way Gāyatrī is the Earth

units.sanskrit: या वै सा पृथिवीयं वाव सा यद् इदम् अस्मिन् पुरुषे शरीरम् ।
units.english: That which is Earth is verily that which is the Body in Man;

units.sanskrit: एतद् एव नातिशीयन्ते ॥
units.english: it is on this that the Vital Airs rest and they do not go beyond it

units.sanskrit: या वै सा पृथिवी गायत्रीयं वाव सेदमेव । तत्किं, यदिदमस्मिन्पुरुषे कार्यकारणसङ्घाते जीवति शरीरं पार्थिवत्वाच्छरीरस्य ।
units.english: That which is the Earthand Gāyatrīis thatWhat is it?It is that which, in living man,as representing an aggregate of causes and effectsis the body; this Body being constituted of Earth

units.sanskrit: कथं शरीरस्य गायत्रीत्वमिति ।
units.english: In what way is the Body, the Gāyatrī?

units.sanskrit: उच्यतेअस्मिन्हीमे प्राणा भूतशब्दवाच्याः प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
units.english: Answer It is on this that rest all these Vital Airsknown by the name ‘Bhūta’ ‘Beings

units.sanskrit: अतः पृथिवीवद्भूतशब्दवाच्यप्राणप्रतिष्ठानाच्छरीरं गायत्री । एतदेव यस्माच्छरीरं नातिशीयन्ते प्राणाः ॥
units.english: Thus, inasmuch as, like the Earth, the Body is the resting place of Vital Airs called by the name ‘Beings’,the Body is the Gāyatrī also, because these Vital Airs do not go beyond this Body

units.sanskrit: यद् वै तत् पुरुषे शरीरम् इदं वाव तद् यद् इदम् अस्मिन्न् अन्तः पुरुषे हृदयम् ।
units.english: That which is the Body in Man is that which is the Heart within the Man

units.sanskrit: अस्मिन् हीमे प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
units.english: Because it is therein that the Vital Airs rest;

units.sanskrit: एतद् एव नातिशीयन्ते ॥
units.english: and they do not go beyond it

units.sanskrit: यद्व तत्पुरुषे शरीरं गायत्रीदं वाव तत् । यदिदमस्मिन्नन्तर्मध्ये पुरुषे हृदयं पुण्डरीकाख्यमेतद्गायत्री ।
units.english: That which is the Body in manwhich is Gāyatrī,is that which, within the Man, is the Heart, known by the name of ‘Puṇḍarīka’, ‘white lotus’; and this is Gāyatrī

units.sanskrit: कथमित्याहअस्मिन्हीमे प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठिता अतः शरीरवद्गायत्री हृदयम् । एतदेव च नातिशीयन्ते प्राणाः ।
units.english: How?Because it is therein that the Vital Airs rest; hence like the Body, the Heart, is Gāyatrī, and this it is beyond which the Vital Airs do not go

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ह पिता । प्राणो माता । इति,अहिंसन्सर्वभूतानिइति च श्रुतेर्भूतशब्दवाच्याः प्राणाः ॥
units.english: That the Vital Airs are meant to be denoted by the term ‘Bhūta’, ‘being’, is indicated by such Vedic Texts as‘The Vital Air is father, the Vital Air is mother’,‘Not injuring any beings’ etc

units.sanskrit: सैषा चतुष्पदा षड्विधा गायत्री । तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्यनूक्तम् ॥
units.english: This Gāyatrī is fourfooted and sixfold;this has been thus declared in the following verse

units.sanskrit: सैषा चतुष्पदा षडक्षरपदा छन्दोरूपा सती भवति गायत्री षड्विधा वाग्भूतपृथिवीशरीरहृदयप्राणरूपा सती षड्विधा भवति
units.english: This Gāyatrī, in the form of the metre, being fourfooted,each of the four feet consisting of six letters,is sixfold; ie, it becomes sixfold,in the form of Speech, Being, Earth, Body, Heart and Vital Airs

units.sanskrit: वाक्प्राणयोरन्यार्थनिर्दिष्टयोरपि गायत्रीप्रकारत्वम् ।
units.english: Though Speech and Vital Airs have been spoken of as something else, yet these also are forms of Gāyatrī;

units.sanskrit: अन्यथा षड्विधसंख्यापूरणानुपपत्तेः ।
units.english: otherwise the number six would not be completed

units.sanskrit: तदेतस्मिन्नर्थ एतद्गीयत्र्याख्यं ब्रह्म गायत्र्यनुगतं गायत्रीमुखेनोक्तमृचापि मन्त्रेणाभ्यनूक्तं प्रकाशितम् ॥
units.english: This same idea,that the Brahman named ‘Gāyatrī’ is represented by the Gāyatrīwhich has been just expounded through the Gāyatrī,has also been declaredexpressed,in the following verseMantraText

units.sanskrit: तावान् अस्य महिमा ततो ज्यायांश् च पुरुषः ।
units.english: ‘Such is His Greatness; greater than that is Puruṣa the Ensouling Entity;

units.sanskrit: पादो ऽस्य सर्वा भूतानि त्रिपाद् अस्यामृतं दिवीति ॥
units.english: all beings are His foot; He is the threefooted immortal, in its Heaven

units.sanskrit: तावानस्य गायत्र्याख्यस्य ब्रह्मणः समस्तस्य महिमा विभूतिविस्तारः ।
units.english: Of the whole Brahman named Gāyatrī, such is the greatnessmajesty, extensive grandeur;

units.sanskrit: यावांश्चतुष्पात्षड्विधश्च ब्रह्मणो विकारः पादो गायत्रीति व्याख्यातः ।
units.english: ie, the greatness that has been described by the mention of the fact that Gāyatrī is the ‘Foot’ of Brahman evolving out of Brahman, fourfooted and sixfold

units.sanskrit: अतस्तस्माद्विकारलक्षणाद्गायत्र्याख्याद्वाचारम्भणमात्रात्ततो ज्यायान्महत्तरश्च परमार्थसत्यरूपो ऽविकारः पूरुषः पुरुषः सर्वपूरणात्पुरि शयनाच्च । तस्यास्य पादः सर्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि तेजोबन्नादीनि सस्थावरजङ्गमानि ।
units.english: Greater than that,ie vaster than the said named ‘Gāyatrī’, which is a mere product of Speech, is the Puruṣa, which is essentially real and unchangeable; this Puruṣa being so called because He fills ie pervades all Pūraṇāt and because He lies within the body Puri śayanāt;of this latter, all beings are the foot, all such beings as light, water, food and the rest, both animate and inanimate

units.sanskrit: त्रिपात्त्रयः पादा अस्य सो ऽयं त्रिपात् । त्रिपादमृतं पुरुषाख्यं समस्तस्य गायत्र्यात्मनो दिवि द्योतनवति स्वात्मन्यवस्थितमित्यर्थ इति ॥
units.english: He is the threefooted,that which has three feet,is immortalcalled ‘Puruṣa’in its Heaven,resting in the Heaven of what forms the entire Gāyatrī; it is called ‘Heaven’‘dyaus’because it is resplendent The meaning is that it rests within itself

units.sanskrit: यद् वै तद् ब्रह्मेतीदं वाव तद् यो ऽयं बहिर्धा पुरुषाद् आकाशः ।
units.english: That which is that Brahman, this indeed is that which is the Ākāśa outside the Puruṣa;the Ākāśa, outside the Puruṣa

units.sanskrit: यद्वै तत् त्रिपादमृतं गायत्रीमुखेनोक्तं ब्रह्मेतीदं वाव तदिदमेव । तद्यो ऽयं प्रसिद्धो बहिर्धा बहिः पुरुषादाकाशो भौतिको यो वै स बहिर्धा पुरुषादाकाश उक्तः ॥
units.english: That Brahman which is the threefooted immortalwhich has been described through the Gāyatrī,is indeed this, which is known as the Ākāśa outside the Puruṣa,ie the elemental substance Ākāśa which lies outside the Puruśa

units.sanskrit: अयं वाव स यो ऽयम् अन्तः पुरुष आकाशः । यो वै सो ऽन्तः पुरुष आकाशः ॥
units.english: This indeed is that Ākāśa which lies within the Puruṣa,that Ākāśa which lies within the Puruṣa

units.sanskrit: अयं वाव स यो ऽयमन्तः पुरुषे शरीर आकाशो यो वै सो ऽन्तः पुरुष आकाशः ॥
units.english: This indeed is that Ākāśa which lies within the Puruṣa,ie, inside the body,that Ākāśa which lies within the Puruṣa

units.sanskrit: अयं वाव स यो ऽयम् अन्तर्हृदय आकाशः ।
units.english: This indeed is that Ākāśa which is in the heart;

units.sanskrit: तद् एतत् पूर्णम् अप्रवर्ति ।
units.english: this is complete, unmoving;

units.sanskrit: पूर्णम् अप्रवर्तिनीं श्रियं लभते य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: one who knows thus obtains complete and unmoving prosperity

units.sanskrit: अयं वाव स यो ऽयमन्तर्हृदये हृदयपुण्डरीक आकाशः ।
units.english: This indeed is that Ākāśa which is in the heart,in the lotus of the heart

units.sanskrit: कथमेकस्य सत आकाशस्य त्रिधा भेद इति ।
units.english: QuestionHow can Ākāśa, which is one only, have three divisions as described in the last three texts?

units.sanskrit: उच्यतेबाह्येन्द्रियविषये जागरितस्थाने नभसि दुःखबाहुल्यं दृश्यते । ततो ऽन्तःशरीरे स्वप्नस्थानभूते मन्दतरं दुःखं भवति स्वप्नान्पश्यतः ।
units.english: Answera In that Ākāśa which is perceptible by the external senseorgan ear, and is the sphere of waking consciousness, we find an excess of suffering and pain b Slightly less than this amount of suffering and pain is the amount of pain found in the Ākāśa within the body, which is the sphere of Dreamcognition, while the man is going through the dreamexperiences

units.sanskrit: हृदयस्थे पुनर्नभसि न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति ।
units.english: c In that Ākāśa which lies within the heart one does not desire any desires, and does not dream any dreams;

units.sanskrit: अतः सर्वदुःखनिवृत्तिरूपमाकाशं सुषुप्तस्थानम् ।
units.english: hence this Ākāśa, which represents the cessation of all suffering and pain, constitutes the sphere of deep sleep

units.sanskrit: अतो युक्तमेकस्यापि त्रिधा भेदान्वाख्यानम् ।
units.english: In its way, it is only right that one and the same Ākāśa should be described in three forms

units.sanskrit: बहिर्धा पुरुषादारभ्या'काशस्य हृदये सङ्कोचकरणं चेतःसमाधानस्थानस्तुतये ।
units.english: Beginning with the Ākāśa outside the Puruṣa, the Text has gradually contracted the sphere of the Ākāśa to within the Heart,for the purpose of eulogising the spot on which the mind is to be concentrated;

units.sanskrit: यथात्रयाणामपि लोकानां कुरुक्षेत्रं विशिष्यते । अर्धतस्तु कुरुक्षेत्रमर्धतस्तु पृथूदकमिति तद्वत् ।
units.english: just as we find in such texts as‘In all the three regions Kurukṣetra is marked out as the best place, half of it is Kurukṣetra and half is Pṛthūdaka’

units.sanskrit: तदेतद्धार्दाकाशाख्यं ब्रह्म पूर्णं सर्वगतं न हृदयमात्रपरिच्छिन्नमिति मन्तव्यम् । यद्यपि हृदयाकाशे चेतः समाधीयते ऽप्रवर्ति न कुतश्चित्क्वचित्प्रवर्तितुं शीलमस्येत्यप्रवर्ति तदनुच्छित्तिधर्मकम् ।
units.english: This Brahman, known as ‘the Ākāśa in the Heart’ is complete,ie it should be regarded as omnipresent, not limited within the Heart, though it is true that the Mind is concentrated in the Heart;it is unmoving;ie by its very nature it is incapable of moving anywhere or under any influence;

units.sanskrit: यथान्यानि भूतानि परिच्छिन्नान्युच्छित्तिधर्मकाणि न तथा हार्दं नभः ।
units.english: ie by its nature it is unperishable As a matter of fact, Ākāśa in the Heart is not limited and perishable as the other elemental substances are

units.sanskrit: पूर्णामप्रवर्तिनीमनुच्छेदात्मिकां श्रियं विभूतिं गुणफलं लभते दृष्टं य एवं यथोक्तं पूर्णाप्रवर्तिगुणं ब्रह्म वेद जानातीहैव जीवंस्तद्भावं प्रतिपद्यत इत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: He obtains complete and unmovingimperishableprosperity, glory, as the visible reward of his qualification, who knows the said Brahman complete and unmoving; that is, even during this very life, he becomes merged in that Brahman

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा एतस्य हृदयस्य पञ्च देवसुषयः ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse In that Heart, there are five divine holes;

units.sanskrit: स यो ऽस्य प्राङ् सुषिः स प्राणः । तच् चक्षुः ।
units.english: that which is its Eastern Hole is Prāṇa, it is the Eye, it is the Sun

units.sanskrit: तद् एतत् तेजो ऽन्नाद्यम् इत्य् उपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon this, as light, water and food;

units.sanskrit: तेजस्व्य् अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: one who knows this becomes resplendent and Eater of Food

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा इत्यादिना गायत्र्याख्यस्य ब्रह्मण उपासनाङ्गत्वेन द्वारपालादिगुणविधानार्थमारभ्यते ।
units.english: With the words ‘In that Heart etc,’ the text proceeds to describe the gates, results and other details as forming part of the meditation of Brahman called ‘Gāyatrī’

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके द्वारपाला राज्ञ उपासनेन वशीकृता राजप्राप्त्यर्था भवन्ति तथेहापीति ।
units.english: In the ordinary world, when the Gatekeepers of the King, on being won over, help a person desiring to see the King to approach the King;

units.sanskrit: तस्येति प्रकृतस्य हृदयस्येत्यर्थः । एतस्यानन्तरनिर्दिष्टस्य पञ्च पञ्चसंख्याका देवानां सुषयो देवसुषयः स्वर्गलोकप्राप्तिद्वारच्छिद्राणि
units.english: If that,ie if the Heart, which forms the subjectmatter of the context‘etasya’ stands for what is mentioned next;there are fivein numberdivine holes,ie the ‘holes of Deities’; these are the holes which serve as gates through which persons, proceed to the celestial regions;

units.sanskrit: देवेः प्राणादित्यादिभी रक्ष्यमाणानीत्यतो देवसुषयस्तस्य स्वर्गलोकभवनस्य हृदयस्यास्य
units.english: and these holes are guarded by Prāṇa lifebreath, Āditya Sun and other divinities; hence they are called ‘Divine holes’

units.sanskrit: यः प्राङ्सुषिः पूर्वाभिमुखस्य प्राग्गतं यच्छिद्रं द्वारं स प्राणस्तत्स्थस्तेन
units.english: Of this Heart, which is the Palace of the Regions, that which is the Eastern Hole,ie the holegate towards the East where the person is standing facing the East,is the Lifebreath, Prāṇa;

units.sanskrit: द्वारेण यः सञ्चरति वायुविशेषः स प्रागनितीति प्राणः ।
units.english: located therein, it is so called because the air breath that passes through that hole moves eastward prāganitiPrāṇiti

units.sanskrit: तेनैव सम्बद्धमव्यतिरिक्तं तच्चक्षुस्तथैव स आदित्यःआदित्यो ह वै बाह्यः प्राणःइति श्रुतेश्चक्षूरूपप्रतिष्ठाक्रमेण हृदि स्थितः ।
units.english: this Prāṇa resides in the Heart, in the order of Eye, Colour and Residence [the Sun residing in the Eye, the Eye apprehending Colour and hence residing therein; and thus the Lifebreath is the same as the Eye

units.sanskrit: स आदित्यः कस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठित इति चक्षुषिइत्यादि हि वाजसनेयके ।
units.english: says Ānandagiri]; all this is thus stated in the Vājasaneyaka the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad in the words‘Wherein does the Sun reside In the Eye’ and so on

units.sanskrit: प्राणवायुदेवतैव ह्येका चक्षुरादित्यश्च सहाऽश्रयेण ।
units.english: The one Divinity of the Lifebreath is the eye as well as the sun along with their substrates

units.sanskrit: वक्ष्यति चप्राणाय स्वाहेति हतुं हविः सर्वमेतत्तर्पयतीति ।
units.english: The Text itself is going to declare later on that ‘when the offering is formed with words ‘Prāṇāyasvāhā this to the Lifebreath, it satisfies all this’

units.sanskrit: तदेत्प्राणाख्यं स्वर्गलोकद्वारपालत्वाद्ब्रह्म ।
units.english: This Hole then, which is called ‘Lifebreath’ is the gatekeeper of the celestial regions, and hence it is Brahman

units.sanskrit: स्वर्गलोकं प्रतिपित्सुस्तेजश्चैतच्चक्षुरादित्यस्वरूपेण, अन्नाद्यत्वाच्च सवितुस्तेजो ऽन्नाद्यमित्याभ्यां गुणाभ्यामुपासीत ।
units.english: Therefore one who seeks to reach the celestial Regions should meditate upon this through the qualities of Light, in the form of the Eye and the Sun,and food,on account of the Sun being the giver of food

units.sanskrit: ततस्तेजस्व्यन्नादश्चा'मयावित्वरहितो भवति य एवं वेद तस्यैतद्गुणफलम् ।
units.english: By so doing, the man becomes resplendent and Eater of food;he becomes free from disease This reward accrues to one who knows this subject thus

units.sanskrit: उपासनेन वशीकृतो द्वारपः स्वर्गलोकप्राप्ति हेतुर्भवतीति मुख्यं च फलम् ॥
units.english: Thus the gatekeeper, having become pleased by the meditation attendance, helps the man to enter the celestial Regions This is the main reward becoming resplendent and foodeater being subsidiaries

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्य दक्षिणः सुषिः स व्यानः ।
units.english: That which is its Southern Hole is Vyāna;

units.sanskrit: तच् छ्रोत्रम् ।
units.english: it is the Ear;

units.sanskrit: स चन्द्रमाः ।
units.english: it is the Moon

units.sanskrit: तद् एतच् छ्रीश् च यशश् चेत्य् उपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon this as Prosperity and Glory

units.sanskrit: श्रीमान् यशस्वी भवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows thus becomes prosperous and glorious

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्य दक्षिणः सुषिस्तत्स्थो वायुविशेषः स वीर्यवत्कर्म कुर्वन्विगृह्य वा प्राणापानौ,
units.english: That which is its Southern Hole,the Air Breath located therein is Vyāna;so called because it performs vigorous functions, or functions Aniti through setting Prāṇa against Apāna, or functions in various ways

units.sanskrit: नाना वानितीति व्यानस्तत्सम्बद्धमेव च तच्छ्रोत्रमिन्द्रियं तथा स चन्द्रमाः । श्रोत्रेण सृष्टा दिशश्च चन्द्रमाश्चेति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: Related to this is the Ear, the Auditory Organ,and also the Moon; this is on the basis of the Vedic Text that ‘It was through the auditory organ that the quarters of the moon were created’;

units.sanskrit: सहाश्रयौ पूर्ववत्तदेतच्छ्रीश्च विभूतिः श्रोत्रचन्द्रमसोर्ज्ञानान्नहेतुत्वमतस्ताभ्यां श्रीत्वम् । ज्ञानान्नवतश्च यशः ख्यातिर्भवतीति यशोहेतुत्वाद्यशस्त्वमतस्ताभ्यां गुणाभ्यामुपासीतेत्यादि समानम् ॥
units.english: One should meditate upon this as Prosperity and Glorybecause the Ear and the Moon are the origin respectively of perception and food, they have the character of prosperity and as the man with knowledge and food becomes famous, and hence as being the source of knowledge and fame, they have the character of glory; hence one should meditate upon the Hole through these two qualities etc, etc,as before

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्य प्रत्यङ् सुषिः सो ऽपानः ।
units.english: That which is its western Hole is Apāna;

units.sanskrit: सा वाक् । सो ऽग्निः ।
units.english: it is Speech and it is Fire

units.sanskrit: तद् एतद् ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अन्नाद्यम् इत्य् उपासीत । ब्रह्मवर्चस्य् अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One should meditate upon this as Brahmic Glory and Food One who knows this becomes endowed with Brahmic glory and an eater of, food

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्य प्रत्यङ्सुषिः पश्चिमस्तत्स्थो वायुविशेषः स मूत्रपुरीषाद्यपनयन्नधो ऽनितीत्यपानः सा तथा वाक् ।
units.english: That which is its Western Hole is Apāna; the particular Air Breath located there,so called because as tending to the evacuation of urine and fæces, it operates downwards adhaḥ aniti

units.sanskrit: तत्सम्बन्धात्तथाग्निस्तदेतद्ब्रह्मवर्चसं,
units.english: It is speech,being related thereto;it is also Fire

units.sanskrit: वृत्तस्वाध्यायनिमित्तं तेजो ब्रह्मवर्चसम् ।
units.english: This should be meditated upon as Brahmic gloryglory that comes to one from the complete mastery of the Veda;

units.sanskrit: अग्निसम्बन्धाद्वृत्तस्वाध्यायस्य । अन्नघ्रसनहेतुत्वादपानस्यान्नाद्यत्वम् । समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: it is so called because the completion of Vedic study is connected with fire,and as food,the Apāna Breath being the means whereby food is swallowed;the rest is as before

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्योदङ् सुषिः स समानः ।
units.english: That which is its northern Hole is Samāna;

units.sanskrit: तन् मनः ।
units.english: it is Mind;

units.sanskrit: स पर्जन्यः ।
units.english: it is Parjanya;

units.sanskrit: तद् एतत् कीर्तिश् च व्युष्टिश् चेत्युपासीत ।
units.english: one should meditate upon this as Fame and Lustre

units.sanskrit: कीर्तिमान् व्युष्टिमान् भवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows this becomes famous and lustrous

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्योदङ्सुषिरुदग्गतः सुषिस्तत्स्यो वायुविशेषः सो ऽशितपीते समं नयतीति समानः ।
units.english: That which is its northern Hole,ie the one towards the North,that is, the particular Air located therein,is Samāna, in the sense that it levels up Samānayati what is eaten and drunk

units.sanskrit: तत्सम्बद्धं मनो ऽन्तःकरणं स पर्जन्यो वृष्ट्यात्मको देवः पर्जन्यनिमित्ताश्चा'प इति ।
units.english: Related to that is the Mind,the Internal Organ; it is Parjanya, ie the deity consisting of Rain, as also water, which is the origin of Parjanya as declared in the Vedic Text

units.sanskrit: मनसा सृष्टा आपश्च वरुणश्चैति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: ‘By the Mind are created Water and Varuṇa’

units.sanskrit: तदेत्कीर्तिश्च । मनसो ज्ञानस्य कीर्तिहेतुत्वात् ।
units.english: This is also fame,the knowledge of Mind being a source of fame

units.sanskrit: आत्मपरोक्षं वुश्रुतत्वं कीर्तिः । यशः स्वकरणसंवेद्यं विश्रुतत्वम् ।
units.english: Fame consists in being known and talked of behind one’s back; while glory spoken in text is selfrecogniśed worthiness;

units.sanskrit: व्युष्टिः कान्तिर्देहगतं लावण्यम् ।
units.english: and lustre is brightness of the body, charm;

units.sanskrit: ततश्च कीर्तिसम्भवात्कीर्तिश्चेति ।
units.english: this also is a sort of fame, as it is a source of fame

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्योर्ध्वः सुषिः स उदानः ।
units.english: That which is its upper Hole is Udāna;

units.sanskrit: स वायुः ।
units.english: it is Air;

units.sanskrit: स आकाशः ।
units.english: it is Ākāśa;

units.sanskrit: तद् एतद् ओजश् च महश् चेत्य् उपासीत ।
units.english: one should meditate upon it as Strength and Greatness;

units.sanskrit: ओजस्वी महस्वान् भवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: one who knows this becomes strong and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यो ऽस्योर्ध्वः सुषिः स उदान आ पादलादारभ्योर्ध्वमुत्क्रमणादुत्कर्षार्थं
units.english: That which is its upper Hole is Udāna; so called because it proceeds upward from the sole of the feet, and also because it aids all acts for one’s improvement

units.sanskrit: च कर्म कुर्वन्ननितीत्युदानः स वायुस्तदाधारश्चा'काशस्तदेतद्वाय्वाकाशयोरोजोहेतुत्वादोजो बलं महत्वाच्च मह इति ।
units.english: It is Air, and also Ākāśa, the substratum of Air As these two, Air and Water, are the source of strength, it should be meditated upon as strength and as greatness, because it is great

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: ते वा एते पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषाः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपाः ।
units.english: Verily these are the five Brahmic Personalities, the Gatekeepers of the Region of Heaven

units.sanskrit: स य एतान् एवं पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषान् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान् वेदास्य कुले वीरो जायते ।
units.english: If one who thus knows these five Brahmic Personalities as the Gatekeepers of the Region of Heaven,in his family is born a heroic person

units.sanskrit: प्रतिपद्यते स्वर्गं लोकं य एतान् एवं पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषान् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान् वेद ॥
units.english: One who thus knows these five Brahmic Personalities as the Gatekeepers of the Region of Heaven, himself reaches the Region of Heaven

units.sanskrit: ते वा एते यथोक्ताः पञ्चसुषिसम्बन्धात्पञ्च ब्रह्मणो हार्दस्य पुरषा राजपुरुषा इव द्वारस्थाः स्वर्गस्य हार्दस्य लोकस्य द्वारपा द्वारपालाः ।
units.english: These five,as described abovepersonalities connected with the five Holes,the Brahmic Personalitiespersonalities related to the Brahman in the Heart,in the same way as the Gatekeepers are related to the King,so are these personalities the Gatekeeperskeepers of the gateof the Region of Heaven,ie of the Heart

units.sanskrit: एतैर्हि चक्षुःश्रोत्रवाङ्मनःप्राणैर्बहिर्मुखप्रवृत्तैर्ब्रह्मणो हार्दस्य प्राप्तिद्वाराणि निरुद्धनि ।
units.english: In fact all the doors of approaching the Brahman within the Heart are barred by these Personalities, in the form of eyes, ear, speech, mind and lifebreath,as functioning outwards

units.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं ह्येतदजितकरणतया बाह्यविषयासङ्गानृतप्ररूढत्वान्न हार्दे ब्रह्मणि मनस्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: It is a wellrecognised fact that, so long as the said organs have not been brought under control, the mind remains attached to external things, and thus rooted in unreality, it cannot be fixed upon Brahman

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्सत्यमुक्तमेते पञ्च ब्रह्मपुरुषाः स्वर्गस्य द्वारपा इति । अतः स य एतानेवं यथोक्तगुणविशिष्टान्स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारपान्वेदोपास्त उपासनया वशीकरोति स राजद्वारपालानिवोपासनेन वशीकृत्य तैरनिवारितः प्रतिपद्यते स्वर्गं लोर्क राजानमिव हार्दं ब्रह्म ।
units.english: Hence it has been rightly said that these five Brahmic Personalities are the Gatekeepers of the Region of Heaven, As a consequence of this, if one knowsie meditates uponcontrols by meditationthese Gatekeepers of the Region of Heaven, as described above with certain qualifications, reaches the Region of Heaven, and also the Brahman in the Heart,just as a man who has won over the warders of the King, is not prevented by them and hence reaches the King

units.sanskrit: किञ्चास्य विदुषः कुले वीरः पुत्रो जायते वीरपुरुषसेवनात् ।
units.english: Further, in the family of this knowing person, a heroic son is born, through his attendance upon a heroic Personality

units.sanskrit: तस्य चर्णापाकरणेन ब्रह्मोपासनप्रवृत्तिहेतुत्वम् ।
units.english: And inasmuch as such a person would clear off his father’s debts, he would be the indirect cause of turning his father’s attention towards meditation upon Brahman;

units.sanskrit: ततश्च स्वर्गलोकप्रतिपत्तये पारम्पर्येण भवतीति स्वर्गलोकप्रतिपत्तिरेवैकं फलम ॥
units.english: and thus indirectly he becomes capable of reaching the Heavenly Region;so that the reaching of the Heavenly Region is the one great Reward

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् अतः परो दिवो ज्योतिर् दीप्यते विश्वतःपृष्ठेषु सर्वतःपृष्ठेष्व् अनुत्तमेषूत्तमेषु लोकेष्व् इदं वाव तद् यद् इदम् अस्मिन्न् अन्तः पुरुषे
units.english: Now, that light which shines above this Heaven,above the Universe, above all,in Unexcelled Regions,in highest Regions,is this same light within the man

units.sanskrit: तस्यैषा दृष्टिर् यत्रैतद् अस्मिञ् छरीरे संस्पर्शेनोष्णिमानं विजानाति ।
units.english: Its visibility lies in this that on touching the body one has the perception of warmth

units.sanskrit: तस्यैषा श्रुतिर् यत्रैतत् कर्णाव् अपिगृह्य निनदम् इव नदथुर् इवाग्नेर् इव ज्वलत उपशृनोति ।
units.english: Its audibility lies in this that on closing the ears, one hears something like rumbling, like bellowing,like the flaming of fire

units.sanskrit: तद् एतद् दृष्टं च श्रुतं चेत्य् उपासीत । चक्षुष्यः श्रुतो भवति य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One should meditate upon this as seen and heard, One who knows this, thus becomes conspicuous and celebrated,yea, one who knows this

units.sanskrit: अथ यदसौ विद्वान्स्वर्गं लोकं वीरपुरुषसेवनात्प्रतिपद्यते ।
units.english: Two statements have been made in this Discourse that the man who knows all this reaches the Heavenly Region by attending upon a heroic person, and that ‘He is the threefooted immortal in its Heaven’ Sec

units.sanskrit: यच्चोक्तंत्रिपादस्यामृतं दिवीति तदिदं लिङ्गेन चक्षुःश्रोत्रेन्द्रियगोचरमापादयितव्यम्,
units.english: , verse ;and all this has been renderedby means of a proper indicativeamenable to perception by the eye and ear;

units.sanskrit: यथाग्न्यादि धूमादिलिङ्गेन । तथा ह्येवमेवेदमिति यथोक्ते ऽथ दृढ प्रतीतिः स्यात् ।
units.english: just as fire is rendered cognisable by means of smoke as the indicative;in this way would follow the firm conviction that the fact is really as stated;

units.sanskrit: अनन्यत्वेन च निश्चय इति ।
units.english: and that the truth could not be otherwise than this

units.sanskrit: अत आहयदतो ऽमुष्माद्दिवो द्युलोकात्परः परमिति लिङ्गव्यत्ययेन । ज्योतिर्दीप्यते । स्वयंप्रभं सदाप्रकाशत्वाद्दीप्यते इव दीप्यत इत्युच्यते ।
units.english: This is what is asserted in the present text That light which shines above this Heaven,the neuter form ‘param’ being construed as masculine, ‘paraḥ’, which is selfluminous, and everluminous,it appears to be shining;

units.sanskrit: अग्न्यादिवाज्ज्वलनलक्षणाया दीप्तेरसम्भवात् । विश्वतः पृष्ठेष्वित्येतस्य व्याख्यान सर्वतः पृष्ठेष्विति ।
units.english: actual shining like fire being impossible in this case;above the Universe,this phrase is explained by the next phrase, above all,ie above the world, the world being all, what is notworldly being one and without distinction;

units.sanskrit: संसारादुपरीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: in unexcelled regions;

units.sanskrit: असंसारिण एकत्वान्निर्भेदत्वाच्च । अनुत्तमेषु तत्पुरुषसमासाशङ्कानिवृत्तय आहोत्तमेषु लोकेष्विति सत्यलोकादिषु हिरण्यगर्भादिकार्यस्थपरस्येश्वरस्या'सन्नत्वादुच्यत उत्तमेषु लोकेष्विति । इदं वावेदमेव तद्यदिदमस्मिन्पुरुषे ऽन्तर्मध्ये ज्योतिश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रग्राह्येण लिङ्गेनोष्णिम्ना शब्देन चावगम्यते ।
units.english: in order that the compound Anuttaṃeṣu may not be taken as a Tatpuruṣa compound, in the sense of ‘notuttama’, the text has added the explanatory phrase in the highest regions Inasmuch as in the Satya and other high regions the Supreme Lord residing in Hīraṇyagarbha and other manifestations, is not far off, it is said to shine in the highest regions,It is this same light which is Within the Man,which is apprehended by means of such indicatives as warmth and sound, as perceived by the Eye and the Ear respectively

units.sanskrit: यत्त्वचा स्पर्शरूपेण गृह्यते तच्चक्षुषैव ।
units.english: When something is apprehended by Touch, it is as good as apprehended by the Eye;

units.sanskrit: दृढप्रतीतिकरत्वात्त्वचः ।
units.english: because the organ of touch brings about a firm conviction;

units.sanskrit: अविनाभूतत्वाच्च रूपस्पर्शयोः ।
units.english: and also because colour and touch are invariable concomitants

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनस्तस्य ज्योतिषो लिङ्गं त्वग्दृष्टिगोचरत्वमापद्यत इति,
units.english: QuestionIn what way does the indicative of the Light become perceptible by the organs of Touch and Vision?

units.sanskrit: अस्मिञ्शरीरे हस्तेना'लभ्य संस्पर्शेनोष्णिमानं रूपसहभाविनमुष्णस्पर्शभावं विजानाति ।
units.english: AnswerWhere,at which time,‘etat’ being an adverb,the body is touched by the hand, one feels, by the organ of Touch, warmth,ie there is a feeling of warmth which is concomitant with colour

units.sanskrit: स ह्यूष्णिमा नामरूपव्याकरणाय देहमनुप्रविष्टस्य चैतन्यात्मज्योतिषो लिङ्गमव्यभिचारात् ।
units.english: When this warmth enters the body, it becomes an infallible indicative of the light of the Self which has entered therein for the differentiation of names and forms

units.sanskrit: न हि जीवन्तमात्मानमूष्णिमा व्यभिचरतिउष्ण एव जीविष्यञ्शीतो मरिष्यन्न् इति हि विज्ञायते ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, so long as the man is alive, the said warmth is inseparable from his Self; it is when the body is warm that the man is regarded as living and he is regarded as dead when the body is cold

units.sanskrit: मरणकाले च तेजः परस्यां देवतायामिति परेणाविभागत्वोपगमात् ।
units.english: It has also been declared that ‘at the time of death, the fire goes over to the Highest Deity’, which means that there is no separation between warmth and the Highest Self

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽसाधारमं लिङ्गमौष्ण्यमग्नेरिव धूमः ।
units.english: Hence it follows that Warmth is a distinctive indicative of the Self,just as smoke is of fire

units.sanskrit: अतस्तस्य परस्यैषा दृष्टिः साक्षादिव दर्शनं दर्शनोपाय इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Hence this is the vision, the direct perception,the means of perceivingthe Supreme Self

units.sanskrit: तथा तस्य ज्योतिष एषा श्रुतिः श्रवणंश्रवणोपायो ऽप्युच्यमानः ।
units.english: Of this light, the audioility,hearingmeans of hearingalso is as is going to be described

units.sanskrit: अपिगृह्यापिधायेत्यर्थो ऽङ्गुलिभ्यां प्रोर्णुत्य निनदमिव रथस्येव घोषो निनदस्तमिव शृणोति नदथुरिव ऋषभकूजितमिव शब्दो यथा चाग्नेर्बहिर्ज्वलत एवं शब्दमन्तः
units.english: When a man wishes to hear this indicative of the light, then he closes his ears thus‘etat’ is an adverb;closes, shuts up with the fingers,he hears sounds like rumblingthe sound made by the moving chariot,like bellowing,the sound made by the bull,like the sound made by fire flaming upward,this sound he hears within his own body

units.sanskrit: तथोपासनाच्चक्षुष्यो दर्शनीयः श्रुतो विश्रुतश्च ।
units.english: For these reasons, one should meditate upon this light as seen and heard

units.sanskrit: यत्स्पर्शगुणोपासननिमित्तं फलं तद्रूपे सम्पादयति चक्षुष्य इति ।
units.english: That is, the effect of the meditation of the quality of colour is transmitted to the colour of the body,which becomes conspicuous in appearance;

units.sanskrit: रूपस्पर्शयोः सहभावित्वात् ।
units.english: and the reason for this lies in the fact that colour and touch are concomitants of one another;

units.sanskrit: इष्टत्वाच्च दर्शनीयतायाः ।
units.english: and also because conspicuousness of appearance is very desirable

units.sanskrit: एवं च विद्यायाः फलमुपपन्नं स्यान्न तु मृदुत्वादिस्पर्शवत्त्वे ।
units.english: In this way would the result of knowledge become properly accomplished,which would not be the case if the body only became soft to the touch

units.sanskrit: य एवं यथोक्तौ गुणौ वेद ।
units.english: One who knows the two qualities as described here attains this visible result

units.sanskrit: स्वर्गलोकप्रतिपत्तिस्तूक्तमदृष्टं फलम् ।
units.english: As for the invisible supersensuous result, that has already been described as consisting in the attaining of the Heavenly Region

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यास आदरार्थः ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the importance of the subject

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य त्रयोदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse The ‘threefooted Immortal Brahman’ described above is equipped with endless qualities and endless powers and is capable of being meditated upon in various ways;and of this Brahman, the Text now proceeds to lay down the meditation, as equipped with certain special qualities and powers

units.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्व् इदं ब्रह्म तज्जलान् इति शान्त उपासीत ।
units.english: All this indeed is Brahman, as it originates, becomes •absorbed and lives in It;

units.sanskrit: अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुर् अस्मिंल् लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति ।
units.english: Now, really, the Man consists of Volition; according as his Volition is in this world, so does he become on departing from here;

units.sanskrit: स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥
units.english: hence he should exercise Volition

units.sanskrit: पुनस्तस्यैव त्रिपादमृतस्य ब्रह्मणो ऽनन्तगुणवतो ऽनन्तशक्तेरनेकभेदोपास्यस्य विशिष्टगुणशक्तिमत्वेनोपासनं विधित्सन्नाहसर्वं खल्विति वाक्यालङ्कारार्थो निपातः । इदं जगन्नामरूपविकृतं प्रत्यक्षादिविषयं ब्रह्मकारणं वृद्धतमत्वाद्ब्रह्म ।
units.english: All,the whole ofthis, indeed,this last term is an indeclinable particle introduced as an ornament of speech,ie the whole of this world, differentiated in name and form, as apprehended by senseperception and other means of cognition, is Brahman, the original source, called ‘Brahman’ on account of its being the highest

units.sanskrit: कथं सर्वस्य ब्रह्मत्वमित्यत आहतज्जलानिति ।
units.english: In answer to the question ‘In what way is all this Brahman?’ it is added As it originates, becomes absorbed and lives in It;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्ब्रह्मणो जातं तेजोबन्नादिक्रमेण सर्वम् । अतस्तज्जम् । तथा तेनैव जननक्रमेण प्रतिलोमतया तस्मिन्नेव ब्रह्मणि लीयते तदात्मतया श्लिष्यत इति तल्लम् ।
units.english: all this world has come out of Brahman, gradually, through light, food etc, hence it is said to originate in It;similarly in the same order of coming out, but reversed, the world becomes absorbed in the Brahman becoming one with it hence it is said to become absorbed in It;similarly while the world continues to exist, it lives, moves, operates, in that same Brahman;

units.sanskrit: तथा तस्मिन्नेव स्थितिकाले ऽनिति प्राणिति चेष्टत इति ।
units.english: hence it is said to live in It

units.sanskrit: एवं ब्रह्मात्मतया त्रिषु कालेष्वविशिष्टं तद्व्यतिरेकेणाग्रहणात् । अतस्तदेवेदं जगत् ।
units.english: Thus at all three points of time, the world remains in the Brahman, undifferentiated from It,as is clear from the fact that it is never perceived apart, from It

units.sanskrit: यस्माच्च सर्वमिदं ब्रह्म,
units.english: From this it follows that, all this is Brahman

units.sanskrit: अतः शान्तो रागद्वेषादिदोषरहितः संयतः सन्यत्तत्सर्वं ब्रह्म तद्वक्ष्यमाणैर्गुणैरुपासीत ।
units.english: Inasmuch as all this is Brahman, one should meditate upon that universal Brahman, through the qualities that are going to be described,calmly,ie, free from all love and hate and selfcontrolled

units.sanskrit: कथमुपासीत ।
units.english: In what way should this meditation be carried on?One should exercise Volition;

units.sanskrit: क्रतुं कुर्वीत क्रतुर्निश्चयो ऽध्यवसाय एवमेव नान्यथेत्यविचलः प्रत्ययस्तं क्रतुं कुर्वीतोपासीतेत्यनेन व्यवहितेन सम्बन्धः ।
units.english: Volition is certain cognition, determination, the decision that this shall be so, not otherwise,this one should exercise;

units.sanskrit: किं पुनः क्रतुकरणेन कर्तव्यं प्रयोजनम् ।
units.english: ie thus should one meditate, this being construed from the preceding sentence

units.sanskrit: कथं वा क्रतुः कर्तव्यः क्रतुकरणं चाभिप्रेतार्थसिद्धिसाधनं कथमित्यस्यार्थस्य प्रतिपादनार्थमथेत्यादिग्रन्थः । अथ खल्विति हेत्वर्थः ।
units.english: Question‘What is the purpose to be served by this exercising of Volition How too should this Volition be exercised? How too is this exercising of Volition to accomplish the desired purpose?’In answer to all this, we have the next sentence Now really etc

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्क्रतुमयः क्रतुप्रायो ऽध्यवसायात्मकः पुरुषो जीवः ।
units.english: Because the man consists of Volition,ie the Jīva, the individualised self, is entirely what his Volition is,ie his nature consists of his volition;

units.sanskrit: यथाक्रतुर्यादृशः क्रतुरस्य सो ऽयं यथाक्रतुर्यथाध्यवसायो यादृङ्निश्चयो ऽस्मिंल्लोके जीवन्निह पुरुषो भवति तथेतो ऽस्माद्देहात्प्रेत्य मृत्वा भवति ।
units.english: According as his Volition is in this Worldie according as his volition, determination, is while he is living in this world,so does he become on departing from hereie on his departure from the body, ie on death

units.sanskrit: क्रत्वनुरूपफलात्मको भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: What is meant is that his condition is in accordance with the character of his Volition

units.sanskrit: एवं ह्येतच्छास्रतो दृष्टम् । यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरमित्यादि ।
units.english: This idea is found to be thus expressed in the scriptures;‘Thinking of whatever form, does the man renounce his body to that does he attain’Bhagvadgītā

units.sanskrit: यत एवं व्यवस्था शास्रदृष्टातः स एवं जानन्कतुं कुर्वीत यादृशं क्रतुं वक्ष्यामस्तम् ।
units.english: Inasmuch as such is the conclusion found in the scriptures, the man, knowing all this, should exercise his Volition, perform meditation,that form of meditation which we are going to describe;

units.sanskrit: यत एवं शास्रप्रामाण्यादुपपद्यते क्रत्वनुरूपं फलमतः स कर्तव्यः क्रतुः ॥
units.english: because it is learnt from the scriptures that results accrue to one in accordance with his Volition therefore the said exerciseof meditation,should be performed

units.sanskrit: मनोमयः प्राणशरीरो भारूपः सत्यसंकल्प आकाशात्मा सर्वकर्मा सर्वकामः सर्वगन्धः सर्वरसः सर्वम् इदम् अभ्यत्तो ऽवाक्य् अनादरः ॥
units.english: Consisting of Mind, with the subtle body for his body, of the colour of light, of true volition, of the nature of Ākāśa, the creator of all, alldesire, allodour, alltaste, pervading over all this, without speech, without perturbation

units.sanskrit: कथम् । मनोमयो मनःप्रायः ।
units.english: QuestionIn what manner is one to meditate upon Brahman?

units.sanskrit: मनुते ऽनेनेति मनस्तत्स्ववृत्त्या विषयेषु प्रवृत्तं भवति तेन मनसा तन्मयः,
units.english: AnswerHe is consisting of Mind;Mind is that whereby one thinks; by its very nature it functions over its objectives; it is of this Mind that He consists;

units.sanskrit: तथा प्रवृत्त इव तत्प्रायो निवृत्त इव च ।
units.english: He operates as the Mind operates, and also ceases to operate as the Mind ceases to operate

units.sanskrit: अत एव प्राणशरीरः प्राणो लिङ्गात्मा विज्ञानक्रियाशक्तिद्वयसंमीर्छितः ।
units.english: the term ‘Prāṇa’ here stands for the Subtle Body wherein the Self resides, endowed with the two functions of Cognition and Action;

units.sanskrit: यो वै प्राणः सा प्रज्ञा या वा प्रज्ञा स प्राणःइति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: as declared in the text‘That which is the subtle body is intelligence, that which is intelligence is the subtle body’;

units.sanskrit: स शरीरं यस्य स प्राणशरीरः ।
units.english: it is this Prāṇa that He has for His Body

units.sanskrit: मनोमयः úआणशरीरनेताइति च श्रुत्यन्तरात् । भारूपः । भा दीप्तिश्चैतन्यलक्षणं रूपं यस्य स भारूपः ।
units.english: It is declared in another Vedic Text that ‘He consists of the Mind, the controller of the Body of Prāṇa’Of the colour of light,His form consists of light in the shape of intelligence;of true volition;

units.sanskrit: सत्या अवितथाः सङ्कल्पा यस्य सो ऽयं सत्यसङ्कल्पः ।
units.english: ie his volitions, wishes, are all true, infallible;

units.sanskrit: न यथा संसारिण इवानैकान्तिकफलः सङ्कल्प ईश्वरस्येत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is to say, the volition of God is not like the volition of the ordinary worldly man, whose volition is not always sure of fruition

units.sanskrit: अनृतेन मिथ्याफलत्वहेतुना प्रत्यूढत्वात्सङ्कल्पस्य मिथ्याफलत्वम् ।
units.english: The volition of the ordinary man is generally beset with untruth, which leads to the falsity of its result; this is what makes the volition false in its fruition;

units.sanskrit: वक्ष्यत्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढा इति ।
units.english: this is going to be described later on in the text‘Beset with untruth etc

units.sanskrit: आकाशात्मा । आकाश इवा'त्मा स्वरूपं यस्य स आकाशात्मा । सर्वगतत्वं सूक्ष्मत्वं रूपदिहीनत्वं चा'काशतुल्यतेश्वरस्य ।
units.english: etc’Of the nature of Ākāśa;He whose form is like the Ākās a; God is like Akāśa, in the sense that He is allpervading, subtle and devoid of colour and other qualities

units.sanskrit: सर्वकर्मा । सर्वं विश्वं तेनेश्वरेण क्रियत इति जगत्सर्वं कर्मास्य स सर्वकर्मा । स हि सर्वस्य कर्ताइति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: The creator of all;the entire universe is created by God; hence the whole universe is his work; that is how He is the creator of all as declared in the Vedic Text‘He is the creator of all’

units.sanskrit: सर्वे कामा दोषरहिता अस्येति सर्वकामः ।
units.english: All desires ie all His desires are free from evil;

units.sanskrit: धर्मविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामो ऽस्मिइति स्मृतेः ।
units.english: as declared in the Smṛtitext‘Among living beings, am such Desire as is not inconsistent with Right’

units.sanskrit: ननु कामो ऽस्मीति वचनादिह बहुव्रीहिस्तथा कामो ऽस्मीतिस्मृत्यर्थो वाच्यः । सर्वगन्धः ।
units.english: For these reasons, the expression ‘ am desire’ in the Smṛtitext quoted is to be taken in the same sense that is afforded by the term ‘alldesire’ taken as a Bahuvrīhicompound

units.sanskrit: सर्वे गन्धाः सुखकरा अस्य सो ऽयं सर्वगन्धः ।
units.english: AllodourHe whose odours are all pleasing;

units.sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यामिति स्मृतेः ।
units.english: as declared in the SmṛtiText‘ am the pure smell in Earth’

units.sanskrit: तथा रसा अपि विज्ञेयाः अपुण्यगन्धरसग्रहणस्य पाप्मसम्बन्धनिमित्तत्वश्रवणात् ।
units.english: Tastes also should be understood in the same way The reason for this lies in the fact that the perception of disagreeable smell and taste has been described as due to the contact of Evil;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तेनोभयं जिघ्रति सुरभि च दुर्गन्धि च । पाप्मना ह्येषु विद्धःइति श्रुतेः । न च पाप्मसंसर्ग ईश्वरस्य, अविद्यादिदोषस्यानुपपत्तेः ।
units.english: as declared in the text‘Therefore, by it one apprehends both agreeable and disagreeable odour, because it is perceived by evil’and God has no contact with evil; as there is no possibility of any such defects in Him as ignorance and the rest

units.sanskrit: सर्वमिदं जगदभ्यात्तो ऽभिव्याप्तः ।
units.english: Pervading overpermeatingall thisuniverse;

units.sanskrit: अततेर्व्याप्त्यर्थस्य कर्तरि निष्ठा । तथावाक्युच्यते ऽनयेति वाग्वागेव वाकः । द्वा वचेर्घञन्तस्य करणे वाक् ।
units.english: the term ‘abhyātta’ being derived from the root ‘atati’, to pervade with the active pastparticipial affix with the prefix ‘abhi’Without speech;‘Vāk’ is that wherewith one speaks;

units.sanskrit: स यस्य विद्यते स वाकी न वाक्यवाकी ।
units.english: one who is endowed with this ‘vāka’ speech, is ‘vākī’; and one who is notVākī is avākī, without speech

units.sanskrit: वाक्प्रतिषेधश्चात्रोपलक्षणार्थः । गन्धरसादिश्रवणादीश्वरस्य प्राप्तानिघ्राणादीनि करणानि गन्धादिग्रहणाय । अतो वाक्प्रतिषेधेन प्रतिषिध्यन्ते तानि ।
units.english: The denial of speech is purely illustrative, it stands for the denial of all those organs of smell, taste and the rest, whose presence in God would be supposed as necessary for the apprehension of smell, taste and other things found mentioned in connection with God; all this is clear also from such Mantratexts as ‘Without hands and feet, He moves fast and holds things;

units.sanskrit: अपाणिपादो जवनो ग्रहीता पश्यत्यचक्षुः स शृणोत्यकर्णःइत्यादिमन्त्रवर्णात् । अनादरो ऽसंभ्रमः । अप्राप्तप्राप्तौ हि संभ्रमः स्यादनाप्तकामस्य ।
units.english: without eyes, He sees; without ears He hears’Without perturbation;not confused; when a man who has not all his desires fulfilled fails to obtain something which he does not possess, he becomes perturbed in mind;

units.sanskrit: न त्वाप्तकामत्वान्नित्यतृप्तस्येश्वरस्य संभ्रमो ऽस्ति क्वचित् ॥
units.english: not so God, who has all his desires fulfilled and is always satisfied and happy; He is never perturbed

units.sanskrit: एष म आत्मा अन्तर्हृदये ऽणीयान् व्रीहेर् वा यवाद् वा सर्षपाद् वा श्यामाकाद् वा श्यामाकतण्डुलाद् वा । एष म आत्मा अन्तर्हृदये ज्यायान् पृथिव्या ज्यायान् अन्तरिक्षाज् ज्यायान् दिवो ज्यायान् एभ्यो लोकेभ्यः ॥
units.english: This is my Self within the heart, smaller than a corn, than barley, than mustard, than the Śyāmākagrain, than the seed of the ŚyāmākagrainThis is my Self within the heart, larger than the Earth, larger than the Sky, larger than Heaven, larger than all these Regions

units.sanskrit: एष यथोक्तगुणो मे ममा'त्मान्तर्हृदये हृदयपुण्डरीकस्यान्तर्मध्ये ऽणीयानणुतरो व्रीहेर्वा यवाद्वेत्याद्यत्यन्तसूक्ष्मत्वप्रदर्शनार्थम्
units.english: Thisthe One described above with the stated qualitiesis my Self, within the heartyin the middle of the lotus of the Heart;smallerin sizethan the corn, than barley etc, etc All this is meant to indicate extreme smallness

units.sanskrit: श्यामाकाद्वा श्यामाकतण्डुलाद्वेति परिच्छिन्नपरिमाणादणीयानित्युक्ते ऽणुपरिमाणत्वं प्राप्तमाशङ्क्यातस्तत्प्रतिषेधाया'रभते एष म आत्मान्तर्हृदये ज्यायान्पृथिव्या इत्यादिना ।
units.english: When the words of the Text have declared the Self to be smaller ‘than the śyāmākagrain, than the seed of the śyāmākagrainit would seem as if it were smaller than all measurable smallness, and hence of the smallest dimension, ie atomic; hence, with a view to preclude such an idea, the text proceeds to addThis is my Self within the heart, larger than the Earth etc, etc

units.sanskrit: ज्यायःपरिमाणाच्च ज्यायस्त्वं दर्शयन्ननन्तपरिमाणत्वं दर्शयति ॥
units.english: By asserting that the size of the Self is larger than all measures of largeness, what is meant is that It is infinite in size

units.sanskrit: सर्वकर्मा सर्वकामः सर्वगन्धः सर्वरसः सर्वम् इदम् अभ्यत्तो ऽवाक्यनादरः । एष म आत्मा अन्तर्हृदये ।
units.english: ‘Allaction, Alldesire, Allodour, Alltaste, pervading over all this, without speech, without perturbation,such is my Self within the heart;

units.sanskrit: एतद् ब्रह्म ।
units.english: it is Brahman;

units.sanskrit: एतम् इतः प्रेत्याभिसंभविता अस्मीति यस्य स्याद् अद्धा न विचिकित्सा अस्ति । इति ह स्माह शाण्डिल्यः शाण्डिल्यः ॥
units.english: shall surely attain that on departing from here,’verily, for one who has this conviction, there is no vacillation or misgiving;so said Śāṇḍilya,yea, Śāṇḍilya

units.sanskrit: मनोमय इत्यादिना ज्यायानेभ्यो लोकेभ्य इत्यन्तेन यथोक्तगुणलक्षण ईश्वरो ध्येयो न तु तद्गुणविशिष्ट एव यथा राजपुरुषमानय चित्रगुं वेत्युक्ते न
units.english: People may have the following ideaGod is surely to be meditated upon in the form indicated by the qualities described,and not as actually endowed with those qualities;just as when it is said, ‘bring the king’s officer who has multicoloured cows’ the man addressed does not proceed to bring the qualification in the shape of the cows;

units.sanskrit: विशेषणश्याप्यानयने व्याप्रियते तद्वदिहापीति प्राप्तमतस्तन्निवृत्त्यर्थ सर्वकर्मेत्यादि पुनर्वचनम् ।
units.english: With a view to preclude this notion, the text reiterates that He is the creator of all etc, et/, the idea being that God should be meditated upon as qualified by the qualifications of consisting of the mind and the rest described above

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्मनोमयत्वादिगुणविशिष्ट एवेश्वरो ध्येयः । अत एव षष्ठसप्तमयोरिव तत्त्वमस्यात्मैवेदं सर्वमिति नेह स्वाराज्ये ऽभिषिञ्चति । एष म आत्मैतद्ब्रह्मैतमितः प्रत्याभिसम्भवितास्मीति लिङ्गान्न त्वात्मशब्देन प्रत्यगात्मैवोच्यते ।
units.english: It is for this reason that what is taught here does not exalt the meditator to that ‘selfsovereignty’ which is attained by the realising of such truths as ‘That Thou Art’,; ‘The Self is all this’, as described under Discourses and ; in fact what the text says here is that ‘Such is my Self, shall surely attain this on departing from here’, which clearly indicates distinction between the human self and the Supreme Self, and it is clear that the term ‘self’ here does not stand for the counterself human self;

units.sanskrit: ममेति षष्ठ्याः सम्बन्धार्थप्रत्यायकत्वादेतमभिसम्भवितास्मीति च कर्मकर्तृत्वनिर्देशात् ।
units.english: because the Genetive ending in ‘mama ātmā’, ‘my self’, connotes relationship, which can only subsist between two distinct things; specially as the phrase ‘ shall attain that’ clearly makes one the human self the active Agent and the other the supreme Self as the objective of attainment

units.sanskrit: ननु षष्ठे ऽप्यथ सम्पत्स्य इति सत्सम्पत्तेः कालान्तरितत्वं दर्शयति ।
units.english: , verse also the expression used is ‘atha sampatsye’ ‘then shall reach perfection’, which clearly shows that the reaching of perfection is further removed in point of time

units.sanskrit: न, आरब्धसंस्कारशेषस्थित्यर्थपरत्वात् न कालान्तरितार्थता ।
units.english: Not so; because what is meant by that expression is the final stage of the process of embellishment, and not any interval of time

units.sanskrit: अन्यथा तत्त्वमसीत्येतस्यार्थस्य बाधप्रसङ्गात् । यद्यप्यात्मशब्दस्य प्रत्यगर्थत्वं सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्मेति च प्रकृतमेष म आत्मान्तर्हृदय एतद्ब्रह्मेत्युच्यते तथाप्यन्तर्धानमीषदपरित्यज्यैवैतमात्मानमितो ऽस्माच्छरीरात्प्रेत्याभिसम्भवितास्मीत्युक्तम् ।
units.english: If it were not so, then this phrase would set aside the idea conveyed by the text ‘That Thou Art’Though it is true that the term ‘Self’ does stand for the human self, that what forms the subjectmatter of the context is Brahman that is all this’, and that this is spoken of as ‘my self within the heart’ and ‘this is Brahman’yet, with all this, when the present Text speaks of ‘reaching that self after departing from here’, it is clear that the distinction between the two is still retained to a certain extent

units.sanskrit: यथाक्रतुरूपस्या'त्मनः प्रतिपत्तास्मीति यस्यैवंविदः स्याद्भवेदद्धा सत्यमेवं स्यामहं प्रेत्य एवं न स्यामिति न च विचिकित्सास्तीत्येतस्मिन्नर्थे क्रतुफलसम्बन्धे स तथैवेश्वरभावं प्रतिपद्यते विद्वानित्येतदाह स्मोक्तवान्किल शाण्डल्यो नामर्षिः ।
units.english: When a man knows this and has the firm conviction ‘ shall attain that Self who is of the nature of volition’, then there is no such uncertainty as ‘may be so, may not be so’; so that in this matter of the connection between the said Volition and the ultimate result, the wise man does attain the position of God;this is what was said by the sage Śāṇḍilya

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यास आदरार्थः ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate respect for the sage

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य चतुर्दशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अस्य कुले वीरो जायत इत्युक्तम् ।
units.english: It has been said above that ‘a heroic person is born in his family’;

units.sanskrit: न वीरजन्ममात्रं पितुस्त्राणाय ।
units.english: but the mere birth of a heroic person is not sufficient for the salvation of the father;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्पुत्रमनुश्ष्टं लोक्यमाहुःइति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । अतस्तद्दीर्घायुष्ट्वं कथं स्यादित्येवमर्थं कोशविज्ञानारम्भः ।
units.english: as has been made clear in the Text‘For this reason it is the Welldisciplined son whom they regard as conducive to the Regions’ Hence it becomes necessary to find out how longevity could be attained in order to enable one to educate his son properly;

units.sanskrit: अभ्यर्हितविज्ञानव्यासङ्गादनन्तरमेव नोक्तं तदिदानीमेवा'रभ्यतेअन्तरिक्षमुदरमन्तःसुषिरं यस्य सो ऽयमन्तरिक्षोदरः कोशः कोश इवानेकधर्मसादृश्यात्कोशः
units.english: and for this a knowledge of the philosophy of the ‘Coffer’ is necessary for which purpose the text proceeds with the next Section This matter was not taken up immediately after the mention of ‘the birth of the heroic son’, because there were more important matters to be expounded

units.sanskrit: स च भूमिबुध्नो भूमिर्बुध्नो मूलं यस्य स भूमिबुध्नो न जीर्यति न विनश्यति त्रैलोक्यात्मकत्वात् ।
units.english: Hence the subject of the ‘Coffers’ is taken up now The Coffer, having the Sky for its inside and the Earth for its bottom, does not decay

units.sanskrit: दिशो ह्यस्य सर्वाः स्रक्तयः कोणाः ।
units.english: The Quarters are its corners; the Heaven is its upper hole

units.sanskrit: द्यौरस्य कोशस्योत्तरमूर्ध्वं बिलं स एष यथोक्तगुणः कोशो वसुधानो वसु धीयते ऽस्मिन्प्राणिनां कर्मफलाख्यमतो वसुधानः ।
units.english: Having the Sky for its insidethat whose inner cavity consists of the Sky,the Coffer,that which resembles the coffer in various qualities such as the following; Having the Earth for its bottom,that of which the Earth is the base

units.sanskrit: यस्मिन्नन्तर्विश्वं समस्तं प्राणिकर्मफलं सह तत्साधनैरिदं यद्गृह्यते प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणैः श्रितमाश्रितं स्थितमित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: ie it is wherein is deposited the entire ‘wealth’ of living beings, in the shape of the results of their actions along with their causes Therein rests, subsists,this Universeall that is perceived through Senseperception and other Means of Cognition

units.sanskrit: तस्य प्राची दिग् जुहूर् नाम । सहमाना नाम दक्षिणा ।
units.english: Its Eastern side is called Juhū\ the Southern side, ‘Sahamānā’;

units.sanskrit: राज्ञी नाम प्रतीची ।
units.english: the Western side, ‘Rājñī’;

units.sanskrit: सुभूता नामोदीची ।
units.english: the Northern side, ‘Subhūtā’

units.sanskrit: तासां वायुर् वत्सः ।
units.english: The Wind is the ‘calf’ of these

units.sanskrit: स य एतम् एवं वायुं दिशां वत्सं वेद न पुत्ररोदं रोदिति ।
units.english: One who thus knows the Wind as the ‘calf’ of the Quarters never weeps for his son

units.sanskrit: सो ऽहम् एतम् एवं वायुं दिशां वत्सं वेद ।
units.english: Verily, do know the Wind as the ‘calf’ of the Quarters;

units.sanskrit: मा पुत्ररोदं रुदम् ॥
units.english: may never weep for my son

units.sanskrit: तस्यास्य प्राची दिग्प्राग्गतो भागो जुहूर्नाम जुह्वत्यस्यां दिशि कर्मिणः प्राङ्मुखाः सन्त इति जुहूनमि ।
units.english: Of the said Coffer, the eastern sidethe part towards the Eastis called ‘Juhū’; it is called ‘Juhū’ because when ritualists are pouring oblations, they do it on this side,themselves facing the East

units.sanskrit: सहमाना मान सहन्ते ऽस्यां पापकर्मफलानि यमपुर्यां प्राणिन इति सहमाना नाम दक्षिणादिक् ।
units.english: The Southern side is called ‘Sahamānā’; this is so called because it is on this side, in the city of Yama, that all living beings suffer the consequences of their evil deeds

units.sanskrit: तथा राज्ञी नाम प्रतीची पश्चिमा दिग्राज्ञी राज्ञा वरुणेनाधिष्ठिता सन्ध्यारागयोगाद्वा ।
units.english: Similarly the Western side is called ‘Rājñī’; so called because it is presided over by the Rājā, Varuṇa; or because it bears the redness of the setting sun

units.sanskrit: सुभूता नाम भूतिमद्भिरीश्वरकुबेरादिभिरधिष्ठितत्वात्सुभूता नामोदीची ।
units.english: The Northern side is called ‘Subhūtā’; so called because it is presided over by such prosperous Bhūtimat personalities as Īśvara, Kubera and the like

units.sanskrit: तासां दिशां वायुर्वत्सो दिग्जत्वाद्वायोः ।
units.english: Of these Quarters, Wind is the calf; so called because the Wind proceeds from the Quarters;

units.sanskrit: पुरोवातैत्यादिदर्शनात् ।
units.english: as is seen in the case of storms

units.sanskrit: स यः कश्चित्पुत्रदीर्घजीवितर्थ्येवं यथोक्तगुणं वायुं दिशां वत्सममृतं वेद स न पुत्ररोदं पुत्रनिमित्तं रोदनं न रोदिति पुत्रो न
units.english: If any one who is desirous of the longevity of his son knows the Wind as described above, as the immortal ‘calf’ of the Quarters, he never Weeps for his son,on account of his son;

units.sanskrit: म्रियत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, his son does not die

units.sanskrit: यत एवं विशिष्टं कोशदिग्वत्सविषयं विज्ञानमतः सो ऽहं पुत्रजीवितार्थ्येवमेतं वायुं दिशां वत्सं वेद जाने । अतो मा पुत्ररोदं रुदं मा रुदं पुत्रमरणनिमित्तम् । पुत्रोरोदो मम मा भूदित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: Because the science of the ‘Coffer’ and the ‘Wind as the calf of the Quarters’ is possessed of such character,therefore, , who am desirous of securing longevity for my son, knowrecognisethe Wind as the calf of the Quarters,May never weep for my son,ie for the death of my son

units.sanskrit: अरिष्टं कोशं प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना ।
units.english: turn to the imperishable Coffer, for such and such and such

units.sanskrit: प्राणं प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना । भूः प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना ।
units.english: turn to Prāṇa, for such and such and such turn to Bhūḥ for such and such and such

units.sanskrit: भुवः प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना । स्वः प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना ॥
units.english: turn to Bhuvaḥ for such and such and such turn to Svaḥ, for such and such and such

units.sanskrit: अरिष्टमविनाशिनं कोशं यथोक्तं प्रपद्ये प्रपन्नो ऽस्मि पुत्रायुषे ।
units.english: ImperishableindestructibleCofferas described above,to this turn,have recourse to, for the sake of my son’s longevity;for such and such and such

units.sanskrit: अमुनामुनामुनेति त्रिर्नाम गृह्णाति पुत्रस्य ।
units.english: ie the speaker mentions the name of his son three times

units.sanskrit: तथा प्राणं प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना, भूः प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना भुवः प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना स्वः प्रपद्ये ऽमुनामुनामुना,
units.english: Similarly, turn to Prāṇa, for such and such and such; turn the Bhūḥfor such and such and such; turn to Bhuvaḥ, for such and such and such; turn to Svaḥ for such and such and such

units.sanskrit: सर्वत्र प्रपद्य इति त्रिनमि गृह्णाति पुनः पुनः ॥
units.english: After pronouncing the term ‘ turn’, he utters the son’s name three times, again and again

units.sanskrit: प्रानो वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यद् इदं किंच ।
units.english: When said ‘ turn to Prāṇa’,Prāṇa is all this whatever exists,to that turned

units.sanskrit: स यदवोचं प्राणं प्रपद्य इति व्याख्यानार्थमुपन्यासः ।
units.english: The Text ‘when said etc’ proceeds to explain what has gone before

units.sanskrit: प्राणो वा इदंसर्वं भूतं यदिदं जगत् ।
units.english: Prāṇa indeed is all thisuniverse that exists;

units.sanskrit: यथा वारानाभाव् इति वक्ष्यति । अतस्तमेव सर्वं तत्तेन प्राणप्रपदनेन प्रापत्सि प्रपन्नो ऽभवम् ॥
units.english: as is going to be described later on in the text ‘As the spokes fixed to the Hub etc’ To all this turned when spoke of the Prāṇa

units.sanskrit: अथ यदवीचं भूः प्रपद्य इति पृथिवीं प्रपद्ये ऽन्तरिक्षं प्रपद्ये दिवं प्रपद्य इत्येव तदवोचम् ॥
units.english: When said ‘ turn to Bhūḥ’, what meant to say was that ‘ turn to the Earth, turn to the Sky, turn to the Heaven’

units.sanskrit: तथा भूः प्रपद्य इति त्रींल्लोकान्भूरादीन्प्रपद्य इति तदवोचम् ॥
units.english: When said ‘ turn to Bhūḥ’, what meant to say was that ‘ turn to the three Regions, Earth and the rest’

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् अवोचं भुवः प्रपद्य इत्य् अग्निं प्रपद्ये वायुं प्रपद्य आदित्यं प्रपद्य इत्य् एव तद् अवोचम् ॥
units.english: When said ‘ turn to Bhuvaḥ’, what meant to say was that ‘ turn to Agni, turn to Vāyu, turn to Āditya’

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् अवोचं स्वः प्रपद्य इत्य् ऋग्वेदं प्रपद्ये यजुर्वेदं प्रपद्ये सामवेदं प्रपद्य इत्य् एव तद् अवोचम् ॥
units.english: When said ‘ turn to Svaḥ’, what meant to say was that ‘ turn to Ṛgveda, turn to Yajurveda, turn to Sāmaveda’;

units.sanskrit: अथ यदवोचं स्वः प्रपद्य इत्यृग्वेदादीन्प्रपद्य इत्येव तदवोचमिति ।
units.english: this was what said When said ‘ turn to Svaḥ’, what meant to say was that ‘ turn to Ṛgveda and the rest’

units.sanskrit: उपरिष्टान्मन्त्राञ्जपेत्ततः पूर्वोक्तमजरं कोशं सदिग्वत्सं यथावद्ध्यात्वा द्विर्वचनमादरार्थम् ॥ इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य पञ्चदशः खण्डः
units.english: These Mantras one should recite after proper meditation of the aforesaid ‘imperishable’ ‘Coffer’, along with the ‘Calf of the Quarters’ The repetition of the phrase ‘what said’ is meant to indicate the importance of the subject End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पुरुषो वाव यज्ञः ।
units.english: Man indeed is the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: तस्य यानि चतुर्विंशतिवर्षाणि तत् प्रातःसवनम् ।
units.english: His twentyfour years are the ‘Morning Extraction’;

units.sanskrit: चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री ।
units.english: the Gāyatrī contains twentyfour letters;

units.sanskrit: गायत्रं प्रातःसवनम् ।
units.english: the ‘Morning Extraction’ is related to the Gāyatrī

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य वसवो ऽन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: Connected with this are the Vasus;

units.sanskrit: प्राणा वाव वसवः ।
units.english: the Prāṇas are the Vasus;

units.sanskrit: एते हीदं सर्वं वासयन्ति ॥
units.english: as they make all this abide vāsayanti

units.sanskrit: जीवन्हि स्वयं पुत्रादिफलेन युज्यते नान्यथा इत्यत आत्मानं यज्ञं सम्पादयतिपुरषः पुरुषो जीवनविशिष्टः कार्यकरणसङ्घातो यथाप्रसिद्ध
units.english: Man;that is, the wellknown particular aggregate of causes and effects, endowed with life;indeedis meant to emphasise the assertion;the sense being that Man is really the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: तथा हि सामान्यैः सम्पादयति यज्ञत्वम् ।
units.english: The text next proceeds to indicate the points of similarity between Man and Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: कथम् । तस्य पुरुषस्य यानि चतुर्विंशतिवर्षाण्यायुषस्तत्प्रातःसवनं यज्ञस्य ।
units.english: How?Of man, the first twentyfour years of life constitute what is the ‘Morning Extraction’ of the Sacrifice known as ‘Man’

units.sanskrit: केन सामान्येनेत्याहचतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्रो छन्दो गायत्रं गायत्रीछन्दस्कं हि विधियज्ञस्य प्रातःसवनम् । अतः प्रातःसवनसम्पन्नेन चतुर्विंशतिवर्षायुषा युक्तः पुरुषः । अतो विधियज्ञसादृश्याद्यज्ञः ।
units.english: What are the points of similarity on which this parallelism is based? AnswerThe Gāyatrīmetrecontains twenty four letters,and the ‘Morning Extraction’ is related to the Gāyatrī,ie the ‘Morning Extraction’ of the Ritualistic Sacrifice is related to the Gāyatrīmetre;hence when the Man becomes twentyfour years of age, he becomes equipped with the ‘Morning Extraction and hence being thus similar to the Ritualistic Sacrifice, the Man is the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: तथोत्तरयोरप्यायुषोः सवनद्वयसम्पत्तिस्रिष्टुब्जगत्यक्षरसंख्यासामान्यतो वाच्या ।
units.english: Similarly, the other two parts of the Man’s life mean equipment with the Midday and Evening Extractions, on the basis of the similarity of the number of years to the number of letters in the Triṣṭup and Jagatī metres

units.sanskrit: किञ्च तदस्य पुरुषयज्ञस्य प्रातःसवनं विधियज्ञस्येव वसवो देवा अन्वायत्ता अनुगताः ।
units.english: Further, connected with the ‘Morning Extraction’ of this ‘SacrificeMan’, are the Vasus, the Deities,just as they are connected with the Ritualistic Sacrifice;

units.sanskrit: सवनदेवतात्वेन स्वामिन इत्यर्थः । पुरुषयज्ञे ऽपि विधियज्ञ इवाग्न्यादयो वसवो देवाः प्राप्ता इत्यतो विशिनष्टिप्राणा वाव वसवो वागादयो वायवश्च ।
units.english: that is, they are the deities, and hence the masters, of the ‘Morning Extraction’ According to this parallelism, it would follow that, as at the ritualistic sacrifice, so at the SacrificeMan also, the deities are the wellknown ‘Vasus’, Agni and the rest;

units.sanskrit: तेहि यस्मादिदं पुरुषादिप्राणिजातमेते वासयन्ति ।
units.english: Because it is these Prāṇas that make all this,living beingsabide

units.sanskrit: प्राणेषु हि देहे वत्सतु सर्वमिद वसति नान्यथा ।
units.english: That is, it is only while the Prāṇas are in the body that all this abides, lives, not otherwise;

units.sanskrit: इत्यतो वसनाद्वासनाच्च वसवः ॥
units.english: and because they make all this abide vāsayanti, therefore, they are ‘Vasus

units.sanskrit: तं चेद् एतस्मिन् वयसि किंचिद् उपतपेत् स ब्रूयात् । प्राणा वसव इदं मे प्रातःसवनं माध्यंदिनं सवनम् अनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानां वसूनां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेति ।
units.english: If, at that age, anything ail him, he should say‘O Ye, Prāṇas and Vasus, extend this my Morning Extraction to the Midday Extraction, so that , the Sacrifice, may not be cut off in the middle of the PrāṇaVasus!’Thereupon, he recovers from the ailment and becomes free from illness

units.sanskrit: तं चेद्यज्ञसम्पादितमेतस्मिन्प्रातः सवनसम्पन्ने वयसि किञ्चिद्व्याध्यादि मरणशङ्कारणमुपतपेद्दुःखमुत्पादयेत्स तदा यज्ञसम्पादी पुरुष आत्मानं यज्ञं मन्यमानो ब्रूयाज्जपेदित्यर्थः इमं मन्त्रं हे प्राणा वसव अदं मे प्रातः सवनं मम यज्ञस्य वर्तते तन्माध्यन्दिनं सवनमनुसन्तनुतेति माध्यन्दिनेन सवनेना'युषा
units.english: When the man has become identified with the Sacrifice, if at that ageie at the age parallel to what, at the Sacrifice, would be the Morning Extraction,anything ail him,any disease or something else involving danger of death,then the Man engaged in sacrifices, who regards himself as the Sacrifice, should say thisie he should repeat the following Mantra’‘O ye, PrāṇasVasus,this the Morning Extraction of my Sacrifice,please extend to the Midday Extraction,ie join it on to and unify it with, that span of my life which is parallel to the Midday Extraction

units.sanskrit: माहं यज्ञो युष्माकं प्राणानां वसूनां प्रातःसवनेशानां मध्ये विलोप्सीय विलुप्येय विच्छिद्येयेत्यर्थः ।
