units.english: So that , the sacrificer may not be cut offmay not drop out in the middle of the PrāṇaVasus, who preside over the Morning Extradiction

units.sanskrit: इतिशब्दो मन्त्रपरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ।
units.english: The particle ‘iti’ after ‘Vilopsīya’ indicates the end of the Mantra to be recited

units.sanskrit: स तेन जपेन ध्यानेन च ततस्तस्मादुपतापादुदेत्युद्गच्छति । उद्गम्य विमुक्तः सन्नगदो हानुपतापो भवत्येव ॥
units.english: By the repeating of this Mantra and by meditation, he recovers from the ailment; and having recovered and got out of it, he becomes free from illness,free from all suffering

units.sanskrit: अथ यानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशद् वर्षाणि तन् माध्यंदिनं सवनम् ।
units.english: The fortyfour years are the Midday Extraction

units.sanskrit: चतुश्चत्वारिंशदक्षरा त्रिष्टुप् ।
units.english: The Triṣṭup metre contains fortyfour letters

units.sanskrit: त्रैष्टुभं माध्यंदिनं सवनम् ।
units.english: The Midday Extraction is related to the Triṣṭup

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्य रुद्रा अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: With this the Rudras are connected

units.sanskrit: प्राणा वाव रुद्राः ।
units.english: The Prāṇas are the Rudras;

units.sanskrit: एते हीदं सर्वं रोदयन्ति ॥
units.english: as it is these that make all this weep rodayanti

units.sanskrit: अथ यानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशद्वर्षाणीत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: The fortyfour years etc,just as before

units.sanskrit: रुदन्ति रोदयन्तीति प्राणा रुद्राः । क्रूरा हि ते मध्यमेवयस्यतो रुद्राः ॥
units.english: Those who weep, and make others weepare the Rudras, who are the Prāṇas In middle age, people are inclined to be cruel,hence called ‘Rudras’

units.sanskrit: तं चेद् एतस्मिन् वयसि किंचिद् उपतपेत् स ब्रूयात् । प्राणा रुद्रा इदं मे माध्यंदिनं सवनं तृतीयसवनम् अनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानां रुद्राणां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेति ।
units.english: If at that age, anything ail him, he should say‘O ye, PrāṇasRudras, extend this my Midday Extraction to the Third Extraction,so that , the Sacrifice, may not be cut off in the middle of the PrāṇasRudras!’Thereafter, he recovers from the ailment and becomes free from illness

units.sanskrit: अथ यान्य् अष्टाचत्वारिंशद् वर्षाणि तत् तृतीयसवनम् ।
units.english: The fortyeight years are the Third Extraction

units.sanskrit: अष्टाचत्वारिंशदक्षरा जगती ।
units.english: The Jagatī metre contains fortyeight letters

units.sanskrit: जागतं तृतीयसवनम् ।
units.english: The Third Extraction is related to the Jagatī

units.sanskrit: तद् अस्यादित्या अन्वायत्ताः ।
units.english: With this the Ādityas are connected

units.sanskrit: प्राणा वावादित्याः ।
units.english: The Prāṇas verily are Ādityas;

units.sanskrit: एते हीदं सर्वम् आददते ॥
units.english: as it is these that take up all this ādadate

units.sanskrit: तं चेद् एतस्मिन् वयसि किंचिद् उपतपेत् स ब्रूयात् । प्राणा आदित्या इदं मे तृतीयसवनम् आयुर् अनुसंतनुतेति माहं प्राणानाम् आदित्यानां मध्ये यज्ञो विलोप्सीयेति ।
units.english: If, at that age, anything ail him, he should say‘O Ye, PrāṇasĀdityas, extend this Third Extraction to the full span of life, so that, , the Sacrifice, may not be cut off in the middle of the ‘PrāṇasĀdityas’

units.sanskrit: उद् धैव तत एत्य् अगदो हैव भवति ॥
units.english: Thereafter, he recovers from the ailment and becomes free from illness

units.sanskrit: तथा'दित्याः प्राणाः । ते हीदं शब्दादिजातमाददते ऽत आदित्यास्तृतीयसवनमायुः षोडशोत्तरवर्षशतं समापयतानुसन्तनुत यज्ञं समापयतेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Similarly the Prāṇas are Ādityas it is they that take up all this,in the shape of sound and the rest ‘O, Ye, Ādityas, complete the Third Extraction, the full span of lifeconsisting of a hundred and sixteen yearsthat is, in this way complete the sacrifice

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: एतद् ध स्म वै तद् विद्वान् आह महिदास ऐतरेयः । स किं म एतद् उपतपसि यो ऽहम् अनेन न प्रेष्याम् इति ।
units.english: Knowing this, MahīdāsaAitareya said‘Wherefore do you afflict me thus, who am not going to die by it?’ And he lived for a hundred and sixteen years

units.sanskrit: प्र ह षोडशं वर्षशतं जीवति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows this lives for a hundred and sixteen years

units.sanskrit: निश्चिता हि विद्या फलायेत्येतद्दर्शयन्नुदाहरतिएतद्यज्ञदर्शनं ह स्म वै किल तद्विद्वानाह महिदासो नामतः ।
units.english: This philosophy of Sacrifice was known to one Mahīdāsaby namewho was Aitareya,the son of Itarā

units.sanskrit: किं कस्मान्मे ममैतदुपतपनमुपतपसि स त्वं हे रोग यो ऽहं यज्ञो ऽनेन त्वत्कृतेनोपतापेन न प्रेष्यामि न मरिष्याम्यतो वृथा तव श्रम
units.english: Wherefore,whydo you afflict me thuswith this afflictionO, ye, Disease,when , who am the Sacrifice, am not going to dieperish, by its affliction? That is, all your labour is useless

units.sanskrit: इत्यर्थः । इत्येवमाह स्मेति पूर्वेण सम्बन्धः ।
units.english: So said hethe words occurring in the beginning of the text

units.sanskrit: स एवंनिश्चयः सन्षोडशं वर्षशतमजीवत् । अन्यो ऽप्येवंनिश्चः षोडशं वर्षशतं प्रजीवति य एवं यथोक्तं यज्ञसम्पादनं वेद जानाति स इत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: With this firm conviction, Mahīdāsa lived for a hundred and sixteen years,Any one else also, who has this same firm conviction, lives for a hundred and sixteen years,that is, if he knows the abovedescribed method of accomplishing the Sacrifice,

units.sanskrit: इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य षोडशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: स यद् अशिशिषति यत् पिपासति यन् न रमते ता अस्य दीक्षाः ॥
units.english: That he hungers, that he thirsts and that he is not happy,these are his Initiations,

units.sanskrit: स यदशिशिषतोत्यादियज्ञसामान्यनिर्देशः पुरुषस्य पूर्वेणैव सम्बध्यते ।
units.english: That he hungers etc,points out the similarity of Man to the Sacrifice in general, and as such is connected with what has been declared above

units.sanskrit: यदशिशिषत्यशितुमिच्छति । तथा पिपासति पातुमिच्छति । यन्न रमत इष्टाद्यप्राप्तिनिमित्तं यदैवञ्जातीयकं दुःखमनुभवति ता अस्य दीक्षाः । दुःखसामान्याद्विधियज्ञस्येव ॥
units.english: That he hungers,wishes to eat,similarly, that he thirsts,wishes to drink,and that he is not happy,ie when he suffers pain on not getting what he desires,these are his Initiations,so called because they are painful, like the Initiatory Rites of fasting etc, of the Ritualistic Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् अश्नाति यत् पिबति यद् रमते तद् उपसदैर् एति ॥
units.english: And that he eats, that he drinks, and that he is happy,thereby he becomes one with the Upasadas

units.sanskrit: अथ यदश्नाति यत्पिबति यद्रमते रतिं चानुभवतीष्टादिसंयोगात्तदुपसदैः समानतामेति । उपसदां च पयोव्रतत्वनिमित्तं सुखमस्ति ।
units.english: That he eats, that he drinks and that he is happy,ie feels pleasure by coming by what he desires,thereby he becomes one withsimilar tothe Upasadas, At the Upasadas there is happiness due to the drinking of milk which is permitted at them;

units.sanskrit: अल्पभोजनीयानि चाहान्याश्वासन्नानीति प्रश्वासो ऽतो ऽशनादीनामुपसदां च सामान्यम् ॥
units.english: and this brings about the consolation that the days are not far off when small quantities of food will be permitted;this is the point of similarity between ‘eating’ etc, and the Upasadas,

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् धसति यज् जक्षति यन् मैथुनं चरति स्तुतशस्त्रैर् एव तद् एति ॥ अथ यद्धसति यज्जक्षति भक्षयति यन्मैथुनं चरति स्तुतशस्रैरेव तत्समानतामेति । शब्दवत्त्वसामान्यात् ॥
units.english: That he laughs, that he eats and that he dallies in couples,thereby he becomes one with the Stuta and Śāstra hymns That he laughs, that he eats and that he dallies in couples,by these he becomes one with,similar tothe Stuta and Śāstra Hymns the recited hymns and the hymns set to music the similarity consisting in being accompanied by some sort of sound

units.sanskrit: अथ यत् तपो दानम् आर्जवम् अहिंसा सत्यवचनम् इति ता अस्य दक्षिणाः ॥
units.english: Now, Austerity, Charity, Uprightness, NonViolence and Truthfulness,these are his Sacrificial Fees

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्तपो दानमार्जवमहिंसा सत्यवचनमिति ता अस्य दक्षिणाः । धर्मपुष्टिकरत्वसामान्यात् ॥
units.english: Now Austerity, Charity, Uprightness, Nonviolence and Truthfulness, these are his sacrificial fees; the point of similarity consisting in the fact that, like the Sacrificial Fee, they serve to strengthen the merit of the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् आहुः सोष्यत्य् असोष्टेति । पुनर् उत्पादनम् एवास्य तत् ।
units.english: Hence, when they say ‘Soṣyati’, ‘shall give birth’ and ‘Aṣoṣṭa’, ‘has given birth’that is his Rebirth

units.sanskrit: मरणम् एवावभृथः ॥
units.english: His Death is the AvabhṛthaBath

units.sanskrit: यस्माच्च यज्ञः पुरषस्तस्मात्तं जनयिष्यति माता यदा तदा'हुरन्ये
units.english: Because the Man is the Sacrifice, therefore, when his Mother shall give birth to him, they will say ‘she shall give birth’, referring to his Mother;

units.sanskrit: सोष्यतीति तस्य मातरं यदा च प्रसूता भवति तदासोष्ट पूर्णिकेति विधियज्ञ इव सोष्यति सोमं देवदत्तो ऽसोष्ट सोमं यज्ञदत्त इति,
units.english: and after she has given birth to him, then they say ‘Purṇikā the Mother has given birth’;just as at the Ritualistic Sacrifice, they say ‘Soṣyati Somam Devdattaḥ’ Devadatta shall extract the Somajuice and ‘Aṣoṣṭa Somam Yajñadattaḥ’ Yajñadatta has extracted the Somajuice

units.sanskrit: अतः शब्दसामान्याद्वा पुरुषो यज्ञः । पुनरुत्पादनमेवास्य तत्पुरुषाख्यस्य यज्ञस्य यत्सोष्यत्यसोष्टेति शब्दसम्बन्धित्वं विधियज्ञस्येव । किञ्च तन्मरणमेवास्य पुरुषयज्ञस्यावभृथः समाप्तिसामान्यात् ॥
units.english: From this similarity of verbal expressions SoṣyatiAṣoṣṭa, used in both cases, it follows that the Man is the Sacrifice When the expressions ‘SoṣyatiAṣoṣṭa’ are used in connection with the Sacrifice called ‘Man’, it is his Rebirth,just as in the case of the Ritualistic Sacrifice Further, it is the Death of the SacrificeMan that is the final AvabhṛthaBath of the Ritualistic Sacrifice;

units.sanskrit: अपिपास एव स बभूव ।
units.english: as both have the common character of being the End

units.sanskrit: सो ऽन्तवेलायाम् एतत् त्रयं प्रतिपद्येताक्षितम् अस्य् अच्युतम् असि प्राणसंशितम् असीति । तत्रैते द्वे ऋचौ भवतः ॥
units.english: Having expounded this to KṛṣṇaDevakīputra, GhoraĀṅgirasa said to him as follows, and he became thirstless,‘At the time of the end, one should have recourse to these three Akṣitamasi, Acyutamasi and Prāṇasaṃśitamasi’On this subject, there are these two verses

units.sanskrit: तद्धैतद्यज्ञदर्शनं घोरो नामत आङ्गिरसो गोत्रतः कृष्णाय देवकीपुत्राय शिष्यायोकत्वोवाच तदेतत्त्रयमित्यादिव्यवहितेन
units.english: ThisPhilosophy of the Sacrifice,the sage, Ghoraby nameĀṅgirasaby Gotrahaving expounded to Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī,his disciple, said to him‘These three etc,’ following in the next sentence

units.sanskrit: स चैतद्दर्शनं श्रुत्वापिपास एवाम्याभ्यो विद्याभ्यो बभूव ।
units.english: Kṛṣṇa, on listening to this Philosophy, became thirstless,that is, he ceased to have a desire for learning other sciences

units.sanskrit: इत्थं च विशिष्टेयं विद्या यत्कृष्णस्य देवकीपुत्रस्यान्यां विद्यां प्रति तृड्विच्छेदकरीति पुरुषयज्ञविद्यां स्तौति ।
units.english: By this the Text means to eulogise the Philosophy of the SacrificeMan as being so effective as to have relieved KṛṣṇaDevakīputra of thirst for all other sciences

units.sanskrit: घोर आङ्गिरसः कृष्णायोक्त्वेमां विद्यां किमुवाचेति तदाहस एवं यथोक्तयज्ञविदन्तवेलायां मरणकाल एतन्मन्त्रत्रयं प्रतिपद्येत जपेदित्यर्थः किं तदक्षितमक्षीणमक्षतं वासीत्येकं यजुः सामर्थ्यादादित्यस्थं प्राणं चैकीकृत्या'ह । तथा तमेवा'हाच्युतं स्वरूपादप्रच्युतमसीति द्वितीयं यजुः । प्राणसंशितं प्राणश्च स संशितं सम्यक्तनूकृतं च सूक्ष्मं तत्त्वमसीति तृतीयं यजुः ।
units.english: QuestionHaving expounded this Philosophy to Krṣṇa, what did GhoraĀṅgirasa say to him? AnswerThe man who knows the Sacrifice as here expounded should, at the time of the endie, at the time of death,have recourse torepeatthe following three MantrasWhich three Mantras?First, the YajusText, ‘Akṣitamasi etc’ MaitrāSaṃhitā, , , ‘Akṣitam’ meaning unperished, undimmed, applies, by implication, to the Sun as identified with Prāṇa;again, the second Yajustext was pointed out as ‘Acyutamasi’, meaning ‘You have not fallen off from your own form’;and the third Yajuṣtext mentioned was ‘Prāṇasaṃśitamasi’, meaning ‘You are Prāṇa properly refined and rendered subtleOn this sifbject of eulogising the Philosophythere are two versesMantras;

units.sanskrit: तत्रैतस्मिन्नर्थे विद्यास्तुतिपरे द्वे ऋचौ मन्त्रौ भवतो न जपार्थे ।
units.english: these two are not meant for being repeated by the dying man;

units.sanskrit: त्रयं प्रतिपद्येतेति त्रित्वसंख्याबाधनात् ।
units.english: if these were so meant, then that would be incompatible with the number ‘three’ specified in the preceding sentence;

units.sanskrit: पञ्चसंख्या हि तदा स्यात् ॥
units.english: as in that case, the number of texts would be five

units.sanskrit: आदित् प्रत्नस्य रेतसः । उद् वयं तमसस्परि । ज्योतिः पश्यन्त उत्तरम् ।
units.english: ‘Āditpratnasya retasaḥ jyotiḥ paśyanti vāsaram, paro yadidhyate diva Of the ancient germ, they see the daylike light which shines supreme in the Effulgent’

units.sanskrit: स्वः पश्यन्त उत्तरम् । देवं देवत्रा सूर्यम् अगन्म ज्योतिर् उत्तमम् इति ज्योतिर् उत्तमम् इति ॥
units.english: jyotiruttamam’ ‘Perceiving above darkness, the Supreme Light, our own, we reached the effulgent divine source of energy, the Sun, the Highest Light,yea, the Highest Light’Ṛgveda;

units.sanskrit: आदिदित्यत्रा'कारस्यानुबन्धस्तकारो ऽनर्थक इच्छब्दश्च ।
units.english: [Of the first mantra, the Text quotes only the opening words, the rest of it has been supplied above

units.sanskrit: प्रत्नस्य चिरन्तनस्य पुराणस्येत्यर्थः । रेतसः कारणस्य बीजभूतस्य जगतः सदाख्यस्य ज्योतिः प्रकाशं पश्यन्ति ।
units.english: so also is the term ‘it’ Of the Ancient ie Longstanding, prime germcause, seedof the Universe, which is called ‘Sat ‘Being’they see the Lightthe effulgence

units.sanskrit: आशब्द उत्सृष्टानुबन्धः पश्यन्तीत्यनेन सम्बध्यते ।
units.english: The Syllable ‘ā’ with which the sentence begins, having dropped its appendage ‘t’ becomes connected with the verb ‘paśyanti’, they see’

units.sanskrit: किं तज्जयोतिः पश्यन्ति ।
units.english: QuestionWhich is the light that they see?

units.sanskrit: वासरमहरहरिव तत्सर्वतो व्याप्तं ब्रह्मणो ज्योतिः ।
units.english: AnswerIt is the light that is daylike,like the day ie it is the light of Brahman which pervades over all things

units.sanskrit: निवृत्तचक्षुषो ब्रह्मविदो ब्रह्मचर्यादिनिवृत्तिसाधनैः शुद्धान्तःकरणा आ समन्ततो ज्योतिः पश्यन्तीत्यर्थः । परः परमिति लिङ्गव्यत्ययेन,
units.english: What is meant is that those persons who have turned back their visual and other organs from their external objectives, and have come to know Brahman and having their inner organ mind clarified by such means of abstinence as Celibacy and the like, see this light on all sides

units.sanskrit: ज्योतिष्परत्वात् । यदिध्यते दीप्यते दिवि द्योतनवति पस्मिन्ब्रह्मणि वर्तमानम् । येन ज्योतिषेद्धः सविता तपति चन्द्रमा भाति विद्युद्विद्योतते ग्रहतारागणा विभासन्ते ।
units.english: ‘Parān’ has to be construed by changing its gender into the neuter, as it is meant to qualify the word ‘Jyotiḥ’lightwhich is Neuter;which shinesglimmersin the Effulgent;ie subsisting in the Effulgent Supreme Brahman,that light, being illumined by which, the Sun blazes, the Moon shines, the lightning flashes and the hosts of planets and stars twinkle

units.sanskrit: किञ्चान्यो मन्त्रदृगाह यथोक्तं ज्योतिः पश्यन् । उद्वयं तमसो ऽज्ञानलक्षणात्परि परस्तादिति शेषः ।
units.english: Further, another MantraSeer Sage having seen the abovementioned Light, says as follows the second Mantra quoted in the Text in full

units.sanskrit: आदित्यस्थं च तदेकं ज्योतिः ।
units.english: Above darkness,ie beyond Ignorance;

units.sanskrit: यदुत्तरमुत्कृष्टतरमूर्ध्वतरं वापरं ज्योतिरपेक्ष्य पश्यन्त उदगन्म वयम् । कमुदगन्मेत्याह । देवं द्योतनवन्तं देवत्रा देवेषु सर्वेषु सूर्यं रसानां रश्मीनां प्राणानां च जगत ईरणात्सूर्यस्तमुदगन्म गतवन्तो ज्योतिरुत्तमं सर्वज्योतिर्भ्य उत्कृष्टतममहो प्राप्ता वयमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: or destructive of ignorance,the light which is supremesubsisting in the Sun;perceiving this light, we reached this verb has to be construed from the latter part of the Mantra;this light is our own,our very own, ie shines in our heart;the light subsisting in the Sun is one light which is supreme, more excellent, higher than the other light;and on perceiving this, we reached,what?the effulgent divine source of energy, the Sun,so called because He energises the Essences, the rays, the organs and the entire universe,we reached this Highest Light, the highest of all lights;the most wonderful!

units.sanskrit: इदं तज्ज्योतिर्यदृग्भ्यां स्तुतं यद्यजुस्त्रयेण प्रकाशितम् । द्विरभ्यासो यज्ञकल्पनापरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥ इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्य सप्तदशः खण्डः
units.english: This is the Light which has been eulogised by these two verses and which had been indicated by the three YajuṣTexts referred to above The repetition‘Yea, the Highest Light’ is meant to indicate the end of the Section dealing with the assumption of Sacrifice as representing the Man End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: मनो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपासीत ।
units.english: One should meditate upon the Mind as Brahman;

units.sanskrit: इत्य् अध्यात्मम् ।
units.english: this is with reference to the Body

units.sanskrit: अथाधिदैवतम् । आकाशो ब्रह्म ।
units.english: With reference to Deities,one should meditate upon Ākāśa as Brahman

units.sanskrit: इत्य् उभयम् आदिष्टं भवत्य् अध्यात्मं चाधिदैवतं च ॥
units.english: In this way both become taught,that with reference to the Body and that with reference to the Deities

units.sanskrit: मनोमय ईश्वर उक्त आकाशात्मेति च ब्रह्मणो गुणैकदेशत्वेन । अथेदानीं मन आकाशयोः समस्तब्रह्मदृष्टिविधानार्थ आरम्भो मनो ब्रह्मेत्यादि । मनो मनुते ऽनेनेत्यन्तःकरणं तद्ब्रह्म परमित्युपासीतेति एतदात्मविषयं दर्शनमध्यात्मम् ।
units.english: God has been spoken of as ‘consisting of the Mind also as ‘consisting of the Ākāśa’, as forming a part of the quality of Brahman; now with the words ‘Mind as Brahman’, the Text proceeds to lay down the meditating of these twoMind and Ākāśaas the entire Brahman Manas, Mind, is that whereby one thinks, the Internal Organsthis is Brahman, the Highest;thus should one meditate

units.sanskrit: अथाधिदैवतं देवताविषयमिदं वक्ष्यामः । आकाशो ब्रह्मेत्युपासीत । एवमभुयमध्यात्ममधिदैवतं चोभयं ब्रह्मदृष्टिविषयमादिष्टमुपदिष्टं भवति ।
units.english: that doctrine which refers to the Deities we are going to expound One should meditate upon Akaśa as BrahmanIn this way boththe doctrines of viewing Brahman in reference to the Body, and that of viewing it in reference to the Deitiesbecome taughtexpounded;

units.sanskrit: आकाशमनसोः सूक्ष्मत्वात् । मनसोपलभ्यत्वाच्च ब्रह्मणो योग्यं मनो ब्रह्मदृष्टेः ।
units.english: Both Mind and Akaśa are subtle entitiesand Brahman is accessible by the Mind; hence it is only fit that the Mind should be looked upon as Brahman

units.sanskrit: आकाशश्च सर्वगतत्वात्सूक्ष्मत्वादुपाधिहीनत्वाच्च ॥
units.english: As for Akaśa, it is allpervading, subtle and free from limitations;

units.sanskrit: तद् एतच् चतुष्पाद् ब्रह्म । वाक् पादः प्राणः पादश् चक्षुः पादः श्रोत्रं पादः ।
units.english: This same Brahman is fourfooted Speech is one foot, Breath is one foot, the Eye is one foot, the Ear is one foot;this is with reference to the Body

units.sanskrit: अथाधिदैवतम् । अग्निः पादो वायुः पाद आदित्यः पादो दिशः पादः ।
units.english: Now with reference to DeitiesAgni is one foot, Vāyu is one foot, Āditya is one foot, the Quarters are one foot

units.sanskrit: इत्य् उभयम् एवादिष्टं भवत्य् अध्यात्मं चाधिदैवतं च ॥
units.english: Thus both become taught,that with reference to the Body and with reference to the Deities

units.sanskrit: तदेतन्मन आख्यं चतुष्पाद्ब्रह्म,
units.english: This same Brahmannamed ‘Mind’is fourfooted;

units.sanskrit: चत्वारः पादा अस्येति ।
units.english: ie It has four feet

units.sanskrit: कथं चतुष्पात्त्वं मनसो ब्रह्मण इत्याहवाक्प्राणश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रमित्येते पादा इत्यध्यात्मम् ।
units.english: In what way is the MindBrahman ‘fourfooted’?Speech, Breath, Eye and Ear are the four ‘feet’;this is with reference to the Body

units.sanskrit: अथाधिदैवतमाकाशस्य ब्रह्मणो ऽग्निर्वायुरादित्यो दिश इत्येते ।
units.english: Now with reference to the Deitiesthe four ‘feet’ of ĀkāśaBrahman are Agni, Vāyu, Āditya and the Quarters

units.sanskrit: एवमुभयमेव चतुष्पाद्ब्रह्मा'दिष्टं भवत्यध्यात्मं चैवाधिदैवतं च ॥
units.english: In this way, both forms of the ‘fourfooted’ Brahman become taught,that with reference to the Body and that with reference to the Deities

units.sanskrit: वाग् एव ब्रह्मणश् चतुर्थः पादः ।
units.english: Speech itself is the fourth foot of Brahman;

units.sanskrit: सो ऽग्निना ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च ।
units.english: it shines and warms with the light of Agni

units.sanskrit: भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows this shines and warms up with renown, fame and Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: तत्र वागेव मनसो ब्रह्मणश्चतुर्थः पाद इतरपादत्रयापेक्षया । वाचा हि पादेनेव गवादि वक्तव्यविषयं प्रति प्रतिष्ठति ।
units.english: Speech itself is the fourth footof the MindBrahman,fourth, in reference to the other three feet; because it is through this ‘foot’ of Speech that the Mind stands upon,becomes fixed uponthe cow and such other things that are spoken of;

units.sanskrit: अतो मनसः पाद इव वाक् ।
units.english: hence Speech is like the foot of Mind

units.sanskrit: तथा प्राणो घ्राणः पादः ।
units.english: Similarly, Breaththe organis one foot;

units.sanskrit: तेनापि गन्धविषयं प्रति चङ्क्रमति ।
units.english: as it is through this that it moves over to objects of olfactory perception

units.sanskrit: तथा चक्षुः पादः श्रोत्रं पाद इत्येवमध्यात्मं चतुष्पात्तवं मनसो ब्रह्मणः ।
units.english: Similarly the Eye is one foot; the Ear is one foot Thus is the fourfootedness of the MindBrahman established, in reference to the Body

units.sanskrit: अथाधिदैवतमग्निवाय्वादित्यदिश आकाशस्य ब्रह्मण उदार इव गोः पादा विलग्ना उपलभ्यन्ते ।
units.english: Now as in reference to the Deities,Agni, Vāyu, Āditya and the Quarters are the four feet of ĀkāśaBrahman; these are found to be attached to Ākāśa just as the four feet of the cow are attached to the belly;

units.sanskrit: तेन तस्या'काशस्याग्न्यादयः पादा उच्यन्ते ।
units.english: hence these Agni and the restare said to be the ‘feet of Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: एवमुभयमध्यात्मं चैवाधिदैवतं चतुष्पादादिष्टं भवति ।
units.english: Thus both forms of ‘fourfootedness’,that relating to the Body, and that relating to the Deitiesbecome taught

units.sanskrit: तत्र वागेव मनसो ब्रह्मणश्चतुर्थः पादः ।
units.english: Now Speech, which is the fourth foot of MindBrahman shines and warms with the light of Agni as pertaining to Deities;

units.sanskrit: सो ऽग्निनाधिदैवतेन ज्योतिषा भाति च दीप्यते तपति च सन्तापं चौष्ण्यं करोति ।
units.english: that is, it generates light and warmth

units.sanskrit: अथवा तैलघृताद्याग्नेयाशनेनेद्धा वाग्भाति च तपति च वदनायोत्साहवती स्यादित्यर्थः । विद्वत्फलं भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं यथोक्तं वेदः ॥
units.english: Or it may mean that Speech becomes energised by the man feeding upon Oil, Butter and other such articles partaking of the nature of the Deity Agni, whereupon it becomes imbued with courage to speakthe reward accruing to one who knows this as above explained is that he shines and warms up with renown, fame and Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: प्राण एव ब्रह्मणश् चतुर्थः पादः ।
units.english: Breath is the fourth foot of Brahman;

units.sanskrit: स वायुना ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च ।
units.english: it shines and warms with the light of Vāyu;

units.sanskrit: भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: one who knows this shines and warms with renown, fame and Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: चक्षुर् एव ब्रह्मणश् चतुर्थः पादः ।
units.english: The Eye is the fourth foot of Brahman it shines and warms with the light of Āditya;

units.sanskrit: भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: one who knows this shines and warms with renown, fame and Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रम् एव ब्रह्मणश् चतुर्थः पादः ।
units.english: The Ear is the fourth foot of Brahman it shines and warms with the light of the Quarters

units.sanskrit: भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows this shines and warms with renown, fame and Brahmic gloryYea, one who knows this

units.sanskrit: तथा प्राण एव ब्रह्मणश्चतुर्थः पादः ।
units.english: Similarly Breath is the fourth foot of Brahman;

units.sanskrit: स वायुना गन्धाय भाति च तपति च । तता चक्षुरादित्येन रूपग्रहणाय श्रोत्रं दिग्भिः शब्दग्रहणाय ।
units.english: for the apprehension of odour, it shines and warms with the light of Vāyu;similarly the Eye shines and warms with the light of Āditya, for the apprehension of colour;the Ear shines and warms with the light of the Quarters for the apprehension of soundsThe reward of knowledge is the same in all cases;

units.sanskrit: विद्याफलं समानं सर्वत्र ब्रह्मसम्पत्तिरदृष्टं फलं य एवं वेद ।
units.english: the imperceptible spiritual reward consists in Union with Brahman, for one who knows this

units.sanskrit: द्विरुक्तिर्दर्शनसमाप्त्यर्था ॥ इति छान्दोग्योपनिषदि तृतीयाध्यायस्याष्टादशः खण्डः
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Exposition of the particular doctrines End of Section of discourse

units.sanskrit: आदित्यो ब्रह्मेत्य् आदेशः ।
units.english: The Sun is Brahman,such is the teaching;

units.sanskrit: तस्योपव्याख्यानम् । असद् एवेदम् अग्र आसीत् ।
units.english: and its exposition is this In the beginning, this was indeed nonexistent;

units.sanskrit: तत् सद् आसीत् । तत् समभवत् ।
units.english: it became existent; it came into being;

units.sanskrit: तद् आण्डं निरवर्तत ।
units.english: it became an egg;

units.sanskrit: तत् संवत्सरस्य मात्राम् अशयत ।
units.english: it lay for the period of one year;

units.sanskrit: तन् निरभिद्यत ।
units.english: it broke open;

units.sanskrit: ते आण्डकपाले रजतं च सुवर्णं चाभवताम् ॥
units.english: then came the two halves of the eggshell, one silver, one gold

units.sanskrit: आदित्यो ब्रह्मणः पाद उक्त इति तस्मिन्सकलब्रह्मदृष्ट्यर्थमिदमारभ्यतेआदित्यो ब्रह्मेत्यादेश उपदेशस्तस्योपव्याख्यानं क्रियते
units.english: The Sun is Brahman,such is the teaching; and now its exposition is done, for the purpose of eulogising it In the beginning,in its previous condition, before it came in existencethiswhole universewas nonexistent;

units.sanskrit: असदव्यकृतनामरूपमिदं जगदशेषमग्रे प्रागवस्थायामुत्पत्तेरासीन्न त्वसदेव । कथमसतः सज्जायेतेत्यसत्कार्यत्वस्य प्रतिषेधात् ।
units.english: That this cannot be the meaning is shown by the Vedic Text which says ‘How could the existing come out of the nonexisting?’, which negatives the view that the effect was absolutely nonexistent, before it was produced

units.sanskrit: नन्विहासदेवेति विधानाद्विकल्पः स्यात् ।
units.english: so that it should be a matter of option, to accept this nonexistence or the existence indicated by the text you have quoted

units.sanskrit: न, क्रियास्विव वस्तुनि विकल्पानुपपत्तेः ।
units.english: there can be no option in regard to the state of things, as there is in regard to actions

units.sanskrit: कथं तर्हीदमसदेवेति ।
units.english: Then, how is it that the present text declares this to be nonexistent?We have already explained that what is meant is that the Universe was undifferentiated as to Name and Form, and hence it was as if nonexistent, and hence spoken of here as ‘nonexistent

units.sanskrit: नन्ववोचामाव्याकृतनामरूपत्वादसदिवासदिति । नन्वेवशब्दो ऽवधारणार्थः ।
units.english: The Text uses the term eva, ‘indeed which serves to emphasise what is declared which therefore cannot be taken in any figurative sense

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं,
units.english: True, it is so;

units.sanskrit: न तु सत्त्वाभावमवधारयति । किं तर्हि?व्याकृतनामरूपाभावमवधारयति नामरूपव्याकृतविषये सच्छब्दप्रयोगो दृष्टः । तच्च नामरूपव्याकरणमादित्यायत्तं प्रायशो जगतः तदभावे ह्यन्धं तम इदं
units.english: but what is emphasised is not the negation of existence, but the absence of differentiation of Name and Form; as a matter of fact, the term ‘sat’, ‘Existent’, is found to be used in the sense of ‘differential ed Name and Form’ and this ‘differentiation of Name and form’ of the Universe is mostly dependent upon the Sun;

units.sanskrit: न प्रज्ञायेत किञ्चनेत्यतस्तत्स्तुतिपरे वाक्ये सदपीदं राज्ञः कुलं सर्वगुणसम्पन्ने पूर्णवर्मणि राजन्यसतीति तद्वत् । न च सत्त्वमसत्त्वं वेह जगतः प्रतिपिपादयिषितमादित्यो ब्रह्मेत्यादेशपरत्वात् ।
units.english: In common parlance things are spoken of as ‘existent’ only when the Sun is there; just as obverse it is said that‘this royal dynasty, equipped with all good qualities, was indeed nonexistent, while king Pūrṇavarman was not there’ In fact, the present text is not meant to expound either the existence or nonexistence of the Universe;

units.sanskrit: उपसंहरिष्यत्यन्त आदित्यं ब्रह्मेत्युपास्त इति ।
units.english: it is meant only to expound the teaching that ‘the Sun is Brahman’;

units.sanskrit: तत्सदासीत्तदसच्छब्दवाच्यं प्रागुत्पत्तेः स्तिमितमनिस्पन्दमसदिव सत्कार्याभिमुखमीषदुपजातप्रवृत्ति सदासीत्ततो लब्धपरिस्पन्दं तत्समभवदल्पतरनामरूपव्याकरणेनाङ्कुरीभूतमि व बीजम् ।
units.english: that which was spoken of as ‘nonexistent’ before coming into existence,ie was as if stagnant, immobile, hence appearing to be nonexistentbecame existent,ie slightly inclined towards producing positive effects, hence existent;that is, it became mobile, and came into being,having its Name and Form slightly differentiated, just like the seed growing into the sprout

units.sanskrit: ततो ऽपि क्रमेण स्थूलीभवत्तदद्भ्य आण्डं समवर्तत संवृत्तम् ।
units.english: Then gradually, it became larger and then it became an egg,coming out of water

units.sanskrit: आण्डमिति दैर्ध्यं छान्दसम् । तदण्डं संवत्सरस्य कालस्य प्रसिद्धस्य मात्रां परिमाणमभिन्नस्वरूपमेवाशयत स्थितं बभूव ।
units.english: The lengthened form ‘Āṇḍam’ is a Vedic anomaly for the simple form ‘aṇḍam ’This egg lay for the period of one year,the measure of time known as ‘one year’;

units.sanskrit: तत्ततः संवत्सरपरिमाणात्कालादूर्ध्वं निरभिद्यत निर्भिन्नं वयसामिवाण्डम् ।
units.english: during all this time it lay entirely undifferentiated in form;after that period of one year, it broke open;

units.sanskrit: तस्य निर्भिन्नस्याण्डस्य कपाले द्वे रजतं च सुवर्णं चाभवतां संवृत्ते ॥
units.english: burst open, like birds’ eggs of the Egg thus broken up, there were two halves of the eggshell,one silver and the other gold

units.sanskrit: तद् यद् रजतं सेयं पृथिवी ।
units.english: That which was silver is this Earth;

units.sanskrit: यत् सुवर्णं सा द्यौः ।
units.english: that which was gold is Heaven;

units.sanskrit: यज् जरायु ते पर्वताः ।
units.english: that which was the thick membrane became the Mountains;

units.sanskrit: यद् उल्बं (स) समेघो नीहारः ।
units.english: that which was the thin membrane became the Mist along with Clouds;

units.sanskrit: या धमनयस् ता नद्यः ।
units.english: what were the arteries became Rivers;

units.sanskrit: यद् वास्तेयम् उदकं स समुद्रः ॥
units.english: that which was the abdominal fluid became the Ocean

units.sanskrit: तत्तयोः कपालयोर्यद्रजतं कपालमासीत्सेयं पृथिवी पृथिव्युपलक्षितमधो ऽण्डकपालमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Of the two halves of the Eggshell, that which was the silver half is this Earth; that is, the lower half of the shell is represented by the Earth

units.sanskrit: यत्सुवर्णं कपालं सा द्यौर्द्युलोकोपलक्षितमूर्ध्वं कपालमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: That which was the golden half is Heaven; that is, the upper half of the shell is represented by the Heavenly Region

units.sanskrit: यज्जरायु गर्भपरिवेष्टनं स्थूलमण्डस्य द्विशकलीभावकाल आसीत्ते पर्वता बभूवुः । यदुल्वं सूक्ष्मं गर्भपरिवेष्टनं तत्सह मेद्यैः समेघो नीहारो ऽवश्यायो बभूवेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: That which was the thick membranewhich was the thick covering over the embryo, at the time that the egg burst into two parts,this became the mountains That which was the thin membrane became the Mistthe frostalong with the clouds

units.sanskrit: या गर्भस्य जातस्य देहे धमनयः शिरास्ता नद्यो बभूवुः । यत्तस्य बस्तौ भवं वास्तेयमुदकं स समुद्रः ॥
units.english: Those that were the arteries of the embryo when born became the rivers That which was the abdominal fluid,the fluid in the abdomen of the born embryo,became the Ocean

units.sanskrit: अथ यत् तद् अजायत सो ऽसाव् आदित्यः ।
units.english: And what was born was the Sun

units.sanskrit: तं जायमानं घोषा उलूलवो ऽनूदतिष्ठन्त् सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामाः ।
units.english: When he was born, shouts, loud and extensive, arose; as also all beings and desires

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तस्योदयं प्रति प्रत्यायनं प्रति घोषा उलूलवो ऽनूत्तिष्ठन्ति सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामाः ॥
units.english: It is for this reason that whenever the Sun rises and sets, shouts, loud and exensive , arise, as also all beings and all desires

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्तदजायत गर्भरूपं तस्मिन्नण्डे सो ऽसावादित्यस्तमादित्यं
units.english: And what was born,in the form of the embryo in the said egg,was the Sun

units.sanskrit: जायमानं घोषाः शब्दा उलूलव उरूरवो विस्तीर्णरवा उदतिष्ठन्नुत्थितवन्त ईश्वरस्येवेह
units.english: When this Sun was born, shoutssoundsloud and extensive,‘ulūlava’ standing for ‘urūravaḥ’; loud and extensive sounds,arose

units.sanskrit: प्रथमपुत्रजन्मनि सर्वाणि च स्थावरजङ्गमानि भूतानि सर्वे च तेषां भूतानां
units.english: just as shouts arise on the birth of the first son of a king as also all beingsanimate and inanimateand all desires of those beings;

units.sanskrit: कामाः काम्यन्त इति विषयाः स्त्रीवस्रान्नादयः ।
units.english: ‘Kāmāḥ’ ‘desires’, here stands for things that are desired, such as women, clothing, food and so forth

units.sanskrit: यस्मादादित्यजन्मनिमित्ता भूतकामोत्पत्तिस्तस्मादद्यत्वे ऽपि तस्या'दित्यस्योदयं प्रति प्रत्यायनं प्रत्यस्तगमनं च प्रत्यथवा पुनः पुनः प्रत्यागमनं प्रत्यायनं
units.english: Inasmuch as on account of the birth of the Sun, the beings and the desired things came into existence,even today,whenever the Sun rises and when he sets,or ‘pratyāgama’ may be taken as rising again and again,on that account, there arise all beings and all desires, and also shouts, loud and extensive

units.sanskrit: प्रसिद्धं ह्येतदुदयादौ सवितुः ॥
units.english: This phenomenon is wellknown as happening at sunrise

units.sanskrit: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् आदित्यं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अभ्याशो ह यद् एनं साधवो घोषा आ च गच्छेयुर् उप च निम्रेडेरन् निम्रेडेरन् ॥
units.english: Now, if any one, knowing this, meditate upon the Sun as Brahman, quickly will pleasant shouts approach him and will continue,yea, will continue

units.sanskrit: स यः कश्चिदेतमेवं यथोक्तमहिमानं विद्वान्सन्नादित्यं ब्रह्मेत्युपास्ते स तद्भावं प्रतिपद्यत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: If any one, knowing the Sun as endowed with the aforesaid greatness, meditate upon the Sun as Brahman, then he attains the same character as the Sun;

units.sanskrit: किञ्च दृष्टं फलमभ्याशः क्षिप्रं तद्विदो यदिति क्रियाविशेषणमेनमेवंविदं साधवः ।
units.english: and further there is a perceptible result also Quicklyvery soon‘Yat’ is an adverb,there approach him pleasantagreeableshouts

units.sanskrit: साधुत्वं घोषादीनां यदुपभोगे पापानुबन्धाभावः ।
units.english: The pleasantness of the shouts etc, consists in this that in their enjoyment there is no element of sin

units.sanskrit: आ च गच्छेयुरागच्छेयुश्चोप च निम्रेडेरन्नुपनिम्रेडेरंश्च न केवलमागमनमात्रं घोषाणामुपसुखयेयुश्चोपसुखं च कुर्यरित्यर्थः ।
units.english: They will approach him, and will also continue; there is not merely approach of the shouts, in fact, they continue to delight him, and bring pleasure to him,The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse and also the great importance of the subject

units.sanskrit: IN REE NICHT ZULÄSSIGE ZEICHEN
units.english: End of Section of Discourse End of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ चतुर्थो ऽध्यायः
units.english: It has been explained above under Sec

units.sanskrit: वायुप्राणयोर्ब्रह्मणः पाददृष्ट्यध्यासः पुरस्ताद्वर्णितः ।
units.english: of Discourse how Vāyu and Prāṇaare to be viewed as the ‘feet’ of Brahman

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीं तयोः साक्षाद्ब्रह्मत्वेनोपास्यत्वायोत्तरमारभ्यते ।
units.english: Now proceeds the teaching that these same Vāyu and Prāṇa are to be meditated upon as Brahman itself

units.sanskrit: सुखावबोधार्था'ख्यायिका, विद्यादानग्रहणविधिप्रदर्शनार्था च श्रद्धान्नदानानुद्धतत्वादीनां च विद्याप्राप्ति साधनत्वं प्रदर्श्यत आख्यायिकया ।
units.english: The story has been introduced, for the purpose of making the teaching easily intelligible, and also for the purpose of laying down the procedure by which the Teaching is to be imparted and received;and the story also shows how the attainment of the knowledge of the Teaching is to be brought about by such means as faiths giving of food, absence of haughtiness humility and so forth

units.sanskrit: जानश्रुतिर्जनश्रुतस्यापत्यम् ।
units.english: Om! There lived a descendant of Janaśruti, his Greatgrandson;

units.sanskrit: हः ऐतिह्यार्थः ।
units.english: he built Resthouses all round,thinking that everywhere they may eat of mine

units.sanskrit: पुत्रस्य पौत्रः पौत्रायणः स एव श्रद्धादेयः श्रद्धापुरःसरमेव ब्राह्मणादिभ्यो देयमस्येति श्रद्धादेयः । बहुदायी प्रभूतं दातुं शीलमस्येति बहुदायी । बहुपाक्यो बहु पक्तव्यमहन्यहनि गृहे यस्यासौबहुपाक्यः ।
units.english: Jānaśruti,the descendant of Janaśrutithe particle ‘ha’ means that such is the story told among people;his greatgrandsonthe son of his grandson;he was a pious giver,ie what he gave to Brāhmaṇas and others was always given with due faith and regard;he was very generous,ie he had the habit of giving away much;he had plenty of cooked food,that is, large quantities of food were cooked in his house, every day;

units.sanskrit: भोजनार्थिभ्यो बह्वस्य गृहे ऽन्नं पच्यत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, in his house much food was cooked for giving away to those seeking for food

units.sanskrit: एवङ्गुणसम्पन्नो ऽसौ जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणो विशिष्टे देशे काले च कस्मिंश्चिदास बभूव ।
units.english: This descendant of Janaśruti, his greatgrandson, endowed with such qualities, lived in a particular place and at a particular time

units.sanskrit: स ह सर्वतः सर्वासु दिक्षु ग्रामेषु नगरेषु चा'वसथानेत्य वसन्ति येष्वित्यावसथास्तान्मापयाञ्चक्रे कारितवानित्यर्थः । सर्वत एव मे ममान्नं तेष्वावसथेषु वसन्तो ऽत्स्यन्ति भोक्ष्यन्त इत्येवमभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: He all roundsin all directions, in villages and in cities,builterectedResthouses, for people to come and live in;his idea being that everywhereliving in these Resthouses,people may eat of mine,ie the food supplied by me

units.sanskrit: अथ ह हंसा निशायाम् अतिपेतुः ।
units.english: Once at night, some flamingoes flew along;

units.sanskrit: तद् धैवं हंसो हंसम् अभ्युवाद । हो हो ऽयि भल्लाक्ष भल्लाक्ष जानश्रुतेः पौत्रायणस्य समं दिवा ज्योतिर् आततं तन् मा प्रसाङ्क्षीस् तत् त्वां मा प्रधाक्षीर् इति ॥
units.english: then one flamingo said to the other flamingo‘Ho, Ho, O, Bhallākṣa, Bhallākṣa! The effulgence of Janaśruti’s greatgrandson is pervading like Heaven; touch it not, lest it scorch thee!

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति राजनि तस्मिन्धर्मकाले हर्म्यतलस्थे ऽथ ह हंसा निशायां रात्रावतिपेतुः ।
units.english: Under such circumstances, once upon a time, during the hot season, while the king was seated on the roof of the palace, one night, some flamingoes flew along;

units.sanskrit: ऋषयो देवता वा राज्ञो ऽन्नदानगुणैस्तोषिताः सन्तो हंसारूपा भूत्वा राज्ञो दर्शनगोचरे ऽतिपेतुः ।
units.english: that is, some ancient sages or deities, being pleased with the king’s generosity in giving food, took the shape of flamingoes and flew along within range of the king’s vision

units.sanskrit: तत्तस्मिन्काले तेषां पततां हंसानामेकः पृष्ठतः पतन्नग्रतः पतन्तं हंसमभ्युवादाभ्युक्तवान्हो हो ऽयीति भो भो इति सम्बोध्य भल्लाक्ष भल्लाक्षेत्यादरं दर्शयन् यथा पश्य पश्याऽश्चर्यमिति तद्वत् । भल्लाक्षेति मन्ददृष्टित्वं सूचयन्नाह । अथवा सम्यग्ब्रह्मदर्शनाभिमानवत्त्वात्तस्यासकृदुपालब्धस्तेन पीड्यमानो ऽमर्षितया तत्सूचयति भल्लाक्षेति ।
units.english: At that time, when the flamingoes were flying along, one of them, flying behind the rest, said to the flamingo flying before him ‘Ho’, ‘ho’Hey, Hey, having attracted his attention by addressing him thusBhallākṣa! Bhallākṣa!by the repetition showing great regard for what he was going to say, just as in the expression ‘See! See! How wonderful it is!’The term ‘Bhallākṣa’ is meant to indicate shortsightedness;or it may be that the flamingo addressed was proud of his superior knowledge of Brahman and on account of his pride, he has been thus taunted by being addressed twice as ‘Bhallākṣa, Bhallākṣa’, by the flamingo behind him who finds his arrogance unpardonable

units.sanskrit: जानश्रुतेः पौत्रायणस्य समं तुल्यं दिवा द्युलोकेन ज्योतिः प्रभास्वरमन्नदानादिजनितप्रभावजमाततं व्याप्तं द्युलोकस्पृगित्यर्थः ।
units.english: He said to himThe Effulgence of Janaśruti’s greatgrandson is like Heaventhe Heavenly Region,ie his effulgent brightness due to the magnificence of his generous distribution of food,pervading! ie it touches Heavenly Regions

units.sanskrit: दिवाह्ना वा समं ज्योतिरित्येतत् ।
units.english: Or the expression ‘samam divā’ may mean that his effulgence is like daylight;

units.sanskrit: तन्मा प्रसाङ्क्षीः सञ्जनं सक्तिं तेन ज्योतिषा सम्बन्धं मा कार्षीरित्यर्थः । तत्प्रसञ्जनेन तज्ज्योतिस्त्वा त्वां मा प्रधाक्षीर्मा दहत्वित्यर्थः पुरुषव्यत्यनेन मा प्रधाक्षीदिति ॥
units.english: hence touch it not,ie do not come into contact with the effulgencelest you do come into contact with that effulgence, it should scorch thee,burn thee! The verb ‘pradhākṣīḥ’ which is in the Second Person has to be construed as ‘pradhākṣīt’ in the Third Person

units.sanskrit: तम् उ ह परः प्रत्युवाच कम् व् अर एनम् एतत् सन्तं सयुग्वानम् इव रैक्वम् आत्थ इति । यो नु कथं सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ॥
units.english: The other replied‘How can you speak of him, being what he is, as if he were Raikva with the Cart?’ ‘Of what sort is this Raikva with the Cart?’

units.sanskrit: तमेवमुक्तवन्तं पर इतरो ऽग्रगामी प्रत्युवाचारे निकृष्टो ऽयं राजा
units.english: When the first flamingo had said as above, the other, which was flying ahead, replied‘Oh! this poor king is a mean fellow;

units.sanskrit: वराकस्तं कमु एनं सन्तं केन माहात्म्येन युक्तं सन्तमिति कुत्सयत्येनमेवं सबहुमानमेतद्वचनमात्थ रैक्वमिव, सयुग्वानं सह युग्वना गन्त्र्या वर्तत इति सयुग्वा रैक्वः ।
units.english: and such as he isthis being added with a tone of reproach‘you yet talk of him with great respect, as if he were endowed with highmindedness,as if he were Raikva with the Cart,ie Raikva who possesses a cart

units.sanskrit: अननुरूपमस्मिन्नयुक्तमीदृशं वक्तुं रैक्व इवेत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: It is incompatible with his character and improper to speak of him as if he were like Raikva with the Cart

units.sanskrit: इतरश्चा'हयो नु कथं त्वयोच्यते सयुग्वा रैक्व इत्युक्तवन्तं भल्लाक्ष आह शृणु यथा स रैक्वः ॥
units.english: The other flamingo then asked‘Of what sort is this Raikva with the Cart?’When he was asked thus, Bhallākṣa said‘Listen, of what sort is Raikva with the Cart?’

units.sanskrit: यथा कृताय विजितायाधरेयाः संयन्त्य् एवम् एनं सर्वं तद् अभिसमेति यत् किंच प्रजाः साधु कुर्वन्ति ।
units.english: Just as all the lower casts of the Dice go over to one who has won the Kṛtacast, so does go over to him whatever good the people do;

units.sanskrit: यस् तद् वेद यत् स वेद स मयैतद् उक्त इति ॥
units.english: so also to him who knows what he knows Such is he who has been spoken of by me

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके कृतायः कृतो नामायो द्यूतसमये प्रसिद्धश्चतुरङ्कः स यदा जयति द्यूते प्रवृत्तानां तस्मै विजिताय तदर्थमितरे त्रिद्व्येकाङ्का अधरे ऽयास्त्रेताद्वापरकलिनामानः
units.english: In common practice, when the Kṛtacast of the Dice which bears four marks and is used in gambling, wins among persons engaged in gambling,to the man who has won with that Kṛtacast,go overbecome included,all the lower casts, bearing three, two and one mark respectively named Tretā, Dvāpara and Kali

units.sanskrit: चतुरङ्के कृताये त्रिद्व्येकाङ्कानां विद्यमानत्वात्तदन्तर्भवन्तीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: That is to say, inasmuch as the number four on the Kṛtacast contains within itself the lower numbers three, two and one, these latter become included in the former

units.sanskrit: यथायं दृष्टान्त एवमेनं रैक्वं कृतायस्थानीयं त्रेताद्यायस्थानीयं सर्वं तदभिसमेत्यन्तर्भवति रैक्वे ।
units.english: so, in the case of Raikva also,who has the same position as the Kṛtacast,there goes over to him everything that is in the position of the other three casts Treta and the rest; that is, everything becomes included in Raikva

units.sanskrit: किं तद्यत्किञ्च लोके सर्वाः प्रजाः साधु शोभनं धर्मजातं कुर्वन्ति तत्सर्वं रैक्वस्य धर्मे ऽन्तर्भवति ।
units.english: What is this everything that becomes included in him?Whatever good the people do,ie whatever good and righteous deeds men do in the world become included in the merit acquired by Raikva;

units.sanskrit: तस्य च फले सर्वप्राणिधर्मफलमन्तर्भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, the reward of the good acts of all living beings become included in the reward of Raikva’s own good acts

units.sanskrit: तथान्यो ऽपि कश्चिद्यस्तद्वेद्यं वेद । किं तद्यद्वेद्यं स रैक्वो वेद ।
units.english: So also to him who knows what he knows;what is it?that which Raikva knows;

units.sanskrit: तद्वेद्यमन्यो ऽपि यो वेद तमपि सर्वप्राणिधर्मजातं तत्फलं च रैक्वमिवाभिसमेतीत्यनुवर्तते ।
units.english: anyone else who knows that, to him also go over the good acts done by all living beings and also the reward of those acts;

units.sanskrit: स एवंभूतो मया विद्वानेतदिक्त एवमुक्तो रैक्ववत्स एव कृतायस्थानीयो भवतीत्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: just in the same way as they go to Raikva Such is hethe knowing man, who, like Raikva, becomes like the Kṛtacast

units.sanskrit: तद् उ ह जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायण उपशुश्राव ।
units.english: Janaśruti’s greatgrandson overheard this;

units.sanskrit: स ह संजिहान एव क्षत्तारम् उवाचाङ्गारे ह सयुग्वानम् इव रैक्वम् आत्थेति । यो नु कथं सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ॥
units.english: and as soon as he rose, he spoke to the Bard‘O friend, speak of Raikva with the Cart‘‘Well, what sort of person is this Raikva with the Cart?’

units.sanskrit: यथा कृताय विजितायाधरेयाः संयन्त्य् एवम् एनं सर्वं तद् अभिसमेति यत् किंच प्रजाः साधु कुर्वन्ति ।
units.english: ‘Just as all the lower casts of the Dice go over to one who has won with the Kṛtacast, so does go over to him whatever good the people do;

units.sanskrit: यस् तद् वेद यत् स वेद स मयैतद् उक्त इति ॥
units.english: and so also to him who knows what he knows Such is he who has been spoken of by me

units.sanskrit: तदु ह तदेतदीदृशं हंसवाक्यमात्मनः कुत्सारूपमन्यस्य विदुषो रैक्वादेः प्रशंसारूपमुपशुश्राव श्रुतवान्हर्म्यतलस्थो राजा
units.english: The said statement made by the flamingo,which eulogised another knowing person in the shape of Raikva, and deprecated himselfthe king, Janaśruti’s greatgrandson heard while seated on the roof of his palace;

units.sanskrit: तच्च हंसवाक्यं स्मरन्नेव पौनः पुन्येन रात्रिशेषमतिवाहयामास ।
units.english: and bearing in mind the flamingo’s words, and cogitating over it over and over again, he passed the remaining portion of the night

units.sanskrit: ततः स बन्दिभी राजा स्तुतियुक्ताभिर्वाग्भिः प्रतिबोध्यमान उवाच क्षत्तारं संजिहान एव शयनं निद्रां वा परित्यजन्नेव हे ऽङ्ग वत्सारे स सयुग्वानमिव रैक्वमात्थ किं माम् । स एव स्तुत्यर्हे नाहमित्यभिप्रायः । अथवा सयुग्वानं रैक्वमात्थ गत्वा मम तद्दिदृक्षा;
units.english: Then, having been roused from his slumber by the eulogistic chants of the Bards,or, on rising from sleep,he spoke to the Bard‘O, my frieùd, speak of Raikva with the Cart,not of me;’ that is, he alone is deserving of all the eulogy that you have been chanting,not ’, or,‘Go and speak to Raikva with the Cart that wish to see him’

units.sanskrit: तदेवशब्दो ऽवधारणार्थो ऽनर्थको वा वाच्यः ।
units.english: In this latter sense, the particle ‘iva’ may be taken as indicating emphasis, or as conveying no meaning

units.sanskrit: स च क्षत्ता प्रत्युवाच रैक्वानयनकामो राज्ञो ऽभिप्रायज्ञो यो नु कथं सयुग्वा रैक्व इति, राज्ञैवं चोक्त आनेतुं तच्चिह्नं ज्ञतुमिच्छन्यो नु कथं सयुग्वा रैक्व इत्यवोचत् ।
units.english: The Bard, understanding the king’s wish and desirous of bringing Raikva with the Cart, said‘What sort of person is this Raikva with the Cart?’ Having been told by the king and being anxious to bring over Raikva, the man naturally wanted to know who this man was

units.sanskrit: स च भल्लाक्षवचनमेवावोचत् ॥
units.english: Upon this, Janaśruti’s greatgrandson repeated the description given by Bhallākṣa, the flamingo

units.sanskrit: स ह क्षत्तान्विष्य नाविदम् इति प्रत्येयाय ।
units.english: The Bard, having searched him, came back, saying ‘ found him not’

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच यत्रारे ब्राह्मणस्यान्वेषणा तद् एनम् अर्च्छेति ॥
units.english: Then the king said‘Oh, that place where search is made for the Brāhmaṇa there search him’

units.sanskrit: तस्य स्मरन्स ह क्षत्ता नगरं ग्रामं वा गत्वान्विष्य रैक्वं नाविदं न व्यज्ञासिषमिति प्रत्येयाय प्रत्यागतवान् ।
units.english: Remembering the king’s words, the Bard went to villages and cities and searched for Raikva, and returned saying ‘ found him not’;that is, could not recognise him

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच क्षत्तरमरे यत्र ब्राह्मणस्य ब्रह्मविद एकान्ते ऽरण्ये नदीपुलिनादौ विविक्ते देशे ऽन्वेषणानुमार्गणं भवति तत्तत्रैनं रैक्वमर्छ ऋच्छ गच्छ तत्र
units.english: Then the king said to the Bard‘Oh, the place where search is made for the Brāhmaṇa knowing Brahman,that is, in some quiet and lonely place or the bank of a river and such places,there,ie in such places,search for him,go and find him in such places

units.sanskrit: सो ऽधस्ताच् छकटस्य पामानं कषमाणम् उपोपविवेश । तं हाभ्युवाद त्वं नु भगवः सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ।
units.english: While he was scratching his itch, seated under the cart, he sat near him and said to him,‘O, Revered sir, are you Raikva with the Cart ’He replied‘Well, fellow, yes, am’

units.sanskrit: अहं ह्य् अरा इति ह प्रतिजज्ञे ।
units.english: The Bard came back saying ‘ have found him’

units.sanskrit: इत्युक्तः क्षत्तान्विष्य तं विजने देशे ऽधस्ताच्छकटस्य गन्त्र्याः पामानं
units.english: Having been thus directed, the Bard searched for him, and in a lonely place, found him under the cart scratching his itch;

units.sanskrit: खर्जूं कषमाणं कण्डूयमानं दृष्ट्वायं नूनं सयुग्वा रैक्व इत्युप समीप उपविवेश
units.english: and he thought that ‘this must be Raikva with the Cart’; he then approached him and sat near him, with great respect;

units.sanskrit: तं च रैक्वं हाभ्युवादोक्तवान् । त्वमसि हे भगवो भगवन्सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ।
units.english: thereupon he said to Raikva,‘O, Revered sir, are you Raikva with the Cart?’Being thus asked, he replied‘Well fellow, yes, am’;

units.sanskrit: एवं पृष्टो ऽहमस्मि ह्यरा अर इति हानादर एव प्रतिजज्ञे ऽभ्युपगतवान् ।
units.english: the term ‘āre’ fellow was meant to indicate disdain Having thus recognised him, the Bard returned saying ‘ have found him

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: तद् उ ह जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणः षट् शतानि गवां निष्कम् अश्वतरीरथं तद् आदाय प्रतिचक्रमे ।
units.english: Then Janaśruti’s greatgrandson took with him six hundred cows, necklace, and a chariot with mules and went over, and said to him

units.sanskrit: एव जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणः षट्शतानि गवां निष्कं कण्ठहारमश्वतरीरथमश्वतरीभ्यां युक्तं रथं तदादाय धनं गृहीत्वा प्रतिचक्रमे रैक्वं प्रति गतवान् ।
units.english: Then, having understood that the sage was Intending to enter the life of a Householder, and also that he was desirous of acquiring wealthJanaśruti’s greatgrandson took with him six hundred cows, necklace, a chariot with mulesyoked with a pair of mules,and along with all this wealth, went over to where Raikva was;

units.sanskrit: तं च गत्वाभ्युवाद हाभ्युक्तवान् ॥
units.english: and having approached him, said to him as follows

units.sanskrit: रैक्वेमानि षट् शतानि गवाम् अयं निष्को ऽयम् अश्वतरीरथः ।
units.english: ‘Raikva, here are six hundred cows, necklace, and a chariot with mules

units.sanskrit: अनु म एतां भगवो देवतां शाधि यां देवताम् उपास्स इति ॥
units.english: Now, revered sir, teach me that Deity which you worship’

units.sanskrit: हे रैक्व गवां षट्शतानीमानि तुभ्यं मया'नीतान्ययं निष्को ऽश्वतरीरथश्चायमेतद्धनमादत्स्व
units.english: ‘O, Raikva, here are these six hundred cows,brought by me for you,here is a necklace,and a chariot with mules;

units.sanskrit: भगवो ऽनुशाधि च मे मामेतां यां च देवतां त्वमुपाःसे तद्देवतोपदेशेन मामनुशाधीत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: please accept all this wealth, and teach me that Deity which you worship; that is, instruct me regarding that Deity

units.sanskrit: तम् उ ह परः प्रत्युवाचाह हारेत्वा शूद्र तवैव सह गोभिर् अस्त्व् इति । तद् उ ह पुनर् एव जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणः सहस्रं गवां निष्कम् अश्वतरीरथं दुहितरं तद् आदाय प्रतिचक्रमे ॥
units.english: The other answered him thus‘O, Śūdra! may this necklace with the chariot and the cows remain with thyself’;thereupon Janaśruti’s greatgrandson again came to him with a thousand cows, a necklace, a chariot with mules and his daughter, and went over to him

units.sanskrit: तमेवमुक्तवन्तं राजानं प्रत्युवाच परो रैक्वः ।
units.english: When the king had said this, the otherie Raikvaanswered him thus

units.sanskrit: अहेत्ययं निपातो विनिग्रहार्थीयो ऽन्यत्रेह त्वनर्थकः । एवशब्दस्य पृथक्प्रयोगात् ।
units.english: but in the present context, it does not signify anything; as the term ‘eva’ has been used separately for the purpose of expressing resentment

units.sanskrit: हारेत्वा हारेण युक्तेत्वा गन्त्री सेयं हारेत्वा गोभिः सह तवैवास्तु तिष्ठतु न ममापर्याप्तेन कर्मार्थमनेन प्रयोजनमित्यभिप्रायो हे शूद्रेति
units.english: ‘May this necklace with the chariot,along with the cows remain with thee thyself;let them be with thyselfO, Śūdra’;the sense is that ‘ have no use for these which are insufficient for my purpose’

units.sanskrit: ननु राजासौ क्षत्तृसम्बन्धात्स ह क्षत्तारमुवाचेत्युक्तम् ।
units.english: ObjectionThe person addressed was a king, as is clear from the fact that he had a Bard in attendance;

units.sanskrit: विद्याग्रहणाय च ब्राह्मणसमीपोपगमाच्छूद्रस्य चानधिकारात्कथमिदमननुरूपं रैक्वेणोच्यते हे शूद्रेति ।
units.english: as has been said before‘He said to the Bard Then again, he had approached the Brāhmaṇa Raikva for the purpose of acquiring knowledge, to which a Śūdra is not entitled

units.sanskrit: तत्रा'हुराचार्याःहंसवचनश्रवणाच्छुगेनमाविवेश । तेनासौ शुचा श्रुत्वा रैक्वस्य महिमानं वा आद्रवतीति ऋषिरात्मनः परोक्षज्ञतां दर्शयञ्शूद्रेत्याहेति ।
units.english: How then is it that Raikva has adopted an improper form of address ‘O, Śūdra’? The revered Teachers have explained this as follows On overhearing the conversation of the flamingoes, the king was struck with sorrow; under this sorrow, ‘śucā’ he heard of Raikva’s greatness, and then became mollified;

units.sanskrit: शूद्रवद्वा धनेनैवैनं विद्याग्रहणायोपजगाम न च शुश्रूषया ।
units.english: or his purpose may be to express displeasure at the king having come to him for acquiring knowledge, through gifts only, and not through service,thus behaving improperly, like a Śūdra

units.sanskrit: न तु जात्यैव शूद्र इति ।
units.english: He did not mean that the king was a Śūdra by caste

units.sanskrit: अपरे पुनराहुरल्पं धनमाहृतमिति रुषैवैनमुक्तवाञ्छूद्रेति ।
units.english: Others have offered the following explanationThe king had brought a small quantity of wealth, hence in anger the sage addressed him as ‘shūdra’;

units.sanskrit: लिङ्गं च बह्वाहरण उपादानं धनस्येति ।
units.english: as indicating the impropriety of this conduct, there is the text that ‘Wealth should be accepted only when it is offered in plenty’

units.sanskrit: तदुहर्षेर्मतं ज्ञात्वा पुनरेव जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणो गवां सहस्रमधिकं जायां चर्षेरभिमतां दुहितरमात्मनस्तदादाय प्रतिचक्रमे क्रान्तवान्
units.english: Therefore, having understood the wishes of the sage Janaśruti’s greatgrandson took with him one thousand cowsmorehis daughter a fit wife for the sage,and came to the sage

units.sanskrit: रैक्वेदं सहस्रं गवाम् अयं निष्को ऽयम् अश्वतरीरथ इयं जायायं ग्रामो यस्मिन्न् आस्से ऽन्व् एव मा भगवः शाधीति ॥
units.english: He said to him‘Raikva’, here are a thousand cows, this necklace, this chariot with mules, this wife, and this village in which you dwell Now, revered sir, teach me

units.sanskrit: तस्या ह मुखम् उपोद्गृह्णन्न् उवाचाजहारेमाः शूद्रानेनैव मुखेनालापयिष्यथा इति ।
units.english: Holding her mouth, he said,‘Thou hast, O, Śūdra, brought these;

units.sanskrit: ते हैते रैक्वपर्णा नाम महावृषेषु यत्रास्मा उवास ।
units.english: by this mouth alone dost thou make me speak’,These are the villages named ‘Raikvaparṇā’ in the Mahāvṛṣa country, where he lived

units.sanskrit: तस्मै होवाच ॥
units.english: He then taught him

units.sanskrit: रैक्वेदं गवां सहस्रमयं निष्को ऽयमश्वतरीरथ इयं जायार्थं मम दुहिता'नीतायं च ग्रामो यस्मिन्नाःसे तिष्ठसि स च त्वदर्थे मया कल्पितः तदेतत्सर्वमादायानुशाध्येव
units.english: ‘O Raikva, here are a thousand cows, this necklace, the chariot with mules, my daughterfor being your wife,all this has been brought by me;and this village also where you dwellthis also has been set apart by me for you Accept all this, and teach me, O revered sir’

units.sanskrit: मा मां हे भगव इत्युक्तस्तस्या जायार्थमानीताया राज्ञो दुहितुर्हैव मुखं द्वारं विद्याया दाने तीर्थमुपोद्गृह्णञ्जानन्नित्यर्थः । ब्रह्मचारी धनदायी मेधावी श्रोत्रियः प्रियः । विद्यया वा विद्या प्राह तानि तीर्थानि षण्मम ॥ इति विद्याया वचनं विज्ञायते हि ।
units.english: On being thus addressed, the sage, holding the mouth of the king’s daughter who had been brought for being his wife,ie knowing the mouth to be the doorway, the proper channel, for the imparting of knowledge,according to the declaration that‘The Religious Student, the giver of wealth, the exceptionally intelligent, the Vedic scholar, a loved person, and learning itself,these are my six channels, said Knowledge;’ such is the declaration known to have been made by Knowledge

units.sanskrit: आजहारा'हृतवान्भवान्यदिमा गा यच्चान्यद्धनं तत्साध्विति वाक्यशेषः । शूद्रेति पूर्वोक्तानुकृतिमात्रं न तु कारणान्तरापेक्षया पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: Knowing this, the sage held her mouth, and said‘Thou hast brought these, cows and other things,and thou bast done well’this has to be supplied, ‘Śūdra’this form of address is only in accordance with the former address, and has no other signification, as on the previous occasion

units.sanskrit: अनेनैव मुखेन विद्याग्रहणतीर्थेना'लापयिष्यथा आलापयसीति मां भाषयसीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: ‘It is by this mouth alone’which is a fit channel of knowing,‘dost thou make me speak’

units.sanskrit: ते हैते ग्रामा रैक्वपर्णा नाम विख्याता महावृषेषु देशेषु यत्र येषु ग्रामेषूवासोषितवान् रैक्वस्तानसौ ग्रामानदादस्मै रैक्वाय राजा ।
units.english: There are the villages known as Raikvaparṇā in the Mahāvṛṣa country, wherein which villageslived Raikva Thereupon he taught him,the Science

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: वायुर् वाव संवर्गः ।
units.english: Air indeed is the Absorbent;

units.sanskrit: यदा वा अग्निर् उद्वायति वायुम् एवाप्येति ।
units.english: when Fire goes out, it goes into Air;

units.sanskrit: यदा सूर्यो ऽस्तम् एति वायुम् एवाप्येति । यदा चन्द्रो ऽस्तम् एति वायुम् एवाप्येति ॥
units.english: when the Sun sets, it goes into Air; when the Moon sets, it goes into Air

units.sanskrit: वायुर्वाव संवर्गो वायुर्बाह्यो वावेत्यवधारणार्थः । संवर्गः संवर्जनात्संग्रहणात्संग्रसनाद्वा संवर्गः । वक्ष्यमाणा अग्न्याद्या देवता आत्मभावमापादयतीत्यतः संवर्गः ।
units.english: Air indeed is the Absorbent;The ‘Air’ meant here is the external Physical air;‘Vāva’ has the restrictive force;Absorbent,so called because it absorbs, swallows or merges in itself, the Air is called the ‘absorbent’ because it absorbs the Fire and other deities mentioned below into itself

units.sanskrit: सवर्जवाख्यो गुणो ध्येयो वायुवत् ।
units.english: So that the quality named ‘absorbence’ is to be meditated upon like the Air;

units.sanskrit: कृतायान्तभर्वदृष्टान्तात् ।
units.english: that such is the meaning is indicated by the example of the winning of the Kṛtāya dice described before

units.sanskrit: कथं संवर्गत्त्वं वायोरित्याह ।
units.english: The text proceeds to show in what way Air is the Absorbent

units.sanskrit: यदा यस्मिन्काले वा अग्निरुद्वायत्युद्वासनं प्राप्नोत्युपशाम्यति तदासावग्निर्वायुमेवाप्येति वायुस्वाभाव्यमपिगच्छति ।
units.english: Whenat which timeFire goes outbecomes extinguished,then itthe Firegoes into Air,that is, becomes of the nature of Air

units.sanskrit: तथा यदा सूर्यो ऽस्तमेति वायुमेवाप्येति ।
units.english: Similarly, when the Sun sets, it goes into Air;

units.sanskrit: यदा चन्द्रो ऽस्तमेति वायुमेवाप्येति ।
units.english: when the Moon sets, it goes into Air

units.sanskrit: ननु कथं सूर्याचन्द्रमसोः स्वरूपावस्थितयोर्वायावपिगमनम् ।
units.english: QuestionAs a matter of fact, the Sun and the Moon continue to exist in their own forms; how then can they be said to go into Air

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not vitiate the doctrine

units.sanskrit: अस्तमने ऽदर्शनप्राप्तेर्वायुनिमित्तत्वात् । वायुना ह्यस्तं नीयते सूर्यः चलनस्य वायुकार्यत्वात् ।
units.english: Because when on setting, the Sun and Moon become invisible, what makes them invisible is Air; it is Air by which the Sun is carried to setting, because every movement is the effect of Air

units.sanskrit: अथवा प्रलये सूर्याचन्द्रमसोः स्वरूपभ्रंशे तेजोरूपयोर्वायावेवापिगमनं स्यात् ॥ यदाप उच्छुष्यन्ति वायुम् एवापियन्ति ।
units.english: Or, the meaning may be that when, at Dissolution, the physical forms of the Sun and Moon perish, and they become dissolved into Light, they go into Air only,

units.sanskrit: वायुर् ह्य् एवैतान् सर्वान् संवृङ्क्ते ।
units.english: When Water dries up, it goes into Air For Air indeed absorbs them all

units.sanskrit: इत्य् अधिदैवतम् ॥
units.english: This is with reference to the Deities

units.sanskrit: तथा यदा'प उच्छुष्यन्त्युच्छोषमाप्नुवन्ति तदा वायुमेवापियन्ति ।
units.english: Similarly, when Water dries upreaches evaporation,it goes into Air;

units.sanskrit: वायुर्हि यस्मादेवैतानग्न्याद्यान्महाबलान्संवृङ्क्ते ।
units.english: because it is Air that absorbs all these extremely powerful elements Fire and the rest

units.sanskrit: अतो वायुः संवर्गगुण उपास्य इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: For this reason Air is to be meditated upon as endowed with the quality of absorbence

units.sanskrit: इत्यधिदैवतं देवतासु संवर्गदर्शनमुक्तम् ॥
units.english: This is with reference to Deities, ie the doctrine of Absorption as applied to Deities

units.sanskrit: अथाध्यात्मम् ।
units.english: Now with reference to the Body

units.sanskrit: प्राणो वाव सम्वर्गः ।
units.english: Breath indeed is the Absorbent

units.sanskrit: प्राणं चक्षुः । प्राणं श्रोत्रम् । प्राणं मनः ।
units.english: When one sleeps, Speech goes into Breath, the Eye goes into Breath, the Ear goes into Breath, the Mind goes into Breath

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ह्य् एवैतान् सर्वान् संवृङ्क्त इति ॥
units.english: For Breath indeed absorbs all these

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरमध्यात्ममात्मनि संवर्गदर्शनमिदमुच्यते ।
units.english: Now, next, follows the doctrine in reference to one’s own body

units.sanskrit: प्राणो मुख्योवाव संवर्गः ।
units.english: Breaththe principal Lifebreathindeed is the Absorbent

units.sanskrit: स पुरुषो यदा यस्मिन्काले स्वपिति प्राणमेव वागप्येति वायुमिवाग्निः प्राणं चक्षुः प्राणं श्रोत्रं प्राणं मनः प्राणो हि यस्मादेवैतान्वागादीन्सर्वान्संवृङ्क्त
units.english: Whenat the time thatone,the mansleeps, Speech goes into Breath,just as Fire goes into Air;the Eye goes into Breath; the Ear goes into Breath; the Mind goes into Breath For Breath indeed absorbs all theseSpeech and the rest These two indeed are the two Absorbents, Air among the Deities and Breath among the Organs

units.sanskrit: इति ॥ तौ वा एतौ द्वौ सम्वर्गौ ।
units.english: These two are the two absorbents,endowed with absorbent properties

units.sanskrit: वायुर् एव देवेषु प्राणः प्राणेषु ॥
units.english: Air is the Absorbent among Deities, and Breath the principal Lifebreathis the Absorbent among the OrgansSpeech and the rest

units.sanskrit: अथ ह शौनकं च कापेयम् अभिप्रतारिणं च काक्षसेनिं परिविष्यमाणौ ब्रह्मचारी बिभिक्षे ।
units.english: Once, while ŚaunakaKāpeya and Abhīpratārin Kākṣaseni were being served with food, a Religious Student begged of them;

units.sanskrit: तस्मा उ ह न ददतुः ॥
units.english: and they did not give to him anything

units.sanskrit: अथैतयोः स्तुत्यर्थमियमाख्यायिका'रभ्यते । हेत्यैतिह्यार्थः ।
units.english: This story is introduced for the purpose of eulogising these two Air and Breath The particle ‘ha’ indicates that the story is current among people

units.sanskrit: शौनकं च शुनकस्यापत्यं शोनकं कापेयं कपिगोत्रमभिप्रतारिणं च नामतः कक्षसेनस्यापत्यं काक्षसेनिं भोजनायोपविष्टौ परिविष्यमाणौ सूपकारैर्ब्रह्मचारी ब्रह्मविच्छण्डो
units.english: ‘Śaunaka the son of Śunaka‘Kāpeya’who belonged to the Kapigotra;‘Abhipratārin’by name‘Kākṣaseni’ the son of Kakṣasena;when these two were seated at their meals, and were being served with food,by the cooks,a Religious Student,proud of his knowledge of Brahmanbegged of themasked for food

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचारिणो ब्रह्मविन्मानितां बुद्ध्वा तं जिज्ञासमानौ तस्मा उ भिक्षां न जजतुर्न दत्तवन्तौ ह किमयं बक्ष्यतीति ॥
units.english: Those two understood that the Religious Student was proud of his knowledge of Brahman, and hence, with a view to test him, did not give to him anything,just waiting to see what he was going to say

units.sanskrit: स होवाच । महात्मनश् चतुरो देव एकः कः स जगार भुवनस्य गोपाः ।
units.english: He said‘The one Deity, Prajāpati, swallowed up the four Highsouled Ones,He, the protector of the universe

units.sanskrit: तं कापेय नाभिपश्यन्ति मर्त्या अभिप्रतारिन् बहुधा वसन्तम् ।
units.english: Him, O Kāpeya, mortals do not perceive, though O Abhipratārin,He dwells in many ways

units.sanskrit: यस्मै वा एतद् अन्नं तस्मा एतन् न दत्तम् इति ॥
units.english: He for whom all this food is,to him it has not been given’

units.sanskrit: स होवाच ब्रह्मचारी महात्मनश्चतुर इति द्वितीयाबहुवचनम् । देव एको ऽग्न्यादीन्वायुर्वागादीन्प्राणः ।
units.english: Hethe Religious Studentsaid ‘The four Highsouled Ones,this is to be construed as the Accusative plural,the one deity Prajāpati, swallowed up’, Vāyu Air swallowing Agni Fire and the rest, and Prāṇa Breath swallowing Vāk Speech and the rest

units.sanskrit: कः स प्रजापतिर्जगार ग्रसितवान् । कः स जगारेति प्रश्नमेके । भुवनस्य भवन्त्यस्मिन्भूतानीति भुवनं भूरादिः सर्वो लोकस्तस्य गोपा गोपायिता रक्षिता गोप्तेत्यर्थः । तं कं प्रजापतिं हे कापेय नाभिपश्यन्ति न जानन्ति मर्त्या मरणधर्माणो ऽविवेकिनो वा हे ऽभिप्रतारिन्बहुधाध्यात्माधिदैवताधिभूतप्रकारैर्वसन्तम्
units.english: Or, as some people explain this latter part of the sentence‘Kaḥ sa jagāra’, ‘who was it that swallowed up?’He the protector of the universe,the term ‘bhuvana’ stands for the whole Universe consisting of the Earth and other regions, in the sense that ‘all living beings live bhavanti thereinof this whole universe,He is the protector, the saviour,Himthis PrajāpatiO Kāpeya, mortalspeople prone to death, lacking in discrimination,do not perceiveknow;though, O, Abhipratārin,He dwells in many ways,spiritual, divine and material related to the Body, to the Deities and to the Elemental Substances

units.sanskrit: यस्मै वा एतदहन्यहन्यन्नमदनाया'ह्रियते संस्क्रियते च तस्मै प्रजापतय एतदन्नं न दत्तमिति ॥
units.english: He for whom all this food is prepared day by day, for whose Eating,to HimPrajāpatiit has not been given

units.sanskrit: तद् उ ह शौनकः कापेयः प्रतिमन्वानः प्रत्येयाय । आत्मा देवानां जनिता प्रजानां हिरङ्यदंष्ट्रो बभसो ऽनसूरिः ।
units.english: Thereupon, ŚaunakaKāpeya, reflecting, approached him and said‘It is the Self, the generator of the Deities and of Beings, He with golden teeth, the Devourer, Notunintelligent

units.sanskrit: महान्तम् अस्य महिमानम् आहुर् अनद्यमानो यद् अनन्नम् अत्ति ।
units.english: They describe his greatness as very great; without being Himself eaten, He eats even what is not food

units.sanskrit: इति वै वयम् ब्रह्मचारिन् नेदम् उपास्महे दत्तास्मै भिक्षाम् इति ॥
units.english: We, O Religious Student, meditate upon this’ ‘Give him food’

units.sanskrit: तदु ह ब्रह्मचारिणो वचनं शौनकः कापेयः प्रतिमन्वानो मनसा'लोचयन्ब्रह्मचारिणं प्रत्येयाया'जगाम ।
units.english: Thereupon, ŚaunakaKāpeya, reflecting pondering in his mind, over the words of the Religious Student, approached himthe Religious Student;

units.sanskrit: गत्वा चा'हयं त्वमवोचो न पश्यन्ति मर्त्या इति तं वयं पश्यामः । कथम्?आत्मा सर्वस्य स्थावरजङ्गमस्य । किञ्च देवानामग्न्यादीनामात्मनि संहृत्य ग्रसित्वा पुनर्जनितोत्पादयिता वायुरूपेणाधिदैवतमग्न्यादीनाम् ।
units.english: and having approached him, said‘He whom, you have said, mortals do not perceive,Him we do perceive’How so?‘It is the Selfof all things, animate and inanimate;further, it is He who absorbs within Himself and swallows Agni and other Deities and produces them again; He, in the form of Vāyu, is the generator of Agni and other Deities, in reference to the Divine form;

units.sanskrit: अध्यात्मं च प्राणरूपेण वागादीनां प्रजानां च दनिता ।
units.english: and in reference to the Body also, He, in the form of Prāṇa, is the generator of Speech and the other organs

units.sanskrit: अथ वा'त्मा देवानामग्निवागादीनां जनिता प्रजानां स्थावरजङ्गमानाम् ।
units.english: Or, the Self is the generator of the Deities, Agni, Vāk Speech and the rest, as also of beingsanimate and inanimate

units.sanskrit: हिरण्यदंष्ट्रो ऽभग्नदंष्ट्र इति यावत् । बभसो भक्षणशीलः ।
units.english: He is with golden teeth, ie His teeth are imperishable, never brokenHe is the Devourer,prone to devour things

units.sanskrit: अनसूरिः सूरिर्मेधावी न सूरिरसूरिस्तत्प्रतिषेधो ऽनसूरिः सूरिरेवेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Not unintelligent‘Sūri’, is intelligent, ‘asuri’, is unintellgent, and ‘anasūri’ is notunintelligent, ie intelligent

units.sanskrit: महान्तमतिप्रमाणमप्रमेयमस्य प्रजापतेर्महिमानं विभूतिमाहुर्ब्रह्मविदः ।
units.english: His Prajāpati’sgreatness,magnificence,theywho know Brahman,decscribe as very greatvery large, immeasurable;as without being Himself eaten devoured

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्स्वयमन्यैरनद्यमानो ऽभक्ष्यमाणो यदनन्नमग्निवागादिदेवतारूपमत्ति भक्षयतीति ।
units.english: by othersHe eats what is not food,ie AgniVāk and the other deities

units.sanskrit: वा इति निरर्थकः ।
units.english: The particle Vā’ is meaning, less

units.sanskrit: वयं हे ब्रह्मचारिन्, आ, इदमेवं यथोक्तलक्षणं ब्रह्म वयमा उपास्महे । वयमिति व्यवहितेन सम्बन्धः । अन्ये न वयमिदमुपास्महे । किं तर्हि परमेव ब्रह्मोपास्मह इति वर्णयन्ति ।
units.english: We, O, Religious Student, meditate upon this Brahman as described in this interpretation the construction is ‘Brahmacārin ā idam vayam upāsmahe’;others however construe the sentence differently as ‘Brahmacārin naidam vayam upāsmahe to mean that ‘we do not meditate upon this Brahman that has been described, but upon the Supreme Brahman’

units.sanskrit: दत्तास्मै भिक्षामित्यवोचद्भृत्यान् ॥
units.english: Thereupon Śaunaka told the servants to ‘give him food’

units.sanskrit: तस्मै उ ह ददुः ।
units.english: They gave it to him

units.sanskrit: ते वा एते पञ्चान्ये पञ्चान्ये दश सन्तस् तत् कृतम् ।
units.english: Now these five and the other five, becoming ten, constitute the Kṛta Dicecast

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् सर्वासु दिक्ष्व् अन्नम् एव दश कृतम् ।
units.english: Therefore in all quarters those ten are the food and the Kṛtacast

units.sanskrit: सैषा विराड् अन्नादी ।
units.english: This is Virāṭ the Eater of Food

units.sanskrit: तयेदं सर्वं दृष्टम् ।
units.english: By this all this becomes seen

units.sanskrit: सर्वम् अस्य इदं दृष्टं भवत्य् अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows thus sees all this and becomes an eater of food,yes, one who knows this

units.sanskrit: तस्मा उ ह ददुस्ते हि भिक्षाम् ।
units.english: They gave food to him

units.sanskrit: ते वै ये ग्रस्यन्ते ऽग्न्यादयो यश्च तेषां ग्रसिता वायुः पञ्चान्ये वागादिभ्यः, तथान्ये तेभ्यः पञ्चाध्यात्मं वागादयः प्राणश्च,
units.english: Now these fivethe five, Agni, and the rest, which are swallowed, and the Vāyu that swallows them,these are five; these are the five, distinct from Speech and the rest and these, Speech and the rest, along with Breath are the other five;

units.sanskrit: ते सर्वे दश सन्तस्तत्कृतं भवति, ते चतुरङ्क एकाय एवं चत्वारः त्र्यङ्कायः एवं त्रयो ऽपरे द्व्यङ्कायः एवं द्वावन्यावेकाङ्काय एवमेको ऽन्य,
units.english: thus making up the number Ten’, and becoming Ten, they constitute the Kṛtacast;the Ekāyacast with four marks, swallows four numbers; then the Dice with three marks swallows three numbers the dice with two marks swallows two numbers, and there is one more;

units.sanskrit: यत एवं तस्मात्सर्वासु दिक्षु दशस्वप्यग्न्याद्या वागाद्याश्च दशसंख्यासामान्यादन्नमेवदशाक्षरा विराड् विराडन्नम् इति हि श्रुतिः ।
units.english: thus there are Ten making up the Kṛtacast And because all this is so, therefore in all ten quarters, Agni and the rest and Vāyu and the rest are the food, because of the number Ten being the common factor As says the Śrutitext

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽन्नमेव दशसंख्यत्वात् । तत एव दश कृतं कृते ऽन्तर्भावाच्चतुरायत्वेनेत्यवोचाम ।
units.english: ‘The Virāṭ is tenlettered,Virāṭ is food,’ Hence all this is food, being ten in number Hence these ten are the Kṛtacast; because they are included in the Kṛtacast which in

units.sanskrit: सैषा विराड्दशसंख्या सत्यन्नं चान्नाद्यन्नादिनी च कृतत्वेन दशसंख्ययान्नं कृतसंख्ययान्नादी
units.english: This Virāṭbeing ten in numberis Food, and also the Eater of food, in the form of the Kṛtacast The number Ten is included in the Kṛtacast, hence it is Food, and also the Eater of food

units.sanskrit: तया अन्नान्नादिन्या इदं सर्वं जगद्दशदिक्संस्थं दृष्टं कृतसंख्याभूतयोपलब्धम् । एवंविदो ऽस्य सर्वं कृतसंख्याभूतस्य दशदिक्संबद्धं दृष्टमुपलब्धं भवति ।
units.english: By this,‘food and Eater of food’all thisuniverse situated in the ten quarters,becomes seen,ie perceived, by its forming the number of the Kṛtacast One who knows this, assumes the number of the Kṛtacast and as such comes to perceive all things connected with the ten quarters

units.sanskrit: किञ्चान्नादश्च भवति य एवं वेद यथोक्तदर्शी ।
units.english: Further, one who knows thisperceives what has been said above, and becomes an eater of food

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यास उपासनमाप्त्यर्थः ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य तृतीयः खण्डः
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the description of this particular form of meditation End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: सत्यकामो ह जाबालो जबालां मातरम् आमन्त्रयां चक्रे ।
units.english: It is said that Satyakāma Jābāla addressed his mother ‘Mother, wish to live the life of the Religious Student;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचर्यं भवति विवत्स्यामि किंगोत्रो न्व् अहम् अस्मीति ॥
units.english: of what family am ?’

units.sanskrit: सर्वं वागाद्यग्न्यादि चान्नान्नादत्वसंस्तुतं जगदेकीकृत्य षोडशधा प्रविभज्य तस्मिन्ब्रह्मदृष्टिर्विधातव्येत्यारभ्यते ।
units.english: Now begins the teaching that ‘all this universe in the form of speech and the rest, and Agni and the rest, which has been hitherto eulogised as Food and Foodeater, should be unified and divided into sixteen, parts and viewed as Brahman

units.sanskrit: श्रद्धातपसोर्ब्रह्मोपासनाङ्गत्वप्रदर्शनाया'ख्यायिका ।
units.english: The story has been introduced with a view to show that Faith and Austerity are necessary adjuncts of meditation on Brahman

units.sanskrit: सत्यकामो ह नामतो हशब्द ऐतिह्यार्थो जबालाया अपत्यं जाबालो जबलां स्वां मातरमामन्त्रयाञ्चक्र आमन्त्रितवान् । ब्रह्मचर्यं स्वाध्यायग्रहणाय हे भवति विवत्स्याम्याचार्यकुले,
units.english: Satyakāmaby name;the particle ‘ha’ is meant to indicate the fact of the story being correct;Jābālathe son of Jabālāaddressed his motherJabālāO, mother, wish to live the life of the Religious Student,in the family of a Teacher,for the purpose of acquiring the Vedic Lore;

units.sanskrit: किङ्गोत्रो ऽहं किमस्य मम गोत्रं सो ऽहं न्वहमस्मीति ॥
units.english: to which family do belongwhat is the name of the Ṛṣi to whose race belong?’

units.sanskrit: सा हैनम् उवाच । नाहम् एतद् वेद तात यद्गोत्रस् त्वम् असि ।
units.english: She said to him‘ do not know, my child’ of what family thou art;

units.sanskrit: बह्व् अहम् चरन्ती परिचारिणी यौवने त्वाम् अलभे ।
units.english: obtained thee when, in my youth, attended upon many people, devoted to their service;

units.sanskrit: साहम् एतन् न वेद यद्गोत्रस् त्वम् असि ।
units.english: so do not know of what family thou art;

units.sanskrit: जबाला तु नामाहम् अस्मि । सत्यकामो नाम त्वम् असि । स सत्यकाम एव जाबालो ब्रुवीथा इति ॥
units.english: but am Jabālā by name and thou art Satyakāma by name; so declare thyself as Satyakāma Jābālā’

units.sanskrit: एवं पृष्टा जबाला सा हैनं पुत्रमुवाचनाहमेतत्तव गोत्रं वेद हे तात यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि । कस्मान्न वेत्सीत्युक्ता'हबहु भर्तृगृहे परिचर्याजातमतिथ्यभ्यागतादि चरन्त्यहं परिचारिणी परिचरन्तीति परिचरणशीलैवाहं परिचरणचित्ततया गोत्रादिस्मरणे मम मनो नाभूत् । यौवने च तत्काले त्वामलभे लब्धवत्यस्मि ।
units.english: Being thus asked, Jabālā said to her son ‘ do not know the Ṛṣi to whose family you belong, O, my child’Being asked‘Why do you not know it’?She said‘In my husband’s house, had to attend upon many people who came as guests and strangers,as servantvery devoted to my duties of attendance on them, and being entirely taken up by such service, my mind never turned towards such information as regards the family to which thou belongest, which therefore do not remember;and it was at that time, in my youth that obtained thee;and soon after your father died;

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽनाथाहं साहमेतन्न वेद यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि ।
units.english: hence, having no protector left for myself, know not to which family thou belongest

units.sanskrit: जबाला तु नामाहमस्मि सत्यकामो नाम त्वमसि स त्वं सत्यकाम एवाहं जाबालो ऽस्मीत्याचार्याय ब्रुवीथाः यद्याचार्येण पृष्ट इत्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: But am Jabālā by name and thou art Satyakāma by name; so declare thyself to thy Teacheras Satyakāma Jābāla saying ‘ am Satyakāma Jābāla’;that is, if you are asked by the Teacher’

units.sanskrit: स ह हारिद्रुमतं गौतमम् एत्योवाच । ब्रह्मचर्यं भगवति वत्स्यामि । उपेयां भगवन्तम् इति ॥ तं होवाच किंगोत्रो नु सोम्यासीति । स होवाच ।
units.english: Having gone to GautamaHārīdrumata, he said to him‘Reverend Sir, wish to live as a Religious Student under you, and would approach you, reverend Sir’He said to him ‘Of what family art thou, my Boy?’He replied‘Sir, do not know of what family am;

units.sanskrit: अपृच्छं मातरम् । सा मा प्रत्यब्रवीद् बह्व् अहम् चरन्ती परिचरिणी यौवने त्वाम् अलभे ।
units.english: asked my mother and she said‘ obtained thee when, in my youth, attended upon many people, devoted to their service;

units.sanskrit: साहम् एतन् न वेद यद्गोत्रस् त्वम् असि ।
units.english: so do not know of what family thou art;

units.sanskrit: जबाला तु नामाहम् अस्मि । सत्यकामो नाम त्वम् असीति ।
units.english: but am Jabālā by name and thou art Satyakāma by name;’so, Sir, am SatyakāmaJābāla

units.sanskrit: स ह सत्यकामो हारिद्रुमतं हरिद्रुमतो ऽपत्यं हारिद्रुमतं गौतमं गोत्रत एत्य गत्वोवाच ब्रह्मचर्यं भगवति पूजावति त्वयि वत्स्याम्यत उपेयामुपगच्छेयं
units.english: He, SatyakāmaJābāla, having gone to Hārīdrumatathe son of HaridrumataGautama, being his family name, said to him‘Reverend Sir, wish to live as a Religious Student under you,and live with you, would approach you

units.sanskrit: शिष्यतया भगवन्तमित्युक्तवन्तं तं होवाच गौतमः । किङ्गोत्रो नु सोम्यासीति विज्ञातकुलगोत्रः शिष्य उपनेतव्य इति पृष्टः प्रत्याह सत्यकामः ।
units.english: When he said this, Gautama said to him‘Of what family art thou, my Boy?’as a disciple has to be admitted only when his family and race are fully known

units.sanskrit: स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद भो यद्गोत्रो ऽहमस्मि ।
units.english: Being thus asked, Satyakāma said‘Sir, do not know of what family am;

units.sanskrit: किं त्वपृच्छं पृष्टवानस्मि मातरम् ।
units.english: but asked my mother;

units.sanskrit: सा मया पृष्टा मां प्रत्यब्रवीन्माता । बह्वहं चरन्तीत्यादि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: and on being asked by me, my mother said to me‘In my youth, attended upon many people etc, etc,’as before
