units.sanskrit: तस्या अहं वचः स्मरामि सो ऽहं सत्यकामो जाबालो ऽस्मि भो इति ॥
units.english: remember her words; so, Sir, am SatyakāmaJābāla

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच । नैतद् अब्रह्मणो विवक्तुम् अर्हति ।
units.english: He said to him‘None but a Brāhmaṇa could thus speak out

units.sanskrit: उप त्वा नेष्ये न सत्याद् अगा इति ।
units.english: thou hast not flinched from the truth’

units.sanskrit: तम् उपनीय कृशानाम् अबलानां चतुःशता गा निराकृत्य उवाचेमाः सोम्यानुसंव्रजेति । ता अभिप्रस्थापयन्न् उवाच ।
units.english: Having initiated him he selected four hundred lean and weak cows and said to him‘Good boy, go with these’While taking them away, he said‘ would not return without a thousand’

units.sanskrit: नासहस्रेणावर्तेयेति । स ह वर्षगणं प्रोवास । ता यदा सहस्रं सम्पेदुः ॥
units.english: He dwelt away for a number of years, by which time the cows came to be a thousand

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच गौतमो नैतद्वचो ऽब्राह्मणो विशेषेण वक्तुमर्हत्यार्जवार्थसंयुक्तम् ।
units.english: Gautama said to him‘No one who is not a Brahmana could speak out so openly and straightforwardly;

units.sanskrit: ऋजवो हि ब्रह्मणा नेतरे स्वभावतः ।
units.english: It is Brāhmaṇas alone, not others, who are, by their very nature, straightforward

units.sanskrit: यस्मान्न सत्याद्ब्राह्मणजातिधर्मादगा नापेतवानसि । अतो ब्राह्मणं त्वामुपनेष्ये ऽतः संस्कारार्थं होमाय समिधं सोम्या'हरेत्युक्त्वा तमुपनीय
units.english: Since thou hast not flinched from the truthwhich is the rightful duty of the Brāhmaṇacaste, accept thee as a Brāhmaṇa and am going to initiate thee; hence for the purpose of the preparatory embellishment, fetch fuel, my Boy, for the firerites

units.sanskrit: कृशानामबलानां गोयूथान्निराकृत्यापकृष्य चतुःशता चत्वारि शतानि गवामुवाचेमा गाः
units.english: Having said this, he initiated him, and having selected out of his herd of cattlefour hundred lean and weak cows, said to him ‘My boy, go with these cows’

units.sanskrit: इत्युक्तस्ता अरण्यं प्रत्यभिप्रस्थापयन्नुवाचनासहस्रेणापूर्णेन सहस्रेण ना'वर्तेय न प्रत्यागच्छेयम् । स एवमुक्त्वा गा अरण्यं तृणोदकबहुलं द्वन्द्वंरहितं प्रवेश्य स ह वर्षगणं दीर्घं प्रोवास प्रोषितवान् ।
units.english: Being thus told, the Boy, while taking them away to the forest,said, ‘ would not return until a thousand cows are completed’ Having said this, he took the cows to the forest, where there was plenty of grass and water and no extremes dangersand dwelt away there for a number of years,ie for a long time;

units.sanskrit: ताः सम्यग्गावो रक्षिता यदा यस्मिन्काले सहस्रं संपेदुः संपन्ना बभूवुः ॥
units.english: till the cows, having been properly looked after, came to be one thousand,complete

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनम् ऋषभो ऽभ्युवाद सत्यकाम इति । भगव इति ह प्रतिशुश्राव । प्राप्ताः सोम्य सहस्रं स्मः ।
units.english: Then the Bull said to him‘Satyakāma’ He answered ‘Yes, sir’‘My Boy, we have reached a thousand;

units.sanskrit: प्रापय न आचार्यकुलम् ॥
units.english: carry us to the Teacher’s House’

units.sanskrit: तमेतं श्रद्धातपोभ्यां सिद्धं वायुदेवता दिक्संबन्धिनी तुष्टा सत्यृषभमनुप्रविश्यर्षभापन्नानुग्रहायाथ
units.english: When the Boy had become duly accomplished with faith and austerity, the deity Vāyu connected with the quarters became satisfied with him, and entering into the body of the Bull,ie having become a Bull for the purpose of helping the Boy

units.sanskrit: तमसौ सत्यकामो भगव इति ह प्रतिशुश्राव प्रतिवचनं ददौ ।
units.english: addressed him by name To him Satyakāma replied‘Yes, Sir’; this was the answer he gave

units.sanskrit: प्रप्ताः सोम्य सहस्रं स्मः पूर्णा तव प्रतिज्ञातः प्रापय नो ऽस्मानाचार्यकुलम् ॥
units.english: My Boy, we have reached a thousand,as you had promised now carry us to the teacher’s House’

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणश् च ते पादं ब्रवाणि इति ।
units.english: ‘ would declare to thee the foot of Brahman’

units.sanskrit: ब्रवीतु मे भगवान् इति ।
units.english: ‘Do tell it to me, revered sir’

units.sanskrit: प्राची दिक् कला । प्रतिची दिक् कला । दक्षिणा दिक् कला । उदीची दिक् कला ।
units.english: ‘The Eastern side is one factor, the Western side is one factor, the Southern side is one factor, the Northern side is one factor

units.sanskrit: एष वै सोम्य चतुष्कलः पादो ब्रह्मणः प्रकाशवान् नाम ॥
units.english: This, My Boy, is Brahman’s fourfactored food, named ‘The Luminous’

units.sanskrit: किञ्चाहं ब्रङ्मणः परस्य ते तुभ्यं पादं ब्रवाणि कथयानि ।
units.english: ‘Further, shall declare to theetell youthe foot of Brahman

units.sanskrit: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचब्रवीतु कथयतु मे मह्यं भगवान् । इत्युक्त ऋषभस्तस्मै सत्यकामाय होवाच । प्राची दिक्कला ब्रह्मणः पादस्य चतुर्थो भागः ।

units.sanskrit: श्रुतं ह्य् एव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्य आचार्याद् धैव विद्या विदिता साधिष्ठं प्रापतीति । तस्मै ह एतद् एव उवाच ।
units.english: ‘For have heard from persons like Your Reverence that it is only knowledge learnt from the Teacher that becomes the best’Thereupon the Teacher taught the same thing, and nothing was omittedyea nothing was omitted

units.sanskrit: किञ्च श्रुतं हि यस्मान्मम विद्यत एवास्मिन्नर्थे भगवत्समेभ्य ॠषिभ्यः । आचार्याद्धैव विद्या विदिता साधिष्ठं साधुतमत्वं प्रापदिति प्राप्नोतीत्यतो भगवानेब ब्रूयादित्युक्त आचार्यो ऽब्रवीत्तस्मै तामेव दैवतैरुक्तां विद्याम् ।
units.english: ‘Further, it has been heard by me, in this connection, from sages like Your Reverence, that it is only knowledge learnt from the Teacher that becomes best, acquires its highest character; hence Your Reverence alone should teach me’Being thus addressed, the Teacher expounded to him the same thing,the same Philosophythat had been taught by the deities Bull, Agni, Flamingo, Acquatic Bird;

units.sanskrit: अत्र ह न किञ्चन षोडशकलविद्यायाः किञ्चिदेकदेशमात्रमपि न वीयाय न विगतमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: and of that philosophy of the sixteen Factors, nothingnot the least part was omittedleft out The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the exposition of this particular philosophy

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यासो विद्यापरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य नवमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse With a view to expound the Philosophy of Brahman in another manner,the Text proceeds to expound the Agnividyā, the Science of the Fires, and to describe the man who knows it

units.sanskrit: उपकोसलो ह वै कामलायनः सत्यकामे जाबाले ब्रह्मचार्यम् उवास ।
units.english: Upakosala, the son of Kamala dwelt as a Religious Student with SatyakāmaJābāla

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह द्वादश वार्षान्य् अग्नीन् परिचचार ।
units.english: It is said that he tended his fires for twelve years

units.sanskrit: स ह स्मान्यान् अन्तेवासिनः समावर्तयंस् तं ह स्मैव न समावर्तयति ॥
units.english: But though the Teacher permitted the other disciples to ‘return’ Home, yet he did not permit Upakosala to ‘return’

units.sanskrit: आख्यायिका पूर्ववच्छ्रद्धातपसोर्ब्रह्मविद्यासाधनत्वप्रदश्रनार्थाउपकोसलो ह वै नामतः कमलस्यापत्यं कामलायनः सत्यकामे जाबाले
units.english: Upakosalaby namethe son of Kamala, dwelt as Religious Student, with SatyakāmaJābāla

units.sanskrit: हः एतिह्यार्थः ।
units.english: The phrase ‘Sa ha’ indicates that this has been said so by people

units.sanskrit: तस्या'चार्यस्य द्वादश वर्षाण्यग्नीन्परिचचाराग्नीनां परिचरणं कृतवान् ।
units.english: He tended histhe Teacher’sfires for twelve years;ie Performed his duties of attending on them

units.sanskrit: स ह स्मा'चार्यो ऽन्यान्ब्रह्मचारिणः स्वाध्यायं ग्राहयित्वा समावर्तयंस्तमेवोपकोसलमेकं न समावर्तयति स्म ह ॥
units.english: But while the Teacher permitted the other disciples to return Home,after having taught them the Veda,he did not permit Upakosala to return

units.sanskrit: तं जायोवाच तप्तो ब्रह्मचारी कुशलम् अग्नीन् परिचचारीत् ।
units.english: His wife said to him‘This Religious Student has performed his austerities, and has tended your fires very well;

units.sanskrit: मा त्वा अग्नयः परिप्रवोचन् । प्रब्रूह्य् अस्मा इति ।
units.english: so that the fires may not blame you, you should teach him’

units.sanskrit: तस्मै हाप्रोच्यैव प्रवासां चक्रे ॥
units.english: But he went away, without having taught him

units.sanskrit: तमाचार्यजायोवाच तप्तोब्रह्मचारी कुशलं सम्यगग्नीन्परिचचारीत्परिचरितवान् । भगवांश्चाग्निषु भक्तं न समावर्तयति ।
units.english: To the Teacher, his wife saidThis Religious Student has performed his austerities, and has tended the fires very well,attended upon them in the proper manner and yet you, sir, are not permitting him, who is so devoted to the fires, to return home complete his course;

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽस्मद्भक्तं न समावर्तयतीति ज्ञात्वा त्वामग्नयो मा परिप्रवोचन्गर्हां तव मा कुर्युः । अतः प्रब्रूह्यस्मै विद्यामिष्टामुपकोसलायेति ।
units.english: so that the fires may not blame you, that you are not completing the course for one so devoted to them,You should teach himthat is, impart to Upakosala the teaching that he desires’

units.sanskrit: तस्मा एवं जाययोक्तो ऽपि हाप्रोच्यैवानुक्त्वैव किञ्चित्प्रवासांचक्रे प्रवसितवान् ॥
units.english: But without having said anything to him,though so requested by his wife,the sage went away

units.sanskrit: स ह व्याधिना अनशितुं दध्रे ।
units.english: Through suffering he resolved not to eat

units.sanskrit: तम् आचार्यजाया उवाच ब्रह्मचारिन्न् अशान । किं नु न अश्नासि इति । स ह उवाच बहव इमे ऽस्मिन् पुरुषे कामा नानात्यायाः ।
units.english: The Teacher’s wife said to him‘O, Religious’ Student, do eat, why do you not eat?He saidThere are, in this person, many longings extending in several directions;

units.sanskrit: व्याधीभीः प्रतिपूर्णो ऽस्मि ।
units.english: am full of sufferings;

units.sanskrit: न अस्।इष्यामि इति ॥
units.english: shall not eat’

units.sanskrit: स होपकोसलो व्याधिना मानसेन दुःखेनानशितुमनशनं कर्तुं दध्रे धृतवान्मनः ।
units.english: HeUpakosalathrough sufferingsmental anguish,resolvedmade up his mindnot to eat,ie to keep fast

units.sanskrit: तं तूष्णीमग्न्यगारे ऽवस्थितमाचार्यजायोवाच हे ब्रह्मचारिन्नशान भुङ्क्ष्व किं नु कस्मान्नु कारणान्नाश्नासीति । स होवाच बहवो ऽनेके ऽस्मिन्पुरुषे ऽकृतार्थे प्राकृते कामा इच्छाः कर्तव्यं प्रति
units.english: When he was sitting quietly in the firehouse the Teacher’s wife said to him‘O, Religious Student, do eat,take your food;whyfor what reasondo you not eat?He said’ In this person,in myself, the common disappointed man,there are manynumerouslongings desiresregarding what shall be done;

units.sanskrit: नानात्ययो ऽतिगमनं येषां व्याधीनां कर्तव्यचिन्तानां ते नानात्यया व्याधयः कर्तव्यताप्राप्तिनिमित्तानि
units.english: and these extend in several directions;ie the extent of those longings and sorrows regarding what should be done goes out in several directions

units.sanskrit: चित्तदुःखानीत्यर्थः । तैः प्रतिपूर्णो ऽस्मि ।
units.english: am full of sufferingsthat is, of mental anguish due to the nonfulfilment of my duties;

units.sanskrit: अतो नाशिष्यामीति ॥
units.english: hence shall not eat’

units.sanskrit: तप्तो ब्रह्मचारी कुशलं नः पर्यचारीत् । हन्तास्मै प्रब्रवामेति तस्मै होचुः ।
units.english: Thereupon the Fires said among themselves‘This Religious Student has performed austerities and has tended us very well; well, let us teach him’

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ब्रह्म कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्मेति ॥
units.english: And they said to him‘Breath is Brahman, Ka is Brahman; Kha is Brahman’

units.sanskrit: उक्त्वा तूष्णींभूते ब्रह्मचारिण्यथ हाग्नयः शुश्रूषया'वर्जिताः कारुण्याविष्टाः सन्तस्रयो ऽपि समूदिरे संभूयोक्तवन्तः । हन्तेदानीमस्मै ब्रह्मचारिणे ऽस्मद्भक्ताय दुःखिताय तपस्विने श्रद्दधानाय सर्वे ऽनुशास्मो ऽनुप्रब्रवाम ब्रह्मविद्यामिति । एवं संप्रधार्य तस्मै होचुरुक्तवन्तः प्राणो ब्रह्म कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्मेति ॥ स होवाच ।
units.english: After having answered the Teacher’s wife, when the Religious Student resumed his silence, the three Fires,having been won over by his service, and roused by pitysaid among themselves‘Well, we should all teach this Religious Student, who is devoted to us and is suffering mental anguish, who has performed his penances and is endowed with full faith,the Philosophy of Brahman’Having thus made up their mind, they said to himBreath is Brahman, ‘Ka’ is Brahman, ‘Kha’ is Brahman

units.sanskrit: विजानाम्य् अहं यत् प्राणो ब्रह्म । कं च तु खं च न विजानामीति ।
units.english: He said‘ understand that Breath is Brahman but do not understand Ka and Kha’

units.sanskrit: यद् वाव कं तद् एव खम् । यद् एव खं तद् एव कम् इति ।
units.english: They said‘What is Ka is Kha, and what is Kha is Ka

units.sanskrit: प्राणं च हास्मै तद् आकाशं चोचुः ॥
units.english: Then they taught him the Breath and also its Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: स होवाच ब्रह्मचारी विजानाम्यहं यद्भवद्भिरुक्तं प्रसिद्धपदार्थकत्वात्प्राणो ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: Hethe Religious Studentsaid‘ understand what has been said by you regarding Breath being Brahman; as the meaning of this term is well known;

units.sanskrit: यस्मिन्सति जीवनं यदपगमे च न भवतीति तस्मिन्वायुविशेषे लोके रूढो ऽतो युक्तं ब्रह्मत्वं तस्य ।
units.english: the term ‘Breath’ Prāṇa is well known among people as standing for that particular form of Air during the presence whereof there is life, and on the cessation of which life disappears; and it is only right that this Breath should be regarded as Brahman

units.sanskrit: तेन प्रसिद्धपदार्थकत्वाद्विजानाम्यहं यत्प्राणो ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: Thus, the meaning of the terms being well known understand that Breath is Brahman;

units.sanskrit: कं च तु खं न विजानामीति ।
units.english: do not, however, understand ‘Ka and Kha’

units.sanskrit: ननु कङ्खंशब्दयोरपि सुखाकाशविषयत्वेन प्रसिद्धपदार्थकत्वमेव,
units.english: ObjectionThe terms Ka and Kha also are wellknown as denoting pleasure and Ākāśa respectively;

units.sanskrit: कस्माद्ब्रह्मचारिणो ऽज्ञानम्?
units.english: why then did the Student not understand them?

units.sanskrit: नृनं सुखस्य कंशब्दवाच्यस्य क्षणप्रध्वंसित्वात्खंशब्दवाच्यस्य चा'काशस्याचेतनस्य कथं ब्रह्मत्वमिति मन्यते ।
units.english: AnswerThe pleasure that is denoted by the term Ka is perishable in a moment; the Ākāśa also, which is denoted by the term Kha, is something inanimate; how then could these two be Brahman which is eternal and allconsciousness?This is what is in the Student’s mind;

units.sanskrit: कथं च भवतां वाक्यमप्रमाणं स्यादिति । अतो न विजानामीत्याह ।
units.english: also‘How too can your statement be wrong?’Hence, he says ‘ do not understand’

units.sanskrit: तमेवमुक्तन्तं ब्रह्मचारिणं ते हाग्नयः ऊचुः यद्वाव यदेव वयं कमवोचाम तदेव
units.english: When the Student had said this, the Fires said to himWhat we have spoken of as ‘Ka’ is what is ‘Kha’ ie Ākāśa;

units.sanskrit: खमाकाशमित्येवं खेन विशेष्यमाणं कं विषयेन्द्रिसंयोगजात्सुखान्निवर्तितं स्यान्नीलेनेव
units.english: so that qualified by this KhaĀkāśathe pleasure denoted by ‘Ka’becomes differentiated from the ordinary pleasure produced by the contact of the object with the senseorgans;

units.sanskrit: विशेष्यमाणमुत्पलं रक्तादिभ्यः ।
units.english: just as the Lotus qualified by the blue colour becomes differentiated from the Red and other lotuses

units.sanskrit: यदेव खमित्याकाशमवोचाम तदेव च कं सुखमिति जानीहि ।
units.english: Similarly, what we have spoken of as ‘Kha’Ākāśayou should know as ‘Ka’Happiness;

units.sanskrit: एवं च सुखेन विशेष्यमाणं खं भौतिकादचेतनात्खान्निवर्तितं स्यान्नीलोत्पलवदेव ।
units.english: so that being qualified by happiness, the KhaĀkāśabecomes differentiated from the purely physical Ākāśa which is insensate;

units.sanskrit: सुखमाकाशस्थं नेतरल्लौकिकम् । आकाशं च सुखाश्रयं नेतरद्भौतिकमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Thus what is meant is the Pleasure centred in Ākāśa, not the ordinary pleasure,and also the Ākāśa as the centre of happiness, not the physical Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: नन्वाकाशं चेत्सुखेन विशेषयितुमिष्टमस्त्वन्यतरदेव विशेषणं यद्वाव कं तदेव खमित्यतिरिक्तमितरत् ।
units.english: If it is desired to qualify Ākāśa by pleasure, let there beonly one of the two qualifying assertions;‘what is Ka is Kha’ is entirely superfluous;

units.sanskrit: यदेव खं तदेव कमिति पूर्वविशेषेणं वा ।
units.english: or it may be the other way about Both assertions are not needed

units.sanskrit: ननु सुखाकाशयोरुभयोरपि लौकिकसुखाकाशाभ्यां व्यावृत्तिरिष्टेत्यवोचाम । सुखेना'काशे विशेषिते व्यावृत्तिरुभयोरर्थप्राप्तैवेति चेत्सत्यमेवं किन्तु सुखेन
units.english: AnswerWe have already explained that what is meant to be done is to differentiate both Happiness and Ākāśa here said to be Brahman from the ordinary worldly Happiness and Ākāśa But when Ākāśa has been qualified and differentiated by Happiness, then by this also the differentiation of both becomes implied

units.sanskrit: विशेषितस्यैवा'काशस्य ध्येयत्वं विहितं न त्वाकाशगुणस्य विशेषणस्य सुखस्य ध्येयत्वं विहितं स्यात् ।
units.english: but what is prescribed here is that this Ākāśa as qualified by Happiness should be meditated upon as Brahman,and not the meditation of Happiness as the differentiating quality of Ākāśa;

units.sanskrit: विशेषणोपादानस्य विशेष्यनियन्तृत्वेनैवोपक्षयात् ।
units.english: because the only purpose served by the mention of the qualification is to restrict the scope of what it qualifies

units.sanskrit: अतः खेन सुखमपि विशेष्यते ध्येयत्वाय ।
units.english: Thus Happiness also is qualified by KhaĀkāśaas something to be meditated upon as Brahman

units.sanskrit: कुतश्चैतन्निश्चीयते ।
units.english: How do you get at this conclusion?

units.sanskrit: कंशब्दस्यापि ब्रह्मशब्दसम्बन्धात्कं ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: This follows from the connection of the term ‘Ka’ with the term ‘Brahman’,in the text ‘Ka is Brahman

units.sanskrit: यदि हि सुखगुणविशिष्टस्य खस्य ध्येयत्वं विवक्षितं स्यात्कं खं ब्रह्मेति ब्रूयुरग्नयः प्रथमम् ।
units.english: In fact, if what the fires intended to convey were the idea that Kha qualified by Happiness should be meditated upon; then they would, at the very first, have declared that ‘KaKha is Brahman’;

units.sanskrit: न चैवमुक्तवन्तः । किं तर्हि कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: and yet this is not what they did declare, what they did declare was that ‘Ka is Brahman, and Kha is Brahman’;

units.sanskrit: अतो ब्रह्मचारिणो मोहापनयनाय कङ्खंशब्दयोरितरेतरविशेषणविशेष्यत्व निर्देशो युक्त एव यद्वाव कमित्यादिः ।
units.english: consequently, for removing the confusion in the mind of the Student, it was only right to declare that Ka Happiness and Kha Ākāśa stand to each other in the mutual relation of the qualifier and the qualified,each, in turn, qualified by the other;

units.sanskrit: तदेतदग्निभिरुक्तं वाक्यार्थमस्मद्बोधाय श्रुतिराहप्राणं च हास्मै ब्रह्मचारिणे ।
units.english: The Text now declares, for our benefit, what the fires taught to the Religious StudentThey taught himthe Religious Student,Breath Prāṇa and its Ākāśa,ie the Ākāśa of Prāṇa;

units.sanskrit: तस्या'काशस्तदाकाशः । प्राणस्य सम्बन्ध्याश्रयत्वेन हार्द आकाश इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: ie, the Ākāśa space within the Heart, which is related to Prāṇa as its substratum

units.sanskrit: सुखगुणवत्त्वनिर्देशात्तं चा'काशं सुखगुणविशिष्टं ब्रह्म तत्स्थं च प्राणं ब्रह्मसम्पर्कादेव ब्रह्मेत्युभयं प्राणं चा'काशं च समुच्चित्य ब्रह्मणी ऊचुरग्नय इति ॥
units.english: What the fires taught were the two Brahmans conjointly,the first, Brahman in the form of Ākāśa qualified by Happinessthis was taught by declaring happiness to be a qualification of Ākāśa,and the second, Brahman in the shape of Prāṇa, located in the Ākāśa and hence connected with Brahman,

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य दशमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनं गार्हपत्यो ऽनुशशास पृथिव्य् अग्निर् अन्नम् आदित्य इति ।
units.english: Then the Gārhapatya Fire instructed him‘Earth, Fire, Food and Sun

units.sanskrit: य एष आदित्ये पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहम् अस्मि स एव अहम् अस्मि इति ॥
units.english: The person that is seen in the Sunthat am, that indeed am ’

units.sanskrit: सम्भूयाग्नयो ब्रह्मचारिणे ब्रह्मोक्तवन्तः ।
units.english: Jointly, the three fires taught the Religious Student as above

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरं प्रत्येकं स्वस्वविषयां विद्यां वक्तुमारेभिरे ।
units.english: Now, then, each of them proceeded to instruct him regarding the philosophy pertaining to itself

units.sanskrit: तत्रा'दावेनं ब्रह्मचारिणं गार्हपत्यो ऽग्निरनुशशास ।
units.english: So, first of all, the Gārhapatya Fire instructed him, the Religious Student;

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्यग्निरन्नमादित्य इति ममैताश्चस्रस्तनवः ।
units.english: ‘Earth, Fire, Food and Sun,these are my four bodies forms

units.sanskrit: तत्र य आदित्य एष पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहमस्मि गार्हपत्यो ऽग्निर्यश्च गार्हपत्यो ऽग्निः स एवाहमादित्यो पुरुषो ऽस्मीति ।
units.english: Of these, the Person that is seen in the Sun,that am, ie the Gārhapatya fire; and that which is the Gārhapatya fire, that indeed am , the person in the Sun’

units.sanskrit: पुनः परावृत्त्या स एवाहमस्मीति वचनम् ।
units.english: There is reiteration of the same in the assertion ‘that indeed am ’

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्यन्नयोरिव भोज्यत्वलक्षणयोः सम्बन्धो न गार्हपत्यादित्ययोः ।
units.english: The relationship between the Gārhapatya Fire and the Sun is not like that between the Fire and the Earth and Food, which latter are in the nature of something to be eaten, enjoyed;

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्यन्नयोस्तु भोज्यत्वेना'भ्यां सम्बन्धः ॥
units.english: that is why there is absolute identity between these two as asserted in the Text’ As for Earth and Food, these are related to the Fire as objects of enjoyment

units.sanskrit: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते । अपहते पापकृत्याम् । लोकी भवति । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति ।
units.english: ‘One who knowing this thus, meditates upon it, destroys sin, wins regions for himself, reaches the full lifespan, lives gloriously, and his descendants never perish

units.sanskrit: उप वयं तं भुञ्जामो ऽस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
units.english: We protect him in this world, and in the other,whosoever knowing this thus meditates upon it’

units.sanskrit: य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते ॥ स यः कश्चिदेवं यथोक्तं गार्हपत्यमग्निमन्नान्नादत्वेन चतुर्धा प्रविभक्तमुपास्ते सो ऽपहते विनाशयति पापकृत्यां पापं
units.english: Any one who knows thisthe abovedescribed Gārhapatya fire as food and foodeater, divided into forms, and meditates upon it,he destroyseradicates sinevil deeds;wins regions for himself, ie, wins the regions of fire, like ourselves;reaches the full lifespanof a hundred years,lives gloriously,that is, does not remain insignificant;

units.sanskrit: न चास्यावराश्च ते पुरुषाश्चास्य विदुषः सन्ततिजा इत्यर्थः । न क्षीयन्ते सन्तत्युच्छेदो न भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: his discendants,that is, persons descended from him, in his line of descent,never perish; that his line never ceases

units.sanskrit: किं च तं वयमुपभुञ्जामः पालयामो ऽस्मिंश्च लोके जीवन्तममुष्मिंश्च परलोके । य एतमेवं विद्वानुपास्ते यथेक्तं तस्यैतत्फलमित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: Further, we protect himwhile he is livingin this world and also in the otherthe other region,him whosoever knowing this, meditates upon what has been described above;to him accrues all this reward

units.sanskrit: अथ ह एनम् अन्वाहार्यपचनो ऽनुशशास आपो दिशो नक्षत्राणि चन्द्रमा इति ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse Then the Anvāhāryapacana Fire instructed him‘Water, Quarters, Stars and Moon

units.sanskrit: य एष चन्द्रमसि पुरुषो दृष्यते सो ऽहम् अस्मि स एव अहम् अस्मि इति ॥
units.english: The person that is seen in the Moon,that am,that indeed am ’

units.sanskrit: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते । अपहते पापकृत्याम् । लोकी भवति । सर्वम् आयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति ।
units.english: ‘One who knowing this thus, meditates upon it, destroys sin, wins regions for himself, reaches the full lifespan, lives gloriously and his descendants never perish

units.sanskrit: उप वयं तं भुञ्जामो ऽस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च । य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते ॥
units.english: We protect him in this world, and also in the other, whosoever knowing this thus meditates upon it’

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनमन्वाहार्यपचनो ऽनुशशास दक्षिणाग्निरापो दिशो नक्षत्राणि
units.english: Next, the Anvāhāryapacana Fire ie, the Dakṣiṇāgniinstructed himWater, Quarters, Stars and Moon;

units.sanskrit: चन्द्रमा इत्येता मम चतस्रस्तनवश्चतुर्धाहमन्वाहार्यपचन आत्मानं प्रविभज्यावस्थितः
units.english: these are my four bodies forms,, Anvāhāryapacana stand thus divided into four forms

units.sanskrit: तत्र य एष चन्द्रमसि पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहमस्मि स एवाहमस्मीति पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: Of these, the person that is seen in the Moonthat am etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: अन्नसम्बन्धाज्ज्योतिष्ट्वसामान्याच्चान्वाहार्यपचनचन्द्रमसोरेकत्वन्दक्षिणा(ण) दिक्सम्बन्धाच्च ।
units.english: The Anvāhāryapacana Fire and the Moon are identified on the ground of their being connected with food, of both being luminous, and also because of their connection with the Southern Quarter

units.sanskrit: अपां नक्षत्राणां च पूर्ववदन्नत्वेनैव सम्बन्धः ।
units.english: As regards Water and Stars, these are related, as before, only as food;

units.sanskrit: नक्षत्राणां चन्द्रमसो भोग्यत्वप्रसिद्धेः ।
units.english: it being wellknown that the stars are objects of enjoyment for the Moon

units.sanskrit: अपान्नोत्पादकत्वादन्नत्वं दक्षिणाग्नेः पृथिवीवद्गार्हपत्यस्य ।
units.english: As regards Water, it is productive of Food, and hence regarded as food for the Dakṣiṇagni,just as Earth is regarded as food for the Gārhapatya fire

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनम् आहवनीयो ऽनुशशास प्राण आकाशो द्यौर् विद्युद् इति ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse Now, the Āhavanīya Fire instructed him‘Breath’ Ākāśa, Heaven and Lightning

units.sanskrit: य एष विद्युति पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहम् अस्मि स एवाहम् अस्मीति ॥
units.english: This person that is seen in Lightningthat am,indeed that am

units.sanskrit: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते । अपहते पापकृत्याम् । लोकी भवति । सर्वम् अयुर् एति । ज्योग् जीवति ।
units.english: ‘One who knowing this thus meditates upon it, destroys sin, wins regions for himself, reaches the full lifespan, lives gloriously and his descendants never perishWe protect him in this world, and also in the other,whosoever knowing this thus, meditates upon it’

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनमाहवनीयो ऽनुशशास प्राण आकाशो द्यौर्विद्युदिति ममाप्येताश्चतस्रस्तनवः ।
units.english: Now, the Āhavanīya Fire instructed himBreath, Ākāśa, Heaven and Lightningthese are my four bodies forms

units.sanskrit: य एव विद्युति पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहमस्मीत्यादि पूर्ववत्सामान्यात् ।
units.english: This person that is seen in lightningthat am etc, etc,as before; on he ground of common characterstics

units.sanskrit: दिवा(द्य्वा) काशयोस्त्वाश्रयत्वाद्विद्युदाहवनीययोर्भोग्यत्वेनैव सम्बन्धः ।
units.english: As for Heaven and Ākāśa, these are related to Lightning and the Āhavanīya Fire, as the ‘food’ of these two respectively

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य त्रयोदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: ते होचुः । उपकोसलैषा सोम्य ते ऽस्मद्विद्यात्मविद्या च ।
units.english: They said‘O, Upakosala, dear Boy, thus has been expounded to thee our philosophy, and also the philosophy of the Self;

units.sanskrit: आचार्यस् तु ते गतिं वक्तेति ।
units.english: the Teacher will expound to thee the process’His Teacher came;

units.sanskrit: तम् आचार्यो ऽभ्युवादोपकोसल इति ॥
units.english: he said to him‘O Upakosala

units.sanskrit: ते पुनः सम्भूयोचुर्हेपकोसलैषा सोम्य ते तवास्मद्विद्याग्निविद्येत्यर्थः । आत्मविद्या पूर्वोक्ता प्राणो ब्रह्म कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्मेति च । आचार्यस्तु ते गतिं वक्ता विद्याफलप्राप्तय इत्युक्त्वोपरेमुरग्नयः ।
units.english: The Fires now again addressed him conjointly ‘O, Upakosala, dear boy, thus has been expounded to thee our philosophy,the Agnividyā, Philosophy of the Fires, as also the Philosophy of the Self,under the Texts‘Breath is Brahman, Ka is Brahman, Kha is Brahman’ The Teacher will expound to thee the process,for the acquiring of the final reward of knowledge’ Having said thus, the Fires retired

units.sanskrit: आजगाम हास्या'चार्यः कालेन ।
units.english: The Teacher came, in due time;

units.sanskrit: तं च शिष्यमाचार्यो ऽभ्युवादोपकोसल इति ॥
units.english: the Teacher said to him,his disciple‘O Upakosala’

units.sanskrit: भगव इति ह प्रतिशुश्राव । ब्रह्मविद इव सोम्य मुखं भाति ।
units.english: He answered‘Yes, Sir’‘My Boy, thy face shines like that of one who knows Brahman

units.sanskrit: को नु त्वानुशशासेति । को नु मानुशिश्याद् भो इतीहापेव निह्नुते । इमे नूनम् ईदृशा अन्यादृशा इतीहाग्नीन् अभ्यूदे । किं नु सोम्य किल ते ऽवोचन्न् इति ॥
units.english: Who has taught thee?’‘Who should teach me, Sir?’, and as if concealing the fact, he added, pointing to the Fires,‘Verily, beings like these, unlike these’‘What did they tell thee, my boy?’

units.sanskrit: इदम् इति ह प्रतिजज्ञे ।
units.english: He replied‘This

units.sanskrit: लोकान् वाव किल सोम्य ते ऽवोचन् ।
units.english: ‘My Boy, they have only expounded the Regions;

units.sanskrit: अहं तु ते तद् वक्ष्यामि यथा पुष्करपलाश आपो न श्लिष्यन्त एवम् एवंविदि पापं कर्म न श्लिष्यत इति ।
units.english: am going to expound to thee that to the knower of which evil does not cling, just as no water clings to the lotusleaf’He said‘Please, Sir, do tell me’,then he expounded it to him

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मविद इव सोम्य ते मुखं प्रसन्नं भाति को नु त्वानुशशासेत्युक्तः प्रत्याह ।
units.english: He answered‘Yes, Sir,’‘My Boy, thy face shinesis happy and brightlike that of one who knows Brahman;

units.sanskrit: को नु मानुशिष्यादनुशासनं कुर्याद्भो भगवंस्त्वयि प्रोषित इतीहापेव निह्नुते ऽपनिह्नुत इवेति व्यवहितेन सम्बन्धो न चापनिह्नुते न च यतावदग्निभिरुक्तं
units.english: who has taught thee?’Thus questioned, he said‘Who should teach me, Sir,impart instruction to me, when you had gone away?’and as if concealing the fact,and yet not actually concealing it‘iva’ being construed after ‘nihnuta’;that is, he was not concealing the facts, and yet not telling him that he had been taught by the Fires;

units.sanskrit: कथमिमे ऽग्नयो मया परिचरिता उक्तवन्तो नूनं यतस्त्वां दृष्ट्वा वेपमाना इवेदृशा दृश्यन्ते पूर्वमन्यादृशाः सन्त इतीहाग्नीनभ्यूदे ऽभ्युक्तवान्काक्वाग्नीन्दर्शयन्
units.english: his meaning being ‘How could these Fires tended by me have taught me, when, in your presence, they appear like these to be trembling,and yet before this, they were unlike these’;he said thispointing to the fires, by gestures

units.sanskrit: किं नु सोम्य किल ते तुभ्यमवोचन्नग्नय इति पृष्ट इत्येवमिदमुक्तवन्त इत्येवं ह प्रतिजज्ञे प्रतिज्ञातवान्प्रतीकमात्रं किञ्चिन्न सर्वं यथोक्तमग्निभिरुक्तमवोचत्
units.english: ‘What did theythe firestell thee, my Boy?, Being thus questioned, he answered‘Thisis what they told me;’that is, he told the Teacher only the opening words and not all that the Fires had told him

units.sanskrit: यत आहा'चार्यो लोकान्वाव पृथिव्यादीन्हे सोम्य किल ते ऽवोचन्न ब्रह्म साकल्येन ।
units.english: That this was so is clear from what the Teacher said‘My Boy, they have expounded only the Regions Earth and the Rest,and not Brahman as a whole

units.sanskrit: अहं तु ते तुभ्यं तद्ब्रह्म यदिच्छसि त्वं श्रोतुं वक्ष्यामि,
units.english: But am going to expound to thee that which thou wishest to hear;

units.sanskrit: शृणु तस्य मयोच्यमानस्य ब्रह्मणो ज्ञानमाहात्म्यं यथा पुष्करपलाशे पद्मपत्र आपो न शिलष्यन्त एवं यता वक्ष्यामि ब्रह्मैवंविदि पापं कर्म न शिलष्यते न सम्बध्यत
units.english: and listen to the high quality of the knowledge of Brahman that am going to expoundJust as no water clings to the lotusleaf,so no evilsinful actclings tocontaminatesthe man who knows the Brahman that am expounding’

units.sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्तवत्याचार्य आहोपकोसलो ब्रवीतु मे भगवानिति तस्मै होवाचा'चार्यः ॥
units.english: When the Teacher had said this, Upakosola said‘Please, Sir, do tell me’ Then the Teacher expounded it to him

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य चतुर्दशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: य एषो ऽक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यत एष आत्मेति होवाच । एतद् अमृतम् अभयम् एतद् ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: ‘This person that is seen in the eye,that is the Self’he said;‘This is the Immortal, the Fearless,this is Brahman

units.sanskrit: तद् यद्य् अप्य् अस्मिन् सर्पिर् वोदकं वा सिञ्चति वर्त्मनी एव गच्छति ॥
units.english: Hence, if one drops butter or water into this Eye, it flows away along the lashes’

units.sanskrit: य एषो ऽक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यते निवृत्तचक्षुर्भिर्ब्रह्मचर्यादिसाधनसम्पन्नैः शान्तैर्विवेकिभिर्दृष्टेर्द्रष्टाचक्षुषश्चक्षुःइत्यादिश्रुत्यन्तरात्
units.english: This person that is seen in the Eye,by persons who have closed their eyes, who are equipped with celibacy and other accessories, and who are calm and collected and endowed with discriminative wisdom;this idea of the person in the eye is based upon the Text ‘He is the Eye of the Eye’ Kena

units.sanskrit: नन्वग्निभिरुक्तं वितथं यत आचार्यस्तु ते गतिं वक्तेति गतिमात्रस्य वक्तेत्यवोचन्भविष्यद्विषयापरिज्ञानं चाग्नीनम् ।
units.english: ObjectionWhat had been said by the Fires turns out to be false they had said the ‘Teacher will expound to thee the Process’; which meant that he was going to expound the Process only;

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not affect the case

units.sanskrit: सुखाकाशस्यैवाक्षिणि दृश्यत इति द्रष्टुरनुवादात् ।
units.english: The statement ‘the person seen in the Eye’ is a reference to the same HappinessĀkāśa which has been expounded by the Fires above, as KaKha

units.sanskrit: एष आत्मा प्राणिनामिति होवाचैवमुक्तवानेतद्यदेवा'त्मतत्त्वमवोचाम । एतदमृतममरणधर्म्यविनाश्यत एवाभयं यस्य हि विनाशाशङ्का तस्य भयोपपत्तिस्तदभावादभयमत एवैतद्ब्रह्म बृहदनन्तमिति ।
units.english: ‘That is the Self,of all living beings’;this is what he said‘this is the truth about the self which spoke ofThis is the Immortal, never subject to death, imperishable,and hence, fearless;it is only one who suspects danger to himself that can have fear; and hence where there is no suspicion of any danger, it is fearless;and hence, it is Brahmanthe Great, the Infinite

units.sanskrit: किञ्चास्य ब्रह्मणो ऽक्षिपुरुषस्य माहात्म्यं तत्तत्र पुरुषस्य स्थाने ऽक्षिणि यद्यप्यस्मिन्यर्पिर्वोदकं
units.english: Question What is the greatness of this Brahman, this Person in the Eye?

units.sanskrit: वा सिञ्चति वर्त्मनी एव गच्छति पक्ष्मावेव गच्छति न चक्षुषा सम्बन्ध्यते पद्मपत्रेणेवोदकम् ।
units.english: It is this If one drops Butter or Water into the Eye, which is the abode of that person, it flows away along the lashes, and does not affect the eye; just as the water does not affect the lotusleaf

units.sanskrit: स्थानस्याप्येतन्माहात्म्यं किं पुनः स्थानिनो ऽक्षिपुरुषस्य निरञ्जनत्वं वक्तव्यमित्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: What is meant is that, when such is the greatness of the abode, what can be said of the Person abiding there, the person in the eye, who remains ever uncontaminated?

units.sanskrit: एतं संयद्वाम इत्य् आचक्षते । एतं हि सर्वाणि वामान्य् अभिसंयन्ति ।
units.english: This they call ‘the Centre of Blessings’, as all blessings converge in This

units.sanskrit: सर्वाण्य् एनं वामान्य् अभिसंयन्ति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: All blessings converge in one who knows this

units.sanskrit: एतं यथोक्तं पुरुषं संयद्वाम इत्याचक्षते । कस्मात् । यस्मादेतं सर्वाणि वामानि वननीयानि संभजनीयानि शोभनान्यभिसंयन्त्यभिसङ्गच्छन्तीत्यतः संयद्वामः ।
units.english: Thisthe said Person in the Eye, they call ‘the Centre of Blessings’;Why?Because all blessings all desirable things, all that people want, all good thingsconverge in this,meet here; hence this is the centre of Blessings

units.sanskrit: तथैवंविदमेनं सर्वाणि वामान्यभिसंयन्ति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows this,in him also converge all blessings

units.sanskrit: एष उ एव वामनीः ।
units.english: This is also the ‘Vehicle of Blessings’;

units.sanskrit: एष हि सर्वाणि वामानि नयति । सर्वाणि वामानि नयति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: because this carries all blessings He carries all blessings who knows this This is also the Vehicle of Blessings;

units.sanskrit: एष उ एव वामनीर्यस्मादेष हि सर्वाणि वामानि पुण्यकर्मफलानि पुण्यानुरूपं प्राणिभ्यो नयति प्रापयति वहति चा'त्मधर्मत्वेन
units.english: because this carriesbrings, presents, lays beforeliving beingsall blessingsthe results of their righteous deeds, in due accordance with their piety,in the shape of Dharma, merit pertaining to the Self

units.sanskrit: विदुषः फलंसर्वाणि वामानि नयति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: The reward to one who knows this is that he carries all blessings, who knows this

units.sanskrit: एष हि सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति ।
units.english: This is also ‘The vehicle of Light’, as this shines in all regions

units.sanskrit: सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति य एवं वेद ॥
units.english: One who knows this shines in all regions

units.sanskrit: एष उ एव भामनीरेष हि यस्मात्सर्वेषु लोकेष्वादित्यचन्द्राग्न्यादिरूपैर्भाति दीप्यते ।
units.english: This is also ‘The Vehicle of Light because in all regions, this is what shines,in the form of the Sun, the Moon, the Fire and so forth;

units.sanskrit: तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभातिइति श्रुतेरतो भामानि नयतीति भामनीः । य एवं वेदासावपि सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति ॥
units.english: as declared in the Vedic Text‘By His light, all this shines’ Katha and because he thus carries luminosity to all things, He is The ‘Vehicle of Light’One who knows this, also shines in all regions

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् उ चैवास्मिञ् छव्यं कुर्वन्ति यदि च नार्चिषम् एवाभिसंभवन्ति ।
units.english: Now, for such a person, whether they perform his obsequies or not, they go to Light;

units.sanskrit: अर्चिषो ऽहः ।
units.english: from Light, to the Day;

units.sanskrit: अह्न आपूर्यमाणपक्षम् ।
units.english: from the Day, to the Bright Fortnight;

units.sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणपक्षाद् यान् षड् उदङ्ङ् एति मासांस् तान् ।
units.english: from the Bright Fortnight, to those six months during which the Sun rises Northward;

units.sanskrit: मासेभ्यः संवत्सरम् ।
units.english: from the Months to the Year;

units.sanskrit: संवत्सराद् आदित्यम् । आदित्याच् चन्द्रमसम् । चन्द्रमसो विद्युतम् ।
units.english: from the Year, to the Sun; from the Sun to the Moon, from the Moon to the Lightning;

units.sanskrit: तत् पुरुषो ऽमानवः ।
units.english: there is a Person, who is not human

units.sanskrit: स एनान् ब्रह्म गमयति ।
units.english: He carries these to Brahman

units.sanskrit: एष देवपथो ब्रह्मपथः ।
units.english: This is the divine path, the path to Brahman

units.sanskrit: एतेन प्रतिपद्यमाना इमं मानवम् आवर्तं नावर्तन्ते नावर्तन्ते ॥
units.english: Betaking themselves to this Path, they do not return to this whirl of HumanityYea, they do not return

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीं यथोक्तब्रह्मविदो गतिरुच्यते ।
units.english: Now the Process, Progress or Path of the man who knows the abovementioned Brahman is described

units.sanskrit: यद्यदि उ चैवास्मिन्नेवंविदि शव्यं शवकर्म मृते कुर्वन्ति यदि च न कुर्वन्ति ऋत्विजः सर्वथाप्येवंवित्तेन शवकर्मणाकृतेनापि प्रतिबद्धो न ब्रह्मद्मटप्राप्नोति ।
units.english: For such a personone who knows what has gone above,whether theythe priests,performhis obsequieson his death,or they do not perform them, in any case, the knowing man is not prevented by the nonperformance of his obsequies from reaching Brahman;

units.sanskrit: न च कृतेन शवकर्मणास्य कश्चनाभ्यधिको लोकः ।
units.english: nor does the performance of the obsequies carry him to any superior region;

units.sanskrit: न कर्मणा वर्धते नो कनीयानिति श्रुत्यन्तरात् ।
units.english: nor does he become smaller by the performance of rites’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: शवकर्मण्यनादरं दर्शयन्विद्यां स्तौति न पुनः शवकर्मैवंविदो न कर्तव्यमिति ।
units.english: By thus showing indifference towards the obsequious rites, the text only means to eulogise the philosophy; and it is not meant that for the knowing man, the obsequies should not be performed

units.sanskrit: अक्रियमाणे हि शवकर्मणि कर्मणा फलारम्भे प्रतिबन्धः कश्चिदनुमीयते ऽन्यत्र ।
units.english: Because, in the event of the obsequies not being performed, it might be inferred that elsewhere in the other world there might be an obstacle in the proper fruition of the acts done by the dead person;

units.sanskrit: यत इह विद्याफलारम्भकाले शवकर्म स्याद्वा न वेति विद्यावतो ऽप्रतिबन्धेन फलारम्भं दर्शयति ।
units.english: because in the present context bearing upon the fruition of the result of knowledge, it is particularly mentioned that ‘whether the obsequies are performed or not, the rewards of the knowledge accrues to the man without any obstruction’ which shows that this is so in this particular case, but it may not be so in the case of other acts

units.sanskrit: ये सुखाकाशमक्षिस्थं संयद्वामो वामनीर्भामनीरित्येवङ्गुणमुपासते प्राणसहितामग्निविद्यां च तेषामन्यत्कर्म भवतु मा वा भूत्सर्वथापि ते ऽर्चिषमेवाभिसम्भवन्त्यर्चिरभिमानिनीं
units.english: Thus then the upshot of the present context is thatthose persons who meditate upon the HappinessĀkāśa, the Person in the Eye, as being the ‘centre of blessings’, ‘the vehicle of blessings’ and the ‘vehicle of light’,and also upon the philosophy of the fires along with Breath,for such persons,whether other acts ate done, or not done,in any case, they go to light;

units.sanskrit: देवतामभिसम्भवन्ति प्रतिपद्यन्त इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, they become absorbed inreachthe deity ensouling the light

units.sanskrit: अर्चिषो ऽर्चिर्देवताया अहरहरभिमानिनीं देवतामह्न आपूर्यमाणपक्षं शुक्लपक्षदेवतामापूर्यमाणपक्षाद्यान्षण्मासानुदङ्ङुत्तरां दिशमेति सविता तान्मासानुत्तरायणदेवतां तेभ्यो मासेभ्यः संवत्सरं संवत्सरदेवतां ततः संवत्सरादादिदित्यमादित्याच्चन्द्रमसं चन्द्रमसो विद्युतं तत्तत्रस्थांस्तान्पुरुषः
units.english: From Lightie from the deity ensouling the Light they go to the Dayie to the deity ensouling the Day;from the Day to the Bright Fortnight,ie the Deity ensouling the Brighter Half of the month from the Bright Fortnight to those months during which the Sun rises northwards,ie the Deity of the Northern Solstice; from the Months, to the Year,to the Deity of the Year,from the Year, to the Sun;from the Sun to the Moonfrom the Moon to the Lightning,When they reach there,a certain Person comes from Brahman’s Regions,who is not humanone who does not form part of the human creation;

units.sanskrit: कश्चिद्ब्रह्मलोकादेत्यामानवो मानव्यां सृष्टौ भवो मानवो न मानवो ऽमानवः स पुरुष एनान्ब्रह्म सत्यलोकस्थं गमयति गन्तृगन्तव्यगमयितृत्वव्यपदेशेभ्यः ।
units.english: That such is the meaning that the men are carried to the Brahman resident in Satyaloka, and not to the One undifferentiated Brahman is clear from the fact that the Text speaks of the person who goes, the person gone to the Brahman and the person who carries them Any such assertion would be incompatible with the reaching of that supreme Brahman who is pure Being;

units.sanskrit: सन्मात्रब्रह्मप्राप्तौ तदनुपपत्तेः । ब्रह्मैव सन्ब्रह्माप्येतीति हि तत्र वक्तुं न्याय्यम् । सर्वभेदनिरासेन सन्मात्रप्रतिपत्तिं वक्ष्यति ।
units.english: as in reference to this latter, the only assertion that could be true would be that ‘Being Brahman, one becomes absorbed in Brahman Because the Text itself is going to declare that, where all diversity is eschewed, one reaches the pure Being

units.sanskrit: न चादृष्टो मार्गो ऽगमनायोपतिष्ठते ।
units.english: And so long as this Path of pure Being has not been perceived, it cannot serve to prevent the going ie passing on and on, of the person

units.sanskrit: स एनमविदितो न भुनक्तिइति श्रुत्यन्तरात् ।
units.english: As says another Vedic Text‘Until it is known, it does not affect him’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: एष देवपथः देवैरर्चिरादिभिः गमयितृत्वेनाधिकृतैः उपलक्षितः पन्था देवपथ उच्यते ।
units.english: This is the Divine Path;the Path characterised by the Deities whose business it is to carry the persons through the Path of Light and the rest, is called the Divine Path

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्म गन्तव्यं तेन चोपलक्षित इति ब्रह्मपथः ।
units.english: It is also called the Path to Brahman, because it is characterised by Brahman as the goal to be reached

units.sanskrit: एतेन प्रतिपद्यमाना गच्छन्तो ब्रह्मेमं मानवं मनुसम्बन्धिनं मनोः सृष्टिलक्षणमावत ना'वर्तन्त आवर्तन्ते ऽस्मिञ्जननमरणप्रबन्धचक्रारूढा घटीयन्त्रवत्पुनः पुनरित्यार्वतस्तं न प्रतिपद्यन्ते ।
units.english: Those who betake themselves togo forward by this Path and reach Brahman, do not return to this whirl of Humanity,ie that connected with the creation set up by Manu;this is called a ‘whirl’ in the sense that it whirls round and round, revolving like the waterwhorl, tied down to the continuous series of Births and Deaths; and the persons in question do not return to this Whirl

units.sanskrit: नावर्तन्ते ना'वर्तन्ते इति द्विरुक्तिः सफलाया विद्यायाः परिसमाप्तिप्रदर्शनार्था ॥
units.english: The repetition of the phrase ‘they do not return’ is meant to indicate the end of the philosophy which brings the said reward

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य पञ्चदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse The next section is introduced now, for the following reasons

units.sanskrit: एष ह वै यज्ञो यो ऽयं पवते ।
units.english: Verily, that which blows is the Sacrifice;

units.sanskrit: एष ह यन्न् इदं सर्वं पुनाति ।
units.english: for he, moving along, purifies all this

units.sanskrit: यद् एष यन्न् इदं सर्वं पुनाति । तस्माद् एष एव यज्ञः ।
units.english: And because, moving along, he purifies all things, therefore he is the ‘Sacrifice’

units.sanskrit: तस्य मनश् च वाक् च वर्तनी ॥
units.english: Thereof Mind and Speech are the paths

units.sanskrit: इदमारभ्यतेएष ह वा एष वायुर्यो ऽयं पवते ऽयं यज्ञः ।
units.english: Verily That etcthatAirwhich blows is the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: ह वा इति प्रसिद्धार्थावद्योतकौ निपातौ ।
units.english: The two particles ‘ha’ and ‘vā’ are meant to indicate the wellknown character of what is stated here

units.sanskrit: वायुप्रतिष्ठो हि यज्ञः प्रसिद्धः श्रुतिषु ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, it is well recognised in Śruti texts that ‘the Sacrifice rests on Air’;

units.sanskrit: स्वाहा वातेधाः ।
units.english: as is clear from such texts as‘Svāhā vātedhāḥ’

units.sanskrit: अयं वै यज्ञो यो ऽयं पवतेइत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः ।
units.english: Saṃhitā, , ‘ayam vai yajño etc’ the present text, and so forth

units.sanskrit: वात एव हि चलनात्मवत्वात्क्रियासमवायी ।
units.english: It is Air as consisting in motion that inheres in all Activity;

units.sanskrit: वात एव यज्ञस्या'रम्भको वातः प्रतिष्ठाइति च श्रवणात् ।
units.english: as declared in the Text that ‘Air itself is the initiation of the Sacrifice, Air is the substratum’

units.sanskrit: एष ह यन्गच्छंश्चलन्निदं सर्वं जगत्पुनाति पावयति शोधयति ।
units.english: It is hethe Airwhich moving along,blowingpurifiesrenders clean,all this,the entire universe

units.sanskrit: यद्यस्माच्च यन्नष इदं सर्वं पुनाति तस्मादेष एव यज्ञो यत्पुनातीति । तस्यास्यैवं विशिष्टस्य यज्ञस्य वाक्च मन्त्रोच्चारणे व्यापृता ।
units.english: Thereof,ie of the Sacrifice thus qualified,Speech,as engaged in the uttering of Mantras;and Mindengaged in apprehending the real nature of things,these two, Speech and Mind,are the Paths,waysthat through which the Sacrificer, on being initiated, proceeds

units.sanskrit: प्राणापानपरिचलनवत्या हिवाचश्चित्तस्य चोत्तरोत्तरक्रमो यद्यज्ञःइति हि श्रुत्यन्तरम् । अतो वाङ्मनसाभ्यां यज्ञो वर्तत इति वाङ्मनसे वर्तनी उच्येते यज्ञस्य ॥
units.english: Says another Vedic Text‘The sacrifice consists in the gradual sequence of Mind and Speech as functioning through the mobility of the Prāṇa and Apāna Breaths’ Thus it is through Mind and Speech that Sacrifice proceeds hence these two are spoken of as ‘Paths’ of the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: तयोर् अन्यतरां मनसा संस्करोति ब्रह्मा ।
units.english: One of these, the Brahman embellishes by means of Mind;

units.sanskrit: वाचा होताध्वर्युर् उद्गातान्यतराम् ।
units.english: by means of Speech, the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu and the Udgātṛ embellish the other

units.sanskrit: स यत्रोपाकृते प्रातरनुवाके पुरा परिधानीयाया ब्रह्मा व्यववदति ॥ अन्यतराम् एव वर्तनीं संस्करोति ।
units.english: If, when the Morning Recitation has commenced, and before the Paridhānīya verse has been reached, the Brahman speaks out, then he embellishes only one of the two paths, and the other becomes defective

units.sanskrit: स यथैकपाद् व्रजन् रथो वैकेन चक्रेण वर्तमानो रिष्यत्य् एवम् अस्य यज्ञो रिष्यति ।
units.english: Just as a singlelegged man going along, or a singlewheeled chariot rolling along, comes to grief,so does this Sacrifice come to grief;

units.sanskrit: यज्ञं रिष्यन्तं यजमानो ऽनु रिष्यति ।
units.english: and when the Sacrifice comes to grief, the Sacrificer comes to grief;

units.sanskrit: स इष्ट्वा पापीयान् भवति ॥
units.english: and he, having sacrificed thus, becomes the worst sinner

units.sanskrit: तयोर्वर्तन्योरन्यतरां वर्तनीं मनसा विवेकज्ञानवता संस्करोति
units.english: Of the two Paths,one path, the BrahmanPriest embellishes by means of Mind,as equipped with discriminativewisdom

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मर्त्विग्वाचा वर्तन्या होताध्वर्युरुद्गातेत्येते त्रयो ऽप्यृत्विजो ऽन्यतरां वाग्लक्षणां
units.english: By means of the Path of Speech, the HotṛPriest, the AdhvaryuPriest and the UdgātṛPriest,all these Three,embellish the other path, of Speech;

units.sanskrit: वर्तनीं वाचैव संस्कुर्वन्ति ।
units.english: that is, they embellish Speech by means of Speech itself

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति वाङ्मनसे वर्तनी संस्कार्ये यज्ञे ।
units.english: Such being the case, it becomes necessary to embellish both speech and mind at the sacrifice

units.sanskrit: परिधानीयाया ऋचो ब्रह्मैतस्मिन्नन्तरे काले व्यववदति मौनं परित्यजति यदि तदान्यतरामेव वाअग्वर्तनीं संस्करोति ब्रह्मणासंस्क्रियमाणा मनोवर्तनी हीयते विनश्यति च्छिद्रीभवत्यन्यतरा । स यज्ञो वाग्वर्तन्यैवान्यतरया वर्तितुमशक्नुवन्रिष्यति ।
units.english: Now at the time that the recitation of the Morning Hymn is begun,and before the Paridhānīya Verse is reached,in between these two,if the BrahmanPriest speaks out,that is, breaks the vow of silence,then, he embellishes only one of the two Paths,and the other Path,ie Mindremaining unembellished by the BrahmanPriest,becomes defective, perishes, becomes riddled with holes;and the Sacrificer being unable to proceed on the single path of Speech,comes to grief

units.sanskrit: कथमिवेत्याह । स यथैकपात्पुरुषो ब्रजन्गच्छन्नध्वानं रिष्यति, रथो वैकेन चक्रेण वर्तमानो गच्छन्रिष्यत्येवमस्य यजमानस्य कुब्रह्मणा यज्ञो रिष्यति विनश्यति ।
units.english: In what manner?Just as a singlelegged man, going along, on the road,comes to grief;or as the chariot rolling along on a single wheel, comes to grief;in the same way the Sacrificer’s sacrifice comes to grief, through the incompetent BrahmanPriest

units.sanskrit: यज्ञं रिष्यन्तं यजमानो ऽरिष्यति । यज्ञप्राणो हि यजमानः । अतो युक्तो यज्ञरेषे रेषस्तस्य ।
units.english: And when the Sacrifice comes to grief, the sacrificer comes to grief;as the life of the sacrificer rests in the sacrifice,it is only right that the destruction of the sacrifice should be followed by the destruction of the sacrificer;

units.sanskrit: स तं यज्ञमिष्ट्वा तादृशं पापीयान्पापतरो भवति ॥
units.english: and he, on having performed such a defective sacrifice, becomes the worst sinner,greater sinner than ever

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्र उपाकृते प्रातरनुवाके न पुरा परिधानीयाया ब्रह्मा व्यववदत्य् उभे एव वर्तनी संस्कुर्वन्ति ।
units.english: TEXTBut, when the morning recitation has commenced,if the Brahman does not speak out before the Paridhānīyā verse is reached,then they embellish both the paths;

units.sanskrit: न हीयते ऽन्यतरा ॥
units.english: and neither one becomes defective;

units.sanskrit: स यथोभयपाद् व्रजन् रथो वोभाभ्यां चक्राभ्यां वर्तमानः प्रतितिष्ठत्य् एवम् अस्य यज्ञः प्रतितिष्ठति यज्ञं प्रतितिष्ठन्तं यजमानो
units.english: And just as a twolegged man moving along, and the twowheeled chariot rolling along, remain steady,so does his Sacrifice become steady; when the Sacrifice becomes steady, the Sacrificer becomes steady;

units.sanskrit: स इष्ट्वा श्रेयान् भवति ॥
units.english: and having performed this sacrifice, he becomes superior

units.sanskrit: अथ पुनर्यत्र ब्रह्मा विद्वान्मौनं परिगृह्य वाग्विसर्गमकुर्वन्वर्तते यावत्परिधानीयाया न व्यववदति तथैव सर्वर्त्विज उभे एव वर्तनी संस्कुर्वन्ति न हीयते ऽन्यतरापि ।
units.english: But, if the BrahmanPriest is learned, and hence, having taken the vow of silence, does not give vent to speechbut remains silent throughoutand does not speak out, before the Paridhānīyā verse is reached,then alone do all the Priests embellish both the paths,and neither one of the two becomes defective

units.sanskrit: किमिवेत्याह ।
units.english: Question Like what?

units.sanskrit: पूर्वोक्तविपरीतौ दृष्टान्तौ ।
units.english: AnswerThe illustration is the obverse of the former one

units.sanskrit: एवमस्य यजमानस्य यज्ञः स्ववर्तनीभ्यां वर्तमानः प्रतितिष्ठति स्वेना'त्मनाविनश्यन्वर्तत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: In this same way the sacrificer’s sacrificeproceeding upon its two paths becomes steady,that is, continues steadily in its own form, without defecting on any point

units.sanskrit: यज्ञं प्रतितिष्ठन्तं यजमानो ऽनुप्रतितिष्ठति स यजमान एवं मौनविज्ञानवद्ब्रह्मोपेतं यज्ञमिष्ट्वा श्रेयान्भवति श्रेष्ठो भवतीत्यर्थः
units.english: When the Sacrifice becomes steady, the Sacrificer becomes steady; and the sacrificer, having performed the sacrifice with the help of the BrahmanPriest wellversed in the practice of silence, becomes superior, ie very great

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि चतुर्थाध्यायस्य षोडशः खण्डः
units.english: and for this purpose it is necessary to describe the Vyāhṛtis To this end, the Text proceeds

units.sanskrit: प्रजापतिर् लोकान् अभ्यतपत् ।
units.english: Prajāpati brooded over the Regions

units.sanskrit: तेषां तप्यमानानां रसान् प्रावृहत् ।
units.english: From these thus brooded over, He squeezed their Essences;

units.sanskrit: अग्निं पृथिव्याः । वायुम् अन्तरिक्षात् । आदित्यं दिवः ॥
units.english: Agni Fire from Earth, Vāyu Air from Sky and Āditya Sun from Heaven

units.sanskrit: होत्रादिकर्मरेषे व्याहृतिहोमः प्रायश्चित्तमिति तदर्थं व्याहृतयो विधातव्या इत्याहप्रजापतिर्लोकानभ्यतपल्लोकानुद्दिश्य
units.english: Prajāpati brooded over the Regions;that is, he performed the penance of contemplation in reference to the Regions, with a view to extracting the essence of these

units.sanskrit: तेषां तप्यमानानां लोकानां रसान्साररूपान्प्रावृहदुद्धृतवाञ्जग्राहेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: From these Regions, thus brooded over He squeezed their essences,their most essential parts

units.sanskrit: कान् । अग्निं रसं पृथिव्याः । वायुमन्तरिक्षात् ।
units.english: What were these essences?Fire was the essence of Earth, Air was the essence of the Sky;

units.sanskrit: आदित्यं दिवः ॥
units.english: and the Sun was the essence of Heaven

units.sanskrit: स एतास् तिस्रो देवता अभ्यतपत् ।
units.english: He brooded over these three Deities;

units.sanskrit: तासां तप्यमानानां रसान् प्रावृहत् ।
units.english: from these, thus brooded over, He squeezed their essences;

units.sanskrit: अग्नेर् ऋचः । वायोर् यजूंषि । सामान्य् आदित्यात् ॥
units.english: the Ṛkverses from Āgni, the Yajustexts from Vāyu, and the Sāmaverses from Āditya

units.sanskrit: पुनरप्येवमेवमग्न्याद्याः स एतास्तिस्रो देवता उद्दिश्याभ्यतपत् । ततो ऽपि सारं रसं त्रयीविद्यां जग्राह ॥
units.english: Again, He brooded over these three Divinities,Agni, Vāyu and Āditya; and from these He extracted their Essence, in the shape of the Triadic Science Three Vedas,

units.sanskrit: स एतां त्रयीं विद्याम् अभ्यतपत् ।
units.english: He brooded over this Triadic Science;

units.sanskrit: तस्यास् तप्यमानाया रसान् प्रावृहत् । भूर् इत्य् ऋग्भ्यः ।
units.english: and from that, thus brooded over He squeezed out their essences, Bhūḥ from the Ṛkverses

units.sanskrit: भुवर् इति यजुर्भ्यः । स्वर् इति सामभ्यः ॥
units.english: Bhūvaḥ from the Yajustexts, and Svaḥ from the Sāmaverses

units.sanskrit: तद् यद्य् ऋक्तो रिष्येद् भूः स्वाहेति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् ।
units.english: If the Sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Ṛkverse, one should offer an oblation into the Gārhapatya Fire, saying Bhūḥ svāhā;

units.sanskrit: ऋचाम् एव तद्रसेनर्चां वीर्येणर्चां यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संदधाति ॥
units.english: thus through this essence of the Ṛkverses, and through the virility of the Ṛkverses, one makes up the defect of Ṛkverses in the sacrifice

units.sanskrit: स एतां पुनरभ्यतपत्त्रयीं विद्याम् ।
units.english: He again brooded over this Triadic Sciencethe Science of the three Vedas;

units.sanskrit: तस्यास्तप्यमानाया रसं भूरिति व्याहृतिमृग्भ्यो जग्राह । भुवरिति व्याहृतिं यजुर्भ्यः । स्वरिति व्याहृतिं सामभ्यः । अत एव लोकदेववेदरसा महाव्याहृतयाः ।
units.english: from this Science, thus brooded over, He squeezed is essence,Bhūḥ,the first Vyāhṛtifrom the Ṛkverses,Bhuvaḥthe second Vyāhṛtifrom the Yayuṣtexts,and Svaḥthe third Vyāhṛti from the Sāmaverses,Thus these three Mahāvyāhṛtis Great Syllables,are the essence of all Regions, all Divinities and all Vedas

units.sanskrit: अतस्तत्तत्र यज्ञे यद्यृक्त ऋक्सम्बन्धादृङ्निमित्तं रिष्येद्यज्ञः क्षतं प्राप्नुयाद्भूः स्वाहेति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् । सा तत्र प्रायश्चित्तिः ।
units.english: At the several sacrificial performances, if the Sacrifice happen to become defective on any point relating to and on account of the ṚkText, one should offer an oblation into the Gārhapatya fire, saying ‘Bhūḥ Svāhā’;this is the extraction for the Defect

units.sanskrit: कथम्, ॠचामेव तदिति क्रियाविशेषणं,
units.english: How so? Thusthis is an adverbial clause

units.sanskrit: रसेनर्चां वीर्येणौजसर्चां यज्ञस्य ऋक्सम्बन्धिनो यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं विच्छिन्नं क्षतरूपमुत्पन्नं सन्दधाति प्रतिसन्धत्ते ॥
units.english: through the essence of the Ṛkverses and the virility of the Ṛkverses, one makes up the defect in the Sacrifice;ie heals up the wound that had been inflicted upon the Sacrifice, in relation to the Ṛk

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि यजुष्टो रिष्येद् भुवः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहुयात् । यजुषाम् एव तद्रसेन यजुषां वीर्येण यजुषां यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संदधाति ॥
units.english: If the Sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Yajus, one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣiṇāgni, saying ‘Bhuvaḥ svāhā’, and thus, through this essence of the Yajus Texts, and through the virility of the Yajustexts, one makes up the defect of the Yajustexts in the sacrifice

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि सामतो रिष्येत् स्वः स्वाहेत्य् आहवनीये जुहुयात् ।
units.english: If the sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Sāma, one should pour an oblation into the Āhavanīya Fire, saying ‘Svaḥ svāhā’

units.sanskrit: साम्नाम् एव तद्रसेन साम्नां वीर्येण साम्नां यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संदधाति ॥
units.english: Thus through the essence of the Sāmaverses, and through the virility of the Sāmaverses one makes up the defect of the Sāmatexts in the sacrifice

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि यजुष्टो यजुर्निमित्तं रिष्येद्भुवः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहुयात् । तथा सामनिमित्ते रेषे स्वः स्वाहेत्याहवनीये जुहुयात् ।
units.english: If there be any defect related to, or caused by, the Yajus,one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣināgṇi, saying ‘Bhuvaḥ svāhā’;similarly, when there is a defect due to Sāma, one should pour an oblation into the Āhavanīy a fire, saying ‘Svāḥ svāhā’

units.sanskrit: तथा पूर्ववद्यज्ञं सन्दधाति ।
units.english: In this way, as before, he makes up this defect in the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मनिमित्ते तु रेषे त्रिष्वग्निषु । तिसृभिर्व्याहृतिभिर्जुहुयात् ।
units.english: When there is a defect due to the BrahmanPriest as described above, one should offer three oblations into the three fires, pronouncing the three Vyāhṛtis Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ;

units.sanskrit: त्रय्या हि विद्यायाः स रेषः । अथ केन ब्रह्मत्वमित्यनयैव त्रय्या विद्ययाइति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: as such a defect would be a defect relating to all the three Vedas,as declared in the Vedic Text‘Now whereby is Brahmanhood attained? By means of the science of the three Vedas!’

units.sanskrit: न्यायान्तरं वा मृग्यं ब्रह्मत्वनिमित्ते रेषे ॥
units.english: Or if this is not found satisfactory some other law will have to be found for rectifying the defect due to the BrahmanPriest

units.sanskrit: तद् यथा लवणेन सुवर्णं संदध्यात् । सुवर्णेन रजतं रजतेन त्रपु त्रपुणा सीसं सीसेन लोहं लोहेन दारु दारु चर्मणा ॥
units.english: Just as one would join gold by salt, silver by gold, tin by silver, lead by tin, iron by lead, wood by iron, and wood by leather;

units.sanskrit: एवम् एषां लोकानाम् आसां देवतानाम् अस्यास् त्रय्या विद्याया वीर्येण यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संदधाति । भेषजकृतो ह वा एष यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद् ब्रह्मा भवति ॥
units.english: So does one make up the defect in the Sacrifice by the virility of these regions, of these divinities and of the science of the three Vedas,That sacrifice verily becomes wellhealed up where there is a BrahmanPriest knowing this

units.sanskrit: तद्यथा लवणेन सुवर्णं सन्दध्यात् । क्षारेण टङ्कणादिना खरे; मृदुत्वकरं हि तत् । सुवर्णेन रजतमशक्यसन्धानं सन्दध्यात् । रजतेन तथा त्रपु त्रपुणा सीसं सीसेन लोह लोहेन दारु दारु चर्मणा चर्मबन्धनेन ।
units.english: Just as one would join gold by salt, ie by Borax and such other salts, which serve to soften the hard goldpieces,silver by gold,silver, which is otherwise unjoinable, becomes joined by gold;Tin by silverlead by tiniron by lead,wood by iron,and wood by leather, by leatherbandagesin this same way one makes good the defect in the Sacrifice, by the virilityie force, called Essenceof the said Regions, Divinities and the Science of the three Vedas

units.sanskrit: भेषजकृतो ह वा एष यज्ञः ।
units.english: That sacrifice verily becomes wellhealed up

units.sanskrit: रोगार्त इव पुमांश्चिकित्सकेन सुशिक्षितेनैष यज्ञो भवति । को ऽसौ । यत्र यस्मिन्यज्ञ एवंविद्यथोक्तव्याहृतिहोमप्रायश्चित्तविद्ब्रह्मर्त्विग्भवति स यज्ञ इत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: just as a sick patient becomes healthy through an expert physician,so does that Sacrifice become,which sacrifice?That sacrifice at which there is a BrahmanPriest knowing thisie who knows the expiatory rite, by means of the Vyāhṛtis

units.sanskrit: एष ह वा उदक्प्रवणो यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद् ब्रह्मा भवति ।
units.english: That Sacrifice indeed is ‘Northsloping’ where there is a BrahmanPriest knowing this

units.sanskrit: एवंविदं ह वा एषा ब्रह्माणम् अनु गाथा । यतो यत आवर्तते तत् तद् गच्छति ॥
units.english: It is in reference to the BrahmanPriest knowing this that there is the saying that ‘Wherever it fails, there he goes’

units.sanskrit: किञ्चैष ह वा उदक्प्रवण उदङ्निम्नो दक्षिणोच्छ्रायो यज्ञो भवति । उत्तरमार्गप्रतिपत्तिहेतुरित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Further, that sacrifice is ‘Northsloping’ rising towards the South,ie it becomes the means of reaching the Northern Path,where there is a Brahman Priest knowing this;

units.sanskrit: यत्रैवंविद्ब्रह्मा भवत्येवंविदं ह वै ब्रह्माणमृत्विजं प्रत्येषानुगाथा ब्रह्मणः स्तुतिपरा ।
units.english: that there is this sayingeulogising the BrahmanPriest‘Wherever itthe action

units.sanskrit: यतो यत आवर्तते कर्म प्रदेशादृत्विजां यज्ञः क्षतीभवंस्तत्तद्यज्ञस्य क्षतरूपं प्रतिसन्दधत्प्रायश्चित्तेन गच्छति परिपालयतीत्येतत्
units.english: Sacrificefails ie from whatever part of the Priests the Sacrifice suffers harm, becomes defectivethat defect of the Sacrifice he heals up by means of the expiatory Rite,and there he goes,ie he protects the Sacrifice

units.sanskrit: मानवः । ब्रह्मैवैक ऋत्विक् कुरून् अश्वाभिरक्षति ।
units.english: The silent Brahman is the one priest who protects the performers, like the Mare

units.sanskrit: एवंविद् ध वै ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजमानं सर्वांश् चर्त्विजो ऽभिरक्षति ।
units.english: The BrahmanPriest who knows this protects the Sacrifice, the Sacrificer, and all the priests

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् एवंविदम् एव ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत नानेवंविदं नानेवंविदम् ॥
units.english: Hence one should have as Brahman Priest only one who knows this,not one who knows this not,yea, knows it not0

units.sanskrit: मानवो भ्रह्मा मौनाचरणान्मननाद्वा ज्ञावनत्त्वात्ततो ब्रह्मैवैकर्त्विक्कुरून्कर्तॄन् । योद्धॄनारूढानश्वा वडवा यथाभिरक्षत्येवंविद्ध वै ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजमानं सर्वांश्चर्त्विजो ऽभिरक्षति तत्कृतदोषापनयनात् ।
units.english: The silent Brahmancalled ‘Mānava’ because he has taken the vow of silence, or because he is possessed of right knowledge,is the only one priest who protects the performers,just as the Horse protects its rider The Brahmanpriest who knows this protects the Sacrifice, the Sacrificer, and all the priestsby removing the defects caused by them

units.sanskrit: यत एवंविशिष्टो ब्रह्मा विद्वांस्तस्मादेवंविदमेव यथोक्तव्याहृत्यादिविदं ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत नानेवंविदं कदाचनेति ।
units.english: Inasmuch as the Brahman should be so learned one should have as Brahman one who knows the Vyāḥrtis and other details described above,and never one who knows not this

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यासो ऽध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ पञ्चमो ऽध्यायः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै ज्येष्ठं च श्रेष्ठं च वेद ज्येष्ठश् च ह वै श्रेष्ठश् च भवति । प्राणो वाव ज्येष्ठश् च श्रेष्ठश् च ॥ सगुण ब्रह्मविद्याया उत्तरा गतिरुक्ता । अथेदानीं पञ्चमे ऽध्याये पञ्चाग्निविदो गृहस्थस्योर्ध्वरेतसां च श्रद्धालूनां विद्यान्तरशीलिनां तामेव गतिमनूद्यान्या दक्षिणदिक्सम्बन्धिनी केवलकर्मिणां धूमादिलक्षणा पुनरावृत्तिरूपा
units.english: The Northern Path has been described aboveas following from the knowledge of the Philosophy of Brahman with Qualification, Now in Discourse , the Text is going to describe the same Path as relating to the Householder knowing the Philosophy of the Fivefires, and also to such ascetics as are imbued with faith and are steeped in other philosophies;and after having done this, it is going to describe another second Path, the Southern one, which falls to the lot of those who merely perform Rites without a knowledge of the Philosophy underlying them,this second path lying through smoke and other things, and leading to rebirth

units.sanskrit: तृतीया च ततः कष्टतरा संसारगतिर्वैराग्यहेतोर्वक्तव्येत्यारभ्यते ।
units.english: Then again, a third Path is going to be described, which is still more painful,the way of the ordinary world;this being described for the purpose of creating disgust in the mind of the pupil against worldliness

units.sanskrit: प्राणः श्रेष्ठो वागादिभ्यः प्राणो वाव संवर्ग इत्यादि च बहुशो ऽतीते ग्रन्थे प्राणग्रहणं कृतम् ।
units.english: Breath Prāṇa is superior to Speech and the other organs; in several places above, this Breath has been spoken of,e g, in the text ‘Breath Prāṇa is the absorbent’

units.sanskrit: स कथं श्रेष्ठो वागादिषु सर्वैः संहत्यकारित्वाविशेषे? कथं च तस्योपासनमिति तस्य श्रेष्ठत्वादिगुणविधित्सयेदमनन्तरमारभ्यतेयो ह वै कश्चिज्ज्येष्ठं च प्रथमं वयसा वाव ज्येष्ठश्च
units.english: The question that arises isIn what way is Breath superior to Speech and the rest, when they are all found to be functioning collectively? In what way too is this Breath to be meditated upon?It is with a view to answer the first of these questions that the Text proceeds to declare the superiority of Breath ‘Om! One who knows the Oldest and the Best himself becomes the Oldest and the Best

units.sanskrit: वयसा वागादिभ्यः ।
units.english: Breath indeed is the Oldest and the Best

units.sanskrit: गर्भस्थे हि पुरुषे प्राणस्य वृत्तिर्वागादिभ्यः पूर्वं लब्धात्मिका भवति यया गर्भो
units.english: Any one who knows the Oldest,the first in point of āge,and the Bestsuperior in qualities,himself becomes the Oldest and the Best

units.sanskrit: विवर्धते चक्षुरादिस्थानावयवनिष्पत्तौ सत्यां पश्चाद्वागादीनां वृत्तिलाभ इति प्राणो ज्येष्ठो वयसा भवति ।
units.english: Having tempted and attracted the attention of the listener by mentioning the reward, the Text declaresBreath indeed is the Oldest, in point of age, among Speech and the rest As a matter of fact, while the man to be born is still in the womb, the functioning of Breath appears before that of Speech and the rest, and it is through the function of the Breath that the foetus grows,and the functioning of the organs of Speech and the rest appear only when, later on, the constituent elements of the eye and other organs take shape;

units.sanskrit: श्रेष्ठत्वं तु प्रतिपादयिष्यति सुहय इत्यादिनिदर्शनेन । अतः प्राण एव ज्येष्ठश्च श्रेष्ठश्चास्मिन्कार्यकरणसङ्घाते ॥
units.english: thus Breath is the Oldest in age,As regards Breath being the Best, that is going to be explained later on under Text , by means of the example of the ‘Spirited House’Thus the conclusion is that in this Bodywhich is an aggregate of causes and effectsBreath is the Oldest and the Best

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै वसिष्ठं वेद वसिष्ठो ह स्वानां भवति ।
units.english: One who knows the Richest, becomes the Richest among his own people

units.sanskrit: वाग् वाव वसिष्ठः ॥
units.english: Speech indeed is the Richest

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै वसिष्ठं वसितृतममाच्छादयितृतमं वसुमत्तमं वा यो वेद स तथैव वसिष्ठो ह भवति स्वानां ज्ञातीनाम् ।
units.english: One who knows the ‘Vasiṣṭha’which may mean ‘the best of coverers’ or the ‘Richesthimself becomes the Richest among his people,his relations

units.sanskrit: कस्तर्हि वसिष्ठ इत्याह ।
units.english: QuestionWho then is the Richest?

units.sanskrit: वाग्वाव वसिष्ठो वाग्मिनो हि पुरुषा वसन्त्यभिभवन्त्यन्यान्वसुमत्तमाश्चातो वाग्वसिष्ठः ॥
units.english: AnswerSpeech indeed is the Richest; people who are good speakers suppress others and also become the Richest; hence speech is the Richest

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै प्रतिष्ठां वेद प्रति ह तिष्ठत्य् अस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
units.english: One who knows firmness becomes firm in this world, and also in the other

units.sanskrit: चक्षुर् वाव प्रतिष्ठा ॥
units.english: The Eye is indeed firmness

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै प्रतिष्ठां वेद स चास्मिंल्लोके ऽमुष्मिंश्च परे प्रतितिष्ठति ह ।
units.english: One who knows firmness becomes firm in this world, and also in the otherhigher one

units.sanskrit: का तर्हि प्रतिष्ठेत्याहचक्षुर्वाव प्रतिष्ठा ।
units.english: QuestionWhat is firmness?

units.sanskrit: चक्षुषा हि पश्यन्समे च दुर्गे च प्रतितिष्ठति यस्मादतः प्रतिष्ठा चक्षुः ॥
units.english: AnswerThe Eye indeed is firmnessWhen a man sees with his eyes, then alone does he remain firm on even as well as on uneven ground; hence the Eye is firmness

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै संपदं वेद सं हास्मै कामाः पद्यन्ते दैवाश् च मानुषाश् च ।
units.english: One who knows Prosperityfor him all desires prosper, divine as well as human

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं वाव संपत् ॥
units.english: The Ear indeed is Prosperity

units.sanskrit: यो ह वै सम्पदं वेद तस्मा अस्मै दैवाश्च मानुषाश्च कामाः सम्पद्यन्ते ह ।
units.english: One who knows Prosperity, for him all desires, human and divine, prosper

units.sanskrit: का तर्हि सम्पदित्याहश्रोत्रं वाव सम्पत् ।
units.english: QuestionWhat is Prosperity? AnswerThe Ear indeed is Prosperity

units.sanskrit: यस्माच्छ्रोत्रेण वेदा गृह्यन्ते तदर्थविज्ञानं च ततः कर्माणि क्रियन्ते ततः कामसम्पदित्येवं कामसम्पद्धेतुत्वाच्छ्रोत्रं वाव संपत् ॥
units.english: It is through the Ear that the Vedas and their meaning are learnt, and hence Rites are performed, whence desires become fulfilled; thus, being the cause of the prosperity or fulfilment of desires, the Ear indeed is Prosperity

units.sanskrit: यो ह वा आयतनं वेदायतनं ह स्वानां भवति ।
units.english: One who knows the Home becomes the Home of his PeopleMind indeed is the Home

units.sanskrit: यो ह वा आयतनं वेदा'यतनं ह स्वानां भवत्याश्रयो भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: One who knows the Home becomes the Home,ie the supportof his people

units.sanskrit: किं तदायतनमित्याहमनो ह वा आयतनम् ।
units.english: QuestionWhat is that Home? AnswerMind indeed is the Home

units.sanskrit: इन्द्रियोपहृतानां विषयाणां भोक्त्रर्थानां प्रत्ययरूपामां मन आयतनमाश्रयः ।
units.english: It is the Mind that is the‘Home’, the support, of all those objects that are presented in the form of Perceptions, by the senseorgans for being experienced by the Enjoyer

units.sanskrit: अतो मनो ह वा आयतनमित्युक्तम् ॥
units.english: Hence, it is said that Mind indeed is the Home

units.sanskrit: अथ ह प्राणा अहंश्रेयसि व्यूदिरे । अहं श्रेयान् अस्म्य् अहं श्रेयान् अस्मीति ॥
units.english: Now, the five senseorgans quarrelled among themselves, as to who was superior,saying ‘ am superior’, ‘ am superior’

units.sanskrit: अथ ह प्राणा एवं यथोक्तगुणाः सन्तो ऽहंश्रेयस्यहं श्रेयानस्म्यहं श्रेयानस्मीत्येतस्मिन्प्रयोजने व्यूदिरे नाना विरुद्धं चोदिर
units.english: Now, the senseorganspossessed of the qualities described above,quarrelled among themselvesas to who was superiorand spoke much against each other,saying ‘ am superior, am superior’

units.sanskrit: उक्तवन्तः ॥ ते ह प्राणाः प्रजापतिं पितरम् एत्योचुः भगवन् को नः श्रेष्ठ इति । तान् होवाच ।
units.english: The senseorgans, having gone to Prajāpati, their Father,said to him‘Sir, who is the best amongst us?’ He saidto them‘He on whose departure the body becomes worst,that amongst you is the Best’

units.sanskrit: ते ह तै हैवं विवदमाना आत्मनः श्रेष्ठत्वविज्ञानाय प्रजापतिं पितरं जनयितारं कञ्चिदेत्योचुरुक्तवन्तो हे भगवन्को नो ऽस्माकं मध्ये श्रेष्ठो
units.english: Thus quarrelling among themselves, each desirous of ascertaining his own superiority,they went to Prajāpati, their Father,creator,and said‘Sir, amongs us, who is best,superior in qualities?this is what they asked him

units.sanskrit: तान्पितोवाच ह यस्मिन्वो युष्माकं मध्ये उत्क्रान्ते शरीरमिदं पापिष्ठमिवातिशयेन जीवतो ऽपि, समुत्क्रान्तप्राणं ततो ऽपि पापिष्ठतरमिवातिशयेन दृष्यते कुणपमस्पृश्यमशुचि दृश्येत स वो युष्माकं श्रेष्ठ इत्यवोचत्काक्वा तद्दुःखं परिजिहीर्षुः
units.english: The Father said to them‘Amongst you, he on whose departure the Body becomes worst;the body is bad enough even when the man is alive, and when life is extinct, it becomes still worse,a corpse, untouchablehe is the best amongst you’ Desiring to avoid giving pain to any one of them, He gave his answer in this indirect manner

units.sanskrit: सा ह वाग् उच्चक्राम ।
units.english: Speech went out;

units.sanskrit: कथम् अशकतर्ते मज् जीवितुम् इति । यथा कला अवदन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
units.english: and having stayed away for a year it came back and said‘How have you been able to live without me‘Just like the dumb, not speaking, but breathing with the Breath, seeing with the Eye, hearing with the Ear, and thinking with the Mind’

units.sanskrit: प्रविवेश ह वाक् ॥
units.english: Then Speech went in

units.sanskrit: चक्षुर् होच्चक्राम ।
units.english: The Eye went out;

units.sanskrit: कथम् अशकतर्ते मज् जीवितुम् इति । यथान्धा अपश्यन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति । प्रविवेश ह चक्षुः ॥
units.english: and after having stayed away for a year, it came back and said‘How have you been able to live without me?’‘Just like the blind, not seeing, but breathing with the Breath, speaking with the Speech, hearing with the Ear, and thinking with the Mind’Then the Eye went in

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं होच्चक्राम ।
units.english: The Ear went out;

units.sanskrit: तत् संवत्सरं प्रोष्य पर्येत्योवाच कथम् अशकतर्ते मज् जीवितुम् इति ।
units.english: and after having stayed away for a year, it came back and said‘How have you been able to live without me?’

units.sanskrit: यथा बधिरा अशृण्वन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
units.english: ‘Just like the deaf,not hearing, but breathing with the Breath, speaking with the Speech, seeing with the Eye and thinking with the Mind’

units.sanskrit: प्रविवेश ह श्रोत्रम् ॥
units.english: The Ear went in

units.sanskrit: मनो होच्चक्राम ।
units.english: The Mind went out;

units.sanskrit: कथम् अशकतर्ते मज् जीवितुम् इति । यथा बाला अमनसः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेणैवम् इति ।
units.english: and after having stayed away for a year, it came back and said‘How have you been able to live without me?’‘Just like infants without minds,breathing with the Breath, speaking with the Speech, seeing with the Eye and hearing with the Ear’

units.sanskrit: प्रविवेश ह मनः ॥
units.english: The Mind went in’

units.sanskrit: तथोक्तेषु पित्रा प्राणेषु सा ह वागुच्चक्रामोत्क्रान्तवती ।
units.english: The senseorgans having been told as above by their father, Speech went out,departed from the body

units.sanskrit: सा चोत्क्रम्य संवत्सरमात्रं प्रोष्य स्वव्यापारान्निवृत्ता सती पुनः पर्येत्येतरान्प्राणानुवाच कथं केन प्रकारेणाशकत शक्तवन्तो यूयं मदृते मां विना जीवितुं धारयितुमात्मानमिति
units.english: Having gone out, it stayed away for a year,desisting from its function;then having come bach, it said to the other organsHowin that mannerdid you live without me?That is, how did you manage to sustain your life without me?They said‘Just like the Dumb etc, etc

units.sanskrit: अकला मूका यथा लोके ऽवदन्तो वाचा जीवन्ति ।
units.english: Just as in the world, dumb persons do not speak, and yet they live

units.sanskrit: कथम्?प्राणन्तः प्राणेन पश्यन्तश्चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवं सर्वकरणचेष्टां कुर्वन्त इत्यर्थः । एवं वयमजीविष्मेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: How so? Breathing with the Breath, seeing with the Eye, hearing with the Ear, thinking with the Mind;ie carrying on the functions of all other organs except Speech;in this manner we lived’Thus having understood that it was not the best among the organs, Speech Went in,ie again became engaged in its own function

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यच्चक्षुर्हेच्चक्राम श्रोत्रं होच्चक्राम मनो होच्चक्रामेत्यादि । यथा बाला अमनसो ऽप्ररूढमनस इत्यर्थः ॥ ॥
units.english: The rest is as before in what followsThe Eye went out, the Ear went out, the Mind went out etc, etc,Just like infants, without minds,ie with their minds still undeveloped

units.sanskrit: अथ ह प्राण उच्चिक्रमिषन् स यथा सुहयः पड्वीशशङ्कून् संखिदेद् एवम् इतरान् प्राणान् समखिदत् ।
units.english: Now, the Breath, on going to depart, uprooted the other organs, just as the fine horse would uproot the pegs to which it is tethered

units.sanskrit: तं हाभिसमेत्योचुः । भगवन्न् एधि । त्वं नः श्रेष्ठो ऽसि ।
units.english: They gathered round him and said, ‘Hail! Prosper, Sir, you are the Best amongst us;

units.sanskrit: मोत्क्रमीर् इति ॥
units.english: do not depart’

units.sanskrit: एवं परीक्षितेषु वागादिष्वथानन्तरं ह स मुख्यः प्राण उच्चिक्रमिषन्नुत्क्रमितुमिच्छन्किमकरोदित्युच्यते ।
units.english: Speech and the rest having been thus tested,now Breath,the Principal Breathon going to depart

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके सुहयः शोभनो ऽश्वः पड्वीशशङ्कून्पादबन्धनकीलान्परीक्षणाया'रूढेन कश्याहतः सन्सङ्खिदेत्समुत्खनेत् समुत्पाटयेत्,
units.english: just as it evinced a desire to go out,what did it do?just as in the world,a fine horsea spirited horseon being struck with the whip by the rider desirous of fastening it,Would uproottear outthe pegs to which it is tethered,in the same manner, Breath uprootedtore upthe other organs

units.sanskrit: एवमितरान्वागादीन्प्राणान्समखिदत्समुद्धृतवान् । ते प्राणाः सञ्चालिताः सन्तः स्वस्थाने स्थातुमनुत्सहमाना अभिसमेत्य मुख्यं प्राणं
units.english: Speech and the rest;thereupon, these organs, having become thus uprooted and hence unable to remain in their places,gathered round himthe Principal Breath,and said to him‘Hail, Sir, prosper;be our master;

units.sanskrit: तमूचुर्हें भगवन्नेधि भव नः स्वामी यस्मात्त्वं नो ऽस्माकं श्रेष्ठो ऽसि मा चास्माद्देहादुत्क्रमीरिति ॥
units.english: because amongst us, you are the Best; and please do not depart from this body’

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनं वाग् उवाच । यद् अहं वसिष्ठो ऽस्मि त्वं तद्वसिष्ठो ऽसीति । अथ हैनं चक्षुर् उवाच ।
units.english: Then Speech said to him‘As am the richest, you are that richest’ Then the Eye said to him‘As am firmness, you are that firmness!’

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनं मन उवाच । यद् अहम् आयतनम् अस्मि त्वं तदायतनम् असीति ॥
units.english: Then the Ear said to him‘As am prosperity, you are that prosperityThen the Mind said to him‘As am the home, you are that home’

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनं वागादयः प्राणस्य श्रेष्ठत्वं कार्येणा'पादयन्त आहुर्बलिमिव हरन्तो राज्ञे विशः ।
units.english: Speech and the rest, establishing, by their action, the superiority of Breath, said to himmaking offerings to him like the people to their King

units.sanskrit: कथं, वाक् तावदुवाच यदहं वसिष्ठो ऽस्मि । यदिति क्रियाविशेषणं यद्वसिष्ठत्वगुणास्मीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: What did they say?Speech said‘As am the richest,‘as’ is an adverb, the meaning being that the quality of richness by which am the richest,by that same quality of richness you are the richest;

units.sanskrit: त्वं तद्वसिष्ठस्तेन वसिष्ठत्वगुणो ऽज्ञानान्ममेति मयाभिमत इत्येतत् ।
units.english: the sense being that ‘the quality of Richness is really due to and belongs to yourself, and it was in sheer ignorance that regarded it as mine’
