units.sanskrit: तथोत्तरेषु योज्यं चक्षुःश्रोत्रमनःसु ॥ ॥
units.english: The same interpretation may be applied to the others,Eye, Ear and Mindalso

units.sanskrit: न वै वाचो न चक्षूंषि न श्रोत्राणि न मनांसीत्य् आचक्षते ।
units.english: And people do not call them ‘Speeches’, ‘Eyes’, ‘Ears’, ‘Minds’;

units.sanskrit: प्राणा इत्य् एवाचक्षते ।
units.english: they call them ‘Breath’;

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ह्य् एवैतानि सर्वाणि भवति ॥
units.english: for Breath indeed is all these

units.sanskrit: श्रुतेरिदं वचो युक्तमिदं वागादिभिर्मुख्यं प्राणं प्रत्यभिहितं
units.english: This text contains the assertion of the VedaText itself What is meant is as followsWhat Speech and the rest said to Breath was quite right

units.sanskrit: यस्मान्न वै लोके वाचो न चक्षूंषि न श्रोत्राणि न मनांसीति वागादीनि करणान्याचक्षते लौकिका आगमज्ञा वा ।
units.english: Because, in the ordinary world, peopleordinary men or personsversed in the Scriptures do not call Speech and the other senseorgans as ‘Speeches’, or ‘Eyes’ or ‘Ears’ or ‘Minds’;

units.sanskrit: किं तर्हि?प्राणा इत्येवा'चक्षते कथयन्ति यस्मात्प्राणो ह्येवैतानि सर्वाणि वागादीनि
units.english: they call them ‘Breaths’ Because all these senseorgans, Speech and the rest, are Breath, therefore what Speech and the rest said to the Principal Breath was quite right

units.sanskrit: करणजातानि भवत्यतो मुख्यं प्रामं प्रत्यनुरूपमेव वागादिभिरुक्तमिति प्रकरणार्थमुपसञ्जिहीर्षति ।
units.english: This has been said in the text for the purpose of summing up the contents of the Section

units.sanskrit: ननु कथमिदं युक्तं चेतनावन्त इव पुरुषा अहंश्रेष्ठतायै विवदन्तो ऽन्योन्यं स्पर्धेरन्निति ।
units.english: ObjectionHow can all this be right and proper? As a matter of fact, it is only persons, who are conscious beings, who quar el among themselves for superiority

units.sanskrit: न हि चक्षुरादीनां वाचं प्रत्याख्याय प्रत्येकं वदनं सम्भवति ।
units.english: Secondly, excepting Speech, it is not possible for any other organ among the Eye and the rest to speak out

units.sanskrit: तथापगमो देहात्पुनः प्रवेशो ब्रह्मगमनं प्राणस्तुतिर्वोपपद्यते ।
units.english: Thirdly, their departure from the body, reentrance into it, coming to Brahmā, eulogising of Breath,none of this can be possible

units.sanskrit: तत्राग्न्यादिचेतनावद्देवताधिष्ठितत्वाद्वागादीनां चेतनावत्त्वं तावत्सिद्धमागमतः तार्किकसमयविरोध इति चेद्देह एकस्मिन्ननेकचेतनावत्त्वे
units.english: AnswerIt is a fact established on the strength of the scriptures that Speech and the other organs are conscious, through being presided over by conscious deities,just in the same way as the fact of fire, earth and the rest being conscious is well recognised

units.sanskrit: ईश्वरस्य निमित्तकारमत्वाभ्युपगमात् ।
units.english: because they posit God as the ‘Operative cause’ of the world

units.sanskrit: ये तावदीश्वरमभ्युपगच्छन्ति तार्किकास्ते मन आदिकार्यकरमानामाध्यात्मिकानां बाह्यानां च पृथिव्यादीनामीश्वराधिष्ठितानामेव नियमेन प्रवृत्तिमिच्छन्ति रथादिवत् ।
units.english: Those logicians who admit the existence of God, hold that the functioning of all ‘internal’ causes and effects as the Mind and the rest, as also of all ‘external’ things like Earth and the rest,is invariably due to their being presided over by God,just as the moving of the chariot and the other things is due to its being operated upon by a conscious person

units.sanskrit: न चास्माभिरग्न्याद्याश्चेतनावत्यो ऽपि देवता अध्यात्मं भोक्त्र्यो ऽभ्युपगम्यन्ते,
units.english: As for ourselves Vedāntins, even though we regard Fire and the rest as endowed with consciousness, we do not regard them as the experience;

units.sanskrit: किं तर्हि,
units.english: of what is occurring in the body;

units.sanskrit: कार्यकरणवतीनां हि तासां प्राणैकदेवताभेदानामध्यात्माधिभूताधिदैवभेदकोटिविकल्पानामध्यक्षतामात्रेण नियन्तेश्वरो ऽभ्युपगम्यते
units.english: what we hold is that all these entities Fire and the rest are made up of so many causes and effects,they are the diverse forms of the one deity ‘Breath’ Prāṇa, and serve as prototypes of the millions of manifestations spiritual, material and divine;and God is posited by us only as the controller of these not their Operative causeand this God is without organs;

units.sanskrit: स ह्यकरणः ।
units.english: as declared in the Text‘Without hands and feet, He runs and holds, without eyes

units.sanskrit: हिरण्यगर्भं जनयामान पूर्वमित्यादि च श्वेताश्वतरीयाः पठन्ति ।
units.english: The followers of the Śvetāśvatara have also the following texts bearing upon this subjecta ‘Look upon Hiraṇyagarbha being born’, Śvetā b ‘First of all He created Hiraṇyagarbha’ Śvetā

units.sanskrit: भोक्ता कर्मफलसम्बन्धी देहे तद्विलक्षणो जीव इति वक्ष्यामः ।
units.english: As for the enjoyer, experiencer, who is related to the rewards of deeds done, he is the Jīva the Corporeal Self in the Body, and this is different from the said God the controller,as we shall explain later on

units.sanskrit: वागादीनां चेह संवादः कल्पितो विदुषो ऽन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां प्राणश्रेष्ठतानिर्धारणार्थम् ।
units.english: As for the dialogue among Speech and the other organs that we have in the present context,it is an imaginary one, set forth for the purpose of establishing the superiority of Breath, by means of negation and affirmation

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके पुरुषा अन्योन्यमात्मनः श्रेष्ठतायै विवदमानाः कञ्चिद्गुणविशेषाभिज्ञं पृच्छन्ति को नः श्रेष्ठो गुणैरिति ।
units.english: In the ordinary world, when people quarrel among themselves, regarding their relative superiority, they go over to some person who is able to judge of the qualities of men and ask him‘Who amongst us is the best, in point of qualifications’

units.sanskrit: तेनोक्ता एकैकश्येनादः कार्यं साधयितुमुद्यच्छत येनादः कार्यं साध्यते स वः श्रेष्ठ इत्युक्तास्तथैवोद्यच्छन्त आत्मनो ऽन्यस्य वा श्रेष्ठवां निर्धारयन्ति ।
units.english: and he says in reply‘Each one of you separately go and do such and such an act; he amongst you who succeeds in doing it is the best’; and on this they go ahead and betake themselves to the act suggested, and ascertain the superiority of one or the other, through their success or otherwise at the said performance

units.sanskrit: ततेमं संव्यवहारं वागादिषु कल्पितवती श्रुतिः ।
units.english: This same procedure the Śruti has asserted in the present context as, having been adopted by Speech and the other organs

units.sanskrit: कथं नाम विद्वान्वागादीनामेकैकस्याभावे ऽपि जीवनं दृष्टं न तु प्राणस्येति प्राणश्रेष्ठतां प्रतिपद्यतेति । तथाच श्रुतिः कौषीतकिनाम्जीवति वागपेतो मूकान्हि पस्यामो जीवति चक्षुरपेतो
units.english: If this had not been done, how could even the learned person realise the superiority of Breath on the basis of the fact that from among Speech and the rest, while life is found to remain even on the departure of the others, but not on the departure of Breath? To the same end is the following text of the Kauṣītakins‘Bereft of speech, man lives,we see dumb persons;

units.sanskrit: ऽन्धान्हि पश्यामो जीवति श्रोत्रापेतो बधिरान्हि पश्यामो जीवति मनोपेतो बालान्हि पश्यामो
units.english: bereft of eyes, man lives,we see the blind; bereft of ears, man lives,we see the deaf; bereft of mind, man lives, we see infants;

units.sanskrit: जीवति बाहुच्छिन्नो जीवत्यूरुच्छिन्नःइत्याद्या ॥
units.english: with arms cut off, man lives; with legs cut off man lives etc, etc Kauṣītakin

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: स होवाच किं मे ऽन्नं भविष्यतीति । यत् किंचिद् इदम् आ श्वभ्य आ शकुनिभ्य इति होचुः ।
units.english: He said‘What shall be my food?’They said‘Whatever there is, from dogs to birds’ This is the food forBreath;

units.sanskrit: तद् वा एतद् अनस्यान्नम् ।
units.english: ‘Ana’ is his distinct name

units.sanskrit: न ह वा एवंविदि किंचनानन्नं भवतीति ॥
units.english: For one who knows this, there is nothing that is notfood

units.sanskrit: स होवाच मुख्यः प्राणः किं मे ऽन्नं भविष्यतीति । मुख्यं प्राणं प्रष्टारमिव कल्पयित्वा वागादीन्प्रतिवक्तॄनिव कल्पयन्ती श्रुतिराहयदिदं लोके ऽन्नजातं प्रसिद्धमा श्वभिः सहाऽशकुनिभ्यः सह शकुनिभिः सर्वप्राणिनां यदन्नं तत्तवान्नमिति होचुर्वागादय इति ।
units.english: Hethe principa Breathsaid‘What shall be my food?’Having imagined Breath to be the questioner, the Text imagines Speech and the rest to be the persons answering the question‘Whatever in this world is known as food,from dogs,ie including dogs,to birds, including birdsthe food of all living beings,that will be your food,so said Speech and the rest

units.sanskrit: प्राणस्य सर्वमन्नं प्राणो ऽत्ता सर्वस्यान्नस्येत्येवं प्रतिपत्तये कल्पिताख्यायिकारूपाद्व्यावृत्य स्वेन श्रुतिरूपेणा'हतद्वा एतद्यत्किञ्चिल्लोके प्राणिभिरन्नमद्यते ऽनस्य प्राणस्य तदन्नं प्राणेनैव तदद्यत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Everything is food for Breath, Breath is the eater of all food,in order to inculcate these truths, the text turns aside from the telling of the story, and makes an assertion of its ownThisie whatever food is eaten by living beings in the world,is food for Breath,ie it is all eaten by Breath alone

units.sanskrit: सर्वप्रकारचेष्टाव्याप्तिगुणप्रदर्शनार्थमन इति प्राणस्य प्रत्यक्षं नाम ।
units.english: ‘Ana’ is the distinct name, of Breath,as indicating the character of permeating through all forms of activity

units.sanskrit: प्राद्युपसर्गपूर्वत्वे हि विशेषगतिरेव स्यात् ।
units.english: The addition of the prefix ‘pra’ to ‘ana’, thus making up the term ‘Prāṇa’ would only serve to express some special feature of activity;

units.sanskrit: तथाच सर्वान्नानामत्तुर्नामग्रहणमितीदं प्रत्यक्षं नामान इति सर्वान्नानामत्तुः साक्षादभिधानम् ।
units.english: thus the text pronounces the name of the Eater of all foods‘Ana’ is the distinct namethe direct connoterof the Eater of all foods

units.sanskrit: न ह वा एवंविदि यथोक्तप्राणविदि प्राणो ऽहमस्मि सर्वभूतस्थः सर्वान्नानामत्तेति तस्मिन्नेवंविदि ह वै किञ्चन किञ्चिदपि प्राणिभिराद्यं सर्वैरनन्नमन्नाद्यं न
units.english: For one who knows thisall that has been said regarding Breath,that ‘ am Breath subsisting in all living beings, the Eater of all foodsfor such a one, there is nothing that can be eaten by living beings,that is notfood;

units.sanskrit: भवति सर्वमेवंविद्यन्नं भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, all edibles become food for him;

units.sanskrit: प्राणभूतत्वाद्विदुषः ।
units.english: and the reason for this lies in the fact that the man knowing this is Breath itself;

units.sanskrit: प्राणाद्वा एष उदेति प्राणे ऽस्तमेतिइत्युपक्रम्यएवंविदो ह वा उदेति सूर्य एवंविद्यस्तमेतिइति श्रुत्यन्तरात् ॥
units.english: as says the text, beginning with the words ‘He rises out of Breath, he sets in Breath’, and concluding with the words ‘from a person knowing this does the sun rise and in him does he set Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: स होवाच किं मे वासो भविष्यतीति ।
units.english: He said‘What shall be my clothing?’they said‘Water’

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् वा एतद् अशिष्यन्तः पुरस्ताच् चोपरिष्टाच् चाद्भिः परिदधति ।
units.english: Hence it is that when going to eat, people cover it, before as well as after, with water

units.sanskrit: लम्भुको ह वासो भवति । अनग्नो ह भवति ॥
units.english: He thus becomes the obtainer of clothing and does not remain naked

units.sanskrit: पूर्ववदेव कल्पना ।
units.english: HeBreathsaidagain The conversation, as before, is purely imaginary

units.sanskrit: किं मे वासो भविष्यतीत्याप इति होचुर्वागादयः ।
units.english: ‘What shall be my clothing?Speech and the rest replied‘Water’

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्प्राणस्य वास आपस्तस्माद्वा एतदशिष्यन्तो भोक्तवन्तश्च ब्राह्मणा विद्वांस एतत्कुर्वन्ति । किम् । अद्भिर्वासस्थानीयाभिः पुरस्ताद्भोजनात्पूर्वमुपरिष्टाच्च भोजनादूर्ध्वं च परिदधति परिधानं कुर्वन्ति मुख्यस्य प्राणस्य लम्भुको सम्भनशीलो
units.english: Inasmuch as water is the clothing of Breath, when learned Brāhmaṇas are going to eat,ie while going to eat and after having eaten,they do this;what?Both before and after eating, they cover the Breath with water, which takes the place of clothing;ie they provide covering for the Principal Breath

units.sanskrit: वासो ह भवति । वाससो लब्धैव भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: He thus becomes the obtainer of clothing,ie obtains clothing;

units.sanskrit: अनग्नो ह भवति ।
units.english: and does not remain naked

units.sanskrit: वाससो लम्भुकत्वेनार्थसिद्धैवानग्नतेत्यनग्नो ह भवतीत्युत्तरीयवान्भवतीत्येतत् ।
units.english: As by obtaining clothing he would naturally cease to be naked, the addition of the phrase ‘does not remain naked’ should be understood to mean that he becomes supplied with the upper clothing also

units.sanskrit: भोक्ष्यमाणस्य भुक्तवतश्च यदाचमनं शुद्ध्यर्थं विज्ञातं तस्मिन्प्राणस्य वास इति दर्शनमात्रमिह विधीयते ।
units.english: The sipping of water that is done when one is going to eat and after one has eaten is known to be for the purpose of purification; hence what is said in the present text should be taken to mean only that the water thus sipped should be looked upon as the ‘clothing’ of Breath

units.sanskrit: अद्भिः परिदधतीति ना'चमनान्तरम् ।
units.english: The phrase ‘covers it up with water’ does not enjoin any other watersipping apart from the two wellknown ones

units.sanskrit: यथा लौकिकैः प्रामिभिरद्यमानमन्नं प्राणस्येति दर्शनमात्रं तद्वत्किं मे ऽन्नं किं मे वास इत्यादिप्रश्नप्रतिवचनयोस्तुल्यत्वात् । यद्याचमनमपूर्वं तादर्थ्येन क्रियते तदा कृम्याद्यन्नमपि प्राणस्य भक्ष्यत्वेन विहितं स्यात् ।
units.english: Just as when ordinary people eat food and it is said that ‘it is the food for Breath’, what is meant is only that the food should be looked upon as being for Breath The question and answer in both cases being similar‘What shall be my food?What shall be my clothing?’If a fresh watersipping were regarded as enjoined here directly for its own sake,as an independent act by itself then the statement of all food being for Breath would have to be regarded as an actual injunction, meaning that ‘all things should be eateneven insects etc’ which is absurd

units.sanskrit: तुल्ययोर्विज्ञानार्थयोः प्रस्नप्रतिवचनयोः प्रकरणस्य विज्ञानार्थत्वादर्धजरतीयो न्यायो न युक्तः कल्पयितुम् । यत्तु प्रसिद्धमाचमनं प्रायत्यार्थं प्राणस्यानग्नतार्थं च न भवतीत्युच्यते न तथा वयमाचमनमुभयार्थं ब्रूमः । किं तर्हि प्रायत्यार्थाचमनसाधनभूता आपः प्राणस्य वास इति दर्शनं चोद्यत इति ब्रूमः ।
units.english: looked uponas ‘food’ and ‘clothing and it would not be right to adopt the ‘half and half method’ of interpreting and taking the fresh statement, regarding food, as laying down the viewing of things in a certain way, and the second statement, regarding clothing, as an actual direct injunction of an independent watersipping As for the argument that the wellknown watersipping cannot serve both the purposesthat of purifying, and that of saving Breath from being nakedwe do not say that the watersipping is for both these purposes, What we do atsserts that the water that is used for the purificatory sipping should be looked upon as the ‘clothing’ for Breath,

units.sanskrit: तत्रा'चमनस्योभयार्थत्वप्रसङ्गदोषचोदनानुपपन्ना ।
units.english: So that the urging of the objection that ‘the watersipping cannot serve both purposes is highly unreasonable

units.sanskrit: वासोर्थ एवा'चमने तद्दर्शनं स्यादिति चेत् । न । वासोज्ञानार्थवाक्ये वासोर्थापूर्वाचमनविधाने तत्रानग्नतार्थत्वदृष्टिविधाने च वाक्यभेदः आचमनस्य तदर्थत्वमन्यार्थत्वं चेति । प्रमाणाभावात् ॥
units.english: as the text is for the purpose of making known what is the ‘clothing’and if this was taken as enjoining fresh watersipping for the providing of clothing,and there were also the other injunction of looking upon it as such,then this would involve syntactical splitand further, there is no authority for the view that the watersipping is for that purpose and also for another

units.sanskrit: तद् धैतत् सत्यकामो जाबालो गोश्रुतये वैयाघ्रपद्यायोक्त्वोवाच । यद्य् अप्य् एनच् छुष्काय स्थाणवे ब्रूयाज् जायेरन्न् एवास्मिञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
units.english: SatyakāmaJābāla, having expounded this to GośrutiVaiyāghrapadya, said‘If one were to say this to a dry stump, branches would shoot forth and leaves would sprout up from it’

units.sanskrit: तदेतत्प्राणदर्शनं स्तूयते ।
units.english: This philosophy of the Breath is now eulogised

units.sanskrit: कथम् । तद्धैतत्प्राणदर्शनं सत्यकामो जाबालो गोश्रुतये नाम्ना वैयाघ्रपद्याय व्याघ्रपदो ऽपत्यं वैयाघ्रपद्यस्तस्मै गोश्रुत्याख्यायोक्त्वोवाचान्यदपि
units.english: In what way?Thisphilosophy of the BreathSatyakāmaJābālahaving expounded to Gośruti by name,the son of Vyāghrapada, saidsomething more, in the shape of the following‘What was it that he said?’

units.sanskrit: वक्ष्यमाणं वचः । किं तदुवाचेत्याहयद्यपि शुष्काय स्थाणव एतद्दर्शनं ब्रूयात्प्राणविज्जायेरन्नुत्पद्येरन्नेवास्मिन्स्थाणौ शाखाः प्ररोहेयुश्च पलाशानि पत्रामि,
units.english: AnswerIf oneconversant with the Philosophy of the Breathwere to sayexpoundthis Philosophy of the Breathto a dry stump, branches would shoot forth, and leaves would sprout out;

units.sanskrit: किमु जीवते पुरुषाय ब्रूयादिति ॥
units.english: what would it not do to a living man?’

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि महज् जिगमिषेत्, अमावास्यायाम् दीक्षित्वा पौर्णमास्यां रात्रौ सर्वौषधस्य मन्थम् दधिमधुनोर् उपमथ्य ज्येष्ठाय श्रेष्ठाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे
units.english: If one desires to attain the Great, then, having become initiated on the Moonless Day, he should, on the night of the Fullmoon, stirup with curd and honey, the mash of all herbs, and then offerelibation of clarified butter into the fire, saying‘Svāhā to the Oldest and the Best’and throw the remnant into the Mash

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरं यदि महन्महत्त्वं जिगमिषेद्गन्तुमिच्छेन्महत्त्वं प्राप्तुं यदिकामयेतेत्यर्थः । तस्येदं कर्म विधीयते । महत्त्वे हि सति श्रीरुपनमते । श्रीमतो ह्यर्थप्राप्तं धनं ततः कर्मानुष्ठानं ततश्च देवयानं पितृयाणं वा पन्थानं प्रतिपत्स्यत इत्येतत्प्रयोजनमुररीकृत्य महत्त्वप्रेप्सोरिदं कर्म न
units.english: Now, after this, if one desire to attain the Greatie if one wishes to reach greatness,then, for him, the following rite is prescribedAs a matter of fact, when there is Greatness, Prosperity comes,and to the prosperous man, wealth comes as a matter of course;this enables him to perform Rites, and thence to pass on either to the path of the Divinities or to the path of the Fathers;it is with a view to this ulterior motive that the man desires greatness, and it is for this purpose that the Rite has been prescribed,not for one who desires merely the pleasures desired from the objects of sense

units.sanskrit: तस्यायं कालादिविधिरुच्यतेअमावास्यायां दीक्षित्वा दीक्षित इव भूमिशयनादिनियमं कृत्वा तपोरूपं सत्यवचनं ब्रह्मचर्यमित्यादिधर्मवान्भूत्वेत्यर्थः
units.english: For this person, the time and other details are prescribed as followsOn the Moonless Night, having become initiated,ie having kept, like the initiated person, such penances and observances as sleeping on the ground, telling the truth, celibacy and the like;it is not meant that he should perform all the detailed rites that have been prescribed for the formal Initiatory Rite;

units.sanskrit: न पुनर्दैक्षमेव कर्मजातं सर्वमुपादत्ते । अतद्विकारत्वान्मन्थाख्यस्य कर्मणः । उपसद्व्रतीइति श्रुत्यन्तरात्पयोमात्रभक्षमं च शुद्धिकारमं तप उपादत्ते ।
units.english: that such cannot be the meaning follows from the fact that the Rite of the Mash is not a ‘modification’ of the Initiatory Rite and it is only a Modification that takes in all the details of its prototype;in fact, according to another text to the effect that ‘He keeps the observances of the Upasad’, BṛhadāUpa the man in question has to keep the penance of living on milk only as a means of purification

units.sanskrit: पौर्णमास्यां रात्रौ कर्मा'रभते सर्वौषधस्य ग्राम्यारण्यानामोषधीनां यावच्छक्त्यल्पमल्पमुपादाय तद्वितुषीकृत्या'ममेव पिष्टं दधिमधुनोरौदुम्बरे कंसाकारे चमसाकारे वा पात्रे श्रुत्यन्तरात्प्रक्षिप्योपमथ्याग्रतः स्थापयित्वा ज्येष्ठाय श्रेष्ठाय स्वाहेत्यग्नावावसथ्य
units.english: On the night of the Fullmoon, he proceeds with the Rite Having collected, to the best of his capacity, small quantities of all the herbsboth cultivated and wild,having cleaned them of all chaff, he should make up a mash of all these without cooking them,and he should throw into it curd and honey,in a vessel made of Udumbara wood, shaped like Kaṃsa goblet or a Camasa cup, as laid down in another Vedic Text,and stir it up and keep it before himselfthen he should offer an oblation of clarified Butter

units.sanskrit: आज्यस्या'वापस्थाने हुत्वा स्रुवसंलग्नं मन्थे संपातमवनयेत्संस्रवमधः पातयेत् ॥ वसिष्ठाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ।
units.english: saying Svāhā’ to the Oldest and the Bestinto the Āvasathya Fire, on the spot prescribed for such offerings;and what may be left attached to the ladle should be thrown as Remnant into the Mash Saying ‘Svāhā to the Richest’, he should offer a libation of clarified Butter into the Fire and throw the remnant into the Mash

units.sanskrit: प्रतिष्ठायै स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् । संपदे स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ।
units.english: Saying ‘Svāhā’ to Firmness, he should offer a libation of charified Butter into the Fire and throw the remnant into the Mash Saying ‘Svāhā to Prosperity’, he should offer a libation of clarified Butter into the Fire and throw the remnant into the Mash

units.sanskrit: आयतनाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ॥
units.english: Saying ‘Svāhā to the Homa’, he should offer a libation into the Fire and throw the remnant into the Mash

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ।
units.english: The rest is as above

units.sanskrit: वसिष्ठाय प्रतिष्ठायै संपद आयतनाय स्वाहेति प्रत्येकं तथैव संपातमवनयेद्धुत्वा ॥
units.english: Having offered the libations ‘to the Richest’, to ‘Firmness’, ‘to Prosperity’ and ‘to the Homa’, he should throw the remnant, each time, into the Mash

units.sanskrit: अथ प्रतिसृप्याञ्जलौ मन्थम् आधाय जपति । अमो नामासि । अमा हि ते सर्वम् इदम् ।
units.english: Then, moving away and holding the Mash in his hands, he recites‘Thou art Ama by name, as all this rests with thee

units.sanskrit: स हि ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठो राजाधिपतिः ।
units.english: He is the Oldest and Best, the King and Sovereign

units.sanskrit: स मा ज्यैष्ठ्यं श्रैष्ठ्यं राज्यम् आधिपत्यं गमयतु । अहम् एवेदं सर्वम् असानीति ॥
units.english: May he lead me to the oldest age, to the best position, to kingship and to sovereignty! May be all this’

units.sanskrit: अथ प्रतिसृप्याग्नेरीषदपसृप्याञ्जलौ मन्थमाधाय जपतीमं मन्त्रम् । अमो नामास्यमा हि ते । अम इति प्राणस्य नाम । अन्नेन हि प्राणः प्राणिति देह इत्यतो मन्थद्रव्यं प्राणस्यान्नत्वात्प्राणत्वेन स्तूयते ऽमो नामासीति ।
units.english: Then moving away,having gone away a little, from the Fire,holding the Mash in his hands, he recites the following Mantra‘Amo nāmāsi amāhite etc, etc‘Ama’ is a name of Prāṇa Breath;it is through food that Breath functions in the body; hence the substance in the Mash, being the food for Breath, is eulogised as Breath itself‘thou art Ama by name’

units.sanskrit: कुतः । यतो ऽमा सह हि यस्मात्ते तव प्राणभूतस्य सर्वं समस्तं जगदिदमतः ।
units.english: How?Because all this rests with thee; ie because the whole of this world rests with thee as representing Breath

units.sanskrit: स हि प्राणभूतो मन्थो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठश्च ।
units.english: This Mash, being Breath, is both the Oldest and the Best;

units.sanskrit: अत एव च राजा दीप्तिमानधिपतिश्चाधिष्ठाय पालयिता सर्वस्य । समा मामपि मन्थः प्राणो ज्यैष्ठ्यादिगुणपूगमात्मनो गमयत्वहमेवेदं सर्वं जगदसानि भवनि प्राणवत् । इतिशब्दो मन्त्रपरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥
units.english: and for this reason, He is also the Kingeffulgentand Sovereignie the lord and protector of all;may hethe Mash representing Breath,lead me to the host of all his own qualities, in the shape of the oldest age and the rest; and may ,like Breathbe all thisin the world’The particle ‘iti’ indicates the end of the Mantra to be recited

units.sanskrit: अथ खल्व् एतयर्चा पच्छ आचामति । तत् सवितुर् वृणीमह इत्य् आचामति । वयं देवस्य भोजनम् इत्य् आचामति ।
units.english: Then he eats with this verse, foot by foot saying ‘We pray for that related to the Progenitor he eats;saying ‘We are the food of the;

units.sanskrit: तुरं भगस्य धीमहीति सर्वं पिबति । निर्णिज्य कंसं चमसं वा पश्चाद् अग्नेः संविशति । चर्मणि वा स्थण्डिले वा वाचंयमो ऽप्रसाहः ।
units.english: Deity’, he eats;saying ‘the best and the allsustaining’, he eats;saying ‘we quickly meditate upon the divine’, he drinks up allHaving washed the goblet or the cup, he lies down behind the fire, on a skin or on the ground, in silence, undisturbed

units.sanskrit: स यदि स्त्रियं पश्येत् समृद्धं कर्मेति विद्यात् ॥
units.english: If he should see a woman, he should know that his business has succeeded

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरं खल्वेतया वक्ष्यमाणयर्चा पच्छः पादश आचामति भक्षयति,
units.english: Then,after this,he eats with thisthe following verse, foot by foot;

units.sanskrit: मन्त्रस्यैकैकेन पादेनैकैकं ग्रासं भक्षयति ।
units.english: ie he eats one morsal with each quarter of the Mantra

units.sanskrit: तद्भोजनं सवितुः सर्वस्य प्रसवितुः । प्राणमादित्यं चैकीकृत्योच्यते ।
units.english: ThatEatingrelated to the Progenitorthe source of all,this is meant to include the Breath and the Sun together into one entity;

units.sanskrit: आदित्यस्य वृणीमहे प्रार्थयेमहि मन्थरूपम् ।
units.english: we pray for ask forthe Mash of the Sun;

units.sanskrit: येनान्नेन सावित्रेण भोजनेनोपभुक्तेन वयं सवितृस्वरूपापन्ना भवेमेत्यभिप्रायः । देवस्य सवितुरिति पूर्वेण सम्बन्धः ।
units.english: the sense being that ‘by eating this food related to the Sun, we shall attain the form of the Sun’‘Of the deity’,this is to be construed with ‘Savituḥ’ of the preceding quarter

units.sanskrit: श्रेष्ठं प्रशस्यतमं सर्वान्नेभ्यः सर्वधातमं सर्वस्य जगतो धारयितृतममतिशयेन विधातृतममिति वा । सर्वथा भोजनविशेषणम् ।
units.english: the best,the most superior of all foods,allsustainingsustaining the entire universe,very sustaining in its properties,all this qualifies ‘food’

units.sanskrit: भगस्य देवस्य सवितुः स्वरूपमिति शेषः ।
units.english: ‘Quicklyspeedilyof the divine, ie the form ofthe divinity, the Sun,we mediate upon’;

units.sanskrit: धीमहि चिन्तयेमहि विशिष्टभोजनेन संस्कृताः शुद्धात्मानः सन्त इत्यभिप्रायः । अथवा भगस्य श्रियः कारणं महत्त्वं प्राप्तुं कर्म कृतवन्तो वयं तद्धोमहि चिन्तयेमहीति सर्वं च मन्थलेपं पिबति निर्णिज्य प्रक्षाल्य कंसं कंसाकारं चमसं
units.english: ‘being embellished with the particular kind of food and having our souls purified’Or the meaning may be that ‘Having performed a Rite for the obtaining of that greatness which is a source of prosperity, we meditate upon it’Having said this, he drinks up all,ie all that remains of the Mash attached to the goblet

units.sanskrit: पीत्वा'चम्य पश्चादग्नेः प्राक्शिराः संविशति चर्मणि वाजिने स्थण्डिले केवलायां वा भूमौ । वाचंयमो वाग्यतः सन्नित्यर्थः । अप्रसाहो न प्रसह्यते नाभिभूयते स्त्र्याद्यनिष्टस्वप्नदर्शनेन यथा तथा संयतचित्तः सन्नित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Having washed the goblet or the cup,ie the vessel of Udumbara wood, shaped like the goblet or the cup,having drunk it off and washed his mouth’, he lies down behind the firewith his head towards the Easteither on a skin or on the bare ground,in silenceundisturbedie so peacefully as not to be disturbed by women or by evil dreams,with mind calm and collected;

units.sanskrit: स एवंभूतो यदि स्रियं पश्येत्स्वप्नेषु तदा विद्यात्समृद्धं ममेदं कर्मेति ॥
units.english: in this condition, if he should seeie dream ofa woman,then he should know that his business has succeeded

units.sanskrit: तद् एष श्लोकः ।
units.english: To this same effect there is the following verse

units.sanskrit: यदा कर्मसु काम्येषु स्त्रियं स्वप्नेषु पश्यति । समृद्धिं तत्र जानीयात् तस्मिन् स्वप्ननिदर्शने तस्मिन् स्वप्ननिदर्शने ॥
units.english: If during the performance of prospective Rites, one should see a woman in his dreams,he should recognise success,yea, in such dreamvision’

units.sanskrit: यदा कर्मसु काम्येषु कामार्थेषु स्रियं स्वप्नेषु स्वप्नदर्शनेषु स्वप्नकालेषु वा पश्यति समृद्धिं तत्र जानीयीत् । कर्मणां फलनिष्पत्तिर्भविष्यतीति जानीयादित्यर्थः । तस्मिन्स्त्र्यादिप्रशस्तस्वप्नदर्शने सतीत्यभिप्रायः । द्विरुक्तिः कर्मसमाप्त्यर्था ॥
units.english: To this same effect there is the following versemantratext‘If during the performance of prospective rites, one should see a woman,either during dreamvision, or at the time of sleepinghe should recognise success;that is, he should understand that the results desired of those Rites will surely be accomplished,in such dreamvision,ie, if he has had such excellent dreams as that of a woman

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Rite of the Mash End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: श्वेतकेतुर् हारुणेयः पञ्चालानां समितिम् एयाय ।
units.english: It is said that ŚvetaketuAruṇeya came to the Assembly of the Pancālas

units.sanskrit: तं ह प्रवाहणो जैवलिर् उवाच । कुमारानु त्वा अशिषत् पितेति ।
units.english: PravāhaṇaJaibali asked him‘Boy, has thy father taught thee?’‘Yes, Sir’

units.sanskrit: इत्यैतिह्यार्थः ।
units.english: ‘Ha’ indicates that the story is wellknown

units.sanskrit: तमागतवन्तं ह प्रवाहणो नामतो जीवलस्यापत्यं जैवलिरुवाचोक्तवान् । हे कुमारानु त्वा त्वामशिषदन्वसिषत्पिता । किमनुशिष्टस्त्वं पित्रेत्यर्थः । इत्युक्तः स आहानु ह्यनुशिष्टो ऽस्मि भगव इति सूचयन्नाह ॥
units.english: Śvetaketuby nameĀruṇeyathe son of Āruṇi who was the son of Aruṇacame to the Assembly of the Pāñcālacountry;when he came there, Pravāhaṇaby nameJaibalithe son of Jibalasaid‘O Boy, has thy father taught thee?’That is, hast thou been properly educated by thy father?’Being thus asked, the boy answered‘Yes, Sir,’ meaning thereby that ‘ have been properly educated’

units.sanskrit: वेत्थ यद् इतो ऽधि प्रजाः प्रयन्तीति । न भगव इति । वेत्थ यथा पुनर् आवर्तन्त इति ।
units.english: ‘Dost thou know where people go to from here?’‘No, Sir‘Dost thou know how they come back?’‘No, Sir?

units.sanskrit: न भगव इति । वेत्थ पथोर् देवयानस्य पितृयाणस्य च व्यावर्तना इति । न भगव इति ॥
units.english: ‘Dost thou know the diverging point between the two paths,the Path of Divinities and the Path of the Fathers?’‘No, Sir,’

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच यद्यनुशिष्टो ऽसि वेत्थ यदितो ऽस्माल्लोकादध्यूर्ध्वं यत्प्रजाः प्रयन्ति यद्गच्छन्ति तत्किं जानीष इत्यर्थः । न भगव इत्याहेतरो न जाने ऽहं तद्यत्पृच्छसि । एवं तर्हि वेत्थ जानीषे यथा येन प्रकारेण पुनरावर्तन्त इति । न भगव इति प्रत्याह । वेत्थ पथोर्मार्गयोः सहप्रयाणयोर्देवयानस्य पितृयाणस्य च व्यावर्तनमितरेतरवियोगस्थानं सह गच्छतामित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Pravāhaṇas aid to the Boy‘If thou hast been properly educated, dost thou know wherewhat upper regionspeople go to from herefrom this worldDost thou know this?’The other replied‘No, Sir, know not what you ask’‘Then, dost thou know howin what mannerthey come back?’‘No, Sir,’he answered ‘Dost thou know the diverging pointthat point from which they diverge, after having gone together at the startbetween the two paths, the path of the Divinities and the path of the Fathersfor people who proceed on those paths?’‘No sir,’

units.sanskrit: न भगव इति ॥ वेत्थ यथासौ लोको न संपूर्यत इति । न भगव इति । वेत्थ यथा पञ्चम्याम् आहुताव् आपः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति ।
units.english: ‘Dost thou know why that other region is not overfilled?’‘No, Sir,’‘Dost thou know how, at the fifth libation, the Water comes to be called Man?’‘Indeed, Sir, no’

units.sanskrit: नैव भगव इति ॥ वेत्था यथासौ लोकः पितृसम्बन्धी यं प्राप्य पुनरावर्तन्ते बहुभिः प्रयद्भिरपि येन कारमेन न सम्पूर्यत इति ।
units.english: ‘Dost thou know whyfor what reasonthat other worldconnected with the Fathersfrom where they come bach,is not overfilled with people going there?’‘No, sir,’he answered

units.sanskrit: वेत्थ यथा येन क्रमेण पञ्चम्यां पञ्चसंख्याकायामाहुतौ हुतायामाहुतिनिर्वृत्ता आहुतिसाधनाश्चा'पः पुरुषवचसः पुरुष इत्येवं वचो ऽभिधानं यासां हूयमानानां
units.english: ‘Dost thou know howby what processat the fifth libationat the offering of the libation which is fifth in number,the waterthat produced by the libation and also that which makes up the libation,comes to be called ‘man’;the water that forms the sixth libation and is offered as such comes to have ‘Puruṣa’ Man as its name;

units.sanskrit: क्रमेण षष्ठाहुतिभूतानां ताः पुरुषवचसः पुरुषशब्दवाच्या भवन्ति पुरुषाख्यां लभन्त इत्यर्थः । इत्युक्तो नैव भगव इत्याह ।
units.english: that is, they come to be expressed by the term ‘Man’,ie they attain this title of manThus questioned, the Boy replied‘Indeed, Sir, noI do not know anything of this’

units.sanskrit: अथानु किम् अनु शिष्ठो ऽवोचथा यो हीमानि न विद्यात् । कथं सो ऽनुशिष्टो ब्रुवीतेति । स हायस्तः पितुर् अर्धम् एयाय । तं होवाचाननुशिष्य वाव किल मा भगवान् अब्रवीद् अनु त्वाशिषम् इति ॥
units.english: ‘Then, why didst thou say thou hadst been properly educated? One who does not know these things,how could he declare himself to be properly educated?’Thus discomfited, he came over to his father’s place, and said to him‘Sir, without having educated me, you said you had educated me’

units.sanskrit: अथैवमज्ञः सन्किमनु कस्मात्त्वमनुशिष्टो ऽस्मीत्यवोचथा उक्तवानसि । यो हीमानि मया पृष्टान्यर्थजातानि न विद्यान्न विजानीत्यात्कथं स विद्वत्स्वनुशिष्टो ऽस्मीति ब्रुवीत । इत्येवं स श्वेतकेतुः राज्ञा'यस्त आयासितः सन्पितुरर्धं स्थानमेयाया'गतवांस्तं च पितुरमुवाचाननुशिष्यानुशासनमकृत्वैव मा मां किल भगवान्समावर्तनकाले ऽब्रवीदुक्तवाननु
units.english: ‘Thus, being wholly ignorant, why didst thou say that thou hadst been properly educated? One who does not know these thingsthat have questioned abouthow could he declare himselfin an assemblage of learned mento be properly educated?’Śvetaketu, being thus discomfitedquelledby the Kingcame over to his father’s place,and said to himto his father‘Without having educated mewithout having accomplished my educationyou saidat the time of my ‘Return’ completion of studyyou had educated me?

units.sanskrit: पञ्च मा राजन्यबन्धुः प्रश्नान् अप्राक्षीत् । तेषां नैकंचनाशकं विवक्तुम् इति ।
units.english: ‘That fellow of a Kṣattriya asked me five questions, and could not answer any one of them’The father said‘As you told me these questions, myself do not know any one of them;

units.sanskrit: यद्य् अहम् इमान् अवेदिष्यं कथं ते नावक्ष्यम् इति ॥
units.english: if had known these, why should not have told you?’

units.sanskrit: स ह गौतमो राज्ञो ऽर्धम् एयाय ।
units.english: Then Gautama came over to the King’s place;

units.sanskrit: तस्मै ह प्राप्तायार्हां चकार ।
units.english: and when he reached there, the King received him with due honours

units.sanskrit: स ह प्रातः सभाग उदेयाय ।
units.english: In the morning he went over to the King when he was in the Assembly

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच । मानुषस्य भगवन् गौतम वित्तस्य वरं वृणीथा इति । स होवाच । तवैव राजन् मानुषं वित्तम् ।
units.english: The King said‘O revered Gautama, please ask for some such boon as pertains to wealth connected with human beings’He replied‘O King, let the wealth connected with human beings rest with thyself;

units.sanskrit: याम् एव कुमारस्यान्ते वाचम् अभाषथास् ताम् एव मे ब्रूहीति ।
units.english: speak to me the same speech that thou spokest to my boy’

units.sanskrit: स ह कृच्छ्री बभूव ॥
units.english: He became perturbed

units.sanskrit: यतः पञ्च पञ्चसंख्याकान्प्रश्नान्राजन्यबन्धू राजान्या बन्धवो ऽस्येति राजन्यबन्धुः स्वयं दुर्वृत्त इत्यर्थः । अप्राक्षीत्पृष्टवांस्तेषां प्रश्नानां नैकञ्चनैकमपि नाशकं न शक्तवानहं विवक्तुं विशेषेणार्थतो निर्णेतुमित्यर्थः । स होवाच पिता यथा मा मां वत्स त्वं तदा'गतमात्र एवैतान्प्रश्नानवद उक्तवानसि तेषां नैकञ्चनाशकं विवक्तुमिति तथा मां जानीहि,
units.english: ‘Because that fellow of a kṣattriyaone who has Ksattriyas for his relatives, but is himself ill behaved, he is only a fellow of a Kṣattriyi,asked me five questions,questions five in number,and of these questions, could not answer any one,could not determine what the sense of it was’The father said‘My Boy, as you told me these questionsimmediately on your arrival, did not know any one of them,that is, know me also to be ignorant;

units.sanskrit: त्वदीयाज्ञानेन लिङ्गेन मम तद्विषयमज्ञानं जानीहीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: from the index of your own ignorance you may infer my ignorance also

units.sanskrit: कथं, यथाहमेषां प्रश्नानामेकञ्चनैकमपि न वेद न जान इति यथा त्वमेवाङ्गैतान्प्रश्नान्न जानीषे तथाहमप्येतान्न जान इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: How?Because of all these questions, / do not know any one; that is, just as, my dear, you do not know these, so too do not know these;

units.sanskrit: अतो मय्यन्यथाभावो न कर्तव्यः ।
units.english: you should not think of me otherwise

units.sanskrit: कुत एतदेवं यतो न जाने यद्यहमिमान्प्रश्नानवेदिष्यं विदितवानस्मि कथं ते तुभ्यं प्रियाय पुत्राय समावर्तनकाले पुरा नावक्ष्यं नोक्तवानस्मीत्युक्त्वा स ह गोत्रतो
units.english: As to how it is to be understood that do not know the questions,If had known these questionswhy should not have told youmy loved son, at the time of your ‘Return’ completion of study?’Having said this, he, Gautama,of the Gotra of Gautamacame over to the king’s placethe place of Jaibali

units.sanskrit: राज्ञो जैवलेरर्धं स्थानमेयाय गतवान् ।
units.english: and next day, in the morning he came over to the King where he was in the Assembly

units.sanskrit: भजनं भागः पूजा सेवा सह भागेन वर्तमानो वा सभागः पूज्यमानो ऽन्यैः स्वयं गौतम उदेयाय राजानमुद्गतवान् । तं होवाच गौतमं राजा मानुषस्य भगवन्गौतम मनुष्यसम्बन्धिनो वित्तस्य ग्रामादेर्वरं वरणीयं कामं वृणीथाः प्रार्थयेथाः । स होवाच गौतमस्तवैव तिष्ठतु राजन्मानुषं वित्तम् ।
units.english: or the word ‘sabhāga’ may stand for ‘sabhāgaḥ’ as qualifying Gautama, ,’the meaning being’ Gautama, who was duly worshipped, honoured, by the other peoplein the Assembly, came to the King’To Gautama, the King said‘O revered Gautama, please ask for some such boonfulfilment of such desire,as pertains to wealthsuch as landed property and the like,connected with human beings’He, Gautamasaid O King, let the wealth connected with human beings rest with thyself;

units.sanskrit: यामेव कुमारस्य मम पुत्रस्यान्ते समीपे वाचं पञ्चप्रश्नलक्षणामभाषथा उक्तवानसि तामेव वाचं मे मह्यं ब्रूहि कथयेत्युक्तो गौतमेन
units.english: speak to me the same speechconsisting of true questionsthou spokest to my boymy son’Being thus addressed by Gautama, the King became perturbed, perplexedas to how he could do what he was asked to do

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच । यथा मा त्वं गौतमावदः । यथेयं न प्राक् त्वत्तः पुरा विद्या ब्राह्मणान् गच्छति ।
units.english: He commanded him‘Stay here for a long time’ Then he said‘As regards what you said to me, O, Gautama, before you, this philosophy never went to Brāhmaṇas;

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् उ सर्वेषु लोकेषु क्षत्रस्यैव प्रशासनम् अभूद् इति । तस्मै होवाच ॥
units.english: it is for this reason that, among all people, it was only with the Kṣattriya that the teaching of this rested’Then he spoke

units.sanskrit: स ह कृच्छ्रीभूतो ऽप्रत्याख्येयं ब्राह्मणं मन्वानो न्यायेन विद्या वक्तव्येति मत्वा तं ह गौतमं चिरं दीर्घकालं वसेत्येवमाज्ञापयाञ्चकारा'ज्ञप्तवान्
units.english: thinking that the request of the Brāhmaṇa could not be denied and the philosophy must be expounded to him, commanded orderedhimGautama‘Stay here for a long time’Inas much as the King had, at first, declined to accede to the Brāhmaṇa’s request, and subsequently ordered him to stay for a long time,he apologises to the Brāhmaṇa, explaining the reason for his conduct

units.sanskrit: मे ब्रूहीत्यज्ञानात्तेन त्वं जानीहि । तत्रास्ति वक्तव्यं यथा येन प्रकारेणेयं विद्या प्राक्त्वत्तो ब्राह्मणान्न गच्छति न गतवती, न च ब्राह्मणा अनया विद्ययानुशासितवन्तः, तथैतत्प्रसिद्धं लोके यतस्तस्मादु पुरा पूर्वं सर्वेषु लोकेषु क्षत्त्रस्यैव क्षत्त्रजातेरेवानया विद्यया प्रशासनं प्रशास्तृत्वं शिष्यामामभूद्बभूव
units.english: Hethe Kingsaid,‘Though you are a Brāhmaṇa knowing all philosophies and sciences,as regards what you said to me, asking me to expound to you the speech propounding the philosophy,because you did not know it,know now that there is something to be said on this subject, as to how, before you, this philosophy never went to Brāhmaṇas,and the Brāhmaṇas never taught this philosophy,this is a fact wellknown among the people;and it is for this reason that, in former days, among all people it was only with the Kṣattriyawith persons belonging to the Kṣattriya castethat the teaching of this instructing pupils in this sciencerested uptil now;

units.sanskrit: क्षत्त्रियपरम्परयैवेयं विद्यतावन्तं कालमागता ।
units.english: this Philosophy has been handed down by unspoken tradition among Kṣattriyas only;

units.sanskrit: तथाप्यहमेतां तुभ्यं वक्ष्यामि च्वत्सम्प्रदानादूर्ध्वं ब्राह्मणान्गमिष्यति ।
units.english: and yet am going to expound it to you; and after it has been imparted to you, it will go to the Brāhmaṇas, Thus then, what said to youfor that you will please pardon me

units.sanskrit: अतो मया यदुक्तं तत्क्षन्तुमर्हसीत्युक्त्वा तस्मै होवाच विद्यां राजा ॥
units.english: Having said this, he spoke to himthe King expounded to him the philosophy

units.sanskrit: अहर् अर्चिः ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पञ्चम्यामाहुतावाप इत्ययं प्रश्नः प्राथम्येनापाक्रियते ।
units.english: First of all, the Text disposes of the question as to the Water coming to be called ‘man’ at the fifth libation;

units.sanskrit: तदपाकरणमन्वितरेषामपाकरणमनुकूलं भवेदिति ।
units.english: because after this has been disposed of, the disposal of the other questions would be easier

units.sanskrit: अग्निहोत्राहुत्योः कार्यारम्भो यः स उक्तो वाजसनेयके । तं प्रति प्रस्नाःउत्क्रान्तिराहुत्योर्गतिः प्रतिष्ठा तृप्तिः पुनरावृत्तिर्लोकं प्रत्युत्थायी इति । तेषां चापाकरणमुक्तं तत्रैवते वा एते आहुती हुते उत्क्रामतस्ते अन्तरिक्षमाविशतस्ते
units.english: The initial proceedings of the two Agnihotralibations have been thus described in the Vājasaneyaka Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa ‘There are these questions raised in regard to the stages of the libations Starting up of the libations, from this world, Movement towards the other world, Resting of the libations, when they have reached the other world, Satisfaction on resting in their own substratum, Returning to this world, and Rising of man towards this world’The answers too to these questions have been supplied in the same text, as follows‘These two libations, on being offered, start up ; then they enter the sky;

units.sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षमेवा'हवनीयं कुर्वाते वायुं समिधं मरीचीरेव शुक्लामाहुतिं ते अन्तरिक्षं तर्पयतस्ते तत उत्क्रामत इत्याद्येवमेव पूर्ववद्दिवं तर्पयतस्ते तत आवर्तेते ।
units.english: they make the sky itself the Āhavanīya fire the locus, the Resting place, of the libations,they make Air the fuel, and the Rays, the white libation; they bring satisfaction to the sky;thence they start up, and as before, they bring satisfaction to Heaven;

units.sanskrit: इमामाविश्य तर्पयित्वा पुरुषमाविशतः । ततः स्रियमाविश्य लोकं प्रत्युत्थाया भवतिइति ।
units.english: then they return and entering this world, and having brought satisfaction, they enter the man;thence entering the woman,it comes to rise towards the world’[NoteThe libations meant here are the Apūrva, the transcendental potencies created by the man’s past deeds;

units.sanskrit: तत्राग्निहोत्राहुत्योः कार्यारम्भमात्रमेवंप्रकारं भवतीत्युक्ताम ।
units.english: etc, etc,says Anandagiri] In this text of the Śatapatha, what has been declared is only the process of the two libations;

units.sanskrit: इह तु तं कार्यारम्भमग्नि होत्रापूर्वविपरिणामलक्षणं पञ्चधा प्रविभज्याग्नित्वेनोपासनमुत्तरमार्गप्रतिपत्तिसाधनं विधित्सन्नाहअसौ
units.english: while in the present text, the said process, consisting of the function of the transcendental potency set up by the Agnihotra, is divided into five partswith a view to laying down the meditation of the said process as Fire, as leading to the attainment of the Northern Path

units.sanskrit: वाव लोको गौतमाग्निरित्यादि ।
units.english: ‘That world, O, Gautama, is the Fire;

units.sanskrit: इह सायंप्रातरग्निहोत्राहुती हुते पय आदिसाधने श्रद्धापुरःसरे आहवनीयाग्निसमिद्धूमार्चिरङ्गारविस्फुलिङ्गभाविते कर्त्रादिकारकभाविते चान्तरिक्षक्रमेणोत्क्रम्य द्युलोकं प्रविशन्त्यौ सूक्ष्मभूते अप्समवायित्वादप्शब्दवाच्ये श्रद्धाहेतुत्वाच्च श्रद्धाशब्दवाच्ये तयोरधिकरणो ऽग्निरन्यच्च तत्सम्बन्धं समिदादीत्युच्यते ।
units.english: That world, O Gautama, etc, etc,When the evening and morning libations of the Agnihotra have been offered,with such accessories as milk and the like,with due faith,fully equipped with the Āhavanīya Fire along with its fuel, smoke, flame, embers and sparks,and accomplished by such active agencies as those of the Doer and the rest,they enter the Heavenly Region in their subtle form,and are spoken of as ‘water on the ground of subsisting in Fire,and also spoken of as ‘faith’, on the ground of their originating in faith;the locus of these libations is the Fire, and the other details relating to it are spoken of as ‘fuel’ and the rest

units.sanskrit: या चासावग्न्यादिभावना'हुत्योः सापि तथैव निर्दिश्यते ।
units.english: The meditation also of the two libations as ‘fire’ and the rest, is indicated in the same manner

units.sanskrit: असौ वाव लोको ऽग्निर्हे गौतम यथाग्निहोत्राधिकरणमाहवनीय इह । तस्याग्नेर्घुलोकाख्यस्या'दित्य एव समित्तेन हीद्धो ऽसौ लोको दीप्यते । अतः समिन्धनात्समिदादित्यः ।
units.english: That world, O Gautama, is the fire, the locus of the libationjust as, O Gautama, in this world at the performance of the Agnihotra the Āhavanīya Fire is the locus of the libation;of this ‘fire’ named the ‘Heavenly Region’, the Sun is the ‘fuel’,because it is only as illumined by the Sun that the other world shines,hence, on account of this flaring up, the Sun is the samidh, ‘Fuel’

units.sanskrit: रश्मयो धूमस्तदुत्थानात्, समिधो हि धूम उत्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: The Rays are the ‘smoke’,because they rise from the Sun, as smoke rises from the fuel;the day is the ‘Flame’

units.sanskrit: अहरर्चिः प्रकाशसामान्यात्, आदित्यकार्यत्वाच्च चन्द्रमा अङ्गाराः ।
units.english: because both have the common character of being bright and being brought about by the Sun;the Moon is the ‘embers’because it appears on the cessation of the day;

units.sanskrit: अर्चिषा हि प्रशमे ऽङ्गारा अभिव्यज्यन्ते । नक्षत्राणि विस्फुलिङ्गाश्चन्द्रमसो ऽवयवा इव विप्रकीर्णत्वसामान्यात् ॥
units.english: just as it is on the cessation of the flame that embers become visibleThe Stars are the ‘sparks’,they are like parts of the moon, as sparks are of the embers, and also both have the common character of being besprinkled about

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवाः श्रद्धां जुह्वति ।
units.english: ‘In this Fire, the Deities pour the libation of Faith;

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेः सोमो राजा संभवति ॥
units.english: and from this libation comes out King Soma’

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नेतस्मिन्यथोक्तलक्षणे ऽग्नौ देवा यजमानप्राणा अग्न्यादिरूपा अधिदैवतम् । श्रद्धामग्निहोत्राहुतिपरिणामावस्थारूपाः सूक्ष्मा आपः श्रद्धाभाविताः श्रद्धा उच्यन्ते ।
units.english: In this fireas described above,the deities,ie the sacrificer’s ‘Breaths’, in the form of Fire and the rest, from the viewpoint of the Deities,pour the libation of Faith;the subtle elements of Water, in the form of the outcome of the Agnihotralibations, which originated in Faith,are what are called ‘faith’ in the present context;

units.sanskrit: पञ्चम्यामाहुतावापः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तिइत्यपां होम्यतया प्रश्ने श्रुतत्वात् ।
units.english: that this is so is also indicated by the fact that water has been spoken of as a substance to be offered into the fire, in the question relating to ‘Water coming to be called Man at the fifth libation’;

units.sanskrit: श्रद्धा वा आपः श्रद्धामेवा'रभ्य प्रणीय प्रचरतिइति च विज्ञायते । तां श्रद्धामब्रूपां जुह्वाति ।
units.english: and it is also learnt from other texts that ‘Faith indeed is water, they begin with Faith and then proceed’This Faith, in the form of water, the Deities pour as libation into the Fire

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेः सोमो राजापां श्रद्धाशब्दवाच्यानां द्युलोकाग्नौ हुतानां परिणामः सोमो राजा सम्भवति ।
units.english: Out of this libation, comes out King Soma;the subtle element of water, subsisting in the Agnihotralibations, spoken of as ‘faith enters the Heavenly Regions, produces their effect in the shape of the Moon, as the result of the two Agnihotralibations;

units.sanskrit: यथर्ग्वेदादिपुष्परसा ऋगादिमधुकरोपनीतास्त आदित्ये यश आदिकार्यं रोहितादिरूपलक्षणमारभन्त इत्युक्तं तथेमा अग्निहोत्राहुतिसमवायिन्यः सूक्ष्माः श्रद्धाशब्दवाच्या आपो द्युलोकमनुप्रविश्य चान्द्रं कार्यमारभन्ते फलरूपमग्निहोत्राहुत्योः । यजमानाश्च तत्कर्तार आहुतिमया आहुतिभावनाभाविता आहुतिरूपेण कर्मणा'कृष्टाः श्रद्धाप्समवायुनो द्युलोकमनुप्रविश्य भवन्ति ।
units.english: just as in the earlier Discourses of the Upaniṣad it has been described thathe Essences of the flowers in the shape of Ṛk and other Vedas, brought up by the Bees in the shape of the Ṛk verse and the rest, produce in the Sun such effects as Fame and the rest, in the shape of the Red and other colours,As for the sacrificers, the performers of the act of Agnihotra become resolved into the libations, being entirely absorbed in the contemplation of the libationsthey become drawn in by the act in the shape of the Libations and subsisting in Faith, they enter the Heavenly Region and become Soma, It was for this purpose that they poured the Agnihotralibations

units.sanskrit: अत्र त्वाहुतिपरिणाम एव पञ्चाग्निसम्बन्धक्रमेण प्राधान्येन विवक्षित उपासनार्थं न यजमानानां गतिः ।
units.english: What is meant to be taught here primarily is the evolution of the Libation in the order of the Five Fires,for the purposes of meditation; and the progress of the sacrificers does not form the main subject of the teaching

units.sanskrit: तां त्वविदुषां धूमादिक्रमेणोत्तरत्र वक्ष्यति विदुषां चोत्तरां विद्याकृताम् ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: This latter subject is going to be expounded later on, where it will be shown that ignorant persons go up by the path leading through smoke etc, and the wise ones go up by the Northern Path, through the influence of their knowledge End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पर्जन्यो वाव गौतमाग्निः ।
units.english: The Deity Parjanya, O Gautama, is the Fire;

units.sanskrit: तस्य वायुर् एव समित् । अभ्रं धूमः । विद्युद् अर्चिः । अशनिर् अङ्गाराः ।
units.english: of that Air is the ‘Fuel’, the Cloud is the ‘Soma the Lightning is the ‘Flame’, the Thunderbolt is the ‘Embers’, and the Thunderings are the ‘Sparks

units.sanskrit: द्वितीयहोमपर्यायार्थमाहपर्जन्यो वाव पर्जन्य एव गौतमाग्निः पर्जन्यो नाम वृष्ट्युपकरणाभिमानी देवताविशेषः ।
units.english: The Text now states the signification of the second state of the Libation?The Deity Parjanya, O Gautama, is FireParjanya is the Deity presiding over the accessories of rainfall

units.sanskrit: तस्य वायुरेव समित् ।
units.english: Of that Fire, the Air is the fuel;

units.sanskrit: वायुना हि पर्जन्यो ऽग्निः समिध्यते । पुरोवातादिप्राबल्ये वृष्टिदर्शनात् ।
units.english: as it is by Air that the Fire of Parjanya is enflamed; this is clear from the fact that Rain is found to follow upon a preceding wind

units.sanskrit: अभ्रं धूमो धूमकार्यत्वाद्धूमवच्च लक्ष्यमाणत्वात् ।
units.english: he Cloud is the smoke,because it is a product of smoke and also because it appears like smoke

units.sanskrit: प्रकाशसामान्यात् । अशनिरङ्गाराः ।
units.english: Lightning is the Flame,because both have the common properly of brightness

units.sanskrit: ह्रादुनयो विस्फुलिङ्गाः । ह्रादुनयो गर्जितशब्दाः ।
units.english: The Thunderings are the Sparks, the term ‘thunderings’ stands for the rumblings of thunder

units.sanskrit: मेघानां विप्रकीर्णत्वसमान्यात् ॥
units.english: the thunderings are sparks because both equally are spread over the clouds

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवाः सोमं राजानं जुह्वति ।
units.english: Into this fire the Deities offer king Soma;

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेर् वर्षं संभवति ॥
units.english: and from this libation comes Rain

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नेतस्मिन्नग्नौ देवाः पूर्ववत्सोमं राजानं जुह्वति ।
units.english: As before,into this fire the deities offer king Soma;

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेर्वर्षं सम्भवति ।
units.english: and from this libation comes rain

units.sanskrit: श्रद्धाख्या आपः सोमाकारणपरिणता द्वितीये पर्याये पर्जन्याग्निं प्राप्य वृष्टित्वेन परिणमन्ते ॥
units.english: Thus the water named ‘faith’ having as the result of the first libation developed into the form of Soma, reaches the second stage, the ParjanyaFire, and develops into Rain

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य पञ्चमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पृथिवी वाव गौतमाग्निः ।
units.english: The Earth, O Gautama, is the Fire;

units.sanskrit: तस्याः सम्वत्सर एव समित् ।
units.english: of that, the Year is the Fuel;

units.sanskrit: आकाशो धूमः ।
units.english: Ākāśa is the Smoke;

units.sanskrit: रात्रिर् अर्चिः ।
units.english: Night is the Flame;

units.sanskrit: दिशो ऽङ्गाराः । अवान्तरदिशो विस्फुलिङ्गाः ॥
units.english: the Quarters are the Embers, and the Intermediate Quarters are the Sparks

units.sanskrit: पृथिवी वाव गौतमाग्निरित्यादि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: The Earth, O Gautama, is the Fire etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: तस्याः पृथिव्याख्यस्याग्नेः संवत्सर एव समित् । संवत्सरेण हि कालेन समिद्धा पृथिवी व्रीह्यादिनिष्पत्तये भवति ।
units.english: Of thatFire named ‘Earth’the Year is the Fuel; it is only after developing throughout the year that the Earth becomes capable of producing Vrīhi and other grains

units.sanskrit: आकाशो धूमः,
units.english: Ākāśa is the Smoke;

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्या इवोत्थित आकाशो दृश्यते । यथाग्नेर्धूमः ।
units.english: because the Ākāśa appears to be rising out of the Earth just as smoke rises out of the Fire

units.sanskrit: रात्रिरर्चिः पृथिव्या ह्यप्रकाशात्मिकाया अनुरूपा रात्रिः ।
units.english: Night is the Flame; as the Night resembles the Earth in not consisting of light, both being of the form of Darkness;

units.sanskrit: अग्नेरिवानुरूपमर्चिः ।
units.english: just as the Flame resembles Fire in point of brightness

units.sanskrit: दिशो ऽङ्गारा उपशान्तत्वसामान्यात् । एवान्तरदिशो विस्फुलिङ्गाः क्षुद्रत्वसामान्यात् ॥
units.english: The Quarters are the Embers, on the ground of the common character of being calm The Inter mediate Quarters are the sparks,because both are insignificant

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा वर्षं जुह्वति । तस्या आहुतेर् अन्नं संभवति ॥
units.english: In that Fire, the Deities offer Rain; out of that libation comes Food In that Fire etc, etc,as before

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेरन्नं व्रीहियवादि सम्भवति ॥
units.english: Out of this libation comes Food,in the shape of Vrīhi and other grains

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य षष्ठः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पुरुषो वाव गौतमाग्निः । तस्य वाग् एव समित् । प्राणो धूमः । जिह्वार्चिः ।
units.english: ‘The Man, O Gautama, is the Fire,of that, Speech is the Fuel,Breath, the Smoke,Tongue, the Flame,Eye, the Embers and Ear, the Sparks’

units.sanskrit: पुरुषो वाव गौतमाग्निः ।
units.english: The Man, O Gautama, is the Fire;

units.sanskrit: तस्य वागेव समित् ।
units.english: of that Speech is the Fuel;

units.sanskrit: वाचा हि मुखेन समिध्यते पुरुषो न मूकः ।
units.english: because it is by Speech that the man becomes bright in his face; a dumb person can never be so bright

units.sanskrit: प्राणो धूमो धूम इव मुखान्निर्गमनात् । जिह्वार्चिर्लोहितत्वात् ।
units.english: Breath is the smoke; because Breath goes out of the mouth, just as smoke goes out of the Fire, Tongue is the Flame,because it is red

units.sanskrit: चक्षुरङ्गारा भास आश्रयत्वात् ।
units.english: the Eye is the Embers; because both contain light

units.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं विस्फुलिङ्गाः ।
units.english: Ear is the Sparks

units.sanskrit: विप्रकीर्णत्वसाम्यात् ॥
units.english: because both are equally scattered about

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा अन्नं जुह्वति ।
units.english: In that Fire, the Deities offer Food;

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेर् रेतः सम्भवति ॥
units.english: out of that libation is produced the Semen

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ।
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: अन्नं जुह्वति व्रीह्यादिसंस्कृतम् ।
units.english: They offer food,in the form of Vrīhi and other grains duly embellished and refined

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुते रेतः सम्भवति ॥
units.english: Out of that libation Semen is produced

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य सप्तमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: योषा वाव गौतमाग्निः ।
units.english: ‘The Woman, O, Gautama, is the Fire;

units.sanskrit: यद् उपमन्त्रयते स धूमः । योनिर् अर्चिः । यद् अन्तः करोति ते ऽङ्गाराः ।
units.english: of that the Organ is the Fuel,the Confabulation, the Smoke,the Vagina, the Flame,the Penetration is the Embers,the Raptures, the Sparks’

units.sanskrit: योषा वाव गौतमाग्निः ।
units.english: The Woman, O Gautama, is the Fire

units.sanskrit: तस्या उपस्थ एव समित् ।
units.english: Of that, the Organ is the Fuel;

units.sanskrit: तेन हि सा पुत्राद्युत्पादनाय समिध्यते । यदुपमन्त्रयते स धूमः । स्रीसम्भवादुपमन्त्रणस्य ।
units.english: because it is by the organ that fire is lighted for the purpose of procreation The Confabulation is the Smoke because the Confabulation proceeds from the Woman just as smoke proceeds from the fire

units.sanskrit: योनिरर्चिर्लोहितत्वात् ।
units.english: because both are red

units.sanskrit: यदन्तः करोति ते ऽङ्गारा अग्निसम्बन्धात् ।
units.english: The Penetration is the Embers,because of its connection with Fire

units.sanskrit: अभिनन्दाः सुखलवा विस्फुलिङ्गाः क्षुद्रत्वात् ॥
units.english: The Rapturesie, the ripples of pleasureare the Sparks;because they are small

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा रेतो जुह्वति ।
units.english: ‘Into this Fire, the Deities offer Semen;

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेर् गर्भः संभवति ॥
units.english: and out of that libation is born the embryo’

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नेतस्मिन्नग्नौ देवा रेतो जुह्वति ।
units.english: Into this Fire, the Deities offer Semen;

units.sanskrit: तस्या आहुतेर्गर्भः सम्भवतीति ।
units.english: out of that libation is produced the Embryo

units.sanskrit: एवं श्रद्धासोमवर्षान्नरेतोहवनपर्यायक्रमेणा'प एव गर्भीभूतास्ताः ।
units.english: Thus, through the gradual stages of the libation, Faith, Soma, Rain, Food, and Semen,the water has become the Embryo

units.sanskrit: तत्रापामाहुतिसमवायित्वात्प्राधान्यविवक्षा'पः पञ्चम्यामाहुतौ पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति ।
units.english: And, inasmuch as Water forms a constituent of the libation, it is spoken of as the most important of all,hence the statement that ‘At the fifth libation, Water comes to be called Man’

units.sanskrit: न त्वाप एव केवलाः सोमादिकार्यमारभन्ते । न चा'पो ऽत्रिवृत्कृताः सन्तीति ।
units.english: Yet it is not Water alone out of which Soma and the other Products are produced;nor again does Water exist, except in its tripartite constitution;

units.sanskrit: त्रिवृत्कृतत्वे ऽपि विशेषसंज्ञालाभो दृष्टः पृथिवीयमिमा आपो ऽयमग्निरित्यन्यतमबाहुल्यनिमित्तः ।
units.english: even in the tripartite constitution, which applies to all the three Earth, Water and Fire, which are compounds formed of themselves, we have found special names applied,such as ‘this is Earth’, ‘this is Water, ‘this is Fire’,on the basis of one or the other of the three forming the predominant factor

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्समुदितान्येव भूतान्यब्बाहुल्यात्कर्मसमवायीनि सोमादिकार्यारम्भकाण्याप इत्युच्यन्ते ।
units.english: A compound in which the proportion of Earthparticles is larger than that of Water or Fire, is named Earth, It is for this reason that all the three elementary substances compounded together enter into the performance of Rites only when bearing a larger proportion of waterparticles, and become productive of Soma and other products;and it is on this account that they are spoken of by the common name of ‘Fire

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते च द्रवबाहुल्यं सोमवृष्ट्यन्नरेतोदेहेषु ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, we actually perceive an excess of fluids in the constitution of Soma, Rain, Food, Semen and Body;

units.sanskrit: बहुद्रवं च शरीरं यद्यपि पार्थिवम् ।
units.english: the Body, though apparently made up of Earth, abounds in fluids

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्याष्टमः खण्डः
units.english: Thus it is that when the fifth libation has been offered Water, in the shape of Semen, becomes the Embryo

units.sanskrit: इति तु पञ्चम्याम् आहुताव् आपः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति । स उल्बावृतो गर्भो दश वा नव वा मासान् अन्तः शयित्वा यावद् वाथ जायते ॥
units.english: End of Section of Discourse ‘Thus, at the fifth libation, Water comes to be called ManThat foetus enclosed in the membrane, having lain within for ten or nine months, more or less, becomes born’

units.sanskrit: इति त्वेवं तु पञ्चम्यामाहुतावापः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति व्याख्यात एकः प्रश्नः । यत्तु द्युलोकादिमां प्रत्यावृत्तयोराहुत्यो पृथिवीं पुरुषं स्रियं क्रमेणा'विश्य लोकं प्रत्युत्थायी भवतीति वाजसनेयक उक्तं तत्प्रासङ्गिकमिहोच्यते
units.english: Thus it is that at the fifth libation, Water comes to be called ‘Man’;thus one of the five questions put by the King has been answered;now this subject has been introduced in the Śathapatha Brāhmaṇa, in the following words‘When the two libations return to this world from the Heavenly Region, they enter the Earth, the Man, the Woman,in this order, it comes to rise towards the world’ See Bhāṣya Introductory to VivI;

units.sanskrit: इह च प्रथमे प्रश्न उक्तं वेत्थ यदितो ऽधि प्रजाः प्रयन्तीति । तस्य चायमुपक्रमः ।
units.english: this subject was introduced here only by the way,in the first question put here, it was asked‘Dost thou know where people go from here?’ See Viii and it is this question that begins to be dealt with now

units.sanskrit: स गर्भो ऽपां पञ्चमः परिणामविशेष आहुतिकर्मसमवायिनीनां श्रद्धाशब्दवाच्यानामुल्बावृत उल्बेन जरायुणा'वृतो वेष्टितो दश वा नव वा मासानन्तर्मातुः कुक्षौ शयित्वा यावद्वा यावता कालेन न्यूनेनातिरिक्तेन वाथानन्तरं जायते ।
units.english: That foetus,the fifth evolute of Water as constituting the act of libation and as known by the name ‘Faith’,enclosed in surrounded bythe membranefor ten or nine months, or for such timemore or lessas may be necessaryhaving lain withinthe mother’s womb,becomes born, ‘Enclosed in the membrane’ and such qualifications have been added for the purpose of creating a feeling of disgust against wordly existence;

units.sanskrit: उल्बावृत इत्यादि वैराग्यहेतोरिदमुच्यते । कष्टं हि मातुः कुक्षौ मूत्रपुरीषवातपित्तश्लेष्मादिपूर्णे तदनुलिप्तस्य गर्भस्योल्बाशुचिपटावृतस्य लोहितरेतो ऽशुचिबीजस्य मातुरशितपीतरसानुप्रवेशेन विवर्धमानस्य निरुद्धशक्तिबलवीर्यतेजःप्रज्ञाचेष्टस्य शयनम् ।
units.english: the sense beingthat it must be extremely painful for the embryonic personality to lie within the mother’s womb,having all his faculties, strength, virility, energy, intelligence and activity held in complete checkgrowing through the absorption of the food and drink taken by the motherhaving its source in very unclean Blood and Semen,covered by the most unclean clothing of the membrane,the bodysmeared with the urine, excreta, wind, bile and phlegm contained in the womb

units.sanskrit: ततो योनिद्वारेण पीड्यमानस्य कष्टतरा निःसृतिर्जन्मेति वैराग्यं ग्राहयति ।
units.english: Then the actual birth, consisting in painful coming out through the vagina,must be still more painful

units.sanskrit: मुहूर्तमप्यसह्यं दश वा नव वा मासानतिदीर्घकालमन्तः शयित्वेति च ॥
units.english: All this gives rise to feelings of Disgust nonattachment Such suffering would be unbearable even for a single momentwhat to say of lying in the womb for such a long time as ten or nine months

units.sanskrit: स जातो यावदायुषं जीवति ।
units.english: ‘Being born, he lives upto his lifespan;

units.sanskrit: तं प्रेतं दिष्टम् इतो ऽग्नय एव हरन्ति यत एवेतो यतः संभूतो भवति ॥
units.english: when he is dead, they carry him, as ordained, to the Fire,whence he came and whence he sprang’

units.sanskrit: स एवं जातो यावदायुषं पुनः पुनर्घटीयन्त्रवद्गमनागमनाय कर्म कुर्वन्कुलालचक्रवद्वा तिर्यग्भ्रमणाय यावत्कर्मणोपात्तमायुस्तावज्जीवति
units.english: Thus being born, he lives upto his lifespan; doing deeds tending to his repeated goings up and comings down, like the revolving of the waterwheel,or like the potter’s wheel, moving about horizontally,he lives up to the full lifespan, which is determined by his past acts

units.sanskrit: तमेनं क्षीणायुषं प्रेतं मृतं दिष्टं कर्मणा निर्दिष्टं परलोकं प्रति यदि चेज्जीवन्वैदिके कर्मणि ज्ञाने वाधिकृतस्तमेनं मृतमितो ऽस्माद्ग्रामादग्नये ऽग्न्यर्थमृत्विजो हरन्ति पुत्रा वान्त्यकर्मणे ।
units.english: When at the end of the lifespan, he dies, they carry him, as ordained,to such other regions as have been allotted to him in accordance with his past deeds,according as during life, he was devoted to the performance of Rituals or to the acquiring of Knowledgethey carry him from the village to the fire,ie, for the sake of being consigned to the fire,this being done by the Priests or by the sons, for the performance of the first Rites

units.sanskrit: यत एवेत आगतो ऽग्नेः सकाशाच्छ्रद्धाद्याहुतिक्रमेण, यतश्च पञ्चभ्यो ऽग्निभ्यः संभूत उत्पन्नो भवति तस्मा एवाग्नये हरन्ति स्वामेव योनिमग्निमापादयन्तीत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: Because it was out of Fire that he came,through the process of the libations of Faith and the restand because it was out of the Fire, the Five Fires, that he sprang,therefore they carry him to the Fire,that is, they consign him to his own origin

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य नवमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: ये चेमे ऽरण्ये श्रद्धा तप इत्य् उपासते । ते ऽर्चिषम् अभिसंभवन्ति ।
units.english: Those who know this, and also those who, in the forest, meditate upon faith and penance, go to light;

units.sanskrit: अर्चिषो ऽहः ।
units.english: from light to day;

units.sanskrit: अह्न आपूर्यमाणपक्षम् ।
units.english: from day to the Bright Fortnight;

units.sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणपक्षाद् यान् षड् उदङ्ङ् एति मासांस् तान् ॥
units.english: from the Bright Fortnight to those six months during which the Sun rises northwards;from these months to the Year;

units.sanskrit: संवत्सराद् आदित्यम् । आदित्याच् चन्द्रमसम् । चन्द्रमसो विद्युतम् ।
units.english: from the Year to the Sun from the Sun to the Moon; from the Moon to Lightning

units.sanskrit: तत् पुरुषो ऽमानवः ।
units.english: There lies a Person, not human;

units.sanskrit: स एनान् ब्रह्म गमयति । एष देवयानः पन्था इति ॥
units.english: he carries them to Brahman, This is the Path of Divinities

units.sanskrit: वेत्थ यदितो ऽधि प्रजाः प्रयन्तीत्ययं प्रश्नः प्रत्युपस्थितो ऽपाकर्तव्यतया ।
units.english: The question introduced for disposal now is ‘Dost thou know where people go to, from here?’ See Viii

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्र लोकं प्रत्युत्थितानामधिकृतानां गृहमेधिनां य इत्थमेवं यथोक्तं पञ्चाग्निदर्शनं द्युलोकाद्यग्निभ्यो वयं क्रमेण जाता अग्निस्वरूपाः पञ्चाग्न्यात्मान इत्येवं विदुर्जानीयुः ।
units.english: From among those householders who aspire towards and are entitled to the Higher Regionsthose who know thisie, those who know the abovedescribed philosophy of the Five Fires, which teaches that we are produced gradually from the fires of the Heavenly and other Regions, and are of the nature of Fire, having our essence in the Five Fires

units.sanskrit: कथमवगम्यत इत्थं विदुरिति गृहस्था एवोच्यन्ते नान्य इति?
units.english: QuestionHow is it understood that the phrase those who know this’ refers to the Householders alone, and not to others?

units.sanskrit: गृहस्थानां ये त्वनित्थंविदः केवलेष्टापूर्तदत्तपरास्ते धूमादिना चन्द्रं गच्छन्तीति वक्ष्यति । ये चारण्योपलक्षिता वैखानसाः परिव्राजकाश्च श्रद्धातप इत्युपासते तेषां चेत्थंविद्भिः
units.english: AnswerIt is going to be asserted in the next text, which clearly confines itself to Householders that from among householders, those who do not know this Philosophy and who are devoted entirely to the performance of works of public utility and charity go to the Moon through smoke and other things; while those who are connected with forestlife, such as hermits and renunciates, are going to be described in the next clause as going through flame and the rest, along with those ‘who know this’

units.sanskrit: सहार्चिरादिना गमनं वक्ष्यति पारिशेष्यादग्निहोत्राहुतिसम्बन्धाच्च गृहस्था एव गृह्यन्त इत्थं विदुरिति ।
units.english: Thus by a process of elimination,and also from the connection of the Agnihotra which must refer to the Householder,it follows that it is Householders who are meant by the phrase ‘those who know this’

units.sanskrit: ननु ब्रह्मचारिणो ऽप्यगृहीता ग्रामश्रुत्यारण्यश्रुत्या विद्यन्ते कथं पारिशेष्यसिद्धिः?
units.english: Objection How can we get at the Householders by a process of elimination when there are the Religious Students still left unnoticed, as they are not included either in the text speaking of villages as Religious Students do not live in villages or in the text speaking of the Forest as this is confined to Hermits and Renunciates?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not vitiate our position

units.sanskrit: पुराणस्मृतिप्रामाण्यादूर्ध्वरेतसां नैष्ठिकब्रह्मचारिणामुत्तरेणार्था इति न विशेषनिर्देशार्हाः ।
units.english: As, on the authority of Purāṇa and Smṛti texts, it is wellknown that Celebates and Lifelong Students also go by the Northern Path of the Sun

units.sanskrit: ननूर्ध्वरेतस्त्वं चेदुत्तरमार्गप्रतिपत्तिकारणं पुराणस्मृतिप्रामाण्यादिष्यत इत्थंवित्त्वमनर्थकं प्राप्तम् । न ।
units.english: Says the OpponantIf Celibacy be the means of reaching the Northern Path, on the authority of Purāṇa and Smṛti texts,then the knowledge of this Philosophy becomes futile

units.sanskrit: गृहस्थान्प्रत्यर्थवत्त्वात् ।
units.english: AnswerNot so, as it has its use in the case of Householders

units.sanskrit: ये गृहस्था अनित्थंविदस्तेषां स्वभावतो दक्षिणो धूमादिः पन्थाः प्रसिद्धस्तेषां यं इत्थं विदुः सगुणं वान्यद्ब्रह्म विदुः । अथ यदु चैवास्मिञ्शव्यं कुर्वन्ति यदि नार्चिषमेवैति लिङ्गादुत्तरेण ते गच्छन्ति ।
units.english: Those Householders who do not know this Philosophy,for those, it is well known, is the natural Southern Path, passing through smoke and the rest From among these, those who know this philosophy or any other qualified form of Brahman,go by the Northern Path,as is indicated by the text ‘For such a person, whether or not they perform the obsequies, he goes to Light etc’ Ibid

units.sanskrit: ननूर्ध्वरेतसां गृहस्थानां च समान आश्रमित्व ऊर्ध्वरेतसामेवोत्तरेण पथा गमनं न गृहस्थानामिति न युक्तमग्निहोत्रादिवैदिककर्मबाहुल्ये
units.english: ObjectionCelibates and Householders, both belonging to the same order the former also living in the House, though without family,it is not right that the Celibates alone should proceed by the Northern Path, and not the Householders,specially when the Householder has to perform many rites such as the Agnihotra and the like which should better entitle him to the Brighter Path

units.sanskrit: च सति । नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not vitiate our position

units.sanskrit: अपूता हि ते ।
units.english: Because as a matter of fact, these Householders are not quite ‘purified’;

units.sanskrit: शत्रुमित्रसंयोगनिमित्तं हि तेषां रागद्वेषौ । तथा धर्माधर्मौ हिंसानुग्रहनिमित्तौ । हिंसानृतमायाब्रह्मचर्यादि च बह्वशुद्धिकारणमपरिहार्यं तेषाम् ।
units.english: they are still influenced by attachment and hatred due to contact with friends and enemies,so also by Demerit and Merit, due to injuring and helping; in fact, for these there are many unavoidable sources of impurity, such as injury, falsehood, deceit, sexuality and so forth;

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽपूताः । अपूतत्वान्नोत्तरेण पथा गमनम् ।
units.english: hence they are ‘not purified’, and being unpurified, they cannot proceed normally by the Northern Path

units.sanskrit: हिंसानृतमायाब्रह्मचर्यादिपरिहाराच्च शुद्धात्मानो हीतरे शत्रुमित्ररागद्वेषादिपरिहाराच्च विरजसस्तेषां युक्त उत्तरः पन्थाः ।
units.english: When however the acts of Injury, Falsehood, Deceit, Sexuality and the rest have been eliminated and they have thereby become purified, and having got rid of the attachment and hatred for friends and enemies,they become free from all ‘foulness’ evil;and then it is only right that they should proceed by the Northern Path

units.sanskrit: तथाच पौराणिकाः ये प्रजामीषिरे ऽधीरास्ते श्मशानानि भेजिरे ।
units.english: So say those learned in the Purāṇas, in the following text‘Those unwise persons who sought for offspring went to the crematorium;

units.sanskrit: ये प्रजां नेषिरे धीरास्ते ऽमृतत्वं हि भेजिरे ।
units.english: while those wise persons who did not seek for offspring attained immortality’

units.sanskrit: इत्थंविदां गृहस्थानामरण्यवासिनां च समानमार्गत्वे ऽमृतत्वफले च सत्यरण्यवासिनां विद्यानर्थक्यं प्राप्तम् । तथाच श्रुतिविरोधः ।
units.english: ObjectionThe Householders who know this philosophy, and the Forestdwellers Hermits and Renunciates if both these equally proceed by the same Northern Path and reach the same goal of immortality,then the superior knowledge of the forestdwellers becomes futile;

units.sanskrit: न तत्र दक्षिणा यन्ति नाविद्वांसस्तपस्विनःइति । स एनमविदितो न भुनक्तिइति च विरुद्धम् । न ।
units.english: and this would be contrary to the scriptures, which declare that‘The Southerners go not there, nor the ignorant ascetics’, and that ‘Unknown, He does, not protect’

units.sanskrit: आभूतसंप्लवस्थानस्यामृतत्वेन विवक्षितत्वात् । तत्रैवोक्तं पौराणिकैःआभूतसंप्तवं स्थानममृतत्वं हि भाष्यते इति ।
units.english: In the present context, the immortality spoken of as the goal attained is only relative immoratality, which has been described as ‘continuity of existence till Final Dissolution’ ViṣṇuPurāṇa, ’;

units.sanskrit: यच्चा'त्यन्तिकममृतत्वं तदपेक्षयान तत्र दक्षिणा यन्तिस एनमविदितो न भुनक्तीत्याद्याः श्रुतय इत्यतो न विरोधः । न च पुनरावर्तन्तैतिमं मानवमावर्तं ना'वर्तन्तैत्यादिश्रुतिविरोध इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: while what the two texts just quoteda ‘The Southerners go not there’, and b ‘Being unknown, he does not protect’,refer to is Absolute Immortality; hence there is no incompatibility between the Philosophy of the Fires and the Vedic Texts quoted The opponent rejoinsIn that case, what is said now regarding this Immortality being only relative will be contrary to such Vedic declarations asa They do not return , Praśna , b They return not to this whirl of humanity Ibid

units.sanskrit: इमं मानवमिति विशेषणात्तेषामिह न पुनरावृत्तिरस्तीति च ।
units.english: which indicate that the Immortality is absolute Not so; because of the specification expressed in the phrase ‘this whirl of humanity’;

units.sanskrit: यदि ह्येकान्तेनैव ना'वर्तेरन्निमं मानवमिहेति च विशेषणमनर्थकं स्यात् । इममिहेत्याकृतिमात्रमुच्यत इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: if the ‘nonreturn’ here spoken of were meant to be absolute Immortality, then the specifying of ‘whirl of humanity’ would be absolutely meaningless OpponentThe particles this and here in the texts only indicate the Universal, the generality and hence the Immortality meant cannot but be of the universal, absolute, type

units.sanskrit: अनावृत्तिशब्देनैव नित्यानावृत्त्यर्थस्य प्रतीतत्वादाकृतिकल्पनानर्थिका ।
units.english: as the term ‘nonreturn’ being sufficient to express eternal, absolute nonreturn, the assumption of the Universal would be purposeless

units.sanskrit: अत इममिहेति च विशेषणार्थवत्त्वायान्यत्रा'वृत्तिः कल्पनीया ।
units.english: Hence in order to make some sense out of the specification implied by the terms ‘this and here’it has to be assumed that there is Return to other lives though not to human life

units.sanskrit: न च सदेकमेवाद्वितीयमित्येवंप्रत्ययवतां मूर्धन्यया नाड्यार्चिरादिमार्गेण गमनम् ।
units.english: As for those persons who have realised the final truth relating to ‘the One Being, without a second’ there is no going out to the Path of Flame etc, through the artery in the Head as there is in the case of the man who reaches only relative Immortality ;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मैव सन्ब्रह्माप्यति ।
units.english: as is clear from hundreds of Vedic texts, such asa ‘Being Brahman, he attains Brahman’ Bṛhada,

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तत्सर्वमभवत् ।
units.english: iv Hence he became all’ Bṛhada

units.sanskrit: न तस्य प्राणा उत्क्रामन्ति ।
units.english: , ‘His lifebreaths do not go out, they become merged herein’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: अत्रैव समवनीयन्तेइत्यादिश्रुतिशतेभ्यः ।
units.english: Objection;

units.sanskrit: ननु तस्माज्जीवादुच्चिक्रमिषोः प्राणा नोत्क्रामन्ति सहैव गच्छन्तीत्ययमर्थः कल्प्यत इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: When this last quoted text asserts that when the Living Being is going out, his Breaths do not depart’, we assume that what is meant is that ‘the Breaths accompany him when he is leaving the body’

units.sanskrit: अत्रैव समवनीयन्त इति विशेषणानर्थक्यात् ।
units.english: as the next sentence says ‘they become merged therein’ and this would have no meaning under the above interpretation

units.sanskrit: सर्वे प्राणा अनूत्क्रामन्तीति च प्राणैर्गमनस्य प्राप्तत्वात् ।
units.english: Then again, the going out of the Breaths having been already declared elsewhere in the text ‘All the breaths go out after him’

units.sanskrit: तस्मादुत्क्रामन्तीत्यनाशङ्कैवैषा ।
units.english: Bṛhadā Upa IViv, there can be no doubt regarding their going out

units.sanskrit: यदापि मोक्षस्य संसारगतिवैलक्षण्यात्प्राणानां जीवेन सहागमाश्ङ्क्य तस्मान्नोत्क्रामन्तीत्युच्यते तदाप्यत्रैव समवनीयन्त इति विशेषणमनर्थकं
units.english: It might be argued that ‘the path of libation being quite different from Births and Rebirths, people might be led to believe that the Breaths do go out with the Living Being, and hence the text in question has declared that they do not go out’ But even so, the objectionthat the additional specification that ‘they become merged therein’ would be meaninglesswould still stand

units.sanskrit: न च प्राणैर्वियुक्तस्य गतिरुपपद्यते जीवत्वं वा ।
units.english: Further, when the person has become separated from the Breaths, there can be no going for him;

units.sanskrit: सर्वगतत्वात्सदात्मनो निरवयवत्वात्प्राणसम्बन्धमात्रमेव ह्यग्निविस्फुलिङ्गवज्जीवत्वभेदकारणमित्यतस्तद्वियोगे जीवत्वं गतिर्वा न शक्या
units.english: nor indeed the character of a Living Being can apply to it If there is any truth in Vedic texts, the Self who is pure Being being allpervading and without constituent parts, the only thing that differentiates the Living Self Jīvātmā, from the Self is its connection with the Breaths;the relationship between the Self and the Living Self being exactly like that between the fire and the sparks going out of it;

units.sanskrit: न सतो ऽणुरवयवः स्फुटितो जीवाख्यः सद्रूपं छिद्रीकुर्वन्गच्छतीति शक्यं कल्पयितुम् । तस्मात्तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेतिइति सगुणब्रह्मोपाकस्य प्राणैः सह नाड्या गमनं सापेक्षमेव चामृतत्वं न साक्षान्मोक्ष इति गम्यते ।
units.english: consequently, when the Breaths have gone out, and their connection with the Living Self has thus ceased, this Self can no longer be regarded as ‘living’ Jīva, or as going out It cannot be assumed that ‘when the entity called’ ‘Jiva’ goes out, he does so as a small part shooting out of the Supreme Being and leaving a hole in this latter’From all this it follows that when the Text says ‘going above that he reaches Immortality,’ what it means is that when the person medicating upon Brahman with qualifications, goes out, along with the Breaths, through the Artery in the head, the immortality that he attains is only relative, and it is not direct Absolute Liberation;

units.sanskrit: तदपराजिता पूस्तदैरं मदीयं सरःइत्याद्युक्त्वातेषामेवैष ब्रह्मलोकःइति विशेषमात् ।
units.english: that it is,so is clear also from such specific statements as ‘that is the unconquered citythat the enchanting lake‘to those alone belongs the Brahmic Region’ which all go to show that absolute immortality is attainable only by those knowing Brahman,

units.sanskrit: अतः पञ्चाग्निविदो गृहस्था ये चेमे ऽरण्ये वानप्रस्थाः परिव्राजकाश्च सह नैष्ठिकब्रह्मचारिभिः श्रद्धा तप इत्येवमाद्युपासते श्रद्दधानास्तपस्विनश्चेत्यर्थः उपासनशब्दस्तात्पर्यार्थः । इष्टापूर्ते दत्तमित्युपासत इति यद्वत् ।
