units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा एतस्यात्मनो वैश्वानरस्य मूर्धैव सुतेजाश् चक्षुर् विश्वरूपः प्राणः पृथग्वर्त्मात्मा संदेहो बहुलो बस्तिर् एव रयिः पृथिव्य् एव पादाव् उर एव वेदिर् लोमाणि बर्हिर् हृदयं गार्हपत्यो मनो ऽन्वाहार्यपचन आस्यम् आहवनीयः ॥
units.english: Of this VaiśvānaraSelf, the Head is the ‘Highly Brilliant’,the Eye is the ‘Multiform’,the Lifebreath is the ‘Diversecoursed Soul,’the Trunk is the ‘Extensive’,the Bladder is ‘Wealth’,the Feet are the ‘Earth’;the Chest is the Altar, the Hairs are the Grass, the Heart is the Gārhapatya Fire, the Mind is the Anvāhāryapacana Fire, and the Mouth is the Āhavanīya Fire

units.sanskrit: कस्मादेवम् ।
units.english: Why is it so as described above?

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्तस्य ह वै प्रकृतस्यैवैतस्या'त्मनो वैश्वानरस्य मूर्धैव सुतेजाश्चक्षुर्विश्वरूपः प्राणः पृथग्वर्त्मा'त्मा सन्देहो बहुलो बस्तिरेव
units.english: Because of this same VaiśvānaraSelf, which is the subjectmatter of the section,the Head itself is the ‘Highly Brilliant’, the Eye is the Multiform,the Lifebreath is the Diversecoursed Soul,the Trunk is the Extensive,‘the Bladder is Wealth and the Earth is the Feet

units.sanskrit: अथवा विध्यर्थमेतद्वचनमेवमुपास्य इति । अथेदानीं वैश्वानरविदो भोजने ऽग्निहोत्रं संपिपादयिषन्नाहएतस्य वैश्वानरस्य भोक्तुरुर एव वेदिराकारसामावन्यात् ।
units.english: Or the whole of this may be taken as an injunction of meditationthe sense being that one should meditate in this manner The text proceeds to show how, in the case of the knower of the VaiśvānaraSelf, the act of Eating constitutes the Agnihotraoffering;

units.sanskrit: लोमानि बर्हिर्वेद्यामिवोरसि लोमान्यास्तीर्णानि (न) दृश्यन्ते । हृदयं गार्हपत्यो हृदयाद्धि मनः प्रणीतमिवानन्तरी भवत्यतो ऽन्वाहार्यपचनो ऽग्निर्मनः । आस्यं मुखमाहवनीय इवा'हवनीयो हूयते ऽस्मिन्नन्नमिति ॥
units.english: of this VaiśvānaraSelf,who is the eater,the chest is the Altar,because it resembles this in shape,the Hairs are the Grass,the hairs are seen to be spread over the chest, just as grass is seen strewn on the Altar,the Heart is the GārhapatyaFiṛe,because the Mind is taken out of the Heart just as the Anvāhāryapacana Fire is taken out of the Āhavanīya and hence is close to it;

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्याष्टादशः खण्डः
units.english: hence the Mind is the Anvāhāryapacana Fire;the Mouth is the Āhavanīya Fire;as like the Āhavanīya Fire, the Mouth is that into which food is thrown in, just as offerings are thrown into the ĀhavanīyaFire End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: तद् यद् भक्तं प्रथमम् आगच्छेत् तद् धोमीयम् ।
units.english: Thus the food that comes first should be an object of libationoffering

units.sanskrit: स यां प्रथमाम् आहुतिं जुहुयात् तां जुहुयात् प्राणाय स्वाहेति ।
units.english: So that when he offers the first libation, he should offer it with the words ‘Svāhā’ to ‘Prāṇa’;

units.sanskrit: प्राणस् तृप्यति ॥
units.english: and thereby Prāṇa becomes satisfied l

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्रैवं सति यद्भक्तं भोजनकाल आगच्छेद्भोजनार्थं तद्धोतव्यम् ।
units.english: Thussuch being the case,when at the time of eating, the food that happens to come firstfor the purpose of eating,it should be an object of libationoffering,ie it should be offered as a libation

units.sanskrit: अग्निहोत्रसम्पन्मात्रस्य विवक्षितत्वान्नाग्निहोत्राङ्गेतिकर्तव्यताप्राप्तिरिह ।
units.english: As it is only the accomplishment of the Agnihotra as a complete whole that is meant to be represented here, the detailed procedure of the Agnihotra finds no place here

units.sanskrit: स भोक्ता यां प्रथमामाहुतिं जुहुयात्तां कथं जुहुतादित्याहप्राणाय स्वाहेत्यनेन मन्त्रेणा'हुतिशब्दादवदानप्रमाणमन्नं प्रक्षिपेदित्यर्थः
units.english: When the eater offers the first libation,how should he offer it? AnswerHe should offer it with the words ‘Svāhā’ to ‘Prāṇa’ ie with this mantra; and as the term ‘libation’ has been used, only that quantity of food should be put into the mouth as is offered in libations

units.sanskrit: तेन प्राणस्तृप्यति ॥
units.english: By this offering, Prāṇa becomes satisfied

units.sanskrit: प्राणे तृप्यति चक्षुस् तृप्यति । चक्षुषि तृप्यत्य् आदित्यस् तृप्यति ।
units.english: Prāṇa being satisfied, the Eye becomes satisfied;the Eye being satisfied, the Sun becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: आदित्ये तृप्यति द्यौस् तृप्यति ।
units.english: the Sun being satisfied, the Heaven becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: दिवि तृप्यन्त्यां यत् किंच द्यौश् चादित्यश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
units.english: the Heaven being satisfied, whatever is under the Heaven and under the Sun becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
units.english: and through the satisfaction thereof, he himself becomes satisfied also with offspring, cattle, food, brightness boldness, and Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: प्राणे तृप्यति चक्षुरादित्यो द्यौश्चेत्यादि तृप्यति यच्चान्यद्द्यौश्चा'दित्यश्च स्वामित्वेनाधितिष्ठतस्तच्च तृप्यति तस्य तृप्तिमनु
units.english: On Prāṇa being satisfied, the Eye becomes satisfied; the Eye, the Sun, and the Heaven,all this becomes satisfied,as all whatever else is under the Heaven and the Sun,as their lord and master,becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: स्वयं भुञ्जानस्तृप्यत्येवं प्रत्यक्षम् ।
units.english: and through the satisfaction thereof, hethe Eater himself also becomes satisfied;all this is quite perceptible

units.sanskrit: किं च प्रजादिभिश्च ।
units.english: And further, he becomes satisfied with offspring and the rest also

units.sanskrit: तेजः शरीरस्था दीप्तिरुज्ज्वलत्वं प्रागल्भ्यं वा, ब्रह्मवर्चसं वृत्तस्वाध्यायनिमित्तं तेजः ॥
units.english: The term ‘tejas’ stands for brightness, effulgence, or it may mean boldness;Brahmic Glory, is glory due to the proper accomplishmentof character and learning

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्यैकोनविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ यां द्वितीयां जुहुयात् तां जुहुयाद् व्यानाय स्वाहेति ।
units.english: Then, when he offers the second libation, he should offer it with the words ‘Svāhā’ to ‘Vyāna’;

units.sanskrit: व्यानस् तृप्यति ॥
units.english: when Vyāna becomes satisfied

units.sanskrit: व्याने तृप्यति श्रोत्रं तृप्यति । श्रोत्रे तृप्यति चन्द्रमास् तृप्यति ।
units.english: On Vyāna being satisfied, the Ear becomes satisfied; on the Ear being satisfied, the Moon becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: चन्द्रमसि तृप्यति दिशस् तृप्यन्ति । दिक्षु तृप्यन्तीषु यत् किंच दिशश् चन्द्रमाश् चाधितिष्ठन्ति तत् तृप्यति ।
units.english: on the Moon being satisfied, the Quarters become satisfied; on the Quarters being satisfied, whatever is under the Moon and the Quarters becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
units.english: through the satisfaction thereof, he himself becomes satisfied; also with offspring, cattle, food, brightness and Brahmic glory

units.sanskrit: अथ यां तृतीयां जुहुयात् तां जुहुयाद् अपानाय स्वाहेति ।
units.english: Then, when he offers the third libation, he should offer it with the words‘Svāhā to ‘Apāna’;

units.sanskrit: अपानस् तृप्यति ॥ अपाने तृप्यति वाक् तृप्यति । वाचि तृप्यन्त्याम् अग्निस् तृप्यति । अग्नौ तृप्यति पृथिवी तृप्यति । पृथिव्यां तृप्यन्त्यां यत् किं च पृथिवी चाग्निश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
units.english: when Apāna becomes satisfied;on Apāna being satisfied, Speech becomes satisfied;on Speech being satisfied, Fire becomes satisfied;on Fire being satisfied, the Earth becomes satisfied;on Earth being satisfied, whatever is under the Earth and the Fire becomes satisfied;through the satisfaction thereof, he becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: तस्यानुतृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
units.english: also with offspring, cattle, food, brightness and Brahmic Glory

units.sanskrit: अथ यां चतुर्थीं जुहुयात् तां जुहुयात् समानाय स्वाहेति ।
units.english: When he offers the fourth libation, he should offer it with the words ‘Svāhā’ to ‘Samāna’;

units.sanskrit: समानस् तृप्यति ॥
units.english: when Samāna becomes satisfied

units.sanskrit: समाने तृप्यति मनस् तृप्यति ।
units.english: On Samāna being satisfied, the Mind becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: मनसि तृप्यति पर्जन्यस् तृप्यति । पर्जन्ये तृप्यति विद्युत् तृप्यति ।
units.english: on Mind being satisfied, Parjanya becomes satisfied on Parjanya being satisfied, Lightning becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: विद्युति तृप्यन्त्यां यत् किं च विद्युच् च पर्जन्यश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
units.english: on Lightning being satisfied, what ever is under Lightning and Parjanya becomes satisfied;through the satisfaction thereof, he becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
units.english: also with offspring, cattle, food, brightness and Brahmic Glory

units.sanskrit: अथ याम् पञ्चमीं जुहुयात् तां जुहुयात् उदानाय स्वाहेति ।
units.english: When he offers the fifth libation, he should offer it with the words ‘Svāhā’ to ‘Udāna’;

units.sanskrit: उदानस् तृप्यति ॥
units.english: when Udāna becomes satisfied

units.sanskrit: उदाने तृप्यति त्वक् तृप्यति त्वचि तृप्यन्त्यां वायुस् तृप्यति । वायौ तृप्यत्य् आकाशस् तृप्यति । आकाशे तृप्यति यत् किंच वायुश् चाकाशश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
units.english: On Udāna being satisfied, the Skin becomes satisfied;on the Skin being satisfied, Air becomes satisfied;on the Air being satisfied, Ākāśa becomes satisfied; On Ākāśa being satisfied, whatever is under Air and Ākāśa becomes satisfied through the satisfaction thereof, he becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
units.english: also with offspring, cattle, food, brightness and Brahmic Glory

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि पञ्चमाध्यायस्य त्रयोविंशः खण्डः
units.english: When he makes the second, third, fourth, fifth offering etc, etc, all which is exactly alike End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: स य इदम् अविद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति यथाङ्गारान् अपोह्य भस्मनि जुहुयात् तादृक् तत् स्यात् ॥
units.english: If, without knowing this, one offers the Agnihotra it would be just like a man removing the live embers and pouring the libation on dead ashes

units.sanskrit: स यः कश्चिदिदं वैश्वानरदर्शनं यथोक्तमविद्वान्सन्नग्निहोत्रं
units.english: If any one, without knowing the above, described Philosophy of the Vaiśvānara

units.sanskrit: प्रसिद्धं जुहोति यथाङ्गारानाहुतियोग्यानपोह्यानाहुतिस्थाने भस्मनि जुहुयात्तादृक्तत्तुल्यं
units.english: were to perform the wellknown Agnihotra this Agnihotraoffering Would be like a man removing the live embers fit for being the recipient of the libations,and pouring the libation on dead asheswhich are not the right place for pouring the libation

units.sanskrit: तस्य तदग्निहोत्रहवनं स्याद्वैश्वानरविदो ऽग्निहोत्रमपेक्ष्येति प्रसिद्धाग्निहोत्रनिन्दया वैश्वानरविदो ऽग्निहोत्रं स्तूयते ॥
units.english: This would be useless in comparison with the Agnihotraoffering made by the person knowing the Vaiśvānara By deprecating the wellknown Agnihotra, the text means to eulogise the Agnihotraoffering made by one who knows the Vaiśvānara

units.sanskrit: अथ य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति तस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु सर्वेष्व् आत्मसु हुतं भवति ॥
units.english: But if one knowing this offers the Agnihotra, his libation falls upon all regions, all beings and all selves

units.sanskrit: अतश्चैतद्विशिष्टमग्निहोत्रम् । कथम् । अथ य एतदेवं विद्वानग्निहोत्रं जुहोति तस्य यथोक्तवैश्वानरविज्ञानवतः सर्वेषु लोकेष्वित्याद्युक्तार्थम् ।
units.english: For this reason, this is a specially qualified Agnihotra;How?Now, if one knowing this offers the Agnihotraof him, who knows the Philosophy of Vaiśvānara as described above,the libations become offered on all regions etc, etc,the meaning of all which has been already explained in connection with the eating of food;

units.sanskrit: हुतमन्नमत्तीत्यनयोरेकार्थत्वात् ॥
units.english: as ‘pouring libation’ and eating of food’ serve the same purpose in this context

units.sanskrit: तद् यथेषीकातूलम् अग्नौ प्रोतं प्रदूयेतैवं हास्य सर्वे पाप्मानः प्रदूयन्ते य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति ॥ किञ्च तद्यथेषीकायास्तूलमग्रमग्नौ प्रोतं प्रक्षिप्तं प्रदूयेत प्रदह्येत क्षिप्रमेवं हास्य विदुषः सर्वात्मभूतस्य सर्वान्नानामत्तुः सर्वे निरवशिष्टाः पाप्मानो धर्माधर्माख्या अनेकजन्मसञ्चिता इह च प्राग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तेर्ज्ञानसहभाविनश्च प्रदूयन्ते
units.english: Just as Reedcotton thrown on the Fire is burnt up, so are burnt up all the evils of one who knowing this thus offers the Agnihotra, Further, just as the cotton of the Reedplant when thrown on the Fire,becomes burnt upquickly,even so are burnt up all the evilsknown by the name of ‘merit and demerit’without any exception,all that had become gathered through several births, and also those that had come into existence prior to and along with the knowledge of Vaiśvānara,of the man who knows the Vaiśvānara, the Self of All, the Eater of all Food;the only evil left unburnt would be that to which the birth of the present body had been due;

units.sanskrit: लक्ष्यं प्रति मुक्तेषुवत्प्रवृत्तफलत्वात्तस्य न दाहः ।
units.english: this last evil is not burnt up, because like the arrow that has been shot, its effects have already begun to appear

units.sanskrit: य एतदेवं विद्वानग्निहोत्रं जुहोति भुङ्क्ते ॥
units.english: All this happens to one who knowing this offers the Agnihotra,ie eats food

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् उ हैवंविद् यद्य् अपि चण्डालाय उच्छिष्टं प्रयच्छेत् । आत्मनि हैवास्य तद् वैश्वानरे हुतं स्याद् इति ।
units.english: Therefore, if one knowing this were to offer the remnant of his food to Caṇḍāla, it would be offering to bis VaiśvānaraSelf

units.sanskrit: तद् एष श्लोकः ॥
units.english: To this end there is the following verse

units.sanskrit: स यद्यपि चण्डालायोच्छिष्टानर्हायोच्छिष्टं प्रयच्छेदुच्छिष्टं दद्यात्प्रतिषिद्धमुच्छिष्टदानं यद्यपि कुर्यादात्मनि हैवास्य चण्डालहेहस्थे वैश्वानरे तद्धुतं स्यान्नाधर्मनिमित्तमिति विद्यामेव स्तौति ।
units.english: If such a person were to offer the remnant of his food to the Caṇḍāla,who does not deserve to receive itand thus make an offering which is forbidden,even so this would be an offering to the VaiśvānaraSelfin the Caṇḍāla’s body; and the act would not be sinful By saying this, the Philosophy is meant to be eulogised

units.sanskrit: तदेतस्मिन्स्तुत्यर्थे श्लोको मन्त्रो ऽप्येष भवति ॥
units.english: To this end ie in praise of the Philosophy,there is the following VerseMa/ifratext

units.sanskrit: यथेह क्षुधिता बाला मातरं पर्युपासते ।
units.english: ‘As here, hungry Children wait upon the Mother, so do all Beings wait upon the Agnihotra

units.sanskrit: एवं सर्वाणि भूतान्य् अग्निहोत्रम् उपासत ॥
units.english: Yea, they wait upon the Agnihotra’

units.sanskrit: यथेह लोके क्षुधिता बुभुक्षिता बाला मातरं पर्युपासते कदा नो मातान्नं प्रयच्छतीत्येवं सर्वाणि भूतान्यन्नादान्येवंविदो ऽग्निहोत्रं भोजनमुपासते कदा त्वसौ भोक्ष्यत इति,
units.english: As in this world, hungry children wait upon the Mother,‘when will our mother give us food’,so do all Beingsthat eat food,wait upon the Agnihotra,ie Eatingof the man who knows this‘when will he eat?’, that is, the whole universe becomes satisfied by the eating, of the man knowing this

units.sanskrit: द्विरुक्तिरध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्था ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse

units.sanskrit: अथ षष्ठोध्यायः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse End of Discourse

units.sanskrit: श्वेतकेतुर् हारुणेय आस ।
units.english: ‘Hariḥ Om!’ There lived one ŚvetaketuĀruṇeya

units.sanskrit: तं ह पितोवाच श्वेतकेतो वस ब्रह्मचर्यम् ।
units.english: His father said to him‘O Śvetaketu, live the life of the Religious Student;

units.sanskrit: न वै सोम्यास्मत् कुलीनो ऽननूच्य ब्रह्मबन्धुर् इव भवतीति ॥
units.english: verily, my boy, no one in our family has ever been unlearned and hence Brāhmaṇa only in name’

units.sanskrit: श्वेतकेतुर्हा'रुणेय आसेत्याद्यध्यायसम्बन्धः ।
units.english: There lived one ŚvetaketuĀruṇeya The connection of the present Discourse with what has gone before is as followsIt has been declared under xiv

units.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानित्युक्तं कथं तस्माज्जगदिदं जायते तस्मिन्नेव च लीयते ऽनिति च तेनैवेत्येतद्वक्तव्यम् ।
units.english: Now, it has to be explained how this whole universe proceeds from, subsists in and becomes absorbed or merged into, that Brahman Then, later on, it has been declared under

units.sanskrit: अनन्तरं चैकस्मिन्भुक्ते विदुषि सर्वं जगत्तृप्तं भवतीत्युक्तं तदेकत्वे सत्यात्मनः सर्वभूतस्थस्योपपद्यते ना'त्मभेदे ।
units.english: that ‘when the knowing man has eaten, the whole universe ‘becomes satisfiednow, this also is possible only if the Self is one only in all beings,and not if there are diverse selves

units.sanskrit: कथं च तदेकत्वमिति तदर्थो ऽयं षष्ठो ऽध्याय आरभ्यते ।
units.english: Now, the present, Sixths Discourse starts to show how it is only one Self in all beings

units.sanskrit: पितापुत्राख्यायिका विद्यायाः सारिष्ठत्वप्रदर्शनार्था ।
units.english: The story relating to the father and son has been introduced for the purpose of indicating the great importance of the Philosophy dealt with

units.sanskrit: श्वेतकेतुरिति नामतो हेत्यैतिह्यार्थः आरुणेयो ऽरुणस्य पौत्र आस बभूव ।
units.english: Śvetaketuby name;‘ha’ implies that the story is well known;Āruṇeya,the grandson of Aruṇa,livedwas

units.sanskrit: तं पुत्रं हा'रुणिः पिता योग्यं विद्याभाजनं मन्वानस्तस्योपनयनकालात्ययं च पश्यन्नुवाच हे श्वेतकेतो ऽनुरूपं गुरुं कुलस्य नो गत्वा
units.english: His father Āruṇi, thinking this son of his to be a fit person to receive the teaching,and noticing that the time for his initiation was passing,said to him‘O Śvetaketu, go to a teacher who is fit for our family, and live the life of the Religious Student;

units.sanskrit: न चैतद्युक्तं यदस्मत्कुलीनो हे सोम्याननूच्यानधीत्य ब्रह्मबन्धुरिव भवतीति ब्राह्मणान्बन्धून्व्यपदिशति न स्वयं ब्राह्मणवृत्त इति ॥
units.english: it is not fit and proper, my boy, that any one of our family should be unlearnedrshould not study, and hence a Brāhmaṇa only in name,ie one who only points to the Brāhmaṇas to whom he is related, and is not himself like a Brāhmaṇa,’

units.sanskrit: स ह द्वादशवर्ष उपेत्य चतुर्विंशतिवर्षः सर्वान् वेदान् अधीत्य महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्ध एयाय ।
units.english: Having gone when twelve years old, he came, back when he was twentyfour years old, having studied all the Vedas, highlyconceited, regarding himself a great scholar, and arrogant

units.sanskrit: तं ह पितोवाच ॥ तस्यातः प्रवासो ऽनुमीयते पितुः ।
units.english: From what follows it seems that the father himself went abroad after the conversation;

units.sanskrit: येन स्वयं गुणवान्सन्पुत्रं नोपनेष्यति ।
units.english: as being fully qualified himself he did not initiate his son into the life of;the Religious Student

units.sanskrit: स पित्रोक्तः श्वेतकेतुर्ह द्वादशवर्षः सन्नुपेत्या'चार्यं यावच्चतुविंशतिवर्षो बभूव तावत्सर्वान्वेदांश्चतुरो ऽप्यधीत्य तदर्थं च बुद्ध्वा महामना महद्गम्भीरं मनो यस्यासममात्मानमन्यैर्मन्यमानं मनो यस्य सो ऽयं महामनाः अनूचानमान्यनूचानमात्मानं
units.english: When he was addressed as above by his father, Śvetaketu, when twelve years old, approached the teacher and becoming initiated by him,and by the time he was twenty four years old, he had studied all the four Vedas, and understood their meaning;’and being highlyconceited,ie not thinking any one to be equal to himself,regarding himself a great scholar,one who is prone to think himself to be a great scholar,arrogant,not endowed with humility,came backhome

units.sanskrit: तमेवंभूतं हा'त्मनो ऽननुरूपशीलं स्तब्धं मानिनं पुत्रं दृष्ट्वा पितोवाच सद्धर्मावतारचिकीर्षया । श्वेतकेतो यन्निवदं महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्धश्चासि कस्ते ऽतिशयः प्राप्त उपाध्यायात्?
units.english: Finding his son so unlike himself in character, arrogant and conceited, the father said to him‘O, Śvetaketu, since thou art so highly conceited, regarding thyself a great scholar and arrogant,what is the exceptional thing thou hast obtained from thy teacher? Didst thou ask the teacher for that teachingthat which can be learnt only from a teacher, or the teaching regarding the Supreme Brahman?’

units.sanskrit: उत तम् आदेशम् अप्राक्ष्यः येनाश्रुतं श्रुतं भवत्य् अमतं मतम् अविज्ञातं विज्ञातम् इति ।
units.english: ‘That through which the unheard becomes heard, the unthoughtof becomes thought of and the unknown becomes known ?’‘What is that teaching

units.sanskrit: कथं नु भगवः स आदेशो भवतीति ॥
units.english: Sir,?

units.sanskrit: तमादेशं विशिनष्टियेना'देशेन श्रुतेनाश्रुतमप्यन्यच्छतं भवत्यमतं मतमतर्कितं तर्कितं भवत्यविज्ञानं विज्ञातमनिश्चितं निश्चितं भवतीति ।
units.english: The father specified the teaching‘that teaching through which when heard,other things even unheard, become heard,the unthoughtofwhat has never been considered,becomes thought of,duly considered,the unknownwhat is not definitely knownbecomes knowndefinitely known

units.sanskrit: सर्वानपि वेदानधात्य सर्वं चान्यद्वेद्यमधिगम्याप्यकृतार्थ एव भवति यावदात्मतत्त्वं न जानातीत्याख्यायिकातो ऽवगम्यते ।
units.english: What is learnt from this story is that even after having read all the Vedas and learnt all else that there is to be learnt,until one knows and understands the essense of the Self,his main purpose in life remains unfulfilled

units.sanskrit: तदेतदद्भुतं श्रुत्वा'हकथं न्वेतदप्रसिद्धमन्यविज्ञानेनान्यद्विज्ञातं भवतीत्येवं मन्वानः पृच्छति कथं नु केन प्रकारेण हे भगवः स आदेशो भवतीति ॥
units.english: Having heard the wonderful assertion made by his father, he said‘Sir, what is that teaching?‘this what he says regarding one thing becoming known by the knowledge of another thing is too strange to be believed’,thinking thus, the son puts the question‘In what manner does that teaching proceed?

units.sanskrit: यथा सोम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
units.english: ‘My Boy, just as through a clod of clay, all that is made of clay would become known;all products being due to words, a mere name;

units.sanskrit: वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
units.english: the clay alone is real’

units.sanskrit: यथा स आदेशो भवति तच्छृणु हे सोम्य । यथा लोक एकेन मृत्पिण्डेन घटशरावादिकारणभूतेन विज्ञातेन सर्वमन्यद्विकारजातं मृन्मयं मृद्विकारजातं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
units.english: Listen how that teaching proceeds, my BoyJust as in the ordinary world, though a single clod of clay,as the material cause of all such things as the Bracelet, the Jar and the like,being known, all else that is made of clayproducts of claywould become known

units.sanskrit: कथं मृत्पिण्डे कारणे विज्ञाते कार्यमन्यद्विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
units.english: QuestionHow can the knowledge of the Material cause, Clay, bring the knowledge of its products, which are totally different things?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not affect our position

units.sanskrit: कारणेनानन्यत्वात्कार्यस्य ।
units.english: Because the producteffect is nondifferent from its material cause

units.sanskrit: यन्मन्यसे ऽन्यस्मिन्विज्ञाते ऽन्यन्न ज्ञायत इति ।
units.english: You think that the knowledge of one thing cannot make another thing known

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं स्यात् । यद्यन्यत्कारणात्कार्यं स्यान्न त्वेवमन्यत्कारणात्कार्यम् ।
units.english: This would be quite true, if the product effect were something totally different from the cause As a matter of fact, however, the effect is not entirely different from its cause

units.sanskrit: कथं तर्हिदं लोक इदं कारणमयस्य विकार इति ।
units.english: QuestionHow then have we such ideas in the world as ‘this is the cause, and that its effect’?

units.sanskrit: शृणु ।
units.english: Listen;

units.sanskrit: वाचा'रम्भणं वागारम्भणं वागालम्बनमित्येतत् । को ऽसौ विकारो नामधेयं नामैव नामधेयं स्वार्थे धेयप्रत्ययः । वागालम्बनमात्रं नामैव केवलं न विकारो नाम वस्त्वस्ति परमार्थतो मृत्तिकेत्येव तु मृत्तिकेत्येव तु मृत्तिकैव सत्यं वस्त्वस्ति ॥
units.english: it is due to wordsie it is based upon words;What is due to words?All product, which thus, is mere name; the term ‘nāmadheya’ is formed with the term ‘nāman’ having the reflexive affix ‘dheya’ added to it the sense is that there is no real entity in the shape of the Product, it exists in name only, being based upon words; in reality the Clay is the only real thing’

units.sanskrit: यथा सोम्यैकेन लोहमणिना सर्वं लोहमयं विज्ञातं स्यात् । वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं लोहम् इत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
units.english: ‘My Boy, just as through a single ingot of gold, all that is made of gold would become known,all Product being due to words, a mere name;

units.sanskrit: यथा सौम्यैकेन लोहमणिना सुवर्णपिण्डेन सर्वमन्यद्विकारजातं कटकमुकुटकेयूरादि विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
units.english: My boy, just as by a single ingotlumpof gold,all that is made of gold,such as armlet, crown, bracelet and the likewould become known

units.sanskrit: वाचा'रम्भणमित्यादि समानम् ॥
units.english: Being due to Words etc, etc,as before

units.sanskrit: यथा सोम्यैकेन नखनिकृन्तनेन सर्वं कार्ष्णायसं विज्ञातं स्यात् । वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं कृष्णायसम् इत्य् एव सत्यम् ।
units.english: ‘My Boy, just as through a single nailclipper, all that is made of iron would become known,all Product being due to words, a mere name;

units.sanskrit: एवं सोम्य स आदेशो भवतीति ॥
units.english: the iron alone being realSuch, my boy, is that Teaching’

units.sanskrit: यथा सौम्यैकेन नखनिकृन्तनेनोपलक्षितेन कृष्णायसपिण्डेनेत्यर्थः । सर्वं कार्ष्णायसं कृष्णायसविकारजातं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
units.english: ‘My Boy, just as through a single nailclipper,which stands here as representing a lump of iron,all that is made of iron,everything that is made of iron,would become known’The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् । अनेकदृष्टान्तोपादानं दार्ष्टान्तिकारेकभेदानुगमार्थं दृढप्रतीत्यर्थं च ।
units.english: The speaker has made use of several illustrative examples for the purpose of including all the endless things meant to be illustrated, and also for the purpose of strengthening the conviction

units.sanskrit: एवं सोम्य स आदेशो यो मयोक्तो भवतीत्युक्तवति पितर्याहेतरो न वै नूनं भगवन्तः पूजावन्तो गुरवो मम ये त एतद्यद्भवदुक्तं वस्तु
units.english: Such, my Boy, is the Teaching spoke of to you’

units.sanskrit: नावेदिषुर्न विज्ञातवन्तो नूनम् ।
units.english: ‘Surely, those Revered Ones did not know this;

units.sanskrit: यद्यदि ह्यवेदिष्यन् विदितवन्त एतद्वस्तु कथं मे गुणवते भक्तायानुगताय नावक्ष्यन्नोक्तवन्तस्तेनाहं मन्ये न विदितवन्त इति ।
units.english: if they had known itthis subject,why should not they have taught it to me? who was duly qualified devoted and obedient? And this fact remains that they did not teach it to me;hence, think that they did not know it

units.sanskrit: अवाच्यमपि गुरोर्न्यग्भावमवादीत्पुनर्गुरुकुलं प्रति प्रेषणभयात् ।
units.english: Though the teacher’s inferiority should never have been spoken of,yet he spoke of it, because he was afraid of being again sent to the house of the same teacher

units.sanskrit: अतो भगवांस्त्वेव मे मह्यं तद्वस्तु येन सर्वज्ञत्वं ज्ञातेन मे स्यात्तद्ब्रवीतु कथयत्वित्युक्तः पितोवाच तथास्तु सौम्येति ॥
units.english: ‘Hence, you, Respected Sir, teach it to me;teach me that subject of philosophythe knowledge whereof would bring to me Omniscience’ The father said ‘Be it so, my dear’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: सद् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् । तद् धैक आहुर् असद् एवेदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ।
units.english: In the beginning, my dear, this was Being only,one, without a second Some say that, in the beginning, this was Nonbeing, only one, without a second

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् असतः सज् जायत ॥
units.english: From that Nonbeing sprang Being

units.sanskrit: सदेव सदित्यस्तितामात्रं वस्तु सूक्ष्मं निर्विशेषं सर्वगतमेकं निरञ्जनं निरवयवं विज्ञानं यदवगम्यते सर्ववेदान्तेभ्यः
units.english: Being onlythe term ‘Being’ stands for that entity which is mere esse,subtile, undefinable, all pervading, one, taintless, impartite, consciousness, as understood from the Vedāntatexts

units.sanskrit: एवशब्दो ऽवधारणार्थः ।
units.english: The particle ‘eva’ ‘only’, serves to emphasise the statement

units.sanskrit: किं तदवध्रियत इत्याह ।
units.english: QuestionWhat is to be understood from this?

units.sanskrit: इदं जगन्नामरूपक्रियावद्विकृतमुपलभ्यते यत्तत्सदेवा'सीदित्यासीच्छब्देन सम्बध्यते ।
units.english: AnswerWhat is understood is that ‘this universe which with its names, forms and activities, is perceived as a modified product,was Being only’; such is the connection of the word ‘was’

units.sanskrit: कदा सदेवेदमासीदित्युच्ते ।
units.english: QuestionWhen was this Being only?

units.sanskrit: अग्रे जगतः प्रागुत्पत्तेः ।
units.english: AnswerIn the beginning,ie, prior to the birth of the universe

units.sanskrit: किं नेदानीमिदं यद्येनाग्र आसीदिति विशेष्यते ।
units.english: QuestionIs not this Being there now, at the present time,that it has been qualifiedas Being so in the beginning?

units.sanskrit: न, कथं तर्हि विशेषणम् । इदानीमपीदं सदेव किन्तु नामरूपविशेषणवदिदंशब्दबुद्धिविषयं चेतीदं च भवति ।
units.english: AnswerNot so Then why the qualification in the beginning?What is meant is that even now, at the present moment, it is Being, but it is accompanied by differentiation of Name and Form,the object of the idea of the term ‘this’, and as such it becomes this

units.sanskrit: प्रागुत्पत्तेस्त्वग्रे केवलसच्छब्दबुद्धिमात्रगम्यमेवेति सदेवेदमग्र आसीदित्यवधार्यते ।
units.english: Before birthin the beginning,however, it was answerable only to the idea and term ‘Being’; hence it is emphasised that ‘in the beginning this was Being only’

units.sanskrit: न हि प्रागुत्पत्तेर्नामवद्रूपवद्वेदमिति ग्रहीतुं शक्यं वस्तु सुषुप्तकाल इव ।
units.english: Before its birth, no object can be apprehended as being such and such in name, or having such and such a form;

units.sanskrit: यथा सुषुप्तादुत्थितः सत्त्वमात्रमवगच्छति सुषुप्ते सन्मात्रमेव केवलं वस्त्विति तथा प्रागुत्पत्तेरित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: it is exactly as during the time of deep sleep What is meant is that immediately on waking from deep sleep, all that one is conscious of is mere existence of things, while during deep sleep, he is conscious of Being alone as the only entity;

units.sanskrit: यथेदमुच्यते लोके पूर्वाह्ने घटादि सिसृक्षुणा कुलालेन मृत्पिण्डं प्रसारितमुपलभ्य
units.english: and so also in the beginningbefore the birth of the universe It is just as all this is spoken of in the ordinary world

units.sanskrit: ग्रामान्तरं गत्वा प्रत्यागतो ऽपराह्ने तत्रैव घटशरावाद्यनेकभेदभिन्नं कार्यमुपलभ्य
units.english: In the morning, one sees the potter spreading out clay for making the jar and other things,and then having gone away to another village, and returning in the afternoon, sees in the same place, many products in the shape of jars, saucers and other articles, all of diverse kinds

units.sanskrit: मृदेवेदं घटशरावादि केवलं पूर्वाह्ने आसीदिति तथेहाप्युच्यते सदेवेदमग्र आसीदिति ।
units.english: One says that ‘all this, jar, saucer and the rest, was, in the morning, clay only’so it is said here that ‘in the beginning this was Being only’

units.sanskrit: एकमेवेति । स्वकार्यपतितमन्यन्नास्तीत्येकमेवेत्युच्यते । अद्वितीयमिति ।
units.english: One;What is meant of the assertion that it was one only, is that even in the form of its product, it does not become something else

units.sanskrit: मृद्व्यतिरेकेण मृदो यथान्यद्घटाद्याकारेण परिणमयितृकुलालादिनिमित्तकारणं दृष्टं तथा सद्व्यतिरेकेण सतः सहकारिकारणं द्वितीयं वस्त्वन्तरं प्राप्तं प्रतिषिध्यते ऽद्वितीयमिति । नास्य द्वितीयं वस्त्वन्तरं विद्यत इत्यद्वितीयम् ।
units.english: Without a second;what is denied by this negation is the likely idea thatJust as in the making of the jar and other things, it was that, apart from the clay, there were other efficient causes,in the form of the Potter and others,so in the case of the Products of Being also, there would be other accessory causes, apart from the BeingThere is no entity, second to it, hence it is without a second

units.sanskrit: ननु वेशेषिकपक्षे ऽपि सत्सामानाधिकरम्यं सर्वस्योपपद्यते । द्रव्यगुणादिषु सच्छब्दबुद्ध्यनुवृत्तेः । सद्द्रव्यं सन्गुणः सत्कर्मेत्यादिदर्शनात् ।
units.english: ObjectionIn the philosophy of the Vaiśeṣika also all things are co ordinated with Being, existencethe term ‘being’ ‘exists’ being found to be applied to substances, qualities and other things, in such expressions as ‘the existing Substance’, ‘the existing Quality’, ‘the existing Action’, and so forth AnswerTrue;

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं स्यादिदानीं प्रागुत्पत्तेस्तु नैवेदं कार्यं सदेवा'सीदित्यभ्युपगम्यते वैशेषिकैः प्रागुत्पत्तेः कार्यस्यासत्त्वाभ्युपगमात् । न चैकमेव सदद्वितीयं प्रगुत्पत्तेरिच्छन्ति । तस्माद्वैशेषिकपरिकल्पितात्सतो ऽन्यत्कारणमिदं सदुच्यते मृदादिदृष्टान्तेभ्यः ।
units.english: But before the birth of the product, it did not exist,say the Vaiśeṣikas; as their doctrine is that ‘before its production, the product is nonexistent’,nor do they accept the view that before production there was a single entity, ‘one without a second’From all this it is clear that what is spoken of in the text, through the example of Clay and other things, is a cause, in the shape of ‘Being’, entirely different from the ‘Existence’ posited by the Vaiśeṣika

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्र हैतस्मिन्प्रागुत्पत्तेर्वस्तुनिरूपण एके वैनाशिका आहुर्वस्तु निरूपयन्तो ऽसत्सदभावमात्रं प्रागुत्पत्तेरिदं जगदेकमेवाग्रे ऽद्वितीयमासीदिति
units.english: In regard to this subject of determining the exact nature of the entity before its birth, the Vaiśeṣikas have asserted, when determining the nature of things, that Before its birth, this universe was nonbeing,ie, mere negation of Being,one, without a second

units.sanskrit: सदभावमात्रं हि प्रागुत्पत्तेस्तत्त्वं कल्पयन्ति बौद्धाः ।
units.english: In fact, he Bauddhas hold the view that before birth, the negation of Being is the only reality;

units.sanskrit: न तु सत्प्रतिद्वन्द्वि वस्त्वन्तरमिच्छन्ति । यथा सच्चासदिति गृह्यमामं यथाभूतं तद्विपरीतं तत्त्वं भवतीति नैयायिकाः ।
units.english: and this ‘NonBeing’ is not regarded by them as some other entity, which is contrary to ‘Being’;as has been assumed by the Naiyāyikas according co whom, ‘Being’ is an entity which is apprehended as it exists, and that which is apprehended as contrary to this is ‘NonBeing’,both being equally real entities one positive and the other negative

units.sanskrit: ननु सदभावमात्रं प्रागुत्पत्तेश्चेदभिप्रेतं वैनाशिकैः कथं प्रागुत्पत्तेरिदमासीदसदेकमेवाद्वितीयं चेति कालसम्बन्धः संख्यासम्बन्धो
units.english: As to the question ‘How did this exist before its birth?’The answer provided by them is that ‘it was NonBeing, one, without a second’, where the thing spoken of is clearly related to a particular point of time ‘before birth’;

units.sanskrit: ऽद्वितीयत्वं चोच्यते तैः ।
units.english: and they also declare its being without a second, and all this makes clear that this thing must be a positive entity AnswerTrue;

units.sanskrit: बाढं न युक्तं तेषां भावाभावमात्रमभ्युपगच्छताम् । असत्तवमात्राभ्युपगमो ऽप्ययुक्त एवाभ्युपगन्तुरनभ्युपगमानुपपत्तेः । इदानीमभ्युपगन्ताभ्युपगम्यते न प्रागुत्पत्तेरिति चेत् । न ।
units.english: but such an opinion is right for those who posit merely a negation of things and do not admit of any positive entity In fact, the opinion that there is ‘non existence only’ is not right; as, if that were so, then the person holding this opinion would himself have to be denied;it might be argued that the holder of the opinion is admitted to be an entity at the present time, not before bis birthBut that cannot be;

units.sanskrit: प्रागुत्पत्तेः सदभावस्य प्रमाणाभावात् प्रागुत्पत्तेरसदेवेतिकल्पनानुपपत्तिः ।
units.english: there is no evidence to show that prior to birth there was negation of Being; so, that there is no reason for the assumption that Before birth, it was only nonBeing

units.sanskrit: ननु कथं वस्त्वाकृतेः शब्दार्थत्वे ऽसदेकमेवाद्वितीयमितिपदार्थवाक्यार्थोपपत्त् इः? तदनुपपत्तौ चेदं वाक्यमप्रमाणं प्रसज्येतेति चेति ।
units.english: ObjectionWhat is denoted by the word is the Form commonality of things, how can there be any meaning of words or of the sentence, in the case of the assertion ‘nonBeing, one, without a second’ as none of these words is denotative of a commonality, and when no such meaning is possible, the assertion would become meaningless and hence wrong, invalid

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not vitiate our position;

units.sanskrit: सद्ग्रहणनिवृत्तिपरत्वाद्वाक्यस्य । सदित्ययं तावच्छब्दः सदाकृतिवाचकः ।
units.english: because what the sentence asserts is the cessation negation of the apprehension of ‘Being’ The term ‘Being’ is denotative of a positive generic entity;

units.sanskrit: एकमेवाद्वितीयमित्येतौ च सच्छब्देन समानाधिकरणौ ।
units.english: and the other two terms ‘one’ and ‘without a second’ are coordinated with qualify the term ‘Being’;

units.sanskrit: तथेदमासीदिति च ।
units.english: so also the term ‘this’ and ‘was’ in the sentence ‘this was nonbeing’

units.sanskrit: तत्र नञ् सद्वाक्ये प्रयुक्तः सद्वाक्यमेवावलम्ब्य सद्वाक्यार्थविषयां बुद्धिं सदेकमेवाद्वितीयमिदमासीदित्येवंलक्षणां ततः सद्वाक्यार्थान्निवर्तयत्यश्वारूढ इवाश्वालम्बनो ऽश्वं तदभिमुखविषयान्निवर्तयति तद्वत् ।
units.english: In this sentence expressing, the Being positive entity, the negative ‘non’ has been introduced; and being thus introduced, it serves, on the basis of the positive sentence itself, etc preclude, from the positive connotation of the sentence, the idea relating to that positive connotation,in the form ‘Being’, ‘one, without a second’;

units.sanskrit: न तु पुनः सदभावमेवाभिधत्तेः ।
units.english: The sentence thus does not connote mere negation of Being

units.sanskrit: अतः पुरुषस्य विपरीतग्रहणनिवृत्त्यर्थपरमिदमसदेवेत्यादि वाक्यं प्रयुज्यते ।
units.english: Hence, we conclude that the sentence, ‘this was nonBeing only etc, etc’, has been used only for the purpose of denying a possible wrong notion that might be entertained by people

units.sanskrit: दर्शयित्वा हि विपरीतग्रहणं ततो निवर्तयितुं शक्यत इत्यर्थवत्त्वादसदादिवाक्यस्य श्रौतत्वं प्रामाण्यं च सिद्धमित्यदोषः ।
units.english: It is only after the wrong notion has been expressed that it can be denied in the next text; in this way the sentence ‘this was nonBeing’ serves a distinctly useful purpose; and hence it, becomes established that it is a Vedic assertion and fully authoritative;

units.sanskrit: तस्मादसतः सर्वाभावरूपात्सद्विद्यमानमजायत समुत्पन्नम् । अडभावश्छान्दसः ॥
units.english: From this NonBeing,the negative of all things,sprang Being’ The form ‘jāyata’ without the initial ‘a’ is a Vedic anomaly

units.sanskrit: कुतस् तु खलु सोम्यैवं स्याद् इति होवाच । कथम् असतः सज् जायेत । सत् त्व् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ॥
units.english: ‘But how could it be so, my dear?’said he;‘How could Being be born from NonBeing?in fact, this was Being only, in the beginning, one, without a second’

units.sanskrit: तदेतद्विपरीतग्रहणं महावैनाशिकपक्षं दर्शयित्वा प्रतिषेधतिकुतस्तु प्रमाणात्खलु हे सोम्यैवं स्यादसतः सज्जायतेत्येवं कुतो भवेन्न कुतश्चित्प्रमाणादेवं
units.english: Having set forth the wrong view propounded by the Mahāvaināśika NihilistBauddha, he proceeds to reject it But how,with what proof,my dear, could it be so? How could it be possible that Being should be born from NonBeing? The meaning is that there can be no proof or reason for such a view

units.sanskrit: यदपि बीजोपमर्दे ऽङ्कुरो जायमानो दृष्टो ऽभावदेवेति तदप्यभ्युपगमविरुद्धं तेषाम् ।
units.english: It is true that the sprout is seen to appear only after the seed has been destroyed But even this instance would not be compatible with the doctrine that ‘it is from Negation alone that things are produced’

units.sanskrit: कथम् । ये तावद्बीजावयवा बीजसंस्थानविशिष्टास्ते ऽङ्कुरे ऽप्यनुवर्तन्त एव न तेषामुपमर्दे ऽङ्कुरजन्मनि ।
units.english: How so?Asa matter of fact, the constituents of the seed, which occupy the space that had been occupied by the seed, continue to subsist in the sprout; and there is no destruction of those constituents on the birth of the sprout

units.sanskrit: यत्पुनर्बीजाकारसंस्थानं तद्बीजावयवव्यतिरेकेण वस्तुभूतं न वैनाशिकैरभ्युपगम्यते यदङ्कुरजन्मन्युपमृद्येत ।
units.english: As for the entity in the shape of the seed itself which ceases to exist, the Nihilists do not admit of any such positive entity, apart from the constituents of the seed, as these would be destroyed on the birth of the sprout;

units.sanskrit: अथ तदस्त्यवयवव्यतिरिक्तं वस्तुभूतं तथा च सत्यभ्युपगमविरोधः ।
units.english: if there is such a positive entity apart from the constituents,then this goes against their doctrine that there is no positive entity

units.sanskrit: अथ संवृत्याभ्युपगतं बीजसंस्थानरूपमुपमृद्यत इति चेत् ।
units.english: It might be argued that what is destroyed, on the birth of the sprout, is the shape and form of the seed, the existence whereof is admitted by the Nihilist, as due to Illusion

units.sanskrit: केयं संवृतिर्नाम किमसावभाव उत भाव?इति । यद्यभावो दृष्टान्ताभावः ।
units.english: But what is this Illusion? Is it positive or negative? If it is negative, then there is no corroborative instance possible in support of the viewthat the positive entity is produced from a negative entity;

units.sanskrit: अथ भावस्तथापि नाभावादङ्कुरोत्पत्तिर्बीजावयवेभ्यो ह्यङ्कुरोत्पत्तिः ।
units.english: That is, just as, according to the Nihilists, there is no positive composite whole in the shape of the seed,so also the constituents cannot be positive entities;

units.sanskrit: अवयवा अप्युपमृद्यन्त इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: and if these are not positive entities, then there can be no destruction of them

units.sanskrit: तदवयवेषु तुल्यत्वात् । यथा वैनाशिकानां बीजसंस्थानरूपो ऽवयवी नास्ति तथावयवा अपीति तेषामप्युपमर्दानुपपत्तिः । बीजावयवानामपि सूक्ष्मावयवास्तदवयवानामप्यन्ये सूक्ष्मतरावयवा इत्येवं प्रसङ्गस्यानिवृत्तेः सर्वत्रोपमर्दानुपपत्तिः ।
units.english: Thus, inasmuch as the constituents of the seed also have their own subtler constituents, and these latter again have their own, still subtler constituents, and so on, there being an infinite series of constituent elements,there is no possibility of destruction total annihilation in any case, and as, all through this infinite series of constituents, there runs the notion of their being ‘Beings’ positive entities,there is no cessation of this ‘existence’ character of ‘being’;

units.sanskrit: सद्बुद्ध्यनुवृत्तेः सत्त्वानिवृत्तिश्चेति सद्वादिनां सत एव सदुत्पत्तिः सेत्स्यति ।
units.english: so that the Theory of the Positivist Upholders of ‘positive Beings’, that ‘Being entity is produced from Being’, becomes established

units.sanskrit: न त्वसद्वादिनां दृष्टान्तो ऽस्त्यसतः सदुत्पत्तेः ।
units.english: As for the upholders of ‘NonBeings’, there is no instance to show that Being Entity is produced from Nonbeing NonEntity

units.sanskrit: मृत्पिण्डाद्घटोत्पत्तिर्दृश्यते सद्वादिनां तद्भावे भावात्तदभावे चाभावात् ।
units.english: As for the Positivists, there is the wellknown instance of the jar an entity being produced from the Clay also an entity; which is clear from the fact that the jar is there when the clay is there, and it is not there when there is no clay

units.sanskrit: यद्यभावादेव घट उत्पद्येत घटार्थिना मृत्पिण्डो नोपादीयेत ।
units.english: If the jar were to be produced out of Negation, then it would not be necessary for the man desirous of making the jar to seek for Clay

units.sanskrit: अभावशब्दबुद्ध्यनुवृत्तिश्च घटादौ प्रसज्येत ।
units.english: It would be possible too, in that case, for the jar and other objects to be conceived and spoken of as negations nonentities

units.sanskrit: न त्वेतदस्त्यतो नासतः सदुत्पत्तिः ।
units.english: But neither of these two contingencies happens

units.sanskrit: यदप्याहुर्मृद्बुद्धिर्घटबुद्धेर्निमित्तमिति मृद्बुद्धिर्घटबुद्धेः कारणमुच्यते
units.english: Some people have held the following viewIt is the idea of the Clay which is the cause source of the idea of the jar;

units.sanskrit: न तु परमार्थत एव मृद्घटो वास्तीति तदपि मृद्बुद्धिर्विद्यमाना विद्यमानाया एव
units.english: so that it is the idea of the Clay which is the cause of the idea of the jar, and there is no such real entity as the clay or the jar But even so it would be an existing positive idea of the clay which would be the cause of the existing positive idea of the jar;

units.sanskrit: घटबुद्धेः कारणमिति नासतः सदुत्पत्तिः ।
units.english: and so there is no production of Being from NonBeing

units.sanskrit: मृद्घटबुद्ध्योर्निमित्तनैमित्तिकतया'नन्तर्यमात्रं न तु कार्यकारणत्वमिति चेत् । न ।
units.english: What we mean is that between the idea of the clay and the idea of the jar, which appear to stand in the relation of cause and effect, there is only immediate sequence, and not the actual relation of cause and effect

units.sanskrit: बुद्धीनां नैरन्तर्ये गम्यमाने वैनाशिकानां बहिर्दृष्टान्ताभावात् ।
units.english: In support of this immediate sequence of ideas, the Nihilists can have no corroborative instance in the external world as being purely internal

units.sanskrit: अतः कुतस्तु खलु सोम्यैवं स्यादिति होवाच कथं केन प्रकारेणासतः सज्जायेतेति । असतः सदुत्पत्तौ न कश्चिदपि दृष्टान्तप्रकारो ऽस्तीत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: It is on account of all this that the father saidHow could it be so, my dear? That is, in what way could Being be produced from NonBeing? The meaning is that there is no instance of Being Entity being ever produced from NonBeing NonEntity

units.sanskrit: एवमसद्वादिपक्षमुन्मध्योपसंहरति सत्त्वेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदिति स्वपक्षसिद्धिम् ।
units.english: Having thus demolished the doctrine of the Negativist Nihilist, he sums up by saying‘In fact, there was Being only, in the beginning’,wherein is contained the affirmation of his own doctrine as fully established

units.sanskrit: ननु सद्वादिनो ऽपि सतः सदुत्पद्यत इति नैव दृष्टान्तो ऽस्ति ।
units.english: Says the opponentFor the Positivist also who holds that Being is produced out of Being, there is no corroborative instance available;

units.sanskrit: घटाद्घटान्तरोत्पत्त्यदर्शनात् ।
units.english: because we do not see a jar being produced out of another jar

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं न सतः सदन्तरमुत्पद्यते किं तर्हि सदेव संस्थानान्तरेणावतिष्ठते ।
units.english: True, it is so; one Being or Entity is not produced from another Entity; it is the same Entity that appears and subsists in another form;

units.sanskrit: यथा सर्पः कुण्डली भवति । यथा च मृच्चूर्णपिण्डघटकपालादिप्रभेदैः ।
units.english: as for instance, when the snake becomes coiled up, or when the clay appears in the diverse forms of dust, clod, jar, potsheds and so forth

units.sanskrit: यद्येवं सदेव सर्वप्रकारवस्थं कतं प्रागुत्पत्तेरिदमासीदिति । उच्यते ।
units.english: Says the opponentIf that is so, and it is the one and the same Being that appears in various forms and conditions, then, how is it that it is asserted as in the text that ‘it existed before being born’?

units.sanskrit: ननु न श्रुतं त्वया सदेवेत्यव धारणमिदंशब्दवाच्यस्य कार्यस्य । प्राप्तं तर्हि प्रागुत्पत्तेरसदेवा'सीन्नेदंशब्दवाच्यमिदानीमिदं जातमिति । न ।
units.english: AnswerApparently it was not heard by you when it was pointed out by us in the beginning of the Bhāṣya on text above that what is intended by the sentence ‘In the beginning this was Being only’ is the emphasising of the positive character of the product denoted by the word ‘this’ ie the Universe

units.sanskrit: सत एवेदंशब्दबुद्धिविषयतयावस्थानाद्यथा मृदेव पिण्डघटादिशब्दबुद्धिविषयत्वेनावतिष्ठते तद्वत् ।
units.english: just as it is Clay itself that comes to subsist and be spoken of as ‘clod’, ‘jar’ and so forth Just as the clay is an entity, so are the clod and jar etc etc, also;

units.sanskrit: ननु यथा मृद्वस्त्वेवं पिण्डघटाद्यपि तद्वत्सद्बुद्धेरन्यबुद्धिविषयत्वात्कार्यस्य सतो ऽन्यद्वस्त्वन्तरं स्यात्कार्यजातं यथाश्वाद्गौः ।
units.english: And yet, as the product is the object of cognition other than the cognition of its cause, the product must be an entity different from the ‘Being’ its cause; just as the cow is different from the horse because it is the object of a cognition different from the cognition of the horse

units.sanskrit: पिण्डघटादीनामितरेतरव्यभिचारे ऽपि मृत्त्वाव्यभिचारात् ।
units.english: because though among the productsclod, jar and the rest,there is mutual difference, yet the character of being ‘clay’ pervades equally over all of them

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि घटः पिण्डं व्यभिचरति पिण्डश्च घटं तथापि मृत्तवं न व्यभिचरतस्तस्मान्मृन्मात्रं पिण्डघटौ ।
units.english: Though the jar is different and separable from the clod, and the clod is different and separable from the jar,yet neither the clod nor the jar is different separable from Clay; hence both the clod and the jar are only Clay

units.sanskrit: (व्यभिचरति त्वश्वं गौरश्वो वा गाम्) ।
units.english: As regards the cow and the horse however, the cow is different from the horse and the horse is different from the cow

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्मृदादिसंस्थानमात्रं घटादयः ।
units.english: From all this it follows that the jar and other products of Clay are only clay in diverse forms

units.sanskrit: एवं सत्संस्थानमात्रमिदं सर्वमिति युक्तं प्रागुत्पत्तेः । सदेवेति ।
units.english: In the same way all this universe is only Being, in diverse forms; and hence it is only right to assert that before birth, it was Being only;

units.sanskrit: वाचारम्भणमात्रत्वाद्विकारसंस्थानमात्रस्य ।
units.english: specially because every form of the product is only a modification based upon words

units.sanskrit: ननु निरवयवं सत्निष्कलं निष्क्रियं शान्तं निरवद्यं निरञ्जनंदिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः
units.english: Says the opponentThis Being is one, indivisible, whole, without parts, inactive, calm and taintless;

units.sanskrit: पुरुषः सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजैत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यो निरवयवस्य सतः कथं विकारसंस्थानमुपपद्यते ।
units.english: as declared in such Vedic texts as ‘The divine, incorporeal Puruṣa, unborn both inside and out’, Muṇḍaka And how can there be any modified form for the Being which is one indivisible whole?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: This does not vitiate our position

units.sanskrit: रज्ज्वाद्यवयवेभ्यः सर्पादिसंस्थानवद्बुद्धिपारिकल्पितेभ्यः सदवयवेब्यो विकारसंस्थानोपपत्तेः ।
units.english: Of the indivisible Being also, it is possible for modified forms to appear out of those illusory component parts of Being which are created by the imagination of man; just as the serpent appears out of those component parts of the rope which are created by the imagination as being those of the serpent

units.sanskrit: वाचा'रम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्येव सत्यमेवं सदेव सत्यमिति श्रुतेः । एकमेवाद्वितीयं परमार्थत इदंबुद्धिकाले ऽपि ॥ तद् ऐक्षत ।
units.english: Because after all ‘all modification is a product of words, existing in mere name, and the Clay is the only reality’; and thus really speaking Being alone is real, one, without a second,even at the time that there is perception of ‘this’ this perception being purely illusory

units.sanskrit: बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति ।
units.english: It conceived‘May become many; may grow forth’;

units.sanskrit: तत् तेजो ऽसृजत ।
units.english: and It created Fire

units.sanskrit: तत् तेज ऐक्षत । बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति ।
units.english: That Fire conceived‘May become many; may grow forth’;

units.sanskrit: तद् अपो ऽसृजत ।
units.english: and it created Water

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् यत्र क्व च शोचति स्वेदते वा पुरुषस् तेजस एव तद् अध्य् आपो जायन्ते ॥
units.english: Therefore whenever a man is hot and perspires, it is water produced from fire Itthat Beingconceived;

units.sanskrit: तत्सदैक्षतेक्षां दर्शनं कृतवत् ।
units.english: it saw and thought

units.sanskrit: अतश्च न प्रधानं सांख्यपरिकल्पितं जगत्कारणम् ।
units.english: From this it follows that the cause origin of the Universe is not the Primordial Matter, as posited by the

units.sanskrit: प्रधानस्याचेतनत्वाभ्युपदमात् ।
units.english: because Primordial Matter has been regarded by them as insentient;

units.sanskrit: इदं तु सच्चेतनमीक्षितृत्वात् ।
units.english: while this Being is sentient;

units.sanskrit: तत्कथमैक्षतेत्याहबहु प्रभूतं स्यां भवेयं प्रजायेत प्रकर्षेणोत्पद्येय । यथा मृद्घटाद्याकरेण यथा वा रज्जवादि सर्पाद्याकारेण बुद्धिपरिकल्पितेन ।
units.english: as only a sentient Being can conceive It conceived‘May become many, may grow forth’may be born well;just as the Clay grows into the form of the jar and other things,or the rope grows into the form of the serpentwhich form, in both cases, is created by the imagination

units.sanskrit: असदेव तर्हि सर्वं यद्गृह्यते रज्जुरिव सर्पाद्याकरेण । न ।
units.english: In that case all that is perceived is unreal, nonexistent, like the rope in the form of the serpentNo;

units.sanskrit: सत एव द्वैतभेदेनान्यथागृह्यमाणत्वान्नासत्त्वं कस्यचित्क्वचिदिति ब्रूमः ।
units.english: what we assert is that it is Being itself which is perceived in a form other than its own, through duality and diversity; and there is no nonexistence of anything anywhere

units.sanskrit: यथा सतो ऽन्यद्वस्त्वन्तरं परिकल्प्य पुनस्तस्यैव प्रागुत्पत्तेः प्रध्वंसाच्चोर्ध्वमसत्त्वं
units.english: It is the logicians who assume things other than Being, and declare that those things are nonexistent, before being produced, and also afterwards, after destruction

units.sanskrit: ब्रुवते तार्किका न तथास्माभिः कदाचित्क्वचिदिपि सतो ऽन्यदभिधानमभिधेयं वा
units.english: We however do not make any assumption of anythingname or named,other than Being at any time or place

units.sanskrit: सदेव तु सर्वमभिधानमभिधीयते च यदन्यबुद्ध्या । तथा रज्जुरेव सर्पबुद्ध्या सर्प इत्यभिधीयते यथा वा पिण्डघटादि मृदो ऽन्यबुद्ध्या पिण्डघटादिशब्देनाभिधीयते लोके । रज्जुविवेकदर्शिनां तु सर्पाभिधानबुद्धी निवर्तेते यथा च मृद्विवेकदर्शिनां घटादिशब्दबुद्धी तद्वत्सद्विवेकदर्शिनामन्यविकारशब्दबुद्धी
units.english: Whatever there is, in the form of name or named,which is imagined to be something differentall this is Being only, just as it is the rope itself which, under the assumption of the serpent, is called ‘serpent’;and just as the clod, jar and the rest come to be spoken of as different from the Clayor the assumption that all that is different from Clay,in ordinary life For those, however, who know the real character of the Rope, the name as well as the idea of serpent’ cease,and for those who know the real character of Clay, the name and idea of ‘jar etc,’ cease;

units.sanskrit: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सहेतिअनिरुक्ते ऽनिलयनैत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः ।
units.english: as declared in such Vedic texts as‘Wherefrom speech turns back, without getting at it, along with the mind’ Taitti , and ‘It is undescribable, imperishable,’ Ibid

units.sanskrit: एवमीक्षित्वा तत्तेजो ऽसृजत तेजः सृष्टवत् ।
units.english: and so forth Having conceived thus, it created fire

units.sanskrit: ननु तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशः संभूत इति श्रुत्यन्तर आकाशाद्वायुस्ततस्तृतीयं तेजः श्रुतमिह तु कथ प्राथम्येन तस्मादेव तेजः सृज्यते तत एव चा'काशमिति विरुद्धम् ।
units.english: ObjectionIn another Vedic Text, it has been declared that ‘From Self was produced Ākāśa’ Taitti and ‘From Ākāśa, Air,and then from Air, Fire’,which thus is the third product; how then, is it mentioned in the present text as the very first product? That Fire as well as Ākāśa, both should be created from the same source is selfcontradictory

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThere is no force in this objection;

units.sanskrit: आकाशवायुसर्गानन्तरं तत्सत्तेजो ऽसृजतेतिकल्पनोपपत्तेः । अथ वाविवक्षित इह सृष्टिक्रमः सत्कार्यमिदं सर्वमतः सदेकमेवाद्वितीयमित्येतद्विवक्षितम् ।
units.english: it is possible to interpret the present text to mean, that It created Fire, after the creation of Ākāśa and Air and thus all the texts become reconciled Or, the order of sequence in the creation is not what is meant to be asserted here; all that is meant to be asserted is that ‘all this is the product of Being entity and hence, all is Being alone, one, without a second’

units.sanskrit: मृदादिदृष्टान्तात् ।
units.english: That this is so meant is clear from the example of Clay that has been cited

units.sanskrit: अथवा त्रिवृत्करणस्य विवक्षितत्वात्तेजोबन्नानामेव सृष्टिमाचष्टे ।
units.english: Or, what is meant to be asserted is the doctrine of ‘Triplication’ as set forth in texts , below;

units.sanskrit: तेज इति प्रसिद्धं लोके दग्धृ पक्तृ प्रकाशकं रोहितं चेति ।
units.english: ‘Tejas Fire, is wellknown in the world as that which burns, cooks and illumines and is red

units.sanskrit: तत्सत्सृष्टं तेज ऐक्षत तेजोरूपसंस्थितं सदैक्षतेत्यर्थः । बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: When this Fire was createdthat is, after the Being had taken the form of Fire, it conceived‘may become many and grow forth as before

units.sanskrit: तदपो ऽसृजत ।
units.english: It created Water;

units.sanskrit: आपो द्रवाः स्निग्धाः स्यन्दिन्यः शुक्लाश्चेति प्रसिद्धा लोके ।
units.english: Water is liquid, viscil, fluid, and white,as is wellknown in the world From Fire came Water as the product;

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्तेजसः कार्यभूता आपस्तस्माद्यत्र क्वच देशे काले वा शोचति सन्तप्यते स्वेदते प्रस्विद्यते वा पुरुषस्तेजस एव तत्तदा'पो ऽधिजायन्ते
units.english: hence it is that at whatever place and time, man becomes hotheatedand perspires, it is water produced from fire The Water conceived‘May become many and may grow forth’;

units.sanskrit: जायते ॥
units.english: it created Food

units.sanskrit: बह्वयः प्रभूताः स्याम भवेम प्रजायेमहि उत्पद्येमहोति । ता अन्नमसृजन्त पृथिवीलक्षणम् ।
units.english: The said Water conceived,as before, Being in the form of Water conceived,‘May become manyprofuseand grow forthbecome produced’It created Foodin ṭhe shape of Earth

units.sanskrit: पार्थिवं ह्यन्नं यस्मादप्कार्यमन्नं तस्माद्यत्र क्व च वर्षति देशे तत्तत्रैव भूयिष्ठं प्रबूतमन्नं भवति ।
units.english: Inasmuch as food, which is of the nature of earth, is the product of Water,wheneverin whatever placeit rains, there is prefuse food produced;

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽद्भ्य एव तदन्नाद्यमधिजायते ।
units.english: hence it is from water that eatable food is produced

units.sanskrit: ता अन्नमसृजन्तेति पृथिव्युक्ता पूर्वमिह तु दृष्टान्ते ऽन्नं च तदाद्यं चेति विशेषणाद्व्रीहियवाद्या उच्यन्ते ।
units.english: At first it is said that when the text spoke of Water having created ‘Food’, it was Earth that was meant to have been created;

units.sanskrit: अन्नं च गुरु स्थिरं धारणं कृष्णं च रूपतः प्रसिद्धम् ।
units.english: Food is wellknown as heavy, firm, nourishing, things and dark in colour

units.sanskrit: ननु तेजः प्रभृतिष्वीक्षणं न गम्यते हिंसादिप्रतिषेधाभावात्त्रासादिकार्यानुपलम्भाच्च तत्र कथं तत्तेज ऐक्षतेत्यादि ।
units.english: ObjectionIt is not possible for Fire and other things to conceive, as there is no prohibition of the killing of these things as there is prohibition of the killing of sentient beings, and also because we do not find in these things any such feelings as Fear and the like which are concomitant with sentience;how is it that the text speaks of Fire having conceived?

units.sanskrit: नेष दोषः ।
units.english: This does not vitiate our position

units.sanskrit: ईक्षितृकारणपरिणामत्वात्तेजः प्रभृतीनां सत इवेक्षितुर्नियतक्रमविशिष्टकार्योत्पादकत्वात् तेजः प्रभृतीक्षत इवेक्षत इत्युच्यते भूतम् ।
units.english: Because Fire and other things are the products evolved out of the cause Being which is the real conceiver; in fact, Being itself is the conceiver, who creates products in a definite order of sequence; and when Fire and the rest are spoken of as having ‘conceived what is meant is that it was as if the elemental substance conceived

units.sanskrit: ननु सतो ऽप्युपचरितमेवेक्षितृत्वम् । न ।
units.english: ObjectionFor the Being also, the conceiving must be only figurative and not real Not so;

units.sanskrit: सदीक्षणस्य केवलशब्दगम्यत्वान्न शक्यमुपचरितं कल्पयितुम् ।
units.english: because ‘conceiving’ by the Being can be known only from Words of the Veda, and hence, it is not possible to assume that it is figurative, not real

units.sanskrit: तेजः प्रभृतीनां त्वनुमीयते मुख्येक्षणाभाव इति युक्तमुपचरितं कल्पयितुम् । ननु सतो ऽपि मृद्वत्कारणत्वादचेतनत्वं शक्यमनुमातुम् । अतः प्रधानस्यैवाचेतनस्य सतश्चेतनार्थत्वान्नियतकालक्रमविशिष्टकार्योत्पादकत्वाच्चैक्षतेवैक्षतेति शक्यमनुमातुमुपचरितमेवेक्षणम्
units.english: Says the opponentAs Being is the cause of Clay, it is possible to infer that it is insentient like its, Product, clay hence it can be presumed that it is the insentient Primordial Matter itself, which functioning for the sentient Being, produces the various products in general, at welldefined times; so that the ‘conceiving’ in this case must be figurative;

units.sanskrit: दृष्टश्च लोके ऽचेतने चेतनवदुपचारः ।
units.english: in ordinary life we have seen that an insentient thing is spoken of and treated as sentient;

units.sanskrit: यथा कूलं पिपतिषतीति तद्वत्सतो ऽपि स्यात् । न ।
units.english: for example, in suchexpressions as the river bank wishes to slide down Of the same kind may be the attributing of ‘conception’ to Being which, as Primordial Matter is really insentient Not so, we reply

units.sanskrit: तत्सत्यं स आत्मेति तस्मिन्नात्मोपदेशात् ।
units.english: Because this Being is going to be spoken of later on as the Self, in the text ‘That is the truth, that is the SelfIt might be argued that ‘this speaking of it as the self also may be figurative;

units.sanskrit: आत्मोपदेशो ऽप्युपचरित इति चेद्यथा ममा'त्मा भद्रसेन इति आत्मनः सर्वार्थकारिण्यनात्मन्यात्मोपचारस्तद्वत् । न ।
units.english: just as is found in such expressions ‘Bhadrasena is my very Self where the character of ‘self’ is attributed to one Bhadrasena who may be doing all that is food to the speaker, and yet is not his Self

units.sanskrit: सदस्मीति सत्सत्याभिसन्धस्यतस्य तावदेव चिरम् इति मोक्षोपदेशात् ।
units.english: as it is taught that Liberation comes to one who regards himself as ‘Being’, having the firm conviction that he is real;

units.sanskrit: सो ऽप्युपचार इति चेत् ।
units.english: Even this may be purely figurative

units.sanskrit: प्रधानात्माभिसन्धस्य मोक्षसामीप्यं वर्तत इति मोक्षोपदेशो ऽप्युपचरित एव ।
units.english: That is to say, when it is said that when one has a firm conviction regarding the Principal Self, Liberation is close to him,this teaching regarding Liberation also may be only figurative

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके ग्रामं गन्तुं प्रस्थितः प्राप्तवानहं ग्राममिति ब्रूयात् त्वरापेक्षया तद्वत् । न ।
units.english: Just as, in the ordinary world, when one has started to go to a village, he may say ‘ have reached the village’, for the purpose of indicating quicknessThat cannot be;

units.sanskrit: येन विज्ञातेनाविज्ञातं विज्ञातं भवतीत्युपक्रमात् । सत्येतस्मिन्विज्ञाते सर्वं विज्ञातं भवति तदनन्यत्वात्सर्वस्याद्वितीयवचनाच्च ।
units.english: because the whole treatment has started with the preface ‘By the knowledge of which all becomes known etc, etc’ It is Being alone, by knowing which all else becomes known; for the simple reason that all things are not different from Being;

units.sanskrit: न चान्यद्विज्ञातव्यमवशिष्टं श्रावितं श्रुत्यानुमेयं वा लिङ्गतो ऽस्ति येन मोक्षोपदेश उपचरितः स्यात् ।
units.english: Nor has the Śruti directly declared anything else as ‘to be known nor can any such be inferred from any indicatives in the Veda,on the basis of which the ‘Liberation’ spoken of could be regarded as figurative

units.sanskrit: सर्वस्य च प्रपाठकार्थस्योपचरितत्वपरिकल्पनायां वृथा श्रमः परिकल्पयितुः स्यात्पुरुषार्थसाधनविज्ञानस्य तर्केणैवाधिगतत्वात्तस्य
units.english: Further, if all that is said in the whole Discourse were to be presumed to be figurative, then the labour of the presumer would be entirely futile; as for him the means of accomplishing the Purpose of man would have been known by means of Ratiocination itself

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्वेदप्रामाण्यान्न श्रुतार्थपरित्यागः ।
units.english: From all this we conclude that as the Veda is fully authoritative, there can be no abandoning of its direct meaning

units.sanskrit: अतश्चेतनावत्कारणं जगत इति सिद्धम् ॥
units.english: Thus it is established that the cause of this Universe is a Sentient conscious Being,

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: तेषां खल्व् एषां भूतानां त्रीण्य् एव बीजानि भवन्त्य् आण्डजं जीवजम् उद्भिज्जम् इति ॥
units.english: Verily, of these Beings there are only three originsBorn from Egg, Born from Living Being, and Born from Roots

units.sanskrit: तेषां जीवाविष्टानां खल्वेषां पक्ष्यादीनां भूतानामेषामिति प्रत्यक्षनिर्देशान्न
units.english: Of these Beingsendowed with life,such as the Bird and the other living beings;the term ‘these’ refers to Fire and the rest spoken of in the preceding section;

units.sanskrit: तु तेजःप्रभृतीनां तेषां त्रिवृत्करणस्य वक्ष्यमाणत्वादसति त्रिवृत्करमे प्रत्यक्षनिर्देशानुपपत्तिः । देवताशब्दप्रयोगाच्च तेजः प्रभृतिष्विमास्तिस्रो देवता इति ।
units.english: because what the text is going to describe is the Triplication of these latter, and so long as this Triplication has not been described, they could not be spoken of directly as ‘these’ also because the term ‘Deity’ has been used with reference to Fire and the rest, in the text ‘These three Deities’ text below

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तेषां भूतानां पक्षिपशुस्थावरादीनां त्रीण्येव नातिरिक्तानि बीजानि कारणानि भवन्ति ।
units.english: Hence what the present text means is that of these living beings, Birds, Animals, Trees and the rest, there are only three,not moreoriginscausessources

units.sanskrit: कानि तानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
units.english: It is next pointed out what these origins area Born from Egg, b Born from Living Being,and c Born from Roots

units.sanskrit: आण्डजमण्डाज्जातमण्डजमण्डजमेवाऽण्डजं पक्ष्यादि ।
units.english: The term ‘āṇḍaja ’ is formed from the term ‘aṇḍaja’ ‘Born from Eggs’, with the reflexive affix,viz

units.sanskrit: पक्षिसर्पादिभ्यो हि पक्षिसर्पादयो जायमाना दृश्यन्ते ।
units.english: Birds, Serpents etc, are seen to be born of birds and serpents etc, only;

units.sanskrit: तेन पक्षी पक्षिणां बीजं सर्पः सर्पाणां तथान्यदप्यण्डाज्जातं तज्जातीयानां बीजमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is to say, Bird is the origin of Birds, the Serpent of Serpents, and so on Other eggborn animals are the origin of those of the same species

units.sanskrit: नन्वण्डाज्जातमण्डजमुच्यते ऽतो ऽण्डमेव बीजमिति युक्तं कथमण्डजं बीजमुच्यते ।
units.english: ObjectionWhat is born from the egg is called Eggborn’; so that it is the Egg that should be regarded as the ‘origin how then is it that what is spoken of as the ‘origin’ of Eggborn animals is ‘what is born from the egg?’

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं स्याद्यदि त्वदिच्छातन्त्रा श्रुतिः स्यात्स्तवतन्त्रा तु श्रुतिर्यत आहाऽण्डजाद्येव बीजं नाण्डादीति ।
units.english: AnswerThis would be quite true if the Veda were dependent upon our wish; as a matter of fact, however, the Veda is not dependent upon anything;

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते चाण्डजाद्यभावे तज्जातीयसन्तत्यभावो नाण्डाद्यभावे ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, too, it is found that it is the absence of Eggborn animal,not the absence of the Egg,that brings about the absence of the future brood of that species

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽण्डजादीन्येव बीजान्यण्डजादीनाम् ।
units.english: Hence, it is the Eggborn that is the ‘origin’ of Eggborn animals

units.sanskrit: तथा जीवाज्जातं जीवजं जरायुजमित्येतत्पुरुषपश्वादि ।
units.english: Similarly, what is born of a living being is born from Living Being’, that is, born of the womb, such as Man, Animal and others

units.sanskrit: उद्भिज्जमुद्भिनत्तीत्युद्भित्स्थावरं ततो जातमुद्भिज्जं धाना वोद्भित्ततो जायत इत्युद्भिज्जं स्थावरबीजं स्थावराणां बीजमित्यर्थः । स्वेदजसंशोकजयोरण्डजोद्भिज्जयोरेव यथासम्भवमन्तर्भावः ।
units.english: immobile beings like trees etc and what is born of these is ‘Born from Roots’ Or ‘Udbhid’, ‘root’, may stand for the seedgrains, and what is born from that is ‘Born of Roots’; so that the root of the immobile Being tree etc is the origin of immobile beings Vegetables As for such other species as ‘born of sweat’ and ‘born of heat’, these are included under the ‘Eggborn’, and

units.sanskrit: एवं ह्यवधारणं त्रीण्येव बीजानीत्युपपन्नं भवति ॥
units.english: ‘Rootborn’ respectively Thus the restriction, that ‘there are only three origins becomes established

units.sanskrit: हन्ताहम् इमास् तिस्रो देवता अनेन जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीति ॥
units.english: This Deity conceived‘Well, now may , entering into these three Divinities through this Living Self jīvātman, differentiate Name and Form’

units.sanskrit: सेयं प्रकृता सदाख्या तेजोबन्नयोनिर्देवतोक्तैक्षतेक्षितवती यथापूर्वं बहु स्यामिति ।
units.english: This Deity,the one that forms the subjectmatter of the Discourse,named ‘Being’, the source of Fire, Water and Food,conceived,thought,as before in the case of the assertion ‘may become many’

units.sanskrit: तदेव बहुभवनं प्रयोजनं नाद्यापि निर्वृत्तमित्यत ईक्षां पुनः कृतवती बहुभवनमेव प्रयोजनमुररीकृत्य ।
units.english: That purpose of ‘becoming many’ has not yet been accomplished; hence the Deity conceived again, accepting as its purpose the same ‘becoming many’

units.sanskrit: कथम् । हन्तेदानीमहमिमा यथोक्तास्तेज आद्यास्तिस्रो देवता, अनेन जीवेनेति, स्वबुद्धिस्थं पूर्वसृष्ट्यनुभूतप्राणधाराणमात्मानमेव स्मरन्त्याहानेन जीवेना'त्मनेति ।
units.english: What did it conceive?Well, now, may , entering into these three Divinities,these three spoken of above as Fire, Water and Food, through this Living Self;in speaking thus, the Being remembers its own self endowed with Life passed through which has experiences during the previous cycle of creation and which Life is still retained in memory;

units.sanskrit: प्राणधारणकर्त्रा'त्मनेति वचनात्स्वात्मनो ऽव्यतिरिक्तेन चैतन्यस्वरूपतयाविशिष्टेनेत्येतद्दर्शयति ।
units.english: hence it speaks of it as ‘this living self’;

units.sanskrit: तेजोबन्नभूतमात्रासंसर्गेण लब्धविशेषविज्ञाना सती, नाम च रूपं च नामरूपे व्याकरवाणि विस्पष्टमाकरवाण्यसौनामायमिदंरूपैति व्याकुर्यामित्यर्थः ।
units.english: and inasmuch as the text speaks of that self which carries on the act of living, what is meant is ‘entering through that which is notdifferent from the Being itself, being of the nature of the same unspecified Consciousness as itself;entering the three Divinities through this,that is, having acquired special cognitions due to the contact of the elements of Fire, Water and Food,may differentiate Name and Form;that is, ‘such and such a thing bears this name and has this form’

units.sanskrit: ननु न युक्तमिदमसंसारिण्याः सर्वज्ञाया देवताया बुद्धिपूर्वकमनेकशतसहस्रानर्थाश्रयं देहमनुप्रविश्य दुःखमनुभविष्यामीति सङ्कल्पनमनुप्रवेशश्च
units.english: ObjectionIt is not right and proper that the Deity Being which, by itself, is not subject to birth and death, and which is omniscient, should deliberately determine to enterand actually enterthe body, which is the receptible of experience; while it is not subject to any other control

units.sanskrit: स्वातन्त्र्ये सति ।
units.english: AnswerTrue;

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं न युक्तं स्याद्यदि स्वेनैवाविकृतेन रूपेणानुप्रविशेयं दुःखमनुभवेयमिति च सङ्कल्पितवती न त्वेवम् ।
units.english: this would be right and proper, if the Deity had determined to enter into the body for suffering painful experiences, in its own unmodified form As a matter of fact, however, it is not so;

units.sanskrit: अनेन जीवेना'त्मनानुप्रविश्येति वचनात् । जीवो हि नाम देवताया आभासमात्रम् ।
units.english: it is clear from the clause ‘through this living self’, that it entered in the form of the Jīva living self, the Jīvātman, Individualised Self

units.sanskrit: बुद्ध्यादिभूतमात्रासंसर्गजनित आदर्श इव प्रविष्टः पुरुषप्रतिबिम्बो जलादिष्विव च सूर्यादीनाम् ।
units.english: This ‘Living Self’, ‘Jīva’, is a mere reflection of the said Deity the Supreme Self, Being brought about by its contact with Intellect and other faculties and with elemental rudiments,just like the reflection of a man standing before a mirror, or the reflection of the Sun and such bodies in water and other reflecting substances

units.sanskrit: अचिन्त्यानन्तशक्तिमत्या देवताया बुद्ध्यादिसम्बन्धश्चैतन्याभासो देवतास्वरूपविवेकाग्रहणनिमित्तः सुखी दुःखी मूढ इत्याद्यनेकविकल्पप्रत्ययहेतुः
units.english: It is the contact of this Deity,which has potencies unthinkable and endless,with intellect and other faculties, and the reflection thereon of Consciousness or Intelligence,which latter is due to the want of proper differentiation of the real positive form of the Deitywhich becomes the cause of various such notions as ‘ am happy ‘ am unhappy’, ‘ am dumbfounded’ and the like

units.sanskrit: छायामात्रेण जीवरूपेणानुप्रविष्टत्वाद्देवता न दैहिकैः स्वतः सुख दुःखादिभिः सम्बध्यते । यथा पुरुषादित्यादय आदर्शोदकादिषु च्छायामात्रेणानुप्रविष्टा आदर्शोदकदिदोषैनं सम्बध्यन्ते तद्वद्देवतापि ।
units.english: Inasmuch as the Deity enters only in the form of its reflection, be in the form of the ‘Living Self’,it does not itself become affected by the pain and other experiences of the body;just as the man, the Sun and other reflected things, entering into the mirror, water or other reflecting media, are not affected by the defects of these reflecting media;

units.sanskrit: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुर्न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥
units.english: To this effect we have the following texts‘Just as the Sun, the Eye of all worlds, is not affected by the external defects of the Eye,so the One Inner Self of all beings is not affected by sufferings of the external world’ Kaṭha

units.sanskrit: आकाशवत्सर्वगतश्च नित्यःइति च वाजसनेयके ।
units.english: , ‘He is allpervading and eternal, like Ākāśa’

units.sanskrit: ननु च्छायामात्रश्चेज्जीवो मृषैव प्राप्तस्तया परलोकेहलोकादि च तस्य ।
units.english: ObjectionIf the ‘Living Self’ is a mere reflection, then it must be unreal, and so also must be its going to the other Regions or even to this Region

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not affect the case;

units.sanskrit: सदात्मना सत्यत्वाभ्युपगमात् ।
units.english: what we hold is that it is, real, in so far as it is of the nature of Being

units.sanskrit: सर्वं च नामरूपादि सदात्मनैव सत्यं विकारजातं स्वस्त्वनृतमेव ।
units.english: In fact, all modificationsName and Form are real in so far as they are of the nature of ‘Being’,in themselves, they are all unreal;

units.sanskrit: वाचा'रम्भण विकारो नामधेयमित्युक्कत्वात् । तथा जीवो ऽपीति ।
units.english: as it has been declared that ‘All modificationis a mere product of words, a mere name’ The same is the case with the ‘Living Self’ Jīva

units.sanskrit: यक्षानुरूपो हि बलिरिति न्यायप्रसिद्धिः ।
units.english: The maxim is well known that ‘The offering is in accordance with the Yakṣa to whom it is offered’;

units.sanskrit: अतः सदात्मना सर्वव्यवहाराणां सर्वविकारामां च सत्यत्वं सतो ऽन्यत्वेनानृतत्वमिति न कश्चिद्दोषस्तार्किकैरिहानुवक्तुं शक्यः ।
units.english: hence under that principle, all activities and all modifications and products are real only in so far as they are of the nature of ‘Being’,and they are unreal in so far as they differ from ‘Being’ To this the logicians cannot take any objection;

units.sanskrit: यथेतरेतरविरुद्धद्वैतवादाः स्वबुद्धिविकल्पमात्रा अतत्त्वनिष्ठा इति शक्यं वक्तुम् ॥
units.english: it can be shown that all doctrines of Duality are mutually contradictory, are mere figments of the imagination of the propounder and are hence rooted in falsity

units.sanskrit: तासां त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतम् एकैकां करवाणीति । सेयं देवतेमास् तिस्रो देवता अनेनैव जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरोत् ॥ सैवं तिस्रो देवता अनुप्रविश्य स्वात्मावस्थे बीजभूते अव्याकृते नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीतीक्षित्वा तासां च तिसृणां देवतानामेकैकां त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतं करवाणि ।
units.english: ‘Of these;May make each one threefold’ conceiving thusthis Deity entered into those Divinities, through this ‘LivingSelf’ and differentiated the Names and Forms Thus entering into these three Divinities, may differentiate the hitherto undifferentiated Names and Forms which, in their own forms, are the ‘seeds’ or ‘origins’Having conceived thus, and also that ‘each of these three Divinities shall make triplicate’;the ‘triplication’ of each would mean the indicating of one of the three constituent factors as the primary and the other two as secondary factors;

units.sanskrit: एकैकस्यास्रिवृत्करण एकैकस्याः प्राधान्यं द्वयोर्द्वयोर्गुणभावो ऽन्थथा हि रज्जवा इवैकमेव त्रिवृत्करणं स्यात् न तु तिसृणां पृथक्पृथक्त्रिवृत्करणमिति
units.english: otherwise if all the three constituents were equal there would be a single common ‘triplication’, and not a distinct ‘triplication’ for each of the three

units.sanskrit: एवं हि तेजोबन्नानां पृथङ्नामप्रत्ययलाभः स्यात्तेज इदमिमा आपो ऽन्नमिदमिति च ।
units.english: In this way, we get at the idea of a separate name for each of the three, Fire, Water and Food in such expressions as ‘this is Fire’ in which the firy factor would be primary, ‘this is Water’ and ‘this is Food’;

units.sanskrit: सति च पृथङ्नामप्रत्ययलाभे देवतानां सम्यग्व्यवहारस्य प्रसिद्धिः प्रयोजनं स्यात् ।
units.english: and when the idea of the separate name of each of them has been got at,there would be an accomplishment of the proper use of the three Divinities

units.sanskrit: एवमीक्षित्वा सेयं देवतेमास्तिस्रो देवता अनेनैव यथोक्तेनैव जीवेन सूर्यबिम्बवदन्तः प्रविश्य वैराजं पिण्डं प्रथमं देवादीनां च पिण्डाननुप्रविश्य यथासङ्कल्पमेव नामरूपे व्याकरोदसौनामायमिदंरूप इति ॥
units.english: Having conceived thus; this Deity Being having entered into these three Divinities, through the aforesaid ‘Living Self’,like the solar orb entering into the reflecting surface,it entered, first of all, into the Mass Body representing Virāṭ the personal creator Prajāpati and then the’ Masses Bodies representing the Divinities,and then, in accordance with Its determination, it differentiated the Names and Forms‘Such and such is the Name of this, and such and such its Form’

units.sanskrit: तासां त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतम् एकैकाम् अकरोत् ।
units.english: It made each one of these triplicate

units.sanskrit: यथा तु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवतास् त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तन् मे विजानीहीति ॥
units.english: As to how each of these three Divinities becomes triplicate,learn that, my dear, from me

units.sanskrit: तासां च देवतानां गुणप्रधानभावेन त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतमेकैकामकरोत्कृतवती देवता ।
units.english: Each of the three Divinities, that Deity made triplicate,by determining which, in each, is the primary and which the secondary factors

units.sanskrit: तिष्ठतु तावद्देवतादिपिण्डानां नामरूपाभ्यां व्याकृतानां तेजोबन्नमयत्वेन त्रिधात्वं, यथा तु खलु बहुरिमाः पिण्डेभ्यस्तिस्रो देवतास्रिवृत्त्रिवृदेकैका भवति तन्मे मम निगदतो विजानीहि विष्टस्पमवधारयोदाहरणतः ॥
units.english: As regards the triplicate character of the ‘bodies’ of the Divinities, as consisting of fire, water and food, as duly differentiated through name and form,that may rest for the present;as to how, out of the external bodies,each of these three Divinities becomes triplicate,that learn from me, while am expounding it;

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य तृतीयः खण्डः
units.english: that is, clearly understand it by means of illustrations End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यद् अग्ने रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् । यच् छुक्लं तद् अपाम् ।
units.english: In Fire, the red colour is the colour of Fire, the white colour is that of Water and the black colour is that of Food Earth;

units.sanskrit: अपागाद् अग्नेर् अग्नित्वम् । वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
units.english: thus vanishes Fireness from Fire, being only a modification of words, a mere Name; and what is real and true is only that there are the three colours

units.sanskrit: यत्तद्देवतानां त्रिवृत्करणमुक्तं तस्यैवोदाहरणमुच्यते ।
units.english: Of the Triplication of the Divinities what has been spoken of before,an illustration is given here;

units.sanskrit: उदाहरणं नामैकदेशप्रसिद्ध्यर्थमुदाह्रियत इति ।
units.english: an illustration is put forward for proving the whole by showing the truth of a part

units.sanskrit: तदेतदाह यदग्नेस्रिवृत्कृतानां, यत्कृष्णं तस्यैवाग्ने रूपं तदन्नस्य पृथिव्या अत्रिवृत्कृताया इति विद्धि ।
units.english: The illustration is thus set forthYou should understand that the red colour that is known to belong to fire in its triplicated form, is really the colour of the Fireelement in Fire in its untriplicated form;

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सत रूपत्रयव्यतिरेकेणाग्निरिति यन्मन्यसे त्वं तस्याग्नेरग्नित्वमिदानीमपागादपगतम् ।
