units.english: Such being the case, that which you regard as Fire apart from the three colours,from that Fire the Fireness, the character of being a single separate entity as Fire has vanished,disappeared

units.sanskrit: प्राग्रूपत्रयविवेकविज्ञानाद्याग्निबुद्धिरासीत्ते साग्निबुद्धिरपगताग्निशब्दश्चेत्यर्थः । यथादृष्यमानरक्तोपधानसंयुक्तः स्फटिको गृह्यमाणः पद्मरागो ऽयमितिशब्दबुद्ध्योः प्रयोजको भवति प्रागुपधानस्फटिकयोर्विवेकविज्ञाने तु पद्मरागशब्दबुद्धी निवर्तेते तद्विवेकविज्ञातुस्तद्वत् ।
units.english: that idea of ‘Fire’ has disappeared, and so also the term ‘fire For instance, when the Rockcrystal is seen resting upon a red surface, it gives rise to the name ‘Ruby’, and also the idea that ‘this is a piece of Rubyso long as the surface and the rockcrystal have not been discriminated;when this discrimination has come about, the name ‘ruby’ and the idea that ‘it is ruby’ both disappear,so far as the discriminating person is concerned;in the same manner it happens in the case in question also

units.sanskrit: ननु किमत्र बुद्धिशब्दकल्पनया क्रियते प्राग्रूपत्रयविवेककरणादग्निरेवा'सीत्तदग्नेरग्नित्वं रोहितादिरूपविवेककरणादपागादिति युक्तं
units.english: ObjectionWhat is the use of assuming the existence of the Idea and the Name of Fire? The right way to put it is that what, prior to the discrimination of the three colours, was only Fire,of that Fire, the Fireness vanished after the discrimination of the red and other colours;

units.sanskrit: यथा तन्त्वपकर्षणे पटाभावः ।
units.english: just as, in the withdrawing of the yarn, the Cloth disappears

units.sanskrit: नैवं, बुद्धिशब्दमात्रमेव ह्यग्निर्यत आह वाचा'रम्भणमग्निर्नाम विकारो नामधेय नाममात्रमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: ReplyNot so Because Fire still exists as mere idea and Word, as is declared in the words of the textFire is only a modification of words, a mere name,nothing more than a Name

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽग्निबुद्धरपि मृषैव ।
units.english: Hence, it follows that the Idea also of Fire is unreal;

units.sanskrit: किं तर्हि तत्र सत्यं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्येव सत्यं नाणुमात्रमपि रूपत्रयव्यतिरेकेण सत्यमस्तीत्यवधारणार्थः ॥
units.english: what is real and true is that there are the three colours; not a jot more than the three colours is real; this is what is meant by the restrictive particle ‘eva’, ‘only’

units.sanskrit: यद् आदित्यस्य रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् । यच् छुक्लं तद् अपाम् ।
units.english: In the Sun, the red colour is the colour of Fire,the white is that of Water,and the black is that of Food Earth;

units.sanskrit: वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
units.english: thus vanishes Sunness from the Sun, being only a modification of words, a mere Name; and what is real is only that there are three colours

units.sanskrit: यच् चन्द्रमसो रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् । यच् छुक्लं तद् अपाम् ।
units.english: In the Moon, the read colour is the colour of Fire,the white is that of Water,the black is that of Food Earth;

units.sanskrit: वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
units.english: thus vanishes Moonness of the Moon, being only a modification of words, a mere Name; and what is real is only that there are three colours

units.sanskrit: यद् विद्युतो रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् । यच् छुक्लं तद् अपाम् ।
units.english: In Lightning, the red colour is the colour of Fire,the white is that of Water and the black that of Food Earth;

units.sanskrit: अपागाद् विद्युतो विद्युत्त्वम् । वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
units.english: thus vanishes Lightningness from Lightning, being only a modification of words, a mere Name; and what is real is only that there are three colours

units.sanskrit: तथा यदादित्यस्य यच्चन्द्रमसो यद्विद्युत इत्यादि समानम् । ननु यथा नु खलु सोम्येमास्तिस्रो देवतास्रिवृत्त्रिवृदेकैका भवति तन्मे विजानीहित्युक्त्वा तेजस एव चतुर्भिरप्युदाहरणैरग्न्यादिभिस्रिवृत्करणं दर्शितं नाबन्नयोरुदाहरणं दर्शितं त्रिवृत्करणे ।
units.english: Similarly, of the Sun, of the Moon, of Lightning, and so on,as before ObjectionWhat the Father had said was ‘Learn from me, my dear, how each of these three Divinities becomes triplicate’;and by means of four illustrations, what has been shown is triplication of the Divinity of fire alone, through fire water and food, and no illustrations have been cited in regard to the triplication of the Divinities of Water and Food

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: ReplyThis does not affect our position;

units.sanskrit: अबन्नविषयाण्यप्युदाहरणान्येवमेव च द्रष्टव्यानीति मन्यते श्रुतिः ।
units.english: what the Vedic text thinks as illustrations regarding the triplication of Water and Food also may be addressed in the same manner;

units.sanskrit: तेजस उदाहरणमुपलक्षणार्थम् ।
units.english: and it was only for the purpose of illustration that the example of the triplication of Fire has been set forth in detail;

units.sanskrit: रूपवत्त्वात्स्पष्टार्थत्वोपपत्तेश्च ।
units.english: and this Divinity of fire has been singled out for this purpose as it has colour and is very clearly perceptible

units.sanskrit: गन्धरसयोरनुदाहरणं त्रयाणामसम्भवात् ।
units.english: That odour and taste have not been included in the illustration, because examples of all the three Fire, Water and Earth are not possible;

units.sanskrit: न हि गन्धरसौ तेजसि स्तः ।
units.english: for instance, there is no odour or taste in Fire

units.sanskrit: स्पर्शशब्दयोरनुदाहरणं विभागेन दर्शयितुमशक्यत्वात् ।
units.english: Similarly, that touch and sound have not been illustrated, because it is impossible to show them separately

units.sanskrit: यदि सर्वं जगत्त्रिवृत्कृतमित्यग्न्यादिवत्त्रीणि रूपाणीत्येव सत्यमग्नेरग्नित्ववदपागाज्जगतो जगत्त्वम् ।
units.english: Thus, then, if the whole Universe has been triplicated, then, just as, in the case of Fire, the Fireness vanished and all that was real was three colours only, so of the Universe also, the universeness should vanish

units.sanskrit: तथान्नस्याप्यप्शुङ्गत्वादाप इत्येव सत्यं वाचारम्भणमात्रमन्नम् ।
units.english: Similarly, Food also being a product of water, Water alone would be the only real element in it, and the Food would be only a modification of words

units.sanskrit: तथापामपि तेजःशुङ्गत्वाद्वाचारम्भणत्वं तेज इत्येव सत्यम् । तेजसो ऽपि सच्छुङ्गत्वाद्वाचारम्भणत्वं सदित्येव सत्यमित्येषोर्ऽथो विवक्षितः ।
units.english: Similarly, Water also being the product of Fire, Water would be a mere modification of words, and Fire would be the only real factor in it Of Fire also,inasmuch as it is the product of Being,Fire would be a mere modification of words, and Being would be the only real factor

units.sanskrit: ननु वाय्वन्तरिक्षे त्वत्रिवृत्कृते तेजः प्रभृतिष्वनन्तर्भूतत्वादवशिष्येते ।
units.english: ObjectionIn the above account Air and AntarikṣaSkyremain untriplicated, as they are not included among Fire and the rest which have been mentioned;

units.sanskrit: एवं गन्धरसशब्दस्पर्शाश्चावशिष्टा इति कथं सता विज्ञातेन सर्वमन्यद्विज्ञातं भवेत्तद्विज्ञाने वा प्रकारान्तरं वाच्यम् ।
units.english: so that they remain untriplicated;similarly, Odour, Taste, Sound and Touch also remain untriplicated;how then can the knowledge of Being make all things known? Or, it behoves you to point out some other way in which these untriplicated things could become known

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not affect the case;

units.sanskrit: रूपवद्द्रव्ये सर्वस्य दर्शनात् ।
units.english: because all these are seen found in coloured substances and colour has been already dealt with

units.sanskrit: तेजसि तावद्रूपवति शब्दस्पर्शयोरप्युलभ्भाद्वाय्वन्तरिक्षयोस्तत्र स्पर्शशब्दगुणवतोः सद्भावो ऽनुमीयते ।
units.english: In what way?In Fire, which is a coloured substance, we perceive Sound and Touch also; and from that it is inferred that Air and Sky also, which have the specific qualities of Touch and Sound respectively, are present in Fire

units.sanskrit: तथाबन्नयो रूपवतो रसगन्धान्तभाव इति ।
units.english: Similarly, Water and Food earth are included in Taste and Odour which are the specific qualities of Water and Air

units.sanskrit: रूपवतां त्रयाणां तेजोबन्नानां त्रिवृत्करणप्रदर्शनेन सर्वं तदन्तर्भूतं सद्विकारत्वात् रूपत्रयवत् विज्ञातं मन्यते श्रुतिः ।
units.english: Thus by showing the triplication of the three coloured substances, Fire, Water and Food,the text thinks that all that is included among those three being the product of Being, comes to be known under ‘three colours’

units.sanskrit: न हि मूर्तं रूपवद्द्रव्यं प्रत्याख्याय वाय्वाकाशयोस्तद्गुणयोर्गन्धरसयोर्वा ग्रहणमस्ति ।
units.english: Ākāśa and Air or their specific qualities, or the qualities of Odour and Taste which are the specific qualities of Earth and Water, are never perceived apart from solid coloured substances

units.sanskrit: अथवा रूपवतामपि त्रिवृत्करणं प्रदर्शनार्थमेव मन्यते श्रुतिः ।
units.english: Or it may be that of coloured substances also, the text has set forth ‘triplication’ only by way of illustrating the triplication of all things

units.sanskrit: यथा तु त्रिवृत्कृते त्रीणि रूपाणीत्येव सत्यं तथा पञ्चीकरणे ऽपि समानो न्याय इत्यतः
units.english: Just as, under the process of ‘triplication’, the only reality is the ‘three qualities’, so also, the same reasons would apply to the process of ‘Quint uplication’ also

units.sanskrit: सर्वस्य सद्विकारत्वात्सता विज्ञातेन सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं स्यात्सदेकमेवाद्वितीयं सत्यमिति सिद्धमेव भवति । तदेकस्मिन्सति विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति सूक्तम् ॥
units.english: Thus it becomes established that all things being the modification of Beings by the knowledge of Being, all things would become known, as‘Being ‘one, without a second Hence, it has been well said that when ‘One Being’ is known, all this becomes known

units.sanskrit: एतद् ध स्म वै तद्विद्वांस आहुः पूर्वे महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियाः ।
units.english: It was on knowing thisthat the ancient great Householders and great Vedic Scholars, said

units.sanskrit: न नो ऽद्य कश्चनाश्रुतम् अमतम् अविज्ञातम् उदाहरिष्यति । इति ह्य् एभ्यो विदां चक्रुः ॥
units.english: For us,there is nothing that any one would point out as being unheard, unthought or unknownand they knew it from these

units.sanskrit: एतद्विद्वांसो विदितवन्तः पूर्वे ऽतिक्रान्ता महाशाला महाश्रोणिया आहुर्ह स्म वै किल ।
units.english: It was on knowing this,when they knew thisthat the ancient great Householders and great Vedic Scholars,of the pastsaid,What did they say?

units.sanskrit: किमुक्तवन्त इत्याहन नो ऽस्माकं कुले ऽद्येदानीं यथोक्तविज्ञानवतां कश्न कश्चिदप्यश्रुतममतमविज्ञातमुदाहरिष्यति
units.english: For us,in our family, we who are possessed of the said knowledge,there is nothing that any one would point out as being unheard, unthought or unknown; no one could point out any such thing;

units.sanskrit: नोदाहरिष्यति सर्वं विज्ञातमेवास्मत्कुलीनानां सद्विज्ञानवत्त्वादित्याभिप्रायः ।
units.english: that is, inasmuch as members of our family would be possessed of the said knowledge, all things would be known to them

units.sanskrit: ते पुनः कथं सर्वं विज्ञातवन्त इत्याहएभ्यस्रिभ्यो रोहितादिरूपेभ्यस्रिवृत्कृतेभ्यो विज्ञातेभ्यः सर्वमप्यन्यच्छिष्टमेवमेवेति विदाञ्चक्रुर्विज्ञातवन्तो यस्मात्तस्मात्सर्वज्ञा
units.english: QuestionHow did these Great Householders know all things? AnswerThey knew it from these;from the knowledge of the three colours, Red and the rest, as triplicated; that is, having known these, they inferred that all that is left would be the same, and thus they knew all things;

units.sanskrit: एव सद्विज्ञानात्त आसुरित्यर्थः ।
units.english: and on account of this knowledge of Being they were omniscient

units.sanskrit: अथवैभ्यो विदाञ्चक्रुरित्यग्न्यादिभ्यो दृष्टान्तेभ्यो विज्ञातेभ्यः सर्वमन्यद्विदाञ्चक्रुरित्येतत् ॥
units.english: Or the meaning of the sentence ‘they knew it from these’ may be that from knowledge of the illustrations of Fire and the rest, they came to know everything

units.sanskrit: यद् उ रोहितम् इवाभूद् इति तेजसस् तद् रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
units.english: Whatever appeared red, they knew it to be the colour of Fire;

units.sanskrit: यद् उ शुक्लम् इवाभूद् इत्य् अपां रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः । यद् उ कृष्णम् इवाभूद् इत्य् अन्नस्य रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ॥
units.english: whatever appeared white, they knew it to be the colour of Water; whatever appeared as black, they knew it to be the colour of Food Earth

units.sanskrit: यद् व् अविज्ञातम् इवाभूद् इत्य् एतासाम् एव देवतानां समास इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
units.english: Whatever appeared to be unknown, they knew it to be a combination of these Divinities

units.sanskrit: यथा नु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवताः पुरुषं प्राप्य त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तन् मे विजानीहीति ॥
units.english: Now, learn, my dear, from me how, on reaching the man, each of these Divinities becomes triplicated

units.sanskrit: कथम् ।
units.english: In what way did they know all?

units.sanskrit: यदन्यद्रूपेण सन्दिह्यमाने कपोतादिरूपे रोहितमिव यद्गृह्यमाणमभूत्तेषां पूर्वेषां ब्रह्मविदां तत्तेजसो रूपमिति विदाञ्चक्रुः तथा यच्छुक्लमिवाभूद्गृह्यमाणं तदापां रूपं यत्कृष्णमिव गृह्यमाणं तदन्नस्येति विदाञ्चक्रुरेवमेवात्यन्तदुर्लक्ष्यं यदु अप्यविज्ञातमिव विशेषतो ऽगृह्यमाणमभूत्तदप्येतासामेव तिसृणां देवतानां समासः
units.english: Whatever else there was in the shape of the Pigeon and the rest, in regard to which there was some doubt,in all this, whatever appeared as red,was perceived as red, by those ancient knowers of Brahman,they knew it to be the colour of Firesimilarly whatever appeáred as white, when perceived, they knew it to be the colour of Water; ‘and whatever appeared as black, when perceived, they knew it to be the colour of Food Earth, Whatever was absolutely imperceptible and hence as if unknown,ie, not distinctly and specifically cognisedthat also they knew to be as combination of these Divinities,ie, an aggregate of these

units.sanskrit: एवं तावद्बाह्यं वस्त्वग्न्यादिवविज्ञातं तथेदानीं यथा नु खलु हे सोम्येमा यथोक्तास्तिस्रो
units.english: Thus, all external things became known, as consisting of Fire and other substances

units.sanskrit: देवताः पुरषं शिरःपाम्यादिलक्षणं कार्यकारणसङ्घातं प्राप्य पुरुषेणोपयुज्यमानास्रिवृत्त्रिवृदेकैका भवति तन्मे विजानीहि निगदत इत्युक्त्वा'ह ॥
units.english: And similarly, my dear, how the said Divinities,on reaching the Man,who is an aggregate of causes and effects, marked by the presence of Head, Hands and other limbs,they come to be used by man,and how each of these becomes triplicated,This, know from me, as proceed to explain

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अन्नम् अशितं त्रेधा विधीयते ।
units.english: Food, eaten, is made threefold;

units.sanskrit: यो मध्यमस् तन् मांसम् । यो ऽणिष्ठस् तन् मनः ॥
units.english: its grossest matter becomes fæces; the middling part, flesh and the subtlest part, mind

units.sanskrit: अन्नमशितं भुक्तं त्रेधा विधीयते जाठरेमाग्निना पच्यमानं त्रिधा विभज्यते ।
units.english: Food, eaten is made threefoldie when digested by the fire in the stomach, it becomes divided into three parts

units.sanskrit: कथं, तस्यान्नस्य त्रिधा विधीयमानस्य यः स्थविष्ठः स्थूलतमो धातुः स्थूलतमं वस्तु विभक्तस्य स्थूलोंऽशस्तत्पुरीषं भवति । यो मध्यमोंऽशो धातुरन्नस्य तद्रसादिक्रमेण परिणम्य मांसं भवति यो ऽणिष्ठो ऽणुतमो धातुः स ऊर्ध्वं हृदयं प्राप्य सूक्ष्मासु हिताख्यासु नाडीप्वनुप्रविस्य वागादिकरणसङ्घातस्य
units.english: In what way?When the food has become threefold, the grossestcoarsestmatter, the heaviest and most voluminous substance,the coarsest part of the divided foodbecomes faeces;the middling matter of the food becomes modified into flesh, step by step, changing through the bodily fluids and other ingredients;the subtlestfinestmatter goes up to the Heart and there enters the fine arteries called the ‘Hitā’ and the rest, and bringing into existence the aggregate of the organs of speech and the rest,ultimately becomes the mind;

units.sanskrit: स्थितिमुत्पादयन्मनो भवति मनोरूपेण विपरिणमन्मनस उपचयं करोति ।
units.english: that is, becoming modified into the form of mind, it goes on adding to the development of that Mind

units.sanskrit: ततश्चान्नोपचितत्वान्मनसो भौतिकत्वमेव न वैशेषिकतन्त्रोक्तलक्षणं नित्यं निरवयं चेति गृह्यते ।
units.english: Thus the Mind, being developed from food, is a material elemental substance, and it is not perceived to be something eternal, and impartible, as defined in the Vaisheṣika system

units.sanskrit: यदपि मनो ऽस्य दैवं चक्षुरिति वक्ष्यति तदपि न नित्यत्वापेक्षया किं तर्हि सूक्ष्मव्यवहितविप्रकृष्टादिसर्वेन्द्रियविषयव्यापकत्वापेक्षया
units.english: Though it is going to be asserted, later on, that ‘the mind is His Divine Eye’ Chāndo xii ,yet, that will not be in view of its eternality, it will be in view of its pervading over all objectives of all senseorgans,even those that are subtle, hidden, remote and so forth

units.sanskrit: यच्चान्येन्द्रियविषयापेक्षया नित्यत्वं तदप्यापेक्षिकमेवेति वक्ष्यामः ।
units.english: As regards its comparative Eternality in comparison to the other senseorgans,that also is merely relative, as we shall explain later on;

units.sanskrit: सदेकमेवाद्वितीयमिति श्रुतेः ॥
units.english: specially as the Vedic Text has declared that ‘Being is one alone, without a second’

units.sanskrit: आपः पीतास् त्रेधा विधीयन्ते ।
units.english: Water, drunk, is made threefold its grossest matter becomes Urine;

units.sanskrit: यो मध्यमस् तल् लोहितम् । यो ऽणिष्ठः स प्राणः ॥
units.english: the middling matter becomes Blood, and the subtlest matter becomes the Lifebreath Prāṇa

units.sanskrit: तथा'पः पीतास्त्रेधा विधीयन्ते तासां यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस्तन्मूत्रं भवति ।
units.english: Similarly, Water, drunk, is made threefold; of this, the grossest material becomes Urine;

units.sanskrit: यो मध्यमस्तल्लोहितं भवति ।
units.english: the middling matter Blood;

units.sanskrit: यो ऽणिष्ठः स प्राणो भवति ।
units.english: and the subtlest matter becomes the LifeBreath;

units.sanskrit: वक्ष्यति ह्यापोमयः प्राणो न पिबतो विच्छेत्स्यत इति ॥
units.english: it is going to be declared that the ‘LifeBreath consisting of water, will never be cut off while the man is drinking it’ Chāndo

units.sanskrit: तेजो ऽशितं त्रेधा विधीयते ।
units.english: vii Fire, eaten, is made threefold;

units.sanskrit: तस्य यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तद् अस्थि भवति ।
units.english: of that, the grossest matter becomes Bone;

units.sanskrit: यो मध्यमः स मज्जा । यो ऽणिष्ठः सा वाक् ॥
units.english: the midddling matter becomes Marrow, and the subtlest matter becomes Speech

units.sanskrit: तथा तेजो ऽशितं तैलघृतादि भक्षितं त्रेधा विधीयते तस्य यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस्तदस्थि भवति ।
units.english: Similarly, Fire, eaten,in the form of oil, clarifiedbutter and the rest;is made threefold; its grossest matter becomes Bone;

units.sanskrit: यो मध्यमःस मज्जास्थ्यन्तर्गतः स्नेहः । यो ऽणिष्ठः सा वाक् ।
units.english: its middling matter becomes Marrow,the only matter inside the Bone;the subtlest matter becomes Speech;

units.sanskrit: तैलघृतादिभक्षणाद्धि वाग्विशदा भाषणे समर्था भवतीति प्रसिद्धं लोके ॥
units.english: by eating oil, clarifiedbutter and other such things, Speech becomes clear, distinct and eloquent,as is wellknown among people

units.sanskrit: अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः ।
units.english: Thus, my dear, Mind is made up of Food;

units.sanskrit: आपोमयः प्राणः । तेजोमयी वाग् इति ।
units.english: Lifebreath is made up Water; and Speech is made up of Fire

units.sanskrit: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘Explain to me again, Revered Sir,’ ‘So be it, my child’ he said

units.sanskrit: यत एवमन्नमयं हि सोम्य मन आपोमयः प्राणस्तेजोमयी वाक् ।
units.english: Because it is as described above, therefore, my dear Mind is [made up of Food, Lifebreath is made up of Water and Speech is made up of Fire

units.sanskrit: ननु केवलान्नभक्षिण आखुप्रभृतयो वाग्मिनः प्राणवन्तश्च तथांमात्रभक्ष्याः
units.english: ObjectionAnimals living on food grains alone, such as, the rat and the like, are possessed of Speech and of Lifebreath without taking water or oils;

units.sanskrit: सामुद्रा मीनमकरप्रभृतयो मनस्विनो वाग्ग्मिनश्च तथा स्नेहपानामपि प्राणवत्त्वं
units.english: similarly, animals living on water alone,such as the fish, allegator and other animals living in the Ocean,are possessed of Mind and are endowed with Speech;

units.sanskrit: चानुमेयं यदि सन्ति तत्र कथमन्नमयं हि सोम्य मन इत्याद्युच्यते ।
units.english: If all this is so, then how can it be said that Mind is made up of food?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: AnswerThis does not affect our position

units.sanskrit: सर्वस्य त्रिवृत्कृतत्वात्सर्वत्र सर्वोपपत्तेः ।
units.english: All things being triplicate in their constitution, everything is possible everywhere

units.sanskrit: न ह्यत्रिवृत्कृतमन्नमश्नाति कश्चिदापो वात्रिवृत्कृताः पीयन्ते तेजो वात्रिवृत्कृतमश्नाति कश्चिदित्यन्नादानामाखुप्रभृतीनां वाग्ग्मित्वं प्राणवत्त्वं
units.english: nor does any one drink Water that is not triplicate, nor does any one eat Fire that is not triplicate in its constitution So that for those who eat Food,such as, rats and the like,there is nothing incongruous in their being endowed with Speech and Lifebreath

units.sanskrit: चेत्याद्यविरुद्धम् । इत्येवं प्रत्यायितः श्वेकेतुराहभूय एव पुनरेव मा मां भगवानन्नमयं हि सोम्य मन इत्यादि विज्ञापयतु दृष्टान्तेनावगमयु नाद्यापि ममास्मिन्नर्थे
units.english: Being thus somewhat convinced, Śvetaketu said‘Revered Sir, explain to me again,how Mind is made up of Food etc, etc, by means of illustrations; as not yet am very sure of all this’

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्तेजोवन्नमयत्वेनाविशिष्टे देह एकस्मिन्नुपयुज्यमानान्यन्नाप्स्नेहजातान्यणिष्ठधातुरूपेण मनःप्राणवाच उपचिन्वन्ति स्वजात्यनतिक्रमेणेति दुर्विज्ञेयमित्यभिप्रायो ऽतो भूय एवेत्याद्याह ।
units.english: What was in Śvetaketu’s mind was this‘It is hard to understand how, in the single body,which consists equally of Fire, Water and Food,when Food, Water and Oils are used, they develop Mind, Lifebreath and Speech respectively, as their subtlest constituents,without transgressing beyond their own essential nature’;

units.sanskrit: तमेवमुक्तवन्तं तथास्तु सोम्येति होवाच पिता शृण्वत्र दृष्टान्तं यथैतदुपपद्यते यत्पृच्छसि ॥
units.english: hence he said ‘Explain again, Sir’ When the son had said this, the Father said‘Be it so, my Boy; listen to the illustrative examples how all this is possible,as you ask’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य पञ्चमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: दध्नः सोम्य मथ्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति । तत् सर्पिर् भवति ॥
units.english: ‘Of the curd, when churned, my dear, the subtlest part rises to the top, and it becomes Butter’

units.sanskrit: दध्नः सोम्य मथ्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमाणुभावः स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति सम्भूयोर्ध्वं नवनूतभावेन गच्छति तत्सर्पिर्भवति ॥
units.english: ‘Of the curd, when churned, my dear, the subtlest part rises to the topgathers togethercomes up as cream, which develops into Butter’

units.sanskrit: एवम् एव खलु सोम्यान्नस्याश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
units.english: ‘So also, when food is eaten, my dear, that which is the subtlest part rises to the top;

units.sanskrit: तन् मनो भवति ॥
units.english: and it becomes Mind’

units.sanskrit: यथायं दृष्टान्त एवमेव खलु सोम्यान्नस्यौदनादेरश्यमानस्य भुज्यमानस्योदर्येमाग्निना वायुसहितेत खजेनेव मथ्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति तन्मनो भवति
units.english: As in the example cited, so also, my dear, when foodin the shape of cooked rice and other things,is eaten,and is churned by the stomachic fire helped by Air, as if by the churning food,its subtlest part rises to the top, and it becomes Mind;

units.sanskrit: मनो ऽवयवैः सह सम्भूय मन उपचिनोतीत्येतत् ॥
units.english: that is, it, becoming mixed with the constituents of the Mind, helps to develop the Mind;this is what is meant’

units.sanskrit: अपां सोम्य पीयमानानां यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
units.english: ‘Of Water, drunk, that which is its subtlest part rises to the top, and it becomes the Lifebreath’

units.sanskrit: सा प्रानो भवति ॥
units.english: and that becomes the Lifebreath

units.sanskrit: तेजसः सोम्याश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
units.english: ‘Of Fire, eaten, the subtlest part rises to the top and it becomes Speech

units.sanskrit: एवमेव खलु सोम्य तेजसो ऽश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति सा वाग्भवति ॥
units.english: Similarly, my dear, when fire is eaten, its subtlest part rises to the top, and it becomes Speech’

units.sanskrit: अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः । आपोमयः प्राणः । तेजोमयी वाग् इति ।
units.english: ‘My dear, Mind is made up of Food, Lifebreath is made up of Water and Speech is made up of Fire’‘Revered Sir, please explain to me again’

units.sanskrit: तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘So be it, my son, he said

units.sanskrit: अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मन आपोमयः प्राणस्तेजोमयी वागिति युक्तमेव मयोक्तमित्यमिप्रायः ।
units.english: ‘My dear, Mind consists of Food, Lifebreath consists of Water, and Speech consists of Fire’,thus that had asserted is right; such is the meaning

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽप्तेजसोरस्त्वेतत्सर्वमेवम् ।
units.english: The Boy thinks as follows‘All this may be so, so far as Water and Fire are concerned;

units.sanskrit: मनस्त्वन्नमयमित्यत्र नैकान्तेन मम निश्चयो जातो ऽतो भूय एव मा भगवान्मनसो ऽन्नमयत्वं दृष्टान्तेन विज्ञापयत्विति ।
units.english: as regards Mind consisting of Food, however, am not yet convinced; and he said‘Revered Sir, please explain to me again‘explain to me by means of illustrations, how Mind is made up of Food’

units.sanskrit: तथा सोम्येति होवाच पिता ॥
units.english: He said‘Be it so, my Boy’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य षष्ठः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: षोडशकलः सोम्य पुरुषः ।
units.english: ‘Man, my dear, is made up of sixteen parts

units.sanskrit: पञ्चदशाहानि माशीः ।
units.english: For fifteen days, do not eat;

units.sanskrit: कामम् अपः पिब ।
units.english: drink as much water as you like;

units.sanskrit: आपोमयः प्राणो न पिबतो विच्छेत्स्यत इति ॥
units.english: Lifebreath is made of water; and if you did not drink water, the Lifebreath would be cut off’

units.sanskrit: अन्नस्य भुक्तस्य यो ऽणिष्ठो धातुः स मनसि शक्तिमधात् सान्नोपचिता मनसः शक्तिः षोडशधा प्रविभज्य पुरुषस्य कलात्वेन
units.english: It has been asserted that the subtlest part of the Food eaten infused force into the Mind; this force, developed through the help accorded by the Food, is divisible into sixteen parts, and is part of the Man;this is what is meant to be asserted here

units.sanskrit: तया मनस्यन्नोपचितया शक्त्या षोडशधा प्रविभक्तया संयुक्तस्तद्वान्कार्यकरणसङ्घातलक्षणो जीवविशिष्टः पिण्डः पुरुषः षोडशकल उच्यते यस्यां सत्यां द्रष्टा श्रोता मन्ता बोद्धा
units.english: As a matter of fact, the man is endowed with this force infused into Mind by Food, and divisible into sixteen partsand being endowed with this, the Man,which here stands for the entire Man consisting of the aggregate of causes and effects in the shape of the physical Body and equipped with the Self Soul; this is the ‘Man that is spoken of here as ‘made up of sixteen parts’

units.sanskrit: कर्ता विज्ञाता सर्वक्रियासमर्थः पुरुषो भवति हीयमानायां च यस्यां सामर्थ्यहानिः ।
units.english: It is only when the said Force of Mind is present that the man becomes capable of seeing, hearing, thinking, cognising, moving, knowing and carrying on all kinds of activities,and all these capacities become lost when the said Force becomes weakened

units.sanskrit: वक्ष्यतिचाथान्नस्या'यी द्रष्टेत्यादि । सर्वस्य कार्यकरणस्य सामर्थ्यं मनःकृतमेव ।
units.english: It is going to be said later on that, ‘It is through Food that one becomes the Seer’ In fact, the capacity of all aggregates of causes and effects is one to the mind;

units.sanskrit: मानसेन हि बलेन सम्पन्ना बलिनो दृश्यन्ते लोके,
units.english: it is only persons endowed with strength of Mind are found to be strong and powerful, in the world

units.sanskrit: ध्यानाहाराश्च केचिदन्नस्य सर्वात्मकत्वात् ।
units.english: In fact, some people are found to feed upon contemplation alone; as food consists of all things

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽन्नकृतं मानसं वीर्यं षोडश कला यस्य पुरुषस्य सो ऽयं षोडशकलः पुरुषः एतच्चेत्प्रत्यक्षीकर्तुमिच्छसि पञ्चदशसंख्याकान्यहानि
units.english: This Virility of Mind brought about by food constitutes the ‘sixteen parts’ of Man; and Man thus is made up of sixteen parts If you wish to perceive this directly, then do not eat for fifteen days;

units.sanskrit: माशीरशनं मा कार्षीः ।
units.english: drink as much water as you like;

units.sanskrit: काममिच्छातो ऽपः पिब यस्मान्नपिबतो ऽपस्ते प्राणो विच्छेत्स्यते विच्छेदमापत्स्यते यस्मादापोमयो ऽब्विकारः प्राण इत्यवोचाम ।
units.english: because if you were not to drink water, your Lifebreath would be cut off; because if your Lifebreath is a product of water, as we have explained already;

units.sanskrit: न हि कार्यं स्वकारणोपष्टम्भमन्तरेणाविभ्रंशमानं स्थातुमुत्सहते ॥
units.english: and a product cannot stay safely, except with the support of its cause

units.sanskrit: स ह पञ्चदशाहानि नाश ।
units.english: For fifteen days he did not eat;

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनम् उपससाद किं ब्रवीमि भो इति । ऋचः सोम्य यजूंषि सामानीति ।
units.english: then he approached him and said‘What shall say, Sir?’‘The Ṛks, the Yajus and the Sāmas, my dear’They do not appear to me, Sir’

units.sanskrit: स हैवं श्रुत्वा मनसो ऽन्नमयत्वं प्रत्यक्षीकर्तुंमिच्छन्पञ्चदशाहानि नाऽशाशनं न कृतवान् । अथ षोडशे ऽहनि हैनं पितरमुपससादोपगतवानुपगम्य चोवाच किं ब्रवीमि भो इति ।
units.english: Having heard this fact of Mind consisting of Food and in order to prove this by direct perception, he did not eat for fifteen days,he did not take any food;on the sixteenth day, he approached his father, and having approached him, he said‘What shall say, Sir?’The father said‘Recite the Ṛks, Yajus and Sāmas, my dear’

units.sanskrit: एवमुक्तः पित्रा'हन वै मा मामृगादीनि मम मनसि न दृश्यन्त इत्यर्थो हे भो भगवन्निति ॥
units.english: Having been thus addressed by his father, he said‘The Ṛks etc do not appear to me; that is, they are not found to my course to my Mind, Sir’

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच यथा सोम्य महतो ऽभ्याहितस्यैको ऽङ्गारः खद्योतमात्रः परिशिष्टः स्यात् । तेन ततो ऽपि न बहु दहेत् । एवं सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानाम् एका कला अतिशिष्टा स्यात् ।
units.english: He said‘Just as, my dear, of a large blazing fire, if a single ember of the size of a firefly is left, it cannot burn any more, than that,so, my dear, of the sixteen parts, only one part should be heft now;

units.sanskrit: तयैतर्हि वेदान् नानुभवसि ।
units.english: by that, therefore, thou dost not perceive the Vedas

units.sanskrit: अशान ।
units.english: Now, eat;

units.sanskrit: अथ मे विज्ञास्यसीति ॥
units.english: then thou wilt know’

units.sanskrit: एवमुक्तवन्तं पिता'हशृणु तत्र कारणं येन ते तान्यृगादीनि न प्रतिभान्तीति (तं होवाच)
units.english: When the son had said as above, the father said‘Hear what the reason is for the fact that the Ṛk etc

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके हे सोम्य महतो महत्परिमाणस्याभ्याहितस्योपचितस्येन्धनैरग्नेरेको ऽङ्गारः खद्योतपरिमाणः शान्तस्य परिशिष्टो ऽवशिष्टः स्याद्भवेत्तेनोङ्गारेण ततो ऽपि तत्परिमाणादीषदपि न बहु दहेदेवमेव खलु सोम्य ते तवान्नोपचितानां षोडशानां कलानामेका कलावयवो
units.english: do not appear to you’ Then he proceeded to say‘In the ordinary world, my dear, just as of a largelargesized,blazing fireburning with fuel,if a single ember of the size of a fireflyas large as a fireflyremained, after the fire has been extinguished,by that ember, even a thing smaller than that ember itself would not be burnt,so my dear, of thy sixteen parts,nourished by food,only one partportion,should be left now;

units.sanskrit: कलावयवो ऽतिशिष्टा स्यात्तया त्वं खद्योतमात्राङ्गारतुल्ययैतर्हीदानीं वेदान्नानुभवसि न प्रतिपद्यसे,
units.english: therefore, by that partwhich must be of the same size as the fireember of the size of firefly,thou dost not perceive the Vedas,thou dost remember them;

units.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा च मे मम वाचमथाशेषं विज्ञास्यस्यशान भुङ्क्ष्व तावत् ॥
units.english: after hearing my discourse, thou wilt know it all,now eat’

units.sanskrit: अथ हैनम् उपससाद ।
units.english: Then he ate; and approached him;

units.sanskrit: तं ह यत् किं च पप्रच्छ सर्वं ह प्रतिपेदे ॥
units.english: whatever he asked him, he knew it all

units.sanskrit: स ह तथैवाऽश भुक्तवानथानन्तरं हैनं पितरं शुश्रूषुरुपससाद
units.english: Then he ate; and after that with a view to attending upon his father, he approached him;

units.sanskrit: तं होपगतं पुत्रं यत्किञ्चर्गादिषु पप्रच्छ ग्रन्थरूपमर्थजातं वा पिता स
units.english: when he saw his son, whatever hethe fatherasked himeither words of the text or their contents,heŚvetaketuknew itṚk and the restall, ie the text as well as the contents

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच । यथा सोम्य महतो ऽभ्याहितस्यैकम् अङ्गारं खद्योतमात्रं परिशिष्टं तं तृनैर् उपसमाधाय प्राज्वलयेत् तेन ततो ऽपि बहु दहेत् ॥
units.english: He said to him‘Just as, my dear, of a large blazing fire, if a single ember, of the size of a firefly, is left,if one were to flare it up by means of grasses, it would burn even more than that

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच पुनः पिता यथा सोम्य महतो ऽभ्याहितास्येत्यादि समानमेकमङ्गारं शान्तस्याग्नेः खद्योतमात्रं परिशिष्टं तं तृणैश्चूर्णैश्चोपसमाधाय प्राज्वलयेद्वर्धयेत् । तेनेद्धेनाङ्गारेण ततो ऽपि पूर्वपरिमाणाद्बहु दहेत् ॥
units.english: The Father said to him again‘Just as, my dear, of a large blazing fire, if a single ember etc, etc,as beforeof the extinguished fire, of the size of a firefly, is left,if one were to flare it upto make it large,by means of grasses and powders,then, by this kindled ember, one would burn even more than the former size

units.sanskrit: एवं सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानाम् एका कलातिशिष्टाभूत् ।
units.english: ‘So, my dear, of thy sixteen parts, only one part remained, and that being nourished by food, was made to flare up;

units.sanskrit: तयैतर्हि वेदान् अनुभवसि ।
units.english: and by that thou perceivest the Vedas

units.sanskrit: अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः । आपोमयः प्राणः । तेजोमयी वाग् इति । तद् धास्य विजज्ञाव् इति विजज्ञाव् इति ॥
units.english: Thus, the Mind is made up of Food, the Lifebreath is made up of Water, and Speech is made up of FireThen he understood it,yea, he understood it

units.sanskrit: एवं सोम्य ते षोडशानामन्नकलानां सामर्थ्यरूपाणामेका कलातिशिष्टाभूदतिशिष्टा'सीत्पञ्चदशाहान्यभुक्तवत एकैकेनाह्नैकैका कला चन्द्रमस इवापरपक्षे क्षीणा सातिशिष्टा कला तवान्नेन भुक्तेनोपसमाहिता
units.english: ‘So, my dear, of thy sixteen parts,the parts of food, which represent strength,only one was left,the other fifteen parts disappeared one by one, day by day, like the digits of the Moon during the darker fortnight;this remaining part, nourishedenlarged and magnifiedby Food, was made to flare up;the correct form is ‘Prājvāli’, elongation of the final ‘ī’ is a Vedic anomaly;

units.sanskrit: प्राज्वालीदिति पाठान्तरं तदा तेनोपसमाहिता स्वयं प्रज्वलितवतीर्यर्थः ।
units.english: ‘Prājvālīt’ is another reading, under which the meaning would be that it flared up of itself

units.sanskrit: तया वर्धितयैतर्हीदानीं वेदाननुभवस्युपलभसे ।
units.english: By thatas thus enlargedthounow perceivest the Vedas,you remember them

units.sanskrit: एवं व्यावृत्त्यनुवृत्तिभ्यामन्नामयत्वं मनसः सिद्धमित्युपसंहरत्यन्नमयं हि सोम्य मन इत्यादि ।
units.english: Thus, the fact of the Mind being made up of food is demonstrated by positive as well as negative illustrations; and recapitulating all that he has said, the father said‘Thus, the Mind is made up of Food etc, etc

units.sanskrit: यथैतन्मनसो ऽन्नमयत्वं तव सिद्धं तथा'पोमयः प्राणस्तेजोमयी वागित्येतदपि सिद्धमेवेत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: That is, just as the fact of the Mind being made up of Food has been demonstrated to thee, so also has been demonstrated the fact of the Lifebreath consisting of Water and of Speech consisting of Fire

units.sanskrit: तदेतद्धास्य पितुरुक्तं मन आदीनामन्नादिमयत्वं विजज्ञौ विज्ञातवाञ्श्वेतकेतुः ।
units.english: Then he understood it,what the father taught about Mind being made up of food, heŚvetaketuunderstood

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यासस्त्रिवृत्करणप्रकरणसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the treatment of the subject of Triplication

units.sanskrit: उद्दालको हारुणिः श्वेतकेतुं पुत्रम् उवाच स्वप्नान्तं मे सोम्य विजानीहीति ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse UddālakaĀruṇi said to his son, Śhvetaketu ‘Learn from me, my dear, the ultimate stage of sleep

units.sanskrit: यत्रैतत् पुरुषः स्वपिति नाम सता सोम्य तदा संपन्नो भवति । स्वम् अपीतो भवति ।
units.english: When a man is said to be sleeping, then, my dear, does he become imbued with Being, and goes to his own

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् एनं स्वपितीत्य् आचक्षते । स्वं ह्य् अपीतो भवति ॥
units.english: Hence, people say ‘he sleeps’ Svapiti, because he is gone to his own’

units.sanskrit: यस्मिन्मनसि जीवेना'त्मनानुप्रविष्टा परा देवता'दर्श इव पुरुषः प्रतिबिम्बेन जलादिविष्विव च सूर्यादयः प्रतिबिम्बैः । तन्मनो ऽन्नमयं तेजो ऽंमयाभ्यां वाक्प्राणाभ्यां संगतमधिगतम् ।
units.english: The Mind which was entered into by the Supreme Deity, through the ‘Living Self’ Individualised,just as the man enters into the mirror through his reflection, or as the Sun and other bodies enter into water and other reflecting surfaces, through their reflection and that Mind made up of Food, because combined with Speech and Lifebreath made up of Fire and Water respectively;all this has been understood

units.sanskrit: यन्मयो यत्स्थश्च जीवो मननदर्शनश्रवणादिव्यावहाराय कल्पते तदुपरमे च स्वं देवतारूपमेव प्रतिपद्यते ।
units.english: And that this combined Trinity is what the ‘Living Self’ consists of, and wherein resident, he is enabled to carry on the functions of reflecting, seeing, hearing and so forth,•and on the cessation of which he reverts to his own form of the Deity

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं श्रुत्यन्तरेध्यायतीव लेलायतीव सधीः स्वप्नो भूत्वेमं लोकमतिक्रामतिस वा आयमात्मा ब्रह्म विज्ञानमयो मनोमयैत्यादि,
units.english: ‘As if reflecting, as if scintillating, becoming dream, he passes beyond the world’ Bṛhadā iv ‘This Self indeed is Brahman’ Bṛhadā iv ‘Consisting of cognitions, consisting of the Mind’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: स्वप्नेन शारीरम् इत्यादि,
units.english: iv ‘Through dream, entering the body etc,’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: प्राणन्नेव प्राणो नाम भवतीत्यादि च ।
units.english: ‘While breathing, he becomes the LifeBreath’ Bṛhadā iv and so forth

units.sanskrit: तस्यास्य मनःस्थस्य मन आख्यां गतस्य मनौपशमद्वारेणेन्द्रियविषयेभ्यो निवृत्तस्य यस्यां परस्यां देवतायां स्वात्मभातायां यदवस्थानं तत्पुत्राया'चिख्यासुरुद्दालको ह किला'रुणिः श्वेतकेतुं पुत्रमुवाचोक्तवान् ।
units.english: Now this ‘Living Self’, subsisting in the Mind and coming to be called by the name of ‘Mind’, becomes turned away from the objects of senseexperience, on the cessation of the Mind, and retires into and subsists in the Supreme Deity which is his own Self;in order to explain all this to his son,UddālakaĀruṇi, said to his son, Śvetaketu, as follows

units.sanskrit: स्वप्नान्तं स्वप्नमध्यं स्वप्न इति दर्शनवृत्तेः स्वप्नस्या'ख्या तस्य मध्यं स्वप्नान्तं सुषुप्तमित्येतत् । अथवा स्वप्नान्तं स्वप्नसतत्त्वमित्यर्थः तत्राप्यर्थात्सुषुप्तमेव भवति । स्वमपीतो भवतीति वचनात् ।
units.english: ‘Learn from me the ultimate stage of sleep;’ie the internal cere of sleep sleep’ is the name of that stage of sleep during which consciousness is still functioning; and the ‘internal core’ or ‘ultimate stage’ is Deep sleep; or the term ‘Svapnānta’ may be interpreted as the ‘satattva’, cause, ‘of Svapna’, of sleep; thus too it would stand for Deep sleep that such is the meaning is also indicated by the assertion ‘He goes to his own’;

units.sanskrit: न ह्यन्यत्र सुषुप्तात्स्वमपीतिं जीवस्येच्छन्ति ब्रह्मविदः । तत्र ह्यादर्शापनयने पुरुषप्रतिबिम्बि आदर्शगतो यथा स्वमेव पुरुषमपीतो भवत्येवं मन आद्युपरमे चैतन्यप्रतिबिम्बरूपेण जीवेना'त्मना मनसि प्रविष्टा नामरूपव्याकरणाय परा देवता सा स्वमेवा'त्मानं प्रतिपद्यते जीवरूपतां मन आख्यां हित्वा ।
units.english: because apart from Deep sleep, there is no condition during which the Knowers of Brahman regard the ‘Living Self’ as ‘going to his own Just as, when the mirror has been removed, the reflection of the man in the mirror ‘goes into its own,’ that is, the Man self himself,in the same manner, when the Mind and other senseorgans have ceased to exist, the Supreme Deity, which had entered the Mind through the ‘Living Self’, for the purpose of differentiating Names and Forms goes to Its own Self, after having abandoned the ‘living individualised form called ‘Mind’

units.sanskrit: अतः सुषुप्त एव स्वप्नान्तशब्दवाच्य इत्यवगम्यते । यत्र तु सुप्तः स्वप्नान्पश्यति तत्स्वाप्नं दर्शनं सुखदुःखसंयुक्तमिति पुण्यापुण्ययोर्हि सुखदुःखारम्भकत्वं प्रसिद्धम् ।
units.english: From all this it follows that it is Deep sleep that is meant by the term ‘ultimate stage of sleep’That stage of sleep during which one sees dreams, is ‘Dreamcognition’ which is accompanied by pleasure and pain, and as such is the effect of Merit and Demerit; it is wellknown that Merit and Demerit are productive of Pleasure and Pain;

units.sanskrit: पुण्यापुण्ययोश्चाविद्याकामोपष्टम्भेनैव सुखदुःखतद्दर्शनकार्यारम्भकत्वमुपपद्यते नान्यथेत्यविद्याकामकर्मभिः संसारहेतुभिः संयुक्त
units.english: as for merit and demerit again, they can be productive of such effects as Pleasure and Pain and their cognition only through the momentum imparted by Ignorance and Desire, never otherwise; hence, Dreamcognition is always combined with such causes of Birth and Rebirth as Ignorance; Desire and Kārmic Residua;

units.sanskrit: एव स्वप्न इति न स्वमपीता भवति ।
units.english: so that in this condition, the Self cannot be gone to his own

units.sanskrit: अनन्वागतं पुण्येनानन्वागतं पापेन तीर्णो हि तदा सर्वाञ्छोकान्हृदयस्य भवतितद्वा अस्यैतदतिच्छन्दाएष परम आनन्दैत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः
units.english: That this is so is clear from such Vedic texts as‘Not followed by Merit, not followed by Demerit’ Bṛhadā iii ‘Then he has crossed beyond all sorrows of the heart’ Bṛhadā iii ‘This is absolute freedom, it is Supreme Bliss’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: सुषुप्त एव स्वं देवतारूपं जीवत्वविनिर्मुक्तं दर्शयिष्यामीत्याह ।
units.english: What thus the Father said was that ‘ am going to show that it is only Deep Sleep the Supreme Deity rests in its own Divine Form, entirely freed from the character of the ‘Living Individualised Self’;

units.sanskrit: स्वप्नान्तं मे मम निगदतो हे सोम्य विजानीहि विस्पष्टमवधारयेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: which is what is meant by the assertion ‘learn from ṇiewhile am expounding itmy dear, the ultimate stage of Sleepplease grasp it carefully and clearly

units.sanskrit: कदा स्वप्नान्तो भवतीत्युच्यते ।
units.english: It is now going to be explained when the ‘ultimate stage of sleep’ is reached

units.sanskrit: यत्र यस्मिन्काल एतन्नाम भवति पुरुषस्य स्वप्स्यतः । प्रसिद्धं हि लोके स्वपितीति । गौणं चेदं नामेत्याह । यदा स्वपितीत्युच्यते पुरुषस्तदा तस्मिन्काले सता सच्छब्दवाच्यया प्रकृतया देवतया संपन्नो भवति संगत एकीभूतो भवति ।
units.english: When,at which timethis name is applied to the man who is going to sleep,the wellknownnamethat ‘he is sleeping’;this name is indirect, figurative;so that the meaning is‘when the Man is said to be sleepingat that time does he become imbued with Being,ie imbued, united, merged in, the Supreme Deity spoken of as ‘Being’;

units.sanskrit: मनसि प्रविष्टं मन आदिसंसर्गकृतं जीवरूपं परित्यज्य स्वं सद्रूपं यत्परमार्थसत्यमपीतो ऽपिगतो भवति ।
units.english: abandoning the form of the ‘Living Self’ due to his entering into the Mind and becoming connected with the Mind and other organs,he goes to his own, retires to his own form of ‘Being’, which is really true;

units.sanskrit: अतस्तस्मात्स्वपितीत्येनमाचक्षते लोकिकाः ।
units.english: and it is for this reason that people say ‘He sleeps Svapiti, because he is gone to his own, ie to his own Self

units.sanskrit: स्वमात्मानं हि यस्मादपीतो भवति ।
units.english: The sense is that the said going to his own is indicated by the wellknown nature and name of sleep

units.sanskrit: ततश्चा'यस्तानां करणानामनेकव्यापारनिमित्तग्लानानां स्वव्यापारेभ्य उपरमो भवति ।
units.english: What happens is that during the waking state, man becomes fatigued through experiencing exertions involved in the pleasures and pains brought about by Merit and Demerit,the organs also, becoming tired by numerous functionings, retire from further functioning;

units.sanskrit: श्रुतेश्चश्राम्यत्येव वाक्श्राम्यति चक्षुर् इत्येवमादि ।
units.english: this is what has been thus declared in Vedic texts ‘Speech is tired, Eye is tired’ etc, etc, Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: तथा चगृहीता वाग्गृहीतं श्रोत्रं गृहीतं मनैत्येवमादीनि करणानि प्राणग्रस्तानि ।
units.english: and again, ‘Speech’ is held up, Eye is held up, Mind is held up’, Bṛhadā i

units.sanskrit: प्राण एको ऽश्रान्तो देहे कुलाये यो जागर्ति तदा जीवः श्रमापनुत्तये स्वं देवतारूपमात्मानं प्रतिपद्यते ।
units.english: which shows that the organs are all swallowed up by the Lifebreath;it is Lifebreath alone which is not tired and lies awake in the nest of the body; it is in this state that the ‘Living Self for the removal of fatigue, retired into its own self, in the form of the Deity;

units.sanskrit: नान्यत्र स्वरूपावस्थानाच्छ्रमापनोदः स्यादिति युक्ता प्रसिद्धिर्लौकिकानां स्वं ह्यपीतो भवतीति ।
units.english: inasmuch as no removal of fatigue would be possible apart from this resting within his own, it is only right that people should entertain the idea that ‘he is gone to his own’

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते हि लोके ज्वरादिरोगग्रस्तानां तद्विनिर्नोके स्वात्मस्थानां विश्रमणं तद्वदिहापि स्यादिति युक्तम् ।
units.english: In the ordinary world, it is seen that when people suffering from fever and other diseases are cured of them, they regain their own and rest; similar is the case here also’, hence, what has been said is quite right;

units.sanskrit: तद्यथा श्येनो वा सुपर्णो वा विपरिपत्य श्रान्तैत्यादिश्रुतेष्च ॥
units.english: this has also been made clear by such texts as ‘just as, the Kite or the Heron having flown and becoming tired etc, etc,’ Bṛhadā iii

units.sanskrit: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनम् अलब्ध्वा बन्धनम् एवोपश्रयते । एवम् एव खलु सोम्य तन् मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनम् अलब्ध्वा प्राणम् एवोपश्रयते ।
units.english: ‘Just as, a bird tied to a string, having flown in several directions and finding no resting place elsewhere, settles down at the place to which it is fastened,so also the Mind, my dear, flying in several directions and finding no resting place elsewhere, settles down at the Lifebreath;

units.sanskrit: प्राणबन्धनं हि सोम्य मन इति ॥
units.english: because, my boy, the Mind is fastened to the Lifebreath’

units.sanskrit: तत्रायं दृष्टान्तो यथोक्तेर्ऽथेस यथा शकुनिः पक्षी शकुनिघातकस्य हस्तगतेन सूत्रेण प्रबद्धः पाशितो दिशं दिशं बन्धनमोक्षार्थी सन्प्रतिशिदिशं पतित्वान्यत्र बन्धनादायतनमाश्रयं विश्रमणायालब्ध्वाप्राप्य बन्धनमेवोपश्रयते । एवमेव यथायं दृष्टान्तः खलु हे सोभ्य तन्मनस्तत्प्रकृतं पोडशकलमन्नोपचितं
units.english: The following example illustrates what has been said above Just as, a bird, tied to a stringin the hands of the Birdkiller,having flown in several directions, with a view to extricate himself from the bondage, having flown in all directions,and finding no resting place support for restelsewhereapart from the place to which it is fastened,settles down at the place to which it is fastened;in the same manner, as has been seen in this example cited, the Mind,which has been the subjectmatter of our conversation, which has been found to have sixteen parts developed by food;

units.sanskrit: मनो निर्धारितं ततेप्रविष्टस्तत्स्थस्तदुपलक्षितो जीवस्तन्मन इति निर्दिश्यते मञ्चाक्रोशनवत् । स मन आख्योपाधिर्जीवो ऽविद्याकामकर्मोपदिष्टां दिशं दिशं सुखदुःखादिलक्षणां जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोः पतित्वा गत्वानुभूयेत्यर्थः । अन्यत्र सदाख्यात्स्वात्मन आयतनं विश्रमणस्थानमलब्ध्वा प्राणमेव प्राणेन सर्वकार्यकरणाश्रयेणोपलक्षिता प्राण इत्युच्यते सदाख्या परा
units.english: the term ‘Mind’ stands for the ‘Living Self’ entering and residing in the Mind and characterised by it,just as, when it is said that ‘the Raised platform shouts’, the terrp ‘Raised platform’ stands for the man on the platform;now, this ‘Living Self’ along with its limiting adjunct called ‘Mind’,having flown in several directions, in the shape of pleasure and pain and other experiences during the waking state and during dreams led thither by his ignorance, desires and Kārmic Residua,ie having experienced all these,and not finding any resting place,shelter for restingelsewhereapart from his own Self called ‘Being’,settles down at the Lifebreath;the term ‘Prāṇa’, ‘Lifebreath here stands for the Supreme Deity named ‘Being’ as characterised circumscribed by the aggregate of all causes and effects,as is indicated by such Vedic texts as‘the Lifebreath of lifebreath, Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: देवता ।
units.english: iv

units.sanskrit: प्राणस्य प्राणंप्राणशरीरो भारूपैत्यादिश्रुतेः । अतस्तां देवतां प्राणं प्राणाख्यामेवोपश्रयते ।
units.english: ‘Having Lifebreath for his body, in the form of Light etc’ Hence, it is this ‘Lifebreath the Deity named ‘Lifebreath’, at which he settles down

units.sanskrit: प्राणो बन्धनं यस्य मनसस्तत्प्राणबन्धनं हि यस्मात्सोम्य मनः प्राणोपलक्षितदेवताश्रयं मन इति तदुपलक्षितो जीव इति ॥
units.english: ‘Because, my dear, Mind is fastened to the Lifebreath‘Mind’ here standing for that Mind in which the said Deity is resting,that is, the ‘Living Self’ characterised by the said ‘Mind’

units.sanskrit: अशनापिपासे मे सोम्य विजानीहीति ।
units.english: ‘Learn from me, my dear, what Hunger and Thirst are

units.sanskrit: यत्रैतत् पुरुषो ऽशिशिषति नामाप एव तद् अशितं नयन्ते ।
units.english: When such and such a Man desires to eat, Water is carrying away what has been eaten by him before

units.sanskrit: तद् यथा गोनायो ऽश्वनायः पुरुषनाय इत्य् एवं तद् अप आचक्षते ऽशनायेति ।
units.english: Hence, just as, they speak of the cowcarrier, the horsecarrier and the mancarrier, so they speak of water as the foodcarrier

units.sanskrit: तत्रैतच् छुङ्गम् उत्पतितं सोम्य विजानीहि ।
units.english: Thus, my dear, know this to be the sprout shot up;

units.sanskrit: नेदम् अमूलं भविष्यतीति ॥
units.english: and it could not be without a root

units.sanskrit: एवं स्वपितिनामप्रसिद्धिद्वारेण यज्जीवस्य सत्यस्वरूपं जगतो मूलं तत्पुत्रस्य दर्शयित्वा'हान्नादिकार्यकारणपरम्परयापि जगतो मूलं सद्दिदर्शयिषुः ।
units.english: The father has so far shown to the son that the root of the universe lies in the real form of the ‘Living Self’ through the wellknown name ‘Svapiti’ sleep; and now he is going to show by tracing the series of causes and effects, from Food onwards that the same Being is the root of the Universe

units.sanskrit: अशनापिपासे अशितुमिच्छाशना यालोपेन । पातुमिच्छा पिपासा ते अशनापिपासे अशनापिपासयोः सतत्वं विजानीहीत्येतत् ।
units.english: ‘Hunger and Thirst’;hunger is desire for eating’; the changes due to the desiderative affix being dropped;thirst is ‘desire for drinking’; the two together are ‘Hunger and Thirst’;

units.sanskrit: यत्र यस्मिन्काल एतन्नाम पुरुषो भवति ।
units.english: It is as followsWhen,at what timesuch and such naming the man;man desires to eat;

units.sanskrit: तदा तस्य पुरुषस्य किनिमित्तं नाम भवतीत्याह ।
units.english: QuestionWhy is the man so called as desiring to eat?

units.sanskrit: यत्तत्पुरुषेणाशितमन्नं कठिनं पोता आपो नयन्ते द्रवीकृत्य रसादिभावेन विपरिणमयन्ते तदा भुक्तमन्नं जीर्यति ।
units.english: AnswerWhatever solid food had been eaten by him,all that the water he has drunk is carrying away,ie it liquified the solid food turning it into juices and then it is that the food eaten becomes digested;

units.sanskrit: अथ च भवत्यस्य नामाशिशिषतीति गौणम् ।
units.english: and when he is said to be ‘desirous of eating’, this appellation is applied to him only figuratively

units.sanskrit: जीर्णे ह्यन्ने ऽशितुमिच्छति सर्वो हि जन्तुः ।
units.english: It is a wellknown fact, all animals become hungry only when the food they had eaten has become digested

units.sanskrit: तत् तत्र अपामशितनेतृत्वादशनाया इति नाम प्रसिद्धमित्येतस्मिन्नर्थे । यथा गोनायो गां नयतीति गोनाय इत्युच्यते गोपालः । तथाश्वान्नयतीत्यश्वनायो ऽश्वपाल इत्युच्यते ।
units.english: Thus, then, inasmuch as water carries the food that has been eaten, it comes to be known as ‘foodarrier’; and in support of this usage there are the following examples the cowherd is called the ‘cowcarrier’ because he carriesleads alongthe cows;

units.sanskrit: पुरुषनायः पुरुषान्नयतीति राजा सेनापतिर्वा ।
units.english: the groom is called the ‘horsecarrier’, because he carriesleadsthe horses; the king or the armycommander is called ‘mancarrier because he carriesleadsthe men

units.sanskrit: एवं तत्तदाप आचक्षते लौकिका अशनायेति विसर्जनीयलोपेन ।
units.english: It is thus that people, in ordinary usage, come to call Water

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सत्यद्भी रसादिभावेन नीतेनाशितेनान्नेन निष्पादितमिदं शरीरं वटकणिकायामिव शुङ्गो ऽङ्कुर उत्पतित उद्गतस्तमिमं शुङ्गं कार्यं शरीराख्यं वटादिशुङ्गवदुत्पतितं
units.english: Such being the case, this body is nourished by the food which is carried along, in the shape of juices, by Water,is like the sprout that has shot out of the seed of the fig tree; therefore, my dear, know thisproduct called ‘Body’ to be a sprout shot out like the sprout of the fig and other trees

units.sanskrit: किं तत्र विज्ञेयमित्युच्यते ।
units.english: QuestionWhat is there to be known in this?

units.sanskrit: शुण्विदं शुङ्गवत्कार्यत्वाच्छरीरं नामूलं मूलरहितं भविष्यतीत्युक्त आह श्वेतकेतुः ॥
units.english: AnswerListen; the Body, being a product like the sprout, cannot be without a root Having been told thisŚvetaketu said as follows

units.sanskrit: तस्य क्व मूलं स्याद् अन्यत्रान्नात् । एवम् एव खलु सोम्यान्नेन शुङ्गेनापो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
units.english: ‘Where could its root be apart from food? So, my boy, from food as the sprout, infer water as the root;

units.sanskrit: अद्भिः सोम्य शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलम् अन्विच्छ । तेजसा सोम्य शुङ्गेन सन्मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
units.english: from water as the sprout, infer fire as the root; from fire as the sprout, infer the Being as the root

units.sanskrit: सन्मूलाः सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सदायतनाः सत्प्रतिष्ठाः ॥
units.english: All these creatures, my dear, have their root in Being, reside in Being and rest in Being

units.sanskrit: यद्येवं समूलमिदं शरीरं वटादिशुङ्गवत्तस्यास्य क्व मूलं स्याद्भवेदित्येवं पृष्ट आह पिता । तस्य क्व मूलं स्यादन्यत्रान्नादन्नं मूलमित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: Śvetaketu said‘If the body has a root, like the sprout of the fig and other trees, and where could the root of the Body be?’Being thus asked, the father said‘Where could its root be, apart from food?, that is to say, food is the root of the body

units.sanskrit: कथम् । अशितं ह्यन्नमद्भिर्द्रवीकृतं जाठरेणाग्निना पच्यमानं रसभावेन परिणमते । रसोच्छोणितं शोणितान्मांसं मांसान्मेदो मेदसो ऽस्थीन्यस्थिभ्यो मज्जा मज्जायाः शुक्रम् । तथा योषिद्भुक्तं चान्नं रसादिक्रमेणैवं परिणतं लोहितं भवति । ताभ्यां शुक्रशोणिताभ्यामन्नकार्याभ्यां संयुक्ताभ्यामन्नेनैव प्रत्यहं भुज्यमानेना'पूर्यमाणाभ्यां
units.english: In what way?when food is eaten, it is liquified by water,it is cooked by the stomachic fire, and then becomes changed into juices, from the juices, proceeds Blood, from Blood, Fleshfrom Flesh, Fatfrom Fat, Bonesfrom Bones, Marrow,from Marrow, Semen;similarly when Food eaten by the woman, becomes modified, in the same way, into blood ovular;it is by these twosemen and ovular blood come together,which are the products of food, and which are fostered and nourished by the food eaten day by day,that the body becomes developed, and built up just as the wall is built up day by day by lumps of clay laid onand thus does this sprout of the body become accomplished out of food as its root

units.sanskrit: कुड्यमिव मृत्पिण्डैः प्रत्युहमुपचीयमानो ऽन्नमूलो देहशुङ्गः परिनिष्पन्न इत्यर्थः । यत्तु देहशुङ्गो ऽन्नमूल एवमेव खलु सोम्यान्नेन शुह्गेन कार्यभूतेनापो मूलमन्नस्य शुङ्गस्यान्विच्छ प्रतिपद्यस्व । अपामपि विनाशोत्पत्तिमत्तवाच्छुङ्गत्वमेवेति अद्भिः सीम्य शुङ्गेन कार्येण कारणं तेजो मूलमन्विच्छ । तेजसो ऽपि विनाशोत्पत्तिमत्तवाच्छुङ्गत्वमिति तेजसा सोम्य शुङ्गेन सन्मूलमेकमेवाद्वितीयं परमार्थसत्यम् ।
units.english: As regards the Food which has been pointed out as the sprout of the Body, that food also, like the body, is liable to production and destruction, and as such, it also is a sprout that has shot out of a root;with this idea in his mind, he says‘Just as the sprout of the body has its root in food, so, my dear, from the food as sproutwhich is a product, effect,infeiunderstandwater as the root of the sprout in the shape of Food;water also is liable to production and destruction, and hence, it also is a sprout, hence, from water as sprouta product,my dear, infer as its Cause, Root, Fire;inasmuch as Fire also is liable to production and destruction, that also is a sprout;

units.sanskrit: यस्मिन्सर्वमिदं वाचा'रम्भणं विकारो नामधेयमनृतं रज्ज्वामिव सर्पादिविकल्पजातमध्यस्तमविद्यया
units.english: all the Universe is a mere modification of words, a mere name,superimposed by Nescience, upon the said Being,in the same manner as the Serpent and other imaginary things are superimposed upon the Rope;

units.sanskrit: तदस्य जगतो मूलमतः सन्मूलाः सत्कारणा हे सोम्येमाः स्थावरजङ्गमलक्षणाः सर्वाः
units.english: hence, this Being is the root of the Universe Hence, my dear, all the creaturesin the shape of animate and inanimate thingshave their rootcause in Being

units.sanskrit: प्रजा न केवलं सन्मूला एवेदानीमपि स्थितिकाले सदायतनाः सदाश्रया एव । नहि मृदमनाश्रित्य घटादेः सत्त्वं स्थितिर्वास्ति ।
units.english: It is not only that they have their root in Being,even now, during the time of their existence, they reside in Beingsubsisting in Being itself; as for example, without subsisting in clay, the jar has no existence or continuance;

units.sanskrit: अतो मृद्वत्सन्मूत्वात्प्रजानां सदायतनं यासां ताः सदायतनाः प्रजाः ।
units.english: hence, as Being is the root of all creatures,like the clay of jar etc These creatures reside in Being;

units.sanskrit: अन्ते च सत्प्रतिष्ठाः सदेव प्रतिष्टा लयः समाप्तिपवसानं परिशेषो यासां ताः सत्प्रतिष्ठाः ॥
units.english: and at the end they rest in Being,that is, they have their rest,they become merged,and have their end, in the same said Being

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्रैतत् पुरुषः पिपासति नाम तेज एव तत् पीतं नयते ।
units.english: ‘Now, when such and ṣuch a man desires to drink, fire is carrying away what has been drunk by him before

units.sanskrit: तद् यथा गोनायो ऽश्वनायः पुरुषनाय इत्य् एवं तत् तेज आचष्ट उदन्येति । तत्रैतद् एव शुङ्गम् उत्पतितं सोम्य विजानीहि ।
units.english: Hence, just as they speak of the cowcarrier, the horsecarrier and the mancarrier, so they speak of the fire as watercarrier, Thus, my dear, know this to be the sprout shot up;

units.sanskrit: नेदम् अमूलं भविष्यतीति ॥
units.english: it could not be without a root’

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीमप्शुङ्गद्वारेण सतो मूलस्यानुगमः कार्य इत्याह । यत्र यस्मिन्काल एतन्नाम पिपासति पातुमिच्छतीति पुरुषो भवति ।
units.english: Proceeding to show that through water as sprout, Being is the root here also, he says‘When,at which time, such and such a mannaming himdesires to drinkthat is, becomes a man desirous oj drinking;

units.sanskrit: अशिशिषतीतिवदिदमपि गौणमेव नाम भवति ।
units.english: like ‘desires to eat the phrase ‘desires to drink’ also is only a figurative name for the Man

units.sanskrit: द्रवीकृतस्याशितस्यान्नस्य नेत्र्य आपो ऽन्नशुङ्गं देहं क्लेदयन्त्यः शिथिली कुर्युरब्बाहुल्याद्यदि तेजसा न शोष्यन्ते ।
units.english: When food eaten has been liquified, water carries it away; when they thus set the foodsprout, Body, it would, through excess of water, make the body benumbed, if the water died,become dried upby fire;

units.sanskrit: नितरां च तेजसा शोष्यमाणा स्वप्सु देहभावेन परिणममानासु पातुमिच्छा पुरुषस्य जायते तदा पुरुषः पिपासति नाम तदेतदाह ।
units.english: when the water is being dried up, and the water is becoming developed into the Body, there arises desire to drink, in the man, and then it is said that ‘the man desires to drink’

units.sanskrit: तेज एव तत्तदा पीतमबादि शोषयद्देहगतलोहितप्राणभावेन नयते परिणमयति ।
units.english: And when fire is drying up the water that has been drunk, it carries and modifies this water into Blood and Lifebreath

units.sanskrit: तद्यथा गोनाय इत्यादि समानमेवं तत्तेज आचष्टे लोक उदन्येत्युदकं नयतीत्युदन्यम् । उदन्येतीति च्छान्दसं तत्रापि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: Just as they speak of the cowcarrier, etc, etc,as before;so they speak of Fire as the watercarrier,‘Udanya’, watercarrier, being that which carries nayati water udaka ;

units.sanskrit: अपामप्येतदेव शरीराख्यं शुङ्गं नान्यदित्येवमादि समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: this form of the word being a Vedic anomaly,as above Thus of water also, this sprout is the same, that is, called Body’, and nothing else

units.sanskrit: तस्य क्व मूलं स्याद् अन्यत्राद्भ्यः । अद्भिः सोम्य शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
units.english: ‘Where could its root be, apart from Water?so, my boy, from Water as sprout, infer Fire as the root;

units.sanskrit: तेजसा सोम्य शुङ्गेन सन्मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
units.english: from Fire as Sprout, infer Being as the root

units.sanskrit: सन्मूलाः सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सद् आयतनाः सत्प्रतिष्ठाः ।
units.english: All these creatures, my dear, have their root in Being, reside in Being and rest in Being

units.sanskrit: यथा नु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवताः पुरुषं प्राप्य त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तद् उक्तं पुरस्ताद् एव भवति ।
units.english: And now, how each of these three deities, on reaching;man, becomes triplicated has been explained to you before

units.sanskrit: अस्य सोम्य पुरुषस्य प्रयतो वाङ् मनसि संपद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस् तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायाम् ॥ सामर्थ्यात्तेजसो ऽप्येतदेव शरीराख्यं शुङ्गम् ।
units.english: When, my dear;the man is departing, his Speech merges into the Mind, Mind merges into Lifebreath, Lifebreath into Fire, and Fire into the Supreme Deity From the force of circumstances it follows that of Fire also, this, that is called ‘Body,’ is the Sprout

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽप्शुङ्गेन देहेना'पो मूलं गम्यते ।
units.english: Hence, from Water as sprout, in the form of the Body, is inferred the root of that Water;

units.sanskrit: अद्भिः शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलं गम्यते । तेजसा शुङ्गेन सन्मूलं गम्यते पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: and from Water as the Sprout is inferred Fire as its root;from Fire as Sprout is inferred Being as its root;as before

units.sanskrit: एवं हि तेजोबन्नमयस्य देहशुङ्गस्य वाचारम्भणमात्रस्यान्नादिपरम्परया परमार्थसत्यं
units.english: Thus, then, of the BodySprout which consists of Fire, Water and Food,which is a mere modification of words, infer the rootthrough the series beginning with foodconsists in Being, which is absolutely real, free from fear and danger and trouble

units.sanskrit: नामप्रसिद्धिद्वारेण यदन्यदिहास्मिन्प्रकरणे तेजोबन्नानां पुरुषेणोपभुज्यमानानां कार्यकरणसंघातस्य देहशुङ्गस्य स्वजात्यसांकर्येणोपचयकरत्वं वक्तव्यं प्राप्तं तदिहोक्तमेव द्रष्टव्यमिति पूर्वोक्तं व्यपदिशति ।
units.english: Having explained all this to his son, by means of the wellknown phrases ‘desirous of eating’ and ‘desirous of drinking’, he points out that whatever else has got to be explained in this connection,with regard to the fact of Fire, Water and Food, as used up by man, making up the BodySprout, which is an aggregate of causes and effects, without intermixing,all this should be taken as already explained

units.sanskrit: यथा नु खलु येन प्रकारेणेमास्तेजोबन्नाख्यास्तिस्रो देवताः पुरुषं प्राप्य त्रिवृत्त्रिवृदेकैका भवति तदुक्तं पुरस्तादेव भवत्यन्नमशितं त्रेधा विधीयत इत्यादि ।
units.english: Hence, he refers to what has been said beforeAnd now, how etc, etc,in what manner,each of these three divinities,Fire, Water and Food, on reaching Man, becomes triplicated has been explained to you before;under the text ‘Food, eaten, is made threefold’ Chāndo

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवोक्तमन्नादीनामसितानां ये मव्यमा धातवस्ते साप्तधातुकं शरीरमुपचिन्वन्तीत्युक्तम् । मांसं भवति लोहितं भवति मज्जा भवत्यस्थि भवति ये त्वणिष्ठा धातवो मनः प्राणं वाचं देहस्यान्तःकरणसंघातमुपचिन्वन्तीति चोक्तंतन्मनो भवति स प्राणो
units.english: In that connection it has been asserted that of the food etc that are eaten, the middling substances go to develop the Body made up of seven substances,‘It becomes Flesh, it becomes Blood, it becomes Marrow and it becomes Bone;while the subtlest substances go to develop Mind, Lifebreath, Speech and the aggregate of the internal organs of the Body ‘It becomes Mind, it becomes Lifebreath, it becomes Speech’

units.sanskrit: सो ऽयं प्राणकरणसंघातो देहे विशीर्णे देहान्तरं जीवाधिष्ठितो येन क्रमेण पूर्वदेहात्प्रच्युतो गच्छति तदाहास्य हे सोम्य पुरुषस्य प्रयतो म्रियमाणस्य वाङ्मनसि संपद्यते मनस्युपसंह्रियते । अथ तदा'हुर्ज्ञातयो न वदतीति ।
units.english: When the Body becomes torn up, the said aggregate of Lifebreath and Organs, occupied by the ‘Living Self’, slips off from the previous body and enters a fresh body, in a separate order of sequence;this is what the text next describes‘When, my dear, the Man is departing,dying,his Speech merges into the Mind,it becomes summated in the Mind,and his relatives say He speaks not’;

units.sanskrit: मनःपूर्वको हि वाग्व्यापारः ।
units.english: the functioning of Speech is always preceded by the Mind;

units.sanskrit: यद्वै मनसा ध्यायति तद्वाचा वदतिइति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: as declared in the Vedic text‘What one thinks of in the Mind, that he speaks by speech’

units.sanskrit: वाच्युपसंहृतायां मनसि मनो मननव्यापारेण केवलेन वर्तते । मनो ऽपि यदोपसंह्रियते तदा मनः प्राणे संपन्नं भवति सुषुप्तकाल इव तदा पार्श्वस्था ज्ञातयो न विजानातीत्याहुः ।
units.english: When speech has become merged into the Mind, then the Mind remains functioning by itself alone;when the Mind also becomes summated, then the Mind merges into the Lifebreath;as during Deep Sleep;

units.sanskrit: प्राणश्च तदोर्ध्वोच्छ्वासी स्वात्मन्युपसंहृतबाह्यकरणः संवर्गविद्यायां दर्शनाद्धस्तपादादीन्विक्षिपन्मर्मस्थानानि निकृन्तन्नन इवोत्सृजन्
units.english: at this time, the relatives by his side say ‘He is not thinking not conscious At this time, the Lifebreath, moving in upward exhalation, withdraws into itself all the external organs as described under the SamvargaVidyā, brings about the throwing about of hands and legs, and cutting into the vital parts of the body, becomes merged,in the same order in which it had gone forth,into Fire;

units.sanskrit: तदा'हुर्ज्ञातयो न चलतीति मृतो नेति वा विचिकित्सन्तो देहमालभमाना उष्णं चोपलभमाना
units.english: when the relatives say ‘He moves not’, and being in doubt as to whether he is alive or not, they touch the body, and if they find the body warm, they say ‘the body is still warm,’ ‘he is alive’

units.sanskrit: देह उष्णो जीवतीति यदा तदप्यौष्ण्यलिङ्गं तेज उपसंह्रियते तदा तत्तेजः परस्यां
units.english: Lastly, when the Fire also as indicated by the warmth, becomes withdrawn, then this Fire becomes merged into the Supreme Divinity

units.sanskrit: तदेवङ्क्रमेणोपसंहृते स्वमूलं प्राप्ते च मनसि तत्स्थो जीवो ऽपि सुषुप्तकालवन्निमित्तोपसंहारादुपसंह्रियमाणः
units.english: When, in this way, the Mind has become summated and merged into its source, the ‘Living Self’ resident therein also becomes withdrawn, as during deep sleep, on account of the merging of his accessories Mind and the rest;

units.sanskrit: सन्सत्याभिसंधिपूर्वकं चेदुपसंह्रियते सदेव संपद्यते न पुनर्देहान्तराय
units.english: and does not enter into another body, in the way in which the man in deep sleep returns to physical consciousness, after the cessation of the sleep

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके सभये देशे वर्तमानः कथञ्चिदिवाभयं देशं प्राप्तस्तद्वत् ।
units.english: For instance, in the ordinary world, a man living in a place full of dangers, on reaching a place of safety, never returns to the former place

units.sanskrit: इतरस्त्वनात्मज्ञस्तस्मादेव मूलात्सुषुप्तादिवोत्थाय मृत्वा पुनर्देहजालमाविशति ॥
units.english: A ‘Living Self’ other than this one, who has not realised his Self, rises again from his source Being,like a man awaking after deep sleep after death, and again enters into the meshes of the Body

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘Now, that which is this Subtle Essence,in that has all this its Self; that is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: that is the Truth;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति ।
units.english: that thou art, O ‘Śvetaketu’

units.sanskrit: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, please explain this to me again’

units.sanskrit: तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘Be it so, my boy’,he said

units.sanskrit: यस्मान्मूलादुत्थाय देहमाविशति जीवः स यः सदाख्य एष उक्तो ऽणिमाणुभावो जगतो मूलमैतदात्म्यमेतत्सदात्मा यस्य सर्वस्य तदेतदात्म तस्य भाव ऐतदात्म्यम् ।
units.english: That which has been spoken of above as named ‘Being’which is the subtlest essence,the point of ultimate subtlety,source of the Universein that has all this its Self‘that which has this Being for its Self’ is Sadātmā’, and the abstract form of this is ‘aitadātmya’

units.sanskrit: एतेन सदाख्येना'त्मना'त्मवत्सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
units.english: That is, it is through this Self known as ‘Being’ that all this Universe is imbued with Self;

units.sanskrit: नान्यो ऽस्त्यस्या'त्मा संसारी ।
units.english: and there is no other Self for this which passes through births and deaths;

units.sanskrit: नान्यदतो ऽति श्रोतृइत्यादिश्रुत्यन्तरात् ।
units.english: as has been declared in such other Vedic texts as‘other than this, there is no Seer, other than this, there is no Heaven’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: येन चा'त्मना'त्मवत्सर्वमिदं जगत्तदेव सदाख्यं कारणं सत्यं परमार्थसत् ।
units.english: viii that through which all this Universe becomes imbued with Self is its origin, called ‘Being’, which is True and Absolutely Real

units.sanskrit: अतः स एवा'त्मा जगतः प्रत्यक्स्वरूपं सतत्त्वं याथात्म्यम् ।
units.english: Hence, it is this that is the Self of the Universe, its counterform, its very essence, its very Soul

units.sanskrit: आत्मशब्दस्य निरुपपदस्य प्रत्यगात्मनि गवादिशब्दवन्निरूढत्वात् ।
units.english: The term ‘Self’ Ātman, without any qualifying prefix has its denotation restricted by convention to the Self in Evolution, Jīvātmā, like the term ‘cow’ and the like;

units.sanskrit: अतस्तत्सत्त्वमसीति हे श्वेतकेतो इत्येवं प्रत्यायितः पुत्र आहभूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयतु
units.english: hence, thou art that Being, O Śvetaketu Having been thus taught, the son said‘Revered Sir, please explain to me again;

units.sanskrit: यद्भवदुक्तं तत्सन्दिग्धं ममाहन्यहनि सर्वाः प्रजाः सुषुप्ते सत्संपद्यन्त इत्येतद्येन तत्संपद्य न विदुः सत्सम्पन्ना वयमिति ।
units.english: still have doubts with regard to what you have told me in regard to all creatures, during deep sleep, becoming merged in Being; if that is so, then, having become so merged, that they do not know that they had been so merged in Being, seems to me doubtful

units.sanskrit: अतो दृष्टोन्तेन मां प्रत्याययत्वित्यर्थः । एवमुक्तस्तथास्तु सोम्येति होवाच पिता ॥
units.english: Hence, please explain this to me further, by means of illustrations’Being thus addressed, the father said‘Be it so, my dear’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्याष्टमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यथा सोम्य मधु मधुकृतो निस्तिष्ठन्ति नानात्ययानां वृक्षाणां रसान् समवहारम् एकतां रसं गमयन्ति ॥
units.english: ‘Just as, my dear, the bees make honey, by collecting the juices of many distant trees, and then reducing them to one unit in the form of one juice’

units.sanskrit: यत्पृच्छस्यहन्यहनि सत्संपद्य न विदुः सत्संपन्नाः स्म इति तत्कस्मादित्यत्र शृणु दृष्टान्तम् । यथा लोके हे सोम्य मधुकृतो मधु कुर्वन्तीति मधुकृतो मधुकरमक्षिका मधु निस्तिष्ठन्ति मधु निष्पादयन्ति तत्पराः सन्तः । कथम्?नानात्ययानां नानागतीनां नानादिक्कानां वृक्षाणां रसान्समवहारं समाहृत्यैकतामेकभावं मधुत्वेन रसान्गमयन्ति मधुत्वमापादयन्ति
units.english: You askhow is it that people being merged into Being day after day do not know that they have become merged into Being?Listen to an illustration‘Just as, in the ordinary world, O my dear, ‘makers of honey’Bees make Honeyprepare it, being entirely absorbed in the work;how?by collecting the juices of many distant treestrees in varying conditions and in various places and then reducing them to one unitin the form of one juice, Honeyie they reduce the various juices to the state of the Honey’

units.sanskrit: ते यथा तत्र न विवेकं लभन्ते ऽमुष्याहं वृक्षस्य रसो ऽस्म्य् अमुष्याहं वृक्षस्य रसो ऽस्मीति ।
units.english: ‘And there, as those juices have no discrimination, such as am the juice of this tree; am the juice of that tree;

units.sanskrit: एवम् एव खलु सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सति संपद्य न विदुः सति संपद्यामह इति ॥
units.english: in the same manner, my dear, all these creatures having merged into Being, do not know that we are merging into Being’

units.sanskrit: ते रसा यथा मधुत्वेनैकतां गतास्तत्र मधुनि विवेकं न लभन्ते । कथम्, अमुष्याहमाम्रस्य पनसस्य वा वृक्षस्य रसो ऽस्मीति । यथा हि लोके बहूनां चेतनावतां समेतानां प्राणिनां विवेकलाभो भवत्यमुष्याहं पुत्रो ऽमुष्याहं नप्तास्मीति ।
units.english: When those juices have been reduced to unity in the form of Honey, then, in the honey, they have no discrimination,how?that am the juice of thismango or jackfruit tree;in the way that there is in the world, when several sentient persons collect together in an assembly, they have the discrimination that am the son of this man, am the grandson of that man,and having got at this discrimination, they do not become mixed up

units.sanskrit: ते च लब्धविवेकाः सन्तो न संकीर्यन्ते न तथेहानेकप्रकारवृक्षरसानामपि मधुराम्लतिक्तकटुकादीनां मधुत्वेनैकतां गतानां मधुरादिभावेन
units.english: though the juices have been collected from several trees, and have taste variously as sweet, acid, bitter, pungent and so forth,and they have been collected in onethe form of Honey, they are no longer able to be discriminated as sweet or bitter etc

units.sanskrit: विवेको गृह्यत इत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: This is the sense of the illustration

units.sanskrit: यथायं दृष्टान्त इत्येवमेव खलु सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहन्यहनि सति संपद्य सुषुप्तकाले मरणप्रलययोश्च न विदुर्न विजानीयुः सति
units.english: Just as, in the case of the illustration cited, so, my dear, all these creatures being mergedday after dayinto Being, during Deep Sleep, at death and at Cosmic Dissolution,do not know,would not know,that we are becoming or becomemerged into Being,

units.sanskrit: त इह व्यघ्रो वा सिंहो वा वृको वा वराहो वा कीटो वा पतङ्गो वा दंशो वा मशको वा यद् यद् भवन्ति तद् आभवन्ति ॥
units.english: ‘Whatever these creatures are herea tiger, or a lion, or a wolf, or a boar, or a worm, or an insect, or a gadfly, or a mosquito,that they become again’

units.sanskrit: यस्माच्चैवमात्मनः सद्रूपतामज्ञात्वैव सत्संपद्यन्ते । अतस्त इह लोके यत्कर्मनिमित्तां यां यां जातिं प्रतिपन्ना आसुर्व्याघ्रादीनां व्याघ्रो ऽहं सिंहो ऽहमित्येवं ते तत्कर्मज्ञानवासनाङ्किताः सन्तः सत्प्रविष्टा अपि तद्भावेनैव
units.english: Because, without knowing that they arc Being,they merge into Being,therefore, in whatever,animalspeciessuch as, the tiger and the like,they have been born in, in this world,each of them knowing himself as a tiger or a lion, so forth,they become impressed with the tendencies of past cognitions and actions, and after having merged into Being at death, they are born again in that same condition with the same tendencies;

units.sanskrit: पुनराभवन्ति पुनः सत आगत्य व्याघ्रो वा सिंहो वा वृको वा वराहो वा कीटो वा पतङ्गो वा दंशो वा मशको वा यद्यत्पूर्वमिह लोके भवन्ति वभूवुरित्यर्थः ।
units.english: and returning from Being, they become a tiger, or a lion, or a wolf, of a boar, or a worm, or an insect, or a gadfly, or a mosquito,whatever they areie were in this world previously,that same they become again,on return rebirth;

units.sanskrit: तदेव पुनरागत्य भवन्ति युगसहस्रकोट्यन्तरितापि संसारिणो जन्तोर्या पुरा भाविता वासना सा न नश्यतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: even though the two consecutive births of an evolving creature be separated by an interval of millions of timecycles, the tendencies imprinted upon it during the preceding life do not cease to exist and affect his later birth;

units.sanskrit: यथाप्रज्ञं हि संभवाःइति श्रुत्त्यन्तरात् ॥
units.english: as has been declared in anotherVedic Text‘Births are in accordance with knowledge’

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘Now, that which is this Subtle Essence,in That has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: स आत्मा ।
units.english: That is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति । भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: That is the True; That thou art; O Śvetaketu’‘Revered Sir, please explain this to me, again’‘Be it so, my boy’, he said’

units.sanskrit: ताः प्रजा यस्मिन्प्रविश्य पुनराविर्भवन्ति । ये त्वितो ऽन्ये सत्सत्यात्माभिसंधा यमणुभावं सदात्मानं प्रविश्य ना'वर्तन्ते स य एषो ऽणिमेत्यादि व्याख्यातम् ।
units.english: That Being wherein having entered, creatures are born again,and wherein having entered in its subtle form of the self, those creatures do not return who are firm in their conviction regarding the Self,that is the Subtle Essence etc, etc,as already explained above

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके स्वकीये गृहे सुप्त उत्थाय ग्रामान्तरं गतो जानाति स्वगृहादागतो ऽस्मीत्येवं
units.english: In ordinary life, when a man rising from sleep, in his house, has gone to another village, he is conscious of his come away from his home;

units.sanskrit: सत आगतो ऽस्मीति च जन्तूनां कस्माद्विज्ञानं न भवतीति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्वित्युक्तस्तथा
units.english: in the same way, why is it that the creatures who have been born after having merged in Being, are not conscious of having come from Being? Please explain this to me again

units.sanskrit: सोभ्येति होवाच पिता ॥
units.english: Being thus addressed, the father said‘Be it so, my boy’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य नवमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: इमाः सोम्य नद्यः पुरस्तात् प्राच्यः स्यन्दन्ते पश्चात् प्रतीच्यः ।
units.english: ‘These rivers, my dear, flow along,the Eastern ones to the East, and the Western ones to the West;

units.sanskrit: ताः समुद्रात् समुद्रम् एवापियन्ति ।
units.english: they go from sea to sea, and they become the sea

units.sanskrit: ता यथा तत्र न विदुर् इयम् अहम् अस्मीयम् अहम् अस्मीति ॥
units.english: And just as these rivers, while there, do not know am this river or that’

units.sanskrit: शृणु तत्र दृष्टान्तं यथा सोम्येमा नद्यो गङ्गाद्याः पुरस्तात्पूर्वां दिशं प्रति प्राच्यः प्रागञ्चनाः स्यन्दन्ते स्रवन्ति । पश्चात्प्रतीचीं दिशं प्रति सिन्ध्वाद्याः प्रतीचीमञ्चन्ति गच्छन्तीति प्रतीच्यस्ताः समुद्रादम्भोनिधेर्जलधरैराक्षिप्ताः
units.english: ‘Just listen to an illustration; my dear, these riversthe Gaṅgā and the rest,the Eastern ones flowing towards the East and the Western onesthe Sindhu and the rest flowing totowards the West; and these become drawn up from the sea by clouds and fall down again in the form of rain, into the Gangā and other rivers and flow into the sea again;

units.sanskrit: समुद्र एव भवति ता नद्यो यथा तत्र समुद्रे समुद्रात्मनैकतां गता न विदुर्न जानन्तीयं गङ्गाहमस्मीयं यमुनाहमस्मीतीयं मह्यहमस्मीति च ॥
units.english: and they become the sea; now these rivers, having become unified inhe ocean, do not know that am this river Gaṅgā,or am that riverYamunā,or am the Mahī;in the same manner’

units.sanskrit: एवम् एव खलु सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सत आगम्य न विदुः सत आगच्छामह इति ।
units.english: ‘In the same manner, all these creatures, having come from Being, know not they come from Being;

units.sanskrit: त इह व्याघ्रो वा सिंहो वा वृको वा वराहो वा कीटो वा पतङ्गो वा दंशो वा मशको वा यद् यद् भवन्ति तद् आभवन्ति ॥
units.english: and whatever these creatures are here,a tiger, or a lion, or a wolf, or a boar, or a worm, or an insect, or a gadfly, or a mosquito,that they become again

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: Now, that which is the Subtle Essence,in that has all this its Self;That is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: That is the True;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति ।
units.english: That thou art, O, Śvetaketu’

units.sanskrit: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, please explain this to me again’

units.sanskrit: तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘Be it so, my boy’,he said
