units.sanskrit: एवमेव खलु सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजा यस्मात्सति सम्पद्य न विदुस्तस्मात्सत आगम्य न विदुः सत आगच्छामह आगता इति वा ।
units.english: ‘In the same manner, my dear, all these creatureswho did not know that they had become merged in Being,do not know that it is from Being that they are coming,or have come again

units.sanskrit: दृष्टं लोके जले वीचीतरङ्गफेनबुदादय उत्थिताः पुनस्तद्भावं गता विनष्टा इति ।
units.english: In the ordinary world, it is seen that in water, there appear many such manifestations as ripples, waves, foam, bubbles and the like,and they revert again to the same form of water, and are destroyed;

units.sanskrit: जीवास्तु तत्कारणमणुभावं प्रत्यहं गच्छन्तो ऽपि सुषुप्ते मरणप्रलययोश्च न विनश्यन्तीत्येतत् भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयतु दृष्टान्तेन
units.english: as for living beings however, though they are, daily, becoming merged in their cause,during deep sleep and at death and at Cosmic Dissolution,they are not destroyed they continue to exist in other forms’

units.sanskrit: तथा सोम्येति होवाच पिता ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य दशमः खण्डः
units.english: ‘Explain this to me again, Revered Sir, by further illustrations’‘Be it so, my boy,’said the father End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अस्य सोम्य महतो वृक्षस्य यो मूले ऽभ्याहन्याज् जीवन् स्रवेद् यो मध्ये ऽभ्याहन्याज् जीवन् स्रवेद् यो ऽग्रे ऽभ्याहन्याज् जीवन् स्रवेत् ।
units.english: Of this large tree, my child, if one were to strike at the root, it would exude juice, while still living; if one were to strike it in the middle, it would exude juice, while still living;

units.sanskrit: स एष जीवेनात्मनानुप्रभूतः पेपीयमानो मोदमानस् तिष्ठति ॥
units.english: This tree, pervaded by the ‘Living Self’, stands firm, drinking and rejoicing

units.sanskrit: शृणु दृष्टान्तमस्य हे सोम्य महतो ऽनेकशाखादियुक्तस्य वृक्षस्यास्येत्यग्रतः स्थितं वृक्षं दर्शयन्नाह । यदि यः कश्चिदस्य मूले ऽभ्याहन्यात्परश्वादिना सकृद्घातमात्रेण न शुष्यतीति जीवन्नेव भवति तदा तस्य रसः स्रवेत् ।
units.english: ‘Listen to the illustration, my child,of this large tree with many large branches,‘this’ being indicated towards a tree standing before them,if some one were to strike at the rootwith an axe or some such weapon, striking at it once onlythe tree would not dry up, it would continue to live,and merely its juice would flow out of the cut

units.sanskrit: तथा यो मध्ये ऽभ्याहन्याज्जीवन्स्रवेत्तथा यो ऽग्रे ऽभ्याहन्याज्जीवन्स्रवेत्स एष
units.english: Similarly, if one were to strike it at the middle, it would exude juice and be still living; and if one were to strike it at the top, it would exude juice while still living

units.sanskrit: वृक्ष इदानीं जीवेना'त्मनानुप्रभूतो ऽनुव्याप्तः पेपीयमानो ऽत्यर्थं पिबन्नुदकं भौमांश्च रसान्मूलैर्गृह्णन्मोदमानो हर्षं प्राप्नुवंस्तिष्ठति ॥
units.english: This tree is, at this moment, pervaded,endowedby the ‘Living self’, and it stands firm, drinkingabsorbing through its roots large quantities of water and other juices out of the Earth and rejoicing,being happy’

units.sanskrit: अस्य यद् एकां शाखां जीवो जहात्य् अथ सा शुष्यति । द्वितीयां जहात्य् अथ सा शुष्यति ।
units.english: ‘If the Living self leaves one of its branches, that branch withers, if it leaves the second branch, that withers, if it leaves the third,that withers;

units.sanskrit: सर्वं जहाति सर्वः शुष्यति ॥
units.english: if it leaves the whole, the whole withers

units.sanskrit: तस्यास्य यदेकां शाखां रोगग्रस्तामाहतां वा जीवो जहात्युपसंहरति शाखायां विप्रसृतमात्मांशम् ।
units.english: ‘Of this tree, if the ‘Living Self’ leaves one branch, which is either diseased or has been struck at,ie withdraws from it that position of Itself which ensouled that branch,then that branch withers;

units.sanskrit: वाङ्मनःप्राणकरणग्रामानुप्रविष्टो हि जीव इति तदुपसंहार उपसंह्रियते ।
units.english: the Living Self enters a living thing in the course of the aggregate of Speech, Mind, Lifebreath, and Organs;

units.sanskrit: जीवेन च प्राणयुक्तेनाशितं पोतं च रसतां गतं जीवच्छरीरं वृक्षं वर्धयद्रसरूपेण जीवस्य सद्भावे लिङ्गं भवति ।
units.english: What happens is that when the ‘Living Self’ endowed with Lifebreath eats or drinks, what is eaten and drunk becomes turned into juices which nourish the tree of which the body is alive and the same juices serve as indicative of the presence of the Living Self

units.sanskrit: अशितपीताभ्यां हि देहे जीवस्तिष्ठति ते चाशितपीते जीवकर्मानुसारिणी इति । तस्यैकाङ्गवैकल्यनिमित्तं कर्म यदोपस्थितं भवति तदा जीव एकां शाखां जहाति शाखाया आत्मानमुपसंहरति ।
units.english: It is through what is eaten and drunk that the ‘Living Self’ stays in the body, and the character of what is eaten and drunk is always in keeping with the Kārmic Residua of the ‘Living Self So that, when the time has arrived for the function of that Kārmic Residua of his which is the cause of his being maimed by a limb, then the Living Self leaves one branch,ie it withdraws itself from that one branch;

units.sanskrit: अथ तदा सा शाखा शुष्यति ।
units.english: and then that branch withers

units.sanskrit: जीवस्थितिनिमित्तो रसो जीवकर्माक्षिप्तो जीवोपसंहारे न तिष्ठति । रसापगमे च शाखा शोषमुपैति ।
units.english: It is by reason of the presence of the ‘Living Self’, that the juices, thrown up by the Kārmic Residua, cease to exist there, on the withdrawal of the ‘Living Self and when the juices have ceased to come up, the Branch withers

units.sanskrit: तथा सर्वं वृक्षमेव यदायं जहाति तदा सर्वो ऽपि वृक्षः शुष्यति ।
units.english: Similarly, when the ‘Living Self’ leaves the whole tree, then the whole tree withers

units.sanskrit: वृक्षस्य रसस्रवणशोषणादिलिङ्गाज्जीववत्त्वं दृष्टान्तश्रुतेश्च चेतनावन्तः स्थावरा इति बौद्धकाणादमतमचेतनाः स्थावरा इत्येतदसारमिति
units.english: That the tree is ensouled by the ‘Living Self’ has been indicated by the phenomena of the flowing of juices and withering ofas shown by the illustration also vouched for the Vedic text; which means that immovable apparently inanimate objects like the tree are endowed with sentience;

units.sanskrit: दर्शितं भवति ॥ एवम् एव खलु सोम्य विद्धीति ह उवाच ।
units.english: ‘Understand this to be similar, my dear,’he said‘Bereft of the Living Self, this perishes;

units.sanskrit: जीवापेतं वाव किलेदं म्रियते न जीवो म्रियत इति ।
units.english: the Living Self never perishes

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: That which is the subtlest Essence,in That has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: That is the True;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति । भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: That thou art, O, Śvetaketu’‘Explain this to me again, Revered Sir,’‘So be it, my boy’he said

units.sanskrit: यथास्मिन्वृक्षदृष्टान्ते दर्शितं जीवेन युक्तो वृक्षो ऽशुष्को रसपानादियुक्तो जावतीत्युच्यते तदपेतश्च म्रियत इत्युच्यते । एवमेव खलु सोम्य विद्धीति होवाचजीवापेतं जीववियुक्तं वाव किलेदं शरीरं म्रियते
units.english: As has been shown in the above example of the tree that, so long as the tree is imbued with the ‘Living Self,’ it does not dry up and continues to be nourished by the drinking in of juices and thus said to be alive and when it becomes bereft of that Self, it is said to ‘die ‘Understand this to be similar,’he said ‘When this body is bereft of the ‘Living Self’,separated from the Self,it perishes;

units.sanskrit: न जीवो म्रियत इति कार्यशेषे च सुप्तोत्थितस्य ममेदं कार्यशेषमपरिसमाप्तमिति स्मृत्वा समापनदर्शनात् ।
units.english: the Living Self never perishes; because it is found that in a case where the man has gone to sleep leaving the work in hand unfinished, on waking from sleep, he remembers his unfinished work and finishes it

units.sanskrit: जातमात्राणां च जन्तूनां स्तन्याभिलाषयादिदर्शनाच्चातीतजन्मान्तरानुभूतस्तन (न्य)
units.english: Further, in the case of creatures just born, they are found to evince desire for milk from the mother’s breasts, fears and such other feelings;

units.sanskrit: पानदुःखानुभवस्मृतिर्गम्यते ।
units.english: and from this it is inferred that they remember the experience, in their previous births, of drinking milk from the mother’s breasts, and also unpleasant experiences

units.sanskrit: अग्निहोत्रादीनां च वैदिकानां कर्मणामर्थवत्त्वान्न जीवो म्रियत इति ।
units.english: Also, because the Agnihotra and other Vedic Rites serve useful purposes, therefore the Living Self cannot die

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमेत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: That which is the Subtlest Essence etc, etc, as before

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनरिदमत्यन्तस्थीलं पृथिव्यादि नामरूपवज्जगदत्यन्तसूक्ष्मात्सद्रूपान्नामरूपरह् इतात्सतो जायत इत्येतद्दृष्टान्तेन भूय एव मा
units.english: How this extremely gross Universe consisting of the Earth and other things, with its diverse names and forms, is produced out of Being which is extremely subtle, is of the essence of pure Being, devoid of all name and formplease explain this to me again, Revered Sir

units.sanskrit: तथा सोम्येति होवाच पिता ॥
units.english: The father said‘Be it so, my boy’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्यैकादशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: न्यग्रोधफलम् अत आहरेति । इदं भगव इति ।
units.english: ‘Fetch a fruit of that Banyantree’‘Here it is, Sir’‘Break it

units.sanskrit: भिन्द्धीति । भिन्नं भगव इति । किम् अत्र पश्यसीति । अण्व्य इवेमा धाना भगव इति । आसाम् अङ्गैकां भिन्द्धीति ।
units.english: ‘It is broken, Sir’‘What dost thou see there?’‘These are very small seeds, Sir’Break one of these, my dear’‘It is broken, Sir’‘What dost thou see there?’‘Nothing, Sir’

units.sanskrit: यद्येतत्प्रत्यक्षीकर्तुमिच्छसि, अतो ऽस्मान्महतो न्यग्रोधात्फलमेकमाहरेत्युक्तस्तथा चकार,
units.english: ‘If you wish to have direct evidence of this, then fetch a fruit of this largeBanyantree’Thus told he did so, and said ‘Here it is, sir;

units.sanskrit: तमाह पिता किमत्र पश्यसीत्युक्त आहाण्व्यो ऽणुतरा इवेमा धाना बीजानि पश्यामि भगव इति । आसां धानानामेकां धानामङ्ग हे वत्स भिन्धीत्युक्त आह भिन्ना भगव इति । यदि भिन्ना धाना तस्यां भिन्नायां किं पश्यसीत्युक्त आह न किञ्चन पश्यामि भगव इति ॥
units.english: have fetched the fruit’When he had shown the fruit, the father said to him Break it’The other said‘It is broken’The father said to him‘What dost thou see here?’the son said‘These very small seeds, see, Sir’‘Of those seeds, my dear boy, break one’Thus told, he said‘It is broken, Sir’‘If the seed has been broken, what dost thou see in that broken seed?’He answered‘ see nothing, sir’

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच यं वै सोम्यैतम् अणिमानं न निभालयस एतस्य वै सोम्यैषो ऽणिम्न एवं महान्यग्रोधस् तिष्ठति ।
units.english: He said to him‘My child, the Subtle Essence which thou dost not perceive,it is from that Subtle Essence that this large Banyantree grows up’

units.sanskrit: श्रद्धत्स्व सोम्येति ॥
units.english: Have faith my son’

units.sanskrit: तं पुत्रं होवाच वटधानायां भिन्नायां यं वटबीजाणिमानं हे सौम्यैतं न निभालयसे न पश्यसि । तथाप्येतस्य वै किल सोम्यैष महान्न्यग्रोधो बीजस्याणिम्नः सूक्ष्मस्यादृश्यमानस्य कार्यभूतः स्थूलशाखास्कन्धफलपलाशवांस्तिष्ठत्युत्पन्नः सन्नुत्तिष्ठतीति वोच्छब्दो
units.english: He said to his son‘On breaking the Banyanseed, that Subtle Essenceof the Banyanseedwhich thou dost not perceivesee,and yet, my boy, it is from Subtle Essence of the seed,which is not visible,that the large Banyantree, fully equipped with thick branches, trunk, fruits, and leavesgrows upas the productor it is produced and rises up,the ‘ut’ being understood before the term ‘tiṣṭhati’Have faith my son, when say that it is from this Subtle Essence of Being that there grows Universe with its names and forms, grows up as the product

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि न्यायागमाभ्यां निर्धारितोर्ऽथस्तथैवेत्यवगम्यते तथाप्यत्यन्तसूक्ष्मेष्वर्थेषु बाह्यविषयासक्तमनसः स्वभावप्रवृत्तस्यासत्यां गुरुतरायां श्रद्धायां दुरवगमत्वं
units.english: Though when a certain fact has been established by reasoning and scriptural authority, it is always understood to be so and true,yet, in the case of extremely subtle things, a man who has his mind taken up by external things, and follows the natural bent of his activities, could find it difficult to understand if he were not imbued with a large degree of faith;

units.sanskrit: स्यादित्याह श्रद्धत्स्वेति । श्रद्धायां तु सत्यां मनसः समाधानं बुभुत्सितेर्ऽथे भवेत्ततश्च तदर्थावगतिः ।
units.english: hence, the father said‘Have faith;’ when there is faith, the mind becomes concentrated on the subject desired to understand, and then the due understanding follows

units.sanskrit: अन्यत्रमना अभूवम् इत्यादिश्रुतेः ॥
units.english: That this is so is clear from such Vedic texts as ‘ had my mind elsewhere’

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘That which is this Subtle Essence,in that has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: That is True;

units.sanskrit: स आत्मा ।
units.english: That is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति ।
units.english: That thou art, O, Śvetaketu’

units.sanskrit: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, please explain this to me again’‘Be it so, my boy’,he said

units.sanskrit: स य इत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ।
units.english: That which etc, etc, this has been already explained

units.sanskrit: यदि तत्सज्जगतो मूलं कस्मान्नोपलभ्यत इत्येतद्दृष्टान्तेन मा भगवान्भूय एव विज्ञापयत्विति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच पिता ॥
units.english: If that Being is the root of the Universe, then why is it not perceived?Please explain this to me again, Revered Sir,by means of illustrations ‘Be it so, my boy’said the father

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य द्वादशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: लवणम् एतद् उदके ऽवधायाथ मा प्रातर् उपसीदथा इति ।
units.english: ‘Having put this salt into water, come to me in the morning’

units.sanskrit: स ह तथा चकार ।
units.english: He did so

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच । यद् दोषा लवणम् उदके ऽवाधा अङ्ग तद् आहरेति ।
units.english: The father said to him‘Bring the salt, my son, which you put into the water at night’

units.sanskrit: तद् धावमृश्य न विवेद ॥
units.english: Having looked for it, he found it not;

units.sanskrit: विद्यमानमपि वस्तु नोपलभ्यते प्रकारान्तरेण तूपलभ्यत इति शृण्वत्र
units.english: as it had melted away ‘Even a thing that exists may not be directly perceived, and yet it may be known in another way;

units.sanskrit: दृष्टान्तम् यदि चेममर्थं प्रत्यक्षो स ह पित्रोक्तमर्थं प्रत्यक्षीकर्तुमिच्छंस्तथा चकार ।
units.english: listen to an example of this, if you wish to have direct evidence of this fact, then, having put

units.sanskrit: स ह पित्रोक्तमर्थं प्रत्यक्षीकर्तुमिच्छंस्तथा चकार । तं होवाच परेद्युः प्रातर्यल्लवं दोषा रात्रावुदके ऽवाधा निक्षिप्तवानस्यङ्ग हे वत्स तदाहरेत्युक्तस्तल्लवणमाजिहीर्षुर्ह किलावमृश्योदके न विवेद न विज्ञातवान्यथा तल्लवणं,
units.english: this saltlumpin water,in a jar or some other vessel,come to metomorrow in the morning’The boy, with a view to see for himself for what father had taught him, did as he was told The next day, the Father said to himin the morning‘The salt that, at night, you put under water,that, my boy, please bring’Being told thus, with a view to bring the salt, having looked for it,in the water,he found it not,he did not per,ceive the salt;

units.sanskrit: विद्यमानमेव सदप्सु लीनं संश्लिष्टमभूतं ॥
units.english: because, even though it was there it had welted awayand merged into the water

units.sanskrit: अन्;गास्यान्ताद् आचामेति ।
units.english: ‘My boy, taste it from the pot;

units.sanskrit: कथम् इति । लवणम् इति । मध्याद् आचामेति ।
units.english: how is it?’‘It is salt’‘Taste it from the middle;

units.sanskrit: कथम् इति । लवणम् इति ।
units.english: how is it?’ ‘It is salt’‘Taste it from the bottom;

units.sanskrit: कथम् इति । लवणम् इति । अभिप्रास्यैतद् अथ मोपसीदथा इति ।
units.english: how is it ‘It is salt’‘Throw it away and come to me’He did so;

units.sanskrit: तच् छश्वत् संवर्तते । तं होवाचात्र वाव किल तत् सोम्य न निभालयसे ऽत्रैव किलेति ॥
units.english: saying ‘It remains for ever’The Father said to him‘Here also, forsooth, thou dost not perceive the Being, while there it is indeed’

units.sanskrit: यथा विलीनं लवणं न वेत्थ तथापि तच्चक्षुषा स्पर्शनेन च पिण्डरूपं लवणमगृह्यमाणं विद्यत एवाप्सूपलभ्यते चोपायान्तरेणेत्येतत्पुत्रं प्रत्याययितुमिच्छन्नाहअङ्गास्योदकस्यान्तादुपरि गृहीत्वा'चामेत्युक्त्वा पुत्रं तथाकृतवन्तमुवाच कथमितीतर आह लवणं स्वादुतः इति । तथा मध्यादुदकस्य गृहीत्वा'चामेति कथमिति लवणमिति ।
units.english: ‘Though you do not perceive the melted salt with the eye, nor feel the lump by your tactile organ, yet it exists in the water all the same and is perceived by other means,’in order to convince of the truth of this, he said to him‘My boy, take some water from the top surface and taste it’Having said this and having found that the son had done as he was asked, he asked him‘How is it?’the other replied‘It is saltin taste’Similarly, ‘Take some water jrom the middle and taste it;how is it?’‘It is salt’So take some water from the bottom‘end’ and taste it

units.sanskrit: तथान्तादधोदेशाद्गृहीत्वा'चामेति कथमिति लवणमिति ।
units.english: How is it?‘It is salt,’‘If that is so, then throw it away,leave it,and having washed your mouthy come to me’He did so;

units.sanskrit: यद्येवमभिप्रास्य परित्यज्यैतदुदकमाचम्याथ मोपसीदथा इति तद्ध तथा चकार लवणं परित्यज्य पितृसमीपमाजगामेत्यर्थः । इदं वचनं ब्रवंस्तल्लवमं तस्मिन्नेवोदके यन्मया रात्रौ क्षिप्तं शाश्वन्नित्यं संवर्तते विद्यमानमेव सत्सम्यग्वर्तते । इत्येवमुक्तवन्तं तं होवाच पिता । यथेदं लवणं दर्शनस्पर्शनाभ्यां पूर्वं गृहीतं पुनरुदके विलीनं ताभ्यामगृह्यमाणमपि विद्यत एवोपायान्तरेण जिह्वयोपलभ्यमानत्वात्
units.english: that is, having thrown away the salt, he went to his father;saying these words‘Exactly the same salt that had put into the water at night, remains for ever,ie it exists quite in the right manner’When he had said this, the Father said to him‘This salt had been perceived by you, in the first instance, with the visual and tactile organs,and when it melted in water, though it was not perceived by those two organs yet it exists there, as shown by the fact that it is perceived by the gestatory organ the tongue;in the same manner, it happens in regard to the body which is of the nature of a sprout, a product of fire, water, food and other things’The particles ‘Vāva’ and ‘Kila’ are meant to indicate the remembrance of the teachings of ancient teachers

units.sanskrit: सत्तेजोबन्नादिशुङ्गकारमं वटबीजाणिमवद्विद्यमानमेवेन्द्रियैर्नोपलभसे न निभालयसे ।
units.english: ‘Here also forsooth, thou dost not perceive the Being’,which is the cause of the sprout made up of fire, water, food and other things,while it is there indeed,like the subtle essence of the BanyanSeed,though thou perceivest it not by the senseorgans

units.sanskrit: यथात्रैवोदके दर्शनस्पर्शनाभ्यामनुपलभ्यमानं लवणं विद्यमानमेव जिह्वयोपलब्धवानसि । एवमेवात्रैव किल विद्यमानं सज्जगन्मूलमुपायान्तरेण लवणाणिमवदुपलप्स्यस इति वाक्यशेषः ॥
units.english: As in this water, though the salt was not perceived by the visual and tactile organs, yet it was there as you perceived it bu the gestatory organ,in the same manner, though the Being exists in this world, as its very root, and thou canst apprehend it by other means,like the subtle essence of the salt,’ this is the final upshot of what he said

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘That which is this Subtle Essence,in that has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: That is the True;

units.sanskrit: स आत्मा ।
units.english: That is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति ।
units.english: That thou art, O, Śvetaketu

units.sanskrit: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, please explain this to me again’‘Be it so, my boy,’he said

units.sanskrit: स य इत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: That which etc, etc just as before

units.sanskrit: यद्येवं लवणाणिमवदिन्द्रियैरनुपलभ्यमानमपि जगन्मूलं सदुपायान्तरेणोपलब्धुं शक्यते यदुपलम्भात्कृतार्थः स्यामनुपलम्भाच्चाकृतार्थः स्यामहं तस्यैवोपलब्धौ क उपाय इत्येतद्भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयतु दृष्टान्तेन तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: If this Being, the root of the Universe,though imperceptible through the senseorgans,is yet capable of being apprephended by other means,just like the subtle essence of the salt,and the apprehension of this Being would fulfil my whole purpose in life, and the nonapprehension of it would make me disappointed in my aim,then, please explain to me again, what is the means by which that Being could be apprehended; please explain this by means of illustration’said the son

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य त्रयोदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यथा सोम्य पुरुषं गन्धारेभ्यो ऽभिनद्धाक्षम् आनीय तं ततो ऽतिजने विसृजेत् । स यथा तत्र प्राङ् वोदङ् वा अधराङ् वा प्रत्यङ् वा प्रध्मायीताभिनद्धाक्ष आनीतो ऽभिनद्धाक्षो विसृष्टः ॥
units.english: ‘Just as, my dear, some one, having brought a man from the Gandhara regions with his eyes bound up, might leave him in a desolate place,and that man would shout towards the East, or towards the North, or towards the South, or towards the West’‘ have been brought here with my eyes bound up and left here with my eyes bound up’

units.sanskrit: यथा लोके हे सोम्य पुरुषं यं कञ्चिद्गन्धारेभ्यो जनपदेभ्यो ऽभिनद्धाक्षं बद्धचक्षुषमानीय द्रव्यहर्ता तस्करस्तमभिनद्धाक्षमेव बद्धहस्तमरण्ये ततो ऽप्यतिजने ऽतिगतजने ऽत्यन्तविगतजने देशे विसृजेत्स तत्र दिग्भ्रमोपेतो यथा प्राङ्वा प्रागञ्चनः प्राङ्मुखो,
units.english: ‘Just as, in the ordinary world, my dear, having brought a man,any onefrom the Gandhāra Regions, with his eyes bound up,a robbermight leave himwith his eyes bound up and his hands tied,in a forest, or in still more desolated place,that man, having lost all sense of direction, would shoutcrytowards the Eastie with his face turned towards the East,or towards the North, or towards the South, or towards the West,saying ~ With eyes bound up have been brought by robbers from the Gandhāra regions, and have been left here with my eyes bound up’

units.sanskrit: तस्य यथाभिनहनं प्रमुच्य प्रब्रूयाद् एतां दिशं गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति ।
units.english: ‘And as some one might remove his bandage and tell himthe Gandhāra regions lie towards this direction, go in this direction,whereupon;

units.sanskrit: स ग्रामाद् ग्रामं पृच्छन् पण्डितो मेधावी गन्धारान् एवोपसंपद्येत । एवम् एवेहाचार्यवान् पुरुषो वेद ।
units.english: asking his way from village to village, and becoming informed and capable of judging by himself, he would reach the Gandhāra regions;in the same manner, in this world, that person knows who has a teacher;

units.sanskrit: तस्य तावद् एव चिरं यावन् न विमोक्ष्ये ऽथ संपत्स्य इति ॥
units.english: and for him, the delay is only so long as am not liberated and become merged’

units.sanskrit: एवं विक्रोशतस्तस्य यथाभिनहनं यथाबन्धनं प्रमुच्य मुक्त्वा कारुणिकः कश्चिदेतां दिशमुत्तरतो गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति प्रब्रूयात्स एवं कारुणिकेन बन्धनान्मोक्षितो ग्रामाद्ग्रामान्तरं पृच्छन्पण्डित उपदेशवान्मेधावो परोपदिष्टग्रामप्रवेशमार्गावधारणसमर्थः
units.english: While he is thus shouting, some one, with a merciful temperament, might remove his bandagecovering over the eyes,and tell him that the Gandhāra regions lie towards thisthe Northerlydirection, go in this direction,that man, being freed by the sympathetic person from his bandage,asking his way from village to village, becoming informed,by advices offered,and capable of judging by himselfcapable of finding the way to villages as pointed out by others,would reach the Gandhāra regions;

units.sanskrit: सन्गन्धारानेवोपसम्पद्येत नेतरो मूढमतिर्देशान्तरदर्शनतृड्वा ।
units.english: such a man alone would reach the place, and not one who is either foolish or desirous of seeing various countries

units.sanskrit: यथायं दृष्टान्तो वर्णितः स्वविषयेभ्यो गन्धारेभ्यः पुरुषस्तस्करैरभिनद्धाक्षो ऽविवेको दिङ्मूढो ऽशनायापिपासादिमान्व्याघ्रतस्कराद्यनेकभयानथर्व्रातयुतमरण्यं प्रवेशितो दुःखार्तो विक्रोशन्बन्धनेभ्यो मुमुक्षुस्तिष्ठति स कथञ्चिदेव कारुणिकेन केनचिन्मोक्षितः स्वदेशान्गन्धारानेवा'पन्नो निर्वृतः सुख्यभूत् ।
units.english: Just as in the illustration as described, the man was brought from his country in the Gandhāra regions, by robbers, with his eyes bound up,and lacking discriminating and confound in regard to the directions, beset with hunger, thirst, and other privations,was brought into a forest infested with tigers, robbers and other dangers,in sore trouble, crying,remains there, eager to be liberated;then he is liberated by some sympathetic person, and ultimately somehow reaches his own Gandhāra country, became happy and contented

units.sanskrit: एवमेव सतो जगदात्मनः स्वरूपात्तेजोवन्नादिमयं देहारण्यं वातपित्तकफरुधिरमेदोमांसास्थिमज्जाशुक्रकृमिमूत्रपुरीषवच्छीतोष्णाद्यनेकद्वन्द्वसुखदुःखवच्चेदं मोहपटाभिनद्धाक्षो भार्यापुत्रमित्रपशुबन्ध्वादिदृष्टादृष्टानेकविषयतृष्णापाशितः पुण्यापुण्यादितस्करैः प्रवेशितोऽहममुष्य पुत्रो ममैते बान्धवाः सुख्यहं दुःखी मूढः पण्डितो धार्मिको बन्धुमाञ्जातो मृतो जीर्णः पापी पुत्रो मे मृतो धनं मे नष्टं हा हतो ऽस्मि कथं जाविष्यामि का मे गतिः किं मे त्राणम् इत्येवमनेकशतसहस्रानर्थजालवान्विक्रोशन्कथञ्चिदेव
units.english: In the same manner, the man is carried away from Being, the Self of the Universe,by robbers in the shape of merit, demerit and other tendencies,and made to enter the forest of this Body made up of Fire, Water, Food and other ingredients, and containing wind, bile, phlegm, blood, fat, flesh, bone, marrow, semen, worms urine and fæces, and beset with several pains of opposites, like heat and cold,with his eyes bound up with the bandage of delusion, caught in the noose of longing for wife, son, friends, cattle, relative and such other perceptible and imperceptible things, enmeshed in the meshes of hundreds and thousands of such evils and austerities and cryingas ‘ am the son of such and such a person,’ ‘these are my relatives,’ ‘ am happy,’ ‘ am unhappy,’ ‘ am deluded, ‘ am wise,’ ‘ am righteous,’ ‘ have many relatives, ‘my son is born, is dead, is sinful’, ‘my property has been lost’, ‘Ah! am damned’, ‘How shall live? ‘What is to be my fate?’ ‘What is to be my refuge?’Then, by the influence of some good fortune due to the excess of merit, he gets a teacher, who is extremely sympathetic, and knows the Being, the Brahman, the Self,and who is himself liberated from all bondage and rests firmly upon Brahman,and this Brahmanknowing teacher, through pity, shows him the way to perceive the defects in worldly objectswhereupon he loses all attachment to these worldly objects,and on being told that ‘thou art not one who passes through the cycle of births and deaths, thou art not the son, or any relation of such and such a person, etc,in fact, thou art pure Being, that which Thou Art,’ and thus he becomes liberated from the bondage of Ignorance,like the man from Gandhāra,reaches his own True Self, Being, and becomes happy and for ever contented’

units.sanskrit: यदा'सादयति तेन च ब्रह्मविदा कारुण्याद्दर्शितसंसारविषयदोषदर्शनमार्गो विरक्तः संसारविषयेभ्यो नासि त्वं संसार्यमुष्य पुत्रत्वादिधर्मवान्किं तर्हि सद्यत्तत्त्वमसीत्यविद्यामोहपटाभिनहनान्मोक्षितो
units.english: It is all this which the Father meant by saying‘That person knows who has a teacher’ For him,for the man who has been liberated from the bondage of Ignorance,the delaythe postponementin merging into his real Self, Beingis only so long;how long is the delay?so long as am liberatedie he becomes liberated

units.sanskrit: गन्धारपुरुषवच्च स्वं सदात्मानमुपसम्पद्य सुखी निर्वृतः स्यादित्येतमेवार्थमाहा'चार्यवान्पुरुषो वेदेति तस्यास्यैवमाचार्यवतो मुक्ताविद्याभिनहनस्य तावदेव तावानेव कालश्चिरं
units.english: The first person in the word ‘Vimokṣye’ is to be taken in the sense of the third person, as such is the force of the sense;ie the delay is only so long as that Kārmic Residue is not exhausted, by experience, by virtue of which his Body has been brought about,and so long as, as the consequence of this, that Body does not fall off;and then there do become merged alsoie he becomes mergedhere also the first person is to be taken in the sense of the third person;

units.sanskrit: क्षेपः सदात्मस्वरूपसम्पत्तेरिति वाक्यशेषः ।
units.english: hence, the word ‘atha’ cannot be taken as expresssing sequence

units.sanskrit: सामर्थ्यात् । येन कर्मणा शरीरमारब्धं तस्योपभोगेन येनाथशब्द आनन्तर्यार्थः स्यात् । ननु यथा सद्विज्ञानान्तरमेव देहपातः सत्सम्पत्तिश्च न भवति कर्मशेषवशात्तथाप्रवृत्तफलानि प्राग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तेर्जन्मान्तरसञ्चितान्यपि कर्माणि सन्तीति तत्फलोपभोगार्थं पतिते
units.english: ObjectionThe falling off of the Body and the merging into Being do not, as a matter of fact, follow immediately after the attaining of the knowledge of Being,on account of there still remaining the remnants of the same Kārmic Residua which have become operative and as such have to be expiated during the present lifenow in the same way even those Karmic Residua which have not yet become operative towards bringing about their results, coming on as stored through other births previous to the attainment of the said knowledge of Being;

units.sanskrit: उत्पन्ने च ज्ञाने यावज्जीवं विहितानि प्रतिषिद्धानि वा कर्माणि करोत्येवेति तत्फलोपभोगार्थं चावश्यं शरीरान्तरमारब्धव्यं ततश्च कर्माणि ततः शरीरान्तरमिति ज्ञानार्थक्यं कर्मणां फलवत्त्वात् ।
units.english: and certainly for the experiencing of the results of these also, another body has to be produced for the man,even after the falling off of the present body;then again even after the said knowledge has come about, the man continues to perform many actssome enjoined, some forbidden,and for the experiencing of the results of these fresh actions also, there has to be another body;then further fresh acts,and further consequent bodies;so that the attaining of knowledge becomes practically futile, inasmuch as actions must produce effects and these must be experienced in a body

units.sanskrit: अथ ज्ञानवतः क्षीयन्ते कर्माणि तदा ज्ञानप्राप्तिसमकालमेव ज्ञानस्य सत्सम्पत्तिहेतुत्वान्मोक्षः स्यादिति शरीरपातः स्यात् ।
units.english: If it be held that for the man who has attained true knowledge all Kārmic Residua disappear,then liberation should appear simultaneously with the attainment of knowledge, and knowledge being the direct cause of mergence into Being,so that the body should fall off immediately

units.sanskrit: तथाचा'चार्याभावैत्याचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेदेत्याचार्यवत्त्वानुपपत्तिर्ज्ञानान्मोक्षाभावप्रसङ्गश्च ।
units.english: The result of this would be that the man would have had no time to approach a teacher, and this would be incompatible with the declaration that ‘he alone knows who has got a teacher and also obviously the possibility of there being no liberation resulting from knowledge;or there would be an element of uncertainty regarding the result of knowledge;

units.sanskrit: देशान्तरप्राप्त्युपायज्ञानवदनैकान्तिकफलत्वं वा ज्ञानस्य । न ।
units.english: and would come to resemble the means of reaching one place from another which may or may not lead to the desired result

units.sanskrit: कर्मणां प्रवृत्ताप्रवृत्तफलवत्त्वविशेषोपपत्तेः ।
units.english: it is possible to make a distinction between,such Kārmic Residua as has already become operative in bringing about its results and such another as has not become so operative

units.sanskrit: यदुक्तमप्रवृत्तफलानां कर्ममां ध्रुवफलवत्त्वाद्ब्रह्मविदः शरीरे पतिते शरीरान्तरमारब्धव्यमप्रवृत्तकर्मफलोपभोगाथर्मित्येतदसत्
units.english: It has been argued thatInasmuch as even these Kārmic Residua which have not become operative must bring about their results, when the present body falls, there must be produced another body, for the experiencing of the results of those actions which had not become already operativeBut this is not right;

units.sanskrit: विदुषस्तस्य तावदेव चिरम् इति श्रुतेः प्रामाण्यात् ।
units.english: because of the authoritative declaration of the Śruti to the effect that ‘for him the delay is only so long etc, etc’ which shows that liberation must follow the falling off of the present body

units.sanskrit: ननुपुण्यो वै पुम्येन कर्मणाभवतिइत्यादिश्रुतेरपि प्रामाण्यमेव ।
units.english: Objection‘Authority also attaches to such declarations as ‘one becomes pure by pure acts’ Bṛhadā iii so that an act must produce a body

units.sanskrit: तस्यमेवम् ।
units.english: True, it is so;

units.sanskrit: तथापि प्रवृत्तफलानामप्रवृत्तफलानां च कर्मणां विशेषो ऽस्ति ।
units.english: yet, there is a difference between such Kārmic Residua as have become operative towards bringing about their results and such others as have not become so operative

units.sanskrit: कथम् । यानि प्रवृत्तफलानि कर्माणि यैर्विद्वच्छरीरमारब्धं तेषामुपभोगेनैव क्षयः ।
units.english: How?These Kārmic Residua which have become operative, and to which the present body of the knowing man is due, can be exhausted by experience alone;

units.sanskrit: यथा'रह्धवेगस्य लक्ष्यमुक्तेष्वादेर्वेगक्षयादेव स्थितिर्न तु लक्ष्यवेधसमकालमेव प्रयोजनं नास्तीति तद्वत् । अन्यानि त्वप्रवृत्तफलानीह प्राग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तेरूर्ध्वं च कृतानि वा क्रियमाणानि वातीतजन्मान्तरकृतानि वाप्रवृत्तफलानि ज्ञानेन दह्यन्ते प्रायश्चित्तेनेव
units.english: just as in the case of the arrow that has been shot at a certain target, it comes to rest only when the momentum is exhausted, and not successively on its reaching the target on account of there being no purpose to be served by its going any further;so in the case in question also,there are however other Kārmic Residua which have not yet become operative,as also those acts that have been done and are being done during the present life, prior to the attaining of knowledge and after it,or those of past lives which have not yet become operative,all these are consumed by True Knowledge, in the same way as they are by expiatory Rites;

units.sanskrit: क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणिइति चा'थर्वणे ।
units.english: and also in the Atharvaṇa‘Kārmic Residua become exhausted’

units.sanskrit: अतो ब्रह्मविदो जीवनादिप्रयोजनाभावे ऽपि प्रवृत्तफलानां कर्मणामवश्यमेव फलोपभोगः स्यादिति मुक्तेषुवत्तस्य तावदेव चिरमिति युक्तमेवोक्तमिति यथोक्तदोषचोदनानुपपत्तिः
units.english: Thus then, though for the man who knows Brahman, there is no further use for life, yet there surely would be experiencing of the results of those Kārmic Residua that have become operative,just as in the case of the arrow that has been shot;and it is only right that for him there is delay only so long etc, etc, and there is no room for the objections that have been urged

units.sanskrit: ज्ञानोत्पत्तेरूर्ध्वं च ब्रह्मविदः कर्माभावमवोचामब्रह्मसंस्थो ऽमृतत्वमेतीत्यत्र ।
units.english: After the appearance of True Knowledge for the knower of Brahman,there is no further Kārmic Residua, as we have already explained, under the text‘the man resting in Brahman attains immortality etc,’ Cā

units.sanskrit: तच्च स्मर्तुमर्हसि ॥
units.english: xxiii you may recall that to your mind

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘That which is this subtlest essence,in that has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: That is True;

units.sanskrit: स आत्मा ।
units.english: that is Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति । भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: That Thou art, O, Śvetaketu’,‘Please explain this to me again, revered Sir ‘So be it, my boy’, he said

units.sanskrit: स य इत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ।
units.english: That which etc as already explained before

units.sanskrit: आचार्यवान्विद्वान्येन क्रमेण सत्सम्पद्यते तं क्रमं दृष्टान्तेन भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: ‘Please explain to me by means of illustrations the order of sequence in which the learned man with a teacher becomes merged into Being’‘Be it so, my boy,’he said

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य चतुर्दशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पुरुषं सोम्योतोपतापिनं ज्ञातयः पर्युपासते जानासि मां जानासि माम् इति । तस्य यावन् न वाङ् मनसि संपद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस् तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायां तावज् जानाति ॥
units.english: ‘My dear, when a man is ill, his relatives assemble round him and askDo you know me ?do you know me ?so long as his speech has not become merged in Mind, Mind in LifeBreath, the LifeBreath in Fire and the Fire in the Supreme Deity,he knows them

units.sanskrit: पुरुषं हे सोम्योतोपतापिनं ज्वराद्युपतापवन्तं ज्ञातयो बान्धवाः परिवार्योपासते मुमूर्षुं जानासि मां तव पितरं पुत्रं भ्रातरं वेति पृच्छन्तस्तस्य
units.english: My boy, when a man is ill,suffering from fever and other diseases,his relatives assemble round himwhen he is about to die,and ask himDo you know meyour father, a son, or brother as the case may be

units.sanskrit: मुमूर्षोर्यावन्न वाङ्मनसि सम्पद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस्तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायामित्येतदुक्तर्थम् ॥
units.english: of the dying man,so long as speech has not become merged in mind, the mind in lifebreath, and lifebreath in fire, etc, etc, all which has been already explained

units.sanskrit: अथ यदास्य वाङ् मनसि संपद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस् तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायाम् अथ न जानाति ॥
units.english: ‘Now, when his Speech becomes merged into mind, the Mind in Life breath, the Lifebreath in Fire and Fire in the Supreme Deity,then he does not know them’

units.sanskrit: संसारिणो यो मरणक्रमः स एवायं विदुषो ऽपि सत्सम्पत्तिक्रम इत्येतदाह परस्यां देवतायां तेजसि सम्पन्ने ऽथ न जानाति
units.english: The text now proceeds to show that manner of mergence into Being, of the Man with knowledge, is the same as that of the ordinary worldly man When the Fire has become merged into the Supreme Deity, then he does not know them

units.sanskrit: अविद्वांस्तु सत उत्थाय प्राग्भावितं व्याघ्रादिभावं देवमनुष्यादिभावं वा विशति ।
units.english: The difference between the two men however is thisAs regards the Man without knowledge, having arisen out of Being, enters into thempredetermined state of the tiger and other animals, or of deities, or men or other beings;

units.sanskrit: विद्वांस्तु शास्राचार्योपदेशजनितज्ञानदीपप्रकाशितं सद्ब्रह्मात्मानं प्रविश्य ना'वर्तत इत्येष सत्सम्पत्तिक्रमः ।
units.english: whereas, the man with knowledge, having entered into BeingBrahmanSelfillumined by the lamp of knowledge derived from the teaching of Teachers and Scriptures,never again returns to Birth; this being his manner of merging into Being

units.sanskrit: अन्ये तु मूर्धन्यया नाड्योत्क्रम्या'दित्यादिद्वारेण सद्गच्छन्तीत्याहुस्तदसत् ।
units.english: Others, however, have held that the man, going out of the artery in the head, reaches Being through the Sun and other Deities

units.sanskrit: देशकालनिमित्तफलाभिसन्धानेन गमनदर्शनात् ।
units.english: Because the progress after death of the Man ego is dependent upon the peculiarities of the notions of time, place and causes and of the motive for results;

units.sanskrit: न हि सदात्मैकत्वदर्शिनः सत्याभिसन्धस्य देशकालनिमित्तफलाद्यनृताभिसन्धिरुपपद्यते ।
units.english: for one, however, who has recognised the Unity of the TrueSelf, and who has no other motive save Truth,there can be no any such false notions as those of Time, Place, Causes or Motive for results;

units.sanskrit: विरोधात् ।
units.english: for the simple reason that the two are incompatible

units.sanskrit: अविद्याकामकर्मणां च गमननिमित्तानां सद्विज्ञानहुताशनविप्लुष्टत्वाद्गमनानुपपत्तिरेव ।
units.english: Further, Ignorance, Desire and Kārmic Residuawhich are the cause of the man’s progression,are all burnt up by the Fire of True Knowledge, and hence, there can be no progressing through the Sun etc for the Man with knowledge;

units.sanskrit: पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तिवहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाःइत्याद्याथर्वणे ।
units.english: this has been thus described in the Ātharvaṇa text‘for one whose all desires have been fulfilled and who has reached the Self,all desires disappear in this life itself’

units.sanskrit: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘That which is this Subtle Essence,in that has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: that is True;

units.sanskrit: स आत्मा ।
units.english: that is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति । भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति । तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: that thou art, Śvetaketu’‘Revered sir, please explain this to me again’‘Be it so, my boy,’he said

units.sanskrit: स य इत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: That which is etc, etc just as before

units.sanskrit: यदि मरिष्यतो मुमुक्षतश्च तुल्या सत्सम्पत्तिस्तत्र विद्वान्सत्सम्पन्नो ना'वर्तत आवर्तते त्वविद्वानित्यत्र कारणं दृष्टान्तेन भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
units.english: If, for the dying man and for the man going to be liberated,for both, the mergence into Being be similar,then, the man with knowledge, on merging into Being, does not return, while the Man without knowledge does return, to worldly existence,‘what is the reason for this?’please explain this further to me by means of illustrations’‘Be it so, my boy’he said

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि षष्ठाध्यायस्य पञ्चदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: पुरुषं सोम्योत हस्तगृहीतम् आनयन्ति ।
units.english: ‘My boy, they bring a man, holding him by the hand, sayingHe has taken something,he has committed theft, heat the axe for him;

units.sanskrit: अपहार्षीत् स्तेयम् अकार्षीत् परशुम् अस्मै तपतेति । स यदि तस्य कर्ता भवति तत एवानृतम् आत्मानं कुरुते ।
units.english: in case he has committed the deed, he makes himself false, on that account, and being addicted to falsehood, he covers himself with falsehood and grasps the heated axe;

units.sanskrit: स दह्यते । अथ हन्यते ॥
units.english: he is burnt, and then he is killed’

units.sanskrit: शृणु यथा सोम्य पुरुषं चौर्यकर्मणि सन्दिह्यमानं निग्रहाय परीक्षणाय वोतापि हस्तगृहीतं बद्धहस्तमानयन्ति राजपुरुषाः किं कृतवानयमिति पृष्टाश्चा'हुरपहार्शीद्धनमस्यायम् । ते चा'हुः किमपहरणमात्रेम बन्धनमर्हति । अन्यथा दत्ते ऽपि धने बन्धनप्रसङ्गादित्युक्ताः पुनराहुः स्तेयमकार्षीत्तौर्येण धनमपहार्षीदिति । तेष्वेवं वदत्स्वितरो ऽपह्नते नाहं तत्कर्तेति ।
units.english: ‘Listen, my boy, when a man is suspected of having committed theft, the king’s officers hold him by the hand with his hands tied up,and bring him for trial and punishment,when asked‘What has he done?’they say‘He has taken something,something belonging to such and such a person the questioner says‘Does he deserve arrest and bondage only for taking something from some one? In that case there could be arrest also when some property is given and received as a gift’The officers say‘He has committed theft,he has taken another man’s property by theft’When the officers have said this, the suspected person denies his guilt‘ have not committed the theft’The officers say to the suspected man‘You have committed theft of this property’When the accused has denied his guilt, they sayHeat the axe for him;let him clear himself by ordeal’If the man has really committed the theft,and denies the guilt only outwardly,he makes himself false,ie, by the mere denial, he represents himself as what he is not;

units.sanskrit: सन्तमन्यथा'मानं कुरुते स तथानृताभिसन्धो ऽनृतेना'त्मानमन्तर्धाय व्यवहितं कृत्वा परशुं तप्तं मोहात्प्रतिगृह्राति स दह्यते ऽथ हन्यते राजपुरुषैः स्वकृतेनानृताभिसन्धिदोषेण ॥
units.english: and thus being addicted to false hood he covers himself with falsehood,ie, hiding himself under untruthhe grasps the heated axefoolishly;and he is burnt and killed by the king’s officers,on account of his own fault of being addicted to falsehood

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि तस्याकर्ता भवति । तत एव सत्यम् आत्मानं कुरुते । स सत्याभिसन्धः सत्येनात्मानम् अन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति । स न दह्यते ।
units.english: ‘If, however, he has not committed it, then he makes himself true on that account and being addicted to Truth, he covers himself by Truth and grasps the heated axe;he is not burnt, he is let off’

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि तस्य कर्मणो ऽकर्ता भवति तत एव सत्यमात्मानं कुरुते
units.english: ‘If, however, the man has not committed the deed,he makes himself true, on that account;

units.sanskrit: स सत्येन तया स्तैन्याकर्तृतया'त्मानमन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति स सत्याभिसन्धः सन्न दह्यते सत्यव्यवधानादथ मुच्यते च मृषाभियोक्तृभ्यः ।
units.english: and covers himself by truth,in the form of not committing theft,he grasps the heated axe,and being addicted to truth, he is not burnt, because of the intervention of truth, and he is let off,rescued from his false accusers

units.sanskrit: तप्तपरशुहस्ततलसंयोगस्य तुल्यत्वे ऽपि स्तेयकर्त्रकर्त्रोरनृताभिसन्धो दह्यते न तु सत्याभिसन्धः ॥
units.english: Though the contact of the heated axe with the hand is practically the same in both cases of the man who has committed the theft and the man who has not committed the theft,the man addicted to untruth is burnt,not so the man addicted to truth

units.sanskrit: स यथा तत्र नादाह्येत । एतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
units.english: ‘And as he is not burnt,in that has all this its Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् सत्यम् ।
units.english: That is the true;

units.sanskrit: स आत्मा ।
units.english: That is the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत् त्वम् असि श्वेतकेतो इति । तद् धास्य विजज्ञाव् इति विजज्ञाव् इति ॥
units.english: that thou art, O, Śvetaketu’Then, he understood it of him,yea, he understood it

units.sanskrit: स यथा सत्याभिसन्धस्तप्तपरशुग्रहणकर्मणि सत्यव्यवहितहस्ततलत्वान्नादाह्येत न दह्येतेत्येतदेवं सद्ब्रह्मसत्याभिसन्धीतरयोः शरीरपातकाले च तुल्यायां सत्सम्पत्तौ विद्वान्सत्सम्पद्य न पुनर्व्याघ्रदेवादिदेहग्रहणाया'वर्तते । अविद्वांस्तु विकारानृताभिसन्धः पुनर्व्याघ्रादिभावं देवतादिभावं वा यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतं प्रतिपद्यते ।
units.english: As in the case cited, the man addicted to truth, on grasping the heated axe, is not burnt, because his palm was protected by truth,in the same way, at the time that the bodies of the man having the true knowledge of BeingBrahman and the other man who has no such knowledge, are dyingthough the merging into Being is similar in both cases, the man with knowledge having become merged into Being, does not return to the body of the tiger, or of a deity or other beings,while the man without knowledge, addicted to the false, in the shape of the products, does return, to be born again as a tiger or a deity or other things, in accordance with his Kārmic Residua, in the manner described in the scriptures

units.sanskrit: यदात्माभिसन्ध्यनभिसन्धिकृते मोक्षबन्धने यच्च मूलं जगतो यदायतना यत्प्रतिष्ठाश्च सर्वाः प्रजा यदात्मकं च सर्वं यच्चाजममृतमभयं शिवमद्वितीयं तत्सत्यं स आत्मा तवातस्तत्त्वमसि हे श्वेतकेतो इत्युक्तार्थमसकृद्वाक्यम् ।
units.english: Thus liberation and bondage are due to addiction to truth and untruth respectively;and that which is the root of the universe, wherein all creatures dwell and rest,and in which all things have their Self,which is immortal, free from dangers, blessed, without a second,that is true, that is thine Selfhence, that thou art, O Śvetaketu

units.sanskrit: कः पुनरसौ श्वेतकेतुस्त्वंशब्दार्थः ।
units.english: QuestionWho is this Śvetaketu, who is spoken of as Thou?

units.sanskrit: यो ऽहं श्वेतकेतुरुद्दालकस्य पुत्र इति वेदा'त्मानमादेशं श्रुत्वा मत्वा विज्ञाय चाश्रुतममतमविज्ञातं विज्ञातुं पितरं पप्रच्छ कथं नु भगवः स आदेशो बवतीति स एषो ऽधिकृतः श्रोता मन्ता विज्ञाता तेजोबन्नमयं कार्यकारणसङ्घातं प्रविष्टा परैव देवता नामस्वरूपव्याकरणाया'दर्श इव पुरुषः सूर्यादुरिव जलादौ प्रतिबोधितस्तत्त्वमसीतिदृष्टान्तैर्हेतुभिश्च तत्पितुरस्य ह किलोक्तं सदेवाहमस्मीति विजज्ञौ विज्ञातवान् ।
units.english: AnswerI, Śvetaketu, who know myself as the son of Uddālaka, having heard the teaching and pondered over it and learnt it, requested the Father to teach him what he had not heard, or pondered over, or known‘What, revered Sir, is that Teaching?’This represents the person who, being entitled to be the hearer, the ponderer and the knower,did not, before he was taught by his father, had not reached the true nature of his own self, as Being, the Self of all, as distinct from all aggregates of causes and effects,whichas the Supreme Deity,has entered into the aggregate of causes and effects made up of Fire, Water and Food, for the differentiating of Names and Forms,just as man enters the mirror, as his own reflection, or the Sun enters into water and other reflecting surfaces, as its own reflection;now however, having been enlightened by his father by the teaching ‘that Thou art’, through a number of illustrations and reasons,he understood from his father that ‘ am Being itselfThe repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse

units.sanskrit: द्विर्वचनमध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थम् । किं पुनरत्र षष्ठे वाक्यप्रमाणेन जनितं फलम्?
units.english: QuestionWhat is the resultant cognition regarding the Self which is brought about by the Verbal means of cognition Vedic text set forth in this Sixth Discourse?

units.sanskrit: आत्मनि कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वयोरधिकृतत्वविज्ञाननिवृत्तिस्तस्य फलं यं वयमवोचाम त्वंशब्दवाच्यमर्थं श्रोतुं मन्तुं चाधिकृतमविज्ञातविज्ञानफलार्थम्
units.english: AnswerWe have already explained above that the result brought about by this Discourse is the setting aside of the notion that ‘Self is the actual doer of acts and enjoyer of the results of those acts;and when we spoke of the entity denoted by the term ‘thou ie the living Self, the Jīva, born in the body and the fact of that entity being one who is to ‘hear’ and ‘reflect upon’ the Self,we did so only for asserting what is not generally known

units.sanskrit: प्राक्चैतस्माद्विज्ञानादहमेवं करिष्याम्यग्निहोत्रादीनि कर्माण्यहमत्राधिकृतः ।
units.english: Before all this is known, the ordinary man has such notions as‘ shall perform these actions, the Agnihotra and the rest

units.sanskrit: एषां च कर्मणां फलमिहामुत्र च भोक्ष्ये कृतेषु वा कर्मसु कृतकर्तव्यः स्यामित्येवं कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वयोरधिकृतो ऽस्मीत्यात्मनि यद्विज्ञानमभूत्तत्तस्य यत्सज्जगतो मूलमेकमेवाद्वितीयं
units.english: am entitled to the performance;the results of these acts shall enjoy in this world and in the other;or having done these acts, shall be happy and contented’,all these notions, which involve the idea of the Self being the actual performer and enjoyer, are set aside by the assertion that ‘Thou art That Being which is the root of the universe, one, without a second’,for the man who has become awakened to true knowledge;

units.sanskrit: तत्त्वमसीत्यनेन वाक्येन प्रतिबुद्धस्य निवर्तते । विरोधात् ।
units.english: that the said notions are set aside by this last assertion follows from the fact that the two are mutually contradictory so that if the latter is true, the former must be false

units.sanskrit: न ह्येकस्मिन्नद्वितीय आत्मन्ययमहमस्मीति विज्ञाते ममेदमन्यदनेन कर्तव्यमिदं कृत्वास्य फलं भोक्ष्य इति वा भेदविज्ञानमुपपद्यते ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, when it has been realised that ‘ am the Self, one, without a secondit is not possible for him to have such notions involving diversity as ‘this is to be done by me,that by another’, ‘that having done this act, shall enjoy its result’;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्सत्सत्याद्वितीयात्मविज्ञाने विकारानृतजीवात्मविज्ञानं निवर्तत इति युक्तम् ।
units.english: hence, it is only right and proper that on the realisation of Being, the Self, the True, without a second, the idea of ‘the Living Self’ being a product and unreal

units.sanskrit: ननु तत्त्वमसीत्यत्र त्वंशब्दवाच्येर्ऽथे सद्बुद्धिराधित्स्यते यथा'दित्यमन आदिषु ब्रह्मादिबुद्धिः ।
units.english: ObjectionWhat is done in the assertion ‘That thou art’ is that the idea of ‘Being’ is attributed to what is denoted by the term ‘thou’ just as this idea of Brahman and other Deities is attributed to the Sun, the Mind and other things,or as in the ordinary world, the idea of

units.sanskrit: यथा च लोके प्रतिमादिषु विष्ण्वादिबुद्धिस्तद्वन्नतु सदेव त्वमिति,
units.english: Viṣṇu and other Deities attributed to the Images;

units.sanskrit: यदि सदेव श्वेतकेतुः स्यात्कथमात्मानं न विजानीयाद्येन तस्मै तत्त्वमसीत्युपदिश्यते । न ।
units.english: and the assertion does not mean that thou art that same Being AnswerNot so;

units.sanskrit: आदित्यादिवाक्यवैलक्षण्यात् ।
units.english: this assertion is entirely different in character of those relating to the Sun and other things

units.sanskrit: आदित्यो ब्रह्मेत्यादावितिशब्दव्यवधानान्न साक्षाद्ब्रह्मत्वं गम्यते ।
units.english: In such passages as the Sun is as Brahman’ should be looked or meditated upon as Brahman, the intervention of the term ‘as’ makes it impossible for it to provide the idea that ‘the Sun is actually Brahman itself’;

units.sanskrit: रूपादिमत्त्वाच्चा'दित्यादीनामाकाशमनसोश्चेतिशब्दव्यवधानादेवाब्रह्मत्वमिह तु सत एवेह प्रवेशं दर्शयित्वा तत्त्वमसीति निरङ्कुशं सदात्मभावमुपदिशति
units.english: also because the Sun and other things have such qualities as colour and the like, and because Ākāśa and Mind are always spoken of along with the term ‘as’,therefore none of these can be Brahman;while in the case of the assertion in question‘That thou art’what is done is that first of all it is shown that the Being enters the world at birth which shows that the Being is something distinct from the world, and then it is declared that ‘That thou art’ which asserts, without the slightest restraint, that the ‘Thou’ is absolutely and entirely the same as Being, the Self

units.sanskrit: ननु पराक्रमादिगुणः सिंहो ऽसि त्वमितिवत्तत्त्वमसीति स्यात् । न ।
units.english: ObjectionThe assertion ‘that thou art’ may be a figurative one, just as a man endowed with courage and other qualities is spoken as ‘you are a lion’

units.sanskrit: मृदादिवत्सदेकमेवाद्वितीयं सत्यमित्युपदेशात् ।
units.english: because it has been taught that Being, one, without a second, is the only real Entitylike ‘clay’ being the one entity pervading all products of clay

units.sanskrit: न चोपचारविज्ञानात्तस्य तावदेव चिरमिति सत्सम्पत्तिरूपदिश्येत । मृषात्वादुपचारविज्ञानस्य ।
units.english: If it were a more figurative expression, the knowledge thereof could not be spoken of as bringing about that mergence into Being where ‘the delay is only so long’ etc, because all figurative notions are false unreal

units.sanskrit: त्वमिन्द्रो ऽसि यम इतिवत् ।
units.english: just like the notions ‘you are Indra’, ‘you are Yama’

units.sanskrit: नापि स्तुतिरनुपास्यत्वाच्छ्वेतकेतोः । नापि सच्छ्वेतकेतुत्वोपदेशेन स्तूयेत ।
units.english: Nor can the figurative expression be regarded as an eulogy, because Śvetaketu is not a person to be worshipped hence eulogised;

units.sanskrit: न हि राजा दासस्त्वमिति स्तुत्यः स्यात् । नापि सतः सर्वात्मन एकदेशनिरोधो युक्तस्तत्त्वमसीति देशाधिपतेरिव ग्रामाध्यक्षस्त्वमिति । न चान्या गतिरिह सदात्मत्वोपदेशादर्थान्तरभूता सम्भवति ।
units.english: certainly the king could not be eulogised as you are the servant Even granting that it is an eulogy of Being It would not be right to restrict the Being, which is the AllSelf, to one point, by asserting ‘That thou art’, which would be like restricting the kingship of the king over the whole country to kingship over a single village

units.sanskrit: ननु सदस्मीतिबुद्धिमात्रमिह कर्तव्यतया चोद्यते न त्वज्ञातं सदसीति ज्ञाप्यत इति चेत् ।
units.english: OpponentAll that is taught here is that one should cultivate the notion that ‘ am Being’, and it does not make known, by saying ‘thou art Being anything that is not already known

units.sanskrit: नन्वस्मिन्पक्षे ऽप्यश्रुतं श्रुतं भवतीत्याद्यनुपपन्नम् ।
units.english: ‘But, even under this view, it would not be possible that the unheard becomes heard etc’Not so;

units.sanskrit: न, सदस्मीतिबुद्धिविधेः स्तुत्यर्थत्वात् ।
units.english: because in reality the idea that ‘ am Being’ is meant to be an eulogy

units.sanskrit: न, आचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेद तस्य तावदेव चिरमित्युपदेशात् ।
units.english: This cannot be right; because it has been taught that ‘the man with a teacher knows;

units.sanskrit: यदि हि सदस्मीति बुद्धिमात्रं कर्तव्यतया विधीयते न तु त्वंशब्दवाच्यस्य सद्रूपत्वमेव तदा ना'चार्यवान्वेदेति ज्ञानोपायोपदेशो वाच्यः यथाग्निहोत्रं जुहुयादित्येवमादिष्वर्थप्राप्तमेवा'चार्यवत्त्वमिति तद्वत् ।
units.english: and for him the delay is only so long etc, etc’If the idea that ‘ am Being’ had been enjoined as one to be cultivated,and not as asserting the fact of the entity devoted by the term ‘Thou’ being of the nature of Being itself,then there would be no point in asserting the means of obtaining that knowledge to be that ‘it is only the man with a teacher who knowsjust as in the case of such injunctions as ‘one should perform the Agnihotra’, the presence of the teacher from whom the Veda is learnt is already implied, and is nowhere actually enjoined

units.sanskrit: तस्य तावदेव चिरमिति च क्षेपकरणं न युक्तं स्यात् ।
units.english: Further, in that case there would be no point in asserting any such interval as is mentioned in the phrase ‘for him the delay is only so long etc, etc’

units.sanskrit: सदात्मतत्त्वे ऽविज्ञाते ऽपि सकृद्बुद्धिमात्रकरणे मोक्षप्रसङ्गात् ।
units.english: Lastly, under this interpretation that even without the realisation of one’s having his self in Being, if one only formed the said idea only once, he would at once attain liberation as he would have fulfilled the injunctions of cultivating the said notion

units.sanskrit: न च तत्त्वमसीत्युक्ते नाहं सदितिप्रमाणवाक्यजनिता बुद्धीर्निवर्तयितुं शक्या नोत्पन्नेति वा शक्यं वक्तुम् ।
units.english: Further, where it has been declared that ‘That thou art’, and its full signification understood as meaning that ‘ am Being’this notion cannot be rejected as being asserted by an unauthoritative assertion, or as not brought about by all by any means of cognition

units.sanskrit: सर्वोपनिषद्वाक्यानां तत्परतयैवोपक्षयात् ।
units.english: Because as a matter of fact, all Upaniṣadic texts point to the same conclusion that ‘ am Being’

units.sanskrit: यथाग्निहोत्रादिविधिजनिताग्निहोत्रादिकर्तव्यताबुद्धीनामतथार्थत्वमनुत्पन्नत्वं वा न शक्यते वक्तुं तद्वत् ।
units.english: in the case of this injunction, it cannot be denied that it lays down the performance of the Agnihotra and other rites, nor can it be denied that this notion is not brought about by that injunction

units.sanskrit: यत्तूक्तं सदात्मा सन्नात्मानं कथं न जानीयादिति । नासौ दोषः ।
units.english: It has been argued that‘If one has his Self in Being, how is it that he does not know himself?’But this does not vitiate our position

units.sanskrit: कार्यकरणसङ्घातव्यतिरिक्तो ऽहं जीवः कर्ता भोक्तेत्यपि स्वभावतः प्राणिनां विज्ञानादर्शनात्किसु तस्य सदात्मविज्ञानम् । कथमेवं व्यतिरिक्तविज्ञाने सति तेषां कर्तृत्वादिविज्ञानं सम्भवति दृश्यते च ।
units.english: Because normally, creatures do not even realise the fact that they are a living entity, the actor and enjoyer,distinct from the aggregate of causes and effects body; how can it be possible there to realise that they are of the nature of ‘Being’? In fact, if they had realised this difference of their selves from the body how could they have the idea of being the actor and enjoyer? and yet this idea is found to be present

units.sanskrit: तद्वत्तस्यापि देहादिष्वात्मबुद्धित्वान्न स्यात्सदात्मविज्ञानम् ।
units.english: In the same manner, so long as this man regards the body as the Self, they cannot realise the idea that they have their Self in Being

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्विकारानृताधिकृतजीवात्मविज्ञाननिवर्तकमेवेदं वाक्यं तत्त्वमसीति सिद्धमिति ॥
units.english: From all this it follows that what the sentence ‘That thou art’ does is to set aside the idea of ‘Self’ in regard to that ‘Living Ego’ which is a product, unreal and entitled to the performance of acts

units.sanskrit: अथ सप्तमो ऽध्यायः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अधीहि भगव इति होपससाद सनत्कुमारं नारदः ।
units.english: End of Discourse ‘Teach me, Revered Sir,’saying this Nārada approached Sanatkumāra

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच यद् वेत्थ तेन मोपसीद ।
units.english: He said to him‘What thou already knowest, come to me with that;

units.sanskrit: ततस् त ऊर्ध्वं वक्ष्यामीति ।
units.english: then shall teach thee beyond that’ He said

units.sanskrit: परमार्थन्तत्त्वोपदेशप्रधानपरः षष्ठो ऽध्यायः सदात्मैकत्वनिर्णयपरतयैवोपयुक्तः ।
units.english: Discourse has been devoted mainly to the expounding of the Highest Truth, and it has been used to determine the unity of Being, Self This teaching is meant for the Disciple of the highest grade

units.sanskrit: न सतोर्ऽवाग्विकारलक्षणानि तत्त्वानि निर्दिष्टानीत्यतस्तानि नामादीनि प्राणान्तानि क्रमेण
units.english: It has not dealt with things lower than the Being, in the form of products worldly things;

units.sanskrit: निर्दिश्य तद्द्वारेणापि भूमाख्यं निरतिशयं तत्त्वं निर्देक्ष्यामीति शाखाचन्द्रदर्शनवदितीनं
units.english: and yet an account of these also is needed for the disciple of the middle grade, who is unable to grasp the Highest Truth;

units.sanskrit: सप्तमं प्रपाठकमारभते ।
units.english: hence, the Seventh Discourse now begins, for the purpose of expounding just those things,beginning with Name and ending with LifeBreath Prāṇa;and then, through these, step by step, leading up to the Highest Truth, under the name of the ‘Bhūma’, ‘Infinite’

units.sanskrit: अनिर्दिष्टेषु हि सतोर्ऽवाक्तत्त्वेषु सन्मात्रे च निर्दिष्टे ऽन्यदप्यविज्ञातं स्यादित्याशङ्का कस्यचित्स्यात्सा मा भूदिति वा तानि निर्दिदिक्षति ।
units.english: Or, these other lower things are expounded now in order to preclude the notion that people might have to the effect that there may be other things yet known,if the text had not described these lower things and had ended with the expounding of Being aloneor, thirdly, it may be that the text proceeds to describe these lower thingsName and the rest,with the idea that, in the manner of ascending by series of steps, shall begin with the grossest things,

units.sanskrit: अथवा सोपानारोहणवत्स्थूलादारभ्य सूक्ष्मं सूक्षमतं च बुद्धिविषयं ज्ञापयित्वा तदतिरिक्ते स्वाराज्ये ऽभिषेक्ष्यामीति नामादीनि निर्दिदिक्षति
units.english: and then rising, step by step, to subtler and subtler things, make these amenable to cognition, and lead on to what lies beyond them, in the form of ‘selfsovereignty’ wherein shall install him the disciple

units.sanskrit: अथवा नामाद्युत्तरोत्तरविशिष्टानि तत्त्वान्यतितरां च तेषामुत्कृष्टतमं भूमाख्यं तत्त्वमिति तत्स्तुत्यर्थं नामादीनां क्रमेणोपन्यासः ।
units.english: Or, fourthly, what is meant is that‘these things, Name and the rest, are, mentioned in the ascending scale of importance the following one being more important than the preceding, and higher than all these stands that Entity called ‘Infinite’; so that it is for the eulogising of this Infinite that Name and the rest have been introduced in a definite order of importance

units.sanskrit: आख्यायिका तु परविद्यास्तुत्यर्था ।
units.english: As for the story, it has been introduced for the purpose of eulogising the Highest Philosophy

units.sanskrit: कथम् ।
units.english: In what way?

units.sanskrit: नारदो देवर्षिः कृतकर्तव्यः सर्वविद्यो ऽपि सन्ननात्मज्ञत्वाच्छुशोचैव किमु वक्तव्यमन्यो ऽल्पविज्जन्तुरकृतपुण्यातिशयो ऽकृतार्थ इति । अथवा नान्यदात्मज्ञानान्निरतिशयश्रेयः साधनमस्तीत्येतत्प्रदर्शनार्थं सनत्कुमारनारदाख्यायिका'रभ्यते । येन सर्वविज्ञानसाधनशक्तिसम्पन्नस्यापि नारदस्य देवर्षेः श्रेयो न बभूव येनोत्तमाभिजनविद्यावृत्तसाधनशक्तिसम्पत्तिनिमित्ताभि मानं हित्वा प्राकृतपुरुषवत्सनत्कुमारमुपससाद श्रेयःसाधनप्राप्तये ऽतः प्रख्यापितं
units.english: Nārada is a Divine Sage, who has fulfilled all his responsibilities, and had attained all knowledge and, yet, as he did not know the Self, he was sorry;what to say, then, of any ordinary creature with little knowledge, who has not acquired any particular kind of merit, and who is still one whose purposes have not been accomplishedOr, with a view to show that, apart from knowledge of Self, there is nothing that can accomplish the Highest Good,the text proceeds with the story of Sanatkumāra and Nārada, The sense is that though Nārada, a Divine sage, was equipped with the faculty of acquiring all knowledge, yet he did not attain the Highest Good,to such an extent that, renouncing all pride of unsurpassed percentage, deep learning, excellent character, and the possession of the power of accomplishing his aim,he approached Sanatkumāra, like an ordinary man, for the purpose of acquiring the means of attaining the Highest Good;

units.sanskrit: भवति निरतिशयप्राप्तिसाधनत्वमात्मविद्याया इति ।
units.english: and it becomes indicated by this story that Self knowledge is the means of attaining the Highest Good

units.sanskrit: अधीह्यधीष्व भगवा भ विन्निति किलोपससाद ।
units.english: ‘Teach me, Revered Sir’thus did Nārada approach Sanatkumāra

units.sanskrit: अधीहि भगव इति मन्त्रः । सनत्कुमारं योगीश्वरं ब्रह्मिष्ठं नारद उपसन्नवान् ।
units.english: The words ‘teach me, Revered Sir’ constitute a mantra, a formula, with which Nārada approached Sanatkumāra, the chief of mystics yogīndra, who stood firm in Brahman

units.sanskrit: तं न्यायत उपसन्नं होवाच यदात्मविषये किञ्चिद्वेत्थ तेन तत्प्रख्यापनेन मामुपसीदेदमहं जान इति ततो ऽहं भवतो विज्ञानात्ते तुब्यमूर्ध्वं वक्ष्यामीत्युक्तवति स होवाच नारदः ॥
units.english: To Nārada, who had approached him in the proper form, he said‘What thou already knowestregarding Self, come to me with that, ie come and give me an account of that,saying ‘this much know’; then shall teach thee beyond that, ie beyond what thou knowest already When he had said this, Nārada said as follows

units.sanskrit: ऋग्वेदं भगवो ऽध्येमि यजुर्वेदं सामवेदम् आथर्वणं चतुर्थम् इतिहासपुराणं पञ्चमं वेदानां वेदं पित्र्यं राशिं दैवं निधिं वाकोवाक्यम् एकायनं देवविद्यां ब्रह्मविद्यां भूतविद्यां क्षत्रविद्यां नक्षत्रविद्यां सर्पदेवजनविद्याम् एतद् भगवो
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, know the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the fourth Atharvaṇa, the ItihāsaPurāṇa, as the fifth of the Vedas,Grammar, the Science of ŚrāddhaRituals, Mathematics, the Science of Portents, the Science of Treasures, Logic, the Science of Ethics, the Science of Philology, the Vedic Science, the Physical Science, the Science of War, the Science of the Stars, the Science of Snakes, the Science of Celestials Fine Arts

units.sanskrit: ऽध्येमि ॥
units.english: All this, know, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: ऋग्वेदं भगवो ऽध्येमि स्मरामि यद्वेत्थेति विज्ञानस्य पृष्टत्वात् ।
units.english: ‘Revered sir, knowrememberthe Ṛgveda;

units.sanskrit: तथा यजुर्वेदं सामवेदमाथर्वणं चतुर्थं वेदं वेदशब्दस्य प्रकृतत्वादितिहासपुराणं पञ्चमं वेदं वेदानां भारतपञ्चमानां वेदं
units.english: that such is the meaning is clear from the question ‘tell me what you know’;similarly, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda and Atharvaṇa, the fourthie the fourth Veda, as it is the Veda that is the subjectmatter of the context;also ItihāsaPurāṇa, the fifth of the Vedas;

units.sanskrit: व्याकरणेन हि पदादिविभागश ऋग्वेदादयो ज्ञायन्ते ।
units.english: which are spoken as ‘having the Mahābhārata for their fifth’;Grammar; grammar has been called ‘Veda’ because, it is with the help of grammar that the Ṛgveda and other Vedas are understood through the various divisions into ‘Pada’ and the rest;

units.sanskrit: पित्र्यं श्राद्धकल्पम् । काशिं गणितम् ।
units.english: ‘Pitṛya’ stands for the Science of the ŚrāddhaRituals;‘Rāśi’ stands for Mathematics;

units.sanskrit: दैवमुत्पातज्ञानम् ।
units.english: ‘Daivata for the Science of Portents’;

units.sanskrit: निधिं महाकालादिनिधिशास्त्रम् । वाकोवाक्यं तर्कशास्रम् । एकायनं नीतिशास्रम् ।
units.english: ‘Nidhi’ for the Science of Treasures as propounded by Mahākāla and others;‘Vākovākya’ for logicthe Science of the Reasoning;‘Ekāyana’ for the Science of Ethics;

units.sanskrit: देवविद्यां निरुक्तम् । ब्रह्मण ऋग्यजुःसामाख्यस्य विद्यां ब्रह्मविद्यां शिक्षाकल्पच्छन्दोविचितयः । भूतविद्यां भूततन्त्रम् ।
units.english: ‘DevaVidyā’, for Nirukta, the Science of Philology;‘Brahmavidyā’ stands for the Vedic Science in the shape of Śikṣā Phonetics, Kalpa Rituals and Chandas Prosody;‘Bhūtavidyā’ is the Science of material substances, Physical Science;

units.sanskrit: क्षत्त्रविद्यां धनुर्वेदम् । नक्षत्रविद्यां ज्यौतिषम् । सर्पदेवजनविद्यां सर्पविद्यां गारुडं देवजनविद्यां गन्धयुक्तिनृत्यगीतवाद्यिशिल्पादिविज्ञानानि ।
units.english: ‘KṣattraVidyā’ is the Science of War, Archery;the Science of Stars, Astronomy;the Science of Snakesas Propounded by Garuḍa;the Science of Celestials,ie Perfumery, Dancing, Singing, Instrumental Music,Arts and Crafts

units.sanskrit: एतत्सर्वं हे भगवो ऽध्येमि ॥
units.english: All this, Revered Sir, know’

units.sanskrit: सो ऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविद् एवास्मि नात्मवित् ।
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, as am, know only the verbal texts, know not the Self

units.sanskrit: श्रुतं ह्य् एव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस् तरति शोकम् आत्मविद् इति । सो ऽहं भगवः शोचामि ।
units.english: It has been heard learnt by me from persons like your reverence that one who knows the Self passes beyond sorrow; am in sorrow;

units.sanskrit: तं होवाच यद् वै किंचैतद् अध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥
units.english: please, sir, make me pass beyond that sorrow’He said to him ‘Whatever you have studied is mere Name’

units.sanskrit: सो ऽहं भगव एतत्सर्वं जानन्नपि मन्त्रविदेवास्मि शब्दार्थमात्रविज्ञानवानेवास्मीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Revered sir, though knowing all this, as am, know only the verbal texts,ie know merely the simple meaning of words;

units.sanskrit: सर्वो हि शब्दो ऽभिधानमात्रमभिधानं च सर्वं मन्त्रेष्वन्तर्भवति । मन्त्रविदेवास्मि मन्त्रवित्कर्मविदित्यर्थः ।
units.english: all words are expression of some meaning; so that the meaning also becomes included in the ‘verbal texts’;thus what he means by saying that ‘ know only the Verbal texts’ is that ‘ know only the Ritualistic Acts’;

units.sanskrit: ऽमन्त्रेषु कर्माणी'ति हि वक्ष्यति ना'त्मविन्ना'त्मानं वेद्भि । नन्वात्मापि मन्त्रैः प्रकाश्यत एवेति कथं मन्त्रविच्चेन्ना'त्मवित् । न ।
units.english: below that ‘Ritualistic Arts are contained in the Mantratexts’; know not the Self; have no knowledge of the Self ObjectionAs a matter of fact, the Self also is described in the Verbal texts; how there could be a man knowing the text and not know the Self?

units.sanskrit: अभिधानाभिधेयभेदस्य विकारत्वात् ।
units.english: because thè very distinction between the denoted word and its denotation what it denotes is a mere product of Illusion, and the Self is not such a product

units.sanskrit: न च विकार आत्मेष्यते । नन्वात्माप्यात्मशब्देनाभिधीयते ।
units.english: But the self also is denoted by the term ‘Self’ ātman so that it would be a Product Not so;

units.sanskrit: नयतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते ।
units.english: because of the following Vedic declarations‘wherefrom Speech recoils’ Taitti

units.sanskrit: यत्र नान्य पश्यतिइत्यादिश्रुतेः ।
units.english: ‘wherein one sees nothing else’, and so forth which shows that the Self is beyond words

units.sanskrit: कथं तर्ह्या'त्मैवाधस्तात्ऽ ऽस आत्मेऽत्यादिशब्दा आत्मानं प्रत्याययन्ति ।
units.english: How then do such words as ‘the Self below’, ‘that is Self’ and the like convey the idea of the Self?

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: This does not vitiate our position

units.sanskrit: देहवति प्रत्यगात्मनि भेदविषये प्रयुज्यमानः शब्दो देहादीनामात्मत्वे प्रत्याख्यायमाने यत्परिशिष्टं सदवाच्यमपि प्रत्याययति ।
units.english: What actually happens is that the word ‘Ātman’ ‘Self’ is actually applied in usage, to the counterSelf the ‘Living Self’ born in the body, which is subject to notions of differentiation,and when the idea of the body and other appertenances being ‘Self’ is, one by one, set aside, then by the process of elimination, it comes to indirectly indicate the Being, even though this latter is not beyond the reach of the word

units.sanskrit: यथा सराजिकायां दृश्यमानायां सेनायां छत्रध्वजपताकादिव्यवहिते ऽदृश्यमाने ऽपि
units.english: For instance, when an army with the king is seen marching along, with umbrellas, flags, standards,even though the king is actually hidden by all this paraphernalia and hence, not visible, yet the expression is used ‘the king is seen’;

units.sanskrit: राजन्येष राजा दृश्यत इति भवति शब्दप्रयोगस्तत्र को ऽसौ राजेति राजविशेषनिरूपणायां दृश्यमानेतरप्रत्याख्याने ऽन्यस्मिन्नदृश्यमाने ऽपि राजनि राजप्रतीतिर्भवेत्तद्वत् ।
units.english: and when it is asked which is the king? and people come to look for the particular person who is the king,everyone of the other persons that are actually visible being rejected as not being the king, there follows as the result of elimination that the person who is not visible is the king,and thus the idea of the ‘king’ is secured;exactly similar is the case in question

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्सोहं मन्त्रवित्कर्मविदेवास्मि कर्मकार्यं च सर्वं विकार इति विकारज्ञ एवास्मि ना'त्मविन्ना'त्मप्रकृतिस्वरूपज्ञ इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Thus then what Nārada means is that ‘ know the verbal texts alone,that is, know only the Ritualistic Acts; and as all effects of actions are mere products, know only products,and know not the Self,ie, the real character of the Self’

units.sanskrit: अत एवोक्तमाचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेदेति ।
units.english: It is with a view to this that the text has declared that ‘it is only the man with a teacher that knows the Self’

units.sanskrit: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्तेइत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यश्च ।
units.english: This is also clear from such texts as ‘wherefrom Speech recoils’

units.sanskrit: श्रुतमागमज्ञानमस्त्येव हि यस्मान्मे मम भगवद्दृशेभ्यो युष्मत्सदृशेभ्यस्तरत्यतिक्रामति शोकं मनस्तापमकृतार्थबुद्धितामात्मविदित्यतः
units.english: ‘It has been learnt by me, have this cognition from a reliable word, verbal authority; since have learnt from Persons like your Reverence that one who knows the self passes beyond sorrow,that is, one who knows the Self goes beyond the reach of the mental anguish due to the idea that he has not accomplished his purpose in life

units.sanskrit: सो ऽहमनात्मवित्त्वाद्धे भगवः शोचाम्यकृतार्थबुद्ध्या सन्तप्ये सर्वदा तं मा मां शोकस्य शोकसागरस्य पारमन्तं भगवांस्तारयत्वात्मज्ञानोडुपेन कृतार्थबुद्धिमापादयत्वभयं गमयत्वित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Thus then, who know not Self,am in sorrow, O Revered sir,ie am constantly suffering from a feeling of disappointment at not having accomplished my purpose in life;please make me pass beyond that sorrow,carry me across to the other side of this sea of sorrow,by means of the raft of Selfknowledge,and make me feel that have accomplished my purpose in life,and thus lead me freedom from all fear’

units.sanskrit: तमेवमुक्तवन्तं होवाच यद्वै किञ्चैतदध्यगीष्ठा अधीतवानसि ।
units.english: When Nārada had said this, Sanatkumāra said, ‘Whatever you have studied is mere Name;study here indicates the understanding of meaning;

units.sanskrit: अध्ययनेन तदर्थज्ञानमुपलक्ष्यते ज्ञातवानसीत्येतन्नामैवैतत् ।
units.english: hence the meaning is that ‘whatever you know is mere Name’;

units.sanskrit: वाचा'रम्भणं विकारो नामधेयमिति श्रुतेः ॥
units.english: according to the Vedic text‘all this is a mere product of words, a mere Name’ Chā

units.sanskrit: नाम वा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेद आथर्वणश् चतुर्थ इतिहासपुराणः पञ्चमो वेदानां वेदः पित्र्यो राशिर् दैवो निधिर् वाकोवाक्यम् एकायनं देवविद्या ब्रह्मविद्या भूतविद्या क्षत्रविद्या नक्षत्रविद्या सर्पदेवजनविद्या ।
units.english: so also the Yajurveda, the Sāmadeva, and the fourth, the Atharvaṇa, the ItihāsaPurāṇa as the fifth of the Vedas,Grammar, the Science of ŚrāddhaRituals, Mathematics, the Science of Portents, the Science of Treasures, Logic, the Science of Ethics, the Science of Philology, the Vedic Science, the Physical Science, the Science of War, the Science of the Stars, the Science of Snakes, the Science of Celestials,all this is mere Name, Meditate upon Name’

units.sanskrit: नामैवैतत् ।
units.english: ‘The Ṛgveda indeed is a Name;

units.sanskrit: नाम वा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेद इत्यादि नामैवैतत् ।
units.english: so also the Yajurveda etc, etc,as all this is mere Name

units.sanskrit: नामोपाःस्व ब्रह्मेति ब्रह्मबुद्ध्या ।
units.english: Meditate upon Namethinking it to be Brahman;

units.sanskrit: यथा प्रतिमां विष्णुबुद्ध्योपास्ते तद्वत् ॥
units.english: just as people worship the Image, then think it to be Viṣṇu Himself

units.sanskrit: स यो नाम ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । यावन् नाम्नो गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो नाम ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगवो नाम्नो भूय इति । नाम्नो वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Name as Brahman becomes free to act as he wishes, in the sphere within reach of Name,for one who meditates upon Name as Brahman’‘Revered sir, is there anything greater than Name?’Certainly there is something greater than Name‘Explain that to me

units.sanskrit: तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: स यस्तु नाम ब्रह्मेत्युपास्ते तस्य यत्फलं भवति तच्छृणु यावन्नाम्नो
units.english: He who meditates upon Name as Brahman, to him accrues a certain reward;

units.sanskrit: गतं नाम्नो गोचरं तत्र तस्मिन्नामविषये ऽस्य यथाकामचारः कामचरणं राज्ञ इव स्वविषये भवति ।
units.english: hear what it is‘In the sphere within the reach of Name,ie so far as Name reaches,in that limited sphere,the man becomes free to act as he wishes,just like the king within his own domain;

units.sanskrit: यो नाम ब्रह्मेत्युपास्त इत्युपसंहारः ।
units.english: ‘for one who meditates upon Name as Brahman,’this is by way of recapitulation

units.sanskrit: किमस्ति भगवो नाम्नो भूयो ऽधिकतरं यद्ब्रह्मदृष्ट्यर्हमन्यदित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: ‘Is there anything greater, larger, higherthan Name, which deserves to be looked upon as Brahman’;

units.sanskrit: सनत्कुमार आह नाम्नो वाव भूयो ऽस्त्येवेत्युक्त आह यद्यस्ति तन्मे भगवान्ब्रवीत्विति ॥
units.english: Sanatkumāra answered‘Certainly, there is something greater than Name’Being told this, Nārada said‘If there is, then please explain that to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: वाग् वाव नाम्नो भूयसी ।
units.english: ‘Speech verily is greater than Name

units.sanskrit: वाग् वा ऋग्वेदं विज्ञापयति यजुर्वेदं सामवेदम् आथर्वणं चतुर्थम् इतिहासपुराणं पञ्चमं वेदानां वेदं पित्र्यं राशिं दैवं निधिं वाकोवाक्यम् एकायनं देवविद्यां ब्रह्मविद्यां भूतविद्यां क्षत्रविद्यां नक्षत्रविद्यां सर्पदेवजनविद्यां दिवं च पृथिवीं च वायुं चाकाशं चापश् च तेजश् च देवांश् च मनुष्यांश् च पशूंश् च वयांसि
units.english: It is Speech that makes known the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the fourth Atharvaṇa, the ItihāsaPurāṇa as the fifth of the Vedas, Grammar, the Science of ŚrāddhaRituals, Mathematics, the Science of Portents, the Science of Treasures, Logic, the Science of Ethics, the Science of Philology, the Vedic Science, the Physical Science, the Science of War, the Science of the Stars, the Science of Snakes, and the Science of Celestials;also Heaven, Earth, Air, Ākāśa, Water, Fire, Divine Beings, cattle, birds, grasses, trees, beasts down to worms and ants, virtue and vice, the true and the false, the good and the bad, the pleasant and the unpleasant

units.sanskrit: यद् वै वाङ् नाभविष्यन् न धर्मो नाधर्मो व्यज्ञापयिष्यन् न सत्यं नानृतं न साधु नासाधु न हृदयज्ञो नाहृदयज्ञः ।
units.english: If there had been no Speech neither virtue nor vice could be known, neither the true nor the false, neither the good, nor the bad, neither the pleasant nor the unpleasant

units.sanskrit: वाग् एवैतद् सर्वं विज्ञापयति वाचम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Speech alone makes known all this Meditate upon Speech’ Speech verily etc

units.sanskrit: वाग्वाव । वागितीन्द्रियं जिह्वाभूलादिष्वष्टसु स्थानेषु स्थितं वर्णानामभिव्यञ्जकम् ।
units.english: ‘Speech’ here stands for the organ of speech, located in eight places within the mouth, such as, the root of the tongue and the rest,which serves to manifest lettersounds;

units.sanskrit: वर्णाश्च नामेति नाम्नो वाग्भूयसीत्युच्यते ।
units.english: and it is letters that constitute the Name;hence speech is said to be ‘greater than Name’;

units.sanskrit: कार्यद्धि कारणं भूयो दृष्टं लोके यथा पुत्रात्पिता तद्वत् ।
units.english: in the world it has been found that the cause is always greater than the effect, as, for instance, the father is greater than the son

units.sanskrit: कथं च वाङ्नाम्नो भूयसीत्याहवाग्वा ऋग्वेदं विज्ञापयत्ययमृग्वेद इति ।
units.english: How is speech greater than Name?Answer ‘It is speech that makes known the Ṛgveda‘This is the Ṛgveda’;

units.sanskrit: तथा यजुर्वेदमित्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: similarly, Yajurveda etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: हृदयज्ञं हृदयप्रियम् । तद्विपरीतमहृदयज्ञम् ।
units.english: The pleasant is that which pleases the mind, and contrary to this is the unpleasant
