units.sanskrit: यद्यदि वाङ्नाभविष्यद्धर्मादि न व्यज्ञापयिष्यद्वागभावे ऽध्ययनाभावे तदर्थश्रवणाभावस्तच्छ्रवणाभावे धर्मादि न व्यज्ञापयिष्यन्न विज्ञातमभविष्यदित्यर्थः ।
units.english: If there had been no Speech neither virtue nor vice could be known; because in the absence of speech, there could be no study of the Veda, and in the absence of study, there would be no learning of what is contained in the Veda,and in the absence of this learning, virtue and the rest could not be known

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्वागेवैतच्छब्दोच्चारणेन सर्वं विज्ञापयत्यतो भूयसी वाङ्नाम्नस्तस्माद्वाचं ब्रह्मेत्युपाःस्व ॥
units.english: Thus it is speech alone which, through the utterance of letters, makes known all this; hence speech is greater than Name; hence meditate upon speech as Brahman’

units.sanskrit: स यो वाचं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । यावद् वाचो गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो वाचं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगवो वाचो भूय इति । वाचो वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Speech as Brahman becomes free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of Speech;for one who meditates upon Speech as Brahman,’Revered Sir, is there anything greater than Speech?Certainly there is something greater than Speech’Explain that to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as above

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: मनो वाव वाचो भूयः ।
units.english: ‘Mind is greater than Speech

units.sanskrit: यथा वै द्वे वामलके द्वे वा कोले द्वौ वाक्षौ मुष्टिर् अनुभवत्य् एवं वाचं च नाम च मनो ऽनुभवति ।
units.english: Just as the closed fist holds two Āmalaka, or two Kola, or two Akṣa, fruits,so does the Mind hold Speech and Name

units.sanskrit: स यदा मनसा मनस्यति मन्त्रान् अधीयीयेत्य् अथाधीते ।
units.english: And when one is minded in his mind to read the Veda, he reads it;

units.sanskrit: कर्माणि कुर्वीयेत्य् अथ कुरुते ।
units.english: when he is minded to perform actions, he performs them;

units.sanskrit: पुत्रांश् च पशूंश् चेच्छेयेत्य् अथेच्छते ।
units.english: when he is minded to desire sons and cattle, he desires them;

units.sanskrit: इमं च लोकम् अमुं चेच्छेयेत्य् अथेच्छते ।
units.english: and when he is minded to desire this world and also that world, he wishes for them

units.sanskrit: मनो ह्य् आत्मा । मनो हि लोकः । मनो हि ब्रह्म ।
units.english: Mind is indeed the Self, Mind is the World, Mind is Brahman

units.sanskrit: मन उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon the Mind

units.sanskrit: मनो मनस्यनविशिष्टमन्तःकरणं वाचो भूयः । तद्धि मनस्यनव्यापारवद्वाचं वक्तव्ये प्रेरयति ।
units.english: ‘Mind’ here stands for the internal organ as endowed with the function of reflecting;and this is greater than Speech When the Mind performs the operation of reflecting, it urges the Speech to say what has to be said;

units.sanskrit: तेन वाङ्मनस्यन्तर्भवति ।
units.english: hence Speech becomes included under Mind;

units.sanskrit: यच्च यस्मिन्नन्तर्भवति तत्तस्य व्यापकत्वात्ततो भूयो भवति ।
units.english: and when one thing is included in another, by reason of the latter being larger in extent it becomes, on that very account, greater

units.sanskrit: यथा वै लोके द्वे वा'मलके फले द्वे वा कोले बदरफले द्वौ वाक्षौ विभीतकफले मुष्टिरनुभवति मुष्टिस्ते फले व्याप्नोति मुष्टौ हि ते
units.english: just as in the world, the closed fist holds two Āmalaka fruits, or two KolaBadara fruits, or two AkṣaVibhītakafruits;ie when the closed fist contains them, when they become included under the closed fist,in the same manner, does the Mind hold Speech and Name, like the Āmalaka and other fruits

units.sanskrit: स यदा पुरुषे यस्मिन्काले मनसान्तःकरणेन मनस्यति मनस्यनं विवक्षाबुद्धिः कथं?
units.english: When at which timeone is minded in his Mind,in his internal organ;‘being minded’ stands for the desire to speak,what is he minded,

units.sanskrit: मन्त्रानधीयीयोच्चारयेयमित्येवं विवक्षां कृत्वाथाधीते तथा कर्माणि कुर्वीयेति चिकीर्षाबुद्धिं
units.english: to read the Veda,to recite it,having thus made up his mind to speak,he reads it;similarly, when he is minded to perform actions, ie has made up his mind to do them,he performs them;

units.sanskrit: कृत्वाथ कुरुते पुत्रांश्च पशूंश्चेच्छेयेति प्राप्तीच्छां कृत्वा तत्प्राप्त्युपायानुष्ठानेनाथेच्छते पुत्रादीन्प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । तथेमं च लोकममुं चोपायेनेच्छेयेति तत्प्रप्त्युपायानुष्ठानेनाथेच्छचे प्राप्नोति । मनो ह्यात्मा'त्मनः कर्तृत्वं भोक्तृत्वं च सति मनसि नान्यथेति मनो ह्यात्मेत्युच्यते ।
units.english: when he is minded to desire sons and cattle,ie having made up his mind to obtain them,and obtain them by having recourse to the means of obtaining them,then he desires them,ie he obtains Sons and other things;similarly, when he is minded to desire this world and also that world,seeks to obtain them by having recourse to the means of attaining them,then he wishes for themie attains them,Mind indeed is the Self;it is only when the Mind is thereand not otherwisethat the Self either performs acts or enjoys experiences hence the Mind is called the ‘Self’

units.sanskrit: मनो हि लोकः सत्येव हि मनसि लोको भवति तत्प्राप्त्युपायानुष्ठानं चेति मनो हि लोको यस्मात्तस्मान्मनो हि ब्रह्म ।
units.english: Mind is the World;it is only when the Mind is there that the World is there, and also the adopting of the means to attain it; hence Mind is the Worldand for that reason Mind is Brahman

units.sanskrit: यत एवं तस्मान्मन उपाःस्वेति ॥
units.english: Because all this is so, therefore meditate upon the Mind

units.sanskrit: स यो मनो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । यावन् मनसो गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो मनो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon the Mind as Brahman, becomes free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of the Mind;for one who meditates upon the Mind as Brahman

units.sanskrit: अस्ति भगवो मनसो भूय इति । मनसो वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: ‘Revered sir, is there anything greater than Mind?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Mind’

units.sanskrit: तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: ‘Explain that to me, Revered sir’

units.sanskrit: स यो इत्यादि समानम् ॥
units.english: ‘One who meditates on the Mind etc, etc’as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य तृतीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: संकल्पो वाव मनसो भूयान् ।
units.english: ‘Will indeed is greater than Mind

units.sanskrit: यदा वै संकल्पयते ऽथ मनस्यति । अथ वाचम् ईरयति ।
units.english: When one wills, then he minds, then he utters Speech;

units.sanskrit: ताम् उ नाम्नीयूअति ।
units.english: then he utters it in Name;

units.sanskrit: नाम्नि मन्त्रा एकं भवन्ति । मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि ॥
units.english: in the Name the mantras become one; and in the Mantras the performances become one’

units.sanskrit: संकल्पो वाव मनसो भूयान् । संकल्पो ऽपि मनस्यनवदन्तःकरणवृत्तिः कर्तव्याकर्तव्यविषयविभागेन समर्थनम् । विभागेन हि समर्थिते विषये चिकीर्षाबुद्धिर्मनस्यनानन्तरं भवति ।
units.english: Will indeed is greater than Mind;‘Will’ also here stands, like the’ act of minding, reflecting,for a particular functioning of the internal organ; that function which consists in determining and discriminating what should be done and what should not be done, it is only when a subject has been duly discriminated and determined upon, that there comes minding or reflection and then the desire to do

units.sanskrit: कथम् । यदा वै संकल्पयते कर्तव्यादिविषयान्विभजत इदं कर्तुं युक्तमिति, अथ मनस्यति मन्त्रानधीयीयेत्यादि । अथानन्तरं वाचमीरयति मन्त्राद्युच्चारणे ।
units.english: In what way?’When one wills,that is, discriminates subjects such as what should be done and the like,determining that ‘it is proper to do this’,then he minds reflects to read the Mantras and so forth;after this he utters speech,in reciting the mantras etc,then he utters it in Name,ie he utters it after having made up his Mind to utter the Name

units.sanskrit: तां च वाचमु नाम्नि नामोच्चारणनिमित्तं विवक्षां कृत्वेरयति नाम्नि नामसामान्ये मन्त्राः शब्दविशेषाः सन्त एकं भवन्त्यन्तर्भवन्तीत्यर्थः सामान्ये हि विशेषो ऽन्तभवति ।
units.english: In the Namein name in general,the Mantras become one,ie become included, because the Particular is always included,under the Universal In the Mantras, the performances become one;

units.sanskrit: मन्त्रेषु कर्माण्येकं भवन्ति । मन्त्रप्रकाशितानि कर्माणि क्रियन्ते नामन्त्रकमस्ति कर्म ।
units.english: as a matter of fact, acts of sacrifice are performed only as they are illumined indicated by the Mantratexts; and there is no sacrificial act without Mantras;

units.sanskrit: यद्धि मन्त्रप्रकाशनेन लब्धसत्ताकं सत्कर्म ब्राह्मणेनेदं कर्तव्यमस्मै फलायेति विधीयते । याप्युत्पत्तिर्ब्राह्मणेषु कर्मणां दृश्यते सापि मन्त्रेषु लब्धसत्ताकानामेव कर्मणां स्पष्टीकरणम् ।
units.english: it is only when the act has come into existence on being indicated by the Mantra that it comes to be enjoined in the form that ‘it should be performed by the Brāhmaṇa, for securing such and such results’; and wherever we find the origin of acts in the Brāhmaṇatexts, it is only the way of making clearer those acts which have already come into existence through Mantras;

units.sanskrit: न हि मन्त्राप्रकाशितं कर्म किञ्चिद्ब्राह्मण उत्पन्नं दृश्यते ।
units.english: there is not a single act found in the Brāhmaṇatexts which has not been indicated by Mantras;

units.sanskrit: त्रयीविहितं कर्मेति प्रसिद्धम् लोके ।
units.english: it is wellknown among people that Acts of sacrifice are laid down in the three Vedas;

units.sanskrit: त्रयीशब्दश्च ॠग्यजुःसामसमाख्या ।
units.english: and the term ‘three Vedas’ is a name for the Ṛk, Yajus, and Sāman

units.sanskrit: मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यन्निति चा'थर्वणे ।
units.english: In the Atharvaṇa, we find it declared that the wise ones saw the Acts in Mantras’

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्युक्तं मन्त्रेषु कर्माण्येकं भवन्तीति ॥
units.english: Thus, it is only right and proper that performances should become one in Mantras

units.sanskrit: तानि ह वा एतानि संकल्पैकायनानि संकल्पात्मकानि संकल्पे प्रतिष्ठितानि ।
units.english: ‘Indeed, all these merge in the Will,are made up of the Will, and abide in the Will

units.sanskrit: समकॢपतां द्यावापृथिवी ।
units.english: Heaven and Earth willed;

units.sanskrit: समकल्पेतां वायुश् चाकाशं च । समकल्पन्तापश् च तेजश् च ।
units.english: Air and Ākāśa willed; Water and Fire willed

units.sanskrit: तेषां संकॢप्त्यै वर्षं संकल्पते । वर्षस्य संकॢप्त्या अन्नं संकल्पते ।
units.english: Through the willing of these Rain wills; through the willing of Rain, food wills;

units.sanskrit: अन्नस्य संकॢप्त्यै प्राणाः संकल्पन्ते । प्राणानां संकॢप्त्यै मन्त्राः संकल्पन्ते ।
units.english: through the willing of Food, LifeBreaths will; through the willing of LifeBreaths, Mantras will;

units.sanskrit: मन्त्राणां संकॢप्त्यै कर्माणि संकल्पन्ते ।
units.english: through the willing of the Mantras, Acts will;

units.sanskrit: कर्मणां संकॢप्त्यै लोकः संकल्पते ।
units.english: through the willing of the Acts, the World wills;

units.sanskrit: लोकस्य संकॢप्त्यै सर्वं संकल्पते ।
units.english: through the willing of the World, all things will

units.sanskrit: स एष संकल्पः ।
units.english: This is Will Meditate upon Will’

units.sanskrit: प्रलयो येषां तानि संकल्पैकायनानि संकल्पात्मकान्युत्पत्तौ संकल्पे प्रतिष्ठितानि
units.english: All theseMind and the restmerge in the Will,ie their origination, birth, also lies in the Will,and abide in the Will,during their existence

units.sanskrit: स्थितौ समकॢपतां संकल्पं कृतवत्याविव हि द्यौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिव्यौ निश्चले लक्ष्येते । तथा समकल्पेतां वायुश्चा'काशं चैतावपि संकल्पं कृतवन्ताविव तथा समकल्पन्तामापश्च तेजश्च स्वेन रूपेम निश्चलानि लक्ष्यन्ते । यतस्तेषां द्यावापृथिव्यादीनां संकॢप्त्यै संकल्पनिमित्तं वर्षं संकल्पन्ते ।
units.english: Heaven and Earth,which stand for all that is immovable,willedperformed the act of volition; so also Air and Ākāśa willed,these also performed the act of volition, as it were;similarly, Water and Firewhich represent all that is immovable in its form,willed Through the willing of theseie on account of the willing of Heaven, Earth and the rest,Rain wills,ie becomes efficient;so throughon account ofthe willing of Rain, Food wills,as it is from Rain that Food is produced;through ie on account ofthe willing of Food, LifeBreaths will;

units.sanskrit: अन्नमया हि प्राणा अन्नोपष्टम्भकाः ।
units.english: because LifeBreaths are made up of Food and are nourished by Food;

units.sanskrit: अन्नं दामैति हि श्रुतिः । तेषां संकॢप्त्यै मन्त्राः संकल्पन्ते । प्राणावान्हि मन्त्रानधीते नाबलः ।
units.english: says the Vedic text‘Food is the bandage’;through the willing of LifeBreaths, the Mantras will; as it is only a man with strong LifeBreaths ie who is powerful who reads the Mantras, not a weak man;

units.sanskrit: मन्त्राणां हि संकॢप्त्यै कर्माण्यग्निहोत्रादीनि संकल्पन्ते ऽनुष्ठीयमानानि मन्त्रप्रकाशितानि समर्थीभवन्ति फलाय ।
units.english: through the willing of LifeBreaths, Acts willie such acts as Agnihotra and the like,ie when they are performed as indicated by the Mantras, they become capable of bringing about their results

units.sanskrit: ततो लोकः फलं संकल्पते कर्मकर्तृसमवायितया समर्थीभवतीत्यर्थः । लोकस्य संकॢप्त्यै सर्वं जगत्संकल्पते स्वरूपावैकल्याय ।
units.english: Through the willing of Acts, the World,the resultwills,ie becomes efficient by containing within itself the Acts and the Actors;through the willing of the World, all things,the entire Universewillsto attain and retain its complete form

units.sanskrit: एतद्धीदं सर्वं जगद्यत्फलावसानं तत्सर्वं संकल्पमूलम् ।
units.english: Thus all this Universe, which culminates in the final result, has its root in Will;

units.sanskrit: अतो विशिष्टः स एष संकल्पः ।
units.english: and thus highly qualified therein is Will;

units.sanskrit: अतः संकल्पमुपाःस्वेत्युक्त्वा फलमाह तदुपासकस्य ॥
units.english: hence meditate upon Will Having said this he describes in the following text the reward that accrues to one who meditates on Will

units.sanskrit: स यः संकल्पं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । कॢप्तान् वै स लोकान् ध्रुवान् ध्रुवः प्रतिष्ठितान् प्रतिष्ठितो ऽव्यथमानान् अव्यथमानो ऽभिसिध्यति । यावत् संकल्पस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यः संकल्पं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Will as Brahman, being himself lasting, wellestablished and undistressed, attains respectively lasting, wellestablished and undistressed regions determined for him;and becomes free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of the Will,for one who meditates upon Will as Brahman

units.sanskrit: अस्ति भगवः संकल्पाद् भूय इति । संकल्पाद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: ‘Revered Sir, is there anything greater than Will?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Will’‘Explain that to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: स यः संकल्पं ब्रह्मेति ब्रह्मबुद्ध्योपास्तेकॢप्तान्वै धात्रास्येमे लोकाः फलमिति कॢप्तान्समर्थितान्संकल्पितान्स विद्वान्ध्रुवान्नित्यानत्यन्ताध्रुवापेक्षया ध्रुवश्च स्वयम् । लोकिनो ह्यध्रुवत्वे लोके ध्रुवकॢप्तिव्यर्थेति ध्रुवः सन्प्रतिष्ठितानुपकरणसंपन्नानित्यर्थः ।
units.english: One who meditates upon Will as Brahman, ie regarding it as Brahman,he attains regions determined for himby God, as that ‘such and such regions will be his rewardthe learned man reaches the regions which have been thus decided upon, willed, for him;these regions are lastingeternal, as compared to things that are absolutely ephemeral,the man himself also being lasting;if the man inhabiting the regions were not lasting, then the very volition of the lasting would be futile;

units.sanskrit: पशुपुत्रादिभिः प्रतितिष्ठतीति दर्शनात्स्वयं च प्रतिष्ठित आत्मीयोपकरणसंपन्नो ऽव्यथमानानमित्रादित्रासरह् इतानव्यथमानश्च स्वयमभिसिध्यत्यभिप्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः
units.english: hence the man himself is lasting;the regions are also wellestablished,wellstocked with accessories,it being found that one becomes established through cattle, offspring and other accessories; and the man himself is also wellestablished,ie fully supplied with his own accessories the regions are undistressed,free from dangers arising from enemies and others;and the man himself is also undistressed;and such a man attains such regions as have been described

units.sanskrit: यावत्संकल्पस्य गतं संकल्पगोचरस्तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति आत्मनः संकल्पस्य न तु सर्वेषां संकल्पस्येति ।
units.english: And in the sphere within reach of the Will, he becomes free to act as he wishes,within reach of his own Will, not within the Will of others;

units.sanskrit: उत्तरफलविरोधात् ।
units.english: if the latter were meant, that would be contrary to the reward going to be described later on

units.sanskrit: यः संकल्पं ब्रह्मेत्युपास्त इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: This is for one who meditates upon Will as Brohman;as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: चित्तं वाव संकल्पाद् भूयः ।
units.english: ‘Intelligence indeed is greater than Will

units.sanskrit: यदा वै चेतयते ऽथ संकल्पयते । अथ मनस्यति । अथ वाचम् ईरयति ।
units.english: When one understands then he wills, then he reflects, then he utters Speech;

units.sanskrit: ताम् उ नाम्नीयूअति ।
units.english: he utters it in Name;

units.sanskrit: नाम्नि मन्त्रा एकं भवन्ति । मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि ॥
units.english: in Name, Mantras become one, and in the Mantras, the sacrificial acts’

units.sanskrit: चित्तं वाव संकल्पाद्भूयः । चित्तं चेतयितृत्वं प्राप्तकालानुरूपबोधवत्त्वमतीतान गतविषयप्रयोजननिरूपणसामर्थ्यं च तत्संकल्पादपि भूयः । कथम् । यदा वै प्राप्तमिति चेतयते तदा दानाय वापोहाय वाथ संकल्पयते ऽथ मनस्यतीत्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: Intelligence indeed is greater than Will;Intelligence is the faculty of understanding, the faculty of realising things at the proper moment, and the faculty of ascertaining the purpose underlying past and further events;thus Intelligence is greater than Will‘How?’ It is when one understands a thing, as ‘this thing happens to be so and so’, that he wills, as to whether it should be given to some one or thrown away;then he reflects, etc, etc as before

units.sanskrit: तानि ह वा एतानि चित्तैकायनानि चित्तात्मानि चित्ते प्रतिष्ठितानि ।
units.english: ‘Indeed all these merge in Intelligence, are made up of Intelligence and abide in Intelligence

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् यद्य् अपि बहुविद् अचित्तो भवति नायम् अस्तीत्य् एवैनम् आहुः । यद् अयं वेद यद् वा अयं विद्वान् नेत्थम् अचित्तः स्याद् इति ।
units.english: Therefore, even if a man knows much, if he be unintelligent, people speak of him as ‘he does not exist, as also what he might know if he were really learned, he would not be so unintelligent

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्य् अल्पविच् चित्तवान् भवति तस्मा एवोत शुश्रूषन्ते ।
units.english: On the other hand, if a man, knowing little, is Intelligent, they listen to him

units.sanskrit: चित्तं ह्य् एवैषाम् एकायनम् । चित्तम् आत्मा । चित्तं प्रतिष्ठा ।
units.english: Intelligence is the one mergent, Intelligence is the origin and Intelligence is the restingplace

units.sanskrit: चित्तम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon Intelligence’

units.sanskrit: तानि संकल्पादीनि कर्मफलान्तानि चित्तैकायनानि चित्तात्मानि चित्तोत्पत्तीनि चित्ते प्रतिष्ठितानि चित्तस्थितानीत्यपि पूर्ववत् ।
units.english: All thesebeginning with Will and ending with the result of Actions,merge in Intelligence,they are made up ofhave their source inIntelligence,and they abiderestin Intelligence,as before

units.sanskrit: किञ्च चित्तस्य माहात्म्यम् ।
units.english: Further, there is further greatness attaching to Intelligence

units.sanskrit: यस्माच्चित्तं संकल्पादिमूलं तस्माद्यद्यपि बहुविद्बहुशास्रादिपरिज्ञानवान्सन्नचित्तो भवति प्राप्तादिचेतयितृत्वसामर्थ्यविरहितो भवति तं निपुणा लौकिकानायमस्ति विद्यमानो ऽप्यसत्सम एवेत्येनमाहुः । यच्चायं किञ्चिच्छास्रादि वेद श्रुतवांस्तदप्यस्य वृथैवेति कथयन्ति ।
units.english: Inasmuch as Intelligence is the root of Will and the rest,even if a man knows much,possessed of much learning of the scriptures, if he be unintelligent,devoid of understanding things as they present themselves,peoplewise persons of the world,speak of him as ‘he does not exist ie even though he is present, he is as good as notpresent,‘so also is whatlittle of the scriptureshe might know whatever he might have learnt is entirely uselessWhy?If he were really learned, he would not be so unintelligent; hence whatever he has learnt is as good as not learnt;

units.sanskrit: कस्मात् ।
units.english: such is the meaning

units.sanskrit: अथाल्पविदपि यदि चित्तवान्भवति तस्मा एतस्मै तदुक्तार्थग्रहणायैवोतापि शुश्रूषन्ते श्रोतुमिच्छन्ति ।
units.english: On the other hand, if a man, knowing little, is intelligent, they listen to him,wish to have what he has to say regarding the subject at issue

units.sanskrit: तस्माच्च चित्तं ह्येवैषां संकल्पादीनामेकायनमित्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: Hence, it is Intelligence alone which is the mergent etc, of Will and the rest etc, etc,as before

units.sanskrit: स यश् चित्तं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । चित्तान् वै स लोकान् ध्रुवान् ध्रुवः प्रतिष्ठितान् प्रतिष्ठितो ऽव्यथमानान् अव्यथमानो ऽभिसिध्यति । यावच् चित्तस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यश् चित्तं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगवश् चित्ताद् भूय इति । चित्ताद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Intelligence as Brahman, being himself lasting, wellestablished and undistressed,attains lasting, wellestablished and undistressed regions prepared for him;and becomes free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of Intelligence,for one who meditates on Intelligence as Brahman’‘Revered Sir, is there anything greater than Intelligence?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Intelligence’‘Explain that to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: चित्तानुपचितान्हुद्धिमद्गुणैः स चित्तोपासको ध्रुवानित्यादि चोक्तार्थम् ॥
units.english: Preparedfully equipped with all those qualities that are found in intelligent man The man who meditates on Intelligence reaches lasting regions etc, etc

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य पञ्चमः खण्डः
units.english: as already explained End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: ध्यानं वाव चित्ताद् भूयः । ध्यायतीव पृथिवी । ध्यायतीवान्तरिक्षम् ।
units.english: ‘Contemplation indeed is greater than Intelligence, the Earth is contemplating, as it were; the skyis contemplating as it were;

units.sanskrit: ध्यायतीव द्यौः । ध्यायन्तीवापः ।
units.english: the Heaven is contemplating as it were; water is contemplating as it were;

units.sanskrit: ध्यायन्तीव पर्वताः ।
units.english: the mountains are contemplating as it were;

units.sanskrit: ध्यायन्तीव देवमनुष्याः ।
units.english: Deities and men are contemplating as it were

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् य इह मनुष्याणां महत्तां प्राप्नुवन्ति ध्यानापादांशा इवैव ते भवन्ति । अथ ये ऽल्पाः कलहिनः पिशुना उपवादिनस् ते ।
units.english: Therefore, one who among men attains greatness seems to have obtained a share of Contemplation; and while small people are quarrelsome and abusive and slandering, great men appear to have obtained a share of Contemplation

units.sanskrit: ध्यानम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon Contemplation’

units.sanskrit: स यो ध्यानं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । यावद् ध्यानस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो ध्यानं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगवो द्यानाद् भूय इति । ध्यानाद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: One who meditates upon Contemplation as Brahman becomes free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of Contemplation,one who meditates upon Contemplation as Brahman’‘Is there anything greater than Contemplation, Revered sir?’‘Certainly there is something greater that Contemplation’‘Please explain it to me, Revered sir’

units.sanskrit: ध्यानं वाव चित्ताद्भूयः ।
units.english: Contemplation indeed is greater than Intelligence

units.sanskrit: ध्यानं नाम शास्रोक्तदेवताद्यालम्बनेष्वचलो भिन्नजातीयैरनन्तरितः प्रत्ययसंतानः ।
units.english: ‘Contemplation’ stands for that unshaken continuous series of conceptions of such objects as a Deity and other beings mentioned in the scriptures, which is uninterrupted by other heterogenous conceptions;

units.sanskrit: एकाग्रतेति यमाहुः ।
units.english: this is what they call ‘onepointedness’, concentration’

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते च ध्यानस्य माहात्म्यं फलतः ।
units.english: How important Contemplation is actually seen in its results

units.sanskrit: कथम् । यथा योगी ध्यायन्निश्चलो भवति ध्यानफललाभे ।
units.english: In what way?When the Yogin is wrapped in Contemplation, he becomes immobile, unshaken, firm, on the attainment of the result of that Contemplation

units.sanskrit: एवं ध्यायतीव निश्चला दृश्यते पृथिवी । ध्यायतीवान्तरिक्षमित्यादि समानमन्यत् ।
units.english: In the same way, the Earth is contemplating as it were, and hence, it is found to be immovable;the Sky is contemplating, as it were;the rest is as before

units.sanskrit: देवाश्च मनुष्याश्च देवमनुष्या मनुष्या एव वा देवसमा देवमनुष्याः शमादिगुणसंपन्ना मनुष्या देवस्वरूपं न जहतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Deities and men which is one way of taking the compound ‘devamanuṣyāḥ’,or Divine Menmenlike Deities, which is another explanation of the Compound ‘devamanuṣyāḥ’, ie men endowed with calmness and other qualities, who never renounce their divine character

units.sanskrit: यस्मादेवं विशिष्टं ध्यानं तस्माद्य इह लोके मनुष्याणामेव धनैर्विद्यया गुणैर्वा महत्तां महत्त्वं प्राप्नुवन्ति धनादिमहत्त्वहेतुं लभन्त
units.english: Inasmuch as Contemplation is so excellent,those who, among men, attain greatness,through wealth, or learning or other qualitiesie, those who acquire wealth and such other sources of greatness, superiority,seem to have obtained a share of Contemplation,ie obtained a part of the effects of Contemplation,and they appear to be immovable,nor like small people;

units.sanskrit: अथ ये पुनरल्पाः क्षुद्राः किञ्चिदपि धनादिमहत्त्वैकदेशमप्राप्तास्ते पूर्वोक्तविपरीताः कलहिनः कलहशीलाः पिशुनाः परदोषोद्भासका उपवादिनः परदोषं सामीप्ययुक्तमेव वदितुं शीलं योषां त उपवादिनश्च भवन्ति । अथ ये महत्त्वं प्राप्ता धनादिनिमित्तं ते ऽन्यान्प्रति प्रभवन्तीति प्रभवो विद्याचार्यराजेश्वरादयो ध्यानापादांशा इवेत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ।
units.english: on the other hand, those who are small,’ mean,who have not obtained even a fraction of the effects of Contemplation,they are quite contrary to the above,are quarrelsomeprone to quarrel with people,abusive finding fault with others,and slanderingspeaking ill of people, as if what is said happened before their eyes;while those who have attained greatness,due to wealth and other things,are great,lord it over other people, like Professors and Emperors,and they appear to have obtained a share of Contemplation;this has been already explained

units.sanskrit: अतो दृश्यते ध्यानस्य महत्त्वं फलतो ऽतो भूयश्चित्तादतस्तदुपाःस्वेत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ॥
units.english: Thus the greatness of Contemplation is seen in its effects; hence, it is greater than Intelligence; for these reasons, meditate upon Contemplation, etc, etc

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य षष्ठः खण्डः
units.english: as already explained End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: विज्ञानं वाव ध्यानाद् भूयः । विज्ञानेन वा ऋग्वेदं विजानाति यजुर्वेदं सामवेदम् आथर्वणं चतुर्थम् इतिहासपुराणं पञ्चमं वेदानां वेदं पित्र्यं राशिं दैवं निधिं वाकोवाक्यम् एकायनं देवविद्यां ब्रह्मविद्यां भूतविद्यां क्षत्रविद्यां नक्षत्रविद्यां सर्पदेवजनविद्यां दिवं च पृथिवीं च वायुं चाकाशं चापश् च तेजश् च देवांश् च मनुष्यांश् च पशूंश् च वयांसि
units.english: ‘Learning indeed is greater than Contemplation,it is by Learning that one knows the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the fourth Atharvaṇa, the ItihāsaPurāṇa as the fifth of the Vedas, Grammar, the Science of ŚrāddhaRituals, Mathematics, the Science of Portents, the Science of Treasures, Logic, the Science of Ethics, the Science of Philology, the Vedic Science, the Physical Science, the Science of War, the Science of stars, the Science of Snakes, and the Science of Celestials;also Heaven, Earth, Ākāśa, Water, Fire, Divine Beings, human beings, cattle, birds, grasses, trees, beasts, down to worms and ants, virtue and vice, the true and the false, the good and the bad, the pleasant and unpleasant, food and juices, this world and that world,all this one knows by Learning,Meditate upon Learning’

units.sanskrit: विज्ञानं वाव ध्यानाद्भूयः ।
units.english: Learning indeed is greater than Contemplation

units.sanskrit: विज्ञानं शास्रार्थविषयं ज्ञानं तस्य ध्यानकारणत्वाद्ध्यानाद्भूयस्त्वम् ।
units.english: ‘Learning’ stands for the knowledge of the subjectmatter of the Scriptures; it is this that is the source of Contemplation;

units.sanskrit: कथं च तस्य भूयस्त्वमित्याहविज्ञानेन वा ऋग्वेदं विजानात्ययमृग्वेद इति प्रमाणतया यस्यार्थज्ञानं ध्यानकारणम् । तथा यजुर्वेदमित्यादि ।
units.english: In what way is it greater?It is by Learning that one knows the Ṛgveda,that ‘this is the Ṛgveda’, the source of right knowledge, the knowledge of the subjectmatter of which is the source of Contemplation;similarly, the Yajurveda etc, etc

units.sanskrit: किञ्च पश्वादींश्च धर्माधर्मौ शास्रसिद्धौ । साध्वसाधुनी लोकतः सिद्धे, स्मार्ते वा दृष्टादृष्टाविषयं च सर्वं विज्ञानेनैव विजानातीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: also cattle and the rest,and virtue and vicewhich are known through the scriptures,the good and the bad,either from the viewpoint of commonsense, or from that of the Smṛtis,and in fact, all imperceptible thingsone knows only by means of Learning

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्युक्तं ध्यानादिज्ञानस्य भूयस्त्वम् अतो विज्ञानमुपाःस्वेति ॥
units.english: Hence, it is only right that Learning should be greater than Contemplation Hence, meditate upon Learning’

units.sanskrit: यावद् विज्ञानस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो विज्ञानं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Learning as Brahman attains the regions of Learning and of Knowledge; he becomes free to do as he wishes, in the sphere within reach of Learning;

units.sanskrit: अस्ति भगवो विज्ञानाद् भूय इति । विज्ञानाद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: he who meditates upon Learning as Brahman’‘Is there anything greater than Learning, ‘Revered Sir?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Learning’‘Explain that to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: शृणूपासनफलं विज्ञानवतो विज्ञानं येषु लोकेषु तान्विज्ञानवतो लोकाञ्ज्ञानवतश्चाभिसिध्यत्यभिप्राप्नोति ।
units.english: Listen to the reward accruing from the said Meditation The regions of Learningthose regions where Learning abounds,as also those where Knowledge abounds,he attainsobtains;

units.sanskrit: विज्ञानं शास्रार्थविषयं ज्ञानमन्यविषयं नैपुण्यं तद्वद्भिर्युक्तांल्लोकान्नाप्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: that is, he reaches those regions which are inhabited by persons possessing Learning,ie, deep knowledge of the subjectmatter of the scriptures

units.sanskrit: यावद्विज्ञानस्येत्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: In the sphere etc, etc, as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य सप्तमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: बलं वाव विज्ञानाद् भूयः ।
units.english: ‘Power is greater than Learning

units.sanskrit: अपि ह शतं विज्ञानवताम् एको बलवान् आकम्पयते ।
units.english: A single man with Power shakes a hundred men with Learning

units.sanskrit: स यदा बली भवत्य् अथोत्थाता भवति ।
units.english: When a man has Power, he rises;

units.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठन् परिचरिता भवति । परिचरन्न् उपसत्ता भवति ।
units.english: rising, he serves; serving, he approaches nearer;

units.sanskrit: उपसीदन् द्रष्टा भवति श्रोता भवति मन्ता भवति बोद्धा भवति कर्ता भवति विज्ञाता भवति ।
units.english: approaching nearer, he sees, hears, reflects, understands, acts and feels

units.sanskrit: बलेन वै पृथिवी तिष्ठति बलेनान्तरिक्षं बलेन द्यौर् बलेन पर्वता बलेन देवमनुष्या बलेन पशवश् च वयांसि च तृणवनस्पतयः श्वापदान्य्
units.english: by Power, the Sky; by Power, the Heaven; by Power, the mountains; by Power, Deities and men; by Power, cattle, birds, grasses and trees, beasts down to ants and worms;

units.sanskrit: बलेन लोकस् तिष्ठति ।
units.english: and by Power does the world stand

units.sanskrit: बलम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon Power’

units.sanskrit: स यो बलम् उपास्ते । यावद् बलस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो बलं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगवो बलाद् भूय इति । बलाद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Power as Brahman, becomes free to do as he wishes, in the sphere within reach of Power;one who meditates upon Power as Brahman‘Is there anything greater than Power, Revered Sir?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Power,’‘Explain that to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: बलं वाव विज्ञानाद्भूयः । बलमित्यन्नोपयोगजनितं मनसो विज्ञेये प्रतिभानसामर्थ्यम् ।
units.english: Power is greater than Learning‘Power’ stands for that capacity of the mind to apprehend things which is due to the use of food;

units.sanskrit: अनशनादृगादीनि न वै मा प्रतिभान्ति भो इति श्रुतेः ।
units.english: as says the Śruti through fasting, the Ṛk and other Vedas do not reveal themselves to me’;in the body also, Power consists in the capacity to rise and do such things

units.sanskrit: शरीरे ऽपि तदेवोत्थानादिसामर्थ्यं यस्माद्विज्ञानवतां शतमप्येकः प्राणी बलवाना कम्पयते यथा हस्ती मत्तो मनुष्याणां शतं समुदितमपि यस्मादेवमन्नाद्युपयोगनिमित्तं बलं तस्मात्स पुरुषो यदा बली बलेन तद्वान्भवत्यथोत्थातोत्थानस्य कर्तोत्तिष्ठंश्च गुरूणामाचार्यस्य च परिचरिता परिचरणस्य शुश्रूषायाः कर्ता भवति परिचरन्नुपसत्ता तेषां समीपगो ऽन्तरङ्गः प्रयो भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Because a single person with Power shakes a hundred men with Learning, just as the infuriated elephants scatter a hundred men even when assembled together,because the Power brought about by the use of Food is so,therefore, when a man has Power,ie, through Power, becomes powerful,then, he rises,ie, he does the act of rising;rising, he servesof instructions and the teacher, the performer of service;serving, he approaches nearer,ie, approaching nearer to the teacher etc, he becomes familiar and dear to them;approaching nearer, he sees, with concentrated attention, the teacher and other instructors;then he hears what they say;then he reflects upon what he has heard, with due reasoning etc

units.sanskrit: ततस्तदुक्तस्य श्रोता भवति । तत इदमेभिरुक्तमेवमुपपद्यत इत्युपपत्तितो मन्ता भवति मन्वानश्च बोद्धा भवत्येवमेवेदमिति । तत एवं निश्चित्य तदुक्तार्थस्य कर्तानुष्ठाता भवति विज्ञातानुष्ठानफलस्यानुभविता भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: ‘This is what they have said, and it is quite reasonable’;having reflected over it, he understands it, concluding that ‘it must be so and so’;having thus come to a definite conclusion, he acts, carries into practice what he has been taught;and then he feels,ie experiences the effects of his action,further, the greatness of Power lies in this that by Power does the world stand etc,, etc,the meaning of all which is simple

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्याष्टमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: अन्नं वाव बलाद् भूयः ।
units.english: ‘Food indeed is greater than Power

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् यद्य् अपि दश रात्रीर् नाश्नीयात् । यद्य् उ ह जीवेत् । अथवाद्रष्टाश्रोतामन्ताबोद्धाकर्ताविज्ञाता भवति ।
units.english: Therefore, if one does not eat for ten nights,even if he keeps alive, he is unable to see, unable to hear, unable to reflect, unable to understand, unable to act, and unable to know

units.sanskrit: अथान्नस्याये द्रष्टा भवति श्रोता भवति मन्ता भवति बोद्धा भवति कर्ता भवति विज्ञाता भवति । अन्नम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: And when he comes by Food, he is able to see, able to hear, able to reflect, able to understand, able to act, and able to know,Meditate upon Food’

units.sanskrit: अन्नं वाव बलाद्भूयः । बलहेतुत्वात् ।
units.english: Food indeed is greater than Power,because it is the source of Power

units.sanskrit: कथमन्नस्य बलहेतुत्वमित्युच्यते ।
units.english: It is next explained how Food is the source of Power

units.sanskrit: यस्माद्बलकारणमन्नं तस्माद्यद्यपि कश्चिद्दश रात्रीर्नाश्नीयात्सो ऽन्नोपयोगानिमित्तस्य बलस्य हान्या म्रियते न चेन्म्रियते यद्यु ह जीवेत् । दृश्यन्ते हि मासमप्यनश्नन्तो जीवन्तः । अथवा स जीवन्नप्यद्रष्टा भवति गुरोरपि तत एवाश्रोतेत्यादि पूर्वविपरीतं सर्वं भवति ।
units.english: Because Food is the source of Power, therefore, if one does not eat for ten nights, he would ordinarily die, on account of the loss of Power or strength which is due to the use of Food; if, however, he does not die,even if he lives;which is not unlikely as we find people keeping alive after having fasted for a month;but even though he may keep alive,he is unable to see and unable to hearthe words of the teacher, and so forth ie it becomes all contrary to what he was before

units.sanskrit: अथ यदा बहून्यहान्यनशितो दर्शनादिक्रियास्वसमर्थः सन्नन्नस्या'यी ।
units.english: And when, having fasted for several days and having been unable to perform the functions of seeing, hearing and the rest,he comes by Food;‘āya’ is coming;

units.sanskrit: आगमनमायो ऽन्नस्य प्राप्तिरित्यर्थः ।
units.english: hence ‘annasyāya’ is coming by Food;

units.sanskrit: सा यस्य विद्यते सो ऽन्नस्या'यी ।
units.english: and one who has come by Food is ‘annasyāyī’;

units.sanskrit: आय इत्येतद्वर्णव्यत्ययेन ।
units.english: the form ‘āyai’ is got at by a change in the vowel;

units.sanskrit: अथान्नस्या'या इत्यपि पाठ एवमेवार्थः ।
units.english: the reading ‘annasyaāyā’ also gives the same sense;

units.sanskrit: द्रष्टेत्यादिकार्यश्रवणात् ।
units.english: because we find the effects described in the form of ‘being able to see’ and the rest

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते ह्यन्नोपयोगे दर्शनादिसामर्थ्यं न तदप्राप्तावतो ऽन्नमुपाःस्वेति ॥
units.english: As a matter of fact, it is found that when one makes use of Food, he regains the faculty of seeing etc, which he does not do if he does not get Food

units.sanskrit: स यो ऽन्नं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अन्नवतो वै स लोकान् पानवतो ऽभिसिध्यति । यावद् अन्नस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो ऽन्नं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Food as Brahman attains regions supplied with Food and Drink; and he is free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of Food;one who meditates upon Food as Brahman’‘Is there anything greater than Food;

units.sanskrit: अस्ति भगवो ऽन्नाद् भूय इति । अन्नाद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: Revered Sir?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Food’‘Explain it to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: फलं चान्नवतः प्रभूतान्नान्वै स लोकान्पानवतः प्रभूतोदकांश्चान्नपानयोर्नित्यसंबन्धाल्लोकानभिसि ध्यति ।
units.english: The reward accruing to the man supplied with Food is as followsHe attains Regions, supplied with large quantities of Food, also those supplied with Drink with large supplies of water,Food and Drink always go together

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य नवमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: आपो वावान्नाद् भूयस्यः ।
units.english: ‘Water indeed is greater than Food

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् यदा सुवृष्टिर् न भवति व्याधीयन्ते प्राणा अन्नं कनीयो भविष्यतीति ।
units.english: Therefore, when there is not sufficient Rain, the Spirits are in agony at the thought that there will be less Food;

units.sanskrit: अथ यदा सुवृष्टिर् भवत्य् आनन्दिनः प्राणा भवन्त्य् अन्नं बहु भविष्यतीति ।
units.english: while, when there is sufficient Rain, the Spirits become joyous at the thought that there will be much Food

units.sanskrit: आप एवेमा मूर्ता येयं पृथिवी यद् अन्तरिक्षं यद् द्यौर् यत् पर्वता यद् देवमनुष्या यत् पशवश् च वयांसि च तृणवनस्पतयः श्वापदान्य् आकीटपतङ्गपिपीलकम्
units.english: It is Water having assumed form that has become Earth, Sky, Heaven, Mountains, Deities and Men, cattle and birds, grasses and trees, beasts down to insects, worms and ants

units.sanskrit: आप एवेमा मूर्ताः ।
units.english: All these are Water having assumed forms

units.sanskrit: अप उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon Water’

units.sanskrit: आपो वावान्नाद्भूयस्यो ऽन्नकारणत्वात् ।
units.english: Water indeed is greater than Food

units.sanskrit: यस्मादेवं तस्माद्यदा यस्मिन्काले सुवृष्टिः सस्यहिता शोभना वृष्टिर्न भवति तदा व्याधीयन्ते प्राणा दुःखिनो भवन्ति । किंनिमित्तमित्याहान्नमस्मिन्संवत्सरे नः कनीयो ऽल्पतरं भविष्यतीति । अथ पुनर्यदा सुवृष्टिर्भवति तदा'नन्दिनः सुखिनो हृष्टाः प्राणाः प्राणिनो भवन्त्यन्तं बहु प्रभूतं भविष्यतीति ।
units.english: Because it is so, therefore, when,at which time,there is not sufficient Rainenough to benefit the crops,then the Spirits of men are in agony,in pain;why?at the thought that ‘this year there will be less Food for usless than usual;while when there is sufficient Rain, then the Spirits become joyous,all living beings become happy, delighted,at the prospect that there will be much Food,Because, solid Food has its source in Water, all these thingsthat are found to be solidified into various forms, as well as formlesssuch as Earth, Sky and the rest,are only Water solidifiedassumed forms;

units.sanskrit: आप एवेमा मूर्ता अतो ऽप उपाःस्वेति ॥
units.english: all these things with forms are Water itself Therefore, meditate upon Water

units.sanskrit: स यो ऽपो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । आप्नोति सर्वान् कामांस् तृप्तिमान् भवति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Water as Brahman secures all desires and becomes satisfied;

units.sanskrit: यावद् अपां गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यो ऽपो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
units.english: he becomes free to act as he wishes, in the sphere within reach of Water,one who meditates upon Water as Brahman’

units.sanskrit: अस्ति भगवो ऽद्भ्यो भूय इति । अद्भ्यो वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: ‘Is there anything greater than Water, Revered Sir?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Water’‘Explain it to me, Revered Sir’

units.sanskrit: फलंस यो ऽपो ब्रह्मेत्युपास्त आप्नोति सर्वान्कामान्काम्यान्मूर्तिमतो विषयानित्यर्थः ।
units.english: The reward is as followsOne who meditates upon Water as Brahman, secures all desires,ie all desirable things with forms

units.sanskrit: अप्संभवत्वाच्च तृप्तेरम्बुपासनात्तृप्तिमांश्च भवति ।
units.english: And because satisfaction proceeds from Water, the man becomes satisfied also by meditating upon Water

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य दशमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: तेजो वावाद्भ्यो भूयः ।
units.english: ‘Fire indeed is greater than Water

units.sanskrit: तेज एव तत्पूर्वं दर्शयित्वाथापः सृजते । तद् एतद् ऊर्ध्वाभिश् च तिरश्चीभिश् च विद्युद्भिर् आह्रादाश् चरन्ति तस्माद् आहुर् विद्योतते स्तनयति वर्षिष्यति वा इति । तेज एव तत्पूर्वं दर्शयित्वाथापः सृजते ।
units.english: then people say ‘it is hot, it burns, it will rain’;it is Fire that having shown itself first, creates Water Then again, when thunderings go on, along with lightnings flashing upwards and horizontally, and people say ‘lightning is flashing, it is thundering, it will rain,’‘it is Fire that, having shown itself first, creates Water

units.sanskrit: तेज उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon fire’

units.sanskrit: तेजो वावाद्भ्यो भूयः ।
units.english: Fire indeed is greater than Water;

units.sanskrit: तेजसो ऽपकारणत्वात् ।
units.english: because Fire has no cause

units.sanskrit: यस्मादब्योनिस्तेजस्तस्मात्तद्वा एतत्तेजो वायुमागृह्यावष्टभ्य स्वात्मना निश्चलीकृत्य वायुमाकाशमभितपत्याकाशमभिव्याप्नुवत्तपति यदा तदा'हुर्लौकिका निशोचति संतपति सामान्येन जगन्नितपति देहानतो वर्षिष्यति वा इति ।
units.english: Why has Fire no cause?Because Fire is the origin of Water, therefore, when itFirehaving held the Air,having closed up the Air,ie having made it immobile by itself,it warms the Ākāśa,ie pervading over warms it up, then, peopleordinary men of the world say, ‘it is hot’the whole world in general,‘it burns’the bodies of living beings, hence‘it will rain’

units.sanskrit: प्रसिद्धं हि लोके कारणमभ्युद्यतं दृष्टवतः कार्य भविष्यतीति विज्ञानम् ।
units.english: It is well known in the world that when one perceives the cause he has the notion that the effect will come

units.sanskrit: तेज एव तत्पूर्वमात्मानमुद्भूतं दर्शयित्वाथानन्तरमपः सृजते ऽतो ऽप्स्रष्टृत्वाद्भून्यो ऽद्भ्यस्तेजः ।
units.english: It is Fire that, having shown itself first,as manifesteditafterwardscreates water; and thus, as it creates water, Fire is greater than Water

units.sanskrit: किञ्चान्यत्तदेतत्तेज एव स्तनयित्नुरूपेण वर्षहेतुर्भवति ।
units.english: There is a further reason; it is this Fire itself which, in the form of Clouds, became the cause of rain

units.sanskrit: कथम् । ऊर्ध्वाभिश्चोर्ध्वगाभिर्विद्युद्भिस्तिरश्चीभिश्च तिर्यग्गताभिश्च सहा'ह्रादाः स्तननशब्दाश्चरन्ति ।
units.english: In what way?Thunderingsof cloud,go on, along with lightnings flashing upwards and horizontally;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्तद्दर्शनादाहुर्लौकिका विद्योतते स्तनयति वर्षिष्यति वा इत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ।
units.english: and on seeing this, people say‘lightning is flashing, it is thundering, it will rain’ etc, etc

units.sanskrit: अतस्तेज उपाःस्वेति ॥
units.english: Hence, meditate upon Fire

units.sanskrit: स यस् तेजो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । तेजस्वी वै स तेजस्वतो लोकान् भास्वतो ऽपहततमस्कान् अभिसिध्यति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Fire as Brahman, being resplendent himself, attains resplendent regions, full of light and free from darkness;

units.sanskrit: यावत् तेजसो गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यस् तेजो ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते ।
units.english: and he becomes free to act as he wishes, in the sphere within reach of Fire,one who meditates upon Fire as Brahman’

units.sanskrit: अस्ति भगवस् तेजसो भूय इति । तेजसो वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: ‘Is there anything greater than Fire, Revered sir?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Fire’‘Please explain to me

units.sanskrit: तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: Revered sir’

units.sanskrit: तस्य तेजस उपासनफलंतेजस्वी वै भवति । तेजस्वत एव च लोकान्भास्वतः प्रकाशवतो ऽपहततमस्कान्बाह्याध्यात्मिकाज्ञानाद्यपनीततमस्कानभिसिध्यति ।
units.english: The reward for meditating upon Fire, is as follows He becomes resplendent,attains resplendent regions, full of light and free from darkness,ie from which all darkness of material and spiritual ignorance

units.sanskrit: ऋज्वर्थमन्यत् ॥
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: आकाशो वाव तेजसो भूयान् । आकाशे वै सूर्याचन्द्रमसाव् उभौ विद्युन् नक्षत्राण्य् अग्निः ।
units.english: ‘Ākāśa indeed is greater than Fire, in the Ākāśa subsist the sun and the moon, lightning, stars and fire

units.sanskrit: आकाशेनाह्वायति ।
units.english: It is through Ākāśa that one calls;

units.sanskrit: आकाशेन सृणोति । आकाशेन प्रतिसृणोति ।
units.english: it is through Ākāśa that one hears; it is through Ākāśa that one hears back;

units.sanskrit: आकाशे रमते । आकाशे न रमते ।
units.english: it is in Ākāśa that one rejoices; it is in Ākāśa that one does not rejoice;

units.sanskrit: आकाशे जायते । आकाशम् अभिजायते ।
units.english: in Ākāśa is everything born; and it is Ākāśa towards which every thing grows

units.sanskrit: आकाशम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: आकाशो वाव तेजसो भूयान् ।
units.english: Ākāśa indeed is greater than Fire;

units.sanskrit: वायुसहितस्य तेजसः कारणत्वाद्व्योम्नो वायुमागृह्येति तेजसा सहोक्तो वायुरिति पृथगिह नोक्तस्तेजसः ।
units.english: because Ākāśa is the cause origin of Fire along with Air In the previous section, Air has been mentioned along with fire, in the phrase ‘having held the Air’; hence Air has been mentioned separately here;

units.sanskrit: कारणं हि लोके कार्याद्भूयो दृष्टम् ।
units.english: in the world, the cause has always been found to be larger than its effect;

units.sanskrit: यथा घटादिभ्यो मृत्तथा'काशो वायुसहितस्य तेजसः कारणमिति ततो भूयान् ।
units.english: e g the clay is larger than the jar; similarly, Ākāśa is the cause of Fire along with Air;

units.sanskrit: कथम् । आकाशो वै सूर्याचन्द्रमसावुभौ तेजोरूपौ विद्युन्नक्षत्राण्यग्निश्च तेजोरूपाण्याकाशे ऽन्तः ।
units.english: How so?In Ākāśa subsist the sun and the moon, both, which are forms of Fire,as also lightning, stars and fire, all in the form of fire, subsist in the Ākāśa;and when one thing subsists in another, the former is smaller and the latter greater

units.sanskrit: यच्च यस्यान्तर्वर्ति तदल्पं भूय इतरत् । किञ्चा'काशेना'ह्वयति चान्यमन्य आहूतश्चेतर आकाशेन शृणोत्यन्योक्तं च शब्दमन्यः
units.english: Further, it is through Ākāśa that one calls another person,and when the person thus called hears, it is through Ākāśa that he hearsthe words uttered by the other;and one hears back another, he does so only through Ākāśa;it is in Ākāśa that one rejoices,all men speak among themselves;

units.sanskrit: प्रतिशृणोत्याकाशे रमते क्रीडत्यन्योन्यं सर्वस्तथा न रमते चा'काशे वध्वादिवियोग आकाशे जायते न मूर्तेनावष्टब्धे । तथा'काशमभिलक्ष्याङ्कुरादि जायते न प्रतिलोमम् ।
units.english: it is in Ākāśa that one does not rejoice,one separates himself from his wife and others;it is in Ākāśa that everything is born,and not in anything already occupied by a solid form;similarly, it is Ākāśa towards which everything grows;upwards, not downwards

units.sanskrit: अत आकाशमुपाःस्व ॥
units.english: For these reasons meditate upon Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: स य आकाशं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । आकाशवतो वै स लोकान् प्रकाशवतो ऽसंबाधान् उरुगायवतो ऽभिसिध्यति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Ākāśa as Brahman attains extensive regions, full of light, free from pressure and spacious;

units.sanskrit: यावद् आकाशस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति य आकाशं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगव आकाशाद् भूय इति । आकाशद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति । तन् मे भगवान् ब्रवीत्व् इति ॥
units.english: and he is free to act as he wishes, in the sphere within reach of Ākāśa,one who meditates upon Ākāśa as Brahman’‘Revered sir, is there anything greater than Ākāśa ?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Ākāśa’‘Please explain that to me, Revered sir’

units.sanskrit: फलं शृण्वाकाशवतो वै विस्तारयुक्तान्स विद्वांल्लोकान्प्रकाशवतः । प्रकाशाकाशयोर्नित्यसंबन्धात्प्रकाशवतश्च लोकानसंबाधान्संबाधनं संबाधः
units.english: Listen to the reward;The wise men attain extensivelargeregions,full of light,on account of the permanent connection with Ākāśa and light,free from pressure‘Sambādha’ is overcrowding and consequent pressure upon one another, and spacious,admitting of free movement

units.sanskrit: यावदाकाशस्येत्याद्युक्तार्थम् ॥
units.english: In the sphere within reach of Ākāśa etc, etc,as explained already

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य द्वादशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: स्मरो वावाकाशाद् भूयः ।
units.english: ‘Memory is greater than Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: तस्माद् यद्य् अपि बहव आसीरन्न् अ स्मरन्तो नैव ते कंचन शृणुयुर् न मन्वीरन् न विजानीरन् ।
units.english: Therefore, even when there would be many persons,if they had no Memory,they could not hear any one, they could not think, they could not know;

units.sanskrit: यदा वाव ते स्मरेयुर् अथ शृणुयुर् अथ मन्वीरन्न् अथ विजानीरन् ।
units.english: if they had Memory, they could hear, they could think, they could know

units.sanskrit: स्मरेण वै पुत्रान् विजानाति स्मरेण पशून् । स्मरम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: It is by Memory that one knows his son, and it is by Memory that one knows his cattle,Meditate upon Memory’

units.sanskrit: स यः स्मरं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । यावत् स्मरस्य गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति यः स्मरं ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगवः स्मराद् भूय इति । स्मराद् वाव भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Memory as Brahman becomes free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of Memory’‘Revered sir, is there anything greater than Memory?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Memory’‘Please explain that to me, Revered sir’

units.sanskrit: स्मरो वावा'काकाशाद्भूयः । स्मरणं स्मरो ऽन्तःकरणधर्मः ।
units.english: ‘Smara’ stands for ‘smaraṇa’,the faculty of remembering, belonging to the internal organ

units.sanskrit: स आकाशाद्भूयानिति द्रष्टव्यं लिङ्गव्यत्ययेन स्मर्तुः स्मरणे हि सत्याकाशादि सर्वमर्थवत्स्मरणवतो भोग्यत्वात् ।
units.english: ‘bhūyaḥ’ neuter form being taken as standing for ‘bhūyān’, masculine form It is only when the man remembers things that all objects, Ākāśa and the rest,have their use; as it is only then that they can be objects of experience;

units.sanskrit: असति तु स्मरमे सदप्यसदेव ।
units.english: when one does not remember things, even what exists is as good as not existent;

units.sanskrit: सत्त्वकार्याभावात् ।
units.english: as it does not perform the functions of a really existing thing

units.sanskrit: नापि सत्त्वं स्मृत्यभावे शक्यमाकाशादीनामवगन्तुमित्यतः स्मरणस्या'काशाद्भृयस्त्वम् ।
units.english: Nor is it possible to apprehend the reality of Ākāśa and the other things, if there is no remembrance Thus, it is that Memory is greater than Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते हि लोके स्मरणस्य भूयस्त्वं यस्मात्तस्माद्यद्यपि समुदिता बहव एकस्मिन्नासीरन्नुपविशेयुस्ते तत्रा'सीना अन्योन्यभाषितमपि न स्मरन्तश्चेत्स्युर्नैव ते कञ्चन शब्दं शृणुयुस्तथा
units.english: Inasmuch as this greatness of Memory is realised in the world,even if many persons would be assembled and seated in any one place,if they happened to have no Memory,they could not hear any one of them speaking,similarly, they could not think, because of want of remembrance,and they could not know

units.sanskrit: यदा वाव ते स्मरेयुर्मन्तव्यं विज्ञातव्यं श्रोतव्यं चाथ शृणुयुरथ मन्वीरन्नथ विजानीरन् ।
units.english: If, on the other hand, they had Memory, they could hear what is to be heard, think of which is to be thought of and know what is to be known

units.sanskrit: तथा स्मरेण वै मम पुत्रा एत इति पुत्रान्विजानाति स्मरेण पशून् ।
units.english: It is by Memory that one knows his sons ‘These are my sons’;and it is by Memory that one knows his cattle

units.sanskrit: अतो भूयस्त्वात्स्मरमुपाःस्वेति ।
units.english: Hence, on account of its being greater than Ākāśa,meditate upon Memory

units.sanskrit: उक्तार्थमन्यत् ॥
units.english: The rest has been already explained

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य त्रयोदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: आशा वाव स्मराद् भूयसी ।
units.english: ‘Hope indeed is greater than Memory

units.sanskrit: आशेद्धो वै स्मरो मन्त्रान् अधीते कर्माणि कुरुते पुत्रांश् च पशूंश् चेच्छत इमं च लोकं अमुं चेच्छते ।
units.english: Fired by hope, Memory reads the Mantras, performs rites, desires sons, desires cattle, desires this world and also that world

units.sanskrit: आशाम् उपास्स्वेति ॥
units.english: Meditate upon Hope’

units.sanskrit: आशा वाव स्मराद्भूयसी । आशाप्राप्तवस्त्वाकाङ्क्षाऽशा तृष्णा काम इति यामाहुः पर्यायैः सा च स्मराद्भूयसी । कथम् ।
units.english: they speak of it by several synonyms, such as ‘Hope’, ‘Longing’, ‘Desire’;this is greater than Memory;in what way?It is when there is Hope in the mind that one remembers what he has to remember;

units.sanskrit: आशया । ह्यन्तःकरणस्थया स्मरति स्मर्तव्यम् ।
units.english: it is only when one remembers the object hoped for that he is to ‘remember things;

units.sanskrit: आशाविषयरूपं स्मरन्नसौ स्मरो भवत्यत आशेद्ध आशयाभिवर्धितः स्मरभूतः स्मरन्नृगादीन्मन्त्रानधीते ऽधीत्य च तदर्थं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विधींश्च श्रुत्वा कर्माणि कुरुते तत्फलाशयैव पुत्रांश्च कर्मफलभूतानिच्छते ऽभिवाञ्छत्याशयैव तत्साधनान्यनुतिष्ठति । इमं च लोकमाशेद्ध एव स्मरंल्लोकसंग्रहहेतुभिरिच्छते ।
units.english: hence, when one is fired by Hope, encouraged by Hopethat one remembers things and reads the MantrasṚk and the rest,and having read them, he learns their meaning from Brāhmaṇas, as also learning from them injunctions bearing upon the rites, he performs these rites,with a view to the results accruing from them,and desires sons and cattle,as results following from the rites;it is through Hope that he performs what are likely to accomplish those results,and he desires this worldin order to secureacquire things,and desires that other world only when he is fired by Hope, and then he performs what is likely to secure it

units.sanskrit: अमुं च लोकमाशेद्धः स्मरंस्तत्साधनानुष्ठानेनेच्छते ऽत आशारशानावबद्धं स्मराकाशादिनामपर्यन्तं जगच्चक्रीभूतं प्रतिप्राणि ।
units.english: Thus, it is found that for each livingbeing the whole world is ope cycle consisting of Memory, Āśā and other things ending with Name, all bed up by the rope of Hope

units.sanskrit: अत्र आश आयाः स्मरादपि भूयस्त्वमित्यत आशामुपाःस्व ॥
units.english: Hence, Hope is greater than Memory; and therefore, meditate upon Hope,

units.sanskrit: स य आशां ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । आशयास्य सर्वे कामाः समृध्यन्ति ।
units.english: ‘One who meditates upon Hope as Brahman, by Hope do all his wishes prosper, his prayers become infallible;

units.sanskrit: अमोघा हास्याशिषो भवन्ति । यावद् आशाया गतं तत्रास्य यथाकामचारो भवति य आशां ब्रह्मेत्य् उपास्ते । अस्ति भगव आशाया भूय इति । आशाया भूयो ऽस्तीति ।
units.english: and he is free to act as he wishes in the sphere within reach of Hope;one who meditates upon Hope as Brahman’‘Revered sir, is there anything greater than Hope?’‘Certainly, there is something greater than Hope’‘Explain that to me, Revered sir’

units.sanskrit: यस्त्वाशां ब्रह्मेत्युपास्ते शृणु तस्य फलम् । आशया सदोपासितयास्योपासकस्य सर्वे कामाः समृध्यन्ति समृद्धिं गच्छन्ति । अमोघा हास्याऽशिषः प्रार्थनाः सर्वा भवन्ति यत्प्रार्थितं सर्वं तदवश्यं भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: One who meditates upon Hope as Brahman,listen to the reward that accrues to himwhen Hope becomes constantly meditated upon, all the wishes of the meditators prosperattain fulfilment;his prayers become infallibleall his prayers become fruitful; that is, whatever he prays for, he surely gets

units.sanskrit: यावदाशाया गतमित्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥
units.english: Within reach of Hope etc, etc,as before

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य चतुर्दश खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: प्राणो वाव आशाया भूयान् ।
units.english: ‘Spirit is greater than Hope

units.sanskrit: यथा वा अरा नाभौ समर्पिता एवम् अस्मिन् प्राणे सर्वं समर्पितम् ।
units.english: Just as the spokes of the wheel are fastened to the nave, so is everything fastened to the Spirit

units.sanskrit: प्राणः प्राणेन याति ।
units.english: Spirit moves by Spirit;

units.sanskrit: प्राणः प्राणं ददाति ।
units.english: Spirit gives the Spirit,to the Spirit;

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ह पिता । प्राणो माता । प्राणो भ्राता ।
units.english: Spirit is the father, Spirit is the mother; Spirit is the brother; Spirit is the sister;

units.sanskrit: प्राण आचार्यः ।
units.english: spirit is the teacher;

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ब्राह्मणः ॥
units.english: Spirit is the Brāhmaṇa’

units.sanskrit: नामोपक्रममाशान्तं कार्यकारणत्वेन निमित्तनैमित्तिकत्वेन चोत्तरोत्तरभूयस्तयावस्थितं स्मृतिनिमित्तसद्भावमाशारशनापाशैर्विपाशितं सर्वं सर्वतो बिसमिव तन्तुभिर्यस्मिन्प्राणे समर्पितम् ।
units.english: Beginning with Name and ending with Hope, everything exists in the relation of constituent cause and product, or of efficient cause and effect, and in a gradually rising degree of greatness,its existence depending upon Memory, and tied up in the bonds of Hope; and all this is fastened on all sides, like lotusfibres, to the Spirit;

units.sanskrit: येन च सर्वतो व्यापिनान्तर्बहिर्गतेन सूत्रे मणिगणा इव सूत्रेण ग्रथितं विधृतं च । स एष प्राणो वा आशाया भूयान् ।
units.english: and it is in this Spiritwhich is allpervading, extending over the interior and exterior of thingsthat everything is hung up, like heads on a string, and held there;this Spirit is greater than Hope

units.sanskrit: कथमस्य भूयस्त्वमित्याह दृष्टान्तेन समर्थयंस्तद्भूयस्त्वम् ।
units.english: QuestionIn what way is it greater?

units.sanskrit: यथा वै लोके रथचक्रस्यारा रथनाभौ समर्पिताः संप्रोताः संप्रवेशिता इत्येतत् । एवमस्मिंल्लिङ्गसंघातरूपे प्राणे प्रज्ञात्मनि देहिके मुख्ये यस्मिन्परा देवता नामरूपव्याकरणाया'दर्शादौ प्रतिबिम्बिवज्जीवेना'त्मनानुप्रतिष्टा यश्च महाराजस्येव सर्वाधिकारीश्वरस्य ।
units.english: The answer is givçn, through an illustration, which supports the idea of the said greatness;just as, in the world the spokes of a chariotwheel are fastened to the nave,fixed to itie thrust into it,in the same manner is everything fastened to the Spirit;this Spirit is the Primary Prāṇa, the aggregate of individual entities, the conscious selfresident into the body, it is into this Spirit that the supreme Deity in the form of the ‘living self’entered, for the purpose of differentiating Names and Forms, just as the man in the form of his reflected image, enters the reflecting surface of the mirror;

units.sanskrit: कस्मिन्नन्न्वहमुत्क्रान्त उत्क्रान्तो बविष्यामि कस्मिन्वा प्रतिष्ठिते प्रतिष्ठास्यामीति स प्राणमसृजतैति श्रुतेः यस्तु च्छायेवानुगत ईश्वरम्
units.english: and it is the Chief Officer of God, like that of a great king, as declared in the Vedic text‘At whose departure shall depart, at whose resting shall rest’with this view he created PrāṇaSpirit’;

units.sanskrit: तद्यथा रथस्यारेषु नेमिरर्पितो नाभावरा अर्पिता एवमेवैता भूतमात्राः प्रज्ञामात्रास्वर्पिताः प्रज्ञामात्राः प्राणे ऽर्पिताः ।
units.english: and it follows God like His Shadow and just as the rim of the wheel is fixed to the spokes, and just as the spokes are fixed to the nave, so are all material substances fixed to the Spiritual Substances, and the Spiritual Substances are fixed to the Spirit;as declared by the Kauṣītakins Kauṣītakī

units.sanskrit: स एष प्राण एव प्रज्ञात्माइति कौषीतकिनाम् ।
units.english: ‘This Spirit is the Conscious Self’

units.sanskrit: अत एवमस्मिन्प्राणे सर्वं यथोक्तं समर्पितम् ।
units.english: It is to this Spirit that everything is fastened

units.sanskrit: अतः स एष प्राणो ऽपरतन्त्रः प्राणेन स्वशक्त्यैव याति नान्यकृतं गमनादिक्रियास्वस्य सामर्थ्यमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Thus, this Spirit is independent by itself, and hence, it is that Spirit moves by spirit,by its own energy;

units.sanskrit: सर्वं क्रियाकारकफलभेदजातं प्राण एव न प्राणाद्बहिर्भूतमस्तीति प्रकरणार्थः ।
units.english: and nothing else has anything to do with such actions of the Spirit as moving and the like;all things, consisting of diverse action, agencies, result, subsist in the Spirit itself;

units.sanskrit: प्राणः प्राणं ददाति यद्ददाति तत्स्वीत्मभूतमेव । यस्मै ददाति तदपि प्राणायैव ।
units.english: Such is the teaching of the whole section Spirit gives the Spirit,what it gives is its own self; and the recipient of the gift also is Spirit itself

units.sanskrit: अतः पित्राद्याख्यो ऽपि प्राण एव ॥
units.english: Hence, father and the rest also are Spirit itself

units.sanskrit: पितृहा वै त्वम् असि मातृहा वै त्वम् असि भ्रातृहा वै त्वम् असि स्वसृहा वै त्वम् अस्य् आचार्यहा वै त्वम् असि ब्राह्मणहा वै त्वम् असीति ॥
units.english: ‘If one says something harsh to his her fat, mother, brother, sister, teacher or a Brāhmaṇa,people say ‘Fie on thee! thou art a fatherkiller, thou art a motherkiller, thou art a brotherkiller, thou art a sisterkiller, thou art a teacherkiller, thou art a Brāhmaṇakiller’

units.sanskrit: कथं पित्रादिशब्दानां प्रसिद्धार्थोत्सर्गेण प्राणविषयत्वमिति ।
units.english: QuestionHow is it that the terms father’ and the rest have been made to surrender their wellknown connotations and are applied to the Spirit?

units.sanskrit: उच्यते सति प्राणे पित्रादिषु पित्रादिशब्दप्रयोगात्तदुत्क्रान्तौ च प्रयोगाभावात् ।
units.english: AnswerIt is only so long as the Spirit is there that the terms ‘father’ and the rest are applied to the particular persons, and they cease to be applied as soon as the Spirit has departed

units.sanskrit: कथं तदित्याह ।
units.english: QuestionWhy is it so?

units.sanskrit: स यः कश्चित्पित्रादीनामन्यतमं यदि तं भृशमिव तदननुरूपमिव किञ्चिद्वचनं त्वङ्कारादियुक्तं प्रत्याह तदैनं पार्श्वस्था आहुर्विवेकिनो धिक्त्वास्तु धिगस्तु त्वामित्येवम् । पितृहा वै त्वं पितुर्हन्तेत्यादि ॥ अथ यद्य् अप्य् एनान् उत्क्रान्तप्राणाञ् छूलेन समासं व्यतिषंदहेत् ।
units.english: AnswerIf one says something harsh,something improper, accompanied by such derogatory words ‘thou’ and the liketo any one of the persons mentioned, ‘father’ and other rest,then wise people standing by say to him ‘Fie on thee!Shame on thee!thou art a fatherkiller,slayer of your father’, etc, etc ‘On the other hand, if the Spirit has departed from them, even if one were to burn them together with a poker,they would not say‘thou art a fatherkiller’, nor ‘thou art a motherkiller’, nor ‘thou art a brotherkiller;

units.sanskrit: नैवैनं ब्रूयुः पितृहासीति न मातृहासीति न भ्रातृहासीति न स्वसृहासीति नाचार्यहासीति न ब्राह्मणहासीति ॥
units.english: nor ‘thou art a sisterkiller’, nor ‘thou art a teacherkiller’, nor ‘thou art a Brāhmaṇakiller’

units.sanskrit: अथैनानेवोत्क्रान्तप्राणांस्त्यक्तदेहानथ यद्यपि शूलेन समासं समस्य व्यतिदहेद्व्यत्यस्य संदहेदेवमप्यतिक्रूरं कर्म समासव्यत्यासादिप्रकारेण दहनलक्षणं तद्देहसंबद्धमेव कुर्वाणं नैवैनं ब्रूयुः पितृहेत्यादि ।
units.english: On the other hand, when the Spirit has departed from themthese same persons,when the Spirit has left their body,even if one were to burn them togetherand those again separately,even if they do such a cruel thing as the burning of the same bodies collectively and singly, turning them overwith a poker,they would not say to him ‘Thou art a fatherkiller’ etc, etc

units.sanskrit: तस्मादन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यामवगम्यत एतत्पित्राद्याख्यो ऽपि प्राण एवेति ॥
units.english: Thus, from the negative and affirmative premises stated above, it follows that the persons called ‘father’ and the rest are the Spirititself

units.sanskrit: प्राणो ह्य् एवैतानि सर्वाणि भवति ।
units.english: Verily, Spirit is all these

units.sanskrit: स वा एष एवं पश्यन्न् एवं मन्वान एवं विजानन्न् अतिवादी भवति ।
units.english: One who sees thus, thinks thus and knows thus becomes a hightalker

units.sanskrit: तं चेद् ब्रूयुर् अतिवाद्य् असीति । अतिवाद्य् अस्मीति ब्रूयात् ।
units.english: If some one were to say to him ‘you are a hightalker’, he should say ‘ am a hightalker’;

units.sanskrit: नापह्नुवीत ॥
units.english: he should not conceal the fact

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्प्राणो ह्येवैतानि पित्रादीनि सर्वाणि भवति चलानि स्थिराणि च ।
units.english: For these reasons, Spirit is all thesefather and the rest, all things, mobile and immobile

units.sanskrit: स वा एष प्राणविदेवं यथोक्तप्रकारेण पश्यन्फलतो ऽनुभवन्नेवं मन्वान उपपत्तिभिश्चिन्तयन्नेवं विजानन्नुपपत्तिभिः संयोज्यैवमेवेति निश्चयं कुर्वन्नित्यर्थः । मननविज्ञानाभ्यां हि संभूतः शास्रार्थो निश्चितो दृष्टो भवेत् ।
units.english: One who knows the Spirit as described, sees it thus,ie directly apprehends it to be thus in effect,who thinks thus,reflects over it with reasons,and who knows thus,having applied reasons to it, comes to this definite conclusion;as a matter of fact, it is by reflection and knowledge combined that the meaning of the scriptures becomes properly understood

units.sanskrit: अत एवं पश्यन्नतिवादी भवति नामाद्याशान्तमतीत्य वदनशीलो भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Hence, one who sees thus becomes a hightalker,ie becomes capable of talking of things beyond things beginning with Name and ending with Hope

units.sanskrit: तं चेद्ब्रूयुस्तं यद्येवमतिवादिनं सर्वदा सर्वैः शब्दैर्नामाद्याशान्तमतीत्य वर्तमानं प्राणमेवं वदन्तमेवं पश्यन्तमतिवदनशीलमतिवादिनं ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्तस्य हि जगतः प्राण आत्माहमिति ब्रुवाणं यदि ब्रूयुरतिवाद्यसीति ।
units.english: To such a person, who is a hightalker,ie who perceives that at all times and by all words people speak of Spirit only, as lying beyond all things beginning with Name and ending with Hope,and who is capable of this high ‘talking’who say ‘ am the Self, the Spirit, of the whole Universe, from Brahman down to the tuft of grass’,if some one were to say ‘you are a hightalker’,he should say Yes;

units.sanskrit: बाढमतिवाद्यस्मीति ब्रूयान्नापह्नुवीत ।
units.english: am a hightalker’, and he should not conceal the fact

units.sanskrit: कस्माद्ध्यसावपह्नुवीत । यत्प्राणं सर्वेश्वरमयमहमस्मीत्यात्मत्वेनोपगतः ॥
units.english: Why should he conceal it, when he has realised the Spirit as the Lord of all in his own Self as ‘ am this?’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य पञ्चदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: एष तु वा अतिवदति यः सत्येनातिवदति ।
units.english: ‘But in reality that person talks high who talks high by the True’

units.sanskrit: सत्यं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् इति । सत्यं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: ‘May , sir, talk high by the True’‘But the True itself has to be soughtto be known’ ‘Sir, do seek to know the True’

units.sanskrit: स एष नारदः सर्वातिशयं प्राणं स्वमात्मानं सर्वात्मानं श्रुत्वा नातः परमस्तीत्युपरराम । न पूर्ववत्किमस्ति भगवः प्राणाद्भूय इति पप्रच्छ । यतस्तमेवं विकारानृतब्रह्मविज्ञानेन परितुष्टमकृतार्थं परमार्थसत्यातिवादिनमात्मानं मन्यमानं योग्यं शिष्यं मिथ्याग्रहविशेषाद्विप्रच्यावयन्नाह
units.english: Nārada, having learnt that Spirit is the highest entity, and that it is his own self and also the self of all things, thought that there was nothing higher than Spirit and hence kept quiet, and did not put his usual question What is it, Revered sir, that is greater than Spirit? The Revered Sanatkumāra found that a capable Disciple has become satisfied with the knowledge of the modifiable hence false Brahman, and though not having his purpose fulfilled, yet he had come to regard himself as a ‘hightalker’ of the Absolutely True;

units.sanskrit: एष तु वा अतिवदति यमहं वक्ष्यामि न प्राणविदतिवादी परमार्थतः ।
units.english: hence, with a view to wearing him away from a wrong conviction, said‘But in reality, that person talks high of whom am going to speak, and one who knows that mere Spirit is not really a ‘hightalker;

units.sanskrit: नामाद्यपेक्षं तु तस्यातिवादित्वम् ।
units.english: he is a ‘hightalker’ only in regard to Name and the rest ending with Hope

units.sanskrit: यस्तु भूमाख्यं सर्वातिक्रान्तं तत्त्वं परमार्थसत्यं वेद सो ऽतिवादीत्यत आहएष तु वा अतिवदति यः सतेयन परमार्थसत्यविज्ञानवत्तयातिवदति
units.english: In reality, he alone is a ‘hightalker’ who knows what is called ‘the Infinite’, which is beyond all things, the True, the absolutely real This is what he says in the sentence ‘In reality that person talks high who talks high by the True;ie is possessed of the knowledge of the Absolutely True’

units.sanskrit: सो ऽहं त्वां प्रपन्नो भगवन्सत्येनातिवदानि तथामां नियुनक्तु भगवान्यथाहं सत्येनातिवदानीत्यभिप्रायः । यद्येवं सत्येनातिवदितुमिच्छसि सत्यमेव तु तावद्विजिज्ञासितव्यमित्युक्त आह नारदः । तथास्तु तर्हि सत्य भगवो विजिज्ञासे विशेषेण ज्ञातुमिच्छेयं त्वत्तो ऽहमिति ॥
units.english: ‘Know that have come to seek refuge under you, sir, may talk high by the True?’ Please direct me so that may talk high by the true,such was the sense of what Nārada said ‘If really you wish to talk high by the True, the True itself has to be sought to be known first’Being thus addressed, Nārada said‘Beit so then, sir, do seek to know the True, am anxious to learn it from you in detail’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य षोडशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यदा वै विजानात्य् अथ सत्यं वदति ।
units.english: ‘When one understands the True, then alone does he declare the True;

units.sanskrit: नाविजानन् सत्यं वदति ।
units.english: without understanding the True, one does not declare the True;

units.sanskrit: विजानन्न् एव सत्यं वदति ।
units.english: it is only when one understands the True that he declares the True

units.sanskrit: विज्ञानं त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् इति । विज्ञानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: But this understanding itself one must seek to understand’ ‘Revered sir, seek to understand this understanding’

units.sanskrit: यदा वै सत्यं परमार्थतो विजानातीदं परमार्थः सत्यमिति, ततो ऽनृतं विकारजातं वाचारम्भणं हित्वा सर्वविकारावस्थं सदेवैकं सत्यमिति तदेवाथ वदति यद्वदति ।
units.english: When one really understands the True,as ‘this is what is really and absolutely True’,then he renounces all that is false, unreal, in the shape of all products, which are the products of mere words,and comes to realise that Being, alone, which pervades over all products, is True;when he declares it

units.sanskrit: ननु विकारो ऽपि सत्यमेव ।
units.english: The product also is real;

units.sanskrit: नामरूपे सत्यं ताभ्य मयं प्राणश्छन्नः ।
units.english: because Name and Form are real and Spirit is covered by Name and Form;

units.sanskrit: प्राणा वै सत्यं तेषामेष सत्यमिति श्रुत्यन्तरात् ।
units.english: as says another Vedic text‘Spirits are True, and of these this is the Truest’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: सत्यमुक्तं सत्यत्वं श्रुत्यन्तरे विकारस्य न तु परमार्थापेक्षमुक्तं किं तर्हीन्द्रियविषयत्वापेक्षं
units.english: True; the other text has declared the product to be real; but it was not meant to be absolute reality, what was said was only relatively to the objects of sensation

units.sanskrit: सच्च त्यच्चेति सत्यमित्युक्तं तद्द्वारेण च परमार्थसत्यस्योपलब्धिर्विवक्षितेति । प्राणा वै सत्यं तेषामेष सत्यमिति चोक्तम् ।
units.english: and thus, on the basis of this comparative or relative reality, the five substances have been called ‘satya’, RealĀnandagiri] and it is on the basis of this relative reality that the substances have been spoken of as ‘True’, and what was meant was that it was through this relative reality that the kruwledge of absolute reality is obtained

units.sanskrit: इहापि तदिष्टमेव ।
units.english: And this sort’, of relative reality we accept in the present case also for all products

units.sanskrit: इह तु प्रणविषयात्परमार्थसत्यविज्ञानाभिमानाद्व्युत्थाप्य नारदं यत्सदेव सत्यं परमार्थतो भूमाख्यं तद्विज्ञापयिष्यामीत्येष विशेषतो
units.english: In the present context, however, what is meant to be expounded specifically to Nāradaas promised in the words ‘that am going to expound’is that which is Pure Being, absolutely real, known by the name of ‘the Infinite’after having weared him from raised him above from the false notion that by knowing the Spirit he has obtained the knowledge of what is absolutely real

units.sanskrit: नाविजानन्सत्यं वदति यस्त्वविजानन्वदति सो ऽग्न्यादिशब्देनाग्न्यदीन्परमार्थसद्रूपान्मन्यमानो वदति न तु ते रूपत्रयव्यतिरेकेण परमार्थः
units.english: Without understanding the True, one does not declare the True;if one speaks of the True without understanding it, he speaks, by means of the words ‘Fire’ and the rest, of Fire and other things Fire, Water and Earth, regarding these latter as absolutely real; as a matter of fact, however, these things have no reality beyond their forms;

units.sanskrit: तथा तान्यपि रूपाणि सदपेक्षया नैव सन्तीत्यतो नाविजानन्सत्यं वदति ।
units.english: and these forms also have no real existence, as compared to Pure Being; thus it is that without understanding the True one does not declare the True;

units.sanskrit: विजानन्नेव सत्यं वदति ।
units.english: and it is only when one understands the True that he declares the True;

units.sanskrit: न च तत्सत्यविज्ञानमविजिज्ञासितमप्रार्थितं ज्ञायत इत्याहविज्ञानं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति । यद्येवं विज्ञानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति । एवं सत्यादीनां चोत्तरोत्तराणां करोत्यन्तानां पूर्वपूर्वहेतुत्वं व्याख्येयम् ॥
units.english: and as regards the understanding of the True, it cannot be acquired unlessit is sought after and prayed for; hence he says‘this understanding itself, one must seek to understand’‘If that is so, then, Revered sir, seek to understand this understanding’In this way, in the series beginning with the True, and ending with Action spoken of in section xxi below, the preceding one should be explained as being the cause of the next following one

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य सप्तदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यदा वै मनुते ऽथ विजानाति ।
units.english: ‘When one reflects, then he understands;

units.sanskrit: नामत्वा विजानाति ।
units.english: without reflecting, one does not understand;

units.sanskrit: मत्वैव विजानाति ।
units.english: one understands only when he has reflected

units.sanskrit: मतिस् त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्येति । मतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: But reflection itself should be sought to be known’‘ seek, Revered sir, to understand Reflection’

units.sanskrit: यदा वै मनुत इति । मतिर्मननं तर्को मन्तव्यविषय आदरः ॥
units.english: When one reflects etc, etc,‘mati’, ‘reflection’, stands for pondering, reasoning and paying attention to the subject of reflection

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्याष्टदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यदा वै श्रद्दधात्य् अथ मनुते ।
units.english: ‘When one has Faith, then he reflects;

units.sanskrit: नाश्रद्दधन् मनुते ।
units.english: without Faith, one does not reflect;

units.sanskrit: श्रद्दधद् एव मनुते ।
units.english: one reflects only when he has Faith

units.sanskrit: श्रद्धा त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्येति । श्रद्धां भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥ आस्तिक्यबुद्धिः श्रद्धा ॥
units.english: But one should seek to understand Faith itself’‘ wish, Revered sir, to understand Faith’ Faith is the idea that thing in question really exists

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्यैकोनविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यदा वै निस्तिष्ठत्य् अथ श्रद्दधाति ।
units.english: ‘When one serves, then one has Faith;

units.sanskrit: नानिस्तिष्ठञ् छ्रद्दधाति ।
units.english: without serving, one has no Faith;

units.sanskrit: निस्तिष्ठन्न् एव श्रद्दधाति ।
units.english: it is only when one serves that he has Faith

units.sanskrit: निष्ठा त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्येति । निष्ठां भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: But service itself should be sought to be understood’‘ wish, Revered sir, to understand Service’

units.sanskrit: निष्ठा गुरुशुश्रूषादिस्तत्परत्वं ब्रह्मविज्ञानाय ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य विंशः खण्डः
units.english: ‘Niṣṭhā’, ‘Service’, stands for attending upon the teacher, and being devoted to him for the purpose of attaining knowledge of Brahman End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यदा वै करोत्य् अथ निस्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: ‘When one acts, then alone does he serve;

units.sanskrit: नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: without acting, one does not serve;

units.sanskrit: कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: only on acting does one serve

units.sanskrit: कृतिस् त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्येति । कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: But Action itself should be sought to be understood’‘ wish, Revered sir, to understand Action’

units.sanskrit: यदा वै करोति । कृतिरिन्द्रियसंयमश्चित्तैकाग्रताकरणं च ।
units.english: ‘Kṛti’, ‘action’, here stands for the controlling of the senses and concentrating of the mind

units.sanskrit: सत्यां हि तस्यां निष्ठादीनि यथोक्तानि भवन्ति विज्ञानावसानानि ॥
units.english: It is only when this Action is present that service and the rest, as described above, become accomplished, ending with true understanding

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्यैकविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यदा वै सुखं लभते ऽथ करोति ।
units.english: ‘When one attains Bliss, then he acts;

units.sanskrit: नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति ।
units.english: without attaining Bliss, he does not act;

units.sanskrit: सुखम् एव लब्ध्वा करोति ।
units.english: only on attaining Bliss, does one act

units.sanskrit: सुखं त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् इति । सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: But Bliss itself should be sought to be understood’‘Revered sir, wish to understand Bliss’

units.sanskrit: सापि कृतिर्यदा सुखं लभते सुखं निरतिशयं वक्ष्यमाणं लब्धव्यं मयेति मन्यते तदा भवतीत्यर्थः । यथा दृष्टफलसुखा कृतिस्तथेहापि नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति । भविष्यदपि फलं लब्ध्वेत्युच्यते ।
units.english: The said Acting also comes about only when one attains Bliss; that is, when he makes up his mind to the effect that ‘the Highest Bliss, going to be described, has to be attained by me’;just as, in the case of actions which are actually found to result in Bliss happiness, so, in the case in question also, without attaining Bliss, one does not act;though it is the future result that is meant here by the attaining Bliss, yet it is spoken of as in the past, by the pastparticiple ‘having attained’;as it is only the future resultsought to be secured by the proposed activity,with a view to which the said action is taken up

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीं कृत्यादिषूत्तरोत्तरेषु सत्सु सत्यं स्वयमेव प्रतिभासत इति न तद्विज्ञानाय पृथग्यत्नः कार्य इति प्राप्तं तत इदमुच्यते ।
