units.english: At this stage, some people may have the notion that when the items beginning with Action are accomplished, the True becomes manifested by itself; so that no separate effect need be put forth for understanding it

units.sanskrit: सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमित्यादि । सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इत्यभिमुखीभूताया'ह ॥
units.english: In anticipation of such a notion, it has been added‘Bliss itself should be sought to be understood etc’‘Revered sir, wish to understand Bliss’

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य द्वाविंशः खण्डः
units.english: When Nārada had thus become duly attentive, Sanatkumāra said to him as follows in the next Section End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा तत् सुखम् ।
units.english: ‘That which is Infinite is Bliss;

units.sanskrit: नाल्पे सुखम् अस्ति ।
units.english: there is no Bliss in what is finite;

units.sanskrit: भूमैव सुखम् ।
units.english: the Infinite alone is Bliss

units.sanskrit: भूमा त्व् एव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति । भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
units.english: But the Infinite itself should be sought to be understood’‘Revered sir, wish to understand the Infinite’

units.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा महन्निरतिशयं बह्विति पर्यायास्तत्सुखम् ।
units.english: That which is Infinite,large, unexcelled highest, Muchall these are synonyms;and this is Bliss;what is less than the Infinite is excelled by this letter;

units.sanskrit: ततोर्ऽवाक्सातिशयत्वादल्पम् ।
units.english: hence, it is called ‘finite’ small;

units.sanskrit: अतस्तस्मिन्नल्पे सुखं नास्ति ।
units.english: hence, in what is finite there is no Bliss;

units.sanskrit: अल्पस्याधिकतृष्णाहेतुत्वात् ।
units.english: because the finite or the small always gives rise to longing for what is more than that;

units.sanskrit: तृष्णा च दुःखबीजं ।
units.english: and all longing is a source of pain;

units.sanskrit: न हि दुःखबीजं सुखं दृष्टं ज्वरादि लोके ।
units.english: and in the world it has been found that what is a source of pain,such as, fever and other diseases,is not Bliss

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्युक्तं नाल्पे सुखमस्तीति ।
units.english: Hence, it is quite correct to say that there is no Bliss in what is finite;

units.sanskrit: अतो भूमैव सुखम् । तृष्णादिदुःखबीजत्वासंभवाद्भूम्नः ॥
units.english: hence, the Infinite alone is Bliss, specially because in the Infinite, there is no possibility of any sources of pain like longing and the rest

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य त्रयोविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: यत्र नान्यत् पश्यति नान्यच् छृणोति नान्यद् विजानाति स भूमा ।
units.english: ‘Wherein one sees nothing else, hears nothing else and understands nothing else,that is the Infinite;

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्रान्यत् पश्यत्य् अन्यच् छृणोत्य् अन्यद् विजानाति तद् अल्पम् ।
units.english: wherein one sees something else, hears something else, and understands smething else,that is Finite

units.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा तद् अमृतम् ।
units.english: That which is Infinite is immortal;

units.sanskrit: स भगवः कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठित इति । स्वे महिम्नि यदि वा न महिम्नीति ॥
units.english: that which is Finite is mortal’ ‘Revered sir, wherein does that rest?’‘In Its own majesty, or not in majesty’

units.sanskrit: किंलक्षणो ऽसौ भूमेत्याहयत्र यस्मिन्भूम्नि तत्त्वे नान्यद्द्रष्टव्यमन्येन करणेन द्रष्टान्यो विभक्तो दृश्यात्पश्यति । तथा नान्यच्छृणोति । नामरूपयोरेवान्तर्भावाद्विषयभेदस्य तद्ग्राहकयोरेवेह दर्शनश्रवणयोर्ग्रहणमन्येषां चोपलक्षणार्थत्वेन ।
units.english: He explains what the distinguishing character of the Infinite isWherein,in which Infinite, as an entity, the seer does not see anything elsewhich is to be seen by means of other sense organs, as distinct from the seer himself;similarly one hears nothing else;inasmuch as Name and Form alone are meant to be included here, the text mentions only the apprehensions of those alonein the shape of seeing and hearing;

units.sanskrit: मननं चात्रोक्तं द्रष्टव्यं नान्यन्मनुत इति । प्रायशो मननपूर्वकत्वाद्विज्ञानस्य । तथा नान्यद्विजानाति ।
units.english: and the others being mentioned as merely illustratives;but reflection should be understood to be included here by some such expression as ‘when one reflects upon nothing else’ as understanding is almost invariably preceded by reflection;similarly, when one understands nothing else

units.sanskrit: एवंलक्षणो यः स भूमा ।
units.english: That which has this character is the Infinite

units.sanskrit: किमत्र प्रसिद्रान्यदर्शनाभावो भूम्न्युच्यते नान्यत्पश्यतीत्यादिना, अथान्यन्न पश्यत्यात्मानं पश्यतीत्येतत् ।
units.english: ObjectionIs it the absence of the seeing of other wellknown things that is denied in reference to the Infinite, by the expressions ‘one sees nothing else’ and the rest? Or is it meant that ‘he sees himself, nothing else’? That is, does the sentence mean merely the denial of the seeing of other wellknown things? Or the affirmative of the man seeing himself, and nothing else?

units.sanskrit: किञ्चातः ।
units.english: What difference would that make?

units.sanskrit: यद्यन्यदर्शनाद्यभावमात्रमित्युच्यते तदा द्वैतसंव्यवहारविलक्षणो भूमेत्युक्तं भवति ।
units.english: If what is asserted is only the absence of the seeing of other things, then the sense comes to be that the Infinite is something entirely different in character from all notions involving Duality

units.sanskrit: अथान्यद्रशनविशेषप्रतिषेधेना'त्मानं पश्यतीत्युच्यते तदैकस्मिन्नेव क्रियाकारकफलभेदो ऽभ्युपगतो भवेत् ।
units.english: If, on the other hand, what is meant by the denial of the seeing of other is that One sees himself, then it would mean the admission of the distinction between action seeing, acting agent seer and the result perception

units.sanskrit: यद्येवं को दोषः स्यात् ।
units.english: What would be the harm, if this were so admitted?

units.sanskrit: नन्वयमेव दोषः संसारानिवृत्तिः ।
units.english: The harm would be that there would be? no cessation of the Cycle of Births and Deaths;

units.sanskrit: क्रियाकारकफलभेदो हि संसार इति ।
units.english: as this Cycle consists in the said distinction between Action, Actor and its Result

units.sanskrit: आत्मैकत्व एव क्रियाकारकफलभेदः संसारविलक्षण इति चेत् । न ।
units.english: But under the Doctrine of the Unity of the Self, the distinction between Action, Actor and Result is entirely different in character from that involved in the Cycle of Births and Deaths Not so;

units.sanskrit: आत्मनो निर्विशेषैकत्वाभ्युपगमे दर्शनादिक्रियाकारकफलभेदाभ्युपगमस्य शब्दमात्रत्वात् ।
units.english: if the Unity of the Self is held to be free from all distinction and diversity, the idea of the distinction between the Action of seeing etc, the Actor and the Result is merely verbal

units.sanskrit: अन्यदर्शनाद्यभावोक्तिपक्षे ऽपि यत्रेत्यन्यन्न पश्यतीति च विशेषणे अनर्थके स्यातामिति चेत् ।
units.english: Even under the view that what is meant is the negation of the seeing of anything else,the very distinctions involved in the terms ‘wherein’ and ‘sees nothing else’ would be meaningless

units.sanskrit: दृश्यते हि लोके यत्र शून्ये गृहे ऽन्यन्न पश्यतीत्युक्ते स्तम्भादीनात्मानं च न न पश्यतीति गम्यते ।
units.english: In the ordinary world, it is found that in an empty room, when it is said that one sees no one else,’ it is not meant that the man’s own self, or the pillars and other things are not seen it means only that no other person is seen

units.sanskrit: एवमिहापीति चेत् । न ।
units.english: So would it be in the case in question also Not so;

units.sanskrit: तत्त्वमसीत्येकत्वोपदेशादधिकरणाधिकर्तव्यभेदानुपपत्तेः । तथा सदेकमेवाद्वितीयं सत्यमिति षष्ठे निर्धारितत्वात् ।
units.english: Further, under Discourse , it has been established that Being alone is ‘True, one, without a second’;and in accordance with the following texts, the perception of self by itself is not possiblea ‘Invisible,not self etc’ Taitti Upa

units.sanskrit: अदृश्ये ऽनात्म्येन संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्यविज्ञातारमरे केन विजानीयातित्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः स्वात्मनि दर्शनाद्यनुपपत्तिः ।
units.english: b ‘Its form is not within the range of vision’ Katha c ‘By what could one know the knower?’ Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: यत्रेति विशेषणमनर्थकं प्राप्तमिति चेत् । न ।
units.english: iv In that case, the qualifying term ‘wherein’ becomes meaningless No;

units.sanskrit: अविद्याकृतभेदापेक्षत्वात् ।
units.english: it is in reference to distinctions based upon Nescience ignorance

units.sanskrit: यथा सत्येकत्वाद्वितीयत्वबुद्धिं प्रकृतामपेक्ष्य सदेकमेवाद्वितीयमिति संख्याद्यनर्हमप्युच्यते ।
units.english: In the text ‘Being, one, without a second’, is found that though Being is really incapable of numerical qualification as expressed by the term ‘one’, yet it is spoken of in that way in reference to these notions of ‘truth’, ‘unity’ and ‘secondless’ as have been dealt with in the context in which the said text Being, one, secondless occurs

units.sanskrit: एवं भूम्न्येकस्मिन्नेव यत्रेति विशेषणम् ।
units.english: In the same manner, though the Infinite is one only, yet the qualification of ‘wherein’ has been applied to it in reference to what is spoken of in the context

units.sanskrit: अविद्यावस्थायामन्यदर्शनानुवादेन च भूम्नस्तदभावत्वलक्षणस्य विवक्षितत्वान्नान्यत्पश्यतीति विशेषणम् ।
units.english: Further, when the text applies to the Infinite the qualification involved in the phrase sees nothing else’ which implies distinction, what it does is to make a reference to the seeing of otherś during the normal state of ignorance, and then to deny that seeing of others in regard to the Infinite

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्संसारव्यवहारो भूम्नि नास्तीति समुदायार्थः ।
units.english: Thus, the upshot of the whole context is that the process of births and deaths is not applicable to the Infinite which is beyond the reach of that process

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्राविद्याविषये ऽन्यो ऽन्येनान्यत्पश्यतीति तदल्पमविद्याकालभावीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: On the other hand, when, in the sphere of ignorance Nescience, one sees something else, through something else, that is Finite; that is, exists only so long as the ignorance lasts;

units.sanskrit: यथा स्वप्नदृश्यं वस्तु प्राक् प्रबोधात्तत्कालभावीति तद्वत् ।
units.english: just as things perceived during a dream lasts only till waking, only so long as the dream lasts

units.sanskrit: तत एव तन्मर्त्यं विनाशि स्वप्नवस्तुवदेव तद्विपरोतो भूमा यस्तदमृतम् । तच्छब्दो ऽमृतत्वपरः । स तर्ह्येवंलक्षणो भूमा हे भगवन्कस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठित इत्युक्तवन्तं नारदं प्रत्याह सनत्किमारः ।
units.english: For that same reason, it is mortal,perishable,like the thing perceived in a dream Contrary to all this is the Infinite, which is immortal;the pronoun ‘tat’ refers to ‘amṛta’ Hence, in the Neuter form Therefore, Nārada saidThis Infinite that you have describedO, Revered sir, wherein does that rest?

units.sanskrit: स्वे महिम्नीति स्व आत्मीये महिम्नि माहात्म्ये विभूतौ प्रतिष्ठितो भूमा ।
units.english: Sanatkumāra answeredIn Its own majesty,ie the Infinite rests in its own majesty, greatness, splendour

units.sanskrit: यदि प्रतिष्ठामिच्छसि क्वचिद्यदि वा परमार्थमेव पृच्छसि न महिम्न्यपि प्रतिष्ठित इति ब्रूमः । अप्रतिष्ठितो ऽनाश्रितो भूमा क्वचिदपीत्यर्थः ॥
units.english: This is the answer for you if you wish to know the resting place of the Infinite in some cases to satisfy your intellectual curiosity; if however you wish to know the real truth, then the answer is that the Infinite does not rest ever upon Majesty;it is without a restingplace, without a substratum, anywhere at all

units.sanskrit: गो ऽश्वम् इह महिमेत्य् आचक्षते हस्तिहिरण्यं दासभार्यं क्षेत्राण्य् आयतनानीति ।
units.english: ‘In the world, what they call Majesty is cows and horses, elephants and gold, slaves and wives, lands and houses

units.sanskrit: नाहम् एवं ब्रवीमि । ब्रवीमीति होवाच । अन्यो ह्य् अन्यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठित इति ॥
units.english: do not say this, he said‘as in that case, one thing would rest upon another What do say is this what follows

units.sanskrit: यदि स्वमहिम्नि प्रतिष्ठितो भूमा कथं तर्ह्यप्रतिष्ठ उच्यते ।
units.english: QuestionIf the Infinite rests upon Its own Majesty, then why is it said that ‘It does not rest upon anything’?

units.sanskrit: शृणु ।
units.english: AnswerListen

units.sanskrit: गो ऽश्वादीह महिमेत्याचक्षते । गावश्चाश्वाश्च गो ऽश्वं द्वन्द्वैकवद्भावः । सर्वत्र गवाश्वादि महिमेति प्रसिद्धं तदाश्रितस्तत्प्रतिष्ठश्चैत्रो भवति,
units.english: In this world, what they call Majesty, is cows, horses and the restthe compound in ‘goaśvam’ is made up of ‘Gāvaḥ’ and ‘aśvaḥ’, and it is copulative and hence, in the singular number It is wellknown everywhere that things like cows and horses make up Majesty greatness;

units.sanskrit: यथा नाहमेवं स्वतो ऽन्यं महिमानमाश्रितो भूमा चैत्रवदिति ब्रवीम्यत्र हेतुत्वेनान्यो ह्यन्यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठित इति व्यवहितेन सम्बन्धः ।
units.english: But do not say this it is not my opinion that the Infinite rests on anything other than Itself, like Caitra; and the reason given for thisis as in that case one thing would rest upon another this has to be connected into the present sentence

units.sanskrit: किन्त्वेवं ब्रवीमीति होवाचस एवेत्यादि ॥
units.english: What do say is this Sa eva etc, etc following text

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य चतुर्विंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: स एवाधस्तात् स उपरिष्टात् स पश्चात् स पुरस्तात् स दक्षिणतः स उत्तरतः ।
units.english: That itself is below, That above, That behind, That before, That to the right, That to the left

units.sanskrit: स एवेदं सर्वम् इति ।
units.english: That itself is all this

units.sanskrit: अथातो ऽहंकारादेश एव । अहम् एवाधस्ताद् अहम् उपरिष्टाद् अहं पश्चाद् अहं पुरस्ताद् अहं दक्षिणतो ऽहम् उत्तरतो ऽहम् एवेदं सर्वम् इति ॥
units.english: Next follows the teaching through the notion of ‘’‘’ itself is below, above, behind, before, to the right, to the left; the ‘’ is all this

units.sanskrit: कस्मात्पुनः क्वचिन्न प्रतिष्ठित इत्युच्यते ।
units.english: It is explained why the Infinite is not based upon anything

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्स एव भूमाधस्तान्न तद्व्यतिरेकेणान्यद्विद्यते यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठितः स्यात् ।
units.english: Because it is the Infinite Itself which is below,and there is nothing else apart from It, which is below it,upon which It would rest

units.sanskrit: तथोपरिष्टादित्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: Similarly, It is above etc, etc,as above

units.sanskrit: सति भूम्नो ऽन्यस्मिन्भूमा हि प्रतिष्ठितः स्यान्न तु तदस्ति ।
units.english: If there existed something apart from the Infinite, then alone could the Infinite rest upon something else;as a matter of fact, however, there is nothing apart from the Infinite;

units.sanskrit: स एव तु सर्वम् ।
units.english: the Infinite Itself is all;

units.sanskrit: अतस्तस्मादसौ न क्वचित्प्रतिष्ठितः ।
units.english: hence, it follows that the Infinite does not rest upon anything

units.sanskrit: यत्र नान्यत्पश्यतीत्यधिकरणाधिकर्तव्यतानिर्देशात्स एवाधस्तादिति च परोक्षनिर्देशाद्द्रष्टर्जीवादन्योभूमा स्यादित्याशङ्का कस्यचिन्मा भूदित्यथातो ऽनन्तरमहङ्कारादेशो ऽहङ्कारेणा'दिश्यत इत्यहङ्कारादेशः ।
units.english: In view of the assertion wherein one seeśnothing else,which implies the idea of container and contained; and the present assertion ‘That is below’,which appears to refer to something not before the eyes of the speaker, and is something different,it would give rise to the idea in some one’s mind that the Infinite is something different from the perceiving the Living Self;

units.sanskrit: द्रष्टुरनन्यत्वदर्शनार्थं भूमैव निर्दिश्यते ऽहङ्कारेणाहमेवाधस्तादित्यादिना ॥
units.english: which shows that the Infinite is nondifferent from the Perceiver; and it Cis the Infinite Itself which is spoken of as ‘’ being below etc, etc

units.sanskrit: अथात आत्मादेश एव ।
units.english: Now follows the teaching through Self

units.sanskrit: आत्मैवाधस्ताद् आत्मोपरिष्टाद् आत्मा पश्चाद् आत्मा पुरस्ताद् आत्मा दक्षिणत आत्मोत्तरत आत्मैवेदं सर्वम् इति ।
units.english: The Self itself is below, the Self above, the Self behind, the Self before, the Self to the right, the Self to the left the Self is all this

units.sanskrit: स वा एष एवं पश्यन्न् एवं मन्वान एवं विजानन्न् आत्मरतिर् आत्मक्रीड आत्ममिथुन आत्मानन्दः स स्वराड् भवति । तस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु कामचारो भवति ।
units.english: One who sees thus, reflects thus and understands thus, loves the Self, revels with the Self, enjoys the company of the Self, and rejoices in the Self, he becomes the ‘Selfsovereign’ or King of Heaven he becomes free to do what he pleases, in all regions;

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽन्यथातो विदुर् अन्यराजानस् ते क्षय्यलोका भवन्ति । तेषां सर्वेषु लोकेष्व् अकामचारो भवति ॥
units.english: while those that know otherwise than this are ruled by others, and live in perishable regions, and they are not free to do what they please, in all regions

units.sanskrit: अहङ्कारेण देहादिसंघातो ऽप्यादिश्यते ऽविवेकिभिरित्यतस्तदाशङ्का मा भूदित्यथानन्तरमात्मादेश आत्मनैव केवलेन सत्स्वरूपेण
units.english: in order to set aside this notion that the notion of ‘’ through which the Infinite has been explained refers to the body,now follows the teaching through Self which is really what the notion of ‘’ stands for;

units.sanskrit: शुद्धेना'दिश्यते ।
units.english: that is, the Infinite is now going to be described through the Self Itself, in the form of Pure Being

units.sanskrit: आत्मैव सर्वतः सर्वमित्येवमेकमजं सर्वतो व्योमवत्पूर्णमन्यशून्यं पश्यन्स वा एष विद्वान्मननविज्ञानाभ्यामात्मरतिरात्मन्येव रती रमणं यस्य सो ऽयमात्मरतिः । तथा'त्मक्रीडः ।
units.english: ‘It is Self Itself that is all everywhere’ the wise man who sees this One, unborn, allpervading, like Ākāśa, full, without a second,and having seen It, reflects upon It and understands It,he comes to love Self;ie has all his love, affection, joy, centered in the Self,so also he revels with the Self;

units.sanskrit: देहमात्रसाधना रतिर्बाह्यसाधना क्रीडा ।
units.english: ‘love’ ‘rati’ stands for what is carried on which the body alone, while ‘Real’ krīḍā, stands for what is carried on through external means entirely;

units.sanskrit: लोके स्रीभिः सखिभिश्च क्रीडतीति दर्शनात् न तथा विदुषः किं तर्ह्यात्मविज्ञाननिमित्तमेवोभयं भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: as is clear from the use of the root ‘krīḍā’ to ‘revel which is used in the world in connection with one’s wives and friends;it is not so for the wise man; for him both these ‘love’ and ‘revelling’ are brought about by his knowledge of the Self

units.sanskrit: मिथुनं द्वंन्द्वजनितं सुखं तदपि द्वन्द्वनिरपेक्षं यस्य विदुषः ।
units.english: The enjoyment of companyis pleasure due to the companionship of two persons,this also for the wise, is independent of duality the second person

units.sanskrit: तथा'त्मानन्दः शब्दादिनिमित्त आनन्दो ऽविदुषां न तथास्य विदुषः किं तर्ह्यात्मनिमित्तमेव सर्वं सर्वदा सर्वप्रकारेण च देहजीवितभोगादिनिमित्तबाह्यवस्तुनिरपेक्ष
units.english: for the Ignorant, there rejoicing due to sound and other objects, not so for the wise, for whom, all rejoicing, at all times and in all ways is due to the Self alone,it is not due to such agencies as the body, the physicallife and experiences, and is entirely independent of all external things

units.sanskrit: इत्यर्थः । स एवंलक्षणो विद्वाञ्जीवन्नेव स्वाराज्ये ऽभिषिक्तः पतिते ऽपि देहे स्वराडेव भवति ।
units.english: The knowing man who is as described becomes the SelfSovereign even while he is still alive, and also when his body dies, he becomes the SelfSovereign or King of Heaven

units.sanskrit: यत एवं भवति तत एव तस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु कामचारो भवति ।
units.english: And inasmuch as he becomes all this, he becomes free to do as he pleases, in all regions

units.sanskrit: प्राणादिषु पूर्वभूमिषु तत्रास्येति तावन्मात्रपरिच्छिन्नकामचारत्वमुक्तमन्राजत्वं चार्थप्राप्तं सातिशयत्वाद्यथाप्राप्तस्वाराज्यकामचारत्वानुवादेन ततन्निवृत्तिरिहोच्यते स स्वराडित्यादिना ।
units.english: The ‘freedom to act as he pleases’ that has been spoken of, in connection with the ‘Spirit’ and other stages,has been with reference to the restricted spheres specially mentioned therein; and the fact being subject to the rule of others was a logical implication, from the fact that there were still higher degrees of freedom etc,while what is done in the present context is that reference is made to the freedom of action and selfsovereignty as suggested by the circumstances of the case and then the cessation of those restricted grades of freedom etc, is stressed, by means of such expressions as ‘he becomes the SelfSovereign’

units.sanskrit: अथ पुनर्ये ऽन्यथात उक्तदर्शनादन्यथा वैपरीत्येन यथोक्तमेव वा सम्यङ्न विदुस्ते ऽन्यराजानो भवन्ति अन्यः परो राजा स्वामी येषां ते ऽन्यराजानस्ते ।
units.english: While those that know otherwise than this,ie who entertain notions contrary to the one herein declared,or who have not rightly understood the view herein propounded,are ruled by others,ie one such as have other persons for their ruler, and also live in perishable regions;

units.sanskrit: भेददर्शनस्याल्पविषयत्वादल्पं च तन्मर्त्यमित्यवोचाम । तस्माद्ये द्वैतदर्शिनस्ते क्षय्यलोकाः स्वदर्शनानुरूप्येणैव भवन्त्यत एव तेषां सर्वेषु लोकेष्वकामचारो भवति ॥
units.english: we have already explained that notions of diversity appertain to the Finite, and the Finite is ‘mortal \ Hence, it follows that those who hold to the idea of duality diversity live in perishable regions, in accordance with the character of their own ideas;and for this same reason they are not free to do as they please, in all regions

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य पञ्चविंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा एतस्यैवं पश्यत एवं मन्वानस्यैवं विजानत आत्मतः प्राण आत्मत आशात्मतः स्मर आत्मत आकाश आत्मतस् तेज आत्मत आप आत्मत आविर्भावतिरोभावाव् आत्मतो ऽन्नम् आत्मतो बलम् आत्मतो विज्ञानम् आत्मतो ध्यानम् आत्मतश् चित्तम् आत्मतः संकल्प आत्मतो मन आत्मतो वाग् आत्मतो नामात्मतो मन्त्रा आत्मतः कर्माण्य् आत्मत एवेदं सर्वम्
units.english: For one who sees thus, reflects thus and understands thus,Spirit springs from the Self,Hope springs from the Self,Memory springs from the Self, Ākāśa springs from the Self,Fire springs from the Self,Water springs from the Self,Appearance and Disappearance spring from the Self,Food springs from the Self,Power springs from the Self,Understanding springs from the Self,Contemplation springs from the Self,Consciousness springs from the Self,Will springs from the Self,Mind springs from the Self,Speech springs from the Self,Name springs from the Self, the Mantra texts spring from the Self,Act springs from the Selfall this springs from the Self

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा एतस्येत्यादि स्वाराज्यं प्राप्तस्य प्रकृतस्य विदुष इत्यर्थः । प्राक्सदात्मविज्ञानात्स्वात्मनो ऽन्यस्मात्सतः प्राणादेर्नामान्तस्योत्पत्तिप्रलयावभूतां
units.english: For one who sees thus etc,, etc, and has attained ‘selfsovereignty’,ie the wise person spoken of in the Context,before his understanding of the True Selfall origination and dissolution of entities beginning with ‘Spirit’ and ending with ‘Name’ proceeded from a Self other than his own;

units.sanskrit: सदात्माविज्ञाने तु सतीदानीं स्वात्मत एव संवृत्तौ तथा सर्वो ऽप्यन्यो व्यवहार आत्मत एव विदुषः ॥
units.english: while, after the understanding of the True Self, they proceed from his own Self; similarly, for the wise man, all operations proceed from his own Self

units.sanskrit: तद् एष श्लोकः । न पश्यो मृत्युं पश्यति न रोगं नोत दुःखताम् ।
units.english: To this effect, there is the following Verse‘One who sees this sees not death, nor disease, nor even pain;

units.sanskrit: सर्वं ह पश्यः पश्यति सर्वम् आप्नोति सर्वशः ।
units.english: he who sees this sees all things; and obtains all things in all ways;

units.sanskrit: स एकधा भवति त्रिधा भवति पञ्चधा ।
units.english: he, being one, becomes three, five, seven and nine;

units.sanskrit: शतं च दश चैकश् च सहस्राणि च विंशतिः ।
units.english: and then he is said to be eleven, a hundred and ten, and a thousand and twenty

units.sanskrit: आहारशुद्धौ सत्त्वशुद्धिः ।
units.english: On the purity of objective cognition, follows the purity of the inner nature;

units.sanskrit: सत्त्वशुद्धौ ध्रुवा स्मृतिः ।
units.english: on the purity of the inner nature, Memory becomes strong;

units.sanskrit: स्मृतिलम्भे सर्वग्रन्थीनां विप्रमोक्षः ।
units.english: and on the strengthening of Memory follows freedom from all ties

units.sanskrit: तस्मै मृदितकषायाय तमसस् पारं दर्शयति भगवान् सनत्कुमारः ।
units.english: After all his impurities had been washed out, the Blessed Sanatkumāra showed Nārada beyond darkness

units.sanskrit: तं स्कन्द इत्य् आचक्षते ॥
units.english: They call him Skanda,yea, they call him Skanda,

units.sanskrit: न पश्यः पश्यतीति पश्यो यथोक्तदर्शी विद्वानित्यर्थः । मृत्युं मरणं रोगं ज्वरादि दुःखतां दुःखभावं चापि न पश्यति ।
units.english: Further, to this same effect, there is the following verseOne who sees thisthe wise man who realises the truth as described above,sees not death; nor disease,such as fever etc,nor even painthe Very idea of suffering;

units.sanskrit: सर्वं ह सर्वमेव स पश्यः पश्यत्यात्मानमेव सर्वं ततः सर्वमाप्नोति सर्वशः सर्वप्रकारैरिति ।
units.english: again, one who sees this sees all things; he sees the Self in all things,and then, he obtains all things, in all ways,in every manner possible

units.sanskrit: किञ्च स विद्वान्प्राक्सृष्टिप्रभेदादेकधैव भवत्येकधैव च संस्रिधादिभेदैरनन्तभेदप्रकारो भवति सृष्टिकाले । पुनः संहारकाले मूलमेव स्वं पारमार्थकमेकधाभावं प्रतिपद्यते स्वतन्त्र एवेति विद्यां फलेन प्ररोचयन्स्तौति ।
units.english: Further, the wise man, before the setting in of the differentiations of creation, is one only, and while being one, he becomes three etc, etc, and through these diversities, he comes to be, at the time of creation, of endless diverse forms;and again at the time of Absorption, he returns to his very source, his own real unity, through his own Self

units.sanskrit: अथेदानीं यथोक्ताया विद्यायाः सम्यगवभासकारणं मुखावभासकारणस्येवा'दर्शस्य विशुद्धिकारणं साधनमुपदिश्यतेआहारशुद्धौ ।
units.english: All this attracts the learner to the Philosophy taught and eulogises it Next is taught the means of the proper understanding of the Philosophy,just like the means of cleaning the mirror for obtaining the proper reflection of the face

units.sanskrit: आह्रियत इत्याहारः शब्दादिविषयविज्ञानं भोक्तुर्भोगाया'ह्रियते विशुद्धिकारणं साधनमुपदिश्यतेआहारशुद्धौ । आह्रियत इत्याहरः शब्दादिविषयविज्ञानं भोक्तुर्भोगाया'ह्रियते तस्य विषयोपलब्धिलक्षणस्य विज्ञानस्य शुद्धिराहारशुद्धी रागद्वेषमोहदोषैरसंसृष्टं विषयविज्ञानमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: On the purity of objective cognition;the term ‘āhāra’ stands for what is presented; ie the cognition of sound and other objects, which presented to the experiencing Agent, for the purpose of being experienced; and the purity of the understanding in the shape of the cognition of those objects, is what is meant by the term ‘āhāraŚuddhi’ Purity of objective cognition, which means the objective cognition untainted by such impurities as love, hate and delusion

units.sanskrit: तस्यामाहाराशुद्धौ सत्यां तद्वतो ऽन्तःकरणस्य सत्त्वस्य शुद्धिर्नैर्मल्यं भवति । सत्त्वशुद्धौ च सत्यां यथावगते भूमात्मनि ध्रुवाविच्छिन्ना स्मृतिरविस्मरमं भवति ।
units.english: When this ‘purity of the objective cognition’ has come about, there follows purity of the inner nature, ie freedom of impurities, for the inner nature internal organ wherein the said cognition subsists;when this purity of the inner nature has come about, the Memory of the Self, the Infinite, becomes stronguninterrupted;

units.sanskrit: तस्यां च लब्धायां स्मृतिलम्भे सति सर्वेषामविद्याकृतानर्थपाशरूपाणामनेकजन्मान्तरानुभवभावनाकठिनीकृतानां हृदयाक्षयाणां ग्रन्थीनां विप्रमोक्षो विशेषेण प्रमोक्षणं विनाशो भवतीति ।
units.english: On the strengthening of Memory,when Memory has been secured,follows freedom from all tiesabsolute sessation , destruction of all those knots in the heart, in the shape of bonds of evil due to Ignorance, hardened by the impressions left by past experiences extending over several births

units.sanskrit: यत एतदुत्तरोत्तरं यथोक्तमाहारशुद्धिमूलं तस्मात्सा कार्येत्यर्थः ।
units.english: And because all this follows, gradually, step by step, from the purity of objective cognition,therefore this latter should be accomplished

units.sanskrit: सर्वं शास्रार्थमशेषत उक्त्वा'ख्यायिकामुपसंहरति श्रुतिःतस्मै मृदितकषायाय
units.english: Having expounded the sense of the entire scripture the text sums up the story After all his impurities had been washed out;

units.sanskrit: वार्क्षादिरिव कषायो रागद्वेषादिदोषः सत्त्वस्य रञ्जनारूपत्वात्स ज्ञानवैराग्याभ्यासरूपक्षारेण क्षालितो मृदितो विनाशितो यस्य नारदस्य तस्मै योग्याय मृदितकषायाय तमसो ऽविद्यालक्षणात्पारं
units.english: the impurities of love, hatred and such others had become attached to Nārada’s inner nature, and coloured itlike the colouring matter from trees,and when all this was washed out, rubbed out, destroyed, by the application of the alkaline fluid of knowledge, and dispassion and exercise,Nārada became a fit disciple,and him the teacher showed beyond darkness,ie the Absolute Truth, beyond the darkness of Ignorance

units.sanskrit: परमार्थतत्त्वं दर्शयति दर्शितवानित्यर्थः । को ऽसौ, भगवानुत्पत्तिं प्रलयं चैव भूतानामागतिं गतिम् । वेत्ति विद्यामविद्यां च स वाच्यो भगवानिति ॥ एवन्धर्मा सनत्कुमारः ।
units.english: Who showed him this?The Blessed Sanatkumāra; the ‘Blessed’ has been thus defined‘one who knows the origin, dissolution, the going and the nongoing of living beings,who knows the Science and the Nescience,is to be called Blessed, ‘Bhagavān’;and these conditions were entirely fulfilled in the case of the sage Sanatkumāra

units.sanskrit: तमेव सनत्कुमारं देवं स्कन्द इत्याचक्षते कथयन्ति तद्विदः ।
units.english: This same Sanatkumāra, people also call the Deity Skanda,people who know his real character

units.sanskrit: द्विर्वचनमध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थम् ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि सप्तमाध्यायस्य षड्विंशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse End of Discourse Commentary Introduction Śaṅkara Bhāṣya

units.sanskrit: अथ यद् इदम् अस्मिन् ब्रह्मपुरे दहरं पुण्डरीकं वेश्म दहरो ऽस्मिन्न् अन्तराकासः । तस्मिन् यद् अन्तस् तद् अन्वेष्टव्यं तद् वाव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् इति ॥ यद्यपि दिग्देशकालादिभेदशून्यं ब्रह्म सदेकमेवाद्वितीयमात्मैवेदं सर्वमिति षष्ठसप्तमयोरधिगतं तथापीह मन्दबुद्धीनां दिग्देशादिभेदवद्वस्त्वित्येवं भाविता बुद्धिर्न शक्यते सहसा परमार्थविषया कर्तुमित्यनधिगम्य च ब्रह्म न पुरुषार्थसिद्धिरिति तदधिगमाय
units.english: Though under Discourses and , it has been learnt that ‘Brahman is real, one, without a second’ and ‘the Self is all this’ free from all diversities of space, place, time and the rest,yet, in the world, there are many persons of dull intellect, among whom the conviction is so strong to the effect that everything real is beset with diversities of space, place and the rest, that it cannot, all at once, be turned towards the Absolutely Realand yet without understanding the real nature of Brahman, the highest purpose of men cannot be fulfilled;hence for the benefit of the duller persons, it is necessary to convey the teaching indirectly, by indicating, in the first instance, the particular spot within the Lotus of the Heart as the abode of the Self, the Brahman

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि सत्सम्यक्प्रत्ययैकविषया कर्तुमित्यानधिगम्य च ब्रह्म न पुरुषार्थसिद्धिरिति तदधिगमाय हृदयपुण्डरीकदेश उपदेष्टव्यः । यद्यपि सत्सम्यक्प्रत्ययैकविषयं निर्गुणं चा'त्मतत्त्वं तथापि मन्दबुद्धीनां गुणवत्त्वस्येष्टत्वात्सत्यकामादिगुणवत्त्वं च वक्तव्यम् । तथा यद्यपि ब्रह्मविदां स्त्र्यादिविषयेभ्यः स्वयमेवोपरमो भवति तथाप्यनेकजन्मविषयसेवाभ्यासजनिता
units.english: Secondly, though the Self in its essence is the object of the single true cognition of ‘Being’ and is devoid of all qualities,yet for the benefit of person with dull intellect has his heart so fixed upon the Highest Being possessing the highest qualities, that it is found necessary to speak of such qualities belonging to him as ‘being of unfailing wish’ and so forth Thirdly, though in the case of persons who have realised Brahman, the avoidance of such objects of sensegratification as the woman and the like comes by itself,yet, it is not easy to divert, all at once, the longing for objects of sensegratification that has grown through long continued indulgence extending over several births;

units.sanskrit: विषयविषया तृष्णा न सहसा निवर्तयितुं शक्यत इति ब्रह्मचर्यादिसाधनविशेषो विधातव्यः ।
units.english: below, when the term is explained as ‘renunciation of desire for women’Fourthly, though in the case of persons who have realised the unity of Self, there can be no goer or going or place to go to all which involve diversity;

units.sanskrit: तथा यद्यप्यात्मैकत्वविदां गन्तृगमनगन्तव्याभावादविद्याविशेषस्थितिनिमित्तक्षये गगन इव विद्युदुद्भूत इव वायुर्दग्धेन्धन इवाग्निः स्वात्मन्येव निवृत्तिस्तथापि
units.english: consequently, what happens is that, on the disappearance of the rootcause of that particular factor of Nescience,they lapse on death into their own Self,just as the lightning lapses into the Ākāśa, as Air lapses into itself as soon as it is manifested, or as the Fire lapses into itself, when the fuel has been entirely burnt up;

units.sanskrit: गन्तृगमनादिवासितबुद्धीनां हृदयदेशगुणविशिष्टब्रह्मोपासकानां मूर्धन्यया नाड्या
units.english: and yet, there are many persons whose minds are still beset with such diversities as the goer, the going and the place to go to,and who are still given to worshipping or meditating upon Brahman as abiding within the Heart and as endowed with qualities;

units.sanskrit: गतिर्वक्तव्येत्यष्टमः प्रपाठक आरभ्यते ।
units.english: It is for all these purposes that the Eighth Discourse is proceeded with

units.sanskrit: दिग्देशगुणगतिफलभेदशून्यं हि परमार्थसदद्वयं ब्रह्ममन्दबुद्धीनामसदिव प्रतिभाति ।
units.english: The Absolutely True Brahman, Being, one, without a second, regarded by persons of dull intellect as nonexistent;

units.sanskrit: सन्मार्गस्थास्तावद्भवन्तु ततः शनैः परमार्थसदपि ग्राहयिष्यामीति मन्यते श्रुतिः ।
units.english: hence, what the Smṛti text thinks is that though the teaching now going to be imparted is not the absolutely right one,yet even through such wrong teaching let these ignorant persons be brought on to the right Path, we shall, gradually, lead them up to the knowledge of the Absolutely True also

units.sanskrit: अथानन्तरं यदिदं वक्ष्यमाणं दहरमल्पं पुण्डरीकं पुण्डरीकसदृशं वेश्मेव वेश्म द्वारपालादिमत्त्वात् ।
units.english: Now,after this,what is going to be described is the small Palace like the white Lotus,which appears like the white Lotus; it is as if it were a palace, guarded as it is like a palace by gatekeepers and others

units.sanskrit: अस्मिन्ब्रह्मपुरे ब्रह्मणः परस्य पुरं राज्ञो ऽनेकप्रकृतिमद्यथापुरं तथेदमनेकेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिभिः स्वाम्यर्थकारिभिर्युक्तमिति ब्रह्मपुरम् पुरे च वेश्म राज्ञो यथा तथा तस्मिन्ब्रह्मपुरे शरीरे दहरं वेश्म ब्रह्मण उपलब्ध्यधिष्ठानमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: In this city of Brahman,the city of the Supreme Brahman; just as the king, who has many subjects under him, has his city,so has the Brahman His city, equipped with the several senseorgans, mind and intelligence devoted to the service of their Master;in the City, there is the palace of the king,so here in Brahman’s city, the Body, there is a small Palace,which is, the locus of the apprehension of Brahman that is, it is the place where Brahman is cognised;

units.sanskrit: यथा विष्णोः शालग्रामः ।
units.english: just as Viṣṇu is cognised in the piece of Black stone

units.sanskrit: अस्मिन्हि स्वविकारशिङ्गे देहे नामरूपव्याकरणाय प्रविष्टं सदाख्यं ब्रङ्म जीवेना'त्मनेत्युक्तम् ।
units.english: In this body, which is an offshoot of one of his products, Brahman named ‘Being’, enters in the form of the Living Self,for the purpose of differentiating Names and Forms;as has been explained above

units.sanskrit: तस्मादस्मिन्हृदयपुण्डरीके वेश्मन्युपसंहृतकरणैर्बाह्यविषयविरक्तैर्विशेषतो ब्रह्मचर्यसत्यसाधनाभ्यां युक्तेर्वक्ष्यमाणगुणवद्ध्यायमानैर्ब्रह्मोपलभ्यत
units.english: For this reason it is in this Palace of the White Lotus in the Heart that Brahman is apprehended by persons who have withdrawn their organs from activity, who are no longer attached to external things, and who are specially equipped with means of success as Celibacy and Truth, and who go on meditating upon Brahman as endowed with the qualities going to be described

units.sanskrit: इति प्रकरणार्थः ।
units.english: Such is the sense of what is taught in the present context

units.sanskrit: दहरो ऽल्पतरो ऽस्मिन्दहरे वेश्मनि वेश्मनो ऽल्पत्वात्तदन्तर्वर्तिनो ऽल्पतरत्वं वेश्मनः । अन्तराकाश आकाशाख्यं ब्रह्म ।
units.english: There is a smallsmaller than the said Palace In the small Palace, there it lies a smallsmaller; the Palace itself being small, what lies within it must be smaller than the Palace;Inner Ākāśa;ie Brahman named Ākāśa’;

units.sanskrit: आकाशो वै नामेति हि वक्ष्यति ।
units.english: it is going to be declared later on that ‘Ākāśa is His name’;

units.sanskrit: आकाश इवाशरीरत्वात्सूक्ष्मत्वसर्वगतत्वसामान्याच्च ।
units.english: and the reason for this lies in the fact that like Ākāśa, Brahman is bodiless, extremely subtle and allpervading

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नाकाशाख्ये यदन्तर्मध्ये तदन्वेष्टव्यम् ।
units.english: What lies withininsidethat Ākāśa should be sought after,that and that alone should be understoodwith particular care;

units.sanskrit: तद्वाव तदेव च विशेषेण जिज्ञासितव्यं गुर्वाश्रयश्रवणाद्युपायैरन्विष्य च साक्षात्करणीयमित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: that is,it should be directly perceived after careful search through such means as going to a teacher, listening to him and so on

units.sanskrit: तं चेद् ब्रूयुर् यद् इदम् अस्मिन् ब्रह्मपुरे दहरं पुण्डरीकं वेश्म दहरो ऽस्मिन्न् अन्तराकाशः किं तद् अत्र विद्यते यद् अन्वेष्टव्यं यद् वाव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् इति ।
units.english: If they should say to him‘In this city of Brahman there is the Small Palace like the White Lotus,and there lies the smaller Inner Ākāśa,what is it that lies within it which should be sought after and should be understood?’,he should say in reply as follows

units.sanskrit: पुण्डरीक एव वेश्मनि तावत्किं स्यात् । किं ततो ऽल्पतरे खे यद्भवेदित्याहुः । दहरो ऽस्मिन्नन्तराकाशः किं तदत्र विद्यते न किञ्चन विद्यत इत्यभिप्रायः । यदि नाम बदरमात्रं किमपि विद्यते किं तस्यान्वेषणेन विजिज्ञासनेन वा फलं विजिज्ञासितुः स्यात् । अतो यत्त्त्रान्वेष्टव्यं विजिज्ञासितव्यं वा न तेन प्रयोजनमित्युक्तवतः स आचार्यो ब्रूयादिति श्रुतेर्वचनम् ॥
units.english: When the Teacher has said above in text ,if the Disciples should sayurge the argumentwhat argument?this‘in this city of Brahman,which is limited in extent,there is the Smaller Palace like the White Lotus,and within that lies the still smaller Inner Ākāśa;what could lie within the Palace of the White Lotus? Only that which should occupy a smaller space than that;that smaller Inner Ākāśa,what is it that lies within it, by seeking after which, or by understanding which, what reward would accrue to the Seeker? Hence, there is no use for that which has been declared to be as to be sought after or understood’When the Disciple has urged this argument, the teacher should say in reply as followssays the Vedic Text

units.sanskrit: यावान् वा अयम् आकाशस् तावान् एषो ऽन्तर्हृदय आकाशः ।
units.english: As large as is this Ākāśa, so large is that Ākāśa, in the Heart

units.sanskrit: उभे ऽस्मिन् द्यावापृथिवी अन्तर् एव समाहिते ।
units.english: Both Heaven and Earth are contained within it;

units.sanskrit: उभाव् अग्निश् च वायुश् च सूर्याचन्द्रमसाव् उभौ विद्युन् नक्षत्राणि । यच् चास्येहास्ति यच् च नास्ति सर्वं तद् अस्मिन् समाहितम् इति ॥
units.english: both fire and air, both the sun and the moon, the lightning and the stars, and whatever there is in this world, and also what is not,all that is contained within it

units.sanskrit: शृणुत ।
units.english: Listen, please

units.sanskrit: तत्र यद्ब्रूथ पुण्डरीकान्तःखस्याल्पत्वात्तत्स्थमल्पतरं स्यादिति ।
units.english: You say that Ākāśa within the White Lotus being small, what is contained therein must be smaller than that

units.sanskrit: तदसत् ।
units.english: This is not right;

units.sanskrit: न हि खं पुण्डरीकवेशमगतं पुण्डरीकादल्पतरं मत्वावोचं दहरो ऽर्स्मिन्नन्तराकाश इति ।
units.english: when said that the ‘Inner Ākāśa within is smaller’, did not mean that the Ākāśa within the White Lotus was ‘smaller’ than the White Lotus;

units.sanskrit: किं तर्हि पुण्डरीकमल्पं तदनुविधायि तत्स्थमन्तःकरणं पुण्डरीकाकाशपरिच्छिन्नं
units.english: what meant was that the WhiteLotus is small, and in keeping with it, the inner organ residing within that Lotus is limited in scope by the Ākāśa in the Lotus;

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन्विशुद्धे संहृतकरणानां योगिनां स्वच्छ इवोदके प्रतिबिम्बरूपमादर्श इव च शुद्धे स्वच्छं विज्ञानज्योतिः स्वरूपावभासं तावन्मात्रं ब्रह्मोपलभ्यत इति
units.english: and when that internal has become purified by the withdrawal of the organs, the Yogin Mystic perceives therein Brahman, pure, appearing like the Light of Consciousness and of the same size as the said inner organ,just as the reflected image of a real substance is seen in clear water or other reflecting substances;this is what meant when said that therein lies the smaller Inner Ākāśa;

units.sanskrit: दहरो ऽस्मिन्नन्तराकाश इत्यवोचामान्तःकरणोपाधिनिमित्तम् ।
units.english: all this being due to the limitation imposed by the internal organ

units.sanskrit: स्वतस्तु यावान्वै प्रसिद्धः परिमाणतो ऽयमाकाशो भौतिकस्तावानेषो ऽन्तर्हृदय आकाशो यस्मिन्नन्वेष्टव्यं विजिज्ञासितव्यं चावोचाम ।
units.english: In reality, by itself,as largein sizeas is this Material Elemental Ākāśa is known to be,so large is that Ākāśa in the Heart,in which, said, was what was to be sought after and understood

units.sanskrit: नाप्याकाशतुल्यपरिमाणत्वमभिप्रेत्य तावानित्युच्यते । किं तर्हि ब्रह्मणो ऽनुरूपस्य दृष्टान्तान्तरस्याभावात् ।
units.english: By the phrase ‘so large’ it is not meant that it is really of the same size as Ākāśa, what is meant is to cite an illustration and no nearer parallel to Brahman could be found

units.sanskrit: कथं पुनर्ना'काशसममेव ब्रह्मेत्यवगम्यते ।
units.english: QuestionBut why should Brahman not be understood as really of the same size as Ākāśa?

units.sanskrit: येना'वृतं खं च दिवं महीं च । तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशः संभूतःएतस्मिन्नु खल्वक्षरे गार्ग्याकाशःइत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः ।
units.english: AnswerBecause of such Vedic texts as‘By whom is covered the Ākāśa, the Heaven and the Earth’ Mahanārāyaṇa ;‘From that Self was produced Ākāśa Taitti ‘In this Imperishable Entity O Gārgī, does Ākāśa subsist’ etc, etc

units.sanskrit: किञ्चोभे ऽस्मिन्द्यावापृथिवी ब्रह्माकाशे बुद्ध्युपाधिविशिष्टे ऽन्तरेव समाहिते सम्यगाहिते स्थिते यथा वा अरा नाभावित्युक्तं हि ।
units.english: Further, within thisBrahmanĀkāśa, as conditioned by the limitations of the intellect,are contained both Heaven and Earth, ie these are properly contained;

units.sanskrit: तथोभावग्निश्च वायुश्चेत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: it has been said before that ‘as the spokes are fastened to the nave etc’so also are contained therein both Fire and Air, etc, as before

units.sanskrit: यच्चास्या'त्मन आत्मीयत्वेन देहवतो ऽस्ति विद्यत इह लोके । तता यच्चा'त्मीयत्वेन न विद्यते । नष्टं भविष्यच्च नास्तीत्युच्यते ।
units.english: Whatever there is in this worldas related to the said conditioned Embodied Self,and so also what is notknown to be so related to it,what is destroyed and what is yet to come both are spoken of as ‘is not’

units.sanskrit: न त्वत्यन्तमेवासत् । तस्य हृद्याकाशे समाधानानुपपत्तेः ॥
units.english: as for an absolutely nonentity it would not be possible to be ‘contained’ in the Ākāśa of the Heart

units.sanskrit: तं चेद् ब्रूयुर् अस्मिंश् चेदं ब्रह्मपुरे सर्वं समाहितं सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामा यद् एनज् जरा वाप्नोति प्रध्वंसते वा किं ततो ऽतिशिष्यत
units.english: If they should say to himIf all this is contained in this City of Brahman, all beings and all desires,then, when decrepitude overtakes it, or when it perishes, what is left of it?

units.sanskrit: तं चेदेवमुक्तवन्तं ब्रूयुः पुनरन्तेवासिनः अस्मिंश्चेद्यथोक्ते चेद्यदि ब्रह्मपुरोपलक्षितान्तराकाश इत्यर्थः । इदं सर्वं समाहितं सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामाः । कथमाचार्येणानुक्ताः कामा अन्तेवासिभिरुच्यन्ते ।
units.english: When he has said above, if the disciples should say to the teacher as followsIf in the abovementioned City of Brahman,ie in the Inner Ākāśa circumscribed by the City of Brahman,is contained all this, all beings and all desires,The teacher has not spoken of the Desires why then should the disciples mention it?There is nothing wrong in this;

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः यच्चास्येहास्ति यच्च नास्तीत्युक्ता एव ह्याचार्येण कामाः ।
units.english: in the expression ‘whatever is in this and what is not used by the teacher in the preceding text has included the Desires also;

units.sanskrit: अपि च सर्वशब्देन चोक्ता एव कामाः ।
units.english: and also the Desires are already included under the term ‘all’

units.sanskrit: यदा यस्मिन्काल एतच्छरीरं ब्रह्मपुराख्यं जरावलीपलितादिलक्षणा वयोहानिर्वा'प्नोति शस्रादिना वा वृक्णं प्रध्वंसते विस्रंसते विनश्यति किं ततो ऽन्यदतिशिष्यते । घटाश्रितक्षीरदधिस्नेहादिवद्घटनाशे देहनाशे ऽपि देहाश्रयमुत्तरोत्तरं पूर्वपूर्वनाशान्नश्यतीत्यभिप्रायः । एवं प्राप्ते नाशे किं ततो ऽन्यद्यथोक्तादतिशिष्यते ऽवतिष्ठते न किञ्चनावतिष्ठत इत्यभीप्रायः ॥
units.english: Whenat which time,this body, called ‘the City of Brahman is overtaken by decrepitudemarked by grey hairs and shrunken skin,or old age,or, on being torn or maimed by weapons, it perishes,decays, is destroyed,what is left of it What is meant is that, just as on the destruction of jar, the milk, curds and oils contained in the jar also become destroyed,so when the body is destroyed, all that is contained in the body should also, gradually one after the other, become destroyed;this destruction, thus, having come about, what is left of it,of what has been described above, what is there left? The sense is that nothing is left

units.sanskrit: स ब्रूयात् । नास्य जरयैतज् जीर्यति न वधेनास्य हन्यते ।
units.english: He should say‘By the decrepitude of this body, that does not age; by the death of this, That is not killed;

units.sanskrit: एतत् सत्यं ब्रह्मपुरम् अस्मिन् कामाः समाहिताः ।
units.english: That is the true BrahmanCity; in this are all desires contained

units.sanskrit: एष आत्मापहतपाप्मा विजरो विमृत्युर् विशोको विजिघत्सो ऽपिपासः सत्यकामः सत्यसंकल्पः ।
units.english: This is the Self, free from evil, free from decrepitude, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger and thirst, with true desires and true volitions

units.sanskrit: यथा ह्य् एवेह प्रजा अन्वाविशन्ति यथानुशासनम् । यं यम् अन्तम् अभिकामा भवन्ति यं जनपदं यं क्षेत्रभागं तं तम् एवोपजीवन्ति ॥
units.english: As in this world, the subjectpeople follow as they are ordered and accordingly live upon that country, that province and that piece of cultivated land, which they desire

units.sanskrit: एवमन्तेवासिभिश्चोदितः स आचार्यो ब्रूयात्तन्मतिमपनयन् ।
units.english: Being thus urged by his disciples, hethe teachershould say as follows removing their misconception

units.sanskrit: कथम् । अस्य देहस्य जरयैतद्यथोक्तमन्तराकाशाख्यं ब्रङ्म यस्मिन्सर्व समाहितं न जीर्यति देहवन्न विक्रियत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: How?By the decrepitude of this BodyThatthe abovedescribed Brahman called the ‘Inner Ākāśa’, wherein all is contained,does not age,ie it does not become changed decay;

units.sanskrit: न चास्य वधेन शस्रादिघातेनैतद्धन्यते यथा'काशं किमु ततो ऽपि सूक्ष्मतरमशब्दमस्पर्शं
units.english: Ākāśa is not affected by any strokes of weapons,what to say then of Brahman which is still subtler, without sound, without touch, is not affected by the defects of the body or the senseorgans

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्म देहेन्द्रियादिदोषैर्न स्पृश्यत इत्येतस्मिन्नवसरे वक्तव्यं प्राप्तं तत्प्रकृतव्यासङ्गो मा भूदिति नोच्यते ।
units.english: It was necessary to explain here why Brahman in the Body is not affected by the defects of the Body and the senseorgans; but it is not explained here, as it would make a break in the continuity of the present Exposition;

units.sanskrit: इन्द्रविरोचनाख्यायिकायामुपरिष्टाद्वक्ष्यामो युक्तितः ।
units.english: we shall explain it with suitable reasons, later on, under the story relating to Indra and Virocana

units.sanskrit: एतत्सत्यमवितथं ब्रह्मपुरं ब्रह्मैव पुरं ब्रह्मपुरं शरीराख्यं तु ब्रह्मपुरं ब्रह्मोपलक्षणार्थत्वात् । तत्त्वनृतमेव । वाचा'रम्भणं विकारो नामधेयमिति श्रुतेः । तद्विकारे ऽनृते ऽपि देहशुङ्गे ब्रह्मोपलभ्यत इति ब्रह्मपुरमित्युक्तं व्यावहारिकम् ।
units.english: That is the truenot unrealBrahman City;hence the term ‘Brahmapura stands for Brahman itself as the City that ‘Brahmapura ’ ‘City of Brahman’, which is called the ‘Body’, only in so far as it characterises the Brahman therein, and it is unreal,as declared in the Vedic text ‘all modification is only a product of words, a mere name’;though the sprout of the body, which, as a product, is unreal, yet, as it is in the body that Brahman is perceived, it is called the ‘City of Brahman’, in the practical not absolutely real sense;

units.sanskrit: सत्यं तु ब्रह्मपुरमेतदेव ब्रह्म ।
units.english: the real ‘Brahmancity’ is Brahman Itself;

units.sanskrit: सर्वव्यवहारास्पदत्वात् ।
units.english: as it is this that forms the basis of all practical usage

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽस्मिन्पुण्डरीकोपलक्षिते ब्रह्मपुरे सर्वे कामा ये बहिर्भवद्भिः प्रार्थ्यन्ते ते ऽस्मिन्नेव स्वात्मनि समाहिताः ।
units.english: For this reason, in thisin the Brahmancity characterised by the White Lotuswhich is your own self,all desires,all that are wished for, by you, in the external worldare contained

units.sanskrit: अतस्तत्प्राप्त्युपायमेवानुतिष्ठत बाह्यविषयतृष्मां त्यजतेत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: That is to say, on account of this, when you are going to employ the means for attaining that Brahman you should give up all desire for external things

units.sanskrit: एष आत्मा भवतां स्वरूपम् ।
units.english: This is the Self,the real Self of you all

units.sanskrit: शृणुत तस्य लक्षणम् । अपहतपाप्मा । अपहतः पाप्मा धर्माधर्माख्यो यस्य सो ऽयमपहतपाप्मा । तथा विजरो विगतजरो विमृत्युश्च ।
units.english: And now listen to what Its character isIt is free from evil,One in whom all ‘evil’, in the shape of Merit and Demerit has been destroyed,free from decrepitude,whose decrepitude has;passed off,free from death

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं पूर्वमेव न वधेनास्य हन्यत इति ।
units.english: This has already been asserted beforeIt is not killed by the death of the body;

units.sanskrit: किमर्थ पुनरुच्यते ।
units.english: why is it asserted again?

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि देहसंबन्धिभ्यां जरामृत्युभ्यां न संबध्यते ऽन्यथापि संबन्धस्ताभ्यां स्यादित्याशङ्कानिवृत्त्यर्थम् ।
units.english: It is reiterated with a view to the possibility of the idea being entertained that ‘though It is not affected by the decrepitude and death of the Body, It may be subject to them in other ways’It is free from sorrow,all sorrow disappeared;

units.sanskrit: विशोको विगतशोकः । शोको नामेष्टादिवियोगनिमित्तो मानसः संतापः । विजिघत्सो विगताशनेच्छः ।
units.english: ‘sorrow’ is the mental suffering caused by separation from what is desirable;it is free from hunger all desire for food gone,‘freefrom thirst’,all desire for drinking gone

units.sanskrit: अपिपासो ऽपानेच्छः । नन्वपहतपाप्मत्वेन जरादयः शोकान्ताः प्रतिषिद्धा एव भवन्ति । कारणप्रतिषेधात् ।
units.english: By the assertion of freedom from evil all else,from decrepitude down to sorrow,becomes precluded, by the preclusion of their cause in the shape of evil, decrepitude and the rest being the effects of ‘evil’

units.sanskrit: जरादिप्रतिषेधेन वा धर्माधर्मयोः कार्याभावे विद्यमानयोरप्यसत्समत्वमिति पृथक्प्रतिषेधो ऽनर्थकः स्यात् ।
units.english: Or, the denial of decrepitude and the rest would imply that there are no effects produced by Merit and Demerit, which thus, even though present, would be as good as nonexistent;

units.sanskrit: सत्यमेवं तथापि धर्मकार्या नन्दव्यतिरेकेण स्वाभाविकानन्दो यथेश्वरे विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्मेति श्रुतेः । तथाधर्मकार्यजरादिव्यतिरेकेणापि जरादिदुःखस्वरूपं स्वाभाविकं स्यादित्याशङ्क्येत । अतो युक्तस्तन्निवृत्तये जरादीनां धर्माधर्माभ्यां पृथक्प्रतिषेधः ।
units.english: yet, it might be thought that‘just as, even though god is free from such pleasures as are due to Merit, yet He has that bliss which is in His very nature,as declared in the text Brahman is Consciousness and Bliss similarly, even though He is free from such decrepitude etc, as are due to demerit, yet the pain due to such decrepitude etc, might be there in His very nature’And for getting rid of such an idea, to deny Decrepitude and the rest, even apart from Merit and Demerit

units.sanskrit: जरादिग्रहणं सर्वदुःखोपलक्षणार्थम् ।
units.english: The mention of ‘Decrepitude’ and the rest stands for all kinds of pain;

units.sanskrit: पापनिमित्तानां तु दुःखानामानन्त्यात्प्रत्येकं च तत्प्रतिषेधस्याशक्यत्वात्सर्वदुःखप्रतिषेधार्थं युक्तमेवापहतपाप्मत्ववचनम् ।
units.english: as the number of Pains due to Sin is endless; it would be impossible to deny each of them singly,hence, for the denying of all sorts of pain, it is only right that ‘freedom from evil’ itself should have been mentioned as the source of all kinds of pain

units.sanskrit: सत्या अवितथाः कामा यस्य सो ऽयं सत्यकामः ।
units.english: He is with true desires,ie all His desires are infallible;

units.sanskrit: तथा कामहेतवः संकल्पा अपि सत्या यस्य स सत्यसंकल्पः । संकल्पाः कामाश्च शुद्धसत्त्वोपाधिनिमित्ता ईश्वरस्य चित्रगुवत् । न स्वतो नेति नेतीत्युक्तत्वात् ।
units.english: in the case of God, both desires and volitions are due to the limitations of Pure Sattva the altitude of Goodness;just like the term ‘Citragu’ ,and they do not really subsist in God Himself, because it has been declared that He can be spoken of only through negations‘not this, not that’

units.sanskrit: यथोक्तलक्षण एवा'त्मा विज्ञेयो गुरुभ्यः शास्त्रतश्चा'त्मसंवेद्यतया च स्वाराज्यकामैः ।
units.english: It is the Self, of this said character that should be learnt by persons desiring ‘selfsovereignty’ from Teachers and from Scriptures, as the one object of selfrealisation

units.sanskrit: न चेद्विज्ञायते को दोषः स्यादिति ।
units.english: If this Self is not known, what would be the harm?

units.sanskrit: शृणुतात्र दोषं दृष्टान्तेन । यथा ह्येवेह लोके प्रजा अन्वाविशन्त्यनुवर्तन्ते ।
units.english: Listen to the harm that am to explain by means of an illustration‘As in this world, subjectpeople follow as they are ordered;

units.sanskrit: यथानुशासनं यथेह प्रजा अन्यं स्वामिनं मन्यमानाः स्वस्य स्वामिनो यथा यथानुशासनं तथा तथान्वाविशन्ति ।
units.english: the common people, knowing that some one else is their master, follow as they are ordered by himwhatthey accordingly live upon that country and upon that piece of cultivated land which they desire,accordance with their own intelligence,and they live upon that same country

units.sanskrit: एष दृष्टान्तो ऽस्वातन्त्र्यदेषं प्रति पुण्यफलोपभोगे ॥
units.english: This example illustrates the harm that accrues to one through not being selfdependent, and being dependent upon the experiences that follow from his merit

units.sanskrit: तद् यथेह कर्मजितो लोकः क्षीयत एवम् एवामुत्र पुण्यजितो लोकः क्षीयते ।
units.english: And just as in this world, the Region won by Action perishes, so also does perish, in the other world, the Region won by righteous deeds

units.sanskrit: तद् य इहात्मानम् अननुविद्य व्रजन्त्य् एतांश् च सत्यान् कामांस् तेषां सर्वेषु लोकेष्व् अकामचारो भवति । अथ य इहात्मानम् अनिवुद्य व्रजन्त्य् एतंश् च सत्यान् कामांस् तेषां सर्वेषु लोकेषु कामचारो भवति ॥
units.english: Those who go from here without having understood the Self and these true desires,for them, in all regions, there is no freedom to do what they wish; while those who go from here after having understood the Self and the true desires, become free, in all regions, to do what they wish

units.sanskrit: अथान्यो दृष्टान्तस्तत्क्षयं प्रति तद्यथेहेत्यादिः ।
units.english: Another example of the perishability of all things but the Self;

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्र यथेह लोके तासामेव स्वाम्यनुशासनानुवर्तिनीनां प्रजानां सेवादिजितो लोकः पराधीनोपभोगः क्षीयते ऽन्तवान्भवति । अथेदानीं दार्ष्टान्तिकमुपसंहरतिएवमेवामुत्राग्निहोत्रादिपुण्यज् इतो लोकः पराधीनोपभोगः क्षीयत एवेत्युक्तो दोष एषामिति विषयं दर्शयतितद्य
units.english: Just as in the world etc, etc,just as in this world, for the subjectpeople who follow the orders of their masters, the Region won by service and other acts, having its enjoyment dependent upon others,perishes comes to an end;the text next proceeds to the other factor of the illustration So also does perish the Region Won by righteous deeds,like the performance of the Agnihotra,having its experiences dependent upon others

units.sanskrit: इत्यादिना ।
units.english: The text next points out the person on whom befall the said undesirable results;those who etc

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्रेहास्मिंल्लोके ज्ञानकर्मणोरधिकृता योग्याः सन्त आत्मानं यथोक्तलक्षणं शास्त्राचार्योपदिष्टमननुविद्य यथोपदेशमनु स्वसंवेद्यतामकृत्वा व्रजन्ति देहादस्मात् प्रयन्ति य एतांश्च यथोक्तान् सत्यान् सत्यसंकल्पकार्यांश्च स्वात्मस्थान् कामानननुविद्य व्रजन्ति तेषां सर्वेषु लोकेष्वकामचारो ऽस्वतन्त्रता भवति ।
units.english: In this world, those who, quite capable of, and entitled to, both Knowledge and Action,without understandingwithout realising in their own consciousness,the Selfas described above, through the teachings of the Scriptures and Teachers,go from here,depart from this present body,as also those who, without understanding the abovementioned true desiresie such desires as arise from true volitions, in the Self,go from’here,for all such people, in all regions, there is no freedom to do as they wish,ie they have no independence, being like subjectpeoplesubservient to the orders of their king

units.sanskrit: अथ ये ऽन्य इह लोक आत्मानं शास्राचार्योरदेशमनुविद्य स्वात्मसंवेद्यतामापाद्य व्रजन्ति यथोक्तांश्च सत्यान्कामांस्तेषां सर्वेषु लोकेषु कामचारो भवति राज्ञ इव सार्वभौमस्येह लोके ॥
units.english: While those in this worldotherswho, go after having understoodrealised in their own consciousness,through the teachings of the scriptures and teachers,the Self, as also the true desires,as described above,for them, in all regions there is freedom to do what they wish;just as there is in this world for the king of the whole world

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य प्रथमः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: स यदि पितृलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य पितरः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Region of the Fathers, by his mere will, his fathers come upto him;

units.sanskrit: तेन पितृलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Region of the Fathers, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: कथं सर्वेषु लोकेषु कामचारो भवतीति, उच्यतेय आत्मानं यतोक्तलक्षणं हृदि साक्षात्कृतवान्वक्ष्यमाणब्रह्मचर्यादिसाधनसंपन्नः संस्तत्स्थांश्च सत्यान्कामान्स त्यक्तदेहो यदि पितृलोककामः पितरो जनयितारस्त एव सुखहेतुत्वेन भोग्यत्वाल्लोका उच्यन्ते तेषु कामो यस्य तैः पितृभिः संबन्धेच्छा यस्य भवति तस्य संकल्पमात्रादेव पितरः समुत्तिष्ठिन्त्यात्मसंबन्धितामापद्यन्ते ।
units.english: It is next explained how the man is free to do what he wishes, in all RegionsIf one,fully equipped with such resources as celibacy and the like, which are going to be described,has realised in his heart, the Self as described above,as also the true desires subsisting therein,then, on relinquishing this body, if he be desirous of the Region of the Fathers;the term ‘pitaraḥ’ here stands for one’s ancestors, and they themselves are here spoken of as ‘Regions’ because, being the source of happiness, they are objects of experience;and if the man has his desire fixed on these ancestors,ie if he has the desire to meet his ancestors,thenby his mere will, his Fathers come up to him,ie become connected with him

units.sanskrit: विशुद्धसत्त्वतया सत्यसंकल्पत्वादीश्वरस्येव तेन पितृलोकेन भोगेन संपन्नः संपत्तिरिष्टप्राप्तिस्तया समृद्धो महीयते पूज्यते वर्धते वा महिमानमनुभवति ॥
units.english: As he is of pure nature and hence his will is infallible, like the will of God Himself,he becomes successful in obtainingthe experience ofthe Region of the Fathers,he feels happy and great, he is honoured and he prospers, or experiences greatness

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि मातृलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य मातरः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Region of Mothers, by his mere will, his mothers come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेन मातृलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Region of Mothers, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि भ्रातृलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य भ्रातरः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Region of the Brothers, by his mere will, his brothers come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेन भ्रातृलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Region of the Brothers he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि स्वसृलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य स्वसारः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति । तेन स्वसृलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: If he be desirous of the Region of Sisters, by his mere will, his sisters come up to him, and having become successful in obtaining the Region of Sisters, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि सखिलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य सखायः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति ।
units.english: If he be desirous of obtaining the Region of Friends, by his mere will, his friends come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेन सखिलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Region of Friends, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि गन्धमाल्यलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य गन्धमाल्ये समुत्तिष्ठतः ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Region of Scents and Garlands by his mere will, scents and garlands come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेन गन्धमाल्यलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Region of Scents and Garlands, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्य् अन्नपानलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्यान्नपाने समुत्तिष्ठतः ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Regions of Food and Drink, by his mere will, food and drink come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेनान्नपानलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Regions of Food and Drink, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि गीतवादितलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य गीतवादिते समुत्तिष्ठतः ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Regions of Song and Music, by his mere will, song and music come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेन गीतवादितलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Regions of Song and Music, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: अथ यदि स्त्रीलोककामो भवति । संकल्पाद् एवास्य स्त्रियः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति ।
units.english: If he be desirous of the Regions of Women, by his mere with, women come up to him;

units.sanskrit: तेन स्त्रीलोकेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having become successful in obtaining the Regions of Women, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: समानमन्यत् ।
units.english: The rest is as before

units.sanskrit: मातरो जनयित्र्यो ऽतीताः सुखहेतुभूताः सामर्ध्यात् ।
units.english: ‘Mothers’ stands for the female ancestors, who were the source of much happiness in the past;

units.sanskrit: न हि दुःखहेतुभूतासु ग्रामसूकरादिजन्मनिमित्तासु मातृषु विशुद्धसत्त्वस्य योगिन इच्छा तत्संबन्धो वा युक्तः ॥
units.english: as it is not right that the Mystic of the pure nature should have any longing for, or connection with, such mothers as may have been the source of suffering and pain, in such lives as that of the villagehog and the like

units.sanskrit: यं यम् अन्तम् अभिकामो भवति । यं कामं कामयते । सो ऽस्य संकल्पाद् एव समुत्तिष्ठति ।
units.english: Whichever country he is attached to, and whichever desirable thing he desires,all this comes up to him, by his mere will;

units.sanskrit: तेन संपन्नो महीयते ॥
units.english: and having been successful in obtaining this, he feels happy and great

units.sanskrit: यं यनम्तं प्रदेशमभिकामो भवति । यं च कामं कामयते यथोक्तव्यतिरेकेणापि सो ऽस्यान्तः प्राप्तुमिष्टः कामश्च संकल्पादेव समुत्तिष्ठत्यस्य । तेनेच्छाविघाततयाभिप्रेतार्थप्राप्त्या च संपन्नो महीयत इत्युक्तार्थम् ॥
units.english: Whichever countryplacehe is attached to, whichever desirable thing he desires,even those in addition to those described above all thisthat is desired by himthe country and the desirable thingcomes up to him, by his mere will;and thus his desires not being thwarted, and having obtained what he desired, he has become successful in obtaining all this,he feels happy and great’, as is already explained

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: त इमे सत्याः कामा अनृतापिधानाः ।
units.english: These are the ‘True Desires’ hidden by the untrue;

units.sanskrit: तेषां सत्यानां सताम् अनृतम् अपिधानम् ।
units.english: though they are true, they are hidden by the untrue;

units.sanskrit: यो यो ह्य् अस्येतः प्रैति न तम् इह दर्शनाय लभते ॥
units.english: for whoever departs from here,him one cannot see again in this world

units.sanskrit: यथोक्तात्मध्यानसाधनानुष्ठानं प्रति साधकानामुत्साहजननार्थमनुक्रोशन्त्याहकष्टमिदं
units.english: For the purpose of encouraging aspirants to adopt the means to accomplish the contemplation of the

units.sanskrit: खलु वर्तते यत्स्वात्मस्थाः शक्यप्राप्या अपि त इमे सत्याः कामा अनृतापिधानास्तेषामात्मस्थानां
units.english: Self as‘described above, the text, would by compassion, saysIt is really a great pity that these ‘True Desires though subsisting in the Self and quite capable of being fulfilled are hidden by the untruth

units.sanskrit: स्वाश्रयाणामेव सतामनृतं बह्यविषयेषु स्त्र्यन्नभोजनाच्छादनादिषु तृष्णा तन्निमित्तं च स्वेच्छाप्रचारत्वं मिथ्याज्ञाननिमित्तत्वादनृतमित्युच्यते । तन्निमित्तं सत्यानां कामानामप्राप्तिरित्यपिधानमिवापिधानम् ।
units.english: Though the ‘Desires’ subsist in the Self and rest in men’s own selves,yet they are ‘hidden’ by the untruth, the term ‘Untrue’stands fora the longing for such external things as women, food, clothes and the rest, and b the consequent freedom of action,these are called ‘untrue’, because they are due to false knowledge, and when the ‘True Desires’ are not fulfilled on account of this false knowledge, this latter acts like a ‘covering’

units.sanskrit: कथमनृतापिधाननिमित्तं तेषामलाभ इति,
units.english: QuestionIn what way is the nonfulfilment of the Desires due to the Covering of the Untrue?

units.sanskrit: उच्यतेयो यो हि यस्मादस्य जन्तोः पुत्रो भ्राता वेष्ट इतो ऽस्माल्लोकात्प्रैति प्रगच्छति म्रियते तमिष्टं पुत्रं भ्रातरं वा स्वहृदयाकाशे विद्यमानमपीह पुनर्दर्शनायेच्छन्नपि न लभते ॥
units.english: AnswerWhoever related to this Man,be it his son, or brother or other loved person,departs from this worlddieshimthe loved one, Son or Brother,one cannot see again in this world,even though he is present in the Ākāśa of one’s own heart and that is because it is hidden by False Knowledge

units.sanskrit: अथ ये चास्येह जीवा ये च प्रेता यच् चान्यद् इच्छन् न लभते सर्वं तद् अत्र गत्वा विन्दते ।
units.english: Now, those of his people who are alive and those who are dead, and whatever else there is which, though desiring, one does not obtain,all this one finds when he goes there

units.sanskrit: अत्र ह्य् अस्यैते सत्याः कामा अनृतापिधानाः ।
units.english: As here are his ‘True Desires hidden by the untrue’

units.sanskrit: तद् यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितम् अक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्य् उपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुः । एवम् एवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहर् अहर् गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्य् अनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
units.english: And just as peoplewho do not know the place walk over the ground and do not know the golden treasure hidden underground,so do all those creatures, though daily going to this BrahmanRegion, know it not; as they are carried away by the untrue

units.sanskrit: अथ पुनर्ये चास्य विदुषो जन्तोर्जीवा जीवन्तीह पुत्रा भ्रात्रादयो वा
units.english: Now those of histhe knowing man’speople who are alive,are living, such as his sons, brothers and others

units.sanskrit: ये च प्रेता मृता इष्टाः संबन्धिनो यच्चान्यदिह लोके वस्त्रान्नपानादि रत्नादि वा वस्त्विच्छन्न
units.english: and those who are dead,friends and relatives,and whatever else there isin the world, in the shape of clothes, food, drink and the like and grams and other such

units.sanskrit: लभते तत्सर्वमत्र हृदयाकाशाख्ये ब्रह्मणि गत्वा यथोक्तेन विधिना विन्दते लभते ।
units.english: thingswhich, though desiring, one does not obtain,all this one finds when he goes there,ie into Brahman called the Ākāśa in the Heart, one finds all this in the manner described above

units.sanskrit: अत्रास्मिन्हार्दाकाशे हि यस्मादस्यैते यथोक्ताः सत्याः कामा वर्तन्ते ऽनतापिधानाः ।
units.english: As here,in this HeartĀkāśa,are all his ‘True Desires hidden by the Untrue’, as described above

units.sanskrit: कथमिव तदन्याय्यमित्युच्यतेतत्तत्र यथा हिरण्यनिधिं हिरण्यमेव पुनर्ग्रहणाय
units.english: But how can this unreasonable thing happen?

units.sanskrit: निधातृभिर्निधीयत इति निधिस्तं हिरण्यनिधिं निहितं भूमेरधस्तान्निक्षिप्तमक्षेत्रज्ञा निधिशास्रैर्निधिक्षेत्रमजानन्तस्ते निधेरुपर्युपरि संचरन्तो ऽपि निधिं न विन्देयुः शक्यवेदनमपि । एवमेवेमा अविद्यवत्यः सर्वा इमाः प्रजा यथोक्तं हृदयाकाशाख्यं ब्रह्मलोकं ब्रह्मैव लोको ब्रह्मलोकस्तमहरहः प्रत्यहं गच्छन्त्यो ऽपि सुषुप्तकाले न विदन्दन्ति न लभन्त एषो ऽहं ब्रह्मलोकभावमापन्नो ऽस्म्यद्येति ।
units.english: AnswerJust as the golden treasuregold buried underground, for future use, by hoarders is called ‘Treasure’this golden treasure under the ground, those people do not know who do not know the place,ie who are unable to discover the land with treasure buried underground, with the half of the Science of Buried Treasures,though they walk over the place, they do not know the treasure, though it can be easily discovered;in the same manner, all these creatureswho are beset with nescience ignorancethough daily going to the BrahmanRegionBrahman itself as the Regionduring deep sleep,know it not,ie they do not realise that ‘ have today become merged in the BrahmanRegion;

units.sanskrit: अनृतेन हि यथोक्तेन हि यस्मात्प्रत्यूढा हृताः स्वरूपादविद्यादिदोषैर्बहिपकृष्टा इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: as they are carried awayled away by the untrue,as described above; that is, they become drawn from their real forms by ignorance and other defects

units.sanskrit: अतः कष्टमिदं वर्तते जन्तूनां यत्स्वायत्तमपि ब्रह्म न लभ्यत इत्यभिप्रायः ॥
units.english: Hence it is that this calamity befalls all creatures that though Brahman is quite within their reach, they do not reach it

units.sanskrit: स वा एष आत्मा हृदि ।
units.english: This Self verily, is in the heart

units.sanskrit: तस्यैतद् एव निरुक्तं हृद्य् अयम् इति तस्माद् धृद् अयम् ।
units.english: Its etymological explanation is thisThis ‘ayam’ is in the heart ‘hṛdi’; hence it is called ‘Hṛdayam’ Hṛdiayam

units.sanskrit: अहर् अहर् वा एवंवित् स्वर्गं लोकम् एति ॥
units.english: One who knows this goes to the Heavenly Region everyday

units.sanskrit: स वै य आत्मापहतपाप्मेति प्रकृतो वैशब्देन तं स्मारयत्येष विवक्षित आत्मा हृदि हृदयपुण्डरीक आकाशशब्देनाभिहितः ।
units.english: This Self,which has been spoken of in the present context as ‘free from evil’, is recalled by the particle ‘vai’ verily;the sense being that this Self, which is going to be described, is in the heart,in the white lotus of the heart,and this same Self has been referred to above by the term ‘Ākāśa’

units.sanskrit: तस्यैतस्य हृदयस्यैतदेव निरुक्तं निर्वचनं नान्यत ।
units.english: The etymological explanation of this, of the Heart ‘Hṛdaya’is this,none other

units.sanskrit: हृद्ययमात्मा वर्तत इति यस्मात् तस्माद्धृदयं हृदयनामनिर्वचनप्रसिद्ध्यापि स्वहृदय आत्मेत्यवगन्तव्यमित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: Because thisSelfexistsin the Heart, therefore it is ‘Hrdayam’, ‘Heart’ What is meant is that, even under the wellknown explanation of the name ‘Hṛdaya’ Heart, the Self should be understood to lie in one’s own Heart

units.sanskrit: अहरहर्वै प्रत्यहमेवंविद्धृद्ययमात्मेति जानन्स्वर्गं लोकं हार्दं ब्रह्मैति प्रतिपद्यते । नन्वनेवंविदपि सुषुप्तकाले हार्दं ब्रह्म प्रतिपद्यत एव सुषुप्तकाले सता सोम्य तदा संपन्न इत्युक्तत्वात् ।
units.english: Every dayday after dayone who knows thiswho knows that the Self is in the Heart,goes to the Heavenly Region,the Brahman in the Heart As a matter of fact, even one who does not have this knowledge reaches the Brahman in the Heart, during deep sleep; as it has been, declared that ‘at that time my dear, he becomes merged in Being

units.sanskrit: बाढमेवं तथाप्यस्ति विशेषः ।
units.english: True, this is so; but there is a difference

units.sanskrit: यथा जानन्नजानंश्च सर्वो जन्तुः सद्ब्रह्मैव तथापि तत्त्वमसीति प्रतिबोधितो विद्वान्सदेव नान्यो ऽस्मीति जानन्सदेव भवति ।
units.english: Whether knowingly or unknowingly, all creatures are really Being, Brahman,yet the man who has been taught that ‘that thou art’ and comes to realise it that ‘ am pure Being, nothing else’, and thence becomes Being itself

units.sanskrit: एवमेव विद्वानविद्वांश्चसुषुप्ते यद्यपि सत्संपद्यते तथाप्येवंविदेव स्वर्गं लोकमेतीत्युच्यते ।
units.english: In the same manner, though the man with knowledge, and the man without knowledge, both attain Being during deep sleep, yet it is only the man with knowledge who goes to the Heavenly Region,as asserted here;

units.sanskrit: देहपाते ऽपि विद्याफलस्यावश्यंभावित्वादित्येष विशेषः ॥
units.english: because, even on the falling off of the body, the reward of knowledge must accrue to him and going to Heaven is that reward, which does not accrue to the man without knowledge; this is the difference

units.sanskrit: अथ य एष संप्रसादो ऽस्माच् छरीरात् समुत्थाय परं ज्योतिर् उपसंपद्य स्वेन रूपेनाभिनिष्पद्यत एष आत्मेति होवाच ।
units.english: Now, this serene and happy Being, after having risen out of this body and having reached the highest light, becomes merged in his own true form; that is the Self,he said

units.sanskrit: एतद् अमृतम् अभयम् एतद् ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: This is the Immortal and the Fearless, this is Brahman;

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा एतस्य ब्रह्मणो नाम सत्यम् इति ॥
units.english: and the name of his Brahman is ‘Satya’ the True

units.sanskrit: सुषुप्तकाले स्वेना'मना सता संपन्नः सन्सम्यक्प्रसीदतीति जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोर्विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगजातं कालुष्यं जहातीति संप्रसादशब्दो यद्यपि सर्वजन्तूनां साधारणस्तथाप्येवंवित्स्वर्गं लोकमेतीति प्रकृतत्वादेष संप्रसाद इति संनिहितवद्यत्नविशेषात्सो ऽथेदं शरीरं
units.english: During deep sleep, the Man, merged into Being, his Self, becomes serene and happy,ie he shakes off the impurity born, during the waking and dream states, of contacṭ of objects with senseorgans though the term ‘serene and happy Being’ is applicable to all creatures,yet, inasmuch as the subjectmatter of the context is one who has been spoken of as ‘one who knows this goes to the Heavenly Region,’it is this person who is spoken of here as this serene and happy Being’, because of the special stress that is laid upon the term ‘this’

units.sanskrit: हित्वास्माच्छरीरात्समुत्थाय शरीरात्मभावनां परित्यज्येत्यर्थः । न त्वासनादिव समुत्थायेतीह युक्तम् ।
units.english: Now, this serene and happy Being, on renouncing the body and having risen out of the body,ie giving up the notion that the Body is the Self,the term ‘rising’ cannot be taken in the ordinary sense of rising from a seat for instance;

units.sanskrit: स्वेन रूपेणेति विशेषणात् । न ह्यन्यत उत्थाय स्वरूपं संपत्तव्यम् ।
units.english: because the text speaks of ‘his own form’, one’s ‘own form’ is not to be attained by rising out of something else;

units.sanskrit: स्वरूपमेव हि तन्न भवति प्रतिपत्तव्यं चेत्स्यात् । परं परमात्मलक्षणं विज्ञप्तिस्वभावं ज्योतिरुपसंपद्य स्वास्थ्यमुपगम्येत्येतत् ।
units.english: in fact, it would not be ‘his own form’ if it had to be reached;having reached the Highest Light,in the form of the Supreme Self, of the nature of pure consciousness that is, having realised his real nature;becomes merged in his own true form

units.sanskrit: स्वेन आत्मीयेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यते प्रागेतस्याः स्वरूपसंपत्तेरविद्यया देहमेवापरं रूपमात्मत्वेनोपगत इति तदपेक्षयेदमुच्यते स्वेन रूपेणेति अशरीरता ह्यात्मनः स्वरूपं यत्स्वं परं ज्योतिःस्वरूपमापद्ये संप्रसाद एष आत्मेति होवाच ।
units.english: Before this mergence into his true form, the man, under the in fluence of ignorance, regarded the body itself as his highest form; and it is in comparison with that position that the present is spoken of as ‘his own form’ in fact, ‘being with a body’ is the ‘own form’ of the Self That Highest Light which is the ‘own form’ reached by the serene and happy Being,is the Self,he said

units.sanskrit: स ब्रूयादिति यः श्रुत्या नियुक्तो ऽन्तेवासिभ्यः ।
units.english: The person referred to here as ‘he’ is the Teacher who has been advised by the Veda above as ‘he should say’ to the disciples under

units.sanskrit: किञ्चैतदमृतमविनाशि भूमा यो वै भूमा तदमृतमित्युक्तम् । अत एवाभयं भूम्नो द्वितीयाभावादत एतद्ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: Further, this is the Immortal,imperishable, Infinite; as has been declared above ‘that which is Infinite is immortal’;and because it is immortal, it is Fearless;

units.sanskrit: तस्य ह वा एतस्य ब्रह्मणो नामाभिधानम् ।
units.english: because the infinite has no secondhence this is Brahman;and the name of this Brahman is ‘Satya’ True

units.sanskrit: किं तत्सत्यमिति । सत्यं ह्यवितथं ब्रह्म ।
units.english: What is True? True is that which is never unreal, and Brahman alone is this;

units.sanskrit: तत्सत्यं स आत्मेति ह्युक्तम् । अथ किमर्थमिदं नाम पुनरुच्यते । तदुपासनविधिस्तुत्यर्थम् ॥
units.english: as asserted abovethat is the true, that is the Self’,Why is this name of Brahman mentioned here?For the purpose of eulogising rṇethod of meditating upon it

units.sanskrit: तानि ह वा एतानि त्रीण्यक्षराणि सतीयमिति तद्यत्सत्त्दमृतमथ यत्ति तन्मर्त्यमथ
units.english: These are the three letters‘Sa ’, ‘ti’ and ‘yam’; the ‘sat’ is the immortal,the ‘ti’ is the mortal,and ‘yam’ for that whereby one joins both;

units.sanskrit: यद्यं तेनोभे यच्छति यदनेनोभे यच्छति तस्माद्यमहरहर्वा एवंवित्स्वर्गं लोकमेति ॥
units.english: because by it one joins both, therefore it is ‘yam’one who knows this daily goes to the HeavenlyRegion

units.sanskrit: तानि ह वा एतानि ब्रह्मणो नामाक्षराणि त्रीण्येतानि सतीयामति सकारस्तकारो यमिति च ।
units.english: These are the three lettersin the name of Brahman ‘sa’ ‘ti’ ‘yam’ ie the letter ‘sa’, the letter ‘ta’ and the syllable ‘yam’;

units.sanskrit: तकार ईकारः उच्चारणार्थो ऽनुबन्धः ।
units.english: as a matter of fact, the ‘t’ in ‘sat’ and the ‘i’ in ‘ti’ have been inserted only for the purposes of pronunciation;

units.sanskrit: ह्रस्वेनैवाक्षरेण पुनः प्रतिनिर्देशात्तेषाम् ।
units.english: because these are again spoken of by the short syllable themselves

units.sanskrit: तत्तत्र यत्सत्सकारस्तदमृतं सद्ब्रह्मामृतवाचकत्वादमृत एव सकारस्तकारन्तो निर्दिष्टः ।
units.english: That which is ‘sat’,ie the letter ‘sa’,is the Immortal;it is immortal, because it denotes the Immortal in BeingBrahman;

units.sanskrit: अथ यद्यमक्षरं तेनाक्षरेणामृतमर्त्याख्ये पूर्वे उभे ऽक्षरे यच्छति यमयति नियमयति वशीकरोत्यात्मन इत्यर्थः । यद्यस्मादनेन यमित्येतेनोभे यच्छति तस्माद्याम् ।
units.english: that is why the ‘sa’ has been mentioned along with ‘t’;that which is ‘ti’ that is, the letter ‘ta’ is the mortal;and that which is ‘yam’,by that letter one joins both,that what were two, mortal and immortal, is joined and combined one, the Imperishable,one joins these, controls thembrings under one’s own control

units.sanskrit: संयते इव ह्येतेन यमा लक्ष्येते ।
units.english: Because by it one joins both, therefore it is ‘yam’;

units.sanskrit: ब्रङ्मनामाक्षरस्यापीदममृतत्वादिधर्मवत्त्वं महाभाग्यं किमुत नामवत इत्युपास्यत्वाय स्तूयते ।
units.english: That the letters composing the name of Brahman are themselves endowed with such character as immortality and the like,is in itself a sign of great fortune;what to say of Him who bears that name?such is the praise sought to be bestowed upon the object of meditation

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्मनामनिर्वचनेनैव नामवतो वेत्तैवंवित् । अहरहर्वा एवंवित्स्वर्गं लोकमेतीत्युक्तार्थम् ॥
units.english: One who knows thisie who knows Brahman, the bearer of the name, through the said explanation of the name,daily goes to the Heavenly Region; as already explained before
