units.english: so that the deficiency of understanding, in the case of Indra, being small,inasmuch as he took the term ‘Seen’ as used by Prajāpati in the sentence ‘the Person seen in the Eye is the Self’, in its direct sense, and as what is actually seen in the Eye is the Reflection he took the teaching to mean that the Reflection in the Eye was the Self;while the other, Virocana, rejected the direct meaning of the term seen’ and took it in its indirect sense, as standing for the source of the Reflection seenin the form of the Body, and understood Prajāpati’s words to mean that ‘the Body is the Self’;

units.sanskrit: ऽयमिति दोषभूयस्त्वात् ।
units.english: and this misunderstanding was due to the deficiencies in his understanding being much larger than in that of Indra

units.sanskrit: यथा किल नीलानीलयोरादर्शे दृश्यमानयोर्वाससोर्यन्नीलं तन्महार्हमिति च्छायानिमित्तं वास एवोच्यते न च्छाया तद्वदिति विरोचनाभिप्रायः स्वचित्तगुणदोषवशादेव हि शब्दार्थावधारणं तुल्ये ऽपि श्रवणे ख्यापितं दाम्यत दत्त दयध्वमिति दकारमात्रश्रवणाच्छुत्यन्तरे ।
units.english: The idea in Virocana’s mind was somewhat like this‘when two pieces of clothone blue and the other notblueare seen reflected in the mirror, they say on looking at the reflected images that the one that is blue is costly, where what is meant to be ‘costly’ is the cloth, and not the reflection so when Prajāpati spoke of the reflection in the Eyes, He must have meant the Body that is reflected and not the reflection’ In all cases, people understand the meanings of the words and expressions in accordance with the efficiency or deficiency of their own minds,though the words used are exactly the same;this has been exemplified in, another Vedic text where various meaningssuch as ‘Dāmyata’, ‘be selfcontrolled’, ‘Datta’, ‘make gifts’, and Dayadhvaṃ ‘be merciful’ have been spoken of as understood from the single letter ‘da’Bṛhadā

units.sanskrit: निमित्तान्यपि तदनुगुणान्येव सहकारीणि भवन्ति ॥
units.english: ii Other accessory auxiliaries also come to function exactly in keeping with the particular man’s understanding

units.sanskrit: एतं त्व् एव ते भूयो ऽनुव्याख्यास्यामि ।
units.english: ‘So it is, O Indra’He said,‘ shall explain this to you again;

units.sanskrit: स हापराणि द्वात्रिंशतं वर्षाण्युवास ।
units.english: dwell here for another thirtytwo years’He dwelt there for another thirtytwo years;

units.sanskrit: तस्मै होवाच ॥
units.english: then Prajāpati said to him as follows

units.sanskrit: एवमेवैष मघवन्सम्यक्त्वयावगतं न च्छायात्मेत्युवाच प्रजापतिर्यो मयोक्त आत्मा प्रकृत एतमेवा'त्मानं तु ते भूयः पूर्वं
units.english: Prajāpati said‘So it is, O Indra,you have understood it rightly that the Reflection is not that Self which is the subjectmatter of our study ThisSelfI shall explain to you again, though had explained it before

units.sanskrit: व्याख्यातमप्यनुव्याख्यास्यामि ।
units.english: shall explain it again

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्सकृद्व्याख्यातं दोषरहितानामवधारणविषयं प्राप्तमपि नाग्रहीरतः केनचिद्दोषेण प्रतिबद्धग्रहणसामर्थस्त्वमतस्तत्क्षपणाय वसापराणि द्वात्रिंशतं वर्षाणीत्युक्त्वा तथोषितवते क्षपितदोषाय तस्मै होवाच ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य नवमः खण्डः
units.english: Even though what explained was quite intelligible to all persons free from all defects,yet you did not understand it;from which it follows that your powers of comprehension have been obstructed by some defects;hence for the removal of that defect, Dwell here for another thirtytwo years, as a religious student’ and after Indra had dwelt as a Religious student for another thirtytwo years,and hence got rid of his defect,Prajāpati said to him as follows End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: य एष स्वप्ने महीयमानश् चरत्य् एष आत्मेति होवाच ।
units.english: ‘He who moves about worshipped, in dreams,that is the Self’;

units.sanskrit: एतद् अमृतम् अभयम् एतद् ब्रह्मेति । स ह शान्तहृदयः प्रवव्राज ।
units.english: and he said‘this is the Immortal and the Fearless, this is Brahman’He went away, satisfied in his heart

units.sanskrit: स हाप्राप्यैव देवान् एतद् भयं ददर्श । तद् यद्य् अपीदं शरीरम् अन्धं भवत्य् अनन्धः स भवति यदि स्रामम् अस्रामः । नैवैषो ऽस्य दोषेण दुष्यति ॥
units.english: But therefore he got at the Devas, he saw this difficulty‘though this is not blind when the body is blind, nor oneeyed when the Body is oneeyed, nor is it affected by the defect of the body,yet etc, etc, continued in the next text

units.sanskrit: य आत्मापहतपाप्मादिलक्षणो य एषो ऽक्षिणीत्यादिना व्याख्यात एष सः । को ऽसौ । यः स्वप्ने महीयमानः स्त्र्यादिभिः पूज्यमानश्चरत्यनेकविधान्स्वप्नभोगाननुभवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: ‘The Self, marked by such characters as freedom from evil and the rest, which has been explained before as ‘the Person in the Eye’,this is that Self;what? He who moves about in dreams, worshippedattended upon by women and other;that is, goes on enjoying many dreamsexperiences,this is the Self’he said etc etc

units.sanskrit: एष आत्मेति होवाचेत्यादि समानम् ।
units.english: as before

units.sanskrit: स हैवमुक्त इन्द्रः शान्तहृदयः प्रवव्राज । स हाप्राप्यैव देवान्पूर्ववदस्मिन्नप्यात्मनि भयं ददर्श ।
units.english: Having heard this, Indra went away, satisfied in his heart;but before he got at the Devas, he saw,as beforethe difficultyin this view of Self also

units.sanskrit: कथम् । तदिदं शरीरं यद्यप्यन्धं धवति स्वप्नात्मा यो ऽनन्धः स भवति । यदि स्राममिदं शरीरमस्रामश्च स भवति नैवैष स्वप्नात्मास्य देहस्य दोषेण दुष्यति ॥
units.english: How?Though when this Body is blind, yet the DreamSelf remains unblind, when the Body is oneeyed, the DreamSelf is not oneeyed,hor does this DreamSelf become affected by the defect of the body,yet etc

units.sanskrit: स होवाच ।
units.english: next text

units.sanskrit: नैवैषो ऽस्य दोषेण दुष्यति ॥ न वधेनास्य हन्यते । नास्य स्राम्येण स्रामः । घ्नन्ति त्व् इवैनम् । विच्छादयन्तीव ।
units.english: ‘Nor is It killed by the killing of the Body, nor does It become oneeyed when the body is oneeyed,yet, they kill It, as it were,chase It, as it were,It becomes conscious of pain, as it were,and weeps as it were; do not see any good in this’

units.sanskrit: अपि रोदितीव ।
units.english: With fuel in his hand, he came back again

units.sanskrit: एवम् एवैष मघवन्न् इति होवाच ।
units.english: Prajāpati said to him‘Indra, you went away satisfied in your heart;

units.sanskrit: एतं त्व् एव ते भूयो ऽनुव्याख्यास्यामि । वसापराणि द्वात्रिंशतं वर्षाणीति ।
units.english: for what purpose do you come again?’He said‘Though This is not blind when the Body is blind, nor oneEyed when the Body is oneeyed, nor is It affected by the defects of the body’

units.sanskrit: स हापराणि द्वात्रिंशतं वर्षाण्युवास ।
units.english: dwell here for another thirtytwo years’ He dwelt there for another thirtytwo years

units.sanskrit: तस्मै होवाच ॥
units.english: Then he said to him

units.sanskrit: नाप्यस्य वधेन स हन्यते छायात्मवन्न चास्य स्राम्येण स्रामः स्वप्नात्मा भवति । यदध्यायादावागममात्रेणोपन्यस्तं नास्य जरयैतज्जीर्यतीत्यादि तदिह न्यायेनोपपादयितुमुपन्यस्तम् ।
units.english: Nor is the DreamSelf killed by the killing of the Body,like the ReflectionSelf; nor does It become oneeyed when the body is oneeyed;it was asserted in the beginning of this discourse , on the strength of the scriptures alone,that ‘the Self does not become decrepit by the decrepitude of the body’;

units.sanskrit: न तावदयं छायात्मवद्देहदोषयुक्तः किन्तु ध्नन्ति त्वेवैनम् । एवशब्द इवार्थे ।
units.english: It is true that this DreamSelf is not beset with the defects of the body; but they kill It, as it were;the particle ‘eva’ stands for ‘iva’, ‘as it were’;

units.sanskrit: घ्नन्तीवैनं केचनेति द्रष्टव्यम् ।
units.english: the sense being that ‘some people kill It, as it were’;

units.sanskrit: प्रजापतिं प्रमाणीकुर्वतो ऽनृतवादित्वापादनानुपपत्तेः । एतदमृतमित्येतत्प्रजापतिवचनं कथं मृषा कुर्यादिन्द्रस्तं प्रमाणीकुर्वन् । ननु च्छायापुरुषे प्रजापतिनोक्ते ऽस्य शरीरस्य नाशमन्वेष नश्यतीति दोषमभ्यधात्तथेहापि स्यात् ।
units.english: as the speaker relies upon the authority of Prajāpati, it would not be right for him to make an assertion that would indicate that what Prajāpati has said regarding Its not being killed is not true When Indra was relying upon the authority of Prajāpati, how could he falsify His statement to the effect that ‘It is immortal’? In reference to the ReflectionSelf spoken of by Prajāpati, it has been pointed out as a defect that ‘it perishes when the Body perishes’;

units.sanskrit: नैवम् ।
units.english: Not so

units.sanskrit: कस्मात् ।
units.english: Why not?

units.sanskrit: य एषो ऽक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यत इति मन्यते तदा कथं प्रजापतिं प्रमाणीकृत्य पुनः श्रवणाय समित्पाणिर्गच्छेत् ।
units.english: If Indra had thought that on being questioned regarding the qualities of being free from evil and the like, Prajāpati has mentioned the ReflectionSelf,then how could he still rely upon the authority of Prajāpati and return to him, with fuel in his hands, to learn more from him

units.sanskrit: जगाम च ।
units.english: And yet he did return to Him

units.sanskrit: तस्मान्न च्छायात्मा प्रजापतिनोक्त इति मन्यते । तथा च व्याख्यातं द्रष्टाक्षिणि दृश्यत इति ।
units.english: From which it follows that what Indra thinks is that ‘it was not the ReflectionSelf that was spoken of by Prajāpati’ It was for this reason that the explanation was given that ‘it is the Seer that is seen in the Eye’

units.sanskrit: तथा विच्छादयन्तीव विद्रावयन्तीव तथा च पुत्रादिमरणनिमित्तमप्रियवेत्तेव भवति ।
units.english: Similarly, they chase it as it were,theymake it run away and about And it becomes conscious of pain,due to the death of the son pr other relatives

units.sanskrit: अपि च स्वयमपि रोदितीव ।
units.english: Further It itself weeps, as it were

units.sanskrit: नन्वप्रियं वेत्त्येव कथं वेत्तेवेति । उच्यतेन अमृताभयत्ववचनानुपपत्तेः ।
units.english: As a matter of fact, It does really feel the pain; why then should it be said that ‘It becomes conscious of pain, as it were?’

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रत्यक्षविरोध इति चेत् । न । शरीरात्मत्वप्रत्यक्षवद्भ्रान्तिसंभवात् ।
units.english: It is not as you think; as this would not be compatible with the assertion that ‘It is immortal and fearless’;

units.sanskrit: तिष्ठतु तावदप्रियवेत्तेव न वेति ।
units.english: But as it stands, it is contrary to what is actually seen No;

units.sanskrit: नाहमत्र भोग्यं पश्यामि ।
units.english: ‘ do not see any good in this’said Indra;

units.sanskrit: स्वप्नात्मज्ञाने ऽपीष्टं फलं नोपलभ इत्यभिप्रायः एवमेवैष तवाभिप्रायेणेति वाक्यसेषः । आत्मनो ऽमृताभयगुणवत्त्वस्याभिप्रेतत्वात् ।
units.english: Prajāpati said ‘So it is’ie ‘according to your idea of the thing’this is to be understood, at the end of the sentence because what is meant is that the Self is qualified by Freedom from Evil and Fearlessness

units.sanskrit: द्विरुक्तमपि न्यायतो मया यथावन्नावधारयति ।
units.english: Thinking that ‘though have explained the matter to him twice in accordance with reason, yet he does not yet understand it as it should be;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्पूर्ववदस्याद्यापि प्रतिबन्धकारणमस्तीति मन्वानस्तत्क्षपणाय वसापराणि द्वात्रिंशतं वर्षाणि ब्रह्मचर्यमित्यादिदेश प्रजापतिः । तथोषितवते क्षपितकल्मषाया'ह ॥ इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य दशमः खण्डः
units.english: so it seems that even now, as before, there is something that is obstructing his understanding hence, for the purpose of removing that obstruction, He instructed Indra to ‘dwell for anthor thirtytwo years’, as a religious student After he had dwelt for another thirtytwo years and had his deficiencies removed, Prajāpati said to him as follows End of Section 0 of Discourse

units.sanskrit: तद् यत्रैतत् सुप्तः समस्तः संप्रसन्नः स्वप्नं न विजानात्येष आत्मेति होवाच । एतद् अमृतम् अभयम् एतद् ब्रह्मेति ।
units.english: ‘That which is fully asleep, at perfect rest, and knows no dreams,that is the Self’,he said,‘that is the Immortal and Fearless, that is Brahman’

units.sanskrit: स ह शान्तहृदयः प्रवव्राज ।
units.english: He went away, satisfied in his heart

units.sanskrit: स हाप्राप्यैव देवान् एतद् भयं ददर्श । नाह खल्व् अयम् एवं संप्रत्य् आत्मानं जानात्य् अयम् अहम् अस्मीति । नो एवेमानि भूतानि ।
units.english: But before he got at the Devas, he saw this difficulty ‘In truth, he does not know the Self at the time as this is , nor does he know these things

units.sanskrit: विनाशम् एवापीतो भवति ।
units.english: It seems as if he had undergone annihilation

units.sanskrit: नाहम् अत्र भोग्यं पश्यामीति ॥
units.english: see no good in this’

units.sanskrit: स समित्पाणिः पुनर् एयाय ।
units.english: With fuel in his hands, he came again

units.sanskrit: तं ह प्रजापतिर् उवाच मघवन् यच् छान्तहृदयः प्राव्राजीः किम् इच्छन् पुनर् आगम इति । स होवाच नाह खल्व् अयं भगव एवं संप्रत्य् आत्मानं जानात्य् अयम् अहम् अस्मीति । नो एवेमानि भूतानि ।
units.english: Prajāpati said to him‘Indra, you went away satisfied in your heart; for what purpose are you coming again?’He said‘Revered sir, he does not know the Self at the time as this is ,nor does he know these things;

units.sanskrit: विनाशम् एवापीतो भवति ।
units.english: it seems as if he had undergone annihilation

units.sanskrit: नाहम् अत्र भोग्यं पश्यामीति ॥
units.english: see no good in this’

units.sanskrit: पूर्ववदेतं त्वेव त इत्याद्युक्त्वा तद्यत्रैतत्सुप्त इत्यदि व्याख्यातं वाक्यम् ।
units.english: As before, having said‘Etaṃ tveva’ etc, ‘this indeed shall explain further’, he has said ‘that which is fully asleep etc,’a passage that has been already explained

units.sanskrit: अक्षिणि यो द्रष्टा स्वप्ने च महीयमानश्चरति स एष सुप्तः समस्तः संप्रसन्नः स्वप्नं न विजानात्येष आत्मेति होवाचैतदमृतमभयमेतद्ब्रह्मेति
units.english: ‘The Seer seen in the Eye’‘Who moves about, worshipped in dream’,‘that which is full asleep’, ‘at perfect rest and knows no dreams’,‘that is the Self the Immortal and Fearless;

units.sanskrit: अयमहमस्मीति नो एवेमानि भूतानि चेति ।
units.english: this is Brahmanall this that He said was fully as he meant it

units.sanskrit: अतो विनाशमेव विनाशमिवेति पूर्ववद्द्रष्टव्यम् । अपीतो ऽपिगतो भवति, विनष्ट इव भवतीत्यभिप्रायः । ज्ञाने हि सति ज्ञातुः सद्भावो ऽवगम्यते नासति ज्ञाने । न च सुषुप्तस्य ज्ञानं दृश्यते ऽतो विनष्ट इवेत्यभिप्रायः न तु विनाशमेवा'त्मनो मन्यते ऽमृताभयवचनस्य प्रामाण्यमिच्छन् ॥
units.english: But Indra saw a difficulty in this alsoHow?‘In truth, hethe Selfdoes not, while in deep sleepknow the Self;he does not know It at all;as what?as ‘this is ’;nor does he know these kings,as he does in the waking or the dreaming state;it seems as if he had undergone annihilation,‘as if’ has to be understood as before;‘undergone’gone to‘annihilationappears as if ie annihilated;that is to say, it is only when the cognition is there and the existence of the Cogniser’ Self can be understood,not when the cognition itself is not there;and when the man is in deep sleep, he is not found to have any cognitions;hence, it follows that the cogniser has become annihilated this is what is meant, and it is not meant that Indra regards the man as to have become really annihilated,at least so long as he believes in the truth of the assertion of his ‘immortality and fearlessness’

units.sanskrit: एवम् एवैष मघवन्न् इति होवाच । एतं त्व् एव ते भूयो ऽनुव्याख्यास्यामि ।
units.english: ‘So it is indeed, O Indra’,said he‘this shall explain to you further;

units.sanskrit: नो एवान्यत्रैतस्मात् ।
units.english: but none other than That;

units.sanskrit: स हापराणि पञ्च वर्षाण्युवास ।
units.english: dwell here for another five years’He dwelt there for another five years;

units.sanskrit: एतत् तद् यद् आहुः । एकशतं ह वै वर्षाणि मघवान् प्रजापतौ ब्रह्मचर्यम् उवास ।
units.english: with regard to íwhich they say ‘for a hundred and one years did Indra dwell as a Religious Student, with Prajāpati’

units.sanskrit: तस्मै होवाच ॥
units.english: He said to him

units.sanskrit: पूर्ववदेवमेवेत्युक्त्वा यो मयोक्तस्रिभिः पर्यायैस्तमेवैतं नो एवान्यत्रैतस्मादात्मनो ऽन्यं कञ्चन किं तर्ह्येतमेव व्याख्यास्यामि स्वल्पस्तु दोषस्तवावशिष्टस्तत्क्षपणाय वसापराण्यन्यानि पञ्च वर्षाणीत्युक्तः स तथा चकार ।
units.english: As before, Prajāpati said, ‘So it is’; wha have explained by means of three practically synonymous expressions,That and none other than That, Selfnot anything elsebut That aloneI shall explain further;only some little defect is left in you, for the removal of which, dwell here for another five years’Having been thus advised, he did as he was told

units.sanskrit: तस्मै मृदितकषायादिदोषाय स्थानत्रयदोषसंबन्धरहितमात्मनःस्वरूपमपहतपाप्मत्वादिलक्षणं मघवते तस्मै होवाच । तान्येकशतं वर्षाणि संपेदुः संपन्नानि बभूवुः ।
units.english: Therefore, when all his impurities and other defects had been completely washed off, Prajāpati explained to Indra the real nature of the Self, as free from the defects due to contact with three states of waking, dreaming and deep sleep, and characterised by freedom from evil and other characteristicsThese thus came to be a hundred and one yearsfully completed;

units.sanskrit: यदाहुर्लोके शिष्टा एकशतं ह वै वर्षाणि मघवान्प्रजापतौ ब्रह्मचर्यमुवासेति तदेतद्द्वात्रिंशतमित्यादिना दर्शितमित्याख्यायिकातो ऽपसृत्य श्रुत्योच्यते ।
units.english: in regard to which cultured people say ‘for a hundred and one years did Indra dwell as a Religious Student with Prajāpati’ This is what has been made up by the mention of ‘thirtytwo’ three times,this is a side remark made by the text, apart from the anecdote relating to VirocanaIndraPrajāpati

units.sanskrit: एवं किलैतदिन्द्रत्वादपि गुरुतरमिन्द्रेणापि महता यत्नेनैकोत्तरवर्षशतकृतायासेन प्राप्तमात्मज्ञानमतो नातः परं पुरुषार्थान्तरमस्तीत्यात्मज्ञानं
units.english: What is done by all this is to eulogise the knowledge of Self as that than which nothing is higher,and which is higher than the position of Indra himself,so much so that the said knowledge was acquired by him with such great effort and trouble extending over a hundred and one years

units.sanskrit: स्तौति ॥
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: मघवन् मर्त्यं वा इदं शरीरम् आत्तं मृत्युना । तद् अस्यामृतस्याशरीरस्यात्मनो ऽधिष्ठानम् ।
units.english: ‘Indra, mortal is this body, held by Death;it is the abode of that Immortal unbodied Self;the bodied one is held by Pleasure and Pain;

units.sanskrit: न वै सशरीरस्य सतः प्रियाप्रिययोर् अपहतिर् अस्ति । अशरीरं वाव सन्तं न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशतः ॥
units.english: for the bodied Being, there is no getting rid of pleasure and pain;but pleasure and pain do not, indeed, touch the unbodied Being’

units.sanskrit: मघवन्मर्त्यं वै मरणधर्मीदं शरीरम् ।
units.english: ‘O Indra, this body is mortal,liable to die

units.sanskrit: यन्मन्यसे ऽक्ष्याधारादिलक्षणः संप्रसादलक्षण आत्मा मयोक्तो विनाशमेवापीतो भवतीति । शृणु तत्र कारणम् । यदिदं शरीरं वै तदेतन्मर्त्यं विनाशि । तच्चा'त्तं मृत्युना ग्रस्तं सततमेव ।
units.english: You think that the Self, which has been expounded by me as contained in the eye, and as marked by restful sleep,becomes annihilated;now listen to the cause of all this ‘This body, that you see, is mortalperishable;it is heldseizedby deathconstantly’ If the term ‘mortal’ meant only ‘liable to die at some time’, then the fear of death would not have been so great as it is when it is said that ‘the Body is held constantly’,pervaded through and throughby death;

units.sanskrit: कदाचिदेव म्रियत इति मर्त्यमित्युक्ते न तथा संत्रासो भवति यथा ग्रस्तमेव सदा व्याप्तमेव मृत्युनेत्युक्त इति वैराग्यार्थं विशेष इत्युच्यत
units.english: hence, for this purpose of creating a feeling of disgust for the body, the particular expression has been used ‘is held by death’

units.sanskrit: आत्तं मृत्युनेति । कथं नाम देहाभिमानतो विरक्तः सन्निवर्तत इति ।
units.english: How is this? When one has become disgusted with the idea of the Body being his Self, he turns back upon regrets that idea

units.sanskrit: शरीरमित्यत्र सहेन्द्रियमनोभिरुच्यते । तच्छरीरमस्य संप्रसादस्य त्रिस्थानतया गम्यमानस्यामृतस्य मरणादिदेहन्द्रियमनोधर्मवर्जितस्येत्येतत् ।
units.english: The ‘body’ here stands for the Body along with the senseorgans, the Mind and the Intellect;this Body is the abode of the Being in restful sleep, who is cognised in these states of waking, dream and deep sleep, the Immortal,free from Death and other qualities besetting the Body, the senseorgans and the Mind

units.sanskrit: अमृतस्येत्यनेनैवाशरीरत्वे सिद्धे पुनरशरीरस्येति वचनं वाय्वादिवत्सावयवत्वमूर्तिमत्त्वे मा भूतामित्यात्मनः ।
units.english: The term ‘Immortal’ itself connoting bodilessness, the reiteration of the same by the additional term ‘unbodied’ is meant to precluding the notion that ‘like Air and other things, the Self is made up of parts and has a material shape;this Body is the abodesubstratum of experiences of the Self;

units.sanskrit: आत्मनो वा सत ईक्षितुस्तेजोबन्नादिक्रमेणोत्पन्नमधिष्ठानम् । जीवरूपेण प्रविश्य सदेवाधितिष्ठत्यस्मिन्निति वाधिष्ठानम् ।
units.english: or it is the abode of the perceiving Living Self when he comes to be born, through fire, water, and the rest in that order;or the body may be regarded as the ‘abode’ of the Being, on the ground that the Being, in the form of the Living Self ‘abides’ in it

units.sanskrit: यस्येदमीदृशं नित्यमेव मृत्युग्रस्तं धर्माधर्मजनितत्वात्प्रियाप्रियवदधिष्ठानं तदधिष्ठितस्तद्वान्सशरीरो भवति ।
units.english: When the Self has for his abode such a Body, which is constantly held by Death, and beset with pleasure and pain brought about by Merit and Demerit,then, abiding in such a body, he becomes ‘bodied’

units.sanskrit: अशरीरस्वभावस्या'त्मनस्तदेवाहं शरीरं शरीरमेव चाहमित्यविवेकादात्मभावः सशरीरत्वं अत एव सशरीरः सन्नात्तो ग्रस्तः प्रियाप्रियाभ्याम्
units.english: Though in his own nature, the Self is unbodied, yet he comes to have such notions as ‘ am the Bodyand the Body is myself’, on account of his not understanding his real nature; and this is what is meant by his becoming bodied;hence having thus become bodied,he becomes held by Pleasure and Pain

units.sanskrit: तस्य च न वै सशरीरस्य सतः प्रियाप्रिययोर्बाह्यविषयसंयोगवियोगनिमित्तयोर्बाह्यविषयसंयोगवियोगौ ममेति मन्यमानस्यापहतिर्विनाश उच्छेदः सन्ततिरूपयोर्नास्तीति ।
units.english: This is a wellknown fact,for this bodied Being, there is no getting rid ofdestruction, removal,of Pleasure and Pain,caused respectively by the connection and disconnection of external thingsand appearing in a continuous series,which connection and disconnection he regards as his own

units.sanskrit: तं पुनर्देहाभिमानादशरीरस्वरूपविज्ञानेन विनर्तिताविवेकज्ञानशरीरं सन्तं प्रियाप्रिये न स्पृशतः ।
units.english: The same Being however, when, his ignorance in the shape of his notion of the Body being the Self has been set aside by his knowledge of his real unbodied nature,then Pleasure and Pain do not touch him;the verb ‘touch’ is to be construed with both ‘pleasure and pain’;

units.sanskrit: स्पृशिः प्रत्येकं संबध्यत इति प्रियं न स्पृशत्यप्रियं न स्पृशतीति वाक्यद्वयं भवति । न म्लेच्छाशुच्यधार्मिकैः सह संभाषेतेति यद्वत् ।
units.english: so that there are two sentences‘Pleasure does not touch him’ and ‘Pain does not touch him’;such construction being like that in the sentence ‘na mlecchāśucyadhārmikaiḥ saha sambhāṣeta’ one should not converse with the mlecha foreignerthe uncleanand the unrighteous

units.sanskrit: धर्माधर्मकार्ये हि ते । अशरीरता तु स्वरूपमिति तत्र धर्माधर्मयोरसंभवात्तत्कार्यभावो दूरत एवेत्यतो न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशतः ।
units.english: The reason for this absence of Pleasure and Pain lies in the fact that Pleasure and Pain are the effects of merit and demerit,while the real nature of the Self is being unbodied,so that merit and demerit being impossible in this latter, the appearance of their effect is still further off;

units.sanskrit: ननु यदि प्रियमप्यशरीरं न स्पृशतीति यन्मघवतोक्तं सुषुप्तस्थो विनाशमेवापीतो भवतीति तदेवेहाप्यापन्नम् ।
units.english: If Pleasure also does not touch the unbodied Self, then it comes to what Indra suspected that ‘during deep sleep, he becomes annihilated’

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः धर्माधर्मकार्ययोः शरीरसंबन्धिनोः प्रियाप्रिययोः प्रतिषेधस्य विवक्षितत्वात् अशरीरं न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशत इति । आगमापायिनोर्हि स्पर्शशब्दो दृष्टो यथा शीतस्पर्श उष्णस्पर्श इति न त्वग्नेरुष्णप्रकाशयोः
units.english: This does not affect our position; what is meant here is the denial of such Pleasure and Pain as are the effects of Merit and Demerit, connected with the Body;this is clear from the statement that ‘Pleasure and Pain do not touch the unbodied Being’ As a matter of fact, the term ‘touch’ has been found to be used in connection with what is liable to appear and disappearsuch as ‘the cold touch’, ‘the warm touch’;

units.sanskrit: स्वभावभूतयोरग्निना स्पर्श इति भवति तथाग्नेः सवितुर्वोष्णप्रकाशवत्स्वरूपभूतस्या'नन्दस्य
units.english: this term ‘touch’ is not used in connection with what forms the very nature of things,in such as the Heat and Brightness of Fire, which form its very nature,which are not spoken of as ‘Touch of fire’;

units.sanskrit: प्रियस्यापि नेह प्रतिषेधःविज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्मआनन्दो ब्रह्मैत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः । इहापि भूमैव सुखमित्युक्तत्वात् ।
units.english: because that bliss is the very nature of the Self has been taught in many Vedic textssuch as Brahman is Consciousness, Bliss’ Bṛhadā ix ,and ‘Brahman is Bliss’ Taitti

units.sanskrit: ननु भूम्नः प्रियस्यैकत्वे ऽसंवेद्यत्वात्स्वरूपेण वा नित्यसंवेद्यत्वान्निर्विशेषतेति नेन्द्रस्य तदिष्टम् ।
units.english: ObjectionIf the Infinite and the Bliss Pleasure be oneand the same, then the latter would be either uncognisable; or it would by its very nature, be constantly cognised; so that there would be no difference between the two;

units.sanskrit: नाह खल्वयं संप्रत्यात्मानं जानात्ययमहमस्मीति नो एवोमानि भूतानि विनाशमेवापीतो भवति नाहमत्र भोग्यं पश्यामिइत्युक्तत्वात् । तद्धोन्द्रस्येष्टं यद्भतानि चा'त्मानं च जानाति न चाप्रियं किञ्चिद्वेत्ति स सर्वांश्च
units.english: and this is not what is desired by Indra, as he has declared that‘He does not at the time know the Self as am this, nor does he know these beings,he seems to have gone to utter annihilation;and see no good in this’what is desired by Indra is that which knows itself, as also the Beings,which knows no pain, and who, by such knowledge, attains all regions and all desires

units.sanskrit: लोकानाप्नोति सर्वांश्च कामान्येन ज्ञानेन सत्यमेतदिष्टमिन्द्रस्येमानि भूतानि मत्तो
units.english: True;

units.sanskrit: ऽन्यानि लोकाः कामाश्च सर्वे मत्तो ऽन्ये ऽहमेषां स्वामीति । न त्वेतदिन्द्रस्य हितम् ।
units.english: this is what is desired by Indra, his idea being that ‘these beings are different from me,than regions and these desires are all different from me,and am the owner of all these’But this is not what is good wholesome for him;

units.sanskrit: हितं चेन्द्रस्य प्रजापतिना वक्तव्यम् ।
units.english: and Prajāpati has to explain what is good fortune

units.sanskrit: व्योमवदशरीरात्मतया सर्वभूतलोककामात्मत्वोपगमेन या प्राप्तिस्तद्धितमिन्द्राय वक्तव्यमिति प्रजापतिनाभिप्रेतम् । न तु राज्ञो राज्याप्तिवदन्यत्वेन ।
units.english: What Prajāpati wishes to explain for the good of Indra is the idea that the Self is unbodied like the Ākāśa and when the text speaks of the attainment of all Regions and Desires,’ what is meant is the realisation of the truth that all these are Self itself;and not that the attainment of something other than the Self,like the attainment of the kingdom by the king

units.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कं केन विजानीयादात्मैकत्व इमानि भूतान्ययमहमस्मीति ।
units.english: Such being the case, what would know what,as ‘these beings’ or ‘ am this’all being the Self which is one only?

units.sanskrit: नन्वस्मिन्पक्षेस्त्रीभिर्वा यानैर्वास यदि पितृलोककामःस एकधा भवतिइत्याद्यैश्वर्यश्रुतयो ऽनुपपन्नाः । न ।
units.english: ‘If he is desirous of the region of the fathers etc’, Chā ii ,, ‘He becomes one, two etc’ Chā xxvi Not so;

units.sanskrit: सर्वात्मनः सर्वफलसंबन्धोपपत्तेरविरोधात् ।
units.english: there is nothing incongruous in the idea that what is the All self is related to all rewards;

units.sanskrit: मृद इव सर्वघचकरककुण्डाद्याप्तिः ।
units.english: just as the clay attains the position of all jars, waterpots and bowls, etc

units.sanskrit: ननु सर्वात्मत्वे दुःखसंबन्धो ऽपि स्यादिति चेन्न, दुःखस्याप्यात्मत्वोपगमादविरोधः ।
units.english: If he is the Allself, then he would be connected with Pain also No; because the Pain also is held to be included in the Allself, there would be no such incongruity as one becoming connected with the other;

units.sanskrit: आत्मन्यविद्याकल्पनानिमित्तानि दुःखानि रज्ज्वामिव सर्पादिकल्पनानिमित्तानि ।
units.english: as a matter of fact, all pains are the effects of imagination due to ignorance imposed on the Self; just as the idea of the serpent is imposed upon the Rope

units.sanskrit: साचाविद्याशरीरात्मैकत्वस्वरूपदर्शनेन दुःखनिमित्तोच्छिन्नेनि दुःखसंबन्धाशङ्का न संभवति ।
units.english: This ignorance, as the [cause of pain, having been destroyed by the perception of real nature of the unity of the body and all things in the Self,there can be no suspicion at all of the connection of Pain

units.sanskrit: शुद्धसत्त्वसंकल्पनिमित्तानां तु कामानामीश्वरदेहसंबन्धः सर्वभूतेषु मानसानां
units.english: As for those desires Pleasures and Powers which have their source in volition abounding Goodness,they are connected with the Body of God, and this connection is in regard to all things,as these have a purely mental existence in the Mind of God

units.sanskrit: पर एव सर्वसत्त्वोपाधिद्वारेण भोक्तेति सर्वाविद्याकृतसंव्यवहाराणां पर एवा'त्मा'स्पदं नान्यो ऽस्तीति वेदान्तसिद्धान्तः ।
units.english: But the real Allself is beyond all this,he becomes the ‘experiencer’ only through his limitations; so that which is called the Self is above all those operations that are due to Ignorance,and none else;such is the doctrine of the Vedānta

units.sanskrit: य एषो ऽक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यति इति च्छायापुरुष एव प्रजापतिनोक्तः ।
units.english: Some people hold the following opinion,In the text it is the person seen in the eye Prajāpati has spoken of the ReflectionSelf as the Self;

units.sanskrit: स्वप्नसुषुप्तयोश्चान्य एव ।
units.english: as, if therefore, there would be selfContradiction

units.sanskrit: न परो ऽपहतपाप्मत्वादिलक्षणो विरोधादिति केचिन्मन्यन्ते । छायाद्यात्मनां चोपदेशे प्रयोजनमाचक्षते । आदावेवोच्यमाने किल दुर्विज्ञेयत्वात्परस्या'त्मनो ऽत्यन्तबाह्यविषयासक्तचेतसो ऽत्यन्तसूक्ष्मवस्तुश्रवणे व्यामोहो मा भूदिति ।
units.english: These people, holding the above opinion, explain the purpose of the teaching of the Reflection and other Selves, as followsif the very obstruse ultimate truth were set forth at the very outset, then inasmuch as the Supreme Self is difficult to understand,on the hearing of such an absolute subtile entity, there would arise sheer confusion in those persons whose minds are addicted to entirely external objects

units.sanskrit: यथा किल द्वितीयायां सूक्ष्मं चन्द्रं दिदर्शयिषुर्वृक्षं कञ्चित्प्रत्यक्षमादौ दर्शयति पश्यामुमेष चन्द्र इति, ततो ऽन्यं ततो ऽप्यन्यं गिरिमूर्धानं च चन्द्रसमीपस्थं एष चन्द्र इति ततो ऽसौ चन्द्रं पश्यति,
units.english: Just as on the second day of the month, when a man wants to see the very thin moon, another man, at first, points out to him the tree which is visible near at hand‘now see this way is the Moon’,then he points out further off to the peak of a high mountain which appeals to be close to the Moon,then the man sees the Moon;

units.sanskrit: एवमेतद्य एषो ऽक्षिणीत्याद्युक्तं प्रजापतिना त्रिभिः पर्यायैर्न पर इति ।
units.english: in the same manner, Prajāpati spoke at the outset by means of the first three illustrations,not of the Supreme Self, butof ‘the Person seen in the Eye’ and so forth

units.sanskrit: चतुर्थे तु पर्याये देहान्मर्त्यात्समुत्थायाशरीरतामापन्नो ज्योतिःस्वरूपम् । यस्मिन्नुत्तमपुरुषे स्त्र्यादिभिर्जक्षत्क्रीडन्रममाणो भवति स उत्त्मः पुरुषः पर उक्त इति चा'हुः ।
units.english: In the fourth illustration, he has spoken of the Highest Person, the Supreme Self, which rising out of the mortal Body, and becoming unbodied and of the nature of pure light, becomes merged in which Highest Person, and he continues to ‘sport and rejoice’, Chā

units.sanskrit: सत्यं, रमणीया तावदियं व्याख्या श्रोतुम् ।
units.english: It is quite true, that this explanation is very pleasing to hear;

units.sanskrit: न त्वर्थो ऽस्य ग्रन्थस्यैवं संभवति ।
units.english: but such cannot be the meaning of the text

units.sanskrit: अक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यत इत्युपन्यस्य शिष्याभ्यां छायात्मनि गृहीते तयोस्तद्विपरीतग्रहणं मत्वा तदपनयायोदशरावोपन्यासः किं पश्यथ इति च प्रश्नः साध्वलङ्कारोपदेशश्चानर्थकः
units.english: Having propounded the teaching that ‘the Person seen in the Eye is the Self’,Prajāpati found that his pupils had understood the Reflection to be the Self,and then with a view to removing this wrong conviction of theirs, he introduced the illustration of the ‘watercup’

units.sanskrit: स्यात् यदि च्छायात्मैव प्रजापतिनाक्षिणि दृश्यत इत्युपदिष्टः । किञ्च यदि स्वयमुपदिष्ट इति ग्रहणस्याप्यपनयकारणं वक्तव्यं स्यात् ।
units.english: the question ‘what do you see?’and then advised them to adorn themselves etc, all this would be meaningless, if what Prajāpati wished to teach was only the ReflectionSelf, by the expression ‘the Person seen in the Eye’, further, after having himself taught that the Reflection was the Self, it would be necessary to explain why he sought to set aside that idea;

units.sanskrit: स्वप्नसुषुप्तात्मग्रहणयोरपि तदपनयकारणं च स्वयं ब्रूयात् न चोक्तंतेनटतेन मन्यामहे नाक्षिणि च्छायात्मा प्रजापतिनोपदिष्टः ।
units.english: and He’would Himself state the reasons for the setting aside of the notions that the DreamSelf or the Self in deep sleep was the Self;but no such reason has been stated;from all which we conclude that Prajāpati did not propound the teaching that the Reflection in the Eye is the Self

units.sanskrit: किं चान्यदक्षिणि द्रष्टा चेद्दृश्यत इत्युपदिष्टः स्यात्तत इदं युक्तम् ।
units.english: Further, if it had been taught that it is the seer that is seen in the eye, then what has been asserted might be right;

units.sanskrit: एतं त्वेव त इत्युक्त्वा स्वप्ने ऽपि द्रष्टुरेवोपदेशः ।
units.english: but as a matter of fact, however, Prajāpati has said that ‘This am going to explain further’, and then has gone on to expound the seer in connection with dream also

units.sanskrit: स्वप्ने न द्रष्टोपदिष्ट इति चेन्न ।
units.english: It might be urged thatThe Seer has not been expounded in connection with DreamsBut that cannot be right;

units.sanskrit: अपि रोदितीवाप्रियवेत्तेवेत्युपदेशात् । न च द्रष्टुरन्यः कश्चित्स्वप्ने महीयमानश्चरति ।
units.english: because such expressions have been used in connection with the DreamSelf as‘weeps, as it were’,‘becomes conscious of pain as it were’;nor does anyone except the Seer ‘move about worshipped’ as declared under x

units.sanskrit: अत्रायं पुरुषः स्वयञ्ज्योतिरिति न्यायतः श्रुत्यन्तरे सिद्धत्वात् । यद्यपि स्वप्ने सधीर्भवति तथापि न धीः स्वप्नभोगोपलब्धिं प्रति करणत्वं भजते ।
units.english: because it has been proved by reasons in another Vedic text, which declares that ‘Herein the Self is selfillumined’Even though during dreams the person remains conscious, yet it is not that consciousness which is the cause of the perception of the dreamexperiences;

units.sanskrit: किं तर्हि पटचित्रवज्जाग्रद्वासनाश्रया दृश्यैव धीर्भवतीति न द्रष्टुः स्वयञ्ज्योतिष्ट्वबाधः स्यात् । किञ्चान्यत् । जाग्रत्स्वप्न्योर्भूतानि चा'त्मानं च जानातीमानि भूतान्ययमहमस्मीति ।
units.english: so that this would not militate against the ‘Selfluminous’ character of the Seer Then again, it has been asserted that ‘during the waking and dreaming states, the man does not know thing, as ‘these things’ nor does he know the Self, as ‘ am This’There could be room for this denial‘In Truth, he does not rightly know himself etc’, or xi

units.sanskrit: प्राप्तौ सत्यां प्रतिषेधो युक्तः स्यान्नाह खल्वयमित्यादि ।
units.english: above,only if the contingency denied were with the bounds of possibility

units.sanskrit: तथा चेतनस्यैवाविद्यानिमित्तयोः शरीरत्वे सति प्रियाप्रिययोरपहतिर्नास्तीत्युक्त्वा
units.english: Thus it is having asserted that so long as the Conscious Being has a body, there is no freedom from the Pleasure and Pain due to Ignorance xii

units.sanskrit: तस्यैवाशरीरस्य सतो विद्यायां सत्यां सशरीरत्वे प्राप्तयोः प्रतिषेधो युक्तो ऽशरीरं
units.english: , he has gone on to add that on that serene Being becoming unbodied,and True Knowledge having come

units.sanskrit: वाव सन्तं न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशत इति ।
units.english: about,there is no Pleasure or Pain;

units.sanskrit: एकश्चा'त्मा स्वप्नबुद्धान्तयोर्महामत्स्यवदसङ्गः संचरतीति श्रुत्यन्तरे सिद्धम् ।
units.english: It has also been declared as a settled fact, in another Vedic text that‘the one Self moves along unaffected, throughout the Dreaming and Waking states, like a huge fish’

units.sanskrit: यच्चोक्तं संप्रसादः शरीरात्समुत्थाय यस्मिन्स्त्र्यादिभी रममाणो भवति सो ऽन्यः संप्रसादादधिकरणनिर्दिष्ट उत्तमः पुरुष इति ।
units.english: It has been alleged thatThe Serene Being rising out of the Body, goes to an abode where he says ‘rejoicing with women and other objects of enjoyment’,and this must be a Being, in the shape of the Highest Person, who is different from the Serene Being, as indicated by the different Abode

units.sanskrit: तदप्यसत् ।
units.english: This is not right

units.sanskrit: चतुर्थे ऽपि पर्याय एत त्वेव त इति वचनात् । यदि ततो ऽन्यो ऽभिप्रेतः स्यात्पूर्ववदेतं त्वेव त इति न ब्रूयान्मृषा प्रजापतिः ।
units.english: Because even in the fourth illustration, Prajāpati has used the same expression as in the other casesviz ‘This same shall explain’If a different Being had been meant, then Prajāpati could not have said ‘this same’, which would be a lie

units.sanskrit: किञ्चान्यत्तेजोबन्नादीनां स्रष्टुः सतः स्वविकारदेहशुङ्गे प्रवेशं दर्शयित्वा प्रविष्टाय पुवस्तत्त्वमसीत्युपदेशो मृषा प्रसज्येत । तस्मिंस्त्वं स्त्र्यादिभी रन्ता भविष्यसीति युक्त उपदेशो ऽभविष्यद्यदि संप्रसादादन्य उत्तमः पुरुषो भवेत् ।
units.english: And further, all that teaching wherein,having shown that the Being who is the creator of Fire, Water and Food and other things entered into his own Product in the shape of the Body, the Teacher has gone on to assert that ‘that thou art’,would become falsified;’and the right teaching would have been that ‘Therein you will come to rejoice with women and other things’if the ‘Highest Person’ were something different from the Serene Being

units.sanskrit: तथा भूम्न्यहमेवेत्यादिश्या'त्मैवेदं सर्वमिति नोपसमहरिष्यद्यदि भूमा जीवादन्यो ऽभविष्यत् । नान्यो ऽतो ऽस्ति द्रष्टाइत्यादिश्रुत्यन्तराच्च । सर्वश्रुतिषु च परस्मिन्नात्मशब्दप्रयोगो नाभविष्यत्प्रत्यगात्मा चेत्सर्वजन्तूनां पर आत्मा न भवेत्तस्मादेक एवा'त्मा प्रकरणी सिद्धः ।
units.english: Further, if the ‘Infinite’ were something totally different from the living Self then the text would not have asserted that ‘ alone am in the Infinite’, and then gone on to sum up with the declaration that All this is Self’;specially in view of another Vedic text, which says‘There is no Seer other than this’;nor, in that case, would all the Vedic texts have applied the term ‘Self’ to the ‘Highest Person’ SupremeSelf; if the ‘living Self’ counterSelf of all living beings were not the same as the Supreme Self

units.sanskrit: न चा'त्मनः संसारित्वम् ।
units.english: This Self itself is not subject to the cycle of Birth and Rebirth

units.sanskrit: अविद्याध्यस्तत्वादात्मनि संसारस्य ।
units.english: Because, as a matter of fact, the Birth and Rebirthcycle is imposed upon the Self by Nescience Ignorance

units.sanskrit: न हि रज्जुशुक्तिकागगनादिषु सर्परजतमलादीनि मिथ्याज्ञानाध्यस्तानि तेषां भवन्तीति ।
units.english: For instance, the serpent, the silver and the darkness, imposed respectively upon the rope, the shell and the Ākāśa, by wrong cognition,do not come to belong to these latter

units.sanskrit: एतेन सशरीरस्य प्रियाप्रिययोरपहतिर्नास्तीति व्याख्यातम् । यच्चस्थितमप्रियवेत्तेवेति नाप्रियवेत्तैवेति सिद्धम् ।
units.english: This explains the statement‘for the bodied Self, there is no freedom from Pleasure and Pain’Then as for the statement that ‘he becomes conscious of pain, as it wereit has been proved that, in reality he is not conscious of pain

units.sanskrit: एवं च सति सर्वपर्यायेष्वेतदमृतभयमेतद्ब्रह्मेति प्रजापतेर्वचनम् ।
units.english: Thus it is clear that throughout all the four illustrations cited by Prajāpati there seems the one idea that ‘this is the Immortal and the Fearless;

units.sanskrit: यदि वा प्रजापतिच्छद्भरूपायाः श्रुतेर्वचनं सत्यमेव भवेत् ।
units.english: this is Brahman’Even if this declaration were taken as emanating from the Veda itself, hidden in the person of Prajāpati,even so, it must be true;

units.sanskrit: न चतत्कुतर्कबुद्ध्या मृषा कर्तुं युक्तम् । ततो गुरुतरस्य प्रमाणान्तरस्यानुपपत्तेः ।
units.english: and it would not be right to prove it to be untrue by means of objectionable reasonings Because there is no Means of Cognition, superior to more reliable than the Vedic text

units.sanskrit: ननु प्रत्यक्षं दुःखाद्यप्रियवेत्तृत्वमव्यभिचार्यनुभूयत इति चेन्न ।
units.english: But that man is conscious of Pain and other disagreeable things is a perceptible fact,found to be invariably true Not so;

units.sanskrit: जरादिरहितो जीर्णो ऽहं जातो ऽहमायुष्मान्गौरः कृष्णो मृत इत्यादिप्रत्यक्षानुभववत्तदुपपत्तेः ।
units.english: as that perception is exactly like all such ideas as ‘ am free from decrepitude’, ‘ am decrepit am born’, ‘ am longlived ‘ am fair’, ‘ am dark’, ‘ am dead’, and so forth which people have, and yet which as applied to the Self, are apparently wrong

units.sanskrit: सर्वमप्येतत्सत्यमिति चेदस्त्येवैतदेवं दुरवगमं येन देवराजो ऽप्युदशरावादिदर्शिताविनाशयुक्तिरपि मुमोहैवात्र विनाशमेवापीतो भवतीति तथा विरोचनो महाप्राज्ञः प्राजापत्यो ऽपि देहमात्रात्मदर्शनो बभूव ।
units.english: True, it is a matter difficult to understand; so difficult indeed that even the king of the Devas Indra was bewildered by the reason for imperishability which was demonstrated by the example of the watercup,and belived that ‘it goes to annihilation’ So also, Virocana, a very wise person, born of Prajāpati himself, accepted the view that the Body is the Self

units.sanskrit: तथेन्द्रस्या'त्मविनाशभयसागर एव वैनाशिका न्यमज्जन् ।
units.english: In fact, it is in this ocean of the ‘annihilation of the Self’ as understood by Indra, that the Nihilists have become submerged

units.sanskrit: तथा सांख्या द्रष्टारं देहादिव्यतिरिक्तमवगम्यापि त्यक्तागमप्रमाणत्वान्मृत्युविषय एवान्यत्वदर्शने तस्थुः ।
units.english: Even the followers of Sāṅkhya, though conscious of the fact that the seer is different from the Body and other things, yet renounced the authority of the scriptures and remained fixed in the idea of Diversity, which is the source of death

units.sanskrit: तथान्ये काणादादिदर्शनाः कषायरक्तमिव क्षारादिभिर्वस्रं नवभिरात्मगुणैर्युक्तमात्मद्रव्यं विशोधयितुं प्रवृत्ताः ।
units.english: Similarly, other philosophers also,such as Kaṇāda and the rest,have set about to purify the substance ‘Self’ with nine qualities of the Self,just like a man going out to colour a piece of cloth, already pale red, with other colours

units.sanskrit: तथान्ये कर्मिणो बाह्यविषयापहृतचेतसो वेदप्रमाणा अपि परमार्थसत्यमात्मैकत्वं विनाशमिवेन्द्रवन्मन्यमाना घटीयन्त्रवदारोहावरोहप्रकारैरनिशं बम्भ्रमति । किमन्ये क्षुद्रजन्तवो विवेकहीनाः स्वभावत एव बहिर्विषयापहृतचेतसः ।
units.english: So also others, who are ‘Ritualists’ having their minds captivated by external things,even though depending upon the authority of the Vedas,have come, like Indra, to regard the absolutely True Unity of the Self as ‘annihilation’, ‘and hence they flounder about up and down like a pulley, When such is the ignorance of such persons what then can be said of those insignificant creatures, who are devoid of discrimination, and by their nature, have their minds captivated by external things?

units.sanskrit: तस्मादिदं त्यक्तसर्वबाह्यैषणैरनन्यशरणैः परमहंसपरिव्राजकैरत्याश्रमिभिर्वेदान्तविज्ञानपरैरेव वेदनीयं पूज्यतमैः प्राजापत्यं चेमं संप्रदायमनुसरद्भिरुपनिबद्धं प्रकरणचतुष्टयेन ।
units.english: From all this it follows that this philosophical system has been set forth in these four Heads by persons following up the the tradition emanating from Prajāpati;and it can be understood only by those highly worshipped persons who have renounced all longings for external things, who seek for no other refuge,who are ParamaHaṃsa, wandering Mendicants, who have reached the final lifestage and are totally devoted to the Philosophy of the Vedānta

units.sanskrit: तथानुशासत्यद्यापि त एव नान्य इति ॥
units.english: And even to this day, it is only these personsand none others,who carry on this teaching

units.sanskrit: अशरीरो वायुः ।
units.english: Unbodied is Air;

units.sanskrit: अभ्रं विद्युत् स्तनयित्नुर् अशरीराण्य् एतानि ।
units.english: and Cloud, Lightning, Thunder,these are unbodied

units.sanskrit: तद् यथैतान्य् अमुष्माद् आकाशात् समुत्थाय परं ज्योतिर् उपसंपद्य स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यन्ते ॥
units.english: Now, as these, rising out of that Ākāśa and having reached the Highest Light, appear in their own forms

units.sanskrit: संप्राप्तस्य शरीरात्समुत्थाय स्वेन रूपेण यथाभिनिष्पत्तिस्तथा वक्तव्येति दृष्टान्त
units.english: It is necessary now to explain in what manner the unbodied Serene Being comes, through Nescience, to be identified with the Body,and actually embodied,and then rises out of the body and appears in its own form;

units.sanskrit: उच्यतेअशरीरो वायुरविद्यमानं शिरःपाण्यादिमच्छरीरमस्येत्यशरीरः । किं चाभ्रं विद्युत्स्तनयित्नुरित्येतानि चाशरीराणि । तत्तत्रैवं सति वर्षादिप्रयोजनावसाने यथा । अमुष्मादिति भूमिष्ठा श्रुतिर्द्युलोकसंबन्धिनमाकाशदेशं व्यपदिशति ।
units.english: and for explaining this, an example is citedUnbodied is Air,ie it is without a body with hands, feet and other limbs;further, Cloud, Lightning and Thunder,these are unbodied;such being the case, in the fulfilment of such purposes as Rainfall and the like,what happens is that, rising out of that Ākāśa;the Vedic text supposed to be on the Earth refers to the Ākāśa connected with the Heavenly Region as ‘that’,these,the said Air and the rest

units.sanskrit: एतानि यथोक्तान्याकाशसमानरूपतामापन्नानि स्वेन वाय्वादिरूपेणागृह्यमाणान्याकाशाख्यतां गतानि यथा संप्रसादो ऽविद्यावस्थायां शरीरात्मभावमेवापन्नः, तानि च तथाभूतान्यमुष्माद्द्युलोकसम्बन्धिन आकाशदेशात्समुत्तिष्ठन्ति वर्षणादिप्रयोजनाभिनिर्वृत्तये ।
units.english: come to assume that same form as Ākāśa, and hence cease to be recognised in their own respective forms of air and the rest, and come to be known by the name of Ākāśa’;just as the Being in restful sleep, in the state of Ignorance, becomes identified with the body;air and the rest again rise out of the Ākāśa of the Heavenly Regions, for the purpose of accomplishing such purposes as Rainfall and the like

units.sanskrit: कथम् । शिशिरापाये सावित्र परं ज्योतिः प्रकृष्टं ग्रैष्मकमुपसंपद्य सावित्रमभितापं प्राप्येत्यर्थः । आदित्याभितापेन पृथग्भावमापादिताः सन्तः स्वेन स्वेन रूपेण पुरोवातादिवायुरूपेण
units.english: In what way?after the laps of Winter, Air and the rest, reach the Highest Lightthe highest form of solar light in Summer,that is, come into contact with Solar heat;they become disjoined and separated into their respective forms, and appear in their separate forms;

units.sanskrit: स्तिमितभावं हित्वाभ्रमपि भूमिपर्वतहस्त्यादिरूपेण विद्युदपि स्वेन ज्योतिर्लतादिचपलरूपेण स्तनयित्नुरपि स्वेन गर्जिताशनिरूपेणेत्येवं प्रावृडागमे स्वेन स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यन्ते ॥
units.english: the Air relinquishes its calm immobility and appears in the form of Storm;the Cloud appears in several such forms as the Earth, the Hill, the Elephant and the like;the Lightning appears in its mobile form of streaks of light;the Thunder also appears in its own form of Thundering and Thunderbolt

units.sanskrit: एवम् एवैष संप्रसादो ऽस्माच् छरीरात् समुत्थाय परं ज्योतिर् उपसंपद्य स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यते ।
units.english: In this way on the approach of the Rainy Season, all these appear in their own forms Thus dues the Serene Being, rising out of this Body and having reached the Highest Light, appears in his own form

units.sanskrit: स उत्तमपुरुषः ।
units.english: That is the Highest Person;

units.sanskrit: स तत्र पर्येति जक्षत् क्रीडन् रममाणः स्त्रीभिर् वा यानैर् वा ज्ञातिभिर् वा नोपजनं स्मरन्न् इदं शरीरम् ।
units.english: there he moves about, laughing, playing and rejoicing,be it with women, or conveyances or relatives,not mending the body in which he was born

units.sanskrit: स यथा प्रयोग्य आचरणे युक्त एवम् एवायम् अस्मिञ् छरीरे प्राणो युक्तः ॥
units.english: Like the horse yoked to the cart, so is the Spirit attached to body

units.sanskrit: यथायं दृष्टान्तो वाय्वादीनामाकाशादिसाम्यगमनवदविद्यया संसारावस्थायां शरीरसाम्यमापन्नो ऽहममुष्य पुत्रो जातो जीर्णो मरिष्य इत्येवंप्रकारं प्रजापतिनेव
units.english: Just as in the instance cited above Air and the rest are reduced to the condition of Ākāśa, so this Serene Being, having, through ignorance, fallen into the cycle of Birth and Rebirth, becomes reduced to the condition of the body, comes to have such notions as ‘ am the son of so and so,bornbecome oldam going to die’;

units.sanskrit: मघवान्यथोक्तेन क्रमेण नासि त्वं देहेन्द्रियादिधर्मा तत्त्वमसीति प्रतिबोधितः सन्स एष संप्रसादो जीवो ऽस्माच्छरीरादाकाशादिव वाय्वादयः समुत्थाय देहादिवैलक्षण्यमात्मनो
units.english: and later on, when,like Indra enlightened by Prajāpati, he comes to be enlightened and to realise the truth that ‘you are not of the nature of the body, the senseorgans and the like ‘that thou art’, and so forth; then this Serene Being, the ‘living Self’ rises out of the Body,as Air etc

units.sanskrit: रूपमवगम्य देहात्मभावनां हित्वेत्येतत् । स्वेन रूपेण सदात्मनैवाभिनिष्पद्यत इति व्याख्यातं पुरस्तात् ।
units.english: rose out of Ākāśa,and having come to realise his own form as distinct from the Body etc, renounces the idea that the Body is the Self; and comes to appear in his own form of the True Self;

units.sanskrit: स येन स्वेन रूपेण संप्रसादो ऽभिनिष्पद्यते प्राक्प्रतिबोधात्तद्भ्रान्तिनिमित्तात्सर्पो भवति यता रज्जुः पश्चात्कृतप्रकाशा रज्ज्वात्मना स्वेन
units.english: That form in which the Serene Being appears, before being enlightened, is due to Ignorance; just as the Rope becomes the serpent and then when illumined by light, it appears in its own form of Rope

units.sanskrit: एवं च स उत्तमपुरुष उत्तमश्चासौ पुरुषश्चेत्युत्तमपुरुषः स एवोत्तमपुरुषो ऽक्षिस्वप्नपुरुषौ व्यक्तावव्यक्तश्च सुषुप्तः समस्तः संप्रसन्नो ऽशरीरश्च स्वेन रूपेणेति । एषामेष स्वेन रूपेणावस्थितः क्षराक्षरौ व्याकृताव्याकृतावपेक्ष्योत्तमपुरुषः कृतनिर्वचनो ह्ययं गीतासु ।
units.english: In the same manner, the Highest Person the Highest of Persons; there are many ‘persons’,such as ‘the Person in the Eye’, ‘the dreaming persons’, ‘the manifested’ and the ‘unmanifested’ persons, ‘the person soundly asleep, happy and serene’, ‘unbodied, in his own form’ and of all these the ‘person’ in his own form is the ‘highest’ as compared to the ‘differentiated’ and the ‘undifferentiated’

units.sanskrit: स संप्रसादः स्वेन रूपेण तत्र स्वात्मनि स्वस्थतया सर्वात्मभूतः पर्येति क्वचिदिन्द्राद्यात्मना जक्षद्धसन्भक्षयन्वा भक्ष्यानुच्चावचानीप्सितान्क्वचिन्मनोमात्रैः संकल्पादेव समुत्थितैर्ब्राह्मलौकिकैर्वा क्रीडन्स्त्र्यादिभी रममाणश्च मनसैव नोपजनं स्रीपुंसयोरन्योन्योपगमेन जायत इत्युपजनमात्मभावेन वा'त्मसामीप्येन जायत इत्युपजनमिदं शरीरं तन्न स्मरन् ।
units.english: Then, the said Serene Being in his own form and resting in himself, as the Allself,moves about,here and there, sometimes in the form of Indra and such other beings,laughing, or eating all kinds of food, good and bad, that he desires,sometimes playingonly in the mind not physically with thingsheavenly as well as earthly brought about by sheer willing,and rejoicingin the mind, with women and others,not minding the Body; the term ‘Upajana’ stands for what is born of the association of men and women,or for that which is born in the form of the Self, or near theSelf

units.sanskrit: तत्स्मरणे हि दुःखमेव स्यात् । दुःखात्मकत्वात्तस्य ।
units.english: He does not mindremember the Bodyas the remembering of it would cause him pain, as the Body abounds in pain

units.sanskrit: नन्वनुभूतं चेन्न स्मरेदसर्वज्ञत्वं मुक्तस्य ।
units.english: ObjectionsIf he does not remember what he has experienced, then Liberated Person is not omniscient

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: This does not affect our position

units.sanskrit: येन मिथ्याज्ञानादिना जनितं तच्च मिथ्याज्ञानादि विद्ययोच्छेदितमतस्तन्नानुभूतमेवेति न तदस्मरणे सर्वज्ञत्वहानिः । न ह्यु न्मत्तेन ग्रहगृहीतेन वा यदनुभूतं तदुन्मादाद्यपदमे ऽपि स्मर्तव्यं स्यात्तथेहापि संसारिभिरविद्यादोषवद्भिर्यदनुभूयते तत्सर्वात्मानमशरीरं
units.english: As a matter of fact the Body owes its origin to ignorance; and all this, ignorance and the rest, has been totally rooted out by True Knowledge, so that, in reality the past experience has not been experienced at all, and hence the not remembering of it does not vitiate his omniscience For instance, what has been experienced by an insane person, or by a person observed by planetary spirits cannot be remembered after the insanity and the observers have passed off

units.sanskrit: अविद्यानिमित्ताभावात् ।
units.english: In the same manner, what is experienced by men involved in the meshes of Birth and Regirth and beset by the evil effects of Ignorance, does not touch the Unbodied AllSelf, for the simple reason’, that the basic cause, Ignorance, is absent in this case

units.sanskrit: ये तूच्छिन्नदोषैर्मृदितकषायैर्मानसाः सत्याः कामा अनृतापिधाना अनुभूयन्ते विद्याभिव्यङ्ग्यत्वात्त एव मुक्तेन सर्वात्मभूतेन संबध्यन्त इत्यात्मज्ञानस्तुतये निर्दिश्यन्ते ऽतः साध्वेतद्विशिनष्टिय
units.english: Those ‘True Desires hidden by the Untrue’ which are experienced persons whose defects have been removed and whose impurities have been washed off,these alone are connected with the liberated AllSelf,as these experiences owe their manifestation to True Knowledge, and hence these are pointed out in eulogising the Knowledge of Self;

units.sanskrit: एते ब्रह्मलोक इति ।
units.english: it is for this reason that the specification that ‘these are experienced in the Brahmic Region’ is quite reasonable;

units.sanskrit: यत्र क्वचन भवन्तो ऽपि ब्रह्मण्येव हि ते लोके भवन्तीति सर्वात्मत्वाद्ब्रह्मण उच्यन्ते ।
units.english: because whereby they occur, they are said to occur in the ‘Region of Brahman’,as Brahman is the AllSelf,

units.sanskrit: ननु कथमेकः'सन्नान्यत्पश्यति नान्यद्विजानाति स भूमा'कामांश्च ब्राह्मलौकिकान्ऽपश्यन् रमत'इति च विरुद्धम् ।
units.english: ObjectionIt has been said that ‘being one only, Infinite does not see another, hear another or know another’,and then again that ‘he rejoices on seeing things of the Brahmic Region’;thus there is SelfContradiction;

units.sanskrit: यथैको यस्मिन्नेव क्षणे पश्यति स तस्मिन्नेव क्षणे न पश्यति चेति ।
units.english: the one, seeing, as well as not seeing, at one and the same moment

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः ।
units.english: This does not affect our position

units.sanskrit: श्रुत्यन्तरे परिहृतत्वात् । द्रष्टुर्दृष्टेरविपरिलोपात्पश्यन्नेव भवति । द्रष्टुरन्यत्वेन कामानामभावान्न पश्यति चेति ।
units.english: This difficulty has been set aside in another Vedic text, where it is shown that ‘on account of the Nondisapperance of the vision of the Seer, He continues to see things’, and yet, inasmuch as the desires have no existence apart from the Seer himself, he does not see them

units.sanskrit: यद्यपि सुषुप्ते तदुक्तं मुक्तस्यापि सर्वैकत्वात्समानो द्वितीयाभावः ।
units.english: Though this explanation has been povided in connection with the Person in Deep Sleep, yet, the ‘absence of the second is equally present in the case of the Liberated Person also, for whom all is one’;

units.sanskrit: केन कं पश्येदिति चोक्तमेव ।
units.english: hence ‘by what could he see what?’As already explained above

units.sanskrit: अशरीरस्वरूपो ऽपहतपाप्मादिलक्षणः सन्कथमेष पुरुषो ऽक्षिणि दृश्यत इत्युक्तः प्रजापतिना ।
units.english: The question that arises now is thisWhen the Self is unbodied, and characterised by freedom from evil etc, then how is it that he has been spoken of by Prajāpati as the Personseen in the Eye

units.sanskrit: तत्र यथासावक्षिणि साक्षाद्दृश्यते तद्वक्तव्यमितीदमारभ्यते ।
units.english: It has got to be explained how the said Self is directly seen in the Eye

units.sanskrit: तत्र को हेतुरक्षिणि दर्शन इत्याहस दृष्टान्तो यथा प्रयोग्यः प्रयोग्यपरो वा सशब्दः ।
units.english: The Text proceeds to explain this; and points out the reason why he is seen in the Eye an example is taken

units.sanskrit: प्रयुज्यत इति प्रयोग्यो ऽश्वो बलीवर्दे वा । यथा लोक आचरत्यनेनेत्याचरणो रथो ऽनो वा तस्मिन्नाचरणे युक्तस्तदाकर्षणाय, एवमस्मिञ्छरीरे रथस्थानीये प्राणः पञ्चवृत्तिरिन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिसंयुक्तः प्रज्ञात्मा विज्ञानक्रियाशक्तिद्वयसंमूर्छितात्मा युक्तः स्वकर्मफलोपभोगनिमित्तं
units.english: Just as the ‘Prayogya’the words may be construed as ‘SaPrayogya’, or simply as ‘Prayogya’, which means that which is yoked, viz Horse or Bullock;in the world,,the term ‘ācaraṇa’ standing for that by which people go about, ie Chariot or Cart,for drawing it,so to this body, which is like the chariot, is yoked the Spirit, with its five functions, endowed with the senseorgans Mind and Intellect, the Conscious Ego with his Self merged in the faculties of Cognition and Action,this Spirit being yoked to the Body for the experiencing of the results of his own Karmic Residua;

units.sanskrit: नियुक्तः । कस्मिन्न्वहमुत्क्रान्त उत्क्रान्तो भविसष्यामि कस्मिन्वा प्रतिष्ठिते प्रतिष्ठास्यामीति ।
units.english: it is this ‘yoking which has been spoken of above in the text‘on whose departure shall depart? on whose firmness shall become firm?’This Spirit is appointed to such functions as seeing, hearing and moving;

units.sanskrit: ईश्वरेण राज्ञेव सर्वाधिकारी दर्शनश्रवणचेष्टाव्यापारे ऽधिकृतः ।
units.english: just as the chief officer is appointed by the king

units.sanskrit: तस्यैव तु मात्रैकदेशश्चक्षुरिन्द्रियं रूपोपलब्धिद्वारभूतम् ॥
units.english: It is of this Spirit that the ‘Visual Organ Eye is a part, and which serves as the vehicle for the perception of Colour

units.sanskrit: अथ यत्रैतद् आकाशम् अनुविषण्णं चक्षुः स चाक्षुषः पुरुषो दर्शनाय चक्षुः ।
units.english: Now, wherein the eye has merged into Ākāśa, that is ‘the person in the Eye’; and the Eye is for the purpose of seeing

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेदेदं जिघ्राणीति स आत्मा गन्धाय घ्राणम् ।
units.english: He who is conscious that ‘ may smell’, is the Self; and the Nose is for perceiving smell

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेदेदम् अभिव्याहराणीति स आत्मा अभिव्याहाराय वाक् ।
units.english: He who is conscious that ‘ may speak is the Self,and the organ of Speech is for speaking

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेदेदं शृण्वानीति स आत्मा श्रवणाय श्रोत्रम् ॥
units.english: And he who is conscious that ‘ may hear’, is the Self,and the Ear is the organ for hearing

units.sanskrit: तत्र स प्रकृतो ऽशरीर आत्मा चाक्षुषश्चक्षुषि भव इति चाक्षुषस्तस्य दर्शनाय रूपोपलब्धये चक्षुः करणं यस्य तद्देहादिभिः संहतत्वात्परस्य द्रष्टुरर्थे सो ऽत्र चक्षुषि दर्शनेन लिङ्गेन दृश्यते परो ऽशरीरो ऽसंहतः ।
units.english: Now, when the eye has merged intobecome connected withthe Ākāśawithin the pupil in the Eye, within the body,then the Self in question who is really unbodied is ‘the person in the Eye;ie the person appearing in the Eye;and for his seeing is the Eye, the organ of vision; and as this organ is attached to the body of the seer, this seer comes to be seen’ through this indication mark in the shape of this Seeing,though in reality He is above all this, unbodied and unattached

units.sanskrit: अक्षिणि दृश्यत इति प्रजापतिनोक्तं सर्वेन्द्रियद्वारोपलक्षणार्थम् ।
units.english: Prajāpati has spoken of it as Seen in the eye; ‘but that is only illustration; what has been stated is true of all senseorgans;

units.sanskrit: सर्वविषयोपलब्धा हि स एवेति ।
units.english: as it is that Self who is the perceiver of all things

units.sanskrit: स्फुटोपलब्धिहेतुत्वात्त्वक्षिणीति विशेषवचनं सर्वश्रुतिषु ।
units.english: And yet in all Vedic texts, ‘He has been spoken of specially as seen in the Eye because it is in the Eye that He is most clearly perceived;

units.sanskrit: अहमदर्शमिति तत्सत्यं भवतीति च श्रुतेः ।
units.english: as says the text‘ saw it, hence it is true’

units.sanskrit: अथापि यो ऽस्मिन्देहे वेद कथमिदं सुगन्धि दुर्गन्धि वा जिघ्राणीत्यस्य गन्धं विजानीयामिति स आत्मा तस्य गन्धाय गन्धविज्ञानाय घ्राणम्
units.english: Further, in this body, he who is consciousof whatthat ‘ may smell’be cognisant ofgood or bad odour,is the Self; and for bringing about his cognition of Smell, Nose is the organ,He who is conscious that ‘ may speak’ words talkis the Self;

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेदेदं वचनमभिव्याहराणीति वदिष्यामीति स आत्माभिव्यवहरणक्रियासिद्धये करणं वागिन्द्रियम् ।
units.english: and for the bringing about of his action of Speech, the organ of Speech is the organ

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेदेदं शृणवानीति स आत्मा श्रवणाय श्रोत्रम् ॥
units.english: Similarly, he who is conscious that ‘ may hear’, is the Self,and the Ear is the organ for hearing

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेदेदं मन्वानीति स आत्मा । मनो ऽस्य दैवं चक्षुः ।
units.english: He who is conscious that ‘ may think’, is the Self,this is his Divine Eye;

units.sanskrit: स वा एष एतेन दैवेन चक्षुषा मनसैतान् कामान् पश्यन् रमते य एते ब्रह्मलोके ॥
units.english: and it is by means of this Divine Eye of the Mind that he sees the ‘desires’those in the Brahman Region,and rejoices

units.sanskrit: अथ यो वेददं मन्वानीति मननव्यापारमिन्द्रियासंस्पृष्टं केवलं मन्वानीति वेद स आत्मा मननाय मनः ।
units.english: Now, he who is conscious that ‘ may think’,that only thinks without even the slightest touch of the functioning of any other senseorganis the Self The mind is so called because of its function ‘thinking’ manana

units.sanskrit: यो वेद स आत्मेत्येवं सर्वत्र प्रयोगाद्वेदनमस्य स्वरूपमित्यवगम्यते ।
units.english: In the case of all organs the phrase ‘He who is conscious is the Self’ is found, which shows that consciousness forms the very nature of the Self

units.sanskrit: यथा यः पुरस्तात्प्रकाशयति स आदित्यो यो दक्षिणतो यः पश्चाद्य उत्तरतो य ऊर्ध्वं प्रकाशयति स आदित्य इत्युक्ते प्रकाशस्वरूपः स इति
units.english: For instance, when it is said that ‘He who illumines the front is the Sun, who shines to the right, who shines to the left, who shines above, is the Sun’, it is understood that Light forms the very nature of the Sun

units.sanskrit: दर्शनादि क्रियानिर्वृत्त्यर्थानि तु चक्षुरादिकरणानि ।
units.english: The organs of the Eye and the rest are for the purpose of bringing about the action of Seeing and the rest

units.sanskrit: इदं चास्या'त्मनः सामर्थ्यादवगम्यते ।
units.english: That this is so follows from the nature of the Self itself

units.sanskrit: आत्मनः सत्तामात्र एव ज्ञानकर्तृत्वं न तु व्यापृततया ।
units.english: Then again, when the Self is spoken of as the Knower,one who does the act of knowing,he is so by his very nature, by mere Existence, not through any action of his;

units.sanskrit: यथा सवितुः सत्तामात्र एव प्रकाशनकर्तृत्वं न तु व्यापृततयेति तद्वत् ।
units.english: just as when the Sun illumines things, it does by its mere presenceand not through any action

units.sanskrit: मनो ऽस्या'त्मनो दैवमप्राकृतमितरेन्द्रियैरसाधारणं चक्षुश्चष्टे पश्यत्यनेनेति चक्षुः ।
units.english: This Mind is the Divine Eye of the Self‘divine’, ie not ordinary, that which is entirely different in character from all other organs; and it is the ‘Eye’ in the sense that ‘one Sees by it’

units.sanskrit: वर्तमानकालविषयाणि चेन्द्रियाण्यतो ऽदैवानि तानि ।
units.english: The other senseorgans all apprehend objects existing in the present, hence they are ‘not divine’;

units.sanskrit: मनस्तु त्रिकालविषयोपलब्धिकरणं मृदितदोषं च सूक्ष्मव्यवहितादिसर्वोपलब्धिकरणं चेति दैवं चक्षुरुच्यते ।
units.english: the Mind on the other hand, is an organ that apprehends objects past, present and future, is free from defects and is capable of apprehending all things, subtile as well as hidden and remote, hence it is called the ‘Divine Eye’

units.sanskrit: स वै मुक्तः स्वरूपापन्नो ऽविद्याकृतदेहेन्द्रियमनोवियुक्तः सर्वात्मभावमापन्नः सन्नेष व्योमवद्विशुद्धः सर्वेश्वरो मनौपाधिः सन्नेतेनैवेश्वरेण मनसैतान्कामान्सवितृप्रकाशवन्नित्यप्रततेन
units.english: The Self thus who has become liberated,reverted to his own form,is entirely disassociated from all products of Nescience, such as the Body, the senseorgans and the Mind,has resumed the position of AllSelf; being so, he is pure like Ākāśa, the Lord of all, with the Mind as his conditioning adjunct;

units.sanskrit: दर्शनेन पश्यन् रमते । कान्कामानिति विशिनष्टिय एते ब्रह्मणि लोके हिरण्यनिधिवद्बाह्यविषयासङ्गानृतेनापिहिताः संकल्पमात्रलभ्यास्तानित्यर्थः ॥
units.english: and it is by means of His Divine Mind that He sees these desires,through a vision that is very operative, like the light of the Sunand rejoices the text defines the Desiresas those in the BrahmanRegionie Hidden, like buried gold, by the ‘Untrue’, and available by mere willing

units.sanskrit: तं वा एतं देवा आत्मानम् उपासते ।
units.english: ‘The Devas meditate upon this Self;

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् तेषां सर्वे च लोका आत्ताः सर्वे च कामाः ।
units.english: therefore are Regions and all Desires obtained by them

units.sanskrit: स सर्वांश् च लोकान् आप्नोति सर्वांश् च कामान् यस् तम् आत्मानम् अनुविद्य विजानाति । इति ह प्रजापतिर् उवाच प्रजापतिर् उवाच ॥
units.english: One who having sought after this Self, understands It, obtains all Regions and all Desires’;thus said ‘Prajāpati;yea, Prajāpati said this

units.sanskrit: यस्मादेष इन्द्राय प्रजापतिनोक्त आत्मा तस्मात्ततः श्रुत्वा तमात्मानमद्यत्वे ऽपि देवा उपासते ।
units.english: Because this Self was expounded to Indra by Prajāpati therefore, having heard it from him, the Devas even now, meditate upon this Self;

units.sanskrit: तदुपासनाच्च तेषां सर्वे च लोका आत्ताः प्राप्ताः सर्वे च कामाः ।
units.english: and by meditating upon It, they obtain all Regions and all Desires

units.sanskrit: यदर्थं हीन्द्र एकशतं वर्षाणि प्रजापतौ ब्रह्मचर्यमुवास तत्फलं प्राप्तं देवैरित्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: That is to say, the Devas obtained that reward for which Indra dwelt as a Religious Student for a hundred and one years, with Prajāpati,

units.sanskrit: तद्युक्तं देवानां महाभाग्यत्वान्न त्विदानीं मनुष्याणामल्पजीवितत्वान्मन्दतरप्रज्ञत्वाच्च संभवतीति प्राप्त इदमुच्यतेस सर्वांश्च लोकानाप्नोति सर्वांश्च कामानिदानीन्तनो ऽपि ।
units.english: This might give rise to the idea that‘All this might have been so in the case of the Devas who are extremely fortunate beings; it cannot be possible for the men of the present day, as they are shortlived and have smaller intelligence Hence, in order to set aside such an idea, the text addsEven at the present time, one obtains all Regions and all Desires

units.sanskrit: को ऽसौ । इन्द्रादिवद्यस्तमात्मानमनुविद्य विजानातीति ह सामान्येन किल प्रजापतिरुवाच ।
units.english: who?One who, like Indra and others, having sought after this Self understands It This General statement was made by Prajāpati

units.sanskrit: अतः सर्वेषामात्मज्ञानं तत्फलप्राप्तिश्च तुल्यैव भवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The sense is that for all men, there is an equal chance of attaining Selfknowledge and securing its rewards

units.sanskrit: द्विर्वचनं प्रकरणसमाप्त्यर्थम् ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the treatment of subject

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य द्वादशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: श्यामाच् छबलं प्रपद्ये । शबलाच् छ्यामं प्रपद्ये ।
units.english: ‘From the Sombre go to the Variegated; from the Variegated go to the Sombre

units.sanskrit: अश्व इव रोमाणि विधूय पापं चन्द्र इव राहोर् मुखात् प्रमुच्य धूत्वा शरीरम् अकृतं कृतात्मा ब्रह्मलोकम् अभिसंभवामीत्य् अभिसंभवामीति
units.english: Shaking off all evil, as the horse shakes off its hairs,and as the moon frees itself from Rāhu’s mouth,so shaking off the Body, and having fulfilled all ends, obtain the uncreated Region of Brahman!Yea, obtain it?

units.sanskrit: श्यामाच्छबलं प्रपद्य इत्यादिमन्त्राम्नाय पावनो जपार्थश्च ध्यानार्थो वा ।
units.english: ‘From the Sombre go to the Variegated etc, etc,’ is a Mantratext, which is purifying in itself, set forth here for the purpose of being repeated, or meditated upon‘Sombre’ is the deep Colour;

units.sanskrit: श्यामो गम्भीरो वर्णः श्याम इव श्यामो हार्दं ब्रह्मात्यन्तदुरवगाह्यत्वात्तद्धार्द
units.english: ‘from the sombre’ means ‘from the sombre as it were’,the term ‘Sombre’ stands for Brahman in the heart, on the ground Brahman being extremely incomprehensible;

units.sanskrit: ब्रह्म ज्ञात्वा ध्यानेन तस्माच्छ्यामाच्छबलं शबल इव शबलो ऽरण्याद्यनेककाममिश्रत्वाद्ब्रह्मलोकस्य
units.english: from this Sombre therefore means ‘from the Brahman in the Heart’ie having come to know the Brahman in the Heart by contemplation,from That, go to the Variegated,the Variegated as it were;

units.sanskrit: शाबल्य तं ब्रह्मलोकं शबलं प्रपद्ये मनसा शरीरपाताद्वोर्ध्वं गच्छेयम् । यस्मादहं शबलाद्ब्रह्मलोकान्नामरूपव्याकरणाय श्यामं प्रपद्ये हार्दभावं प्रपन्नो ऽस्मीत्यभिप्रायः । अतस्तमेव प्रकृतिस्वरूपमात्मानं शबलं प्रपद्य इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: the ‘Variegated’ character of the BrahmicRegion being a Common mixture of Forests and other Desirable things,to this variegatedBrahmicRegionmay go, in my mind, after the death of the Body The meaning is thatbecause from the VariegatedBrahmicRegionI gofor the purpose of differentiating Name and Formto the Sombre,ie because have attained the position of this Brahman in the Heart,therefore go to that Variegated Selfin the form of Prakṛti

units.sanskrit: कथं शबलं ब्रह्मलोकं प्रपद्य इत्युच्यतेअश्व इव स्वानि लोमानि विधूय कम्पनेन
units.english: It is next described in what manner go to the Variegated BrahmicRegionAs the Horse shaking off its hairs,ie by shaking, removes his fatigue and also dust etc

units.sanskrit: पापं धर्माधर्माक्यं चन्द्र इव च राहुग्रस्तस्तस्माद्रहोर्मुखात्मप्रमुच्य भास्वरो भवति यथैवं धूत्वा प्रहार शरीरं सर्वानर्थाश्रयमिहैव ध्यानेन कृतात्मा
units.english: from his hairs,becomes free from dirt, clean,so, in the same manner, having shaken off all evilcalled Merit and Demerit,and asreflectedMoon frees itself from Rāhu’s mouth and becomes bright,so shaking off the Bodygetting rid of it, as the receptacle of all evil,and by means of contemplation, having fulfilled all ends

units.sanskrit: कृतकृत्यः सन्नकृतं नित्यं ब्रह्मलोकमभिसंभवामीति ।
units.english: obtain the uncreatedEternalRegion of Brahman

units.sanskrit: द्विर्वचनं मन्त्रसमाप्त्यर्थम् ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Mantratext

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य त्रयोदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Section of Discourse

units.sanskrit: आकाशो वै नाम नामरूपयोर् निर्वहिता ।
units.english: That which is named ‘Ākāśa’ is the revealer of Name and Form;

units.sanskrit: ते यदन्तरा तद् ब्रह्म तद् अमृतं स आत्मा ।
units.english: and that inside which these two lie is Brahman; that is the Immortal; That is the Self

units.sanskrit: प्रजापतेः सभां वेश्म प्रपद्ये यशो ऽहं भवामि ब्राह्मणानां यशो राज्ञाम् यशो विशाम् ।
units.english: ‘ enter the Assembly House of Prajāpati; am the glory of Brāhmaṇas, the glory of Kṣattriyas, the glory of Vaiśyas; wish to attain that glory;

units.sanskrit: स हाहं यशसां यशः ।
units.english: am the glory of glories

units.sanskrit: श्येतम् अदत्कम् अदत्कं श्येतं लिन्दु माभिगां लिन्दु माभिगाम् ॥
units.english: May never go to that which is Red and Toothless, though devouring and slipperyyea, may never go to it’

units.sanskrit: आकाशो वा इत्यादि ब्रह्मणो लक्षणनिर्देशार्थमाध्यानाय । आकाशो वै नाम श्रुतिषु प्रसिद्ध आत्मा ।
units.english: The text beginning with the words ‘that which is Ākāśa etc, etc’ is for the purpose of providing a definition of Brahman for purposes of meditation,that which is named Ākāśa,ie the Self wellknown as such in Vedic Texts;

units.sanskrit: आकाश इवाशरीरत्वासूक्ष्मत्वाच्च । स चा'काशो नामरूपयोः स्वात्मस्थयोर्जगद्बीजभूतयोः सलिलस्येव फेनस्थानीययोर्निर्वहिता निर्वोढा व्याकर्ता ।
units.english: so named because of His being like Ākāśa, incorporeal and extremely subtilethis Ākāśa is the revealermaintainer, differentiatorof Name and Formboth these subsisting in His own Self and serving as the Seed of the Universe, and standing to Brahman in the same relationship as Foam does to Water

units.sanskrit: ते नामरूपे यदन्तरा यस्य ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तरा मध्ये वर्तेते, तयोर्वा नामरूपयोरन्तरा मध्ये यन्नामरूपाभ्यामस्पृष्टं यदित्येतत्तद्ब्रह्म नामरूपविलक्षणं नामरूपाभ्यामस्पृष्टं तथापि तयोर्निर्वोढुत्वं
units.english: ThatBṛahamaninside,withinwhich these two lie,or, that which lies within Name and Form, and which is not touched by Name and Form,is Brahman entirely different from Name and Form, untouched by Name and Form, and yet the Revealer of both these,such is Brahman

units.sanskrit: लक्षणं ब्रह्मेत्यर्थः । इदमेव मैत्रेयीब्राह्मणेनोक्तं चिन्मात्रानुगमात्मसर्वत्र चित्स्वरूपतैवेति गम्यत एकवाक्यता ।
units.english: This is what has been expounded in the MaitreyīBrāhmaṇa And in all these accounts of Brahman, Pure Consciousness is the common element running through all, it is understood that Brahman is of the nature of Pure Consciousness;

units.sanskrit: कर्थ तदवगम्यत इत्याहस आत्मा । आत्मा हि नाम सर्वजन्तूनां प्रत्यक्चेतनः स्वसंवेद्यः प्रसिद्धस्तेनैव स्वरूपेणोन्नीयाशरीरो व्योमवत्सर्वगत आत्मा ब्रह्मेत्यवगन्तव्यम् ।
units.english: In what way is this nature of Brahman understood? That is the Self;this term ‘Self’ stands for the Personified Consciousness Soul of all creatures which Selfcognisable and is wellknown as such; and it is in this form of Soul that, It is to be understood as being the Self, the Brahman, without Body and allpervading, like Ākāśa

units.sanskrit: तच्चा'त्मा ब्रह्मामृतममरणधर्मा ।
units.english: That Se is Brahman, immortal,not subject to death

units.sanskrit: अत ऊर्ध्व मन्त्रः ।
units.english: What follows after this is a Mantratext

units.sanskrit: प्रजापतिश्चतुर्मुखस्तस्य सभां वेश्म प्रभुविमितं वेश्म प्रपद्ये गच्छेयम् ।
units.english: Prajāpati is the fourfaced Deity;His Assembly Housethe Royal Hall, entergo into

units.sanskrit: किञ्च यशो ऽहं यशो नामा'त्माहं भवामि ब्राह्मणानाम् ।
units.english: Further, am the glory,ie the Self named ‘glory’of Brāhmaṇas;

units.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणा एव हि विशेषतस्तमुपासते ततस्तेषां यशो भवामि । तथा राज्ञां विशां च ।
units.english: Brāhmaṇas alone particularly meditate upon the Self, hence am the glory of Brāhmaṇas;so also of Kṣattriyas and Vaiśyas

units.sanskrit: ते ऽप्यधिकृता एवेति तेषामप्यात्मा भवामि ।
units.english: these also are entitled to meditate upon, hence am the Self of those men also

units.sanskrit: तद्यशो ऽहमनुप्रापत्स्यनुप्राप्तुमिच्छामि स हाहं यशसामात्मनां देहेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिलक्षणानामात्मा ।
units.english: wish to attain that Glory am the glorythe Selfof gloriesie of the Selves that have to be associated with, and characterised by, the body, the senseorgans, mind and intellect

units.sanskrit: किमर्थमहमेवं प्रपद्य इति,
units.english: Why do enter the House?

units.sanskrit: उच्यतेश्येतं वर्णतः पक्वबदरसमं रोहितम् । तथादत्कं दन्तरहितमप्यदत्कं भक्षयितृ स्रीव्यञ्जनं तत्सेविनां तेजोबलवीर्यविज्ञानधर्माणामपहन्तृ विनाशयित्रित्येतत् । यदेवंलक्षणं श्येतं लिन्दु पिच्छिलं तन्माभिगां माभिगच्छेयम् ।
units.english: Śyeta is Red,in colour, like the ripe plum, ruddy,and ‘adatka’ is toothless,without teeth,and yet, again adatka is devouring,this refers to the female organ, which devours ie destroys, those who are addicted thereto, by depriving them of Energy, Strength, Virility, Understanding and Merit,this that is red and sljpperymay never go to

units.sanskrit: द्विर्वचनमत्यन्तानर्थहेतुत्वप्रदर्शनार्थम् ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate that which is mentioned as a source of great Evil

units.sanskrit: तद् धैतद् ब्रह्मा प्रजापतय उवाच प्रजापतिर् मनवे मनुः प्रजाभ्यः ।
units.english: End of Section of Discourse Brahmā expounded this to Prajāpati, Prajāpati to Manu and Manu to the People

units.sanskrit: आचार्यकुलाद् वेदम् अधीत्य यथाविधानं गुरोः कर्मातिशेषेणाभिसमावृत्य कुटुम्बे शुचौ देशे स्वाध्यायम् अधीयानो धर्मिकान् विदधद् आत्मनि सर्वेन्द्रियाणि संप्रतिष्ठाप्याहिंसन् सर्वभूतान्य् अन्यत्र तीर्थेभ्यः । स खल्व् एवं वर्तयन् यावद् आयुषं ब्रह्मलोकम् अभिसंपद्यते । न च पुनर् आवर्तते न च पुनर् आवर्तते ॥
units.english: Having read the Veda at the Teacher’s house according to the prescribed rule,during the time left after performing his duties to the Teacher,having obtained his discharge and settled in his Household,studying the Veda in a clean spot,having brought on righteous persons,and having withdrawn all his senseorgans into the Self,never causing pain to any living beings, except in places specially ordained,one who behaves thus throughout life reaches the Region of Brahman and does not return,yea, does not return

units.sanskrit: तद्धैतदात्मज्ञानं सोपकरणमोमित्येतदक्षरमित्याद्यैः सहोपासनैस्तद्वाचकेन ग्रन्थेनाष्टाध्यायीलक्षणेन सह ब्रह्मा हिरण्यगर्भः परमेश्वरो वा तद्द्वारेण प्रजापतये कश्यपायोवाच । असावपि मनवे स्वपुत्राय ।
units.english: ThisPhilosophy of the Selfalong with its auxiliaries, in the shape of ‘the syllable Om’ along with the Meditationsand the Treatise dealing with these subjects, consisting of eight! Discourses,BrahmāHiraṇyagarbha or the Supreme God Himself, through Hiraṇyagarbha,expounded to Prajāpatito Kāśyapa;this Kāśyapa expounded it to his Son, Manu,and Manu expounded it to the people

units.sanskrit: मनुः प्रजाभ्य इत्येवं श्रुत्यर्थसंप्रदायपरम्परया'गतमुपनिषद्विज्ञानमद्यापि विद्वत्स्ववगम्यते ।
units.english: Such is the Philosophy of the Upaniṣads which is still understood to be the Essence of the Veda, handed down through the said tradition

units.sanskrit: यथेह षष्ठाद्यध्यायत्रये प्रकाशितात्मविद्या सफलावगम्यते तथा कर्मणां न कश्चनार्थ इति प्राप्ते तदानर्थक्यप्राप्तिपरिजिहीर्षयेदं कर्मणो विद्वद्भिरनुष्ठीयमानस्य विशिष्टफलवत्त्वेनार्थवत्त्वमुच्यतेआचार्यकुलाद्वेदमधीत्य सहार्थतो ऽध्ययनं
units.english: In the last three Discourses beginning with the Sixth, ie in Discourses , , , the Science of the Self has been revealed, and it is understood to be fruitful;so that there is no useful purpose served by Actions Sacrifices prescribed in the scriptures There being a possibility of such an idea being entertained, the Teacher,with a view to refute this uselessness of Actions,proceeds to describe the usefulness of Actions as performed by the learned and wise, which bring about very excellent results

units.sanskrit: कृत्वा यथाविधानं यथास्मृत्युक्तैर्नियमैर्युक्तः सन्नित्यर्थः । सर्वस्यापि विधेः स्मृत्युक्तस्योपकपर्वाणकं प्रति कर्तव्यत्वे गुरुशुश्रूषायाः प्राधान्यप्रदर्शनार्थमाहगुरोः कर्म यत्कर्तव्यं तत्कृत्वा कर्मशून्यो यो ऽतिशिष्टः कालस्तेन कालेन वेदमधीत्येत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Having read the Veda at the Teacher’s House,ie read the Vedic text along with its meaning,according to the prescribed rule,carefully following the rules laid down in the Smṛtis;inasmuch as for the person who is going to enter the Household, it is necessary to act up to all the rules prescribed in the Smṛtis, the text lays special stress upon one of these, the attendance upon the Teacher,during the time that is leftunspecified after performing all that is due to the Teacher,during such time not specified, having read the Veda;

units.sanskrit: एवं हि नियमवताधीतो वेदः कर्मज्ञानफलप्राप्तये भवति नान्यथेत्यभिप्रायः ।
units.english: the sense is that it is only when the Veda is read in this manner, strictly in accordance with these rules,not otherwisethat it brings about its fruit in the shape of Action and Knowledge;

units.sanskrit: अभिसमावृत्य धर्मजिज्ञासां समापयित्वा गुरुकुलन्निवृत्य न्यायतो दारानाहृत्य कुटुम्बे स्थित्वा गार्हत्थ्वे विहिते कर्मणि तिष्ठन्नित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Having obtained his discharge,after having completed the Inquiry into Duty and returned from the Teacher’s House; Taking a wife according to law, and settled in the Household,ie duly carrying on the Duties of the Householder;

units.sanskrit: तत्रापि गार्हस्थ्यविहितानां कर्मणां स्वाध्यायस्य प्राधान्यप्रदर्शनार्थमुच्यतेशुचौ विविक्ते ऽमेध्यादिरहिते देशे यतावदासीनः स्वाध्यायमधीयानो नैत्यकमधिकं च
units.english: and in order to emphasise the allimportance of Vedic Study among all the duties of the Householder, it is addedstudying the Veda in a clean spot,secluded and free from unclean things, seated in the prescribed manner;learning the compulsory portion of the Ṛk and other Vedas, and also as much more as he can;

units.sanskrit: यथाशक्ति ऋगाद्यभ्यासं च कुर्वन्धार्मिकान्पुत्राञ्शिष्यांश्च धर्मयुक्तान्विदधद्धार्मिकत्वेन
units.english: Having brought up righteous personsequipping his sons and pupils with rightconduct training them to a righteous life

units.sanskrit: तान्नियमयन्नात्मनि स्वहृदये हार्दे ब्रह्मणि सर्वेन्द्रियाणि संप्रतिष्ठाप्योपसंहृत्येन्द्रियग्रहणात्कर्माणि
units.english: Having withdrawndrawn awayall his senseorgans into the Self,into the Brahman in the Heartaway from the apprehending of their objects;and having renounced all actions;

units.sanskrit: च संन्यस्याहिंसहिंन्सां परपीडामकुर्वन्सर्वभूतानि स्थावरजङ्गमानि भूतान्यपीडयन्नित्यर्थः । भिक्षानिमित्तमटनादिनापि परपीडा स्यादित्यत आहअन्यत्र तीर्थेभ्यः ।
units.english: Not causing pain to living beings,moving and unmoving;as there is some sort of pain inflicted in the begging for food and considering about which are prescribed for the renunciate also,the text adds the qualifying clause ‘except in places specially ordained’;

units.sanskrit: तीर्थं नाम शास्रानुज्ञाविषयस्ततो ऽन्यत्रेत्यर्थः ।
units.english: the term ‘tīrtha’ stands for that which is sanctioned by the scriptures;

units.sanskrit: सर्वाश्रमिणां चैतत्समानम् तीर्थेभ्यो ऽन्यत्रहिंसैवेति । अन्ये वर्णयन्ति कुटुम्ब एवैतत्सर्वं कुर्वन्स खल्वधिकृतो यावदायुषं यावज्जीवमेवंयथोक्तेन प्रकारेणैव वर्तयन्ब्रह्मलोकमभिसंपद्यतेदेहान्ते न च पुनरावर्तते शरीरग्रहणाय ।
units.english: and these are excepted;This is a duty common to men in all stages of life; some people go even so far as to assert that the ‘Hiṃsā’ done at sanctioned places is not Hiṃsā at all; One who does all this while Settled in the Household, the man who thus becomes entitled to further progress throughout life,as long as he lives and behaves thusreaches the Region of Brahman, on the death of the Body;and he does not return,for taking up another Body;

units.sanskrit: पुनरावृत्तेः प्राप्तायाः प्रतिषेधात् ।
units.english: this clause denies the Rebirth which might be considered likely

units.sanskrit: अर्चिरादिना मार्गेण कार्यब्रह्मलोकभिसंपद्य यावद्ब्रह्मलोकस्थितिस्तावत्तत्रैव तिष्ठति प्राक्ततो ना'वर्तत इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: What is meant is that having, through the Path of light and the rest, having reached the created region of the created and hence comparatively ephemeral Brahman the Man stays in that Region as long as that Region itself lasts, and before thattill then ie till Final Dissolutionsays Ānandagirihe does not return to life

units.sanskrit: द्विरभ्यास उपनिषद्विद्यापरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥
units.english: The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the treatise on the PHILOSOPHY of the UPANIṢADS

units.sanskrit: इति च्छान्दोग्योपनिषदि अष्टमाध्यायस्य पञ्चदशः खण्डः
units.english: End of Discourse End of Chāndogya Upaniṣad
